# Runtime UI

<!-- index: Runtime UI -->
<!-- index: HUD -->
<!-- index: Theme -->
<!-- index: Focus ring -->
<!-- index: Safe area -->
<!-- index: Toast -->
<!-- index: Screen reader -->
<!-- index: Icon atlas -->

`regia_ui` is the runtime (in-game) UI — HUD, menus, toasts — driven by taffy layout and
cosmic-text, behind `UiPlugin` (added by `DefaultPlugins` when the `ui` feature is on).
The runtime is [spec 18](docs/specs/18-runtime-ui.md). The default look is
[the UI default design](docs/specs/ui-default-design.md). A task procedure is
[UI and audio](book/how-to/play/ui-and-audio.md).

## Authoring

UI is authored as `.ui.ron` and spawned as an entity, or built in code from widgets. The frozen
shape, version 11 since text input options and image fit (`docs/formats/ui-ron.example.ui.ron`; older files still
load and `regia upgrade-project --write` renumbers them), is a `version` and a `root` node with `style`
and `children` — a simple HUD:

```ron,ui
(
    version: 3,
    root: (
        name: "hud",
        style: (direction: column, padding: 16, gap: (8, 8)),
        children: [
            (
                name: "score",
                classes: ["surface"],
                style: (padding: 8, size: (200, Auto)),
                text: (spans: ["Score: 0"], style: (font_px: 22)),
                bind: (source: "Score.value", format: "Score: {:03}"),
            ),
            (
                widget: button,
                interactable: true,
                style: (padding: 10),
                children: [(
                    text: (spans: [Loc("menu-start")]),
                )],
            ),
        ],
    ),
)
```

`spawn_ui` uses only the root's `style` and `children`; put `safe_area` (and `background`, …) on a
child. A `format` keeps literal text around its one placeholder, so `"Score: {:03}"` paints
`Score: 007`.

A node carries `text`, an `image` fill and `style` directly. The `widget:` field adds behavior:
`button`, `toggle`, `slider`, `progress`, `text_input`, `dropdown`, `tab_bar`, `modal`, `tooltip`,
`scroll`, `list`, `focusable`, `popup_menu`, `context_menu`, `menu_bar`, and the touch controls
`stick` and `v_button` — see `docs/formats/ui-ron.md`. Bindings
like `bind: (source: "Score.value", format: "…")` update from reflected state, so a HUD tracks the
world without a system per label.

A text input takes optional limits after its placeholder and multi-line flag:
`text_input("PIN", false, (max_chars: 4, secret: '*', filter: integer))` keeps at most four digits and draws stars
(`read_only: true` allows selecting but not editing). An image fills its node by `fit`: `stretch`, `contain`
(letterboxed, the default) or `cover` (fills the node and crops the overflow, centred).

## Game widgets

A lobby list, a scoreboard, a radar and minimap, world markers and target brackets come ready to use, in code or in
`.ui.ron`: see [Game widgets](book/user-guide/game-widgets.md).

## Themes and widgets

Colors, spacing, type scale and per-widget looks come from a `.theme.ron` of design tokens. A theme
can extend another, and the built-ins are `regia-dark` (default), `regia-light`,
`regia-high-contrast` and `regia-light-high-contrast`. See [UI themes (agents)](book/agents/ui-theme.md) and
[widget styles](book/agents/ui-widget-style.md). The [radial menu](book/user-guide/radial-menu.md) is a ready-made
wheel widget.

## Graphs and meters

`UiCanvas { rects }` draws filled rectangles over a node, placed in the node's unit square
(`min`/`max` in 0..1). Changing it redraws only that node's subtree and never runs layout again, so
a graph can update every frame cheaply. The [performance overlay](book/user-guide/performance-overlay.md)'s
frame-time graph is one `UiCanvas`.

## Toasts

The event router raises **toasts** — short on-screen messages (a sim event fires one, a settings
change can announce one). They surface as `toast` entries in the agent protocol's
[`events.read`](book/agents/events.md), which is how tests assert a message appeared.

## Accessibility

`GameSettings`'s `accessibility` section sets subtitles and UI text scale; text renders through
cosmic-text with script fallback (Latin, Arabic, CJK). Localization is fluent-bundle + BCP-47
(`GameSettings.language`).

The focus ring shows only while the player navigates with a keyboard or gamepad; a mouse click or touch
hides it and keeps focus where it was. Set `FocusRingPolicy::Always` to show it in every input mode (or
`Never` if the game draws its own focus visuals). Its colour, width and offset are the theme tokens
`color.focus-ring`, `border.width.focus` and `border.width.focus-offset`; list rows draw it inset. See
[UI focus ring](book/agents/ui-focus-ring.md).

## Safe areas

The `SafeArea` resource reports display cutouts and system insets; the UI keeps interactive widgets
inside it on notched phones and handhelds (`docs/specs/18-runtime-ui.md`).

## Controller navigation

Arrows, Tab, the D-pad, the left stick and the shoulder buttons move focus through one focus graph. Put a `Focusable`
on every interactive node and a `DefaultFocus` on every screen; geometry does the rest. To shape the moves, put a
`FocusGroup` on a container: its children are searched first, and each edge escapes (default), stops or wraps.

```rust,wrap
# use regia::prelude::*;
# let mut commands: Commands = todo!();
# let world: &mut World = todo!();
# let app: &mut App = todo!();
# let (card_row, pause_menu, inventory, play_button, version_label): (Entity, Entity, Entity, Entity, Entity) = todo!();
use regia_ui::{FocusGroup, TabIndex};

// A row of cards that wraps left and right, and a pause menu the D-pad cannot leave.
commands.entity(card_row).insert(FocusGroup::wrap_horizontal());
commands.entity(pause_menu).insert(FocusGroup::trap());
// A list that remembers the row you left when you come back to it.
commands.entity(inventory).insert(FocusGroup::new().remembering());
// Tab visits "Play" first; the version label is skipped by Tab but reachable with the arrows.
commands.entity(play_button).insert(TabIndex(1));
commands.entity(version_label).insert(TabIndex(-1));
```

If the focused node is despawned or hidden while the player uses a controller, focus moves to the nearest node, so the
focus ring is never lost. Agents can inspect the graph with `ui.nav_graph` and check it with `ui.nav_lint`
([UI focus graph](book/agents/ui-navigation.md)).

## Themes

Classed nodes take their look from the active `.theme.ron` theme (`regia-dark` by default). A node's classes name a
widget type and variations (`button` is `Button`, `primary` is `Button.primary`); each property comes from the node's
`ThemeOverride`, then the variation, the type and the theme defaults. Swap the theme at runtime by writing the
`ActiveTheme` resource; colors cross-fade over the theme's base motion time.

```rust,wrap
# use regia::prelude::*;
# let mut commands: Commands = todo!();
# let world: &mut World = todo!();
# let app: &mut App = todo!();
*world.resource_mut::<regia_ui::ActiveTheme>() = regia_ui::ActiveTheme::named("regia-light");
```

A disabled widget draws at 0.45 opacity (`UiThemes::disabled_opacity`; `1.0` turns it off). Writing your own theme and the
resolution rules: [UI themes](book/agents/ui-theme.md).

## Input events and layers

Besides `Click`, a node can raise `DoubleClick`, `ContextClick`, `MiddleClick`, `Scroll`, `LongPress` (with `LongPressable`)
and `Repeat` (with `RepeatOnHold`). A node with `InputLayer` is a layer root: only the top layer's subtree gets hover,
clicks and focus, and an open `Modal` is a layer by itself. Details and the `ui.layers` method:
[UI input](book/agents/ui-input.md).

## Motion presets

Add `UiMotion` to a node to animate it on enter, exit, hover and press without writing tweens. `UiMotion::preset` has
`button` (pressed sink), `card` (hover lift, pressed sink), `popup` (zoom), `dialog` and `toast` (slide; a toast despawns
when it leaves) and `page` (fade). Close a node with `UiMotionState::request_exit`. Durations and curves come from the
theme's `motion.*` and `ease.*` tokens. The player's reduced-motion setting (`GameSettings.accessibility.reduced_motion`)
makes moves jump and keeps only a short fade; plain tweens and theme swaps stop animating.

```rust,wrap
# use regia::prelude::*;
# let mut commands: Commands = todo!();
# let world: &mut World = todo!();
# let app: &mut App = todo!();
# let dialog_node: regia_ui::UiNode = todo!();
commands.spawn((dialog_node, regia_ui::UiMotion::preset("dialog").unwrap_or_default()));
```

Details and the `ui.motion` method: [UI motion presets](book/agents/ui-motion.md).

## Driving the UI from an agent

`ui.query`, `ui.state`, `ui.click`, `ui.focus`, `ui.type` and `ui.set_value` find and operate nodes through the same input
path a mouse uses; `play.wait_until` has `ui.node_exists` and `ui.node_state`. See [Runtime UI (agents)](book/agents/ui.md).

## Text edge cases

Unwrapped text with `TextOverflow::Ellipsis` ends in "…" on its visual end, the left for right-to-left lines. An emoji
followed by U+FE0F uses the color emoji face; Arabic letters in a mixed label use the Naskh face while the Latin
words keep Inter. CR LF, CR and U+2028 all break a line once, and invisible format characters never draw a box.
Changing a span's color shows on the next frame without reshaping. `ShapedText` reports its lines and
`missing_glyphs`; agents read them with `ui.text_shape`: [UI text shaping](book/agents/ui-text.md).

## Screen readers

`regia_ui::a11y` builds an accessibility tree (roles, names, values, states) from the widgets; add `Accessible` to
override a node's role or name, hide decoration, or make a status text a live region. A `ScreenReaderBackend` gets
the changes; on Linux an AT-SPI stub records them (`REGIA_SCREEN_READER=1`). Nothing is built while no reader is
active. Details and `ui.a11y_tree`: [UI accessibility tree](book/agents/ui-a11y.md).

## Switching themes at runtime

Labels under themed nodes follow the theme's text color through the cross-fade (add `KeepTextColor` to a `Text` to
keep its color). The player's high-contrast setting selects the high-contrast theme and reduced motion makes the swap
instant. To follow a light or dark preference, set `ThemeMode::follow` and report the OS scheme in
`ThemeMode::system_scheme`. See [UI runtime theme switch](book/agents/ui-theme-switch.md).

High contrast keeps the player's scheme: the built-ins include `regia-light-high-contrast` next to
`regia-high-contrast`. On Windows, macOS and Android the OS light/dark appearance arrives as `SystemThemeChanged` and
`ThemeMode { follow: Some(SchemePreference::System), .. }` follows it without host code. The swap fade follows the
theme's `ease.standard` curve and blends in OKLab, so a dark-to-light switch brightens evenly; set the
`ThemeTransition` resource to change its length, curve or blend space. Read `ThemeChanged` and `ThemeFadeFinished`
messages to switch non-UI colors (a clear color, a post-process tint) in step with the UI. A settings menu stores the
player's light/dark choice in `GameSettings` `accessibility.color_scheme`.

## Icons

Load an `IconSheet` (RGBA pages and named drawings such as `gear@16`, `gear@24`) into the `IconAtlas` resource and
spawn `Icon::new("gear")`: the icon picks the drawing that matches its size (`IconSize::Small`, `Medium`, `Large`
follow the theme's icon size tokens), tints with the surrounding text color and recolors on a theme switch. The engine
ships no icon artwork yet. See [UI icons](book/agents/ui-icons.md).

## Default design, and what is still open

The default design ([spec file](docs/specs/ui-default-design.md), ADR-274) is largely
built. The ADR is still `proposed`. Treat the code and this chapter as the status, and treat
§ 10 of that file as the audit.

Built and covered above: `.theme.ron` themes `regia-dark`, `regia-light`,
`regia-high-contrast`, and `regia-light-high-contrast`; token resolution; the default widgets
that have types; the focus ring in navigation mode; icon atlases once you supply a sheet; theme
swap, including a light high-contrast variant and reduced motion.

Still open. None of these block the four shipped themes. Do not describe them as done:

- `font.mono` names JetBrains Mono, and no TTF for it ships under `regia_ui/assets/fonts`. The
  platform monospace draws.
- The engine ships no default icon glyphs. `<icon=name>` selects the font family `icon-<name>`.
- There is no Checkbox widget. Radio, spin box, foldable, split, tabs, toast, progress, and
  scroll draw with button or panel looks. They have no theme type of their own.
- Toast role bars and hover-to-pause are not built. The compact tree indent and the split view's
  5 percent keyboard step are not built.
- `focus_mode` (`all`, `click`, `none`) is not a setting. Default edge rules for lists, menus,
  and tab strips are not installed for you. `FocusGroup` rules work when the game sets them.
- Gamepad-cursor snapping (`soft_cursor`) is not built.
- Elevation tokens resolve onto the themed node. Nothing draws them as a drop shadow.
- There is no JSON Schema for `.theme.ron`. `Regia.toml` has no `[ui] theme` key. Select a theme
  with `ActiveTheme` or `ui.theme_select`.

Hot reload of a theme polls every 30 frames and reports on the status line, not as a toast.
The `wait_until` predicate is `{ "predicate": "ui.theme_generation", "at_least": n }`. Touch is
not its own `UiInputMode`. Modes are `Pointer` and `Navigation`. An active touch turns the hover
layer off.

<!-- source: book/user-guide/radial-menu.md -->
# Radial menu (weapon wheel, unit wheel)

`regia_ui::RadialMenu` is a reusable wheel for gamepad stick, mouse and touch: two to twelve sectors, an
optional centre action, an icon and a label per sector, hold-to-open or toggle, release-to-select or
press-to-select, and an open/close animation. The `ui_gallery` sample has a "Wheel" page (key `4`).

```rust,wrap
use regia_ui::prelude::*;
# use regia_ecs::prelude::{Commands, Entity, MessageReader, Single, With};
use regia_ui::{RadialConfirm, RadialEvent, RadialEventKind, RadialOpen, spawn_radial_menu};

fn spawn_weapon_wheel(mut commands: Commands, hud: Single<Entity, With<UiRoot>>) {
    let menu = RadialMenu::new(vec![
        RadialSector::new("rifle", "Rifle"),
        RadialSector::new("pistol", "Pistol"),
        RadialSector::new("grenade", "Grenade").enabled(false),
        RadialSector::new("knife", "Knife"),
    ])
    .with_center(RadialSector::new("holster", "Holster"))
    .with_open(RadialOpen::Hold)
    .with_confirm(RadialConfirm::Release)
    .with_open_action("WeaponWheel"); // a VirtualButtons action; or call menu.set_held(bool) yourself
    spawn_radial_menu(&mut commands, *hud, menu); // centred in the parent, starts closed
}

fn on_wheel(mut events: MessageReader<RadialEvent>) {
    for e in events.read() {
        if let RadialEventKind::Select { id, .. } = &e.kind {
            let _selected_id = id;
        }
    }
}
```

## Input

| Source | Selects with | Confirms with |
|---|---|---|
| Stick (right by default, `stick`) | the stick angle; magnitude below `dead_zone` (0.35) selects nothing, or the centre action | releasing the open control (hold), `A` (`UiNavActions::submit`) |
| Mouse | the cursor angle around the wheel's centre once the cursor moves; inside the hub (`inner_radius`) selects the centre action | button release (`Release`) or press (`Press`) |
| Touch | the finger's drag from where it landed (`touch_range` outer radii is full deflection) | lifting the finger (`Release`) or touching down (`Press`) |
| D-pad, shoulders, Tab | steps to the next enabled sector | `A` |

`B` / `Escape` cancels. While a wheel is open it takes the navigation actions (stick, d-pad, `A`, `B`), so the
focus ring does not move behind it, and it marks the pointer as consumed.

Hold mode opens while the open control is held and, under `Release`, selects the highlight when it is
released (releasing with nothing highlighted cancels). Under `Press` releasing cancels and a click or tap on a
sector selects. Toggle mode opens on the control's press and closes on the next press (a cancel).

## Selection feel

The math is `RadialGeometry`, pure and tested for 2 to 12 sectors: sector 0 is centred on `start_angle_deg`
(up by default), sectors run clockwise, and the angle wraps. A highlight only moves once the pointer is
`hysteresis` (0.12) of a sector past the boundary, so a stick resting on a boundary does not flicker; a
highlighted sector also survives the stick dipping to 80 % of the dead zone.

## Look

Each sector is a rounded chip placed on the ring (no arc-shaped quad, so no renderer change). Colours come from
the active theme (`surface_hi`, `primary`, `on_primary`, `text`, `text_dim`, `overlay`); `RadialStyle`
overrides any of them. Open and close ease over `animation_secs` (0.12; 0 is instant) and are driven by frame
time, so they run the same at 30 and 60 fps. Disabled sectors dim and cannot be selected.

## Events

`RadialEvent { target, kind }` messages: `Opened`, `Hover(selection)` (also `None` when the highlight leaves),
`Select { selection, id }`, `Cancel` and `Closed` (after `Select` and `Cancel`). `RadialMenu::selection`,
`open`, `progress` and `phase()` expose the live state.

Agents: see [Radial menu (agent guide)](book/agents/radial-menu.md).

<!-- source: book/user-guide/game-widgets.md -->
# Game widgets

Most multiplayer and action games need the same few screens. `regia_ui::game_widgets` has them ready: a lobby list, a
scoreboard, a radar and minimap, world markers, and target brackets with lead. Each is a component on a UI node, or a
`.ui.ron` widget for designers, and each takes its data from the game. They draw with the normal theme colors. The net
game template uses all of them: start from `regia new --template net-game`, or read `samples/net_game/src/hud.rs`.
For agents: [Game widgets (agents)](book/agents/ui-game-widgets.md).

## In the UI designer

The designer's preset list has `lobby_list`, `scoreboard`, `radar`, `minimap` and `marker_layer`. The preview fills them
with invented rows, so you can see the layout before there is a match. In a `.ui.ron` file they look like this:

```ron
(
    version: 10,
    root: (
        children: [
            (widget: marker_layer(())),
            (
                style: (size: (Points(200.0), Points(200.0))),
                widget: radar((range: 75.0)),
            ),
            (
                style: (size: (Points(240.0), Points(240.0))),
                widget: radar((world_rect: (-50.0, -50.0, 50.0, 50.0), map_image: 77)),
            ),
            (
                widget: scoreboard((
                    title: "Scores",
                    columns: [(key: "tags", title: "Tags", width: 64.0)],
                    hold_action: "Scores",
                )),
            ),
            (
                style: (size: (Points(520.0), Points(360.0))),
                widget: lobby_list((title: "Matches", create: "loc:lobby-create")),
            ),
        ],
    ),
)
```

A word in a label may be `"loc:<key>"`, a localization key. `docs/formats/ui-ron.md` lists every field. A map image is an
image id, as in the `image` field of any node.

The game does three things for these to come alive: it puts `HudFocus` on the player's pawn, `RadarBlip`, `WorldMarker`
or `TargetLock` on what should show, and returns standings from its rules.

## Scoreboard

Rules return their standings from one method, and a board shows them. The rules read whatever holds the scores: on a client,
the replicated components.

<!-- ignore-reason: a fragment of a game's rules; Player and Stats are the game's own components -->
```rust,ignore
impl GameRules for MyRules {
    fn on_player_joined(&mut self, _: &mut RulesCtx, _: Entity) -> Option<SpawnRequest> { None }

    fn scoreboard(&mut self, ctx: &mut RulesCtx) -> Option<ScoreSheet> {
        let mut players = ctx.world.query::<(&Player, &Stats)>();
        Some(ScoreSheet {
            columns: vec![ScoreSheetColumn::new("kills", "Kills")],
            rows: players
                .iter(ctx.world)
                .map(|(p, s)| ScoreSheetRow {
                    id: p.id,
                    name: p.name.clone(),
                    team: Some(p.team),
                    local: p.local,
                    values: vec![ScoreCell::Int(s.kills)],
                })
                .collect(),
            teams: Vec::new(),
        })
    }
}
```

A board groups teams with their totals (`group_by_team`), sorts by a column (a click on a heading sorts, again flips), and
breaks ties by name, then id, so two clients show one order. `Scoreboard::held("Scores")` shows it while that input action
is held. A game without `GameRules` sets `from_rules: false` and writes `table` itself.

A game on the match core writes no `scoreboard` method: `MatchSessionRules` (on the server) and `ReplicatedMatchRules`
(on a client) already return one row per player with kills, deaths, assists, objective points and score, under each
team's total ([Game modes](book/user-guide/game-modes.md#server-authoritative-games)).

## Lobby list

With `regia_net`'s `LobbyPlugin`, a `LobbyList` shows the compatible lobbies and refreshes itself. Its rows join on a click.
In a lobby it shows the members and their ready marks, a ready button, a leave button and, for the owner, a start button
that opens once all are ready. `LobbyListBridge` holds the choices: the data keys it shows as name and detail, the query, how
often to refresh, and where "start match" sends everyone (`server`; without one the app's `NetSession` hosts). A game with
its own server browser sets `manual: true`, writes the rows, and reads `LobbyListRequest`.

## Radar and minimap

<!-- ignore-reason: lines from a HUD setup system; hud, pawn, enemy and MAP_IMAGE are the game's own -->
```rust,ignore
spawn_radar(&mut commands, hud, Radar::with_range(75.0), [200.0, 200.0]);
spawn_radar(&mut commands, hud, Radar::minimap([-50.0, -50.0, 50.0, 50.0]).with_map(MAP_IMAGE, [0.0; 4]), [240.0, 240.0]);
commands.entity(pawn).insert(HudFocus);
commands.entity(enemy).insert(RadarBlip { clamp_to_edge: true, ..RadarBlip::dot(RED) });
```

North is world −Z, at the top. A radar centers on `follow`, else the `HudFocus` entity, else `center`; `rotate: true` turns
it so the player's heading points up. With a `map`, a radar shows a window of the image that scrolls with the center and a
minimap the whole image. The UI has no rotated image, so a radar with a map stays north up. Blips come from `RadarBlip`
components; `layer` and `layer_mask` choose which radar shows which. When there are more than `max_blips` the nearest win.
The entity at a radar's center draws no blip of its own; on a minimap it draws one like any other. A round radar with a map
needs a square node, or the image stretches. In `.ui.ron`, a radar with no `size` is 200 px square and a `marker_layer` with
no `size` fills its parent.
Moving blips cost no layout pass.

## World markers

A `MarkerLayer` node over the screen shows every `WorldMarker` where its entity is, through the same camera the frame draws
with. With `clamp_to_edge` an off-screen marker pins to the screen edge along its bearing, also when it is behind the camera.
`fade` fades it with distance; `offset` lifts it above the head. A layer under `UiRoot::camera` follows that camera, for
split screen.

A marker with `plate: Some(WorldPlate::default())` is instead a name plate in the world, on the world-space UI: it faces the
camera and scene geometry can hide it. Each plate has its own texture, so use them for a few things, and overlay markers for
many.

## Target brackets with lead

A `TargetLock` frames its entity with four corners sized from `radius_m`, never smaller than `min_px`, with a label and the
distance. With a `projectile_speed` it also draws a pip where to aim, so a projectile fired now meets the target. Velocities
come from `velocity` and `shooter_velocity`, or are estimated from the motion over about a tenth of a second. The projectile
inherits the shooter's velocity, and `gravity` raises the aim point. A shot that cannot catch the target draws no pip.

## Limits

A board draws at most 128 lines and 8 columns, a list 64 rows, a radar 1024 blips, a layer 256 markers and 32 brackets. Past
those the nearest (or the first in order) win. All of it runs only while such a widget exists.

# Runtime UI: a tour

[Runtime UI](book/user-guide/ui.md) shows how to author a HUD. This page is the map of everything else `regia_ui` does
today: which part owns which job, where its settings live, and which agent-guide page goes deeper. It lists
the shipped UI lanes of ADR-273 (the runtime lanes L1 to L8 and the default-design lanes D1 to D11). Each
agent-guide page named here has the exact method shapes and error codes.

Not every item below is in every build you may have: the table says which lane added it, and the release
notes (`docs/releases/`) name the version. If a method answers `unknown_method`, the build predates that lane.

## The pieces

| Job | Where it lives | Lane | Read |
|---|---|---|---|
| See and drive the UI from a script or test: find nodes, click, focus, type, wait on a state | `regia_ui::agent_bridge`, `ui.*` methods | L1 | [Runtime UI (agents)](book/agents/ui.md) |
| Click kinds (double, context, middle), scroll, long press, repeat; stacked input layers for modals and menus | `UiEvent`, `regia_ui::layers` | L4 | [UI input and layers](book/agents/ui-input.md) |

| Popups that escape clipping; dropdowns, tooltips, menus, menu bars, context menus | `regia_ui::popup`, `regia_ui::menu` | L5 | [UI popups and menus](book/agents/ui-menus.md) |

Lane D4 (the default icon set and a monospace font) has not shipped. The icon atlas mechanism has (D16,
[UI icons](book/agents/ui-icons.md)), but the engine ships no icon artwork: you load your own icon sheets.

## How a frame goes

1. Input arrives (mouse, touch, keyboard, gamepad, or an agent call, which becomes the same input).
2. The top input layer decides which subtree can receive it. A modal, a menu and a popup are layers.
3. Widgets react and send `UiEvent`s. Shortcuts fire here as `ShortcutTriggered` messages.
4. Tweens and theme cross-fades advance on the game clock. A paused or fixed-step game reproduces them exactly.
5. Themes resolve: type, variation, state layers, then `disabled` last. See [widget style](book/agents/ui-widget-style.md).
6. Layout runs, then the visual transform is applied to the computed rects.
7. The draw list is built and the overlay draws it.

Because time comes from the game clock, a test steps with `play.step` and compares; nothing needs a wall-clock
wait.

## Settings a player can change

`GameSettings.accessibility` holds `text_scale`, `reduced_motion` and `high_contrast`. The theme picks the
palette and the density. The focus ring follows `FocusRingPolicy`. All of them can be set from an agent, so a
test can check the UI at 150 percent text, in a right-to-left locale, with the high-contrast theme, with the
same script.

## A first menu in code

A menu is a node with the widget attached; the entries are data. Fragments in this chapter are not compiled
(`rust,ignore`); the agent pages show the JSON a test sends.

```rust,wrap
# use regia_ui::menu::{MenuEntry, MenuItem, PopupMenu};
let file_menu = PopupMenu {
    entries: vec![
        MenuItem::new("save", "Save").with_shortcut("Ctrl+S").into(),
        MenuEntry::Separator,
        MenuItem::new("quit", "Quit").into(),
    ],
    ..Default::default()
};
// Spawn it on the node that opens it (a button), next to the node's own bundle.
```

The same menu from a `.ui.ron` file uses `widget: popup_menu([...])`; see
[UI popups and menus](book/agents/ui-menus.md). To check it from a test:

```json
{"method": "ui.menu", "params": {"name": "file_menu"}}
{"method": "ui.menu_activate", "params": {"name": "file_menu", "path": ["save"]}}
```

## Checking your UI with an agent

A typical check of a settings screen, written as agent calls. The `ui.query` reply carries the slider's `value`,
which should now read 0.4:

```text
ui.set_value {"name": "volume", "value": 0.4}
play.step {"frames": 2}
ui.query {"type": "Slider", "name": "volume"}
```

The [UI agent map](book/agents/ui-map.md) lists every method, the permission each needs, and the error codes by
page.

## What is not done

- Rotation in `UiTransform`, text outline and underline, gradients and group opacity need shader work.
- World-space UI is not built. A tree view and a data grid are: see [UI tree](book/agents/ui-tree.md).
- IME composition is stored but not drawn; right-to-left caret movement is logical, not visual.
- The icon mechanism ([UI icons](book/agents/ui-icons.md)) and the UI sound table ([UI sounds](book/agents/ui-sounds.md)) are built, but the engine ships no icon artwork and no default UI sound set.

The full gap list with status is `docs/specs/ui-parity-roadmap.md`.

# Navigation & AI

<!-- index: Navmesh -->
<!-- index: Navigation agent -->
<!-- index: Crowd -->
<!-- index: Off-mesh link -->
<!-- index: Behavior tree -->
<!-- index: Perception -->
<!-- index: Formation -->
<!-- index: Flow field | see: Navigation agent -->

`regia_nav` builds a navmesh from level geometry and moves agents over it with pathfinding and
local avoidance. `regia_ai` adds behavior trees and a blackboard for decision-making. The tier-2
scope is [spec 22](docs/specs/22-tier2.md). Off-mesh links are
[spec 92](docs/specs/92-navmesh-offmesh.md). State trees are
[spec 38](docs/specs/38-state-trees.md). Which stack to call from a game is
[Choosing a navigation stack](book/user-guide/choosing-navigation.md). Goal-oriented planning is
[GOAP](book/user-guide/goap.md).

## Navmesh generation

```rust
use regia_core::math::Vec3;
use regia_nav::{NavMesh, NavMeshBuilder};

fn build_a_navmesh() -> Result<NavMesh, regia_nav::NavBuildError> {
    // A triangle soup (e.g. the level's static colliders), then build.
    let triangles = [
        [Vec3::new(-4.0, 0.0, -4.0), Vec3::new(4.0, 0.0, -4.0), Vec3::new(4.0, 0.0, 4.0)],
        [Vec3::new(-4.0, 0.0, -4.0), Vec3::new(4.0, 0.0, 4.0), Vec3::new(-4.0, 0.0, 4.0)],
    ];
    NavMeshBuilder::default().build(&triangles)
}
```

The pipeline is Recast-style (voxelization → walkable marking → regions → polygons). Polygons are a greedy rectangle merge of the
walkable grid; contours are traced separately for display and do not feed them.
`NavAgentParams` (radius, height, max_climb, max_slope) describe the creature the mesh is for; the
radius erodes the walkable surface away from walls. `NavMeshBuildParams` set the horizontal voxel
size (`cell_size`), the span-merge gap (`cell_height`: stacked spans in one column merge when the
gap is at most half of it; surface heights stay on the source triangles) and the border.

## Moving agents

An agent is an entity with a `NavAgent` (movement parameters) and a `NavAgentState` (velocity,
waypoints). `NavPlugin` steers them in `FixedUpdate` with ORCA local avoidance, integrating by
the fixed step (`FixedTime::step`), so speed does not depend on the frame rate.

```rust
use regia::prelude::*;
use regia_nav::{NavAgent, NavAgentState, NavPlugin};

fn add_nav_agents(app: &mut App, agent: Entity) {
    app.add_plugins(NavPlugin);
    app.world_mut().entity_mut(agent).insert((
        NavAgent { radius: 0.35, max_speed: 3.5, ..Default::default() },
        NavAgentState::default(),
    ));
}
```

Plan a path with `NavQuery` and install it:

```rust
use regia::prelude::*;
use regia_core::math::Vec3;
use regia_nav::{NavAgentState, NavMesh, NavObstacles, NavQuery};

fn plan(mesh: &NavMesh, obstacles: &NavObstacles, state: &mut NavAgentState, from: Vec3, to: Vec3) {
    let query = NavQuery { mesh, obstacles: Some(obstacles) };
    if let Some(path) = query.find_path(from, to, Vec3::splat(2.0)) {
        state.set_path(path);
    }
}
```

`find_path` runs A* over the polygon graph, then string-pulling (the funnel algorithm) to a smooth
waypoint list.

The agent step runs in the `NavStep` set and advances by the fixed step (`FixedTime::step()`), so
agents move at the same speed at any frame rate. Order a system that plans paths `.before(NavStep)`,
so agents follow the new plan on the same step. Order a system that reads the moved agents
`.after(NavStep)`. Left unordered, the executor may run them either way, and replays then depend on
the thread count (see [Replay soak](book/agents/replay-soak.md)).

## Dynamic obstacles

`NavObstacles` carves axis-aligned boxes out of the mesh; the carved surface is skipped by
pathfinding until the obstacle is removed.

```rust
use regia_core::math::Vec3;
use regia_nav::NavObstacles;

fn carve_then_reopen(obstacles: &mut NavObstacles) {
    let id = obstacles.add_box(Vec3::new(1.0, 0.0, 1.0), Vec3::new(2.0, 2.0, 2.0));
    // ... pathfinding routes around the box ...
    assert!(obstacles.remove(id));
}
```

## Tile cache and crowds

For obstacles that come and go often (doors, vehicles, dropped props), build a `NavTileCache`
instead of a single mesh. It keeps the voxelised walkable surface, cuts it into square tiles and
rebuilds only the tiles an obstacle touches:

```rust,wrap
# use regia_nav::*;
# use regia_core::math::Vec3;
# let level_triangles: Vec<[Vec3;3]> = todo!();
# let (min, max, from, to) : (Vec3, Vec3, Vec3, Vec3) = todo!();
let mut cache = NavTileCache::build(
    NavTileCacheParams { build: NavMeshBuildParams::default(), tile_size: 32 },
    &level_triangles,
)?;
let door = cache.add_obstacle(NavObstacleShape::Box { min, max })?;
cache.update(); // rebuilds the touched tiles only; `NavTileUpdate::rebuilt` lists them
let path = cache.query().find_path(from, to, Vec3::splat(2.0));
cache.remove_obstacle(door)?;
```

`NavObstacleShape::Cylinder { base, radius, height }` stands on `base`. Footprints are grown by the
agent radius. `update_limited(n)` spreads rebuilds over frames.

`NavCrowd` steers many agents along navmesh corridors with local avoidance (velocity sampling
against neighbours and walls), separation and collision resolution. It runs in whole fixed steps,
so two runs with the same inputs are bit-identical (`NavCrowd::digest`):

```rust,wrap
# use regia::prelude::*;
# use regia_core::math::Vec3;
# use regia_nav::*;
# let app: &mut App = todo!();
# let cache: NavTileCache = todo!();
# let (start, goal): (Vec3, Vec3) = todo!();
let mut crowd = NavCrowd::new(NavCrowdConfig::default())?;
let id = crowd.add_agent(cache.mesh(), start, CrowdAgentParams::new(0.35, 1.6, 3.5, 8.0))?;
crowd.set_target(cache.mesh(), id, goal)?;
app.insert_resource(cache).insert_resource(crowd).add_plugins(NavCrowdPlugin);
```

`NavCrowdPlugin` rebuilds queued tiles and steps the crowd once per `FixedUpdate` (set
`NavCrowdStep`), replanning corridors when tiles were rebuilt. Read agent positions with
`crowd.agent(id)` after `NavCrowdStep`. Agents report `Idle`, `Walking`, `Arrived` or `NoPath`, and
`OffMeshLink`, `Dormant`, `AwaitingTile`, `LinkQueued` or `LinkTimedOut` when off-mesh links or tile
streaming are in use.
The agent-protocol surface is on [navigation crowds](book/agents/navigation-crowds.md).

## Raycasts, random points and partial paths

`NavQuery` also answers the questions AI code asks between paths (NM-1):

- `raycast(start, end, extents, filter)` walks the mesh surface along a straight line and stops at
  the first wall or left-out area. `hit`, `t` (how far along), the wall `normal` and the polygons
  crossed come back in a `NavRaycastHit`: can this agent walk straight there, and where does a
  charge stop?
- `random_point(filter, rng)` gives a point uniform over the walkable surface, and
  `random_point_in_radius(center, radius, extents, reachable_only, filter, rng)` one within a
  circle; `reachable_only` skips islands the agent could never reach. The `Rng` is yours: the same
  seed gives the same point on every platform, so wander and patrol picks replay.
- `find_path_partial(start, end, extents, filter)` returns `NavPathResult::Complete`, `Partial`
  (the goal is unreachable: a path to the reachable point nearest it) or `NoStart`. `find_path`
  still returns `None` for an unreachable goal.

```rust
use regia_core::math::{Rng, Vec3};
use regia_nav::{NavPathResult, NavQuery, NavQueryFilter};

/// A reachable wander target within 8 m, replayable from `seed`.
fn wander_target(query: &NavQuery, here: Vec3, seed: u64) -> Option<Vec3> {
    let filter = NavQueryFilter::default();
    let mut rng = Rng::new(seed);
    let picked = query.random_point_in_radius(here, 8.0, Vec3::splat(2.0), true, &filter, &mut rng);
    picked.ok().flatten().map(|(_, point)| point)
}

/// Walk as close to `goal` as the mesh allows.
fn approach(query: &NavQuery, here: Vec3, goal: Vec3) -> Option<Vec<Vec3>> {
    match query.find_path_partial(here, goal, Vec3::splat(2.0), &NavQueryFilter::default()) {
        NavPathResult::Complete(path) | NavPathResult::Partial(path) => Some(path.waypoints),
        NavPathResult::NoStart => None,
    }
}
```

## Stuck agents

Agents get stuck: pinned in a corner by others, wedged head-on in a corridor too narrow to pass.
Set `NavCrowdConfig::stuck_window_steps` (or call `NavCrowd::set_stuck_detection`) and a walking
agent that has not come `stuck_min_progress_m` closer to its next corner for that many fixed steps
first re-plans, then is nudged toward the center of the polygon under it, then gives up as
`CrowdAgentState::Stuck`. Each rung is a `NavStuckEvent` (`NavCrowd::stuck_events`, and a message
with `NavCrowdPlugin`); `CrowdStats` counts them. A stuck agent walks again when you give it a
new target. `NavAgent` steering has the same ladder: insert a `NavAgentStuckConfig` resource and
read `NavAgentState::stuck.is_stuck()` or the `NavAgentStuck` messages. Both are off by default.

## Keeping the navmesh matched to the world

When the level itself changes, rebuild the navmesh under the change. Add `NavWorldPlugin` from
`regia_framework::nav_world` next to your `NavTileCache`, and chunks leaving a destructible and
runtime terrain edits rebuild the tiles under them, a few per fixed step:

```rust,wrap
# use regia::prelude::*;
# let app: &mut App = todo!();
app.add_plugins(regia_framework::nav_world::NavWorldPlugin);
```

The result equals a full build from the same geometry, and crowd agents replan on their own. For
geometry the plugin does not know, call `NavTileCache::rebuild_region` yourself, or write a
`NavRegionDirty` message and set your own source with `NavRegionQueue::set_source`.

A streamed world keeps its navmesh in cooked cells: see
[Navigation: region rebuilds and tile streaming](book/agents/navigation-world.md), which also lists the
agent methods.

Ground can have a cost. Paint an area over the mud and price it, and paths go around it:

```rust,ignore
use regia_nav::{NavAreaCosts, NavAreaVolume, NavObstacleShape};

cache.add_area_volume(NavAreaVolume::new(
    NavObstacleShape::Box { min: Vec3::new(-6.0, -1.0, -8.0), max: Vec3::new(6.0, 1.0, 8.0) },
    MUD,
))?;
let mut costs = NavAreaCosts::default();
costs.set(MUD, 8.0)?;
cache.set_area_costs(costs);

// This unit does not mind mud, and never swims.
params.link_filter = params.link_filter.with_area_cost(MUD, 0.125)?.without_area(WATER)?;
```

In a scene, a `regia_framework::nav_world::NavAreaZone` component paints a box around its entity.

For crowds in the distance, lanes cost no pathfinding: a `NavLaneGraph` of one-way lanes, from code or a
`.navlanes.ron` file, and a `NavLaneCrowd` that follows, passes and takes junctions with a fixed step. See
[Navigation: area costs and crowd lanes](book/agents/navigation-lanes.md).

## Behavior trees

A tree is authored as a flat node arena (`BehaviorTreeDef`, serializable to `.bt.ron`), compiled to
a runtime `BehaviorTree`, and ticked by `AiPlugin`. Leaf tasks are Rust types:

```rust
use regia_ai::{BtContext, BtStatus, BtTask};

#[derive(Default, regia_ai::BtTask)]
struct SeekTarget;

impl BtTask for SeekTarget {
    fn tick(&mut self, ctx: &mut BtContext<'_>) -> BtStatus {
        // ctx.world (exclusive), ctx.entity, ctx.dt, and the Blackboard via ctx.blackboard().
        let _ = ctx.dt;
        BtStatus::Running
    }
}
```

Composites (selector, sequence, parallel), decorators (condition, cooldown, repeat, timeout,
inverter) and **services** (a task run every tick for state updates, returning its child's status)
compose these leaves. Attach a `BehaviorTree` + `Blackboard` to the agent entity and register the
task in the `BtTaskRegistry`; `AiPlugin` ticks every tree each `FixedUpdate` and writes a reflected
`BehaviorTreeStatus` snapshot (root + per-node status) so the editor and agent protocol can inspect
the running tree.

The tick runs in the `AiStep` set, and `BtContext::dt` is the fixed step. The tick is an exclusive
system, so give it a place among your fixed-step systems. For example, the arena chains
`(PhysicsStep, AiStep, NavStep, ...)` so the trees plan paths that the nav step then follows on the
same step.

## Perception

A `Perception` component (sight radius and half-angle, hearing radius, team) gives an agent senses.
`line_of_sight` raycasts through the physics world, `in_sight_cone` tests the cone, `can_hear`
filters by distance, and `HearingEvent` is a message for team-filtered sound cues. Turn on
`AiPerceptionGizmos` to draw the senses ([Gizmos](book/user-guide/gizmos.md)).

## Stealth-style perception

Leave the defaults and an agent still acquires a target on the first clear look and forgets it
after `max_age_ticks`. For a stealth, squad or indoor game, turn on the pieces you need:

- **Hiding.** Put `Visibility` on the target (`factor` from 0 to 1: light, stance, camouflage).
  Put `SightSamples` on the observer to cast several rays across the body's bounds. Set
  `PerceptionSettings.detection_threshold` above 0. The meter fills from the clear fraction, the
  visibility and how far the target sits from the center of the cone. A half-hidden or dark
  target takes more steps to notice. A target the agent already knows stays known while any
  sample is clear.
- **Memory that fades.** Set a sense's `*_confidence_half_life`. Confidence falls while the
  target is unseen, and the last known position keeps moving by the last known velocity. With
  the half-life left unset, nothing moves and confidence stays 1.
- **Touch and scent.** `touch_radius` feels contact with no line of sight. `PerceptionSenses`
  registers a named callback (a scent trail, a heat sense) that returns a strength or nothing.
- **Squads.** `share_knowledge` writes what this agent sensed into `TeamKnowledge` for its team
  and, when it has an `AiSquadMember`, for its squad. A mate reads that list and can react to a
  target it never saw.

`ai.perception_get` reports confidence, the last known velocity and the meter.
`ai.team_knowledge` reads one team's shared facts. `ai.senses` lists the registered callbacks.
The agent page is [AI perception](book/agents/ai-perception.md).

See `samples/arena` for a flag-gated example (`ArenaConfig::use_navmesh`): bots navigate on the
navmesh and are driven by a behavior tree composed of a `SeekEnemy` and a `FireAtEnemy` leaf.

## Moving a thousand units to one place

On the deterministic grid (`regia_nav::det`, for lockstep games), a group move order should not plan one route per
unit. Build one flow field toward the destination and let every unit read its next step from it:

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;
use regia_nav::det::flow::{FlowCache, FlowCacheSettings, FlowSettings};
use regia_nav::det::grid::{GridSettings, NavGrid, NavStatic, Profile};

# fn main() -> Result<(), regia_nav::det::grid::GridError> {
let grid = NavGrid::new(Arc::new(NavStatic::build(None, Arc::new(GridSettings::hover_ground_jet()))?))?;
let mut flows = FlowCache::new(FlowCacheSettings::default());
let rally = grid.cell_at(200.0, 150.0);
let units: Vec<[f32; 2]> = (0..1000).map(|i| [-300.0 + (i % 40) as f32 * 4.0, -200.0 + (i / 40) as f32 * 4.0]).collect();
// Every unit with this order shares one field; the second lookup is a cache hit.
let field = flows.field(&grid, Profile::HOVER, &[rally], FlowSettings::default());
for pos in &units {
    if let Some(dir) = field.direction_at(*pos) {
        // Feed `dir` to the unit's steering (and the deterministic avoidance on top).
        let _ = dir;
    }
}
# Ok(())
# }
```

- Each tick, after `grid.sync_stamps(...)`, call `flows.on_sync(&grid, &sync)`. Full fields are rebuilt on next use;
  clustered flows rebuild only what the change touched.
- On a big map (past about 512 x 512 cells) use `flows.cluster_flow(&grid, profile, &[rally])` instead: it builds only
  the clusters units stand in and the chain to the goal. Its routes can cost up to about an eighth more than the full
  field's; reachability is the same.
- Turn on `FlowSettings { los_cells: 32, .. }` so units in plain sight of a single goal head straight for it instead of
  along 8-way steps, and `blend: true` for smoother turns between cells.
- A unit standing on a blocked cell gets `None`: move it to `grid.nearest_passable(...)` first.
- To see a field, hand `FlowDebug::new(&field)` to the deterministic debug draw (`DetDebugDraw::record`) and turn on
  its `flow` part; arrows point along each cell's move. To let an agent read fields, publish the grid into
  `DetFlowView` each tick (`view.publish(tick, &grid)`); `sim.grid_flow` then answers the directions and costs of any
  window for a goal it names.

Everything is integer cost and deterministic: two peers with the same grid and goals get the same field bit for bit.
Details and the costs: [Deterministic navigation grid](book/agents/det-grid.md#flow-fields).

## Moving agents from a tree: `MoveTo`, and which stack to use

`regia_ai::MoveTo` is a ready-made move leaf (and state-tree task): it plans through a named path provider (this
navmesh, the deterministic grid or the deterministic navmesh), follows the path or hands it to the crowd, succeeds
inside its acceptance radius and re-plans when the target moves. `AiPlugin` registers it and a `navmesh` provider. The
page [Choosing a navigation stack and a utility AI](book/user-guide/choosing-navigation.md) says when to use this navmesh, the lockstep
grid or the lockstep navmesh, and which utility reasoner goes with each.

## Group movement

A squad can move in a shape. Put an `AiFormation` on the squad, or load a `.formation.ron` file (named slots
around the leader, optional role tags, a spacing scale). The three built-in shapes are ring, line and wedge.

To have the navigation crowd keep that shape, mark each follower with a leader and a slot offset
(`NavCrowd::set_agent_group`). The leader walks its path. Followers steer to their slots and match the leader's
speed. In a doorway narrower than the shape they fall into a column behind the leader, then spread back into
the shape on the far side. When the leader stops, the group keeps the facing it had while moving. Turn on
the `ai_formation` gizmo group to see the slots and the column.

## Seeing AI in play

The behavior-tree debugger and the state-tree panel are editor panels. In a running game the same
information is an in-world overlay, off until you turn it on.

In the viewport, open **Show** and tick the row you want: Behavior tree, State tree, GOAP, Squad,
Formation, Move target, or Blackboard. Those rows stay as you set them when Game view is on. The
behavior-tree row writes the running leaf's name above the agent. The state-tree row writes the
active state. GOAP writes the current plan step and the goal. Squad draws a line from the leader
to each other member and a letter for the role. Formation marks each slot. Move target draws the
point the agent is walking to and the rest of its path. Blackboard writes the keys you asked to
watch.

The overlay can follow the selection, everyone within a radius, or every agent. It keeps at most
64 text labels a frame unless you raise that cap; the rest are counted and skipped. Shapes are
not capped. Turn the rows off and the overlay draws nothing.

# Goal-oriented action planning (GOAP)

<!-- index: GOAP -->
<!-- index: World state -->
<!-- index: Planner -->

`regia_ai::goap` is a planner for agents that choose *what to do next* by chaining actions:
give it the actions an agent can perform (each with preconditions, effects and a cost), the
world as it is now, and a goal as a partial description of the world as it should be. It
returns a minimum-cost sequence of actions that reaches the goal, or says why it cannot.
The formulation is Jeff Orkin's GOAP ("Three States and a Plan", GDC 2006); see
`docs/provenance.md` for the sources. GOAP has no spec file of its own. It ships beside the
behavior trees in [spec 22](docs/specs/22-tier2.md). It plans action names. It does not
apply damage, play montages, or move the body. A tree leaf or a character step does that. See
[Combat and abilities](book/how-to/play/combat-abilities.md).

GOAP complements behavior trees: a tree decides *that* the agent wants a table, the planner
works out *how* (fetch an axe, chop, craft — or the expensive stick-collecting fallback when
no axe exists), and tree leaf tasks execute the plan steps by action name.

## World state and facts

A `WorldState` is a fixed-size snapshot: up to 128 boolean facts (`MAX_BOOL_FACTS`, a
two-word bitset) plus up to 16 small integer facts (`MAX_INT_FACTS`, counts, resource
amounts). Facts are addressed by index; the meaning of each index is your game's convention.
A consistent bijection of the used boolean and integer indices preserves a planning problem:
relabel the start state, partial goal, and every action precondition and effect together. A
unique minimum-cost plan then keeps the same action-name sequence and cost, and its final state
maps back through the inverse bijection. Equal-cost alternatives need only preserve plan cost
and validity; tie order is deterministic for a fixed action declaration order, not invariant to
fact indices. Successful cache entries remain specific to the start state, goal and options.
A `FactTable` maps blackboard key names to fact indices once, then snapshots a `Blackboard`
into a `WorldState` to plan from (and can write a simulated state back):

```rust
use regia_ai::Blackboard;
use regia_ai::goap::{FactTable, WorldState};

fn snapshot_facts(blackboard: &Blackboard) -> WorldState {
    let mut facts = FactTable::new();
    let _has_axe = facts.add_bool("has_axe").expect("under the 128-fact limit");
    let _wood = facts.add_int("wood").expect("under the 16-fact limit");
    // Later, per planning request:
    facts.snapshot(blackboard)
}
```

Out-of-range fact indices never panic anywhere in the module: reads return the default
(`false` / `0`). Boolean builders and `Goal` ignore an index at or past the table (128 boolean
facts, 16 integer facts). An action's integer precondition or effect at or past 16 is stored, and
`Planner::plan` and `Planner::try_new` return `PlanError::InvalidAction` for that action.

## Actions, goals, planning

```rust
use regia_ai::goap::{Action, Goal, Plan, PlanError, PlanOptions, Planner, WorldState};

fn plan_for_planks() -> Result<Plan, PlanError> {
    // Fact indices: 0 = has_axe, 1 = has_wood, 2 = has_planks.
    let planner = Planner::new(vec![
        Action::new("pick_up_axe", 1.0).sets(0, true),
        Action::new("chop_tree", 2.0).requires(0, true).sets(1, true),
        Action::new("saw_planks", 1.0).requires(1, true).sets(2, true),
    ]);
    let start = WorldState::new();
    let goal = Goal::new().require(2, true);
    let plan = planner.plan(&start, &goal, &PlanOptions::default())?;
    for step in plan.steps() {
        // step.name, step.action_index, step.cost
        let _ = step;
    }
    Ok(plan)
}
```

- An `Action` has boolean preconditions/effects (`requires` / `sets`), optional integer
  preconditions (`requires_int` with an `IntCondition`) and effects (`sets_int` /
  `adds_int`, saturating), and a static cost — or a dynamic cost callback
  (`with_dynamic_cost`) for state-dependent pricing (a shortcut that is only cheap while a
  gate is open). The callback must be a pure, deterministic function of the state returning
  a finite, non-negative cost.
- A `Goal` is partial: only the facts it mentions must match. Per-fact weights
  (`with_weight`, `require_int_weighted`) shape the search heuristic only, never success.
- `Planner::plan` runs a forward A* search with an admissible heuristic (the weighted count
  of unsatisfied goal facts, scaled so it never overestimates), so the returned plan has
  minimum total cost. Ties break deterministically in action-declaration order: the same
  request always returns the same plan.
- Errors are `PlanError::NoPlan` (goal unreachable), `PlanError::LimitReached` (the
  `PlanOptions` node or depth budget ran out first — a plan may still exist) and
  `PlanError::InvalidAction` (empty action name, negative/non-finite cost including from a
  dynamic callback, integer fact out of range). `Planner::try_new` rejects a malformed
  action set at build time. A start state that already satisfies the goal is an empty plan,
  not an error.

`PlanOptions` sets the node budget (`max_nodes`, default 10 000), the plan length cap
(`max_depth`, default 64), the heuristic weight (`1.0` optimal; `0.0` is Dijkstra; above
`1.0` is faster weighted A* with bounded suboptimality) and whether to use the planner's
plan cache. Successful plans are cached by (state, goal, options); `Plan::cache_hit` tells
you a plan came from the cache, and adding an action clears it.

## Executing and replanning

Plans go stale: the axe breaks, another agent takes the wood. Before running each step (or
when the world changes), re-validate the remaining suffix against the current state:

```rust,wrap
# use regia_ai::goap::{Action, Goal, PlanOptions, Planner, WorldState};
# let planner = Planner::new(vec![
#     Action::new("pick_up_axe", 1.0).sets(0, true),
#     Action::new("chop_tree", 2.0).requires(0, true).sets(1, true),
#     Action::new("saw_planks", 1.0).requires(1, true).sets(2, true),
# ]);
# let current_state = WorldState::new();
# let goal = Goal::new().require(2, true);
# let options = PlanOptions::default();
# let plan = planner.plan(&current_state, &goal, &options)?;
# let next_step = 0;
let verdict = plan.validate_remaining(&current_state, next_step);
if !verdict.is_valid() {
    // verdict.first_invalid_step names the step whose preconditions stopped holding.
    let plan = planner.replan(&plan, &current_state, next_step, &goal, &options)?;
}
```

`Plan::validate(&state)` is the whole-plan form. `Planner::replan` keeps the still-valid
suffix unchanged (so an agent does not jitter between equal routes) and only searches
afresh when a precondition actually stopped holding, the suffix no longer reaches the
goal, or the goal changed. `Plan::simulate` gives the state a suffix would reach, which is
handy for debugging and editor previews.

## Limits, ties and cost

- **Depth limit.** `max_depth` is exact: if any plan of at most `max_depth` steps exists, the
  cheapest such plan is returned (within the node budget), even when a cheaper but longer
  plan exists. `LimitReached` from the depth limit means the search ran out of room, not
  that no plan exists.
- **Ties.** Between plans of equal cost, a path with fewer steps to the same state is kept;
  among equal-cost, equal-length plans the earlier-declared actions win. The result never
  depends on hash order or timing.
- **Threads.** `Planner`, `Plan`, `Goal` and `FactTable` are `Send + Sync`, so a planner can
  live in a component or resource; the plan cache is behind a lock.
- **Search effort.** The heuristic counts unsatisfied goal facts, which guides the search
  well when each action changes a few goal facts and poorly in dense domains where many
  actions touch many facts. On a seeded 128-fact, 60-action domain, goals reachable in 4
  actions expand a median of 540 nodes (worst of 20 seeds about 13 000), goals reachable
  in 6 actions a median of 6 700 (worst about 196 000). Keep action sets small per agent,
  keep `max_nodes` as a budget, and treat `LimitReached` as "replan later or fall back".

## On entities: `GoapAgent`

`GoapPlugin` (opt-in, ADR-2565) runs a planner per entity. Build the `Planner` once and share it between agents of a kind; its
plan cache is shared with it. The agent needs a `Blackboard`, which is where its facts come from:

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;

use regia_ai::goap::{Action, FactTable, Goal, Planner};
use regia_ai::{Blackboard, GoapAgent};

fn guard_agent() -> (GoapAgent, Blackboard) {
    let mut facts = FactTable::new();
    let has_wood = facts.add_bool("has_wood").unwrap_or_default();
    let has_table = facts.add_bool("has_table").unwrap_or_default();
    let planner = Arc::new(Planner::new(vec![
        Action::new("gather", 1.0).sets(has_wood, true),
        Action::new("craft", 1.0).requires(has_wood, true).sets(has_table, true),
    ]));
    let goal = Goal::new().require(has_table, true);
    (GoapAgent::new(planner, facts, goal), Blackboard::new())
}
```

Add `GoapPlugin` and spawn both on the entity. Each fixed step in `GoapStep`, before `AiStep`, an agent whose blackboard changed:

1. takes a finished search's result, exactly `GoapSettings::plan_latency_ticks` steps after it started;
2. reads its facts from the blackboard;
3. advances past each step whose effects now hold;
4. searches again when a remaining precondition no longer holds or the goal moved.

The planner does not run actions: game code does. Read the action name from the blackboard key `goap_action`
(`GoapAgent::action_key`), for example from a behavior-tree leaf, and write the effect's fact when the work is done. A valid plan
is kept when a cheaper one appears unless `replan_on_any_change` is set. `GoapAgent::set_goal` changes the goal.

**Budget.** A search stops after `options.max_nodes` expanded nodes (default 2 000) with `limit_reached`, and
`GoapSettings::max_plans_per_tick` limits how many start per step. A search that failed is not repeated until the facts or the
goal change, since it would fail the same way; call `GoapAgent::retry` after raising the budget.

**Determinism.** A search runs on the async compute pool, but its result is taken at a fixed step, never earlier. If the pool has
not finished it by then, the same search runs on the fixed step's thread, bounded by the budget, and gives the same plan. Two runs
replan on the same steps and get the same plans on any machine. Raise `plan_latency_ticks` if `GoapStats::searches_run_inline`
climbs.

`GoapStatus` is the reflected view (`state`, `steps`, `next_step`, `total_cost`, `replans`, `error`). The agent method
`ai.goap_plan` shows the whole plan (it answers `ai_goap_unavailable` without `GoapPlugin`): see
[AI perception](book/agents/ai-perception.md).

# Gameplay: players, characters, rules and save games

<!-- index: Gameplay -->
<!-- index: Player -->
<!-- index: Player controller -->
<!-- index: Character -->
<!-- index: Game rules -->
<!-- index: Save game -->
<!-- index: Gameplay tag -->
<!-- index: Ability | see: Combat and abilities -->

`regia_framework` is the gameplay layer: players and controllers, characters, game rules, scripts,
settings, and save games. It is the framework half of
[spec 14](docs/specs/14-scene-and-framework.md). Character motion against colliders is
[spec 15](docs/specs/15-physics.md) § 4 and
[spec 93](docs/specs/93-character-physics.md). Attributes, effects, and abilities are
[spec 53](docs/specs/53-abilities-attributes-effects.md). Save slots and character records
are [spec 91](docs/specs/91-character-save-templates.md). Procedures:
[Move a character](book/how-to/play/character.md) and
[Combat and abilities](book/how-to/play/combat-abilities.md).

## Players and controllers

A **player** is a human participant, local or in a network session. A **controller** drives a
character: `PlayerController` for humans, `AiController` for bots.

```rust
use regia::prelude::*;
use regia_scene::prelude::*;
use regia_framework::prelude::*;
use regia::core::math::Vec3;

fn spawn_player(mut commands: Commands) {
    let character = commands
        .spawn((
            Character,
            CharacterMovement::default(),
            Transform::from_translation(Vec3::new(0.0, 1.0, 0.0)),
        ))
        .id();
    let mut controller = PlayerController::new(0);
    controller.possess(character);
    commands.spawn((controller, PlayerStart));
}
```

`PlayerManager` tracks indices (split-screen local players); possession switches what a controller
drives. The protocol's `players.list` / `scene.possess` read and change this — see
[the agent guide's gameplay page](book/agents/gameplay.md).

## Characters

A `Character` is a capsule that moves with modes (`MovementMode`: walking, falling, flying,
swimming, custom) and can jump, crouch and sprint, driven by `CharacterInput`:

```rust
use regia::prelude::*;
use regia_framework::prelude::*;
use regia::core::math::Vec3;

fn apply_input(mut query: Query<(&mut CharacterInput, &CharacterState)>) {
    for (mut input, state) in &mut query {
        input.move_dir = Vec3::new(1.0, 0.0, 0.0);
        if state.grounded {
            input.jump = true;
        }
    }
}
```

Movement resolves against the world through the `CollisionQuery` backend (rapier, or the
flat/heightfield stubs — see [Physics](book/user-guide/physics.md)). `CharacterState` is the read-out for animation
and gameplay: velocity, `grounded`, `mode`, time in air.

## Game rules

`GameRules` is the per-level win/lose and spawn logic: hooks for level start, a player joining
(where and what to spawn), a character dying, a per-tick update, and whether the match is over.
Implement it (or use `DefaultRules`, free-for-all with no limits) and install it in the
`GameRulesResource`, or register it by name in `GameRulesRegistry` so a level selects it through
`LevelSettings.game_rules` (`RulesPlugin` resolves that name when a level loads). The framework
calls `on_player_joined` when a local player joins; the game calls `tick`, `on_level_start`,
`on_character_died` and `is_match_over` from its own systems, at the moments it defines. The
[arena tutorial](book/tutorials/arena.md) shows the pattern.

For a multiplayer mode (teams, flags, a hill, rounds, ready-up) use the match core instead of
writing those rules: [Game modes](book/user-guide/game-modes.md#which-layer-do-i-use) says which layer fits, and
the [capture-the-flag tutorial](book/tutorials/capture-the-flag.md) plays one with bots.

## Game states and GameFlow

Game flow (menus, loading, play, pause) is a set of **states** (`regia_ecs::state`, from
`bevy_state`). Add `GameFlowPlugin` for the standard flow, Boot → MainMenu → Loading → Playing ⇄
Paused, or declare your own:

```rust
use regia::prelude::*;

#[derive(States, Reflect, Default, Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
enum Level {
    #[default]
    Forest,
    Cave,
}

fn build(app: &mut App) {
    app.init_state::<Level>()
        .add_systems(OnEnter(Level::Cave), spawn_cave)
        .add_systems(Update, drip_water.run_if(in_state(Level::Cave)));
}

fn spawn_cave(mut commands: Commands) {
    // Despawned automatically when the game leaves Level::Cave.
    commands.spawn((Name::new("cave"), DespawnOnExit(Level::Cave)));
}

fn drip_water() {}
```

Change state with `ResMut<NextState<Level>>::set(Level::Cave)`; the switch happens once per frame,
right after `PreUpdate`, running `OnExit` of the old value, then `OnTransition`, then `OnEnter` of
the new one. `App::add_sub_state` adds states that exist only under one value of another
(`#[source(GameFlow = GameFlow::Paused)]`); `App::add_computed_state` adds states derived from
others (implement `ComputedStates`). A computed state that maps several source values to the same
value (Playing and Paused → `InGame`) should set `ALLOW_SAME_STATE_TRANSITIONS = false`, or moving
between those values re-runs its `OnExit`/`OnEnter` and despawns its scoped entities. States must
derive `Reflect`: that is what lets the agent protocol (`state.get` / `state.set`, see
[Game states](book/agents/states.md)) and the editor see them.

With `GameFlowPlugin`, register load work in `OnEnter(GameFlow::Loading)` through
`LoadingTasks::begin` and mark it done with `LoadingTasks::finish`; play starts on the first frame
nothing is pending. `regia_framework::flow::request_pause` / `toggle_pause` move between
Playing and Paused, and Paused freezes `Time`.

## Scripts

A **script** is a Rust behavior attached to an entity, editable in the inspector. Derive it and
register it:

```rust
use regia::prelude::*;
use regia_framework::prelude::*;

#[derive(Script, Reflect, Default, Clone)]
#[script(order = -7)]
struct Door {
    open: bool,
}

impl regia_framework::script::Script for Door {
    fn update(&mut self, ctx: &mut ScriptCtx) {
        // read/write the entity's components through ctx
    }
}

fn register(app: &mut App) {
    app.register_script::<Door>();
}
```

Scripts are ordinary reflected data with an `update` hook (plus `start`, `fixed_update`,
`late_update`, `on_event` and `on_message`), held as slots in an entity's `Scripts` component — the
simplest way to give an entity behavior. The editor's `editor.create_script` writes a new script and registers it at
`// REGIA:SCRIPTS`.

Inside a hook, `ctx` reaches the entity (`get`, `get_mut`, `insert`, `remove`, `transform_mut`,
`despawn`), the world (`spawn`, `find_by_name`, `commands`, `world`), other scripts
(`with_script`, `send_message`, `broadcast`, `send_message_in`), the clock (`delta_secs`, `time`),
input (`action2d`, `action_pressed`), timers and coroutines (`after`, `every`, `start_coroutine`),
seeded random numbers (`rand_f32`, `rand_range`) and physics queries: `ctx.physics()` returns the
raycast, shapecast, overlap and closest-point queries over the physics world, or `None` without
physics. Messages are delivered after every `update` of the frame; one sent from `on_message`,
`on_event` or `late_update` arrives on the next frame. A system that must run after the scripts'
`late_update` orders itself `.after(ScriptsSet::Late)`.

## Coroutines

Sequences that span frames — a cutscene, a tutorial step, spawn waves — are easiest to write as a
**coroutine**: an `async` block the engine polls once per frame (`CoroutinePlugin`). The block gets a
`Co` context instead of the world; world access goes through closures the executor runs between
polls, so nothing is borrowed across an `.await`:

```rust
use regia::prelude::*;
use regia_framework::coroutine::{Co, start_coroutine};

#[derive(Resource, Default)]
struct Wave(u32);

fn start_waves(world: &mut World, spawner: Entity) {
    // Bound to `spawner`: despawning it cancels the sequence.
    start_coroutine(world, Some(spawner), |co: Co| async move {
        for _ in 0..3 {
            co.queue(|world| world.resource_mut::<Wave>().0 += 1); // spawn a wave
            co.wait_seconds(10.0).await; // game time: pausing stops the clock
        }
        co.wait_until(|world| world.resource::<Wave>().0 >= 3).await;
        let finished_on = co.with_world(|world| world.resource::<Time>().frame_count()).await;
        co.queue(move |world| world.resource_mut::<Wave>().0 = finished_on as u32);
    });
}
```

`wait_frames(n)` / `next_frame()` count frames the game runs unpaused (a frame with `Time::paused` set does not
count, ADR-10105), `with_world` returns a value in the same frame, and
`Coroutines::take_result` reads a finished coroutine's output. Scripts start owner-bound coroutines
with `ctx.start_coroutine(..)`. **Coroutines are not saved and do not survive a hot reload**: keep
progress in reflected state and restart the sequence from it after loading. Agents see running
coroutines with `coroutines.list` ([agent page](book/agents/coroutines.md)).

## Settings

`GameSettings` is the persisted, live-applied configuration (graphics preset, display, audio,
input, language, accessibility). Load from `user://settings.ron`; every change is applied and
saved. The agent protocol exposes it as `settings.get` / `settings.set` (see
[the agent guide's framework page](book/agents/framework.md)).

## Save games

Mark entities `Saveable` and register saveable resources; `SavePlugin` serializes the world to a
named slot (atomic write, CRC-32 checked) and restores it with migrations:

```rust
use regia::prelude::*;
use regia_framework::prelude::*;

#[derive(Component, Reflect, Default, Clone)]
#[reflect(Component, Default)]
struct Coin {
    count: u32,
}

fn spawn_coin(mut commands: Commands) {
    commands.spawn((Saveable, Coin { count: 1 }));
}
```

`save.save` / `save.load` / `save.list_slots` drive it from the protocol; see
[the agent guide's gameplay page](book/agents/gameplay.md) and `docs/formats/save-format.md`.

Add `SaveFlowPlugin` to save from ordinary systems: write a `SaveRequest` (`Save`, `Load`, `Delete`,
`QuickSave`, `QuickLoad`) and read the `SaveOutcome` the next frame. Bind the `QuickSave` and `QuickLoad`
actions for quicksave keys. `SaveInfo` (display name, level, play time, save count) and `SaveBlobs` (your
own bytes by key) are saved in every slot. Insert a `SaveStore` to keep saves somewhere other than files,
for example `SaveStore::new(SteamRemoteStorage::new(&steam))` for Steam cloud saves. `MoveTo` walks a
character to a point. The `third_person` and `top_down` templates use the save flow (quicksave keys,
`SaveInfo`, `SaveOutcome`); details on the
[save flow](book/agents/save-flow.md) page.

## Gameplay tags

`regia_framework::tags` gives entities hierarchical tags such as `Combat.Damage.Fire`. Add `TagPlugin`, list the
tags your game uses in a `game.tags.ron` (`TagRegistry::load`), put a `TagContainer` on an entity, and ask it
questions with `has` (a held `Combat.Damage.Fire` satisfies `Combat.Damage`), `has_exact`, or a `TagQuery` such
as `AllOf([Has("Combat.Damage"), NoneOf([Has("Status.Immune")])])`. A `TagsChanged` message fires when a
container changes. The format and the agent methods are on the [gameplay tags](book/agents/gameplay-tags.md) page.

## Abilities, attributes and effects

Health and a `DamageEvent` are enough for a hit that lowers a number. Stacking modifiers, timed
effects, costs, and cooldowns are `regia_framework::abilities` (`AbilityPlugin`). Assets are
`.attrs.ron`, `.effect.ron`, and `.ability.ron`. Cues ask the presentation layer to play a montage
or a sound. They do not change the simulation. The step-by-step is
[Combat and abilities](book/how-to/play/combat-abilities.md). Methods and refusal causes are on
[Abilities (agents)](book/agents/abilities.md).

`regia_ai::abilities` is a separate, smaller slot list for AI cooldowns. It does not share types
with `AbilityPlugin`. Network prediction of the spec 53 book is not in this version. The spec
reserves an intent sequence and does not replicate grants.

<!-- source: book/systems/sim-bridge.md -->
# Networking and the sim bridge

<!-- index: Sim bridge -->
<!-- index: Lockstep -->
<!-- index: Rollback -->

Some games keep their authoritative state outside the engine: a deterministic lockstep or
rollback simulation, a server-authoritative model, a simulation written as a separate library and
shared with a dedicated server. Regia Engine supports this pattern, the **sim bridge**
(`regia_framework::sim_bridge`, `docs/specs/25-sim-bridge-and-do27.md` § 3): the simulation owns
the truth and its own clock; Regia Engine is the presentation layer that sends it input and draws
what it reports. Choosing lockstep, rollback, or a replicated server is
[Lockstep and rollback](book/how-to/online/lockstep-and-rollback.md).

> **Networking status.** Regia Engine ships its own client-server networking crate, `regia_net`
> (since v0.2.5; replication, prediction, interpolation, lag compensation, lobbies and a
> dedicated-server host followed through v0.2.10). Start at [Networking](book/user-guide/networking.md)
> and [Build a networked game](book/tutorials/networked-game.md).
> The sim bridge is the other path: a game that keeps its own netcode inside an external
> simulation connects that simulation to the engine through the bridge; this is how
> *Direct Order 27* works. The two do not exclude each other.
> Steam sockets and Steam lobbies are mock-tested (ADR-2828, 2026-11-05). QUIC is partial and is
> not a session transport for a shipped game. See [Host a game](book/how-to/online/host-a-game.md).

## How it fits

Every frame, `SimBridgePlugin`:

1. reads the `BridgeInput` resource (movement axes and action edges your input systems wrote)
   and calls `ExternalSim::submit_input`;
2. calls `ExternalSim::read_snapshot` and **reconciles** entities: a new sim id spawns an entity
   (with `SimId`, `SimKind`, `Team` and whatever its kind registers), a known id gets its
   `Transform` and `SimExtras` rewritten, a vanished id is despawned;
3. calls `ExternalSim::drain_events` and sends each event as a `SimEvent<E>` message, and routes
   it through the data-driven `EventRouter`.

Nothing downstream of the bridge ever writes simulation state: authority stays with the sim. The
bridge copies the snapshot pose into `Transform`. `to_regia_pose` returns its inputs unchanged,
is not called by reconcile, and is not a hook. A sim converts inside `read_snapshot`.

## Implementing a sim

```rust
use std::time::Duration;

use regia::prelude::*;
use regia_core::math::{Quat, Vec3};
use regia_framework::sim_bridge::{
    BridgeInput, EventRouter, ExternalSim, KindRegistry, SimBridgePlugin, SimEntityView, SimEvent,
    SimSnapshot, SnapshotTick,
};

/// One drone in the snapshot.
struct Drone {
    id: u64,
    position: Vec3,
}

/// What the sim reports each frame.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct DroneSnapshot {
    drones: Vec<Drone>,
}

impl SimSnapshot for DroneSnapshot {
    fn for_each_entity(&self, mut f: impl FnMut(SimEntityView<'_>)) {
        for drone in &self.drones {
            f(SimEntityView {
                id: drone.id,
                kind: "drone",
                team: 0,
                translation: drone.position,
                rotation: Quat::IDENTITY,
            });
        }
    }
}

/// A toy authoritative sim: drones drift in the direction the player pushes. The bridge keeps
/// it as a resource.
#[derive(Resource)]
pub struct DroneSim {
    tick: u64,
    push: Vec3,
    positions: Vec<Vec3>,
    events: Vec<String>,
}

impl ExternalSim for DroneSim {
    type Snapshot = DroneSnapshot;
    type Event = String;

    fn submit_input(&mut self, input: &BridgeInput) {
        self.push = Vec3::new(input.move_axes.x, 0.0, -input.move_axes.y);
    }

    fn read_snapshot(&mut self, _frame_time: Duration, out: &mut DroneSnapshot) -> SnapshotTick {
        self.tick += 1;
        for p in &mut self.positions {
            *p += self.push * 0.05;
        }
        if self.tick == 1 {
            self.events.push("sim_started".into());
        }
        out.drones = self
            .positions
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(i, p)| Drone { id: i as u64 + 1, position: *p })
            .collect();
        SnapshotTick(self.tick)
    }

    fn drain_events(&mut self, out: &mut Vec<String>) {
        out.append(&mut self.events);
    }

    fn event_kind(event: &String) -> String {
        event.clone()
    }
}

/// Reacts to sim events in game code.
fn on_sim_event(mut events: MessageReader<SimEvent<String>>) {
    for event in events.read() {
        info!("sim event: {}", event.0);
    }
}

pub struct Game;

impl Plugin for Game {
    fn build(&self, app: &mut App) {
        let sim = DroneSim {
            tick: 0,
            push: Vec3::ZERO,
            positions: vec![Vec3::ZERO, Vec3::new(2.0, 0.0, 0.0)],
            events: Vec::new(),
        };
        let kinds = KindRegistry::from_ron(r#"(kinds: { "drone": (presentation_scripts: []) })"#)
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let router = EventRouter::from_ron(r#"(routes: { "sim_started": [Toast(text: "Sim online")] })"#)
            .unwrap_or_default();
        app.add_plugins(regia_scene::ScenePlugin)
            .add_plugins(SimBridgePlugin::new(sim).kinds(kinds).events(router))
            .add_systems(Update, on_sim_event);
    }
}
```

Your input systems write `BridgeInput` (`move_axes` and the names of action `edges` pressed this
frame) from the action layer ([Input](book/user-guide/input.md)); the bridge hands it to the sim.
In a real game the sim runs on its own thread (or is a client of a server) and `read_snapshot`
copies out the latest state, interpolating to the frame time if it wants to.

## Kinds and presentation scripts

`config/kinds.ron` (a `KindRegistry`) says what each kind of sim entity looks like:

```ron
(kinds: {
    "warhull": (prefab: Some("prefabs/units/warhull.prefab.ron"),
                presentation_scripts: ["my_game::scripts::HullPresenter"]),
})
```

Presentation scripts are ordinary [scripts](book/user-guide/gameplay.md) attached on spawn. They read
`SimExtras`, the extra `(name, value)` pairs the snapshot reported for that entity
(`SimSnapshot::extras_for`: damage, lean, turret yaw, a team color), and drive meshes,
animation and effects. The bridge records the `prefab` path; instantiating that prefab on spawn,
and `death_prefab` on vanish, is **planned** (`docs/specs/25` § 3). Today a game attaches meshes
to new `SimKind` entities itself (as `samples/sim_bridge` does).

## Routing events

`config/events.ron` (an `EventRouter`) maps an event kind to reactions without code:

```ron
(routes: {
    "explosion": [CameraShake(amplitude: 0.3, frequency_hz: 18.0, duration_secs: 0.6, falloff: 2.0),
                  Toast(text: "Hull breach")],
    "artillery": [SoundCue(cue: "boom_far", max_distance: Some(800.0))],
    "footstep":  [SoundCue(cue: "step")],
})
```

The bridge applies every reaction. `CameraShake` (needs `CameraPlugin`) shakes the camera and
`Toast` raises a `ToastRaised` message the runtime UI shows. On a client build `Vfx` spawns the
named effect from the `VfxScene` library, `Decal` places the named `DecalLibrary` prefab
(`scorch`, `rut`, a loaded `.decal.ron`) facing up into the `DecalPool`, `SoundCue` plays the
named audio cue (spatially at the event's place when it has one, flat when it has none) and
`Announcer` plays a line from the named announcer bank (rotation, pre-emption
and ducking as in [audio](book/user-guide/audio.md)). `Vfx` and `Decal` need to know where the event happened:
implement `ExternalSim::event_place` to return `EventPlace::At(position)` or
`EventPlace::Entity(sim_id)` (the entity's current position). An event without a place skips its
placed reactions.

A placed `SoundCue` plays through the engine's default emitter, which carries **50 m**: past that the
play is refused (counted as `sounds_refused`, no voice starts). Give a far-carrying event its own
range with `max_distance` (meters), as `artillery` does above; leave it out and the 50 m default
applies. A value that is not finite and positive falls back to the default. An unplaced cue plays
flat and ignores the field.

Variations (effect seed, decal spin, cue pick) come from a seed derived from the
snapshot tick, the event's index and its kind, so a replay plays the same ones. Unknown names,
unplaced events and missing subsystems are counted in `RoutedReactionStats` (the agent's
`sim.counters` `reactions`), never fatal. A server build (no `client` feature) counts them as
`no_subsystem`. For anything else, read `SimEvent<E>` in a system.

## Frame-rate independence

A simulation must advance on its own clock, never on the presentation frame rate. `SimCounters`
records snapshot ticks, input calls and drained events; the agent methods `sim.counters` and
`sim.check_framerate_independence` run the game at two frame rates and compare the sim-side
