# Tunnels Stage B: the switch note for DO27

This page is for Direct Order 27 (DO27), the game that matches Regia Engine's tunnel query bit for bit today. It
says what changes when DO27 moves from **Stage A** (the compat path, `regia_world_geom::compat`, DO27's own T3
arithmetic copied unchanged) to **Stage B** (the native world-geometry query and mesh layers behind the `stage_b`
feature), what DO27 re-cooks, which pins it re-records, and what holds if a bar is still missed. The general
adoption rules are in [Adopting engine features](book/user-guide/adopting-features.md); the field-by-field host changes are in the
[DO27 host checklist](book/user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md).

Written on the v0.7 line (lane v07-tunnels-repin-switch-note, ADR-10082) after the four W-11 speed lanes, the W-29
acceptance suite, Stage B correctness (ADR-8898) and the cooked-format step (ADR-8816) merged.

## The statement (ADR-8538)

W-29's native acceptance suite reruns W-05's Stage A proofs against the native query on cooked fixtures, plus the
bars that decide DO27's Stage B bump (spec 121 § 13.2, § 13.3, § 14 rule 3). DO27 can run that one suite to decide
the bump. The tunnel fight, which needs DO27's whole simulation, is rebuilt as a Regia two-peer drive
(`two_peer_tunnel_drive_checksums_equal_x86_aarch64`); DO27 keeps its own pin and re-records it in the bump.

**DO27's Stage B switch is one sim-version bump, outside an alpha week** (spec 121 § 14 rule 3; owner,
2026-11-16). DO27 replaces `ir_content::surface::column` and `TunnelsState::{support, place_floor, confine,
underground}` with thin calls on `WorldGeom::{floors_at, support, place_floor, push_disc, covered_at}`. The waist
rule, the hover rules and the on-foot grid stay DO27's. It adds `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` and `MATH_BITS_VERSION` to its
handshake beside `content_hash`, folds `GeomState::state_hash` into its checksum (one more little-endian `u64` term of
its FNV-1a-64 fold), and re-records in the same bump: the tunnel-fight pin
(`switchbacks_tunnel_fight_lockstep_checksum_is_pinned`), the predicted-hull drive
(`a_net_client_predicting_its_hull_through_the_tunnels_never_shows_a_vertical_jump`),
`determinism_fuzz_short_fixtures_agree_every_tick`, the 3600-tick replay hash and the lockstep checkpoints. Old
replays play on old builds.

**When.** The bump is v0.7.x work, not part of the v0.7.0 tag (owner, 2026-11-19): v0.7.0's bar is "ready for DO27
to switch". DO27 is paused until the tag; its own pin runs and the sim-version bump follow on v0.7.x with a 48 h fix
turnaround from Regia.

## What stays the same

- **Stage A does not move.** `stage_a_bits` (with and without `stage_b`) is green on this line with the same table;
  `compat` never reads `cfg(feature = "stage_b")` and `det-scan` refuses one there. Until DO27 makes the bump it keeps
  matching Stage A bit for bit, with no checksum change.
- **`QUERY_BITS_VERSION` is 8** on this line. None of the W-11 speed work moved a query answer (each lane pins its
  fast path equal to the per-call form). `MATH_BITS_VERSION` is 1: the `atan2` canonicalization (plan section B)
  already moved it — DO27 sends 1 today and re-records the pins that call `math::atan2` once; if it moves again
  before DO27's bump, DO27 sends the new value. It does not change the tunnel query, which reads no trigonometry.

## What DO27 re-cooks

| Data | Why | How |
|---|---|---|
| Every `<map>.meshlayers` (cooked, `terrain-mesh-layers-cooked`) | Version 2 (ADR-8816): fixed-width ground counts behind a hashed head; `content_hash` is now the BLAKE3 of that head, so **every cooked map's `content_hash` changed** even where the cooked value did not | `regia upgrade-project --write` migrates a v1 file to the same value with its v2 hash (`cooked::migrate_file`); a fresh `regia cook` writes v2. Anything DO27 stored with a hash (handshake fixtures, a saved `GeomState`) needs the new one |
| Maps with a filled skylight mouth (Switchbacks `west`, `mid_east`) | ADR-8898: the cook cuts every filled mouth from the layout as meshed, so the whole skylight climb K8 opens is cut from the ground. The cooked value moves (`lattice_cook_hashes_are_pinned` re-pinned) | Run `regia cook` after `regia upgrade-project --write`. ADR-10346 invalidates a migrated package's input hash and revisions the cook key, so ordinary cooking rebuilds the cuts, including in already-upgraded legacy caches. The migrator preserves geometry; the source cook applies the new cuts. No `--clean` is required |
| Nav cells (`nav-cell`) | Version 3 (ADR-8899, lane w11-fmt-nav-cell-v3): conservative rasterization. A v1 or v2 cell still loads, with a warning that names the re-cook | Re-cook. **Not on this line yet**: the lane reported PARTIAL and lands through the format batch 2 integration |
| The terrain index section | Terrain index v3 (unequal spacing and masked rasters, plan section F) | **Not built on this line**: scheduled for format batch 2 (freeze Sat 11-28). Until it lands, DO27's current terrain index stays valid |

## The bars, measured per device

The bars are spec 121 § 11 (absorb plan § 4.7). Each W-11 lane measured its own calls on its own branch; the combined
line is measured below where a device was reachable. "Build host" is an idle core of the build host (the build server; the
the test machine was used where no idle the build server core existed, which is not a clean bar measurement).

Combined line = this page's line (all four W-11 lanes merged), measured 2026-11-20 with release benches built on
the build server: the Deck on core 3 (`taskset -c 3`, idle), the test machine on its least busy core pair (a shared host
at load 17-20). Lane = the W-11 lane's own branch, before the merge (ADR-8815 to ADR-8818). Raw output:
`docs/evidence/v07-tunnels-repin-switch-note/` and each lane's `docs/evidence/w11-*` folder.

| Bar (spec 121 § 11) | Steam Deck | Android test device (Pixel 9 Pro) | Build host |
|---|---|---|---|
| 500 mixed queries ≤ 0.5 ms Deck, ≤ 0.8 ms Android, ≤ 0.25 ms build host (p50; 0 allocations) | **0.269-0.271 ms, met** (combined, 3 runs; 1.64 ms before W-11) | **met by each lane alone**: 0.239 ms (lane 001, one run), 0.717 ms (lane 003); combined line not measured (the device was off adb) | combined on the test machine: **0.110 ms** (2 runs; 0.183 ms in a run with a busy sibling thread), under 0.25 ms but on a shared host. Idle the build server core: 0.363-0.398 ms with lane 001 alone (missed); the combined line is not measured there (the build server at load 420) |
| The same tick after one 6 m crater (no bar) | 0.289-0.294 ms (5.90 ms before W-11) | 0.270 ms (lane 001) | the test machine 0.118 ms |
| The same tick after 30 craters (no bar) | 0.315-0.318 ms (6.54 ms before lane 004) | 0.99-1.02 ms (lane 004, before lane 001's descent merged) | the test machine 0.131 ms |
| Index build ≤ 50 ms (load of the cooked Switchbacks) | **28.6 ms, met** (combined; strict load 19.5-19.7 ms; 79 ms before W-11) | **49.3-49.6 ms, met** by under 1 ms (lane 002; p99 50.8-52.2 ms) | the test machine 14.1-16.3 ms (combined) |
| D1 crater, 6 m radius ≤ 0.2 ms | **0.086-0.092 ms, met** (combined; 3 m radius 0.023-0.028 ms) | **0.060-0.065 ms, met** (lane 004) | the test machine 0.045-0.067 ms (combined) |
| D4 column (`support`) ≤ 150 ns and ≤ 0.25 of compat | **missed**: 500-1430 ns, ratio 1.07-2.04 (combined) | **missed**: 325-814 ns, ratio 1.13-2.22 (lane 003) | **missed**: the test machine 370-1012 ns, ratio 1.28-2.46 (lane 003, loaded) |
| Sim geometry RAM ≤ 35 MB | 34,368,306 B on Switchbacks (combined; counter, every host) | same | same |

D4 is at parity with the compat kernel, not at a quarter of it: `support` is 1.5-3.1 times faster than before W-11
and bit-identical. Inside the mixed tick it costs about 0.49 µs a call on the Deck, and the tick meets its bar with it.

## If a bar is missed: the fallback

The plan's fallback (plan-v07-to-v10 § 5) holds: if the W-11 bars are still over 1.5x at the 11-30 checkpoint,
**v0.7 ships Stage A as the default** and Stage B behind its feature with the measured numbers as a known issue. DO27
then switches on Stage A with no checksum change, and Stage B with its one sim-version bump moves to v0.8. A bar is
re-set only by a written owner ruling with the measured number; this page never re-sets one.

**Waiting for an owner ruling (recorded here, not re-set):**

- **D4, the column bar** (150 ns, 0.25 of compat; ADR-8817). Measured above on every device; the lane recommends
  option C, accept the measured numbers for v0.7. Until the ruling, D4 is a missed bar.
- **The build-host bar** (0.25 ms on an idle the build server core). The combined line reads 0.110 ms on the test machine, a shared
  host; the idle-the build server number is owed (the build server had no idle core during this lane).
- **The Pixel's combined numbers** are owed: each lane met its bar alone; the merged line was not run on the device.
- **D6, crater radius or diameter**: both readings meet 0.2 ms on every device measured, so the ruling no longer
  decides pass or fail.
- `native_resident_geometry_fits_the_sim_budget` is red on this line: the 35 MB bar is met (34,368,306 B), but the
  cook's estimate leaves out the run-time query tables and reads 1.35 % low against the test's 1 % rule (ADR-10082 lists
  the options). It is a consistency check of the cook's figure, not a memory bar.

D4 is the one bar over the 11-30 checkpoint's 1.5x trigger (500 ns and up against 150 ns on the Deck). Every other
bar measured on this line is met, including the mixed tick that `support` sits inside. So the D4 ruling decides
whether the fallback applies: if the owner accepts the measured numbers (option C), no measured bar triggers it.

## Running the checks

```text
cargo test -p regia_world_geom --features stage_b,fixtures --test native_acceptance --test host_step_echo -- --nocapture
cargo test -p regia_world_geom --test stage_a_bits                      # Stage A bits without Stage B
cargo test -p regia_world_geom --features stage_b --test stage_a_bits   # ... and with it: the same table
cargo test -p regia_world_geom --features stage_b,stats,fixtures --test lattice_ground --test native_table
cargo bench -p regia_world_geom --features stage_b --bench mixed_calls   # the mixed tick, the crater, the index build
```

The two-peer golden's aarch64 leg is the `native_acceptance` run on an aarch64 host (the Mac, or the test binary on
the Android device with `REGIA_DET_GOLDEN_DIR` pointing at a copy of `crates/regia_world_geom/goldens`); a passing
run with `REGIA_BLESS=1` records that target's line. `cargo xtask det-golden` covers `regia_detsim`'s goldens, not
this one.

The acceptance bars and what each test proves are in [Terrain mesh layers](book/agents/terrain-mesh-layers.md),
"Acceptance".

# DO27 switch package for v0.7

This page is for Direct Order 27 (DO27), the game that is moving its engine-general code onto Regia Engine. It is
the v0.7 switch package: what DO27 switches to, what changes in the tunnel query, what DO27 re-cooks for format
batch 2, and what Regia promises after the tag. It links the pages that hold the detail and does not restate them:

- [Adopting engine features](book/user-guide/adopting-features.md): how to adopt a row (turn it on beside the host's code, run the
  check, delete the host's code in the change that makes the engine feature the default).
- [DO27 host checklist](book/user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md): field-by-field host changes.
- [DO27 interface contracts](book/user-guide/do27-interface-contract.md): the data DO27 and the engine exchange.
- [Tunnels Stage B: the switch note for DO27](book/user-guide/tunnels-stage-b-switch.md): the tunnel query's switch.

**The bar for v0.7 is "ready for DO27 to switch", not "DO27 has switched"** (owner, 2026-11-19). DO27 is paused until
the v0.7 tag. Its own pin runs and its sim-version bump are v0.7.x work (section (d)).

Every Regia name on this page was checked against the code on the v0.7 integration line (integ-v07c, 71773be0c) on
2026-11-20, name by name. DO27's side is described from the absorb plan and the lane reports only.

## (a) What DO27 switches to

How to read the tables. One row per DO27 component in the absorb plan's switch table (absorb plan § 6), plus the
absorb-gaps rows (ids in brackets) the plan briefed later. "Regia API" names the crate path and main types; "Format"
is the name in `docs/formats/format-hashes.ron` (or "none": the system reads no file of its own); "Parity test" is a
test that proves the behavior DO27 relies on (the plan's acceptance test where it exists on the line); "State" is
**ready** (built and merged on this line), **ready, checks owed** (merged; a platform leg or a gate check is still
owed, named), **partial** (what is missing) or **not on this line** (the lane that owns it). Adopt a row with the
steps in [Adopting engine features](book/user-guide/adopting-features.md#how-to-adopt-a-row).

## (b) The tunnel query: Stage B

[Tunnels Stage B: the switch note for DO27](book/user-guide/tunnels-stage-b-switch.md) is the switch note. It says what changes when
DO27 moves from Stage A (`regia_world_geom::compat`, DO27's own arithmetic, no checksum change) to Stage B (the native
query behind the `stage_b` feature): the calls DO27 replaces, the two version numbers its handshake adds
(`QUERY_BITS_VERSION`, `MATH_BITS_VERSION`), the state hash it folds into its checksum, the pins it re-records in the
same bump, the bars measured per device, and the fallback if a bar is still missed at the 11-30 checkpoint (v0.7 ships
Stage A as the default). This page does not copy it.

On this line `QUERY_BITS_VERSION` is 8 and `MATH_BITS_VERSION` is 1. If either moves before DO27's bump, DO27 sends the
new value.

## (c) Format batch 2: what DO27 re-cooks

Format batch 2 is the one set of format steps in v0.7 (owner-approved 2026-11-19, freeze Sat 11-28). The upgrade
guide for the whole batch is `docs/guide/upgrade-v07.md`, written by the freeze lane (v07-fmt-batch2-freeze) when it
runs the single `check-formats --update`; it covers every project. The table below is DO27's part of it: the formats
DO27's content uses whose version moved since v0.6.0, and what DO27 runs for each. Versions are the ones in
`docs/formats/format-hashes.ron` on this line; each row links the lane's release notes.

| Format | v0.6.0 → v0.7 | What moved | What DO27 runs | Release notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nav-cell` | 2 → 3 | `NAV_CELL_FORMAT_VERSION`: conservative rasterization (a cell takes every triangle that overlaps it). Same bytes, new height meaning; navmeshes change at triangle edges and thin geometry now blocks or carries agents | **Re-cook** the streamed levels' navigation (`regia cook`). A v1 or v2 cell still loads with a warning that names the re-cook; a build older than v0.7 refuses a v3 cell (`nav_cell_version`). No `regia upgrade-project` row: the cell is cooked output | nav cell v3 (`docs/releases/v0.1.28-w11-fmt-nav-cell-v3.md`) |
| `terrain-mesh-layers-cooked` | 1 → 2 | The tunnel index section of every `<map>.meshlayers`: fixed-width ground counts behind a hashed head, so **every cooked map's `content_hash` changes** even where the cooked value does not | `regia upgrade-project --write` brings a v1 file to v2 with the same geometry, then `regia cook` rebuilds it from source. ADR-10346 invalidates the migrated cache identity and revisions the cook key, so filled skylight mouths receive the current cuts even if their chunk LOD files survive or the package was already upgraded. See the [switch note](book/user-guide/tunnels-stage-b-switch.md#what-do27-re-cooks). Anything DO27 stored with a hash takes the new one | index build (`docs/releases/v0.1.28-w11-index-build.md`) |
| `terrain-index` | 2 → 3 | `TERRAIN_INDEX_FORMAT_VERSION`: the cooked terrain index (`terrain/index`) can hold a Z sample spacing unequal to X and cooked masks | `regia upgrade-project --write` rewrites each v1 or v2 index as v3 (`terrain_index_migration_sources`); a full `regia cook` writes v3 too. A v2 index still loads | terrain index v3 (`docs/releases/v0.1.28-v07-fmt-terrain-index-v3.md`) |
| `scene` | 13 → 14 | TerrainMap spacing: `SCENE_FORMAT_VERSION` 14 adds `LevelTerrain::sample_layout` (`TerrainSampleLayout`: `VertexCentered`, the default, or `CellCentered`) | `regia upgrade-project --write` (a v13 level's terrain block gains `sample_layout: VertexCentered`; nothing moves). **Re-cook** only a level switched to `CellCentered`: its `<map>.meshlayers`, scatter, navigation and GI heightfield move by up to half a cell. A host that builds `LevelTerrain` or `LevelGround` literals adds the field | TerrainMap spacing (`docs/releases/v0.1.28-v07-fmt-terrainmap-spacing.md`) |
| `gpu-mesh` | 2 → 3 | `GPU_MESH_VERSION`: GPU-ready layout for skinned and morphing meshes in desktop paks | **Re-cook** desktop paks (`regia cook --ship`). Older paks load unchanged; a v0.6 runtime refuses a v3 entry, so ship the runtime and the paks together. `GpuMeshView` gains `extras` | GPU mesh v3 (`docs/releases/v0.1.28-v07-fmt-gpu-mesh-v3.md`) |
| `decal` | 2 → 3 | `DECAL_FORMAT_VERSION`: decal prefabs (`.decal.ron`) gain `surface` (the footstep surface name, `DecalPrefab`) | `regia upgrade-project --write` rewrites v1 and v2 prefabs (version number only, with backups). **No re-cook**: `.decal.ron` is read as source. A host that spawns decals through `DecalPool::spawn_with` calls `set_footstep_surface` to keep footsteps | decal v3 (`docs/releases/v0.1.28-v07-fmt-decal-v3.md`) |

Run `regia upgrade-project` without `--write` first: it lists every file it would change. Then run it with `--write`,
then `regia cook` (and `regia cook --ship` for the paks). The revision-aware input key forces the first
mesh-layer source cook to rebuild legacy skylight cuts (ADR-10346); `--clean` is no longer required.
A second unchanged cook writes nothing, and a second `--write` changes nothing.

Two more batch 2 steps touch DO27 without a re-cook. The net wire is version 6 (`REGIA_NET_WIRE_VERSION`): every
peer of a session runs the same Regia build. The rules formats (`rules-ron`, `playlist-ron`, `match-result`) are
new in v0.7, so DO27 has no old files to migrate; the gait and other v0.7 rows are listed in the upgrade guide.

## (d) After the tag: the v0.7.x promise

DO27 is paused until the v0.7 tag, so two pieces of the switch are DO27's own work on v0.7.x, not part of the tag:

- **DO27's own pin runs.** DO27 re-records its own pins on its own content (the tunnel-fight lockstep checksum, the
  predicted-hull drive, the determinism fuzz fixtures, the replay hash, the lockstep checkpoints; the list is in the
  [switch note](book/user-guide/tunnels-stage-b-switch.md#the-statement-adr-8538)) and runs its play gate on the v0.7 tag.
- **The sim-version bump.** The Stage B switch is one sim-version bump, outside an alpha week (spec 121 § 14 rule 3).
  DO27 picks the week.

**Regia's side: a 48 h fix turnaround** (owner, 2026-11-19). An engine bug that blocks DO27's pin runs or its
sim-version bump on v0.7.x gets a fix on the v0.7.x line within 48 h of the report. A report names the Regia tag, the
failing check (a test name, an agent method and its answer, or a `regia` command and its output) and, for a pin, the
expected and measured values. A fix that would move a frozen format or a Regia pin says so in its release notes and
waits for DO27's go before it merges. A missed bar is not a bug: it goes to the owner for a ruling with the measured
number (the [switch note](book/user-guide/tunnels-stage-b-switch.md#if-a-bar-is-missed-the-fallback) lists the open ones).

# Performance & benches

## Picking the GPU

Every headless or offscreen device goes through `RenderDevice::headless`. That covers tests,
`render_lab`, `lookdev` (`look_r2`, `do27_chase`), `vfx_lab`, `terrain_lab`, and the terrain's
block-compression device. On a machine with several cards, set **one** of these variables to choose the card for
all of them:

| variable | selects |
|---|---|
| `REGIA_GPU_UUID=GPU-748396be…` | an NVIDIA GPU by UUID or unique prefix (case-insensitive, optional `GPU-`). Linux resolves it from `/proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/*/information` when that procfs tree exists; if `/proc/driver/nvidia` is absent, Linux uses the same bounded `nvidia-smi` query as other platforms |
| `REGIA_GPU_PCI=0000:41:00.0` | the adapter on that PCI bus (Vulkan or `nvidia-smi` spelling) |
| `REGIA_GPU_INDEX=2` | the n-th adapter in Vulkan order |
| `REGIA_GPU_NAME=7900` | the first adapter whose name contains the text (case-insensitive) |

Precedence is **PCI, then UUID, then index, then name** (ADR-7958). The device logs the adapter it chose, with its backend and
driver, at `info`. If a value matches nothing (an index out of range, an unknown name or UUID), the device logs a
`warn` that lists the adapters and falls back to the usual high-performance pick.
`RenderDevice::adapter_selection()` reports what happened. With `REGIA_GPU_STRICT=1` an unmatched
request is an error (`RenderError::GpuSelection`) instead of a fallback. Use it on shared machines, where the
default pick may be someone else's card. The Vulkan loader's own filter
(`VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_SELECT`, e.g. `'*lvp*'` for lavapipe) applies first.

On Linux, UUID lookup reads the `GPU UUID`, `Bus Location` and `Device Minor` fields in
NVIDIA's procfs information files when `/proc/driver/nvidia` exists. It does not run `nvidia-smi`
on that path. An exact full UUID still selects its card when another card's file is malformed,
unreadable, or the uninitialized placeholder `GPU-????…` (persistence mode off, or the card has
not been opened). A shorter prefix fails if any card cannot be read, and the error names that
card. Set `REGIA_GPU_PCI` to pin directly in that case. When `/proc/driver/nvidia` does not exist
(WSL2, some containers), Linux uses the same three-second `nvidia-smi` query as other platforms.
An unknown UUID or an ambiguous prefix is still a selection error (or the usual warning and
fallback without strict mode).

If both PCI and UUID are set, PCI wins. Linux cross-checks only that card's information file:
a UUID that does not match the file logs a warning, but the explicit PCI value still wins **even
under `REGIA_GPU_STRICT=1`**. An unreadable or unresolved cross-check does not invalidate the PCI
pin, and it does not open any other card's file. No platform launches a UUID subprocess for a
PCI-pinned request. The pre-rename spellings of these variables follow the same rules (the
`REGIA_*` value takes precedence).

On other platforms, a UUID-only request runs `nvidia-smi` with a three-second deadline. Timeout,
unsuccessful exit, or invalid output is a selection error. On timeout the child is sent a kill
request; the caller does not wait indefinitely for cleanup. This bounds UUID lookup, not Vulkan
initialization or arbitrary driver calls. See [GPU selection for agents](book/agents/gpu-selection.md).

List the adapters a variable can select, with their PCI buses and drivers:

```
cargo run --release -p lookdev --bin do27_chase -- --list-gpus
```

`regia_render::list_adapters()` returns the same list.

## The DO27 frame bench

`do27_chase` (in `samples/lookdev`) replays DO27's chase on DO27's own content through the full runtime frame
(`REGIA_DO27_CONTENT=<content dir>`). Two frames are kept in flight. It prints wall, CPU and per-pass GPU p50/p99,
the terrain's own share of the prepass and forward pass, and per-cascade shadow timing.

- `--plates` measures the six UE plate cameras instead of the chase.
- `--tier mid` turns on the opt-in `TerrainBudget`.
- `--sync --idle-ms N` lets the GPU idle between frames. An idle GPU clocks down, and every pass then reads about 2× longer.

Measure with the GPU busy. Results are in `docs/evidence/perf/`.

## The unit-budget bench

`crates/regia_render/tests/unit_budget.rs` measures DO27's frozen per-class triangle table on the GPU it runs on,
without DO27 content. Hulls are procedural (closed, displaced ellipsoid pieces with an exact triangle count). They
are written as a glTF and cooked by the real importer with `generate_lods`, so every LOD chain comes from the
engine's meshopt simplifier. Frames take the runtime path: ECS entities with `MeshRenderer` and `MeshLodChain`,
`extract_frame`, `select_mesh_lods`, `extract_glass`, then `render_extracted_into` with Desktop High.

```text
cargo test -p regia_render --test unit_budget --release -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1
```

For each class (skimmer, battle, walker, structure exterior, walk-in interior, seated cockpit), resolution (720p,
1080p, 1440p) and hull count (1, 5, 10, 20, 40), it prints:

- GPU ms per frame (median and p90 of the timestamp nodes) and the top nodes;
- the geometry passes (shadows, prepass, cull, forward) and the glass section;
- visible triangles and the body LOD histogram;
- mesh draws (`DrawStats`), VRAM (allocator report: total and meshes), and CPU ms.

The cases cover (a) every hull at LOD0, (b) the engine's selection on a by-distance layout, and the same places
with DO27's intended mix pinned (2 at LOD0, a fifth at LOD1, the rest LOD2/LOD3), (c) the walker as rigid through
the visibility buffer and as skinned through the forward path, (d) glass in its `BLEND` material and in the opaque
body material, and (e) the seated cockpit (near plane 0.05 m). A least-squares fit then gives the GPU cost per 100k
visible triangles for each path.

Those layouts pin the mesh LOD tier scales at the values that select as before them (distance 1,
shadow 0.5), so their rows compare with earlier runs. Two layouts at the same places measure the tier
scales (v0.1.20, [Mesh LOD tiers](book/agents/mesh-lod-tiers.md)): `close20` holds the body's colour LOD 0 to
20 m (the distance scale that puts its LOD0→1 colour switch there) with shadows at the table mix (shadow scale
1 / distance scale), and `ultra` runs Desktop Ultra's scales as shipped. Each row also gives the body's shadow
LOD histogram. Before the cases, a table lists every class's body switch distances (colour and shadow,
LOD0→1→2→3) for every preset at every resolution.

Narrow the run with `UNIT_BUDGET_CLASSES`, `UNIT_BUDGET_RES`, `UNIT_BUDGET_N`, `UNIT_BUDGET_LAYOUTS` (`lod0`,
`mix`, `table`, `close20`, `ultra`), `UNIT_BUDGET_WARM`, `UNIT_BUDGET_FRAMES` and `UNIT_BUDGET_TEXTURE`.
`UNIT_BUDGET_OUT` writes the markdown table to a file.
`unit_budget_depth_precision` (also ignored) counts z-fighting between an unlit panel and the wall a fraction of a
millimetre behind it, at 0.5 m to 50 m from a 0.05 m near plane. The fast, non-ignored smoke case renders 5 hulls
of 10k triangles on lavapipe and checks that the frame is not black; a second fast case checks the selection
with the tier scales on the cooked chain (no GPU).

<!-- source: book/user-guide/merge-gate.md -->
# The merge gate and goldens across machines

Every merge to `main` passes one gate: `cargo fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`, every workspace test, rustdoc with
`-D warnings`, the packaging end-to-end test (`package_e2e -- --ignored`), the Khronos glTF samples, and the
`xtask` checks (`check-versions`, `notices --check`, `check-formats`, `book-check`, `check-shaders`,
`check-unwraps`, `check-layers`). `book-check` also runs `agent-coverage` (`cargo xtask agent-coverage`):
every method registered in `regia_agent`'s dispatcher has a schema entry, a bundled `agent.guide` topic
that names it, a `book/COVERAGE.md` row, a mention on that guide page (and of each of its parameters, ADR-5866),
and a test that calls it. A gated `main` commit is tagged `green-YYYYMMDD-HHMM` (and `green`); consumers such
as DO27 pin those tags.

The gate runs on two kinds of host:

- **the workstation** (`gate.sh`): lavapipe on Mesa 26.2 / LLVM 23. The goldens are blessed here. Since 2026-10-14 nothing
  builds on the workstation, so `gate.sh` is not the merge gate any more. It also never ran `check-shaders`,
  `check-unwraps` or the doc tests.
- **The build machines** (`fgate.sh`, one gate at a time under `<scratch>`): 48 cores and shared
  RTX 5090s. It gates a commit, not a working tree. Before anything builds, it refuses the commit when:
  - a merge is in progress;
  - a `.rs`, `.toml`, `.md` or `.wgsl` file has a line that starts with a conflict marker (seven `<` or `>` and a
    space);
  - the commit's manifests do not parse as a git dependency from a throwaway host crate (what DO27 does).

  The commit is then exported with `git archive` and built in its own tree and target dir. Two passes run at the
  same time:
  1. **lavapipe pass**: every check above, goldens compared, and the doc tests. clippy and rustdoc build in their
     own target dirs beside the test build. The test binaries run up to 12 at a time, longest first, each the way
     `cargo test` runs it (package directory as cwd, `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` set), with a 1200 s limit per binary.
     Wall-clock-bound binaries run alone after the pool.
  2. **real-GPU pass** on a 5090: every test binary of the rendering crates that creates a device, with
     `REGIA_SKIP_GOLDENS=1`, 4 at a time, with the per-binary limit of `fgate-remote.sh` (600 s now). It must pass,
     apart from its quarantine list. With `REGIA_PLATE_DIR` set, the pass also records each golden's PSNR, and `cargo xtask plate-floors check
     --vendor nvidia` fails it when a plate is under the NVIDIA floor (ADR-2089).
     A plate under its floor is not yet a card defect: `cargo xtask plate-floors attribute --plates <that run> --reference
     <the same test binaries' plates on lavapipe> --vendor nvidia` says, per plate, whether the golden moved on every
     device (`GOLDEN`) or the card's frame differs from the lavapipe frame (`VENDOR`) (ADR-5798). It fails (exit 1) on
     every other verdict: `SHARED` when the frames agree but the lavapipe run is not under a lavapipe floor of its own,
     `INCONSISTENT` when the scores and frames cannot come from one build (ADR-5897). A `GOLDEN` plate is a failure of
     `plate-floors check --vendor lavapipe` on the lavapipe run, so wiring that excuses one runs that check too.

     With `FGATE_GPU_HOST=the test machine` (ADR-3317; the default is `the build server`) this pass runs on the test machine's RTX 5080
     instead: the rig builds the test binaries itself from the same commit (`git archive`), runs the same binaries with
     the same limits and retries, card pinned by UUID under its lock, and prints the same result lines. The per-binary
     limit and the package list are those of `fgate-remote.sh` (600 s now). Lanes run short card tests on the 5080 with
     `rig-slot.sh --card the test machine CMD...`; while a gate holds the card they wait. Recipe and details:
     `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 21 (`tools/gaterig/`).

  In both passes a binary that fails is run once more alone. If it passes alone, the gate reports
  `FLAKY UNDER LOAD` and does not count the failure; if it fails alone, it fails the gate. A binary over its time
  limit is rerun alone and reported as `HANG`. A signal at process exit after every test passed counts as passed
  and is printed as `EXIT-CRASH`. The exact rules, the solo and quarantine lists, and how a flake is recorded:
  [Flaky tests, retries and nightly jobs](book/user-guide/flaky-tests.md). Nothing else is retried.

## Before you submit: `cargo xtask preflight`

`cargo xtask preflight` runs the gate's cheap checks in the gate's order and stops at the first failure:
- the gate's conflict-marker refusal;
- `fmt --check`;
- a fast pre-check for bare `rust` fences in `book/` that cannot compile;
- clippy and rustdoc;
- the xtask checks in the farm gate's order: `check-versions`, `notices --check`, `check-formats`, `book-check`,
  `check-shaders`, `check-unwraps`, `check-layers`, `check-packaging`, `api-snapshot` (a removed or changed public
  item of a stable crate; `docs/api-snapshots/README.md` says how to update the snapshots, the deprecation window and the `freeze` switch);
- `doc-examples` (the compiled doc examples of the stable crates may not drop; `docs/ci/doc-examples.toml` holds the floors and `docs/04-conventions.md` § 14 the rule);
- the feature matrix (`cargo xtask check-features`, below; `--no-features` skips it);
- a test build (`cargo test --workspace --no-run`; `--no-build` skips it).

The options:
- `--changed` limits the cargo steps to the crates that differ from `main` (a renamed file counts for both crates)
  and the crates that depend on them.
- `--keep-going` (`-k`) runs every step and lists every failure at the end. That is one fix round instead of one per
  failing step.
- Every run ends with a table of step times. `--timings FILE` also writes the times as JSON (`scope`,
  `total_secs`, and per step `name`, `command`, `secs`, `outcome` = `passed` / `failed` / `not_run`).

Preflight prints the build-wrapper command to use on the workstation and never edits a file. It does not run the
tests themselves, the doc tests or the git-dependency parse.

## Optional features: `cargo xtask check-features`

The workspace clippy builds each crate once, with the features the workspace turns on. Code behind a feature no crate
turns on (DLSS, the Steamworks backend, the media codecs, `lua`, `xr`, the `regia` re-exports) and the build a shipped
game compiles (`regia_render` and `regia` with their defaults off) would otherwise never be compiled before a game
does. `cargo xtask check-features` runs `cargo clippy -p <crate> --features <set> -- -D warnings` once per row of the
feature matrix (`xtask/src/feature_matrix.rs`; the table is in `docs/04-conventions.md` § 11), keeps going after a
failure and ends with every failing row, its command and its error lines:

```text
check-features: rows
  render-shipping          ok    41.2s
  steamworks               FAILED 18.9s
  media-av1-nasm           skipped (needs `nasm` on PATH)
  ...
check-features: 1 row(s) FAILED
  steamworks: cargo clippy --locked -p regia_steam --features steamworks --all-targets --message-format short -- -D warnings
      crates/regia_steam/src/backend.rs:88:9: error[E0599]: no method named `...`
```

- `--list` prints each row's command and what it compiles; `--set NAME` runs one row; `--packages a,b` runs the rows
  of those crates (what preflight `--changed` does); `--check` uses `cargo check` (faster, warnings do not fail);
  `-j N` caps rustc jobs per row; `--fail-fast` stops at the first failure.
- A row that needs something the host lacks (`nasm` for the x86 AV1 assembly, Windows for `static-dxc`) is skipped
  and says why; it does not fail.
- Before it compiles anything it checks the table: a `[features]` key of a `crates/*` manifest that no row names
  fails the command (`--coverage-only` runs only this check). Add the row in the same commit as the feature.
- The DLSS rows compile the linked NGX path over a check stub of the binding (`REGIA_DLSS_CHECK_STUB=1`): no NVIDIA
  SDK is needed, nothing is linked, and only `check` and `clippy` work that way.

It compiles; it does not run a feature's tests. CI runs it in the `linux` job after clippy.

Formatting: lanes run `cargo fmt --all` before each commit. `gate.sh` (main checkout) and `fgate.sh` format and commit
`style: cargo fmt` themselves; the farm's lavapipe pass (`fgate-remote.sh`) only checks and fails on a diff, as does
preflight.

## Goldens on another lavapipe build

Goldens are single-reference (ADR-025). SSIM goldens (≥ 0.98) pass on every lavapipe build we have seen.
Pixel-exact goldens (a per-channel bound, e.g. ±2) can flip a handful of edge pixels when the LLVM that compiles
lavapipe's shaders changes. Compare them through `regia_test_utils::golden::check_pixel_golden`:

```rust,ignore
// In a test (regia_test_utils is a dev-dependency):
let reference = PixelTolerance { max_channel_diff: 2, outlier_ppm: 0 };
match check_pixel_golden(&device.adapter.get_info(), "my_shot", &pixels, &golden, w, h, reference) {
    Ok(verdict) => eprintln!("{verdict}"),
    Err(verdict) => panic!("my_shot drifted: {verdict}"),
}
```

`pixel_golden_for` decides the compare from the adapter:

| adapter | compare |
|---|---|
| lavapipe, LLVM 23 (the reference), WARP, any unlisted LLVM | the test's own tolerance, no outliers |
| lavapipe, LLVM listed in `LAVAPIPE_ICD_TOLERANCES` (19: 30 ppm) | same per-channel bound, up to that many ppm of pixels beyond it |
| hardware GPU | SSIM against the lavapipe golden (`ssim_threshold_for`, ADR-025) |

To add a lavapipe build, render the pixel goldens on it, count the pixels beyond each test's bound, and record
the numbers in `docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` § 2 next to the new table entry. Never re-bless a golden on a
non-reference build.

## Variables

| variable | effect |
|---|---|
| `REGIA_SKIP_GOLDENS=1` | `compare_rgba8_to_png` and, on hardware adapters, `check_pixel_golden` skip the lavapipe compare and print a note. Only set by the real-GPU pass. |
| `REGIA_PLATE_DIR=<dir>` | every golden compare records a plate there, also under `REGIA_SKIP_GOLDENS=1`: the frame as a PNG and its PSNR against the golden as a `.plate` line. `cargo xtask plate-floors check` holds them to the per-vendor floors in `docs/ci/plate-floors.toml` (`docs/06-testing-and-ci.md` section 13). |
| `REGIA_SPIRV_VAL_FALLBACK=1` | when `spirv-val` is **not installed**, `check-shaders` and the shader tests run naga validation and the explicit-layout scan alone. Without the variable a missing `spirv-val` is an error. Only a gate host without SPIRV-Tools sets it, and a warning is printed. The scan (`regia_render::spirv_explicit_layout_violations`, ADR-026's rule) runs on every host anyway, because older `spirv-val` releases (the build server's 2025.1) do not check that rule. An explicit layout on Function or Private storage is an error; `ArrayStride` on a Workgroup array is naga 30's known output and is reported as a warning (ADR-135), as is `spirv-val`'s VUID-10684 for it. |
| `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` | followed by the terrain cook test (finds `regia` beside its own executable) and by `regia package` (looks there first for the binary it built). |

<!-- source: book/user-guide/look-ci.md -->
# Look CI: the look check at every green tag

The merge gate proves a tag builds and its goldens hold. Goldens are small lavapipe frames of
small scenes, so a merge can still change how DO27's maps look and pass the gate. Look CI renders
the twelve UE parity plates on DO27's content at every green tag. It compares them with the
previous green tag and flags what changed.

## What one run does

For a tag `T` and the previous green tag `P`:

1. Renders the twelve parity plates (`look_r2 --set parity` framing, 960×540, converged) at
   Desktop High and at the Deck tier on a shared RTX 5090 (`LOOK_R2_TIER=desktop-high|deck`).
   The plates are `bore_twelve_{wide,mid,close}`, `switchbacks_{wide,mid,close}`,
   `tunnel_interior`, `cockpit`, `dusk_vista`, `set_piece_borehole`, `fireball_20m` and `smoke_80m`.
2. Runs `do27_chase --plates` (the six landscape plate cameras, 2560×1440, 180 frames) on the
   exclusive bench 5090 and keeps the per-frame CSV.
3. Compares `T` with `P` and with the UE plates. It writes sheets, heat maps, `compare.json` and a
   markdown summary.

`P` is rendered too if it has no render set yet. A finished render set is not rendered again,
so a second run only redoes the comparison (seconds).

## Pinned content

DO27's content changes between tags as well as the engine. If `T` and `P` were rendered on
different content, the content changes would be flagged as engine changes. This happened once:
one commit rendered at two times gave FLIP 0.64 on `tunnel_interior`, because DO27 had re-exported
the switchbacks map in between. So every run pins the content:

1. The script hashes the content drop: sha256 of every file, then one hash over the sorted list
   of paths and hashes. The first 12 hex digits are the snapshot's *fingerprint*.
2. It copies the drop once to `lookci/content/<fingerprint>/` on the farm. Unchanged files are
   hard links to the previous snapshot. If the drop changes during the copy, the script retries.
3. Both tags render from that snapshot. Each render set records its fingerprint in `content`.
4. If `P`'s set was rendered on another snapshot, the script renders `P` again on this one into
   `lookci/<P>/c-<fingerprint>/`. The binaries of every rendered commit are cached in
   `lookci/bin/<sha>/`, so this does not rebuild `P`.

The summary names the snapshot. Content changes themselves are not flagged; a re-export shows up
as a re-rendered `P`.

## Flags

| flag | rule |
|---|---|
| frame changed | FLIP mean (or p95) of a plate against `P` > 3 × the noise floor between two renders of one tree. Floors: mean 0.004, p95 0.02 |
| UE drift | the plate's gap to the UE plate grows by > 10 percentage points of the UE value (mean luma, contrast, saturation), or by > 6° (hue) |
| GPU cost | a plate's GPU frame p50 rises by > 10 % |

A *frame changed* flag means "look at this plate", not "this is a regression". Intended look work
raises it too. The sheet shows whether the change is good. The UE-drift flags are the ones that
mean "further from UE than before".

Plate statistics are the look-r2 measures, computed on the displayed 8-bit frame:

- **luma:** BT.709 mean and median
- **contrast:** standard deviation of the luma
- **saturation:** mean HSV saturation
- **hue:** circular mean hue of the saturated pixels (S ≥ 0.35, V ≥ 0.12), undefined below 1 % of
  the frame
- **clipping:** per cent of pixels with any channel ≥ 250

UE plates are box-filtered to the render size. Every tag is measured by one build of `look_ci`.
A tag rendered by an older harness is therefore scored on the same definitions as a new one.

## The `look_ci` binary

```text
look_ci render  --out <dir> [--ue <ue plates dir>] [--width W] [--height H] [--frames N]
                                                        # 12 plates at LOOK_R2_TIER + metrics.json
look_ci metrics --dir <dir> [--ue <ue plates dir>]      # metrics.json for an existing plate dir
look_ci compare --this <set> [--prev <set>] [--ue <dir>] [--noise noise.json]
                [--this-label T] [--prev-label P] [--location text] [--md path]
                [--content <fingerprint>]
look_ci noise   --a <set> --b <set> --out noise.json    # FLIP + GPU spread of two identical runs
```

A *set* is a directory with `desktop-high/<shot>.png`, `deck/<shot>.png` and `timing.csv`.
`compare` writes into the set:

- `compare/<tier>/<shot>.png`: four 960×540 panels, **UE | previous | this | FLIP heat map**
  (black, magenta, orange, white as the error grows)
- `overview_<tier>.png`: all twelve rows at half size
- `compare.json` and `summary.md`

FLIP and SSIM come from `regia_render::compare::compare_srgb8`, which scores two display-encoded
RGBA8 frames.

## Running it

The orchestration script is `.claude/orchestration/lookci.sh`. It is not in git, because it drives
the build machines.

```text
lookci.sh <tag>                 # renders on the build server, summary -> .claude/orchestration/lookci/<tag>.md
lookci.sh --calibrate <tag>     # renders <tag> twice -> noise.json (the FLIP noise floor)
```

The output goes to `the build server:<build-dir>>/` (`<tag>/c-<fingerprint>/`
when the tag is rendered again on newer content). DO27's content snapshots and the UE plates are
copied to the farm read-only. Never commit them or renders of them to this repository.

# Sky Lab: a day and a change of weather

<!-- index: Sky Lab -->
<!-- index: Time of day -->
<!-- index: Cloud settings -->
<!-- index: Weather -->
<!-- index: Precipitation -->
<!-- index: Surface weather -->
<!-- index: Scene wind -->
<!-- index: Rain -->
<!-- index: Snow -->

Sky Lab (`samples/sky_lab`) is a small headless sample for the sky. It answers one question: what
do the sun, the sky and the clouds look like across a whole day, and across a change of cloud
cover? Rain, snow, wet ground, and the wind near the ground are a separate system, in
[Weather in a project](#weather-in-a-project) below.
The scene is a plain, a ridge to the north and the sky. The camera stands 3 m above the ground and
looks north, away from the midday sun, tilted up so clouds fill the top half of the frame.

## A first run

```sh
cargo run -p sky_lab -- --out /tmp/sky_lab_run
```

This renders 120 frames at 320x180. The sun climbs from 5:30 to a midday peak and sets by 18:30,
while the clouds change from a few scattered cumulus (`fair`) to a dense, windy storm layer
(`storm`). The tool writes `frame_0000.png`, `frame_0020.png` and so on, plus `report.json` with
the hour, the sun's elevation, the cloud coverage and the mean brightness of each frame. Open the
first, middle and last PNG side by side to see the change.

Other starting points:

```sh
# An overcast afternoon, larger images, a frame every 10.
cargo run -p sky_lab -- --from overcast --to overcast --start-hour 13 --end-hour 17 --size 640x360 --every 10 --out /tmp/sky_overcast

# Sunset with the sky clearing.
cargo run -p sky_lab -- --from broken --to clear --start-hour 16 --end-hour 20 --out /tmp/sky_sunset
```

## Using the same pieces in a game

The sample sets two things every frame: a `TimeOfDay` for the sun and a `CloudSettings` for the
layer. A game sets the same resources:

```rust
use regia::prelude::*;
use regia::render::{CloudSettings, TimeOfDay};

fn advance_the_day(mut time: ResMut<TimeOfDay>, mut clouds: ResMut<CloudSettings>, dt: Res<Time>) {
    time.hour = (time.hour + dt.delta_secs() * 0.01).rem_euclid(24.0);
    clouds.time_s += dt.delta_secs();
}
```

The presets and the blend function live in the sample crate (`sky_lab::WeatherPreset`,
`sky_lab::blend_clouds`); they are ordinary `CloudSettings` values, so a game can copy the numbers
it likes. Sky Lab only changes the cloud layer. It does not wet the ground or draw rain.

Two things to know when changing that cloud layer at runtime:

- Moving coverage or cloud type rebuilds the cloud map (128×128 by default). That is cheap, but it
  happens on every frame of a slow blend. It does not change surface wetness.
- The wind drifts the clouds by `wind_m_per_s * time_s`. Changing the wind speed while `time_s` is
  large makes the whole cloud field jump, because the drift is the product. Blend the wind and keep
  `time_s` as the integral of the speed over time if the jump matters to you. That product is the
  cloud layer's clock. It is not `SceneWind`.

## Weather in a project

`docs/specs/99-weather-precipitation.md` is the project weather. It decides what falls, how
exposed surfaces get wet or collect snow, and the wind 10 m above the ground. Sky Lab's cloud
blend does not run it. Changing a Sky Lab preset does not change `SurfaceWeather`.

Three effects stay off until `assets/config/weather.ron` turns them on: drawn precipitation,
surface weather, and weather-driven scene wind. The file format is `docs/formats/weather-ron.md`
(read as `config://weather.ron`). A missing file leaves every effect off. `regia new` writes the
file with all three on for the `blank`, `first_person`, `third_person`, and `top_down` templates.
`net_game` and `quick` do not ship it. With the effects off, a `Weather` kept for its clouds
renders the same frames as before, including a map that sits in `overcast` (that preset's
precipitation would otherwise drizzle). Turned on, they still do nothing until the weather has
precipitation, a wind, or a surface state that is not dry.

| Preset | With the effects on |
|---|---|
| `overcast` | 2 mm/h of rain. Surfaces wet. Puddles do not fill. |
| `rain` | 6 mm/h. Puddles fill in about 85 minutes from dry. |
| `storm` | 50 mm/h, and visibility of 3 km. |
| `snow` | 1.2 cm/h of snow. The ground is covered in about 2.5 hours. |
| `blizzard` | 5 cm/h of snow, and visibility of 400 m. Cover in about 35 minutes. |

`precipitation_kind` defaults to `auto`: snow at or below 0 °C, rain at or above 2.5 °C, and a
blend between those temperatures. `rain`, `snow`, and `sleet` force the kind. Rates and the
checks an agent can run are on
[Rain, snow, wet surfaces and the wind near the ground](book/agents/weather-precipitation.md).

`SceneWind` is the wind near the ground. Mode `Weather` means the weather writes it.
`Manual` holds a value you set. `Off` reads as no wind. Grass, rain, snow, and the foliage wind
follow it. Cloth does not: cloth wind stays the host's value.
`SurfaceWeather` is wetness, puddles, and snow cover. Mode `Simulated` integrates over game
time. Mode `Manual` holds the numbers (a wet street with no weather clock).
`WeatherAir` is the extra extinction while rain or snow is falling. The frame applies it where
it applies fog.

Terrain layers answer the same surface state. Format v5 carries a per-layer `weather` block
(`porosity`, `snow`, `porosity_from_orm`) and the stack's `puddles`. See
[Photoreal terrain](book/user-guide/terrain-photoreal.md). A roof stays dry when the precipitation occlusion
view is on. `render.surface_exposure` compares a point under the roof with a point beside it.

Not in this version, from spec 99 § 16: lightning, drops on the lens, streaks running down
walls, hail, footprints and other snow deformation, rain shafts under single clouds, and
regional weather volumes. The weather is one state for the whole scene. The path tracer and
baked GI stay dry. Local lights do not light the rain and snow. Rain does not fall onto water
bodies, and the sea state is not driven from this page. The sea-state table is a water extra
and is off by default (`docs/specs/100-water-extras.md`).

## What to look for

- Dawn and dusk: the sun below the horizon still lights the upper layer for a while; the frames are
  dark but not black.
- Midday: the brightest frames, a blue sky between the clouds, the ground lit by the sun.
- Overcast: the layer is low and thick; the sun disk is hidden and the light is flat.

The agent-oriented description (flags, the report fields, exit codes and the tests) is in
[Sky Lab (agent guide)](book/agents/sky-lab.md).

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor.md -->
# Editor

The editor (`regia-editor`) is a docking UI over the engine's own ECS: a **Viewport**, **Outliner**,
**Inspector**, **Content Browser** and **Output Log**, all editing the same world the game runs.

```console
$ regia-editor --project my_game
```

Without `--project` it shows the project browser (recent projects, Blank, Open folder). With
`--project`, it opens the startup level from `Regia.toml`.

## The edit world

The editor keeps an **edit world** (a minimal `App` with the agent protocol server and editor
resources). Every panel edit is a command on a shared **undo stack** (Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+Shift+Z
or Ctrl+Y redoes; Cmd on macOS; one gizmo drag or slider scrub is one step); Play runs a **copy** of the
world (play-in-editor), so play never writes your edit. Autosave writes
`.regia/autosave/<stem>.level.ron` (`<stem>~<8 hex digits>.level.ron` when another level shares the stem) every five minutes while a level is dirty, and offers Restore
on the next launch.

## Panels

- **Viewport** — the scene view: a sky dome, lit proxy cubes, a grid, gizmos (translate/rotate/scale) and selection labels. Editing uses a cheap stable profile (native scale, no temporal jitter). Play shows the same camera over the play world; Stop restores the edit view.
- **Outliner** — the entity hierarchy with a name search; reparent by dragging rows (a selected row drags the
  whole selection; drop under the tree to move to the root; world poses are kept). Shift-click selects a range;
  Delete, Ctrl+D (duplicate) and Ctrl+G (group) act on the selection. See
  [Outliner hierarchy edits](book/agents/hierarchy.md).
- **Inspector** — the reflected fields of the selection, with ranges/units/tooltips from editor
  attributes.
- **Content Browser** — import (glTF/PNG/audio), create materials/prefabs/levels, drag into the
  viewport.
- **Output Log** — the engine log, filtered. `path:line[:col]` opens in your code editor (Preferences ▸ Code ▸ Code
  editor command: `code`, `zed`, `$EDITOR` or a command with `{file}`, `{line}`, `{col}`), and an asset path opens the
  asset. Paths with spaces work.
- **World Settings** — **Edit ▸ World settings…**: the current level's gravity, environment, game rules, ambient
  audio, streaming, atmosphere, look and audio medium. Edits are undoable and save with the level. What reads the
  settings live changes at once; what a level load applies (game rules, baked GI, lightmap) takes effect when the level
  opens again. The viewport's `editor` quality keeps its own sky and exposure: pick another quality to see the atmosphere
  and look.
- **Kit** — a Tincal kit folder opened with **File ▸ Open kit…** (or from the project browser, no
  project needed): metadata, checksums, clips, sockets and the model with its cockpit. See
  [Open kit](book/user-guide/open-kit.md).

## Viewport and outliner keys

Keys act on the pane the pointer is over. Every one is a command: search the palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) and press F2, or use
Preferences ▸ Keymap, to move it. A user shortcut replaces the built-in key.

| Key | Does | Command |
|---|---|---|
| W, E, R | translate, rotate, scale gizmo | `gizmo.translate`, `gizmo.rotate`, `gizmo.scale` |
| Ctrl (held) | invert the toolbar's Snap toggle while dragging (grid, angle or scale step) | |
| V (held) | vertex snap while translating: the pivot goes to the nearest vertex of the triangle under the pointer | `gizmo.vertex_snap` |
| End | drop the selection onto the first surface below it | `selection.drop_to_floor` |
| C | collider handles on the selection, instead of its gizmo | `collider.toggle_handles` |
| F | frame the selection (an eased 0.25 s move) | `view.frame_selection` |
| 1, 2, 3, 4 | perspective, top, front, side view preset (eased) | |
| Ctrl+0…9, Shift+0…9 | store, recall a camera bookmark | |
| Ctrl+D (viewport) | duplicate the selection | |
| Alt+drag on the gizmo | duplicate the selection and move the copies (one undo step) | |
| G | game view | |
| Right mouse + W, S, A, D, E, Q | fly forward, back, left, right, up, down | `camera.fly_forward`, `camera.fly_back`, `camera.fly_left`, `camera.fly_right`, `camera.fly_up`, `camera.fly_down` |
| Delete, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+G (pointer over the outliner) | delete, duplicate, group the selection | `outliner.delete`, `outliner.duplicate`, `outliner.group` |
| Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z | undo, redo | `edit.undo`, `edit.redo` |
| Ctrl+Shift+P | command palette | |

The viewport toolbar's **Pivot** choice sets where a multi-selection rotates and scales about: the median point, each
entity's own origin, or the active (last selected) entity. The Outliner row's eye hides an entity in the viewport (one
undo step) and its lock keeps it from being picked or box-selected; a link icon marks a prefab instance and a dot one with
overrides. **File** has Save all, Recent and Exit; **Edit** has Cut, Copy, Paste, Duplicate, Delete and Select all
(ADR-7204).

**Align to surface** in the viewport's **Tools** menu makes End also turn the selection's up onto the surface normal
(`placement.toggle_align_normal`). With **Collider handles** on (same menu), grips on the faces of a box, the surface of a sphere and
the ends and sides of a capsule change its size about its center, and the grip at its center moves its offset; each drag is
one undo step. See [Viewport tools](book/agents/viewport-tools.md).

## Graybox shapes

**Create ▸ Shape** spawns a parametric shape at the viewport's orbit target and selects it: cuboid,
sphere, capsule, cylinder, cone, conical frustum, plane, torus, tetrahedron, ramp or prism. It is a
`Primitive` component (shape, parameters, color, roughness, metalness) on an entity with a
`Transform`, so the inspector edits its size and resolution, the viewport and the game draw the real
mesh, it saves in the level file, and Undo removes it. Agents use `scene.spawn_primitive`
([scene page](book/agents/scene.md)). The meshers are ported from Bevy's `bevy_mesh` primitives
(MIT; see `docs/ported-sources.toml`).

## Placeable actors

Beside Shape, the **Create** menu places a **Player start**, **Trigger volume**, **Point light**,
**Spot light**, **Directional light**, **Camera**, **Reflection capture**, **Audio emitter**,
**Rect light**, **Tube light**, **Decal**, **Post-process volume**, **Spline**, **Nav link** and
**Smart object** at the viewport's orbit target. Each is one entity named after the entry, carrying
the runtime component with its default values (a rect light faces the floor; a decal names the
built-in scorch marking; a spline has two points 4 m apart), selected and saved with the level; one
Undo removes it. Agents use `editor.create_entity { kind }` ([Create menu](book/agents/create-menu.md)).
Water planes and fog volumes are not Create entries yet.

## Editing and play

The editor edits through reflection, so every saved type is editable, and every property edit is undoable (`editor.set_render_override` is a live tint and is not).
Play-in-editor (Play / Pause / Step / Stop) runs the game crate if one is open (hot-reloaded), or
the engine's built-in systems otherwise. **⧉ Play in window** plays in a separate window with the game's
camera: a click in it captures the mouse, Shift+F1 frees it, and closing it stops play. The window opens at
the size (and, off Wayland, the place) the last one had. The **⛶** menu next to it picks the size the
game renders at in that window: the window's own, 720p, 1080p, a 9:16 or 9:19.5 phone, a 3:4 tablet, or a
custom size. The picture is scaled to fit with black bars, and clicks land where they would on that screen.
While the window is open, the viewport shows a note instead of a second copy of the game. The toolbar's other controls, pause, step and the Game tabs are on [Play-in-editor](book/user-guide/editor-guide/play-in-editor.md). A listen or dedicated session with several clients is the [Net](book/user-guide/editor-guide/net.md) tab (panel id `net`), not a match between two machines. See `docs/specs/19-editor.md` and the
[agent guide's editor page](book/agents/editor.md) for the full `editor.*` method surface.

## Scripts

`editor.create_script <name>` writes `game/src/scripts/<name>.rs` and registers it at
`// REGIA:SCRIPTS`; the next play (or hot reload) picks it up. Scripts are the intended way to
attach behavior without leaving the editor.

## Bake, budgets, the content index and hierarchy drops

- **Bake runner** tab: runs `regia bake-gi` on a built-in scene or one of the project's `.bake.ron`
  descriptions. **Validate** is a dry run: it checks the description and lays out the probes, with
  no GPU and nothing written. **Bake** traces the volume in a separate process, so the editor keeps
  drawing; a progress bar shows the stage and the probes done. **Cancel** stops it. Then the panel
  shows the probe counts and the file written, or the error with the description key at fault. The
  editor runs the `regia` CLI next to its own executable (or `REGIA_CLI`). See
  [Editor Bake runner panel](book/agents/editor-bake.md).
- **Budget meters**: the Kit panel shows the kit's triangles, materials, texture memory and the
  other model limits against its class (from `kit.json`; pick another class beside it), plus its
  LOD chain. Prefab mode shows the same line in its banner (hover for every meter). Green is under
  80 % of a limit, amber is near it, red is over. See [Editor budget meters](book/agents/editor-budget.md).
- **Content Browser** speed: the asset list comes from a cached scan. It is not walked every frame,
  and only the rows in view are drawn. Changes made outside the editor show up within a second; ↻
  rescans at once. See [Editor content index](book/agents/editor-content-index.md).
- **Content Browser grid and search**: **Grid** (beside **List**) shows thumbnails of textures and
  models, kept in `.regia/thumbs` (safe to delete). The search box ignores case; `-word` hides,
  `type:mesh` / `type:texture` / ... keeps one asset type, and `ext:png` keeps one file suffix. Best
  matches (file names that start with your first word) come first. Projects of tens of thousands of
  assets stay smooth: a folder costs its own size, typing narrows the last result, and an outside
  change re-lists only its folder. See [Editor asset browser](book/agents/editor-asset-browser.md).
- **Outliner drops**: drag a row onto another row to parent it, or onto the strip under the tree to
  unparent it. A selected row brings the whole selection along. Entities keep their place in the
  world (hold Alt to keep the local transform instead). A drop into the dragged entity's own subtree
  is outlined in red and refused. One Ctrl+Z undoes the whole drop. See
  [Editor hierarchy drag and drop](book/agents/editor-hierarchy.md).

## Several entities in the Inspector

Select more than one entity and the Inspector shows a field's value when they agree, and an em dash
when they do not. Changing a field writes it onto every selected entity that has the component.
A vector axis, a color channel and one Euler axis change on their own: the other axes stay as each
entity had them. A component that only some of the selection has is labeled "on k of n" and can
still be edited on those entities. Add component and Remove component apply to the whole selection.
One Ctrl+Z undoes the edit for every entity. On a prefab instance the edit is recorded as an
override of that instance, and one undo restores the previous value and override state.

Prefab overrides appear in bold with an entity id and field path. Revert and Apply target that
instance. Apply updates the loaded template in memory; one undo restores the template and marker.

## Conversation graph editor

The **Conversation** tab (in the bottom tab group of the default layout) shows a conversation (`assets/conversations/<id>.conv.ron`) as a
graph. Type the path and press **Open**. Blocks of lines sit between labels; `If`, `Choice` and `End` steps are nodes
of their own, and arrows show where each jump, branch and option goes (a red dangling arrow is a jump to a label
that does not exist). The layout is automatic and does not move when you edit a line; drag a node to place it by
hand (the position is kept in `.regia/conversation_layout/`, not in the conversation file). The wheel zooms, dragging
the background pans, **Fit** frames the whole graph, and **Search** finds nodes by text, key, label or speaker.

Click a node to edit its steps on the right: speaker, text key and note of a line, a choice's prompt and options
(text, condition, target), an `If`'s condition and branches, event names, and label names (renaming a label updates
every jump to it). Buttons below insert new lines and steps after the node. To retarget a jump, drag the small circle
at the bottom of a node onto a node that starts with a label. Every change is one Ctrl+Z step. **Save** writes the
file in its standard layout; opening and saving without changes leaves the file byte for byte as it was.

Problems the conversation checker finds (unreachable lines, missing labels, choices without options, missing voice
clips per language, lines too long for their subtitle time) are drawn on the nodes and listed under **Findings**;
click one to jump to its node. **Preview** plays the conversation from the start or from the selected node: tick the
conditions you want true, click through lines and pick choices, and turn on **Play voice** to hear recorded clips. A
file that does not parse opens read-only with the error and its line. Agents use the same panel through
[the conversation editor methods](book/agents/conversation-editor.md).

## When the editor crashes

If the editor closes unexpectedly, the next launch says so. A level that was left unsaved still
offers **Restore** and **Discard autosave**. When a crash report was written, the same dialog
offers **View report**, **Copy to clipboard** and **Open folder**. The report holds the panic
message, the backtrace, the editor build, the operating system, the GPU adapter and the last
200 log lines. Home directories in the report are shown as `~`.

A panic inside game code while playing in the editor writes a report marked `pie`, stops play,
and leaves the editor running. A native crash (the process died without a Rust panic) is saved
as a feedback bundle next to the text reports. On Windows that capture stays off unless you
turn it on (`REGIA_NATIVE_CRASH=1`); `REGIA_NO_NATIVE_CRASH=1` turns it off on every desktop.

Nothing in a report is sent anywhere. Share the file yourself if you want someone to look at it.
Agents can list and read the same files with `editor.crash_reports` and
`editor.crash_report_read` ([Editor crash reports](book/agents/editor-crash-reports.md)).

**Dismiss report** hides the offer for the current session and keeps the report on disk.

## Status bar, drawers and the console

The status bar's indicators are buttons: **Content** and **Log** open the drawers, **Unsaved: N** saves
the level (File ▸ Save all; other documents save from their own panels for now), **Jobs: N** lists the running background jobs with their progress and a
Cancel each, **Trace** starts and stops a trace recording, and **Problems: N** opens the Problems tab.
A drawer slides the Content Browser or the Output Log up over the dock without changing your layout;
Esc, a click elsewhere or moving the focus away closes it (Esc then does nothing else), and **Dock**
keeps it as a normal tab. Ctrl+Shift+Space toggles the content drawer outside play and text fields
(rebind it in the command palette with F2).

The Output Log ends with a console line: type a command id (`edit.undo`), an agent method with JSON
parameters (`editor.focus {"entity": 12}`) or a console variable the project registered. Tab completes
names and shows a method's parameters, Up and Down walk the history (kept per project), and the result
is printed in the log. The main toolbar's **Quick settings** gathers snapping and its steps, the realtime
viewport, the main viewport's show flags and preview sun, and autosave. Agents use the same features
through [the status bar, drawer and console methods](book/agents/editor-console.md).
