# Cargo features

Every Cargo feature of the engine crates is listed, with what it does and its guide page, in § 1 of the
[coverage map](book/COVERAGE.md); `cargo xtask book-coverage` fails when a crate gains a feature with no row there
([book coverage](book/agents/book-coverage.md)). This page says which ones a game chooses.

## What a game turns on

A game depends on `regia`. Its default features (`agent`, `ui`, `quick`) suit development: the agent server, the
runtime UI and the one-file app helpers. Shipping builds turn the defaults off (`regia package` does it) unless the game
opts back in. The optional ones a game may add:

| Feature | When |
|---|---|
| `steam` | The game ships on Steam (`regia::steam`) |
| `crash` | The game uploads crash reports (`regia::crash`; add `regia_crash/tls` for `https://` endpoints) |
| `net` | The game uses client-server replication (`regia::net`) |
| `voice-net` | The game carries voice chat over `regia::net` (`regia::net::voice`, implies `net`) |
| `voice-opus` | Voice chat speaks Opus (`regia::media::voice_opus`, implies `media`) |
| `physics2d` | The game uses 2D bodies and colliders |
| `frame-gen` | FSR 3 frame generation: an interpolated frame between every two rendered ones, desktop only, off until the game or an agent enables it (`render.set_frame_gen`) |
| `dev-assets` | Dev runs only (`regia run --dev`): never in a shipped build |
| `static-dxc` | Windows builds that use the DX12 fallback with the statically linked DXC |
| `accesskit` | The game's UI talks to the player's screen reader (AT-SPI, UI Automation, NSAccessibility; [Accessibility](book/user-guide/accessibility.md)) |

`regia_dylib` has the same features and forwards each to `regia`: the editor's hot-reload build links the engine
through it ([hot reload](book/user-guide/hot-reload.md)).

## Internal features

Some features exist for the engine's own tests and tools and are never turned on by a game:

- `regia_render/test-hooks`: out-of-memory hooks (`texture_stream::inject_stream_texture_oom`,
  `inject_stream_upload_oom`, `gpu_health::release_texture_mip_hold`) that allocate a huge texture on purpose. The
  renderer's own tests turn it on through a dev-dependency.
- `regia_agent/reference-trace` and `denoise`, `regia_pt/denoise`: desktop tools only (the reference path tracer and
  the native OIDN denoiser).
- `regia_ecs/debug_names` and `regia_app/debug_names` (on by default): keep system and component names for the agent
  protocol, the profiler and `App::shuffle_schedules`; a shipping build may turn them off.

<!-- source: book/user-guide/accessibility.md -->
# Accessibility

Regia Engine's runtime UI builds an accessibility tree from your widgets, and with the `accesskit` feature it
sends that tree to the player's screen reader. You get a tree without extra work: buttons, check boxes, sliders,
text fields, dialogs and lists get their role, name, value and states from the widget components. You add an
`Accessible` component where the inferred result is wrong or missing.

## What you get for free

- **Roles and names.** A `Button` with a `Text` child is a button named by that text. A `Slider` is a slider
  with its number, range and step. A `TextInput` with a placeholder and no label is named by the placeholder.
  Unnamed plain containers are flattened, so the tree reads like the screen.
- **States.** Focus, disabled, selected, invalid, checked, expanded (combo boxes, dialogs) and read-only text
  fields.
- **Dialogs.** An open `Modal` is the top input layer. Everything under it is inert: a screen reader is told the
  dialog is modal and the controls behind it offer no actions.
- **Requests.** A screen reader can press, focus, step a slider, set a text field's text, close a dialog and
  scroll. These go through the same path as a key press or a click, so a disabled control refuses them.

## Turning the screen-reader bridge on

```toml
[dependencies]
regia = { workspace = true, features = ["accesskit"] }
```

With the feature, the bridge talks to AT-SPI on Linux (Orca), UI Automation on Windows (Narrator, NVDA),
NSAccessibility on macOS (VoiceOver) and TalkBack on Android. It costs nothing until a screen reader connects.
After that it sends only what changed each frame, and spreads a very large change over several frames (256
changed nodes per frame), so a frame never stalls. On Android the adapter injects into the game's surface
view; the Java class travels inside the crate (`embedded-dex`), so the activity shim is unchanged. TalkBack
connecting asks for a full tree on the next update.

`REGIA_ACCESSKIT=0` turns the OS side off without a rebuild.

## Fixing names and roles: `Accessible`

```rust
# use regia::prelude::*;
use regia::ui::a11y::{A11yRole, Accessible, Politeness};

# fn spawn_menu(mut commands: Commands) {
// An icon button: no text, so give it a name (a localization key wins when defined).
commands.spawn((UiNode, Button, Focusable::default(), Accessible::default().with_label_key("menu-settings")));

// A score readout the screen reader announces when it changes.
commands.spawn((
    UiNode,
    Text::new("0"),
    Accessible::default().with_role(A11yRole::Status).with_label("Score").with_live(Politeness::Polite),
));

// Decoration: leave it out of the tree.
commands.spawn((UiNode, UiImage::default(), Accessible::decorative()));
# }
```

To say something once (a save finished, a match starts), call
`ScreenReader::announce("Game saved", Politeness::Polite)`. Use `Politeness::Assertive` only for messages that
must interrupt.

## Checklist

1. Every control has a name. Read `ui.a11y_tree` and look for empty `name` on buttons, check boxes, sliders and
   text fields.
2. Icon-only buttons have a label or label key.
3. Decorative images are `Accessible::decorative()`.
4. Status text that changes during play (score, timers, objectives) is a live region, `Polite` unless urgent.
5. Dialogs are `Modal`s, so what is behind them is inert.
6. With the bridge on, connect a screen reader (or `ui.a11y_platform_connect`) and walk the menus with the
   keyboard and the reader's own navigation.

## Auditing a screen

A theme can pass its contrast lint and still ship a screen with white text on a light picture, a 12 px close box,
a button with no name, or a label cut off at double text size. The audit checks the screen you actually built, from
its computed layout, its accessibility tree and its resolved theme. It adds nothing to the frame, so it costs
nothing until you call it, and it leaves the UI as it was.

From an agent:

```json
{"method": "ui.a11y_audit", "params": {}}
```

From a test or a debug key:

```rust
# use regia::prelude::*;
use regia::ui::a11y_audit::{AuditOptions, AuditProfile, audit_ui};

# fn print_audit(world: &mut World) {
let report = audit_ui(world, &AuditOptions {
    profile: AuditProfile::Touch, // on phones and tablets
    ..Default::default()
});
for finding in &report.findings {
    println!("{} {}: {} (needs {})", finding.rule.code(), finding.path, finding.measured, finding.required);
}
# }
```

What it checks:

- Every control has a name.
- Text contrast against what is really behind the text: 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text.
- The focus ring and control boundaries: 3:1.
- Targets are at least 24 UI px per side, or the theme's `size.touch-min` with the touch profile.
- Navigation reaches every control, and each control shows a focus indicator.
- No text is lost at 200 % text size.
- Nothing keeps animating with reduced motion on.

Read the results this way:

- **`error`** breaks the rule. Fix it.
- **`warning`** is probably wrong, or wrong in a way that loses nothing.
- **`info`** means the audit cannot tell. Text over an image or over the running game gets it, because the audit
  does not read pixels. Look at those by eye, on the real background. They are not passes.

Common fixes:

- A control whose label sits beside it needs its own name: `Accessible::default().with_label("Volume")`. Only a
  label inside the control names it.
- Give text fields and combo boxes the `Panel.field` or `Button.field` class. The default `surface` and `button` edges
  are under 3:1, which is fine for a button because its text identifies it.
- Keep a page that may not fit inside a scroll view that can shrink: `flex_shrink: 1.0`, a `min_size` height of 0, and
  clipped overflow. Flex items do not shrink by default, so a tall page otherwise runs off the window.
- Theme text color reaches labels through plain containers. A node with its own `Background` stops it, so choose
  that text's color yourself.

A target that is small on purpose can say why with the `TargetExemption` component (`Equivalent`, `Inline`,
`UserAgentControl`, `Essential`). The audit lists every exception it used, so a reviewer can see what was excused.

To keep a screen clean, compare `finding.key()` against a checked-in list in a test, as
`samples/ui_gallery/tests/a11y_audit.rs` does. Keys hold no entity ids, so the list stays valid between runs.

A clean audit is not a screen-reader test: still run your menus with a real screen reader, and read
[the rule list](book/agents/ui-a11y-audit.md) for what each rule measures.

## Checking it with an agent

- [UI accessibility tree and screen readers](book/agents/ui-a11y.md): `ui.a11y_tree`, `ui.a11y_announce`,
  `ui.a11y_act`.
- [Screen-reader OS bridge](book/agents/ui-a11y-platform.md): `ui.a11y_platform_tree`, `ui.a11y_platform_connect`,
  `ui.a11y_platform_action` (the tree as the OS sees it).
- [UI accessibility audit](book/agents/ui-a11y-audit.md): `ui.a11y_audit` (defects on the screen shown now).

## Limits

- Steam Deck game mode has no screen-reader path (desktop mode on the Deck is Linux, so AT-SPI). Android
  TalkBack is ADR-3454: there is no callback when TalkBack turns off, so the bridge stays active until the
  process ends or `ui.a11y_platform_connect` is sent `false`. A shipping build (`panic = "abort"`) still
  ends if AccessKit's own JNI unwrap fires after the preflight.
- The bridge is off by default. The Linux adapter's D-Bus thread can panic if the accessibility bus fails in an
  unexpected way, which ends a shipping (`panic = "abort"`) build. Test with your target desktops before you
  ship with it.

## Player assists: input, audio and color vision

Four more settings in `GameSettings.accessibility` (ADR-2646). They persist with the other settings and apply
live; your options menu only has to write them.

```rust,wrap
use regia::framework::settings::GameSettings;
use regia_input::{ActionAssist, PressMode, RepeatRate};
use regia::render::color_vision::{ColorVisionDeficiency, ColorVisionFilter, ColorVisionMode};
# use regia_ecs::prelude::ResMut;

fn apply_menu_choices(mut settings: ResMut<GameSettings>) {
    let a = &mut settings.accessibility;
    // Crouch latches on one press and off on the next; Fire repeats while held.
    a.input_assists.insert("Crouch".into(), ActionAssist { mode: PressMode::Toggle, ..Default::default() });
    a.input_assists.insert("Fire".into(), ActionAssist { repeat: Some(RepeatRate::DEFAULT), ..Default::default() });
    // The whole output in both ears.
    a.mono_audio = true;
    // Shift red/green confusions into colors a deuteranope can tell apart.
    a.color_vision = ColorVisionFilter::new(ColorVisionMode::Compensate, ColorVisionDeficiency::Deuteranopia);
}
```

- **Input assists** (per action): hold or toggle, a minimum hold time that drops short accidental presses,
  auto-repeat while held, and a cool-down (`cooldown_steps`, a minimum number of evaluations between accepted
  presses). The default set is `input_assists`. `input_assists_by_player` and `input_assists_by_gamepad` overlay
  it for one local player or one pad. Your triggers still run as authored, on the assisted input. Call
  `Actions::release_toggle` when the game must drop a latched action (a cutscene, a death).
  [Input assists](book/agents/input-assists.md).
- **Rumble and phone vibration**: `a.rumble_scale` and `a.vibration_scale` (`0` off to `1`) scale gamepad rumble
  and `PhoneVibration::vibrate`. Reduced motion does not change either.
  [Input assists](book/agents/input-assists.md).
- **Scene motion**: `a.camera_shake_scale` (`0` to `1`) scales authored camera shake without rewriting the
  camera. `a.motion_blur` is `None` (leave the render profile), `Some(false)` (force off) or `Some(true)` (allow
  it; the velocity target is still required). `a.fov_override_deg` replaces the gameplay camera's field of view
  in degrees (`None` keeps the camera's value; shots and the sequencer keep theirs). `a.reduced_motion` also
  sets the effective shake scale and the head-bob scale to `0` and forces motion blur off. Framework effects
  that animate on their own: camera shake, handheld sway and breathing, and the walk bob all honor it. Field-of-view
  kicks stay as authored unless the override replaces the gameplay camera's fov.
  [Settings](book/agents/framework.md).
- **Look**: `GameSettings.input.sensitivity` and `invert_y` scale the actions named in `InputConfig.look_actions`.
  With that list empty the game reads the two fields itself.
  [Input assists](book/agents/input-assists.md).
- **Mono audio**: the output is downmixed to mono before the master limiter. [Mono audio](book/agents/audio-mono.md).
- **Color vision**: `Simulate` shows the game as a player with protanopia, deuteranopia or tritanopia sees it (use
  it while designing); `Compensate` is the player option. It works through the view's color LUT, after your grade,
  and does not filter the UI. [Color-vision filters](book/agents/color-vision.md).

What the engine covers, and what is still the game's job, is listed against public accessibility guidelines in
`docs/accessibility-review.md`.

## Photosensitivity check

Before a release, run the flash check on any sequence that strobes on purpose: a trailer, a
render-out, a muzzle flash, an explosion, lightning. It counts general flashes and saturated-red
flashes the way WCAG 2.2 success criterion 2.3.1 describes them, and it fails a sequence with more
than three flashes in any one second when that flash covers more than a quarter of a 10 degree
field.

On a folder of PNG frames (file-name order, one directory, no subfolders):

```text
cargo xtask flash-check captures/trailer --fps 30
cargo xtask flash-check captures/trailer --fps 30 --json
```

`--fps` is the rate the frames were captured at. Exit 0 means the sequence passed, exit 2 means it
failed the thresholds, and exit 1 means the folder or a frame could not be read. `--json` prints
the same report the agent returns: `passed`, `max_flashes`, `window_start_s`, `region`,
`area_fraction` and `kind` (`general` or `red`).

From a running game, `seeing.flash_check` analyzes a folder the same way, or captures the window
now (`frames` from 2 to 600, `fps` the analysis rate). The call and its error codes are on the
[seeing](book/agents/seeing.md#photosensitivity-check) page.

The 10 degree field is 341×256 pixels on a 1024×768 screen at a typical viewing distance. Pass
`reference_width`, `reference_height`, `ten_degree_width_px` and `ten_degree_height_px` when the
player sits closer or the frame is a different size, and record that geometry with the result.
`cell_px` (default 8) trades exactness for speed. Use `1` when a small region matters.

This check is an aid. It is not a certification and it is not a guarantee that a sequence is safe
to watch. It does not apply the exception for a balanced pattern of squares smaller than 0.1
degree, and it does not limit flashes while the game is running. A failure is a reason to change
the effect or to warn the player, not a medical verdict.

# Editor guide

One page per area of the editor: what it is for, its main actions with their keyboard shortcuts,
and the agent method that does each action, so a person and an agent can do the same work. The
shortcuts on these pages are the ones the editor's code handles (the command table in
`crates/regia_editor/src/command_palette.rs` and the key handling of each panel); an action
listed with no key has none. Hands-on walk-throughs are the tutorials
[Your first scene in the editor](book/tutorials/editor-first-scene.md),
[Your first material graph](book/tutorials/editor-first-material.md) and
[Package a build](book/tutorials/package-a-build.md).

The editor overview (launching, levels, hot reload) is [Editor](book/user-guide/editor.md); the editor's
whole agent surface is [Editor surface](book/agents/editor.md); keyboard reachability, focus and
contrast are reviewed in [Editor accessibility](book/user-guide/editor-guide/accessibility.md).

## The window

The menu bar has **File**, **Create**, **Edit** and **View**. Below it, the play toolbar
([Play-in-editor](book/user-guide/editor-guide/play-in-editor.md)), then the dock: every panel is a tab. The default layout
puts the **Outliner** left, the **Viewport** in the middle, the **Inspector** right, and
**Content**, **Output Log**, **Project Settings** and the other tool tabs in the group under the
viewport. Drag a tab to move it, out of the window to float it; **View ▸ Reset layout** restores
the default and brings back a closed tab.

An agent brings a tab forward (adding it when it is closed) with
`editor.layout_apply {"open": "<id>"}`; the ids are the tab names in snake case
(`viewport`, `outliner`, `inspector`, `content`, `material_graph`, `seq_curves`,
`ui_designer`, `project_settings`, `fracture`, `proc_graph`, ...). `editor.layout_get`,
`editor.layout_save` and `editor.layout_reset` read, save and reset the arrangement
([Editor preferences, keymap, layout](book/agents/editor-preferences.md)). Named layouts,
workspaces, maximize (Ctrl+Space), the full-screen viewport (F11), the `+` and Replace with
pane controls and feature profiles are on [Layouts, workspaces and feature profiles](book/user-guide/editor-guide/layouts-workspaces.md).

## Keys that work everywhere

| Key | Action | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Ctrl+Z | Undo the last edit (not while a text field has focus: the field keeps its own undo; not during play) | `editor.undo` |
| Ctrl+Shift+Z, Ctrl+Y | Redo | `editor.redo` |
| Ctrl+Shift+P | Open the command palette: type to search every command, Enter runs the highlighted one | `editor.command` |
| F2 (in the palette) | Record a new shortcut for the highlighted command | `editor.keymap_bind` |
| Alt+P | Play in the editor (when no session runs) | `editor.play` |
| Escape | Stop play when a session runs; otherwise ask to close the editor. A panel that uses Escape (a text field, a menu) gets it first | `editor.stop`, `quit.request` |
| Ctrl+Alt+F11 | Compile the game crate and hot-reload it | `editor.code_status` reports the build |
| Ctrl+= or Ctrl+Plus, Ctrl+-, Ctrl+Alt+0 | Zoom the whole editor interface in, out, or back to 100 % (**View ▸ Reset zoom**); the zoom is the **UI scale** preference, kept between sessions; rebindable (`view.zoom_in`, `view.zoom_out`, `view.reset_zoom`, ADR-7733) | `editor.command` `run: "view.zoom_in"`, `editor.prefs_set` `appearance.ui_scale` |
| Ctrl+0 | In the viewport, stores camera bookmark 0; it no longer resets the interface zoom (Ctrl+Alt+0 does; [finding E-10, FU-4](book/user-guide/editor-guide/accessibility.md)) | `editor.bookmark` |

Ctrl is Cmd on macOS. Every palette command can be given a shortcut in **Edit ▸ Preferences… ▸
Keymap** or with F2 in the palette; the bindings are saved per user in `editor_keymap.ron`
([Editor command palette](book/agents/editor-command.md)). Ctrl+Shift+P cannot be rebound.

Every panel of this guide can be brought forward from the keyboard: Ctrl+Shift+P, type `open`,
pick **Open the … tab** (commands `window.open_viewport`, `window.open_outliner`, ...,
[Editor command palette](book/agents/editor-command.md)); bind one in the Keymap tab to get a
direct key.

## Which panel gets a key

Keys go to the panel under the pointer or with keyboard focus, and only when no text field has
focus: typing a `W` into the Inspector's name field never switches the gizmo. The viewport's keys
work in the active pane (the last one clicked); the Outliner's Delete, Ctrl+D and Ctrl+G work
while the pointer is over the Outliner. Tab and Shift+Tab move keyboard focus between the
widgets of a panel, Space or Enter presses the focused button, and the arrow keys move in a
focused slider or list.

## Coming in v0.6.0

Everything below is **planned** unless it says **built**: a built item has landed on the v0.6 line and links its
page. The plan is ADR-7752 and the
"As planned" sections of the specs for the editor, the UI designer, the runtime UI and localization. Each feature will
have an agent method, so an agent can do whatever a person can, and each is reachable from the keyboard.

Shell, search and settings:

- Named layouts and workspaces (Level, Animation, Materials, UI, World, Cinematics, Debug): **built**
  ([Layouts, workspaces and feature profiles](book/user-guide/editor-guide/layouts-workspaces.md)).
- Maximize a panel or the viewport; add or replace a panel in any pane: planned.
- Floated panels as operating-system windows, and further copies of the Outliner, Content Browser and Inspector: **built**, with a limit. A game `Window` component still becomes an OS window only for the primary window ([Editor](book/user-guide/editor.md#windows)). Editor floats follow `ui.floating_windows` (`os` or `in_window`). Extra Outliner, Content and Inspector copies use the same panel ids.
- A clickable status bar, content and log drawers, and a console line for commands and agent methods: **built** ([Editor](book/user-guide/editor.md#status-bar-drawers-and-the-console)).
- One search window for assets, entities, commands, menus, settings and agent methods: planned.
- Keymap presets, shortcuts that depend on the focused panel, and F1 help for the focused panel: **built** ([Keymap](book/user-guide/editor-guide/keymap.md)).
- One Settings window with search, changed-value marks and reset per category: planned.

Viewport:

- More camera options: inverted axes, six orthographic views, zoom to cursor, navigation presets: planned.
- Pilot a camera, light or entity, a picture-in-picture camera preview and high-resolution screenshots: planned.
- World, local, parent and view reference spaces, more pivots and snapping to surfaces: planned.
- Lasso selection, select similar, pick from a stack under the cursor and a measure tool: planned.
- A view-mode menu (wireframe, overdraw and more), icon filters and a Rendering Debug panel: planned.

Outliner and Inspector:

- Rename in place, a query language for filtering, and folders: planned.
- Configuration warnings, badges, columns and row colors: planned.
- Property search, categories, pinned fields and an Inspector that stays on one entity: planned.
- Copy and paste values, reset to default, conditional fields, expressions with units: planned.
- Asset and entity pickers, inline curves and gradients, and a full color picker: planned.
- A Bulk Edit grid for many entities or assets at once: **built** ([Bulk Edit](book/user-guide/editor-guide/bulk-edit.md)).

Content, import and problems:

- Folder tree, breadcrumbs, favorites, filter chips and collections in the Content browser: planned.
- Bulk actions, a Save all dialog, delete with "replace references with": planned.
- Drop files from the operating system, asset packages and an import dialog with presets: planned.
- Problems grouped by source and a Project Health panel: **built** ([Problems](book/user-guide/editor-guide/problems.md),
  [Project Health](book/user-guide/editor-guide/project-health.md)).

Prefabs, levels and graphs:

- A prefab Overrides window and in-context prefab editing: planned.
- Level variants, layer locks and several levels open at once: planned.
- Material parameters panel, shader statistics and a WGSL code node: planned.
- Logic graph search, a Variables panel, breakpoints and stepping: planned.
- A structural diff of assets and graphs against a git revision: planned.

Animation, effects and world:

- A retargeting panel: **built** ([Retarget](book/user-guide/editor-guide/retarget.md)). Animation debugger and clip preview options: planned.
- Sequence event tracks, track lock, mute and solo, and a dope sheet for UI animations: planned.
- Effects overview, mixer effect chains and navigation path view: planned.
- A world streaming map: **built** ([World Map](book/user-guide/editor-guide/world-map.md)). Terrain brush options, terrain edit layers, tile tools
  and CSG blockout: planned.

UI designer, theme and localization:

- Anchor presets, aspect and effect rows, and a preview that uses the project's scale rule: planned.
- Split, foldable and tab containers, markup text, focus-only styles and layout variants: planned.
- An interactive preview, a view of which style wins, and live style edits in a running game: planned.
- A theme editor with a live gallery of every widget state: planned.
- A localization compile step, translator comments, a preview-language picker and table import and export: planned.

Play, devices and debugging:

- Play start options, time scale, device frames, touch and gamepad simulation: planned.
- Separate-process play in a dock tab, remote Outliner and Inspector for a running game: **built**
  ([Play-in-editor § Game tabs](book/user-guide/editor-guide/play-in-editor.md#game-tabs), [Live edit (agents)](book/agents/live-edit.md)).
- Asset push to a launched game and device mirroring: planned.
- Profiler modules and monitors, memory snapshots, a GPU resource browser and a frame debugger: planned.

Undo, revision control and collaboration:

- An Undo History panel, transactions and safe mode: **built** ([Undo History](book/user-guide/editor-guide/undo-history.md); transactions and
  safe mode: [Shared undo history and recovery (agents)](book/agents/undo.md)).
- Kept versions, project backup and project duplicate: planned.
- A Revision Control panel for git, with lock on edit for projects that use git LFS locks: planned.
- Review notes pinned in the world and an Activity timeline: **built** ([Notes and Activity](book/user-guide/editor-guide/notes-activity.md)).
- LAN presence between editors, off by default: planned.

Build, extensions, accessibility and agents:

- Launch profiles, a Platforms panel and a package size report: planned.
- Extension commands, settings, hooks and utility panels; a samples browser: planned.
- Editor themes with a high-contrast theme, a text scale and a color-vision filter: planned.
- A project browser with thumbnails and level templates: planned.
- An Agent panel that runs an agent command you configure, in Ask-only, Propose or Act mode: **built**
  ([Agent](book/user-guide/editor-guide/agent-panel.md)).

Not planned for v0.6.0: code editing inside the editor (use your own IDE), an asset marketplace, and editing on touch
devices or in a browser. In-editor polygon modeling, posing a rig in the viewport and a node-based audio graph each need
their own spec first.

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/viewport.md -->
# Viewport

Panel id: `viewport`.

The **Viewport** tab shows the level as the game renders it, from an editor camera you fly or
orbit, in one pane or four (perspective plus top, front and side). You select, move, rotate and
scale entities here, frame them, keep camera bookmarks, and during play possess the game camera.
Depth: [Viewport tools (agents)](book/agents/viewport-tools.md), [Viewports
(agents)](book/agents/viewports.md), [Independent viewports](book/user-guide/viewports.md),
[Gizmos](book/user-guide/gizmos.md).

The keys below act on the active pane (the one last clicked) while no text field has focus. A
user shortcut bound to the same command (Preferences ▸ Keymap) replaces the built-in key.

## Camera

| Action | Mouse / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Orbit | Alt+left-drag; right-drag orbits at half speed | none (a mouse gesture; `editor.focus` and `editor.bookmark` place the camera) |
| Pan | Middle-drag (right- or middle-drag in an orthographic pane) | none |
| Zoom | Scroll, or Alt+right-drag | none |
| Fly | Hold the right button and press W / S / A / D (forward, back, left, right), E / Q (up, down); right button + scroll changes the fly speed | none (a held-key gesture) |
| Frame the selection | F (also **View ▸ Frame selection (F)**) | `editor.focus` |
| Store a camera bookmark | Ctrl+0 … Ctrl+9 | `editor.bookmark` |
| Recall a bookmark | 0 … 9 | `editor.bookmark` |

## Selection and gizmos

| Action | Mouse / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Select | Click an entity; Shift+click adds, Ctrl+click toggles | `editor.select`, `editor.pick` |
| Box select | Left-drag on empty space; Shift adds, Ctrl+Shift removes, Ctrl toggles | `editor.box_select` |
| Lasso select | Hold L while left-dragging (or run **Lasso select** from the palette to make every drag a lasso); same modifiers as the box | `editor.lasso_select` |
| Select similar | **Edit ▸ Select ▸ All of the same kind / with the same components / using the same asset / in the same layer**, or the Outliner row menu's **Select similar** | `editor.select_similar` |
| Pick from overlapping objects | Alt+click lists everything under the cursor, nearest first; Up / Down / Enter pick, Escape closes (palette: **List the objects under the cursor**) | `editor.pick_stack` |
| Select a group by clicking a part | Outliner row menu ▸ **Selection root**; Ctrl+click still picks the part | `editor.selection_root` |
| Hover highlight | Rest the pointer on an entity: a thin outline shows what a click selects | none (pointer only) |
| Place an asset | Drag it from the Content Browser: a wire box shows where it lands; release places it, Escape cancels | `editor.drop_preview` |
| Measure | M, then drag for a distance, click again for the angle; hold V to snap to vertices; Escape leaves | `editor.measure` |
| Move gizmo | W | `editor.set_gizmo {"mode":"translate"}` |
| Rotate gizmo | E | `editor.set_gizmo {"mode":"rotate"}` |
| Scale gizmo | R | `editor.set_gizmo {"mode":"scale"}` |
| Snap while dragging | Hold Ctrl | `editor.set_gizmo {"snap":true}` |
| Snap to a vertex | Hold V while dragging | `editor.vertex_snap` |
| Drop the selection to the floor | End | `editor.drop_to_floor` |
| Collider handles | C (bare C; Ctrl+C belongs to copy), or **Tools ▸ Collider handles (C)** | `editor.collider_handles` (reads or sets the tool), `editor.collider_handle_drag` |
| Align new placements to the surface | **Tools ▸ Align to surface** | `editor.placement_options` |
| Move an entity exactly | the gizmo, or type in the Inspector | `editor.set_transform` |

## Toolbar and overlays

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Four views | **4 views** | `editor.set_viewport` (layout) |
| Game view (hide editor overlays) | **Game view (G)**, G | `editor.set_viewport` (`game_view`) |
| Render quality of the pane | **Quality: …** | `editor.set_viewport` (quality) |
| Show grid, icons, bounds, outline, proxies, audio ranges, stats | **Show** menu; **View ▸ Grid**, **Selection labels**, **Realtime viewport** | `editor.set_viewport` (show flags), palette commands `view.toggle_grid`, `view.toggle_labels`, `view.toggle_realtime`, `view.toggle_audio_gizmos` |
| Draw the baked navigation mesh | **Show ▸ Navigation** | `editor.set_viewport` (`navigation`) ([Create menu and helpers](book/agents/create-menu.md)) |
| Place a player start, trigger volume, light, camera, audio emitter, decal, post-process volume, spline, nav link or smart object at the focus point | **Create ▸ Player start**, **Trigger volume**, **Point light**, **Spot light**, **Directional light**, **Camera**, **Reflection capture**, **Audio emitter**, **Rect light**, **Tube light**, **Decal**, **Post-process volume**, **Spline**, **Nav link**, **Smart object** (and **Create ▸ Shape**) | `editor.create_entity` ([Create menu and helpers](book/agents/create-menu.md)) |
| Possess the game camera during play | **Possess (F8)**, F8 | `editor.set_viewport` (`possessed`) |
| Debug views and overlays | none in the toolbar | `editor.set_render_override`, `editor.set_scalar_overlay` |
| Look at a capture | none | `editor.capture_viewport`, `editor.viewport_stats` |

The **Icons** flag also draws a player start's flag and a facing arrow on the floor, and every
trigger volume (a sensor collider) as a dashed pink outline (the **Colliders** overlay draws
sensors solid instead).

## Terrain and 2D modes

With the terrain tool on, the viewport paints the heightfield:

| Action | Key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Terrain tool on or off | T (pointer over the viewport) | `terrain.stroke` paints without the tool |
| Brush size smaller / larger | `[` / `]` | `terrain.stroke` `radius` |
| Strength down / up | `-` / `=` | `terrain.stroke` `strength` |
| Brush mode | 0 … 9 | `terrain.stroke` `mode` |
| Previous / next paint layer | `,` / `.` | `terrain.stroke` `layer` |
| Stroke; inverted stroke | left-drag; Shift+left-drag | `terrain.stroke`, `editor.terrain_scatter_brush` |

2D mode ([2D](book/user-guide/2d.md), [Editor 2D mode](book/agents/editor-2d.md)): B turns it on and off;
`,` / `.` step the tile layer and `[` / `]` the terrain set; Shift erases while painting. Agent
methods `editor.mode2d_set`, `editor.mode2d_get`, `editor.tile_stroke`, `editor.tile_stamp`,
`editor.tilemap_save`.

## Keyboard and accessibility notes

Every viewport action with a key above is reachable without the mouse except picking a single
entity, box select and the camera's mouse gestures: select from the [Outliner](book/user-guide/editor-guide/outliner.md)
instead (its rows take keyboard focus), and frame with F. Findings and follow-ups are in
[Editor accessibility](book/user-guide/editor-guide/accessibility.md).

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/outliner.md -->
# Outliner

Panel id: `outliner`.

The **Outliner** tab (docked left) is the level's entity tree: every entity by name, children
under their parents. Search it, select from it, rename, reparent by dragging, group, duplicate
and delete. A multi-entity edit is one undo step. Depth: [Editor hierarchy drag and
drop](book/agents/editor-hierarchy.md), [Hierarchy](book/agents/hierarchy.md), [Entity
kinds](book/user-guide/entity-kinds.md).

Delete, Ctrl+D and Ctrl+G act while the pointer is over the Outliner and no text field has
focus; a user shortcut for `outliner.delete`, `outliner.duplicate` or `outliner.group`
(Preferences ▸ Keymap) replaces the built-in key.

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Select | Click a row; Ctrl+click toggles, Shift+click selects a range, Ctrl+Shift+click adds a range | `editor.select`, `editor.get_selection` |
| Select everything | **Select all** | `editor.select` |
| Search | The search field (`kind:<name>`, `kind:none`, `kind:?` filter by kind) | `editor.hierarchy` |
| Group rows by category | **Group by category** | `editor.hierarchy` |
| Rename | Right-click ▸ **Rename…** | `editor.set_property` (the `Name` component) |
| New child | Right-click ▸ **Create empty child** | `editor.spawn` with `parent` |
| Duplicate | Right-click ▸ **Duplicate**, Ctrl+D | `editor.duplicate` |
| Group | Right-click ▸ **Group**, Ctrl+G | `editor.group` |
| Make a prefab of the selection | Right-click ▸ **Create prefab from selection…**, type the file (under `assets/`, ending in `.prefab.ron`), **Create prefab** | `editor.create_prefab` ([Create prefab from selection](book/agents/prefab-create.md)) |
| Reparent | Drag a row onto another row, or onto **Move to root**; hold Alt to drop without keeping the world transform | `editor.reparent` |
| Unparent | Right-click ▸ **Unparent** | `editor.reparent` with a null parent |
| Select a subtree or the children | Right-click ▸ **Select subtree**, **Select children** | `editor.select_hierarchy` |
| Delete | Right-click ▸ **Delete**, Delete | `editor.delete` |
| Undo, redo | Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y | `editor.undo`, `editor.redo` |

The row's ▾ / ▸ button folds a subtree. With the selection made here, the
[Viewport](book/user-guide/editor-guide/viewport.md)'s F frames it and the [Inspector](book/user-guide/editor-guide/inspector.md) edits it, so the whole
select-and-edit loop works from the keyboard. Findings: [Editor accessibility](book/user-guide/editor-guide/accessibility.md).

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/inspector.md -->
# Inspector

Panel id: `inspector`.

The **Inspector** tab (docked right) shows the components of the selection through reflection:
one collapsing section per component, one row per field. Every edit is an undoable property
change. With several entities selected, fields that agree show their value and fields that
differ are marked mixed; an edit sets it on all of them as one undo step. Depth: [Editor
surface](book/agents/editor.md), [Editor § several entities](book/user-guide/editor.md).

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Read the selection's components | the sections | `editor.inspect_selection`, `scene.get_entity` |
| Edit a field | Type or drag in its row; Enter confirms a text field | `editor.set_property` (one entity or `entities`) |
| Move, rotate, scale exactly | The `Transform` section | `editor.set_transform` |
| Add a component | **Add component…**, then search and pick (Up/Down highlight a row; Enter adds it, or the first match when none is highlighted) | `editor.add_component` |
| Remove a component | **✕ Remove** in its section or **Remove …** in its header's right-click menu (one entity), **Remove component** menu (several) | `editor.remove_component` |
| Set an asset field (mesh, material, sound, ...) | Drop an asset from the Content Browser on the field, or pick one with its 🔍 button (search, thumbnails) | `editor.asset_field_choices`, then `editor.set_property` |
| Use the Content Browser's selected asset, clear, show in the Content Browser | **Use selected**, **Clear**, **Browse** beside the field | `editor.asset_field_set` (`from_selection`, or `path`) |
| See whether an asset is shared; give this field its own copy | the link icon and count beside the field; **Make unique** | `editor.asset_referencer_count`, `editor.make_unique` |
| Edit the asset a field uses (data asset, material, physics material) in place | the ▶ arrow before the field: the asset's fields under it; each edit is one undo step; **Save** there or File ▸ **Save all** writes the file | `editor.inspect_asset_inline`, `editor.asset_inline_set`, `editor.save_all` |
| Point an entity field at another entity | **Pick**, then click the entity in the viewport or Outliner (Esc cancels) | `editor.set_property` |
| Edit a curve or gradient field | click its mini graph (or Enter): canvas, key table, **Add key**, presets | `editor.curve_field_edit` |
| Pick a color | click the swatch: RGB, 0-255, HSV, OKLCH, hex, intensity (HDR), swatches, recent | `editor.set_property`, `editor.color_swatches` |
| Pick a color from the screen | the drop button beside the swatch, then click any pixel of the editor window, viewport included (or arrow keys and Enter); Esc or a right click cancels; one undo step for every selected entity | `editor.color_eyedropper` |
| List and map elements | the **+**, **−**, **↑**, **↓** buttons of the field | `editor.set_property` with the whole value |
| Prefab override | **Revert**, **Apply** on an overridden field | `editor.set_variant_override` |
| Undo, redo | Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y (outside text fields) | `editor.undo`, `editor.redo` |

An asset field shows the asset's thumbnail beside its path. While you drag an asset over it, the field is
outlined in the selection color when it takes that asset and in red when it does not; a refused drop changes nothing
and says why under the field (`assets/props/crate.gltf is not a material (material)`). A material field takes
materials, material graphs and material instances; a mesh field takes meshes and the built-in cube, plane and
sphere. Depth: [Inspector asset fields (agents)](book/agents/inspector.md).

Ctrl+F (with the pointer over the Inspector) focuses its search box; Esc clears it. Tab and Shift+Tab move
between its fields; Enter commits a numeric text field, and in the **Add component…** picker adds the highlighted row (Up/Down), or the first match. Findings about its icon buttons and unlabeled checkboxes:
[Editor accessibility](book/user-guide/editor-guide/accessibility.md).

## Finding and keeping fields

| Task | Do | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Find a field | Type in the search box (Ctrl+F): letters in order, not necessarily together (`lgtclr` finds a light's color); matches are highlighted and their components open | `editor.inspect_selection { search }` |
| See only what you changed | **Modified only**: hides fields equal to their default, or to the prefab's value on a prefab instance | `editor.inspect_selection { modified_only }` |
| Keep a field at the top | Right-click its name ▸ **Pin to top** (keyboard: Tab to the name, Shift+F10, Tab to **Pin to top**, Enter); it shows in **Pinned** on every entity with that component (saved for you, not the project) | `editor.inspector_pin` |
| Keep the Inspector on one entity | 🔒 **Lock**; select other entities freely | `editor.inspector_lock` |
| Watch several entities | ⧉ **Open pinned inspector**: a floating Inspector for this entity; open more for others | `editor.inspector_open_pinned` |
| Add a component | **Add component…**, type to search (grouped by category, recent first; grayed entries say why) | `editor.component_types`, `editor.add_component` |

With several entities selected, the search box and **Modified only** filter the rows too (a field counts as modified when
it differs on any selected entity), the reset arrow resets the field on every entity, a linked vector gives every entity
the typed value with its other lanes following that entity's own ratio, and a `@Button` runs on every entity; each of
these is one undo step.

Fields a component marks with `@Category("…")` sit under their own collapsible headers, after the fields without a
category. An entity with many components gets a **Filter components** box above the list.

## Field help

Hover a field label, or reach it with Tab, and press F1 to open the component's manual section.
When no component section exists, F1 opens the Inspector guide. The rendered book navigates to
the section anchor; a source-only installation opens the Markdown page. Agents use
`editor.help_context { field: { component, path }, open: true }`.

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/content-browser.md -->
# Content browser

Panel id: `content`.

The **Content** tab (first tab under the viewport) is the project's `assets/` folder: a folder
tree and a list or thumbnail grid of assets, with search, create, import, validate, rename,
move, delete (after a check of what refers to the asset) and reimport. Drag an asset into the
viewport to place it; double-click opens it in its editor. Depth: [Content
browser](book/agents/content-browser.md), [Editor asset browser](book/agents/editor-asset-browser.md),
[Editor content index](book/agents/editor-content-index.md), [Asset validators](book/agents/asset-validators.md),
[Importing assets](book/user-guide/importing-assets.md), [Import settings panel and mesh viewer overlays](book/agents/import-settings.md).

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Search | The search field | `editor.content_index`, `editor.list_assets` |
| Import files | **Import…** | `editor.import` |
| New material, prefab, level or folder | **New** ▸ Material / Prefab / Level / Folder | `editor.create_asset` |
| List or grid, tile size | **List**, **Grid**, the size slider | `editor.content_view` |
| Validate | **Validate project**; row menu ▸ **Validate…** | `editor.asset_validate` |
| What refers to it, what it costs | Row menu ▸ **Reference graph**, **Size map**, **Audit to CSV** | `editor.asset_graph`, `editor.asset_size_map`, `editor.asset_audit` |
| Rename or move | Row menu ▸ **Rename / Move…** | `editor.rename_asset`, `editor.move_asset` |
| Delete | Row menu ▸ **Delete…** (lists referencers first) | `editor.delete_asset` |
| Reimport | Row menu ▸ **Reimport (forget cache)** | `editor.reimport` |
| Import settings | Row menu ▸ **Import settings…** (images, meshes, sounds): typed fields, **Apply** writes the `.meta` and re-cooks, **Revert** | `editor.import_settings_open`, `editor.import_settings_edit`, `editor.import_settings_apply`, `editor.import_settings_revert`, `editor.import_settings_state`, `editor.set_import_settings` |
| Mesh helpers | Row menu on a `.glb` / `.gltf`: **Add simple collision**, **Generate lightmap UV** (opens the mesh viewer with the atlas), **Build nav preview here**; the same three buttons are in the mesh viewer's Helpers row | `editor.mesh_helper` |
| Mesh overlays | Asset Viewer ▸ **UV0**, **UV1**, **Normals**, **Collision** | `editor.view_asset { overlay }` |
| Content chunk of an asset | Row menu ▸ **Why is this in its chunk?** | `editor.content_chunks_why` |
| Open | Double-click: a level opens in the viewport, a prefab in prefab mode, a material in its editor, a graph in its panel, other assets in the **Asset Viewer** | `level.open` (`editor.open_level` headless), `editor.open_prefab`, `editor.view_asset`, `editor.matgraph_open` |
| Place in the level | Drag into the viewport | `editor.spawn_prefab`, `scene.spawn_primitive` |
| Thumbnails | the grid | `editor.asset_thumbnails`, `editor.thumbnails` |
| Copy path, show in file manager | Row menu ▸ **Copy path**, **Show in file manager** | none (read `path` from `editor.list_assets`) |
| Rescan | **↻** | `editor.content_index` |

The Content tab has no keyboard shortcuts of its own. Its rows and buttons take focus with Tab;
dragging into the viewport has a keyboard-free agent twin but no keyboard twin. Findings:
[Editor accessibility](book/user-guide/editor-guide/accessibility.md).

## Complete a search token

In Search, Tab completes a filter prefix or asset type (for example `type:te` becomes
`type:texture`). The candidate queries appear beside the field; press Tab again to cycle them.
Editing the search starts a new candidate list. Shift+Tab leaves the field. Agents can request
these candidates with `editor.content_index { complete: "type:te" }`.

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/material-graph.md -->
# Material graph

Panel ids: `material` and `material_graph`.

The **Material Graph** tab edits a `.matgraph.ron` as a node canvas: a box per node with a pin
per input, a **Surface** box with the surface outputs (base color, alpha, metallic, roughness,
normal, occlusion, emissive, world position offset), a live preview sphere, and each compile
error shown on the node it belongs to. Material functions (`.matfunc.ron`) and instances
(`.matinst.ron`) open as more tabs in the same panel. The simpler **Material** tab edits a
`.material.ron`'s parameters (base color, metallic, roughness) with a preview. Walk-through:
[Your first material graph](book/tutorials/editor-first-material.md). Depth: [Material graph
editor](book/agents/material-graph-editor.md), [Material graphs](book/agents/material-graph.md),
[Materials](book/user-guide/materials.md).

## Material Graph tab

| Action | Control / gesture / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| New graph | **New** | `editor.matgraph_open` with `create` |
| Open | Type a path, **Open** | `editor.matgraph_open` |
| Save, save as | **Save**, **Save as** (the path field's path) | `editor.matgraph_save` |
| Undo, redo | **Undo**, **Redo**; Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y | `editor.undo`, `editor.redo` |
| Add a node | Right-click the canvas ▸ **Add node** | `editor.matgraph_edit` `add` |
| Connect, disconnect | Drag from an output pin to an input pin; the canvas's wire gestures disconnect | `editor.matgraph_edit` `connect`, `disconnect` |
| Move a node | Drag it (one undo step per drag) | `editor.matgraph_edit` `move` |
| Drive a surface output | Wire into the **Surface** box, or right-click a node ▸ **Drive output** | `editor.matgraph_edit` `output` |
| Duplicate, delete a node | Right-click ▸ **Duplicate**, **Delete** | `editor.matgraph_edit` `add`, `remove` |
| Functions | Right-click ▸ **Collapse into function…**, **Expand inline**, **Open function** | `editor.matgraph_function_collapse`, `editor.matgraph_function_expand`, `editor.matgraph_function_open` |
| Parameters, textures, switches, shading | Side column: edit the block's RON, **Apply** | `editor.matgraph_edit` `params`, `textures`, `switches`, `shading` |
| Compile status | The header shows **compiles** or the error count; click an error row to select its node | `editor.matgraph_state`, `editor.matgraph_compile` |
| Preview | The side column's sphere (needs a GPU) | `editor.matgraph_preview` |
| Instance overrides | **Override**, **Clear override** | `editor.matgraph_instance_set` |
| Tabs | The tab strip; **Close tab** | `editor.matgraph_tabs` |

The runtime twins `material.graph_get`, `material.graph_set` and `material.compile` read and
write graphs without the panel ([Material graphs](book/agents/material-graph.md)).

## Material tab

| Action | Control | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Edit base color, metallic, roughness | The fields | `editor.edit_material` |
| Save | **Save material** | `editor.edit_material` (saves) |
| Undo, redo | **Undo**, **Redo** | `editor.undo`, `editor.redo` |
| Reload | **Reload from disk** | none |

## Keyboard and accessibility notes

The **Nodes** column beside the canvas is the keyboard route (ADR-7383). It lists every node by
name (only the rows in view are drawn, so large graphs stay fast); Tab reaches it. With a row
focused:

| Key | Does | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Up / Down | Focus the previous / next node | none |
| Enter or Space | Select the node and frame it on the canvas | none |
| Ctrl+Shift+A, or **Add node…** | Open the palette: type to filter, Enter adds the first match (or Tab to a kind and press Enter). The node is placed to the right and its first input is wired from the focused node, one undo step | `editor.matgraph_edit` `add`, then `connect` |
| **Connect…** | Type the target node's name (or `Surface` / `Outputs` for the sink) and its input pin; Enter connects | `editor.matgraph_edit` `connect`, `output` |
| Delete, or **Delete node** | Remove the node | `editor.matgraph_edit` `remove` |
| Alt+Left / Right / Up / Down | Move the node 16 units, one undo step per press | `editor.matgraph_edit` `move` |

The buttons act on the last focused row, so Shift+Tab from a row reaches them. An instance tab is
read-only: the list selects and frames only. The canvas is announced as "Material graph canvas, N
nodes". Box select and the wire drag gestures stay mouse-only. Findings: [Editor
accessibility](book/user-guide/editor-guide/accessibility.md).

# Sequencer

Panel ids: `shots` and `seq_curves`.

The editor's sequencer is the **Sequence Curves** tab: pick a `SequencePlayer` and one of its
float or vec3 tracks, edit the curve's keys and tangents, scrub, and open or save the
`.seq.ron`. Its section strip shows the clip, audio, sub-sequence and video tracks as bars you
move and trim. The **Shots** tab edits the camera curves (field of view, roll, focus, aperture)
of the loaded shot sequence. Depth: [Sequencer](book/user-guide/sequencer.md), [Camera shot
sequences](book/user-guide/shot-sequences.md), [Sequence curves panel](book/agents/seq-curve-panel.md),
[Shot panel](book/agents/shot-panel.md), [Sequence player](book/agents/sequence-player.md),
[Take recorder](book/agents/sequence-take-recorder.md).

## Sequence Curves tab

| Action | Control / gesture / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Pick the player and track | **Player**, **Track** | `editor.seq_curve_state` |
| Open, save | **Open**, **Save** | `editor.seq_curve_open`, `editor.seq_curve_save` |
| Add a key | Double-click the curve | `editor.seq_curve_edit` |
| Move a key or a tangent | Drag it; hold Alt to break the tangent | `editor.seq_curve_edit` |
| Key menu | Right-click a key: ease and tangent modes, **Delete key**; on empty space **Zoom to fit** | `editor.seq_curve_edit` |
| Zoom, pan | Scroll (Shift: time only, Ctrl: value only); right- or middle-drag pans | none |
| Move or trim a section | Drag a bar; drag its edge | `editor.seq_section_edit` |

## Shots tab

## Keyboard and accessibility notes

A float or vec3 track shows a **Keys of <track>** list left of the curve, and a section track a
**Sections of <track>** list under the strip (ADR-7383). Rows are named `<track> key <i> at <time>
s` and `<track> section <i> at <time> s, <what it plays>`. With a row focused:

| Key | Does | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Up / Down | Focus the previous / next key or section | none |
| Enter or Space | Select it (the curve and the number row follow) | `editor.seq_curve_state`, `editor.seq_sections_state` |
| Left / Right | Move it one frame (1/fps) earlier / later, one undo step per press | `editor.seq_curve_edit` `move`, `editor.seq_section_edit` `move` |
| Delete | Remove it | `editor.seq_curve_edit` `remove`, `editor.seq_section_edit` `remove` |

The curve and the strip are announced as "Sequence curve, N keys" and "<kind> section strip, N
sections". Tangent handles, trims and scrubbing stay mouse-only (the number row and the agent
methods cover them). Findings: [Editor accessibility](book/user-guide/editor-guide/accessibility.md).

More sequencer authoring (track add and remove, keyframes from the viewport) is on the branch
`lane/sprint-v06-seq-authoring`; this page gains it at the v0.6 integration.

# Profiler

Two floating windows, turned on and off from the **View** menu. **View ▸ Profiler** shows the
frame time, a flame view of the span call tree and the GPU passes, and captures a frame.
**View ▸ Diagnostics** has a **GPU** tab (GPU breadcrumbs and the last crash bundle) and a
**Timeline** tab that records and shows a `.regiatrace`. Depth: [Profiler
(agents)](book/agents/profiler.md), [Editor diagnostics](book/agents/editor-diagnostics.md),
[Profiling and performance tools](book/systems/profiling.md), [Performance
overlay](book/user-guide/performance-overlay.md).

## Profiler window

| Action | Control | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Show or hide | **View ▸ Profiler** | none (the window is UI only; the data is below) |
| Record the call tree | **Record call tree** | `profiler.set_capture` |
| Capture a frame to a file | **Capture** | `profiler.capture` |
| Read a frame's spans | The flame view (hover a span for its name and time) | `profiler.frame` |

## Diagnostics window

| Action | Control | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Show or hide | **View ▸ Diagnostics** | none |
| GPU breadcrumbs | **GPU** tab | `editor.diagnostics` |
| Load the last crash bundle | **Load last crash bundle** | `editor.diagnostics` with `load_crash` |
| Record a trace | **Timeline** tab ▸ **Record**, **Stop recording** | `editor.trace_record` |
| Open the newest trace | **Open newest** | `editor.trace_timeline` |
| Zoom and pan the timeline | **−**, **+**, the **pan** slider | `editor.trace_timeline` |

## Keyboard and accessibility notes

The flame view and the trace timeline are drawn shapes, announced as "Flame view, N spans" and
"Trace timeline, N items in view". Under each is a focusable list (ADR-7383) with what a hover
shows: **Spans** rows read `<name> in <parent>, main thread, <inclusive> ms inclusive, <self> ms
self, <calls> calls` (every span of the call tree, the ones too thin for a bar too), and **Items in
view** rows read `<name>, <lane> lane, frame <n>, <ms> ms` (marks and screenshots name their frame).
Tab reaches the list; Up and Down move through it. The agent twins are `profiler.frame` and
`editor.trace_timeline`. Findings: [Editor accessibility](book/user-guide/editor-guide/accessibility.md).

A dockable profiler panel with frame history and counters is on the branch
`lane/sprint-v06-profiler-panel`; this page gains it at the v0.6 integration.

# Play-in-editor

<!-- index: Play in editor -->

The play toolbar above the dock runs the level inside the editor. Play copies the edit world
into a fresh play world, so nothing you do while playing changes the level; Stop drops the play
world and the edit world is exactly as before. The **Net** tab (panel id `net`, [Net](book/user-guide/editor-guide/net.md)) plays with a listen server or a
dedicated server and several clients. A separate process shown in the dock uses panel id `game_view` ([Game tabs](#game-tabs)). Walk-through: [Your first scene in the editor
§ 5](book/tutorials/editor-first-scene.md#step-5-play-in-the-editor). Depth: [Editor
surface](book/agents/editor.md), [PIE with several clients and net stats](book/agents/pie-net.md),
[Hot reload](book/user-guide/hot-reload.md).

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Play | **▶ Play**, Alt+P (when no session runs and no text field has focus) | `editor.play` |
| Pause | **⏸ Pause** | `editor.pause` (`play.pause` in the play world) |
| Resume | **▶ Resume** while paused | `editor.resume` |
| Step one frame | **⏭ Step** (while paused) | `editor.step` (`frames` for more) |
| Stop | **⏹ Stop**, Escape (when no panel uses Escape) | `editor.stop` |
| Session state | The status text on the toolbar | `editor.play_state` |
| Possess or eject the game camera | **Possess (F8)** in the viewport toolbar, F8 | `editor.set_viewport` (`possessed`) |
| Compile the game and hot-reload it | **⚙ Compile**, Ctrl+Alt+F11 | `editor.code_status` (reads the build state) |
| Static entities that moved | none | `editor.static_move_warnings` |
| Several clients, listen or dedicated server | **Net** tab | `editor.pie_net_config`, `editor.pie_net_run`, `editor.pie_net_state`, `editor.pie_net_clients`, `editor.pie_processes` |
| Show a separate process in a Game tab (pause, step, speed, mute, input, pop out) | **Net** tab ▸ **Show in a Game tab**; in the tab, click or Tab to the picture, Shift+F1 to leave | `editor.pie_process_view` |

While a session runs, the runtime `play.*` methods (`play.wait_until`, `play.expect`,
`play.inject_input`, ...) act on the play world ([Agent protocol](book/user-guide/agent-protocol.md)).

## Keyboard and accessibility notes

Play, Stop and possession have keys; Pause, Resume and Step are focusable toolbar buttons. Before
this guide's review the toolbar had no resume: while paused, **⏸ Pause** stayed enabled and did
nothing and **▶ Play** started a new session. The toolbar now shows **▶ Resume** while paused
([Editor accessibility](book/user-guide/editor-guide/accessibility.md), finding E-1).

The separate play window is [Play window](book/user-guide/editor-guide/play-window.md). Several clients are [Net](book/user-guide/editor-guide/net.md).

## Game tabs

With **Separate processes** checked in the Net tab, each running process (the dedicated server and every
client) has a **Show in a Game tab** button. The tab shows that process's pictures with the frame number and the
latency, and a toolbar: **Pause** / **Resume**, **Step** (one frame of game time), **Slower** / **Faster**,
**Mute**, **Pop out** (a client starts again in its own window) and **Stop process**. Every control is a
focusable button or checkbox. Click the picture, or reach it with Tab, to send keys and the mouse to that process
only (Tab and the arrows go to the game too); **Shift+F1** gives the keyboard back to the editor. Closing the tab
leaves the process running. Details: [PIE with several clients and net stats § Game
tabs](book/agents/pie-net.md#game-tabs).

# Project settings

Panel ids: `project_settings` and `preferences`.

The **Project Settings** tab (**Edit ▸ Project settings…**) edits the project's `Regia.toml`
and keeps every key it does not show: name, id, version, build number, organization, the
default level, the platform targets and their quality presets, the content chunk rules, and the
input maps of `config/input.ron`. The **Preferences** tab (**Edit ▸ Preferences…**) holds your
own editor settings and the keymap; it saves as you change it. Chords, scopes and presets are on

## Keyboard and accessibility notes

Every row is a focusable field or button, so the whole tab works from the keyboard. Some
fields' labels are separate widgets rather than the field's own label; see
[Editor accessibility](book/user-guide/editor-guide/accessibility.md).

## Changed project settings

In **Edit ▸ Preferences… ▸ Project Settings**, a dot and bold label mark settings that differ
from a documented default. **Revert** resets one key; **Reset project** or the corresponding
category button resets every supported key in that category, even when search hides some rows.
Each action saves immediately and takes one undo step. Tab and Enter operate both controls.

Hover a key to read its default. Project identity and keys without a documented default remain
visible and are preserved by Reset. The exact defaults and agent parameters are listed in
[Project defaults and revert](book/agents/editor-preferences.md#project-defaults-and-revert-adr-8196).

# Procedural graph

| Inspect a node's data | Node menu ▸ **Inspect (I)**, I | `editor.procgen_table` |

## Keyboard and accessibility notes

Selection, visualize, inspect, bypass, delete, duplicate, copy and paste have keys. The **Nodes**
column left of the palette is the keyboard route for the canvas (ADR-7383): one row per node,
named `<type> #<id>` (only the rows in view are drawn). With a row focused:

| Key | Does | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Up / Down | Focus the previous / next node | none |
| Enter or Space | Select the node and frame it on the canvas | `editor.procgen_state` reads the selection |
| Ctrl+Shift+A, or **Add node…** | Open the palette filtered to types that accept the node's first output: type to filter, Enter adds the first match, wired from that output, one undo step | `procgen.graph_edit` `add_node`, `connect` |
| **Connect…** | Type the output pin (empty: the first), the target (`12`, `#12` or its row name) and the input pin; Enter connects | `procgen.graph_edit` `connect` |
| Delete, or **Delete node** | Remove the focused node (with a row focused, Delete acts on that row, not the selection) | `procgen.graph_edit` `remove_node` |
| Alt+Left / Right / Up / Down | Move the node 16 units, one undo step per press | `procgen.graph_edit` `move` |

The canvas is announced as "Procedural graph canvas, N nodes". Box select stays mouse-only. The

# Logic graph

Panel id: `logic_graph`.

The **Logic Graph** tab edits a `.logic.ron` logic graph: a list of *when event E happens, if condition C holds,
run actions A1, A2, …* rules, drawn as nodes on a canvas. Events sit on the left, conditions in the middle and
actions on the right; a rule is one event node wired through zero or more condition nodes into one or more action
nodes, in the order they run. While the game plays the tab shows which rules fired, matched or were rejected on
the newest tick of a running graph, and that graph's variables. Depth: [Logic graphs (agents)](book/agents/logic-graph.md),
the file format [`docs/formats/logic-ron.md`](docs/formats/logic-ron.md) and spec 102.

## Opening it

The tab sits in the group under the viewport in the default layout; **View ▸ Reset layout** brings it back if you
closed it. An agent brings it forward with `editor.layout_apply {"open": "logic_graph"}`. Double-clicking a
`.logic.ron` in the Content Browser, clicking a `.logic.ron` link in the Output Log or calling `editor.open_asset`
opens the file in the tab and brings the tab forward. The tab has no palette command and no key.

## Walk-through: a door that counts its visitors

1. In the Content Browser, open the folder the graph should live in (for example `assets/logic`) and choose
   **New ▸ Logic graph**. The browser writes an empty graph (`logic_graph-1.logic.ron`, or the next free number),
   selects it and says so in its toast. Rename it if you like (**Rename / Move…** in its context menu). Inside the tab,
   **New…** with a path does the same without the browser: type `assets/logic/door.logic.ron` and click **Create**
   (the file is written on the first **Save**).
2. Double-click the file. The tab opens it; its path shows in the tab's top bar.
3. In the **Palette** on the left, under **Events**, click **Entity event**. An event node appears in the events
   column. Select it: the inspector names the rule (**Rule name**, for example `visit`) and holds its event as RON
   (**Event (RON)**: type `EntityEvent("visit")` and press Enter). The **priority** and **cooldown ticks** fields
   below it set the rule's order among rules on the same event and how often it may run.
4. Under **Conditions**, click **Key** for a condition node, select it and set **Condition (RON)** to `Key("locked")`.
   Its mode buttons switch the node between `leaf`, `all`, `any` and `not`: pick **not** so the rule runs only while
   the door is not locked.
5. Under **Actions**, click **logic::SetBlackboard**. In the inspector add the parameters `key` with the value
   `Literal(String("local/visits"))` and `op` with `Literal(String("increment"))` (**Add parameter**, then type the
   RON binding and press Enter). The `local/visits` variable needs a declaration: an agent adds it with the
   `set_local` operation (see the agent page), as the canvas has no locals editor yet.
6. Wire the rule: drag from the event node's output to the condition's input, then from the condition's output to
   the action's input. Dropping a wire on empty canvas opens **Add and connect**, which adds the node you pick and
   wires it in one step. Right-click a pin to remove its wire; right-click empty canvas for **Add node**; a node's
   menu has **Delete**.
7. The issue list under the canvas names each problem with its code (`dangling_wire`, `unknown_task`,
   `unknown_scope`, `duplicate_name`, `bad_value`, …) and the node it is about; clicking a row selects that node. A
   node with errors shows a warning sign.
8. Click **Save**. The tab writes the canonical `.logic.ron` and, next to it, `door.logic.layout.ron` with the node
   positions (the graph file itself has no positions). A graph with errors is not saved: the top bar says why.
   Re-saving an unchanged graph writes the same bytes.

Every edit is one undo step on the editor's undo stack: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y (and `editor.undo`, `editor.redo`) undo
and redo node adds, wires, inspector edits and node drags in order with your level edits. **New…** and **Open…**
replace the open graph; save it first.

## Wire events to actions

A rule's event is one of the arms in the palette: **Start** (the graph's first tick), **Timer** (every N fixed
steps, with optional jitter), **Blackboard changed** (a watched key was written since the last tick) and **Entity
event** (a named event arrived in the entity's inbox). Sequence markers, input actions and network messages arrive
as entity events named `sequence_marker:<sequence>#<marker>`, `input_action:<action>` and `net_message:<id>`
(see [Integrations](book/agents/logic-graph.md#integrations-phase-3)).

Conditions read three scopes: `local/x` (the graph's own variables), `x` or `entity/x` (the entity's blackboard)
and `world/<board>/x` (a world blackboard the graph declares). A rule with no condition node always runs; two
condition nodes in a row must both hold.

Actions are the built-in `logic::SetBlackboard`, `logic::EmitEvent`, `logic::EnableEntity` and
`logic::DisableEntity`, plus every task the game registers (with the umbrella crate's `logic` feature:
`logic::PlaySequence`, `logic::PlayCue` and, with `lua`, `logic::CallLua`). A rule's actions run in wire order; a
task that is still running holds the chain until a later tick, and a failure stops it.

To run a graph, put it on an entity: the game compiles the file with `LogicGraph::compile` and spawns it with a
`Blackboard` and a `LogicInbox` (the agent page shows the code). Gameplay code, Lua (`regia.emit`) and agents
(`logic.emit`) send it events.

## Debug a running graph

Press Alt+P to play. The **Live** area lists the running graphs (`entity <id>`); pick one to watch. Each rule shows
what it did on the newest tick: **fired** (its actions started), **matched** (its condition held but cooldown or a
busy chain kept it from running), **rejected** (its condition was false) or **failed** (an action failed). The
variable table shows its `local/`, entity and `world/` values. If the running graph is not the open document the
area says **differs from the document**.

**Pause**, **Resume** and **Step** (run one tick, then pause) control the watched graph. A graph runs a whole tick at
a time, so the finest step past one tick is **Step to next fired rule**: it runs until a tick in which a rule fires,
then pauses.

Breakpoints: click the dot in front of a rule's event node (or select any node of the rule and press F9) to pause the
game's graphs that run this file at the end of a tick in which the rule fires; an event node's menu has **Break when
… arrives** for events that come through the inbox. The **Breakpoints** tab lists them: tick a box to enable or
disable one, **Go to** selects its node, ✕ removes it. Breakpoints are yours, not the file's: they are kept in
`.regia/logic_breakpoints.ron` and work in development builds. **Paused at rule …** says which one stopped the graph.

The **Watch** tab pins variables (type `local/n`, `world/gatehouse/alarm` or an entity key and press Enter) and
condition results (a condition node's menu, **Watch this condition**). Values update when the graph pauses; turn on
**Live** to refresh them every frame while it runs. Hovering a condition node's title shows whether it holds now.
While paused, the box under the Live controls evaluates a condition written like the inspector's Condition field,
for example `Compare(key: "local/n", op: Gt, value: 0.0)`. The wires of rules that just fired pulse for half a
second.

The open graph's issues also appear in the editor's **Problems** panel; a row opens the graph at its node.

Saving while the game plays reloads every running graph that uses the file: locals, the inbox and fire counts are
kept by rule name (**kept**), or the graph restarts when its running state cannot carry over (**restarted**). The
line under the picker counts what the last save did; a file that does not compile in the game is **rejected** and
the old graph keeps running.

## Actions

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Create a graph file | Content Browser **New ▸ Logic graph**; the tab's **New…** | `editor.create_asset {"kind": "logic_graph"}`, `editor.logic_open {"create": true}` |
| Open a file | Double click in the Content Browser, an Output Log link, **Open…** | `editor.open_asset`, `editor.logic_open` |
| Add, wire, change, move or remove nodes; select a node | Palette, canvas menus, wire drags, inspector, node drags | `editor.logic_edit` |
| Read the graph, its issues and the live view | The canvas, the issue list, **Live** | `editor.logic_state` |
| Check a graph | The issue list | `editor.logic_validate`, `logic.compile` |
| Save | **Save** | `editor.logic_save` |
| Watch a running graph; pause, resume, step it | **Live** picker, **Pause**, **Resume**, **Step** | `editor.logic_edit {"watch": …, "control": …}` |
| Find a node to add | Palette **Search nodes**, a dropped wire's menu | `editor.logic_palette_search` |
| Declare, rename, retype locals and boards | **Variables** tab | `editor.logic_variables`, `editor.logic_variable_set`, `editor.logic_variable_remove` |
| Breakpoints | Rule dot, F9, event node menu, **Breakpoints** tab | `editor.logic_breakpoint_set`, `editor.logic_breakpoint_list` |
| Step to the next fired rule | **Step to next fired rule** | `editor.logic_edit {"control": "step_to_fire"}` |
| Watch values; evaluate a condition while paused | **Watch** tab, hover, the evaluate box | `editor.logic_watch`, `editor.logic_evaluate` |
| Open the graph at an issue's node | A **Problems** row | `editor.logic_goto_node` |
| Disabled rules | none | `logic.debug` |
| Send an event, read the runtime status, reload | none | `logic.emit`, `logic.status`, `logic.reload`, `logic.control` |
| Undo, redo | Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y | `editor.undo`, `editor.redo` |

## Keyboard

F9 sets or removes the breakpoint of the selected node's rule. Enter in **Search nodes** adds the best match; Enter in
the Variables, Watch and evaluate fields applies them. Tab and Shift+Tab move between controls, and Space or Enter
presses the focused button ([Editor guide](book/user-guide/editor-guide/index.md)).

## Known limits

- Events, conditions and parameter values are edited as RON text in the inspector (no per-field widgets yet).
- Entity variables have no type or default in the Variables tab (the entity's blackboard holds them).
- Disabled rules are set through `logic.debug` only; breakpoints apply in development builds only.
- A graph runs from a prefab through its `LogicGraphRef` component: in prefab edit mode the banner's **New graph for
  this prefab** creates one next to the prefab and attaches it, **Open graph** opens it ([Prefab logic](book/agents/prefab-logic.md)).
  Saving a graph during play reloads a prefab's running copies only when the reference has no `overrides`.
- Without the game's task registry loaded in the editor, an unknown action task is a warning, not an error; the
  game checks it again when it compiles the graph.

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/play-window.md -->
# Play window

Play-in-editor normally shows the game inside the **Viewport** tab. The play window shows it in a
second operating-system window instead, titled `Regia Engine Play`, with no editor overlays and at a
resolution you choose, so you can see the game at a phone or tablet size while the editor stays open.
It is not a dock tab: it is a mode of the play toolbar ([Play-in-editor](book/user-guide/editor-guide/play-in-editor.md)). Depth:
[PIE modes and editor jobs](book/agents/pie-modes.md).

The window needs a window system. A host with none (the headless editor, CI) does not show the
toolbar's play window controls, and `editor.play` with `window: true` answers `play_window_unavailable`.

## Open it

- Click **⧉ Play in window** on the play toolbar. Closing the play window, or pressing **⏹ Stop**,
  ends play; the edit world was never touched.
- Agents call `editor.play` with `{"window": true}` and read the result with `editor.play_state`.

## Walk-through: check a level at phone size

1. Click the **⛶** button next to **⧉ Play in window** (it reads **⛶ Window size** until you pick a
   size) and choose **Phone 9:16 portrait (1080 × 1920)**. The choice is saved in the editor
   preferences as `play.resolution`.
2. Click **⧉ Play in window**. The game opens in the `Regia Engine Play` window. The picture is scaled to
   fit the window with its aspect ratio kept and black bars around it; the game's own window reports
   1080 × 1920, so its UI lays out as on that screen.
3. Click in the window to capture the mouse (the cursor is confined and hidden). A click on a point of
   the picture reaches the same point of the play world; a press or the wheel over the black bars
   reaches nothing. Press **Shift+F1** to release the mouse without stopping play.
4. While the window is open the **Viewport** tab does not draw the play world: it shows a note naming the
   window and its size. The **Outliner** and **Inspector** still show the play world, so you can inspect
   entities as the game runs.
5. Close the window (or press **⏹ Stop**) to end play. The window's size and position are remembered for
   the next one.

To play with two to four local players, open the **Play** menu, then **Players**, and pick a count
while play is stopped. With two or more players the play window shows one pane per player: two side
by side, three as one on top and two below, four in quarters.

## Actions

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Play in the separate window | **⧉ Play in window** (toolbar) | `editor.play` with `window: true` |
| Choose the play resolution | **⛶** menu: a preset or a **Custom** width and height with **Use** | `editor.prefs_set` `play.resolution` (and `play.resolution_width`, `play.resolution_height`); `editor.play` `preset` or `size` for one session |
| Run with no local player | **▶ Simulate** (toolbar, **Play** menu) | `editor.play` with `mode: "simulate"` |
| Choose the local player count | **Play ▸ Players** (1 to 4, only while stopped) | `editor.play` with `players` |
| Copy the play state of the selection back to the level | **⤓ Keep changes** (enabled while a session runs) | `editor.keep_simulation_changes` |
| Release a captured mouse | Shift+F1 in the play window or the possessed viewport | none |
| Stop play and close the window | **⏹ Stop**, Escape in the editor window, or close the play window | `editor.stop` |
| Read the window's state | none | `editor.play_state` (`play_window`: `open`, `size`, `render_size`, `picture`, `panes`, `counters`) |

## Resolution presets

The **⛶** menu lists these presets, in this order, and **Custom**. Each side of a custom size must be
from 16 to 16384 pixels.

| Preset id | Size |
|---|---|
| `window` | the window's own size, no bars |
| `hd_720` | 1280 × 720 |
| `hd_1080` | 1920 × 1080 |
| `phone_9_16_portrait` | 1080 × 1920 |
| `phone_9_19_5_portrait` | 1080 × 2340 |
| `phone_9_19_5_landscape` | 2340 × 1080 |
| `tablet_3_4_portrait` | 1536 × 2048 |
| `tablet_3_4_landscape` | 2048 × 1536 |
| `custom` | `play.resolution_width` × `play.resolution_height` |

A change made in the menu while the window is open applies at once.

## Keyboard

Shift+F1 is the only key the play window handles for itself: it frees a captured mouse and never
reaches the game. Every other key, mouse and wheel event in the play window goes to the play world only,
and the editor window's events never reach the play world. Alt+P (play) and Escape (stop) work in the
editor window as on the [play toolbar](book/user-guide/editor-guide/play-in-editor.md#keyboard-and-accessibility-notes).

## Known limits

- On Wayland a window cannot read or set its own position, so the window system places the play window
  and the remembered position is not used there.
- If the window system refuses to open the window, play goes on in the viewport and
  `editor.play_state` reports the reason in `play_window.error`.
- `editor.play` with `preset` or `size` but without `window: true` is refused
  (`play_resolution_needs_window`): the viewport always renders at its own size.
- The mouse writes one cursor in play pixels; routing the pointer to one player is the game's job
  (gamepads are per player).
- A level or game with no cameras of its own gets a stand-in camera for each local player in split screen;
  a game that authors its own cameras controls how the panes look.

## See also

[PIE modes and editor jobs](book/agents/pie-modes.md) (every `editor.play` option, the preset list,
error reasons), [PIE with several clients and net stats](book/agents/pie-net.md),
[Editor preferences](book/agents/editor-preferences.md), [Play-in-editor](book/user-guide/editor-guide/play-in-editor.md).
