- Only the program the editor started is stopped; a tool that starts children should end them when
  its connection drops.

See also: [Editor guide](book/user-guide/editor-guide/index.md).

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/dcc-feed.md -->
# DCC Feed

Panel id: `dcc_feed`.

The **DCC Feed** tab controls the live scene feed: a content tool (a modeling or animation
application with a feed add-on) streams meshes, transforms and clips into the running editor, where
they appear as ordinary entities marked as feed-owned. When you are happy with the result you
**bake** the items into normal `.glb` assets. The feed is a development channel. The `regia` crate
feature `dcc-feed` is off by default and is not part of a shipping profile. The editor turns on
`regia_agent`'s `dcc-feed-assets` feature, so this tab is in the editor, and the listener stays off
until the project sets `[dcc_feed]` with `enabled = true` in `Regia.toml`.
Depth: [DCC scene feed (agents)](book/agents/dcc-feed.md). Spec: `docs/specs/60-dcc-scene-feed.md`.

## Open it

The tab is part of the default layout (the group under the viewport); **View ▸ Reset layout**
brings it back when closed. An agent uses `editor.layout_apply {"open": "dcc_feed"}`. The command
palette has no `open` command for this tab. In a build without the feed the tab reads "The DCC feed
is not in this build."

## Stream a scene and bake it

1. Turn the feed on in `Regia.toml` with a `[dcc_feed]` section (`enabled = true` and a `listen`
   list; the agent page lists every key). An absent section means off.
2. Open the tab and check **Listening**. The addresses the editor listens on appear under the
   header. If `allow_remote` is on, a warning says the protocol has no TLS: use an SSH tunnel or a
   VPN.
3. Connect the content tool. Over a network transport it needs the token: tick **Show token** to
   read it, or **Rotate token** to replace it.
4. A client whose name is not in `auto_accept` appears under **Sessions** as pending. Press
   **Accept** (tick **Remember this client** first to save its name for next time) or **Reject**. An
   active session has **Disconnect**.
5. Items appear in the **Items** grid: key, kind, state (declared, active, stalled, detached,
   baked or removed), frames applied, and seconds since the last frame. In the Outliner a feed-owned
   entity carries a **FEED** badge (**FEED stalled** or **FEED detached** when its feed stopped).
6. To bake, type a folder under `assets/` in the field beside **Items**. Optionally set **Scale**
   (0 keeps the scale the client sent), **LODs** (0 generates none) and **Collision**. Press **Bake
   all**, or **Bake...** on one item. Skeleton and generic items have no **Bake...** button. Only
   one bake runs at a time. The panel then shows a "Last bake" line with the job's state and its file count.
7. To capture a session, type a path in the first field of the record row (the hint reads
   `take.rfdrec`) and press **Record**, then **Stop**. To play a take back, type its path in the
   second field and press **Replay**; a `done / total` counter shows progress.

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Start or stop listening | **Listening** | `dcc_feed.listen` |
| Read status, sessions, items | the panel | `dcc_feed.status`, `dcc_feed.items` |
| Replace the token | **Rotate token** | `dcc_feed.rotate_token` |
| Accept a pending client | **Accept** | `dcc_feed.accept` |
| Reject or disconnect a session | **Reject**, **Disconnect** | `dcc_feed.disconnect` |
| Bake items to assets | **Bake all**, **Bake...** | `dcc_feed.bake` (`dry_run` plans without writing) |
| Read a bake | the "Last bake" line | `dcc_feed.bake_status` |
| Record a session | **Record**, **Stop** | `dcc_feed.record` |
| Replay a recording | **Replay** | `dcc_feed.replay` |

## Keyboard

The tab has no shortcuts. Its boxes, fields and buttons take focus with Tab.

## Known limits

- A bake replaces the live feed entities with ordinary content that uses the new assets (the
  panel does not offer the agent method's `replace_live: false`).
- Windows has no named pipe yet: use loopback TCP or WebSocket with the token.
- Morph targets, curves, USD and two-way sync are not delivered yet.

See also: [Content browser](book/user-guide/editor-guide/content-browser.md), [Outliner](book/user-guide/editor-guide/outliner.md).

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/content-chunks.md -->
# Content Chunks

Panel id: `content_chunks`.

The **Content Chunks** tab shows how your project's cooked assets split into content chunks
(the base game, DLC and downloadable packs) under the `[cook.chunks.*]` rules in `Regia.toml`. It shows
what the next cook writes, using the same functions the cook uses, so you can check a rule change
before you cook, and ask "why is this asset in this chunk?". Depth: [Content Chunks panel
(agents)](book/agents/content-chunks-panel.md), [Content chunks](book/agents/content-chunks.md).

## Open it

The tab is in the default bottom group (**View ▸ Reset layout** restores a closed one). An agent opens it with
`editor.layout_apply {"open": "content_chunks"}`. It needs an open project that has been cooked: with no project it
shows `content_chunks_no_project`, and with no cooked registry for the platform `content_chunks_no_cook` (cook
first). The first time the tab is drawn it computes its view.

## Walk-through: find out why an asset is in a chunk

1. Open **Content Chunks**. The table lists one row per chunk in mount order with **Chunk**, **Delivery**, **Assets**,
   a size bar and **Requires**.
2. Choose what the bars show with **Disk** (the chunk's pak bytes; 0 until a cook has written the chunk paks) or
   **Memory** (the cooked bytes of its members). The **Platform** box picks the cooked cache; empty means this
   machine's platform. Press **Refresh** after a cook or after you edit the rules.
3. Click a chunk's name. Below the table it lists **Direct assets of `<chunk>`** (the ones its own rule selected), each
   with the selector that picked it, and a collapsible **Size map of `<chunk>`**: its assets, largest first, each with a
   bar relative to the largest and its type. Both lists show at most 100 entries.
4. Click an asset path in either list, or type an `assets/...` path (or an asset id) into **Why is this asset here?** and
   press **Explain** (or Enter). The answer reads `<path> is in chunk <chunk> (<reason>)`, then the rule selector, the chain
   back to a direct asset (`via a <- b`), and the other chunks holding a copy.
5. Under it, **References** lists what the explained asset references and **Referenced by** what references it; an entry in
   another chunk names that chunk. Click any path to walk the graph.
6. Reference problems are listed in yellow under the table; errors among them fail the next cook.

You can also right-click an asset in **Content** and choose **Why is this in its chunk?**: the toast names the chunk and
reason, and this tab holds the details.

The chunk rules themselves (include globs, tags, requires, delivery, priority, **Add chunk**, **Remove rule**) are edited in
the **Project Settings** tab ([Project settings](book/user-guide/editor-guide/project-settings.md)); press **Refresh** here afterwards.

## What is on screen

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Read the chunks and their sizes | the table | `editor.content_chunks_state` |
| Switch the bars between disk and memory | **Disk**, **Memory** | `editor.content_chunks_state` with `show` |
| Pick the platform's cooked cache | **Platform** box | `editor.content_chunks_state` with `platform` |
| Recompute | **Refresh** | `editor.content_chunks_state` with `refresh: true` |
| Select a chunk | Click its name | `editor.content_chunks_state` with `chunk` |
| Size map of a chunk | **Size map of `<chunk>`** | `editor.content_chunks_size_map` |
| Explain an asset | **Explain**, or a path link | `editor.content_chunks_why` |
| References of an asset | **References** list | `editor.content_chunks_references` |
| Change a chunk rule | Project Settings tab | `editor.content_chunks_set_rule` |
| Page and filter the unshipped assets | **Unshipped**: **Filter**, **Previous**, **Next** | `editor.content_chunks_unshipped` |
| Preview a settings change before saving | Project Settings: **Preview chunk assignment** | `editor.content_chunks_preview` |

## Keyboard

Enter in the **Why is this asset here?** box runs **Explain**. Nothing else has a shortcut; the buttons and links are
focusable (Tab, then Space or Enter).

## Known limits

- It reads the cooked asset registry, so it needs a cook first; **Refresh** recomputes the view from the current
  `Regia.toml` rules and that registry.
- **Disk** bars read 0 for a chunk until a cook has written its pak.
- `Platform` must be empty or a short lowercase tag (letters, digits, `_`, `-`); anything else is refused.
- Direct assets, size-map rows, references and referrers each show at most 100 entries. An agent reads more:
  `direct_assets_total` in `editor.content_chunks_state`, `limit` on `editor.content_chunks_size_map`, and the full
  lists of `editor.content_chunks_references`.

## See also

[Project settings](book/user-guide/editor-guide/project-settings.md), [Content browser](book/user-guide/editor-guide/content-browser.md), [Size Map](book/user-guide/editor-guide/size-map.md), [Content Chunks
panel (agents)](book/agents/content-chunks-panel.md), [Content chunks](book/agents/content-chunks.md).

## Missing dependencies stop shipping

A shipped asset's required dependency must have a registry record, a cooked file and a place in
the shipped content. This applies to both chunks and named build profiles, even with cook
validation set to `Warn` or `Off`. `content_dependency_missing` tells you whether the target ID
is unknown, the profile excluded a required target, or its cooked file is missing. The message
and JSON `root_path` show how the shipped root reaches it. Restore the target, fix its reference,
or remove the exclusion, then cook and package again.

`content_registry_invalid` means the registry is unreadable or malformed. Rebuild the cooked
cache; the tools will not replace a corrupt registry with an empty dependency graph. An absent
registry still permits the legacy cache-manifest fallback. `regia assets chunks --json` exposes
`complete` and structured `problems`, so tools can distinguish a diagnostic report from a
complete shipping graph. Reference cycles are allowed and do not count as missing assets.

For a deliberate optional exclusion, keep using the referring asset's `optional_references`
tag with a matching target path glob. This only covers a known target; it cannot make an
unknown ID optional. Field-level optional-reference annotations are not supported. The existing
pak hash checks and unwritten-asset diagnostics remain in place.

## Why each root ships, and dynamic roots

The panel, `regia cook` and `regia package --profile` find their starting points the same way: the
startup level (or a profile's entry levels), every top-level `ui/*.ui.ron`, the procedural bakes of
each level reached, and what those files name. The panel's state lists each root with the reason it
exists, for example `declared_by: "[cook.chunks.base] entry[0]"` or `via: "levels/a.level.ron"`.

A level or texture your game opens by a name it builds at run time (a level-select screen, a random
skin) is named by no file, so nothing finds it. Declare it as a **dynamic root**: add its path or a
glob to the chunk's `entry` list, and to the profile's `include` list. Both then ship it and say
why.

If a file's format has no typed reader (a JSON table, a custom text file), its strings are still
followed, but the report marks it under root coverage as a fallback scan: check that what it names
is what you expect. A level or UI layout that does not parse, or a file that cannot be read, stops
the cook and the package with a `content_root_*` code instead of shipping less.

## Choosing what ships: closure settings

By default every cooked asset ships (`content = "all"`), and an asset no rule selects goes to `base`. With
**closure** content only what the game can reach ships: the startup level, the top-level UI layouts,
what they reference, and the **entry roots** you declare per chunk for content the game loads by a name
it builds at run time. Everything else is listed as **Unshipped**. Both are set in **Project Settings**
under `[cook.chunk_options]` (**Content: all / closure**) and in each chunk rule (**Entry roots**,
comma-separated globs under `assets/`).

### Walk-through: leave old content out on purpose

1. Cook the project, then open **Project Settings**. Set **Content** to **closure**.
2. Press **Preview chunk assignment**. A moment later (it computes on a worker thread) it shows how many
   assets ship and how many do not, each declared root, and the assets whose chunk changes:
   `assets/ui/old_logo.png: base -> unshipped` is the old logo nothing uses any more. That is what you
   want, so leave it.
3. Press **Save**, then **Refresh** in **Content Chunks**. **Unshipped** lists the logo; type `ui/` (or a glob
   such as `ui/*.png`) into **Filter** to find it among many, and use **Next** to page through long lists:
   each page holds 100 paths and the header gives the total. Click a path to see what references it.
4. Changed your mind? **Edit ▸ Undo** puts `Regia.toml` back exactly as it was, comments included.

### Walk-through: a dynamic root that is missing

1. Your wave spawner loads `spawn/wave_01.table` by name. In the preview it is in the **unshipped**
   count, because no file names it.
2. In the `base` rule, type `spawn/**` into **Entry roots** and preview again: it moves from
   `unshipped` to `base`, and the root reads `[cook.chunks.base] entry[0] = spawn/**`.
3. Mistype it as `spwan/**` and preview: the root is red (**matches nothing**) and the preview says
   `will not save: content_chunks_entry_unmatched`. **Save** refuses with the same message and writes
   nothing, so the project never claims a working closure that would ship without the tables. Fix the
   glob and save.

If you edit `Regia.toml` or re-cook while a preview is computing, the preview reads **stale** and is
dropped; press the button again. Without a cook, roots cannot be checked: the save goes through and the
toast says the entry roots were not checked, and the next cook checks them.

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/extensions.md -->
# Extensions

Panel id: `extensions`.

The **Extensions** tab lists the extensions your project can use (versioned bundles of code,
content or tools, described by a `regia-plugin.toml` manifest), shows what each one asks for, and
enables, disables or reloads it. It also hosts the tabs extensions add to the editor. Source
extensions are built (spec `docs/specs/57-plugin-extension-api.md`): Rust and content the project
compiles in. A dynamic extension is a library the editor can reload in a development build. A
shipping player does not load one, and this version has no extension registry or marketplace. The
manifest can carry publisher and licence fields. Depth:
[Extensions (agents)](book/agents/plugins.md), [Hot reload](book/user-guide/hot-reload.md).

**In-process extension code is trusted native code with the editor's full privileges.** The tab
shows a banner saying so; capabilities are a review aid, not a sandbox. Enable an extension only
from a source you trust.

## Open it

The tab is part of the default layout (the group under the viewport); **View ▸ Reset layout**
brings it back when closed. An agent uses `editor.layout_apply {"open": "extensions"}`. The command
palette has no `open` command for this tab.

## Review and enable an extension

1. Open the tab. The left column lists every extension as an id followed by its version, each with a colored dot:
   green is active, red is failed, gray is any other state (hover the dot for the state name).
   With no project open the tab says to open one; with none found it says "(no extensions found)".
2. Click an extension. The right column shows its name, version, state, kind, publisher, license,
   description, **Capabilities** (each one with its grant, or "not granted"), **Dependencies** (and
   what was found for each), what it **Registered**, and its **Diagnostics**.
3. Read the capabilities. For an extension that is available or disabled the button reads
   **Enable**, or **Grant (the missing capabilities) and enable** when it asks for capabilities that are not yet
   granted (`systems` and `settings` are granted implicitly). Press it. For an enabled extension the
   button reads **Disable**.
4. Read the message above the details. Code takes effect at the next start: the message then says
   "Done. Restart the editor to apply it.", and the bottom of the list shows "Restart the editor: N
   code change(s) pending".
5. For an extension the editor loaded as a dynamic library (built with `regia plugin build`),
   **Reload** swaps in the newly built library without a restart and reports "Reloaded (generation
   N)."

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| List extensions | the left column | `plugin.list` |
| Read one extension | click it | `plugin.info` |
| Enable, with grants | **Enable** / **Grant ... and enable** | `plugin.enable` |
| Disable | **Disable** | `plugin.disable` |
| Reload a dynamic extension | **Reload** | `plugin.reload` |
| Dry-run the resolver | none (not in the panel) | `plugin.check` |

`plugin.enable`, `plugin.disable` and `plugin.reload` need the `build` permission when an agent
calls them; the panel runs the same functions for a person.

## Tabs that extensions add

An extension can register an editor panel. While the extension is active, the editor adds a tab
with the title the extension chose, in the group that has focus, and removes it when the extension
is disabled or reloaded away; a tab whose extension is not loaded reads "(this extension is not
loaded)". Such a tab is not stored in a saved layout and has no id for `editor.layout_apply`: it
appears and disappears with the extension. What the tab shows and which keys it handles is up to
the extension.

## Keyboard

The Extensions tab has no shortcuts. List rows, **Enable**, **Disable** and **Reload** take focus
with Tab and press with Enter or Space.

## Known limits

- The tab never runs the dry-run resolver; use `plugin.check` or `regia plugin` on the command
  line.
- **Reload** appears only for a dynamic extension. A source extension reloads with the game's hot
  reload, and a content-only extension remounts by disabling and enabling it.
- Dynamic libraries are for development only: they never load in a shipping player and do not
  exist on Android.

See also: [Editor guide](book/user-guide/editor-guide/index.md).

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/tables.md -->
# Tables

Panel id: `tables`.

The **Tables** tab opens three kinds of gameplay data table from the project's `assets/` folder and edits them:
**Curves** (`.curves.ron`, `.curves.csv`: named curves of keys), **Chooser** (`.chooser.ron`: a table of rows and
columns that picks a result from a context) and **Data** (`.table.ron`, `.table.csv`: typed rows of one struct,
one row per key). Edits change the table in memory with the same library calls as the agent methods; **Save**
writes the file. Depth: [Editor data panels (agents)](book/agents/editor-data-panels.md), [Curve tables
(agents)](book/agents/curve-tables.md), [Choosers (agents)](book/agents/choosers.md), [Data tables
(agents)](book/agents/data-tables.md), [Data tables](book/user-guide/data-tables.md).

## Opening it

The tab sits in the group under the viewport in the default layout; **View ▸ Reset layout** brings it back if you
closed it. An agent brings it forward with `editor.layout_apply {"open": "tables"}`. It has no palette command and no
key.

## Walk-through: tune a curve

1. Type a path under `assets/` (for example `tables/falloff.curves.ron`) in the box and click **Open**. A
   `.curves` file opens on the **Curves** tab, a `.chooser.ron` on **Chooser** and a `.table` file on **Data**.
2. Click a curve in the list to select it. The graph overlays every curve and draws the selected one thicker with
   its keys. Drag a key to move it; double-click empty graph space to add a key on the curve; click a key to
   select it. Right-drag or middle-drag pans the graph and the mouse wheel zooms around the pointer.
3. A selected key shows tangent handles: drag one to change the tangent. Hold Alt to break the tangent so only the
   dragged side moves.
4. With a key selected, type exact **x** and **y** values, click **Auto tangents** to return the tangents to the
   derived ones, or **Delete key**.
5. Use **Add curve** (type a name first), **Rename** and **Delete curve** to manage curves, and the **interp**, **pre** and
   **post** (extrapolation) drop-downs per curve. The **Grid** section lists one column per x value and one row per curve, with a
   **+** to add a key; the CSV box at the bottom (**Replace the table with this CSV**) replaces the whole table.
6. Click **Save**. The title shows a `*` after the path while there are unsaved edits.

## Walk-through: test a chooser

1. Open a `.chooser.ron`. The **Test context** strip has a box per declared input and a **seed** drag value; type a
   value and leave the box to apply it.
2. The panel re-evaluates after every change. The line under the strip reads `row <id> → <result>` (or
   `catch-all → <result>`, or **no result**). In the grid, cells are green when they pass, red when they fail and
   amber when they score, and the selected row is marked blue.
3. Edit the table: the **on** check boxes enable or disable a column or a row, **▲**/**▼** reorder rows, **✕** removes a
   row or a column, the result box edits a row's result as RON, **Add row** adds a row and **Add column** adds a
   column of the chosen kind (the kind list, and for a distance column its influence, maximum distance, **wrap** and
   **drop beyond** settings). The **Options** bar sets the mode, the result type, the catch-all, the **near-best
   band** and **recency**.
4. Click **Save**.

## Walk-through: fix a data table

1. Open a `.table.ron` or `.table.csv`. The line above the grid shows the row type, the row count and where the
   schema came from.
2. Edit a cell as text and leave the box to apply it. A cell with an error is filled red-brown (a warning, amber), and
   hovering it shows the issue; an edit that would add a schema error is refused with the error shown, and the cell
   returns to its stored text.
3. Use **▲**/**▼** to move a row, **✕** to remove one, and type a key and click **Add row** for a new one. Remaining
   problems are listed under the grid.
4. Click **Save**.

## Actions

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Open a table | Path box, **Open** | `editor.tables_panel_open` |
| Read the panel (all three tabs) | The panel | `editor.tables_panel_get` |
| Add, move, delete keys, tangents, curves; paste CSV | The graph, key boxes, curve buttons, CSV box | `editor.tables_panel_curve_edit` |
| Edit chooser cells, rows, columns, options | The grid, **Add row**, **Add column**, **Options** bar | `editor.tables_panel_chooser_edit` |
| Set the chooser's test context and seed | **Test context** strip | `editor.tables_panel_set_context` |
| Edit data cells, rows | The data grid, **Add row** | `editor.tables_panel_data_edit` |
| Undo the last edit of the shown tab | **Undo** | `editor.tables_panel_undo` |
| Save | **Save** | `editor.tables_panel_save` |
| Rename a data row's key, clear a data cell to its default | none (agent only) | `editor.tables_panel_data_edit` (`rename_row`, `clear_cell`) |

## Keyboard

The panel handles no keys of its own. Tab and Shift+Tab move between its controls, and Space or Enter presses the
focused button ([Editor guide](book/user-guide/editor-guide/index.md)). The graph is a pointer canvas: the same curve edits are available from the
**Grid** section and the key boxes, and from `editor.tables_panel_curve_edit`.

## Known limits

- The panel's **Undo** is its own: it keeps 32 steps per open table and does not use Ctrl+Z.
- Edits never write the file until **Save**; each of the three tabs holds one open table at a time.
- A `.csv` table is written back as CSV; a `.table.ron` is written as canonical RON, and its comments are not kept.
- Paths are relative to the project's `assets/` folder.

## See also

[Data tables](book/user-guide/data-tables.md), [Editor data panels (agents)](book/agents/editor-data-panels.md), [Choosers
(agents)](book/agents/choosers.md).

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/abilities.md -->
# Abilities

Panel id: `abilities`.

The **Abilities** tab inspects one entity's gameplay-ability data: its attributes (base value, current value and
how the current value was reached), the effects live on it, and the abilities it has been granted. It reads the
play world while a play session runs and the edit world otherwise, so the same tab shows a level being authored
and a game being played. A collapsible editor at the bottom opens the three ability asset files
(`.attrs.ron`, `.effect.ron`, `.ability.ron`) in a typed form with validation. Depth: [Abilities
(agents)](book/agents/abilities.md), [Editor gameplay data panels](book/agents/editor-data-panels.md),
[Gameplay](book/user-guide/gameplay.md).

## Opening it

The tab sits in the group under the viewport in the default layout; **View ▸ Reset layout** brings it back if you
closed it. An agent brings it forward with `editor.layout_apply {"open": "abilities"}`. The panel has no palette
command and no key.

## Walk-through: give an entity an attribute set and apply an effect

1. Select an entity in the Outliner. With **follow selection** chosen in the entity picker the panel inspects
   it; pick an entity from the same picker to pin it instead.
2. Type an attribute set's path under `assets/` (for example `attrs/hero.attrs.ron`) in the box under the
   attributes and click **Add attributes**. The attributes grid appears with a **name**, **base**, **current**
   and **range** column.
3. Drag a **base** value to change it. Hover the **current** value to read its breakdown (the base, each
   modifier's contribution, clamping). A derived attribute's base is not editable.
4. Open the **effect…** drop-down, pick an effect asset and click **Apply effect**. It appears under **Live
   effects** with its level, stack count, remaining ticks and a suspended mark when suspended; **Remove** takes it off.
5. Pick an ability in the **ability…** drop-down and click **Grant**. It appears under **Abilities** with its state
   (ready, running, ending or cooling) in color. **Revoke** takes it away.
6. Press Alt+P to play. The tab now shows the play world: **Start** runs a granted ability.

In the edit world, **Add attributes** and **Apply effect** are one undo step each (Ctrl+Z puts the entity's
attributes, effects, grants and counted tags back). Operations in the play world are not undoable: the play world is
thrown away at Stop.

## Actions

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Pin an entity, or follow the selection | Entity drop-down (**follow selection** or a listed entity) | `editor.abilities_panel_select` |
| Draw the state rings in the viewport | **Overlay** check box | `editor.abilities_panel_select` (`overlay`) |
| Read what the panel shows | The panel | `editor.abilities_panel_get` |
| Change an attribute's base | The **base** drag value | `editor.abilities_panel_call` (`set_base`) |
| Add an attribute set | **Add attributes** | `editor.abilities_panel_call` (`add_attributes`) |
| Apply an effect | **Apply effect** | `editor.abilities_panel_call` (`apply_effect`) |
| Remove a live effect | **Remove** | `editor.abilities_panel_call` (`remove_effect`) |
| Grant an ability | **Grant** | `editor.abilities_panel_call` (`grant`) |
| Revoke a grant | **Revoke** | `editor.abilities_panel_call` (`revoke`) |
| Start a granted ability (play only) | **Start** | `editor.abilities_panel_call` (`activate`) |
| Open, edit and save an asset file | **Asset** section: **Open**, the form, **Save** | `editor.abilities_panel_asset` |
| Show the raw text instead of the form | **Advanced (raw text)** | none (view only) |

## The asset editor

Open the **Asset (.attrs / .effect / .ability)** section, type a path under `assets/`
(for example `effects/burn.effect.ron`) and click **Open**. The file is checked as you edit:

- The typed form has one row per top-level field of the asset, with nested records and lists under it. Numbers
  are drag values, booleans are check boxes, an enum has a variant picker and a list has **Add entry** and
  **Remove entry**. A validation message appears beside the field it names; messages about the whole asset and parse
  errors (with a line and column) appear under the form.
- `format_version` is shown but not edited in the form.
- **Advanced (raw text)** shows the text itself (it is also shown while the text does not parse).
- The title shows the path with a `*` while there are unsaved changes. **Save** is enabled only when the text
  differs from the saved file and validation finds no error, and it writes the file atomically.
- A typed edit writes the format's canonical text, which drops RON comments. A banner above the form warns about
  this before your first typed edit of a file that has comments; edit in **Advanced** to keep them.

## Keyboard

The panel handles no keys of its own. Tab and Shift+Tab move between its controls; the global keys (Ctrl+Z,
Ctrl+Y, Alt+P) work as everywhere ([Editor guide](book/user-guide/editor-guide/index.md)).

## Known limits

- The entity list shows at most 256 entities (in id order).
- **Start** works only while playing (it is disabled in the edit world); the tab reads "no ability plugin in this
  world" when the world does not run the ability plugin.
- Play-world entity ids differ from edit-world ids, so the pin is dropped when a play session starts.
- Edits to a base value while playing change the play world only.

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/problems.md -->
# Problems

Panel id: `problems`.

The **Problems** tab lists what the asset validators found: a missing reference, a bad name, a
texture over its size limit, an orphaned asset, and the rules of the project's
`config/validation.ron`. It is the one list a validation run, a level save and an agent all fill.
Clicking a row selects the asset in the Content tab. The panel never changes content. Depth: [Asset
validators and the dependency graph (agents)](book/agents/asset-validators.md).

## Open it

The tab is in the default bottom group (**View ▸ Reset layout** restores a closed one); an agent
opens it with `editor.layout_apply {"open": "problems"}`. Validation reads the editor's loaded
asset registry, so cook the project first (`registry_not_loaded: cook the project first` appears
in red otherwise). Before any run it says "Nothing validated yet: use Validate in the Content
Browser, or Re-run."

## Walk-through: clean up a folder

1. In the **Content** tab, right-click a folder or asset and choose **Validate** (just that
   path) or **Validate with dependencies** (it and everything it reaches), or press the **Validate
   project** button in the Content tab's header.
2. Open **Problems**. The line under the toolbar reads `N passed, N failed, N with warnings, N not
   validated`. Rows follow, worst first (error, warning, info) and each reads `<severity> <code>
   <asset>: <text>`.
3. Hover a row for the validator's hint, when it has one.
4. Narrow the list: untick **error**, **warning** or **info** to hide a severity, or pick one
   validator in the drop-down (it lists the validators that have findings).
5. Click a row. The Content tab opens that asset's folder and selects it.
6. Fix the asset, cook, and press **Re-run**. It repeats the last scope (the whole project the first
   time).

Saving a level also queues a validation of what changed; its report fills this tab too, unless
`validate_on_save` is false in `config/validation.ron` ([the agents page](book/agents/asset-validators.md)
has the rule file).

## What is on screen

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Validate a path, a path with its dependencies, the whole project | Content tab right-click menu ▸ **Validate**, **Validate with dependencies**; header button **Validate project** | `editor.problems_panel` with `run: true` (and `assets`), or `editor.asset_validate` |
| Repeat the last run | **Re-run** | `editor.problems_panel` with `run: true` |
| Hide or show a severity | The **error**, **warning**, **info** checkboxes | `editor.problems_panel` with `hide` |
| One validator only | The validator drop-down (**all validators** shows all) | `editor.problems_panel` with `validator` |
| Select the asset of a row | Click the row | `editor.problems_panel` with `select` |
| Read the whole panel | the tab | `editor.asset_panels_state` |
| Control the validate-on-save trigger | none | `editor.save_validation` |

The list lays out only the rows in view, so a project-wide run with tens of thousands of findings
stays responsive.

## Keyboard

None of its own. The checkboxes, the drop-down and **Re-run** are focusable (Tab, then Space or
Enter); each row is a selectable label.

## Known limits

- Needs a cooked registry; findings are about the registry's assets and the project's `.ui.ron`
  layouts, not about uncooked edits.
- A `config/validation.ron` that does not load is reported as an error and the run does not start.
- The panel shows findings; it does not fix them.

## See also

[Reference Graph](book/user-guide/editor-guide/reference-graph.md), [Size Map](book/user-guide/editor-guide/size-map.md), [Content
browser](book/user-guide/editor-guide/content-browser.md), [Asset validators and the dependency graph
(agents)](book/agents/asset-validators.md).

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/reference-graph.md -->
# Reference Graph

Panel id: `reference_graph`.

The **Reference Graph** tab answers "what uses this asset, and what does it use?" as columns:
the assets that refer to it on the left (referrers), the asset itself in the middle, and what it
refers to on the right (dependencies), one column per hop. Use it before you delete, move or
rename an asset, and to find out why something ends up in a cook. The panel only reads; it never
changes content. Depth: [Asset validators and the dependency graph
(agents)](book/agents/asset-validators.md), [Content browser](book/user-guide/editor-guide/content-browser.md).

## Open it

The tab is part of the default bottom group (**View ▸ Reset layout** brings it back when closed).
An agent opens it with `editor.layout_apply {"open": "reference_graph"}`. The panel reads the
editor's loaded asset registry, so cook the project first; without one it says
`registry_not_loaded: cook the project first` in red. A fresh panel shows "Use Reference graph in
the Content Browser."

## Walk-through: why is this texture in my level?

1. In the **Content** tab, right-click the texture and choose **Reference
   graph**. The Reference Graph tab fills with the asset in the **selection** column.
2. Read the **referrers 1** column on the left: the assets that name the texture directly.
3. Raise the **referrers** value (0 to 8) to follow the chain further back, for example from a
   material to a mesh to a scene. A column holds the assets first reached at that hop.
4. Click any asset name to **re-center** the graph on it. The Content tab also selects that asset
   and opens its folder.
5. Use **<** and **>** to step back and forward through the graphs you have shown.
6. Click **Open size map** to see what the selection costs in bytes ([Size
   Map](book/user-guide/editor-guide/size-map.md)).

## What is on screen

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Show the graph of an asset | Content tab right-click menu ▸ **Reference graph** | `editor.reference_graph_panel` with `action: "open"` and `asset` |
| Re-center on another asset | Click a name (its hover text says "re-center here") | `editor.reference_graph_panel` with `action: "recenter"` |
| Back, forward | **<**, **>** (grayed out when there is no earlier or later graph) | `action: "back"`, `action: "forward"` |
| How many hops of referrers or dependencies | The **referrers** and **dependencies** drag values, 0 to 8 (default 1 each) | `action: "depth"` with `side` and `depth` |
| How many assets per column | The **width** drag value, 1 to 500 (default 50) | `action: "width"` with `width` |
| Filter by asset type | The **types:** chips (one per type present; with none chosen every type shows) | `action: "kind"` with `kind` |
| Show the rest of a long column | The **N more** button under a column; the last chunk wraps to the first | `action: "more"` with `side` and `hop` |
| Open the size map of the same assets | **Open size map** | `action: "open_size_map"` |
| Read the whole panel | the tab | `editor.asset_panels_state` |

Assets that the selection names but that are not in the registry are listed under **missing:**
below the columns. Reading the same graph without the panel, or with several roots, is
`editor.asset_graph` with `assets`.

## Keyboard

The panel has no shortcuts of its own. Every button, drag value and name is a focusable widget:
Tab moves between them and Enter or Space presses the focused one.

## Known limits

- It needs a cooked registry. Changes you have not cooked are not in it.
- A graph is capped by the width setting: only the assets listed in a column are followed to the
  next hop, so raise **width** or page with **more** to follow a long column.

## See also

[Size Map](book/user-guide/editor-guide/size-map.md), [Problems](book/user-guide/editor-guide/problems.md), [Content browser](book/user-guide/editor-guide/content-browser.md), [Asset
validators and the dependency graph (agents)](book/agents/asset-validators.md).

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/size-map.md -->
# Size Map

Panel id: `size_map`.

The **Size Map** tab draws what an asset, or a set of assets, costs: every asset the selection
reaches is a rectangle in a treemap whose area is its cooked size. Use it to find the one
texture that makes a level heavy, and to see how many bytes deleting the selection would free. The
panel only reads. Depth: [Asset validators and the dependency graph
(agents)](book/agents/asset-validators.md).

## Open it

The tab is in the default bottom group (**View ▸ Reset layout** restores a closed one); an agent
opens it with `editor.layout_apply {"open": "size_map"}`. It needs the loaded asset registry, so
cook the project first. A fresh panel reads "Use Size map in the Content Browser or in the
Reference graph."

## Walk-through: what makes this level heavy?

1. In the **Content** tab, right-click the level and choose **Size map**. The tab fills in.
2. The line at the top reads `N assets, <total> in total, <shared> shared, <exclusive> exclusive`.
   *Total* counts every reached asset once. *Exclusive* is what removing the selection would free;
   *shared* is what other assets still use.
3. Each rectangle's area is proportional to its size, so the biggest asset is the biggest
   rectangle. Names are drawn on rectangles wide and tall enough to hold them.
4. Hover a rectangle: the tooltip shows the full name, its size with its share of the total in
   percent, and its exclusive size.
5. To go from a big rectangle to the assets that pull it in, right-click it in the Content tab
   and choose **Reference graph** ([Reference Graph](book/user-guide/editor-guide/reference-graph.md)).

## What is on screen

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Show the size map of an asset | Content tab right-click menu ▸ **Size map**; or **Open size map** in the Reference Graph tab | `editor.size_map_panel` with `assets` |
| Read a rectangle | Hover it | `editor.size_map_panel` with `hover: [x, y]` (and `area: [w, h]` for the layout size) |
| Group rows by asset, kind, folder or tag | none in the panel (it groups by asset; at most 200 asset rows, the rest fold into one `(other)` row) | `editor.size_map_panel` with `group_by` and `top` |
| Write the numbers to a file | Content tab right-click menu ▸ **Audit to CSV** (writes `.regia/audit/<path>.csv`) | `editor.asset_audit` |
| Read the whole panel | the tab | `editor.asset_panels_state` |

## Keyboard

None. The treemap is a hover view; there is no focusable item per rectangle, so use the agent
method or the CSV for a text form of the same numbers.

## Known limits

- It needs a cooked registry; sizes come from the registry.
- The panel does not offer a grouping control; the grouping and `top` choices are agent-only.
- A rectangle's label is hidden when it is too small; hover reads it.

## See also

[Reference Graph](book/user-guide/editor-guide/reference-graph.md), [Problems](book/user-guide/editor-guide/problems.md), [Content
browser](book/user-guide/editor-guide/content-browser.md), [Asset validators and the dependency graph
(agents)](book/agents/asset-validators.md).

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/layers.md -->
# Layers

Panel id: `layers`.

The **Layers** tab works with the data layers of the open level: named groups of entities (night
props, a quest's actors) that a game switches together. In the editor you show, hide, load and
unload a layer to work on one group at a time, choose which layers new entities join, add the
selection to a layer, define and bind layers, and edit a placed level (a saved level placed inside
this one) on its own. Depth: [Levels: per-entity files, data layers and placed
levels](book/agents/levels-layers-instances.md).

## Open it

The tab is in the default bottom group (**View ▸ Reset layout** restores a closed one). An agent
opens it with `editor.layout_apply {"open": "layers"}`. With no layer bound by the level the table
says "This level binds no layers."

## Walk-through: work on one layer

1. Open **Layer definitions** and press **Bind** next to a `.layers.ron` file of the project to bind it to the
   open level. If there is none, type a **file** (relative to `assets/`) and a **name** and press **Create layer**;
   tick **Editor only** for a layer that is absent in play.
2. The table lists each layer with columns **layer**, **visible**, **loaded**, **current**, **initial** and
   **members**. Untick **visible** to hide a layer's members (the layer is parked: still there, hidden, not
   simulated). Untick **loaded** to remove them from the world (the layer is absent). Tick **loaded** again to bring
   them back parked, and **visible** to show them.
3. Select entities and press **add selection** or **remove selection** on a layer's row. This is one undo step.
4. Tick **current** on a layer: while the current set is not empty, entities you place join it. The line above the
   table reads `New entities join: <names>`; **clear** empties the set.
5. Pick the layer's state at load time in the **initial** drop-down (`absent`, `parked` or `live`). This one is saved
   with the level (one undo step, written on the next save); the **visible** and **loaded** ticks are not.
6. Press Play: the session starts from the **initial** states again, whatever you toggled.

The **visible**, **loaded** and **current** toggles are a working state: they change no file and not the level's
initial states.

## Placed levels

Under the toolbar, a **Create placed level** section moves the selected entities into a new level file at
`assets/<path>`, picking a pivot (**lowest center**, **center**, or **primary selection**), and puts one instance in
their place (**Create from selection**). With a placed-level instance selected, the tab shows `Placed level <name>`
with **Edit placed level** and **Break placed level**. Editing opens that level on its own with a banner `Editing
placed level <path>`; **Commit** saves it and reopens the host, **Discard** reopens the host unchanged. Breaking
replaces the instance with ordinary entities.

## What is on screen

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Show or hide a layer | **visible** checkbox | `editor.layers_panel_set` with `layer` and `visible` |
| Load or unload a layer | **loaded** checkbox | `editor.layers_panel_set` with `layer` and `loaded` |
| Set the layers new entities join | **current** checkboxes, **clear** | `editor.layers_panel_set` with `current` |
| Add or remove the selection | **add selection**, **remove selection** | `editor.layers_panel_set` with `add_selection`, `remove_selection` |
| Initial state at load | **initial** drop-down | `editor.layer_initial` |
| Create a layer (and its file) | **Create layer**, **Editor only** | `editor.layer_create` |
| Bind or unbind a definition file | **Bind**, **Unbind** | `editor.layer_bind` |
| Delete a layer | **Delete layer** | `editor.layer_delete` |
| Rescan `.layers.ron` files | **Refresh** | none (view only) |
| Create a placed level | **Create from selection** | `editor.placed_create` |
| Edit a placed level on its own | **Edit placed level**, **Commit**, **Discard** | `editor.placed_edit` |
| Break a placed level | **Break placed level** | `editor.break_placed` |
| Read the tab | the tab | `editor.layers_panel_state` |

The run-time view of the same layers is `level.layers` and `level.set_layer_state`.

## Keyboard

None of its own. Checkboxes, drop-downs and buttons are focusable (Tab, then Space or Enter).

## Known limits

- **Create layer** and **Delete layer** rewrite the definition file directly and are not undo steps; deleting a
  layer is refused while a level that binds it has members in it (the error line names the reason).
- Editing a placed level needs a saved host level (the host is closed during the session, not dimmed).
- The table lists at most 100 layer findings (yellow lines) and then says how many more there are; an agent's
  `editor.layers_panel_state` has them all.
- Errors from an action show on a red line at the top of the tab.

## See also

[Outliner](book/user-guide/editor-guide/outliner.md) (the row menu has the same placed-level items), [Problems](book/user-guide/editor-guide/problems.md), [Levels: per-entity
files, data layers and placed levels](book/agents/levels-layers-instances.md).

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/tests.md -->
# Tests

<!-- index: Functional test -->

Panel id: `tests`. The **Tests** tab lists the functional tests placed in the open level, runs them inside
play-in-editor, and shows each test's verdict and step-by-step report. A functional test is an
entity with a `FunctionalTest` component whose body (a script or Rust code) plays the game and
checks the outcome, so a level carries its own gameplay checks. The tab is the human view of
the same run an agent starts with `editor.tests_panel_run`. Spec: `docs/specs/41-functional-tests-and-session-harness.md`. Depth: [Functional tests (agents)](book/agents/functional-tests.md).

## Open it

The tab is in the default bottom group (**View ▸ Reset layout** restores a closed one). An agent
opens it with `editor.layout_apply {"open": "tests"}`. It lists the tests of the open level; with
no test placed the table is empty.

## Walk-through: run the level's tests

1. Open the level and press **Refresh** to read its tests. Each row shows a checkbox, the test's
   name (hover it for its description), its tags, its owner, and its last verdict.
2. Tick the tests you want, or leave every box clear to run all. The run button reads **Run all**
   when none is ticked and **Run selected** otherwise. A disabled test cannot be ticked and shows
   `disabled` as its verdict; disabled tests are skipped.
3. Press **Run all** or **Run selected**. When play is stopped, the editor starts play first and the status text
   reads `N test(s) queued`, then `running`. The button is grayed out while a run is in progress.
4. When the run ends, the status text shows the counts (for example `2 passed, 1 failed`) and each row's
   **last** column shows its verdict.
5. Under the table, one collapsible section per test shows its verdict, its message, each step with its verdict and
   frame count, and the message of each pass.
6. Click a test's name to select its placed entity (open the Inspector or Outliner to edit it). With the viewport's **Bounds and ranges** show
   option on, a placed test is drawn as a green box with its name and a line to its viewpoint.

## What is on screen

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Re-read the level's tests | **Refresh** | `editor.tests_panel_state` (reads them fresh) |
| Choose tests to run | The checkboxes | `editor.tests_panel_run` with `tests` |
| Run (starting play if needed) | **Run all** / **Run selected** | `editor.tests_panel_run` |
| Read the list, verdicts, status and report | the tab | `editor.tests_panel_state` |
| Select a test's placed entity | Click the test's name | `editor.tests_panel_open` with `test` |
| Place a test or run one without the panel | none | `functest.create`, `functest.run`, `functest.status`, `functest.results` |

An agent polls `editor.tests_panel_state` for the report after `editor.tests_panel_run`.

## Keyboard

None of its own. The buttons and checkboxes are focusable (Tab, then Space or Enter).

## Known limits

- A run needs a play session whose app has the functional-test runner; otherwise the status reads
  `no_runner: this play session has no functional-test runner`.
- If you stop play while a run is going, the run is gone with its world and the status reads `play stopped before
  the run ended`.
- Running nothing is not a pass: with no enabled test selected the run is refused (`no_tests`), and a second run is
  refused while one is in progress (`already_running`).
- Errors from an agent call: `no_tests`, `already_running`, `test_not_found` (an unknown name in `tests` or `test`),
  `bad_params`.
- Command-line runs (`regia test`) are described on the agents page.

## See also

[Play-in-editor](book/user-guide/editor-guide/play-in-editor.md), [Functional tests (agents)](book/agents/functional-tests.md), [Layers](book/user-guide/editor-guide/layers.md).

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/state-trees.md -->
# State trees

Panel ids: `state_trees` and `state_tree_editor`.

Two tabs work with state trees, the hierarchical decision model of the AI system (`.statetree.ron` files).
**State Tree Editor** authors a tree: a node view of its states and transitions, a palette, an inspector for the
selected state and a live list of problems. **State Trees** debugs the trees that run in the game: which state is
active, which transitions hold, the blackboard and the recent trace. Depth: [State tree editor
(agents)](book/agents/state-tree-editor.md), [State trees (agents)](book/agents/state-tree.md), [Editor gameplay
panels](book/agents/editor-gameplay-panels.md).

## Opening them

Both tabs sit in the group under the viewport in the default layout; **View ▸ Reset layout** brings back a
closed one. An agent brings one forward with `editor.layout_apply {"open": "state_tree_editor"}` or
`{"open": "state_trees"}`. Neither has a palette command or a key.

## Walk-through: author a small tree

1. Open **State Tree Editor**. Click **New** for a tree with a root state named `Root`, or type a path such as
   `assets/ai/guard.statetree.ron` in the box and click **Open**.
2. In the **Palette**, type a name in **new state** and click **Add under Root** (the button names the selected state,
   or the root when none is selected). Do the same for a second state.
3. Click a state in the **Node view** to select it. The **Inspector** shows its name (**Rename**), **Parent**,
   **Selection** (First, Utility or Weighted), tasks, parameters, transitions and the enter condition. Conditions
   are typed as RON text and applied with **Apply**.
4. With a state selected the palette offers **New transition from** that state: choose a trigger and a target and
   click **Add transition**. The transition is drawn as an arrow in the node view.
5. Watch the toolbar: it says **valid** or **N error(s)**. Every problem is listed under **Problems**; a state with an
   error is outlined red in the node view, and clicking a problem selects its state.
6. Click **Save** (it is disabled while there are errors; **Save as** writes to the path in the box).
7. Press Alt+P. The **Play** section lists the agents whose `StateTreeSource` names the open file; pick one in
   **Agent** and the node view fills the active path green. Saving reloads the file into those agents.

Every edit is one undo step; **Undo** and **Redo** on the toolbar (their hover text names the step) and Ctrl+Z
and Ctrl+Y use the editor's undo stack. **New** and **Open** refuse the first time when the open tree has unsaved
changes and say so; press again to discard them.

## Walk-through: debug a running tree

1. Press Alt+P. **State Trees** lists every entity with a `StateTree` in the world it shows, one line per tree:
   name, status (`not_started`, `running`, `succeeded` or `failed`), `paused` when paused, the active path and the
   tick count. With no tree it says so and reminds you that trees run in play.
2. Click a tree. **Pause** (or **Resume** while paused), **Restart**, and **Send event** (type an event name first)
   steer it.
3. Under **States and transitions** the active states are green and bold; each transition line reads `-> target on
   trigger`, with its condition, priority and hold time, amber while it holds and blue once taken (with the tick).
4. **Blackboard** shows the entity's blackboard (or says it has none); **Trace** shows the recent trace newest first.

## Actions

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Start a new tree, open a file | **New**, path box and **Open** (State Tree Editor) | `editor.statetree_open` |
| Edit states, transitions, tasks, includes, tree fields | Node view, Palette, Inspector, **Tree: fields, ambient tasks, includes** | `editor.statetree_edit` |
| Read the document and its problems | The node view and **Problems** | `editor.statetree_state` |
| Save | **Save**, **Save as** | `editor.statetree_save` |
| Undo, redo | **Undo**, **Redo**, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y | `editor.undo`, `editor.redo` |
| Read the debugger | State Trees tab | `editor.state_tree_panel_get` |
| Choose the tree shown in detail | Click a tree in the list | `editor.state_tree_panel_select` |
| Pause, resume, restart, send an event | **Pause**/**Resume**, **Restart**, **Send event** | `editor.state_tree_panel_control` (`pause`, `resume`, `restart`, `send_event`) |
| Skip a state, pause when one is entered | **skip**, **pause on enter** check boxes (development builds only) | `editor.state_tree_panel_control` (`debug`) |
| Reload a tree from a file | none in the panel | `editor.state_tree_panel_control` (`reload`) |

## Keyboard

Neither panel handles keys of its own. Tab and Shift+Tab move between controls and Space or Enter presses the
focused button; the global keys work as everywhere ([Editor guide](book/user-guide/editor-guide/index.md)). The node view is a drawn canvas
operated by pointer click only; the same edits are available from the keyboard through the Inspector, the Palette
and the Problems list, and the agent route is `editor.statetree_edit`.

## Known limits

- State Trees only shows trees that exist in the world it reads (the play world while a session runs, else the edit
  world), up to 512 trees.
- The **skip** and **pause on enter** switches exist only in development (debug) builds of the editor.
- A tree with validation errors is not saved: fix the errors first.
- Including another tree adds its states under a prefix; list the included root under a state with **List under**
  in the **Tree** section to reach it.

## See also

[Editor gameplay panels](book/agents/editor-gameplay-panels.md), [Navigation and AI](book/user-guide/navigation-ai.md), [Behavior
tree](book/user-guide/editor-guide/behavior-tree.md).

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/audio-mixer.md -->
# Audio mixer

Panel id: `audio_mixer`.

The **Audio Mixer** tab shows the audio bus tree with a fader, a mute and a solo button per bus, and live meters
(peak, RMS and short-term loudness per bus, plus the loudness of the whole output) while the game plays in the
editor. Use it to balance music, effects and voice against each other and to see which bus is loud, without
editing a file. Depth: [Audio mixer (agents)](book/agents/audio-mixer.md), [Audio](book/user-guide/audio.md),
[Loudness](book/user-guide/loudness.md).

## Opening it

The tab sits in the group under the viewport in the default layout; **View ▸ Reset layout** brings it back if you
closed it. An agent brings it forward with `editor.layout_apply {"open": "audio_mixer"}`. It has no palette command
and no key.

## Walk-through: balance a bus while playing

1. Press Alt+P to play. The line at the top reads **Meters: play**; before play it reads **Meters: none** with a
   reminder to press Play, or **Meters: edit** when the edit world has an audio engine.
2. Find the bus in the tree (children are indented under their parent). Drag its slider, which runs from -80 to
   +6 dB, to change its fader. The three bars under the bus (**peak**, **rms**, **LUFS**) show its level; they turn
   amber above -9 dB and red above -1 dB.
3. Click **M** to mute the bus. Click **S** to solo it: with any bus soloed, only the soloed buses, their
   ancestors and their descendants sound, and a bus silenced only by a solo is marked **(solo)**. A mute still wins.
4. The **Program** rows show the loudness of the whole output: **M** (momentary), **S** (short-term), **I**
   (integrated) and **TP** (true peak) as bars, the loudness range (LRA) and the measured seconds. **Reset** starts the
   measurement again.
5. Press Ctrl+Z to undo a change. Every fader move, mute and solo is one undo step, and consecutive moves of one
   fader are a single step.

The mixer starts from the project's bus layout in `config/audio.ron` (the default tree when there is none). It
changes the running session's mixer; **Save layout** writes the file.

## Walk-through: an effect chain, a send and a snapshot

1. Click **Chain** on a bus. Its effect chain opens under it. Pick a kind in the list (EQ, Low-pass, High-pass,
   Reverb, Delay, Compressor, Distortion, Convolution) and click **Add effect**: the effect is added at the end at a
   near-neutral setting.
2. **Bypass** skips an effect without losing its settings; **Move up** and **Move down** reorder the chain;
   **Remove** deletes the effect.
3. Under the chain, each send bus (such as **Reverb**) has a row: **Add send** routes the bus to it (silent at
   first), the slider sets the send level from -60 dB (silent) to +6 dB, and **Remove send** removes the route.
   A send is taken after the fader and mute unless **Pre** is on: a pre-fader send is taken before them, so the
   reverb keeps its feed when you pull the bus fader down or mute the bus.
4. Below the buses, type a name and click **Save snapshot**: every fader, mute and send level is stored under that
   name. **Apply** blends the mixer to a snapshot over its blend time (the seconds field on its row); **Release**
   blends back. **Delete** removes a snapshot.
5. Click **Save layout** to write everything to `config/audio.ron`; until then the panel shows **· unsaved
   changes**. The game builds that bus tree when it starts.

Changing a chain, adding or removing a send, toggling **Pre**, or bypassing an effect rebuilds the mixer's buses, which stops the
sounds playing at that moment; moving a send slider or applying a snapshot does not.

## Actions

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Move a bus's fader | The bus's slider | `editor.audio_mixer_set` (`volume_db`) |
| Mute a bus | **M** | `editor.audio_mixer_set` (`mute`) |
| Solo a bus | **S** | `editor.audio_mixer_set` (`solo`) |
| Read the buses and meters | The panel | `editor.audio_mixer_get` |
| Restart the program loudness measurement | **Reset** | none (view only) |
| Open a bus's effect chain and sends | **Chain** | none (view only) |
| Add, remove, reorder or bypass an effect | **Add effect**, **Remove**, **Move up**, **Move down**, **Bypass** | `editor.audio_mixer_chain` |
| Set, add or remove a send | The send slider, **Add send**, **Remove send** | `editor.audio_mixer_send` |
| Take a send before or after the fader | **Pre** | `editor.audio_mixer_send` (`tap`) |
| Save, apply, release or delete a snapshot; set its blend time | **Save snapshot**, **Apply**, **Release**, **Delete**, the seconds field | `editor.audio_mixer_snapshot` |
| Write the layout to `config/audio.ron` | **Save layout** | `editor.audio_mixer_save` |
| Undo | Ctrl+Z | `editor.undo` |

## Keyboard

The panel handles no keys of its own. Tab and Shift+Tab move between sliders, lists, fields and buttons (the open
chain and the snapshot rows included); the arrow keys move a focused slider and Space or Enter presses a focused
button such as **M**, **S**, **Chain**, **Bypass**, **Pre**, **Add effect** or **Apply** ([Editor guide](book/user-guide/editor-guide/index.md)).

## Known limits

- Meters read silence outside play unless the edit world has its own audio engine; the source is named in the top line.
- Effect settings other than the kind are not edited in the panel: a new effect starts near neutral; other
  settings are edited in `config/audio.ron`.
- The meter bars are drawn shapes; the agent read of the same numbers is `editor.audio_mixer_get`.

## See also

[Cue editor](book/user-guide/editor-guide/cue-editor.md), [Audio mixer (agents)](book/agents/audio-mixer.md), [Audio
loudness (agents)](book/agents/audio-program-loudness.md).

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/cue-editor.md -->
# Cue editor

Panel id: `cue_editor`.

The **Cue Editor** tab edits a sound cue, a `.cue.ron` file that names a set of sound variations and how the game
picks and plays one: weights, pick mode, what happens at the instance limit, the volume and pitch ranges, a low-pass
filter and a caption for subtitles. Its **Audition** button draws a variation the way the cue would and plays the
file. Depth: [Audio mixer and cue editor (agents)](book/agents/audio-mixer.md), [Audio](book/user-guide/audio.md).

## Opening it

The tab sits in the group under the viewport in the default layout; **View ▸ Reset layout** brings it back if you
closed it. An agent brings it forward with `editor.layout_apply {"open": "cue_editor"}`. It has no palette command
and no key.

## Walk-through: tune a footstep cue

1. Type a project path such as `audio/footstep.cue.ron` in the box and click **Open**. The cue's name and path
   appear on a line with **Save** and **Audition**; **(edited)** is added to the path while there are unsaved changes.
2. Under **Variations**, each row shows a sound path, a weight (drag the number) and **Remove**. To add a sound,
   type its path (for example `audio/step_03.wav`) and click **Add variation**.
3. Choose the **mode** (random, shuffle or sequential) and the **steal** policy (oldest, quietest or none) from
   the two drop-downs.
4. Set **volume dB** and its **range**, the **pitch** range, and **max instances** (0 means unlimited).
5. Tick **low-pass** to filter the cue: the cutoff in Hz and an octave offset appear. Tick **caption** to attach a
   subtitle: type the **caption key**, pick its kind (sound, speech or narration), set the priority and the planned
   length in milliseconds, and click **Set caption**.
6. Click **Audition**. The line under the controls reports the variation drawn, its volume in dB and its pitch;
   it adds **(not played)** when the file could not be played.
7. Click **Save**. **Save** is enabled only while the cue is edited.

Every change is one undo step (Ctrl+Z), and scrubbing one value is a single step. A cue you did not edit is never
rewritten: its bytes stay as they were. An edited cue is written with the engine's own serializer, so a
hand-formatted file is reformatted on its first saved edit.

## Actions

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Open a cue | Path box, **Open** | `editor.cue_edit` (`path`) |
| Read the open cue | The panel | `editor.cue_edit` (`op: "get"`) |
| Add or remove a variation, change a weight | **Add variation**, **Remove**, the weight drag value | `editor.cue_edit` (`add_sound`, `remove_sound`, `set_weight`) |
| Mode, steal, volume, pitch, instances, filter, caption | The drop-downs, drag values, **low-pass**, **caption** | `editor.cue_edit` (`set`) |
| Bus, cooldown, no repeat of the last variation | none (not in the panel) | `editor.cue_edit` (`set`) |
| Save | **Save** | `editor.cue_edit` (`save`) |
| Audition | **Audition** | `editor.cue_edit` (`audition`) |
| Undo | Ctrl+Z | `editor.undo` |

## Keyboard

The panel handles no keys of its own. Tab and Shift+Tab move between its controls, and Space or Enter presses the
focused button ([Editor guide](book/user-guide/editor-guide/index.md)).

## Known limits

- A cue holds at most 256 variations.
- **Audition** plays the drawn file at its own level and pitch: the drawn volume and pitch are reported, not applied
  to the preview.
- The cue's bus, cooldown and no-repeat setting are read and written through the agent method only.
- A cue file newer than this engine cannot be opened.

## See also

[Audio mixer](book/user-guide/editor-guide/audio-mixer.md), [Audio](book/user-guide/audio.md), [Audio mixer and cue editor (agents)](book/agents/audio-mixer.md).

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/agent-changes.md -->
# Agent Changes

Panel id: `agent_changes`.

When an agent wants to change project files, it does not write them. It **proposes** a set of text
files with a reason, and the proposal waits in the **Agent Changes** tab. You read each file's diff
and accept or reject. Nothing changes in the project until you accept. An agent cannot approve its
own work: the `review` permission is in no default profile. Depth: [Staged review
(agents)](book/agents/staged-review.md).

## Open it

The tab is part of the default layout (the group under the viewport); **View ▸ Reset layout**
brings it back when closed. An agent uses `editor.layout_apply {"open": "agent_changes"}`. The
command palette has no `open` command for it.

## Review a proposal

1. Open the tab. The header counts the changes pending and shows the last status line. With
   nothing waiting it reads "No agent changes wait for review."
2. The left column groups changes by set. Each set starts with its number and title, the client
   that proposed it (with its model when known), and **Accept set** and **Reject set** buttons.
   Under it each change is a row with its kind, project path and the lines added and removed.
3. Click a row to select it. The right column shows the path, the **Reason** the agent gave, the
   paths of any before and after screenshots it attached, and the unified diff (added lines green,
   removed lines red, hunk headers blue).
4. Optionally type a reviewer **Note**. It is stored with the decision and cleared afterward.
5. Press **Accept** or **Reject** for the selected change, or the set buttons for the whole set.
   Accepting writes each file atomically if it still holds the text the agent saw when it
   proposed. A file that changed since is a conflict: its change stays pending and the status line
   counts it, so ask the agent to propose again. Accepting also stamps the file's `.meta`
   provenance as reviewed by the owner.
6. Each accepted change is one undo step, described as "Accept agent change to" and the file's path:
   **Ctrl+Z** puts the file's old text back (or removes a file the change created).

A proposal for a golden image stays pending: the status line says to accept it at a terminal with
`regia golden accept` and the change id.

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Read the queue and the selected diff | the tab | `editor.agent_changes_state` |
| Select a change | click its row | `editor.agent_changes_select` |
| Accept a change or a set | **Accept**, **Accept set** | `review.accept` (needs the `review` permission) |
| Reject a change or a set | **Reject**, **Reject set** | `review.reject` |
| List pending changes and read a diff | the tab | `review.list`, `review.diff` |
| Propose a change set (the agent's side) | none | `review.propose` |

## Keyboard

The tab has no shortcuts of its own; Ctrl+Z undoes an accepted change like any edit. Rows and
buttons take focus with Tab.

## Known limits

- Only text files can be proposed, and files under `.regia/` and `.git/` are not reviewable.
- The tab decides as the owner at the editor; an agent that holds `review` can accept with
  `review.accept`, which the owner should grant only to a review bot that acts for them.
- The queue is saved in the project, so a proposal waits across editor restarts.

See also: [Editor guide](book/user-guide/editor-guide/index.md).

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/behavior-tree.md -->
# Behavior tree

Panel id: `behavior_tree`.

The **Behavior Tree** tab edits a `.bt.ron` behavior tree: a palette of node kinds and registered leaf tasks, the
tree as an indented outline, an inspector for the selected node and a list of validation problems. While the game
plays it shows the last status of every node (running, success or failure) for the agent you pick. Depth: [Behavior
tree editor (agents)](book/agents/behavior-tree-editor.md), [Navigation and AI](book/user-guide/navigation-ai.md).

## Opening it

The tab sits in the group under the viewport in the default layout; **View ▸ Reset layout** brings it back if you
closed it. An agent brings it forward with `editor.layout_apply {"open": "behavior_tree"}`. It has no palette
command and no key.

## Walk-through: build a guard tree

1. Click **New** for an empty tree, or type a path such as `assets/ai/guard.bt.ron` and click **Open**.
2. In the **Add:** row click **selector**. With no root yet the node becomes the root. The row's hover text says
   where a click adds the node: under the selected node, as the root, or as an unconnected node.
3. Select the selector in the outline, then add a **sequence** and a **condition**: each is added under the
   selected node when it can take a child (a decorator takes exactly one child; a leaf, condition, compare or
   state tree node takes none).
4. In the **Leaf:** row click a registered task to add a leaf that runs it (the row shows one **leaf** button when
   no tasks are registered).
5. Select a node to edit it in the inspector: its name and, for the kinds that use them, the blackboard key,
   comparison operator, value type, other key, seconds, repeat count, abort mode, parallel policy and task. **Move up**
   and **Move down** reorder it among its siblings, **Disconnect** detaches it from its parent, **connect under**
   attaches it to another node that can take a child, **Make root** makes it the root, **Remove** removes it with
   everything below it, and **Remove (keep children)** removes only the node.
6. The top bar says **compiles** or **N error(s)**; the problem list at the bottom names each problem, and clicking
   one selects its node. A node with problems is marked with a warning sign and its count in the outline.
7. Click **Save** (when the tree has a path; **Save as** writes to the path in the box). A tree with errors is
   saved too, so you can build it up through invalid states.
8. Press Alt+P. The line **Live state** appears when an agent runs a tree: choose the agent, and each node in the
   outline takes the color of its status. If the running tree differs from the open document the panel says so and
   does not color the nodes.

Every edit is one undo step; **Undo** and **Redo** on the toolbar show the step's name on hover, and Ctrl+Z and
Ctrl+Y use the editor's undo stack. **New** and **Open** warn the first time when the open tree has unsaved changes
("unsaved changes: press again to discard them"); press again to discard.

## Actions

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Start a tree, open a file | **New**, path box and **Open** | `editor.bt_open` |
| Add, connect, reorder, change or remove nodes | **Add:** and **Leaf:** rows, the inspector | `editor.bt_edit` |
| Read the tree and its problems | The outline and problem list | `editor.bt_state` |
| Save | **Save**, **Save as** | `editor.bt_save` |
| Undo, redo | **Undo**, **Redo**, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y | `editor.undo`, `editor.redo` |
| Check or edit a file without the panel | none | `ai.bt_validate`, `ai.bt_edit`, `ai.bt_get` |

## Keyboard

The panel handles no keys of its own. Tab and Shift+Tab move between controls, and Space or Enter presses the
focused button or selects the focused outline row ([Editor guide](book/user-guide/editor-guide/index.md)).

## Known limits

- Node kinds are `selector`, `sequence`, `parallel`, `inverter`, `condition`, `compare`, `cooldown`, `repeat`,
  `timeout`, `service`, `state_tree` and `leaf`; leaf tasks are the ones the game registers (with none registered,
  the editor skips the task check).
- Nodes without a parent are listed under **Unconnected nodes** until you connect them.
- The outline is a list, not a canvas: there is no drag to move a node; reorder and connect with the inspector
  controls.

## See also

[State trees](book/user-guide/editor-guide/state-trees.md), [Behavior tree editor (agents)](book/agents/behavior-tree-editor.md), [Navigation and
AI](book/user-guide/navigation-ai.md).

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/ui-inspector.md -->
# UI Inspector

Panel id: `ui_inspector`.

The **UI Inspector** tab answers "why does this widget look like this, and which widget is that?"
for the interface of a running game. It shows the live UI tree, a map of every node's rectangle,
and for the selected node its resolved properties, where each value came from (the theme, the node
itself, an animation or a binding), its bindings, focus and accessibility data. It only reads; it
never changes the game's UI. Depth: [UI runtime inspector (agents)](book/agents/ui-inspector.md),
[UI layout debug overlay](book/agents/ui-debug-overlay.md), [UI designer](book/user-guide/editor-guide/ui-designer.md).

## Open it

The tab is part of the default layout (the group under the viewport); **View ▸ Reset layout**
brings it back when closed. An agent uses `editor.layout_apply {"open": "ui_inspector"}`. There is
no menu item and no command palette `open` command for it.

## Inspect a node

1. Choose what to inspect. For the play-in-editor world, press Play (Alt+P), then click **PIE
   world** at the top of the tab. For a game running separately, type its project directory into
   the box ("project dir of a running game") and press **Attach**; the tab connects over that
   game's agent socket. A failed connection shows its error in red. Until one is chosen the tab
   says "Press Play, then choose "PIE world", or attach to a running game."
2. The left column is the **tree**. A `>` or `v` button expands or collapses a node; click a node's
   label to select it. The search box above the tree ("search kind, name, text, class, id") keeps
   matching nodes and their ancestors.
3. The right column shows the **layout map**: every node's rectangle scaled to fit, with the
   selected node outlined in yellow. Turn **Pick** on and hover the map to select the topmost node
   under the pointer (the game's own z-order and layers decide which that is); a click on the map
   picks too.
4. Below the map the property table describes the selected node: its type, name, rectangle and z,
   its accessible name and role, and whether it can take focus. The **visual**, **content** and
   **layout** groups each list property, value, source (`default`, `theme`, `inline`, `animation`
   or `binding`, each in its own color) and detail (for a theme value, the layer that won). A
   **bindings** group lists each binding's source, target, mode and last value.
5. Selecting a node also outlines it in the game itself, through the game's UI debug overlay.
   Selecting nothing clears the outline.
6. The numeric field with the `Hz` suffix sets how often the tree and the selection refresh (0.5 to
   10 Hz; it starts at 4).

| Action | Control / key | Agent method |
|---|---|---|
| Read the tree | the tree column | `ui.query` |
| Inspect one node | click its label | `ui.inspect` |
| Find the node under a point | **Pick** and the layout map | `ui.pick_at` |
| Outline a node in the game | selecting a node | `ui.highlight` |
| Choose the PIE world or attach to a game | **PIE world**, **Attach** | none (the tab's own state; an agent calls the `ui.*` methods on the game directly) |

## Keyboard

The tab has no shortcuts. The expand buttons, node labels, search box, **Attach**, **PIE world**
and **Pick** take focus with Tab. The layout map is a drawn shape that responds to the mouse only;
the tree gives the same selection from the keyboard.

## Known limits

- The tab reads the live UI; with no session running and nothing attached it shows nothing.
- It asks for at most 1,000 nodes per refresh, the limit of `ui.query`.
- It needs a game with the agent protocol on to attach to a separate process.
- **Pick** and the tree only select; to change a style, edit the theme or the node in the [UI
  designer](book/user-guide/editor-guide/ui-designer.md).

See also: [Game UI](book/user-guide/ui.md).

<!-- source: book/user-guide/editor-guide/vfx-editor.md -->
# VFX Editor

Panel id: `vfx_editor`.

The **VFX Editor** tab edits a `.vfx.ron` particle effect: the list of emitters, each emitter's
module stack (gravity, drag, size over life, ...), curve and gradient editors, a live preview and a
table of what each emitter costs. Every change is one step on the editor's shared undo stack and is
checked by the `.vfx.ron` validator; an edit the validator refuses changes nothing. Depth: [VFX
(agents)](book/agents/vfx.md) and [VFX](book/systems/vfx.md).

## Open it

The tab is part of the default layout (the group under the viewport). If you closed it,
**View ▸ Reset layout** brings it back. An agent brings it forward with
`editor.layout_apply {"open": "vfx_editor"}`. The command palette has no `open` command for this tab.

## Edit an effect

1. Type the project-relative path of an effect (for example `vfx/explosion.vfx.ron`) in the path
   box at the top and press **Open**. The panel does not read a selection from the Content browser.
2. Pick an emitter in the **Emitters** list. **Up** and **Down** reorder emitters, **Remove**
   deletes one (not the last), and the box under the list with **Add emitter** adds a new one with
   the name you typed.
3. Under **Module stack** each module is a collapsible row named `<stage> / <module>`. Open a row
   to edit its parameters. The box in the row header is the A/B switch: unchecking it takes the
   module out of the effect for the preview and the saved file (the row turns gray and reads
   "(disabled)"); checking it puts the exact values back. **Remove** deletes an optional module.
   The `spawn`, `init` and `render` modules are always there: they have no switch and no Remove.
4. To add a module, pick it in the list next to **Add module** and press the button. The list
   offers only the optional modules the emitter does not have yet.
5. Under **Curves** and **Gradients**, double-click an empty spot to add a key, drag a key to move
   it, and right-click a key to delete it (gradients: click a marker to select it, then edit its
   time and color in the key row, or **Delete** it). Curves are linear between keys.
6. Watch the **Preview** on the right. **Play** and **Pause** run the preview clock, **Restart**
   starts over, **seed** and the **time s** slider (0 to 30 s) pick a deterministic frame. Under
