  the forward pass applies them; a thin lens (`PtCamera::with_lens`).
- Not traced: fog volumes, ozone, particles and decals, parallax, edge wear, glass
  tint and Fresnel on shadow rays, refraction offsets of thick glass, and the Earth night sky
  (stars only on airless planets). A `current` trace with `clouds` set to `droplet` or `raster`
  also traces the frame's cloud layer when the frame has one (below); `off`, the default, traces
  none. A host with several views exports the last one it drew.

## From the command line

- `regia render --reference --project <dir> [--spp 1024] [--width 1280 --height 720]
  [--out-dir DIR]` starts `seeing.reference_trace` on the running app's current view, prints
  progress, and prints the finished job (EXR, preview, metadata paths). Without `--reference`
  it saves the real-time window (`--out render.png`).
- `render_lab pt <scene> [--spp N] [--bounces N] [--width W --height H] [--out DIR]` traces a
  lab scene (`material_grid`, `clustered_lights`, `light_shadows`, `surface_maps`,
  `alpha_modes`, `ibl_spheres`) or a validation scene (`cornell`, `cornell_room`, `furnace`)
  and writes `<scene>_pt.exr/.png/.json` next to the real-time `<scene>_rt.png`.
- `pt_plates --evidence docs/evidence/pt` (in `samples/lookdev`, with `REGIA_DO27_CONTENT`)
  is the nightly ground-truth job: all twelve parity plates at 1280×720 / 2048 spp into
  `docs/evidence/pt/<date>/` with `scores.json`, a score table in `README.md` and one contact
  sheet per plate; `--resume` continues a killed run.
- `regia bake-gi <scene> [--out X.fgiv] [--rays N] [--samples N] [--bounces N] [--seed N]
  [--no-filter]` bakes a diffuse GI probe volume with the same kernels (baked lighting,
  phase 1; part of the baked-light release, v0.2.0): `<scene>` is `cornell`, `furnace`, `rolling-hills` or a bake description `.ron`
  (raw u16 heightfield, sun, sky, sky bodies, terrain layer spacing and levels, detail bricks).
  It prints a JSON summary (`report.valid`, `relocated`, `inside_geometry`, `under_terrain`,
  `rays_traced`, `seconds`). Per probe: L1 SH of incident radiance per component (`sun_bounce`,
  `sky`, `fill`, `emissive`; the sun disc and local lights stay live), octahedral distance
  moments, validity. Format and description: `docs/formats/baked-gi.md`. Same seed, same bytes.

## Denoised previews

```json
seeing.reference_trace { "scene": "current", "width": 1280, "height": 720, "spp": 64, "denoise": true, "wait": true }
→ { "job": 2, "status": "done", "denoised": true, "exr": ".../preview.exr", "preview_png": ".../preview.png",
    "raw": { "exr": ".../reference.exr", "preview_png": ".../reference_preview.png", … },
    "metadata": { "spp": 64, "denoiser": "oidn 2.5 RT hdr albedo+normal high", "denoise_seconds": 0.4, … },
    "total_seconds": 3.1, "png_base64": "…" }
```

- For look iteration: a low-spp trace plus Intel Open Image Denoise is a quick preview, not a
  reference. The repository holds no measured comparison against a converged trace; measure it with
  `seeing.compare` (a converged raw trace as `a`, the preview as `b`), and read the denoise cost from
  `metadata.denoise_seconds`.
  Only `beauty` is filtered; the other AOVs are the raw trace's.
- Needs a host built with `regia_agent`'s `denoise` feature (it links Intel's native OIDN
  library; desktop tools only). Without it, `denoise: true` answers `F0013`.
- **A preview is never a reference.** Denoising trades noise for bias, so the preview's EXR
  header and PNG carry `regia.denoiser`, and `seeing.compare` answers `F0002` when one is
  given as `a` (the job id of a denoised trace resolves to its preview). Score with the raw
  trace (`raw.exr`) or a converged trace as `a`; a preview may be `b`, which is how its own
  error is measured.

## Compare

```json
seeing.compare { "a": { "job": 1 }, "b": "/tmp/frame_hdr.exr", "aov": "beauty", "ev100": 12.5 }
→ { "flip_mean": 0.041, "flip_p95": 0.12, "ssim": 0.93, "rmse": 210.0, "rel_rmse": 0.08,
    "mean_reference": 2600.0, "mean_test": 2510.0, "psnr_db": 31.4, "aov": "beauty",
    "flip_map_png": "…", "mime": "image/png", "png_base64": "…" }
```

- `a` is the reference, `b` the image under test: EXR (linear) or PNG (display-encoded), or a
  finished trace job.
- **FLIP** (Andersson et al. 2020) runs on both images through the runtime's AgX at `ev100`,
  so it measures what a viewer sees. 0 is identical; below about 0.05 a viewer flipping
  between the two hardly sees a change; 0.1–0.2 is a visible but local difference. `flip_p95`
  catches small, strongly wrong regions the mean hides.
- **RMSE** is on linear luminance (`rel_rmse` = RMSE / reference mean): energy errors that the
  tonemap would hide (exposure, albedo, a missing bounce).
- **SSIM** on display luma, the goldens' structure metric.
- **PSNR** (`psnr_db`, ADR-2315) on the same display-encoded pair as FLIP and SSIM, peak 1:
  `10 log10(1 / MSE)` over every RGB channel. `null` when the images are equal. `mode: "rmse"` keeps it,
  `flip` and `ssim` drop it. Every mode also returns `aov`, `mime` (`image/png`), `flip_map_png` and
  `png_base64`. The v0.3.0 lightmap evidence (`docs/evidence/lightmaps-v030/`) records it per AOV.
- The heat map (`flip_map_png`) is black where the frames agree, magenta → orange → white
  where they differ.

## Scoring GI

Compare `indirect_diffuse` (plus `indirect_specular` for reflections) of the reference with
the real-time frame's indirect light. A real-time frame's indirect is its linear HDR minus
the same frame with every indirect term off; `lookdev`'s `pt_plates` does exactly that for the
parity plates and writes `<shot>_scores.json` with beauty, direct and GI scores. The ★ targets
of spec 27 § 2.2 (GI mean FLIP ≤ 0.08, p95 ≤ 0.20) are first guesses until the measured values
are written into the spec.

## Validation (why the reference can be trusted)

`cargo test -p regia_pt` runs § 1.5 on the same kernels at tiny sizes: furnace spheres
match their BRDF albedo to 0.3 %, a closed white sphere matches the bounce series, a plane
under a sun, a sphere light and an emissive quad match their analytic irradiance, the Cornell
room matches an independent radiosity solution, the forward pass's direct term equals the
tracer's `direct` AOV (also with anisotropy, packed ORM and detail maps), and two runs with
one seed are bit-identical. v2 adds: transmittance through absorbing slabs and exponential
layers is exact, a conservative chromatic fog in a uniform sky returns the sky's radiance in
every direction, a sky body delivers its disc irradiance, a quad light matches Lambert's
polygon formula and a thin lens blurs a point by its circle of confusion.

## Bindless step 1: draw counters and the bindless tier

Two read-only calls measure what the renderer pays for binding before the bindless work goes
further (ADR-316). Both are pure reads; neither changes a frame.

`render.get_frame_stats` returns the encoder calls of the runtime renderer's last main-view frame,
per pass and in total:

```json
{
  "frame": 120,
  "passes": {
    "shadow":            { "draws": 0, "pipeline_switches": 0, "bind_group_switches": [0, 0, 0, 0], "bind_group_switches_total": 0, "material_batches": 0 },
    "depth_prepass":     { "draws": 4, "pipeline_switches": 1, "bind_group_switches": [1, 4, 2, 0], "bind_group_switches_total": 7, "material_batches": 2 },
    "visbuffer_resolve": { "draws": 0, "...": "..." },
    "opaque":            { "draws": 4, "pipeline_switches": 1, "bind_group_switches": [1, 4, 2, 0], "bind_group_switches_total": 7, "material_batches": 2 },
    "translucent":       { "draws": 0, "...": "..." }
  },
  "total": { "draws": 8, "pipeline_switches": 2, "bind_group_switches": [2, 8, 4, 0], "bind_group_switches_total": 14, "material_batches": 4 },
  "material_constants": { "path": "storage_arena", "live": 2, "capacity": 256, "stride": 352, "buffer_creates": 1, "epoch": 0 }
}
```

- `draws`: draw calls (`draw`, `draw_indexed`, one per `draw_indexed_indirect`).
- `pipeline_switches`: `set_pipeline` calls that bound a different pipeline.
- `bind_group_switches`: `set_bind_group` calls that bound a different group, per group slot
  (0 view or shadow tile, 1 object, 2 material, 3 the pass extra: refraction, glass, mask decals).
- `material_batches`: runs of consecutive draws that share one material bind group. This is the
  number a bindless renderer would merge into fewer calls.
- `material_constants`: `path` is `per_material` (each material has its own uniform buffer, tier
  `none`) or `storage_arena` (every standard material's constants in one storage buffer). For the
  arena, `live` is the materials that hold a slot, `capacity` and `stride` are the buffer's size in
  slots and bytes per slot, `buffer_creates` is how many buffers it ever created (it stays flat after
  warm-up, however many materials come and go), and `epoch` counts the times it grew.

The shadow numbers sum every shadow pass of the frame (cascades, atlas tiles, page clears). Calls
other modules record inside a pass are not counted: the shared terrain draw, the sky, the
visibility-buffer rasters and the translucent shadow casters. The counts are exact for a given scene
and view and do not depend on timing, so a test can assert them (`bindless::frame_tests` does on a
fixed four-quad scene). A texture view's draws are not part of these counts.

Without an app, `cargo run --release -p regia_render --example draw_counts [WIDTH HEIGHT]` prints
the same counters for the hard-surface lookdev scenes (the hull close-up and the 12-hull grid) on a
headless device, with the device's tier.

`render.get_capabilities` reports the render device: `adapter`, `backend`, the optional `features`
the renderer uses, the binding `limits`, the active capability `fallbacks` (the same codes as
`render.problems`), and `bindless`:

```json
"bindless": { "tier": "material_ssbo", "adapter_tier": "texture_arrays", "material_path": "storage_arena",
              "binding_arrays": false,
              "non_uniform_indexing": false, "partially_bound": false, "max_binding_array_elements": 0,
              "storage_buffers_per_stage": 1048576, "max_storage_buffer_binding_size": 2147483644,
              "storage_offset_alignment": 16 }
```

`tier` is the device's: `none` (per-material uniform buffers: fewer than 12 storage buffers per stage,
as on min-spec mobile), `material_ssbo` (material constants in one storage buffer), or
`texture_arrays` (texture binding arrays as well; step 2 uses them). `adapter_tier` is what the adapter
could reach once the renderer asks for its binding-array features. `material_path` is where this
device's material constants actually live: `storage_arena` from tier `material_ssbo` up, except on
Android, which keeps `per_material` on every tier until the storage path is measured on phones. The
device logs the same once at creation (`bindless tier: …; material constants: …`).

Driver workarounds show in `fallbacks` too. `fallback_sun_shadow_pcf_only` (ADR-1749): on a Qualcomm Adreno
adapter the forward shader is composed with `SUN_SHADOW_PCF_ONLY`, so the sun shadow is PCF on the cascades
only, with no near tile and no PCSS soft shadows. The Adreno 643 compiler of a Fairphone 5 crashed on the
full shader at every launch. `REGIA_SUN_SHADOW_PCF_ONLY=1` forces the workaround on for any adapter, so you
can look at it on a desktop; `=0` turns it off on Adreno, to re-test a newer driver. The device logs
`sun shadow: PCF on the cascades only ...` once at creation when it is on. The same workaround also sets
`STUDIO_IBL_OFF` (ADR-2042) and `FORWARD_TRIM` (ADR-3145). With `FORWARD_TRIM` the full shader has no light
from fitted emitters or LTC sphere lights, no surface weather and no aerial haze in the weather in-scatter, and
a pane behind the nearest one keeps its environment reflection. Without that define, the Adreno 643
(Fairphone 5) and Adreno 504 (Galaxy Tab A 8.0) compilers crashed on the opaque and GPU-driven colour
pipelines. The lite Mobile shader is not affected.

Errors: without a `RuntimeRenderer` (`render.get_frame_stats`) or a `RenderDevice`
(`render.get_capabilities`) the call fails with the protocol's not-found error, whose hint says to add
`regia_render::RenderPlugin`. There are no other error codes.

## Bindless level 3: the texture table

At bindless level 3 (ADR-863) every standard material samples its seven textures through one
per-device texture table, and every standard material binds one shared material group: the
material constants arena at the material's own dynamic offset. A pass then binds one material
group whatever the number of materials, and creating or replacing a material creates no bind
group. Graph materials keep their own groups and pipelines.

Level 3 is opt-in while its acceptance runs on the gate's GPUs. Set the level before the device
is created (it changes shader defines and layouts, so it is read once per device):

```sh
REGIA_BINDLESS_LEVEL=3 cargo run --release -p lookdev
```

`0` is the per-material uniform path, `1` (the default) the material constants arena of step 1,
`3` the texture table. `2` and `4` are reserved for the per-draw slot and the single-pass
visibility resolve (ADR-356): today `2` behaves as `1` and `4` as `3`. A device takes the table only when it can:

`render.get_capabilities` reports the decision in `bindless.texture_table`:

```json
"texture_table": { "path": "table", "capacity": 4032, "fallback": null }
"texture_table": { "path": "per_material", "capacity": null, "fallback": "not_requested" }
```

`capacity` is the number of views the table holds: the device's binding-array budget less 64
for the other textures a material pass samples, at most 4096. Off the table, `fallback` names
the first requirement that is missing. The codes are stable:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `not_requested` | The adapter could carry the table, but the level is below 3. |
| `uniform_materials` | Material constants use per-material uniform buffers (tier `none`, or Android). |
| `backend` | GL or WebGPU: no binding arrays through wgpu. |
| `no_binding_arrays` | The device has no `TEXTURE_BINDING_ARRAY`. |
| `no_non_uniform_indexing` | The device has no `SAMPLED_TEXTURE_AND_STORAGE_BUFFER_ARRAY_NON_UNIFORM_INDEXING`. |
| `array_elements` | Fewer than 4096 binding-array elements per shader stage. |
| `bind_groups` | Fewer than five bind groups (the table is group 4). |

The table binds every element (unused ones hold the white view), so partially bound arrays are
not required and Metal qualifies.

`render.get_frame_stats` gains `texture_table` (`null` off the table path):

```json
"texture_table": { "capacity": 4032, "live": 37, "overflows": 0, "rebuilds": 2, "refreshes": 120,
                   "last_rebuild_us": 41, "record_groups": 1 }
```

- `live`: distinct material textures that hold a table index (materials sharing a texture share
  its index).
- `overflows`: texture slots that did not fit the table and sample their neutral view instead (a
  warning is logged once). Above zero means the scene has more textures than the table holds, and
  `render.problems` then reports `texture_table_full` with the counts. A larger table needs no
  rebuild: set `REGIA_TEXTURE_TABLE_VIEWS` (4096 to 65536; the device's budget still caps it)
  before the device is created. Every table rebuild then binds that many views.
- `rebuilds`: table bind groups built. wgpu bind groups cannot be edited, so a texture entering
  or leaving the table means a new table group. The renderer rebuilds it at most once per frame,
  before the first pass binds it, so `rebuilds` never grows faster than `refreshes` (the frames
  that checked it).
- `last_rebuild_us`: CPU time of the last rebuild, for profiling only.
- `record_groups`: shared material groups built, one per material arena buffer (the arena doubles
  when full). It stays flat while materials come and go.

On the table path each pass's `material_batches` is 1 (graph materials add their own runs), and
`bind_group_switches[2]` counts the dynamic-offset changes, one per material change, the same
number the per-material path counts as group changes. A streamed texture changing residency
rewrites 16 bytes of its material's record and marks the table for the next rebuild; the
material's group is not rebuilt.

Known limit at level 3: a graph material with mask decals draws with its graph pipeline and no
decals (the mask-decal variant uses the standard material layout; at level 1 such a draw takes
the standard surface with decals instead). Glass instances apply to standard materials only, as
before. Blended graph materials still cast translucent shadows, through a caster variant over
their own group. The pixels of standard materials are byte-identical to level 1 on lavapipe
(`texture_table::frame_tests`).

### More `seeing.reference_trace` parameters

The schema (`agent.schema`) also lists these optional parameters:

- `max_bounces` (number): Maximum path length (default 12, at most 1024). A cloud field wants 128 or more.
- `clouds` (string): For current: off (default), droplet or raster traces the frame's cloud layer as a medium (ADR-2127, [Path-traced cloud layer](book/agents/pt-cloud-layer.md)) with the physical phase and albedo, or the raster march's own.
- `aovs` (array): EXR layers to write (default all of specs/27 § 1.2).
- `subsurface` (boolean): For current: `true` traces each material's subsurface scattering with Burley's normalized
  diffusion (ADR-2725); `false` (default) traces the light that lands. With any other `scene` it is `invalid_params`.
  Material graphs are always traced with their own surface code; refusals are listed in `metadata.surface_graphs`.

### More `seeing.compare` parameters

The schema (`agent.schema`) also lists these optional parameters:

- `mode` (string): flip, rmse, ssim or all (default).
- `ppd` (number): Viewer pixels per degree (default 67).
- `map_png` (string): Where to write the FLIP map (default next to b).

## Quality presets (ADR-2433)

`seeing.reference_trace {preset}` runs a named quality table instead of one fixed operating point: `draft`, `preview`,
`final` or `reference`. `reference` is the plain trace (bit for bit); `draft` and `preview` are biased, denoised
previews that `seeing.compare` refuses as the reference. The tables, the built-in denoiser, adaptive sampling, the
caustics modes and the parameters (`preset`, `caustics`, `clamp_indirect`, `firefly_threshold`, `adaptive`, `denoiser`)
are on [Path tracer presets](book/agents/pt-presets.md).

## The rest of the spec 27 surface

Spec 27 § 5 names eight methods. The two above are on this page; the others have their own pages:

| Method | What it gives | Page |
|---|---|---|
| `seeing.capture_plate` | One named shot (camera, time of day, profile) rendered through the runtime frame to files plus a `regia.plate/1` sidecar | [Plates and the reference overlay](book/agents/plates.md) |
| `render.set_reference_overlay` | A reference PNG drawn over the live frame: `off`, `blend`, `wipe`, `difference`, `flip` | [Plates and the reference overlay](book/agents/plates.md) |
| `seeing.temporal_chart` | The five § 2.3 temporal numbers from the chart scene | [Temporal chart](book/agents/temporal-chart.md) |
| `play.hitch_report` | The § 2.4 hitch numbers: percentiles, frames over 2 × p50, longest frame, device-call counters | [Hitches](book/agents/hitches.md) |
| `render.set_gi_mode` | Live switch of the GI technique for A/B against a trace | [Dynamic GI](book/agents/dynamic-gi.md) |
| `render.set_upscaler` | Live switch of the upscaler and its scale | [Upscalers](book/agents/upscalers.md) |

Two differences from the spec's table, recorded in ADR-5630: `seeing.reference_trace` takes `width` and
`height` (not `size`) and traces the frame's own camera when `scene` is `current` (no `camera` parameter),
and the overlay's `flip` mode is a per-pixel HyAB heat map, not the full FLIP score (`seeing.compare` stays
the number of record). The overlay loads the PNG given in `path`; to overlay a trace, pass the trace's
`preview_png`.

## Capturing and judging a plate

1. Capture the shot at the current pin: `seeing.capture_plate { "shot": { …, "format": "exr" } }`, then
   poll the plate id until its files and sidecar are written ([Plates](book/agents/plates.md)). The same shot twice gives the same
   frame hash, so a changed hash means the picture changed.
2. Trace the same view: `seeing.reference_trace { "scene": "current", "spp": 1024 }` with the plate's
   camera still applied, and wait for the job.
3. Score it: `seeing.compare { "a": { "job": <id> }, "b": "<stem>_000000.exr" }` for the whole frame, then per
   AOV (the `aov` parameter: `direct`, `indirect_diffuse`, `shadow`, …) where the frame under test has
   that layer, to find which technique carries the error.
4. Look at it: `render.set_reference_overlay { "mode": "wipe", "path": "<preview_png>" }` and move the
   split, then `difference` to see where the two disagree.
5. Judge it. The numbers attribute the error; they do not judge the look. Spec 27 § 3.1: an Opus look
   director writes two to four concrete observations per shot, the verdict table holds no severity 4 row,
   and the owner's eye is final. Never report a look as a count of passing tests.

## What a ★ means

A ★ beside a target in spec 27 § 2 marks a first guess: nobody has measured that row against the reference
yet, or the measurement did not support a fixed bar. A ★ row is reported, not enforced. When a lane measures
it (a run on the § 3.2 acceptance scenes, with the device, the head and the cache state stated), the measured
value replaces the ★ in the spec. A ★ is never removed by lowering the target to what the renderer reaches;
a platform that cannot meet a row gets a measured, platform-specific bound written into the spec (§ 6).

<!-- source: book/agents/testing.md -->
# Testing gameplay: pause, step, wait_until, expect

The protocol runs the game deterministically for you: pause, step exact frames, inject input, and
verify the world with predicates (`play.wait_until`) and assertions (`play.expect`). This is how
engine milestones verify themselves.

## Deterministic play

- `play.pause` / `play.resume` — freeze or unfreeze game time (frames keep rendering).
- `play.step {"frames": 10}` — while paused, run exactly 10 frames of game time, then answer with
  the new `frame`. One step at a time (a second call while stepping answers `F0009`). At most
  10,000 frames per call; a larger count answers `F0002`. The frame the request arrives on does
  not count when it ran no game time (it was paused), so `{"frames": 1}` always moves the game one
  frame.
- `play.set_time_scale {"scale": 0.5}` — slow motion (or fast-forward) without losing determinism.
  The scale is `0..=1000`.
- `play.get_diagnostics` — fps, frame times, entity count, draw calls.

### Conditions that hold only for a few frames

The game keeps running between your calls. A `play.wait_until` checks every frame, but only the
frames after it arrives: if you press a key and then send the wait, the frames in between are
never checked, and how many there are depends on how fast your client runs. For a short window
(a jump's apex, a character crossing a stair flight), pause first, set up and press the key while
paused, then `play.step {"frames": 1}` and `play.expect` the condition after each step until it
passes or a frame budget runs out; `play.resume` when done. Every frame from the key press on is
checked, on any machine (`samples/third_person/tests/agent_expect.rs` does this for the fox on the
stairs). Each `play.step` is a mutating call: a script that steps frame by frame for longer than
about 50 frames needs a higher `rate_limit_per_second` in the project's `.regia/agent.toml`
(refusals answer `F0007`).

## Injecting input

`play.inject_input` sends raw events (to the primary window) and/or scheduled action values:

```json
{ "events": [
    { "type": "key", "key": "KeyW", "text": "w", "state": "pressed" },
    { "type": "cursor", "x": 400, "y": 300 },
    { "type": "touch", "id": 0, "phase": "started", "x": 100, "y": 200 }
] }
```

```json
{ "actions": [
    { "action": "Move", "value": [0.0, 1.0], "at_frame": 120, "duration_frames": 10 },
    { "action": "Jump", "value": 1.0 }
] }
```

Action values are numbers, `[x, y(, z)]` arrays or `{x, y, z}` objects; `at_frame` defaults to now
and `duration_frames` to 1 (action injection needs `regia_input::InputPlugin` — otherwise `F0013`).
`at_frame` is clamped to 10 000 000 frames ahead and `duration_frames` to 1 000 000. The call does
not refuse a long `events` or `actions` list.

## Conditions

`wait_until` and `expect` share one condition grammar. Entities may be ids or lookups that
re-resolve every frame (`{"name": "Player*"}`, `{"component": "Player"}`) — lookups survive entity
churn.

| Condition | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `{ "entity": e, "component": "Transform", "path": "translation.y", "op": "gte", "value": 2.0 }` | A reflected field compares against `value`. `op`: `eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`. `path` uses reflection field names; omit it to compare the whole component |
| `{ "a": { "name": "Player" }, "b": { "name": "Door" }, "op": "within", "meters": 2.0 }` | Distance between two `Transform`s; `within` or `beyond` |
| `{ "resource": "GameSettings", "path": "input.sensitivity", "op": "eq", "value": 1.0 }` | A well-known resource: `GameSettings`, `SimCounters`, `Diagnostics`, `Time`, `QuickDraw` ([quick draw](book/agents/quick-draw.md)), `QuickDraw2d` ([quick draw 2D list](book/agents/quick-draw2d.md)), `Content` ([content chunks](book/agents/content-chunks.md): the manager's requests as `content.progress` answers, `requests.N.state`) |
| `{ "state": "GameFlow", "op": "eq", "value": "Playing" }` | A game state's current value (`null` while it does not exist); see [game states](book/agents/states.md) |
| `{ "logs_contain": "level started" }` | Any recent log record contains the text |
| `{ "events_contain": "toast" }` or `{ "events_contain": { "kind": "sim_event", "contains": "explosion" } }` | The tapped engine messages (see [events](book/agents/events.md)) |
| `{ "all": [c1, c2] }`, `{ "any": [c1, c2] }`, `{ "not": c1 }` | Combinators; `all` stops at the first failure |

## wait_until

`play.wait_until { condition, timeout_ms? }`:

```json
{ "condition": { "entity": { "name": "Player" }, "component": "Transform",
                 "path": "translation.x", "op": "gte", "value": 3.5 },
  "timeout_ms": 5000 }
→ { "satisfied": true, "frame": 240, "waited_ms": 1830, "detail": "..." }
```

The condition is polled every frame; the call answers when it holds, or with
`satisfied: false` and the last evaluation detail when `timeout_ms` (default 10 s, capped at
120 s) passes. A larger `timeout_ms` waits 120 s. A
timeout is a *result*, not an error — check `satisfied`. At most 64 waits are pending at once;
one more answers `too_many_pending` (JSON-RPC -32600). Send waits with an id: a notification has no
reply, so its wait only occupies a slot.

## expect

`play.expect { assertions }` evaluates assertions **now** and reports each one:

```json
{ "assertions": [
  { "name": "discs hover at 1.5 m", "condition": { "entity": { "component": "SimId" },
      "component": "Transform", "path": "translation.y", "op": "eq", "value": 1.5 } },
  { "name": "player moved", "condition": { "entity": 7, "component": "Transform",
      "path": "translation.x", "op": "gt", "value": 5.0 } }
] }
→ { "results": [{ "name": ..., "pass": true|false, "detail": ..., "error": ...? }],
    "passed": 1, "failed": 1, "pass": false }
```

A malformed condition marks that assertion failed with an `error` (it does not fail the call).
Capture state with [seeing](book/agents/seeing.md) screenshots for review evidence, and drive the frames with
`play.step` between assertions for exact reproducibility.

<!-- depth-2:method-reference -->

## Call reference

Parameters, results and error codes for every method on this page. Types and defaults come from the schema and handlers; limits include the contract. Error codes are in `data.code`; names explicitly labeled `data.reason` are additional handler reasons. Every method can also return `F0001`, `F0002`, `F0004`, `F0007` and `F0012`. The server can return `F0005`, `F0006`, `request_too_large`, or `F0008` when the method is not registered; see [protocol](book/agents/protocol.md).

Unless a lower or explicit method limit is listed, the dispatcher accepts at most 65,536 items in a top-level array parameter and 1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes in a string parameter. A limit violation returns `F0002`.

The request in each fence is the call that was sent with `regia agent call`.
The line under it is the host's answer.
A second fence tagged `json,ignore` is an error answer. Large fields are elided with `...`. A fence tagged `json,ignore` is a real call on a host or plugin method that the runtime schema does not list.


### `play.expect`

Evaluate assertions against the world now; returns a pass/fail report.

*Read, does not mutate.*

| Param | Type | Required | Default and limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `assertions` | array | yes | [{ name?, condition }]; conditions as for wait_until. |

`assertions` has at most 256 items.

Result: `{ results: [{ name, pass, detail, error? }], passed, failed, pass }`.

No error codes beyond the universal set.

```json
play.expect {"assertions": [{"name": "clock runs", "condition": {"resource": "Time", "path": "frame", "op": "gte", "value": 0}}]}
→ { "failed": 0, "pass": true, "passed": 1, "results": [ { "detail": "Time.frame = 297, gte 0", "error": null, "name": "clock runs", "pass": true } ] }
```

<!-- capture:play.expect -->

### `play.get_diagnostics`

Frame rate, frame times, entity count and memory of the running app.

*Read, does not mutate.*

No parameters.

Result: with Diagnostics installed, `{ fps, frame_time_avg_ms, fps_1pct_low, entity_count, draw_calls, allocated_bytes, frames, paused }` (allocated_bytes may be null). Without that resource: `{ note, frame, elapsed_secs, paused }`. Both also carry `game_frames` (frames that ran game time; a `play.step` adds exactly one), `injected_events` and `injected_keys` (raw events `play.inject_input` wrote; ADR-7831).

No error codes beyond the universal set.

```json
play.get_diagnostics {}
→ { "allocated_bytes": null, "draw_calls": 0, "entity_count": 202, "fps": 81.60769776034202, "fps_1pct_low": 8.763480138509959, "frame_time_avg_ms": 12.253746, "frames": 165, "paused": true }
```

`paused` reports the current Time pause flag.

<!-- capture:play.get_diagnostics -->

### `play.inject_input`

Inject raw input events and/or action values (deterministic, replayable).

*Play, mutating.*

| Param | Type | Required | Default and limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `events` | array | no | Raw events: { type: key/mouse_button/cursor/wheel/touch/back, ... }. |
| `actions` | array | no | { action, value, at_frame?, duration_frames? } — values: number, [x,y(,z)] or {x,y,z}. |

Result: `{ injected, scheduled, frame }`.

Errors besides the universal codes: `F0003`, `F0013`, `play_gate_text`.

A key event may set `scancode` (a physical key: a non-negative integer that fits in `u32`). The player sees `physical_key` `scancode:N` and an empty `logical_key`. A scancode together with non-empty `text` is `play_gate_text` and that batch writes nothing. A key that omits `scancode` still uses `key`. An omitted `text` on that name copies the name into `logical_key`.

```json
play.inject_input {"events": [{"type": "key", "key": "KeyW", "text": "w", "state": "pressed"}, {"type": "cursor", "x": 400, "y": 300}], "actions": [{"action": "Jump", "value": 1.0}]}
```

```json,ignore
→ { "message": "no InputInjection in this app", "code": -32004, "data": { "code": "F0013", "hint": "action injection needs regia_input::InputPlugin" } }
```

The host returned this error. `code` is the JSON-RPC code and `data` is the protocol object.

<!-- capture:play.inject_input -->

### `play.pause`

Pause gameplay time (frames keep rendering).

*Play, mutating.*

No parameters.

Result: `{ paused, frame }`.

Errors besides the universal codes: `F0018`.

```json
play.pause {}
→ { "frame": 165, "paused": true }
```

<!-- capture:play.pause -->

### `play.resume`

Resume gameplay time.

*Play, mutating.*

No parameters.

Result: `{ paused, frame }`.

Errors besides the universal codes: `F0018`.

```json
play.resume {}
→ { "frame": 299, "paused": false }
```

<!-- capture:play.resume -->

### `play.set_time_scale`

Set the gameplay time scale (1 = real time, 0.5 = slow motion).

*Play, mutating.*

| Param | Type | Required | Default and limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scale` | number | yes | New scale (0..=1000). |

Result: `{ before, after }`.

Errors besides the universal codes: `F0018`.

```json
play.set_time_scale {"scale": 0.5}
→ { "after": 0.5, "before": 1.0 }
```

<!-- capture:play.set_time_scale -->

### `play.step`

While paused, run exactly `frames` frames of game time, then answer.

*Play, mutating.*

| Param | Type | Required | Default and limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frames` | number | no | Frames to run (default 1, at most 10000). |
| `timeout_ms` | number | no | Answer deadline in ms (the connection waits this long plus a 5 s grace; default 30000). |

`frames` is from 1 to 10000.

Result: `{ frame, paused }`.

Errors besides the universal codes: `F0009`, `F0018`.

```json
play.step {"frames": 10}
→ { "frame": 310, "paused": true }
```

<!-- capture:play.step -->

### `play.wait_until`

Block until a world condition holds (checked every frame) or it times out.

*Read, does not mutate.*

| Param | Type | Required | Default and limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `condition` | object | yes | Predicate (see the guide's testing page): { all/any/not/entity/resource/state/logs_contain/events_contain }. |
| `timeout_ms` | number | no | Give up after this long (default 10000, capped at 120000). |

Result: `{ satisfied, frame, waited_ms, detail, last_error? }`.

Errors besides the universal codes: `F0014`, `too_many_pending` (both in `data.code`). At most 64 waits may be pending.

```json
play.wait_until {"condition": {"resource": "Time", "path": "frame", "op": "gte", "value": 1}, "timeout_ms": 5000}
→ { "detail": "Time.frame = 311, gte 1", "frame": 311, "satisfied": true, "waited_ms": 0 }
```

<!-- capture:play.wait_until -->

## Workflow: check one frame of gameplay

1. `play.pause`. The answer's `paused` is true and `frame` is the frame you are on.
2. `play.inject_input` with the key or action that should start the move.
3. `play.step` with `frames` 1. Wait for that answer before the next step. A second step while one is running is `F0009`.
4. `play.expect` the condition. A miss lists the failures; it does not throw the game away.
5. Repeat step and expect until the condition holds or you hit the frame budget you chose, then `play.resume`.
6. `F0007` limits mutating calls per second, not frames per call. Batch a known frame count into play.step when intermediate assertions are unnecessary, and wait for each response before submitting the next call.

<!-- source: book/agents/hitches.md -->
# Hitches (`play.hitch_report`, the DO27 soak)

`specs/27` § 2.4 makes zero hitches a hard gate: after a 2 s warm-up, no pipeline or bind group is
created on the frame path, no frame blocks on the GPU, no frame is over 50 ms, at most 0.1 % of
frames are over 2 × p50, p99/p50 ≤ 1.3, p99.9/p50 ≤ 2.0, and the longest frame is ≤ 2.5 × p50.

## Measuring a running app

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"play.hitch_report","params":{"seconds":60,"warmup_s":2,"drive":"chase","timeout_ms":62000}}
```

The reply arrives after `warmup_s + seconds`. Omit `timeout_ms` and the connection waits exactly 30000 ms, then answers `F0006` while the measurement continues; a second call is `F0017`. A present `timeout_ms` waits that many milliseconds (at most 24 h) plus a 5 s grace. Set it to at least `(warmup_s + seconds) × 1000` (62000 here; the grace is extra). Each frame's interval is `RealTime::raw_delta()` (not clamped to 250 ms, so a 4.7 s stall reads 4700 ms; what a
player sees); CPU and GPU times come from the `RuntimeRenderer`. The report turns its GPU
timestamps on for the run and off after; `gpu` is `null` only on a device without timestamp
queries. `gpu_passes` is the last frame's GPU time per pass (`shadows_ms`, `gi_ms` (GI Depth's probe
update and screen lookup; 0 under Balanced), `prepass_ms`, `forward_ms`, `ssao_ms`,
`contact_shadows_ms`, `ssgi_ms`, `ssr_ms`, `taau_ms`, `scene_ms`, `post_ms`, `frame_ms`, ...), which shows
where a GPU-bound frame goes (on a phone, see [render profile](book/agents/render-profile.md)).

`gpu_passes.nodes` lists the same frame's GPU-timed passes in graph order, each named after the frame-graph node
that records it (`[{ node, pass, ms }]`, ADR-5386): the names are the `render.graph` `dispatch.recorded` names, so a
slow pass points at a node of the [render graph](book/agents/render-graph.md). A pass is listed only when its closing timestamp
was written. `gi probes` there is the probe update alone; the irradiance screen lookup is its own entry
(`gi lookup`, node `ssao`, which records it). `gpu_passes.stamps_outside_nodes` lists every timestamp written outside
its node's record site (`[{ query, owner, written_in }]`); it is empty on a correct frame, and anything there means
a pass time mixes in another node's work. `gpu_passes` is `null` without timestamp queries.

Device calls are the renderer's process-wide counters:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `p50_ms`, `p99_ms`, `p999_ms`, `*_over_p50` | Frame-interval percentiles (nearest rank) and their ratio to the median |
| `over_2x_p50`, `over_50ms`, `longest_ms` | The hitch counts the gate reads |
| `device_calls` | `pipelines`, `bind_groups`, `blocking_polls`, `buffers`, `textures` (+ bytes), `upload_bytes`, `map_asyncs`, `submits`, `inline_sky_bakes` after warm-up |
| `bound` | What limited the measured frames, each frame's GPU time against its interval: `verdict` (`cpu_bound`, `gpu_bound`, `balanced`, `mixed` when no class has a majority, `unknown` without GPU timing), the frame count per class and `gpu_bound_pct`/`cpu_bound_pct`. GPU-bound: a lower render scale helps; CPU-bound: the GPU waits, so look at main-thread work, a frame cap or vsync. Same thresholds as `telemetry.live` |
| `creates`, `creates_dropped` | Every frame-path create after the warm-up, by `kind` (`pipeline`, `bind_group`, `buffer`, `texture`) and `label`, with `count`, `first_frame` and `last_frame` (measured frames from 0). `creates_dropped` counts creates the renderer's 32-entry create ring overwrote before a frame read it (more than 32 in one frame): counted in `device_calls`, not named |
| `blocking_poll_sites`, `blocking_poll_sites_unnamed` | Where the measured window's blocking polls (`device_calls.blocking_polls`) were called: one row per `TrackedDevice::poll` call site, `site` (`file:line` of the call) and `count`, most first. The renderer keeps the first 32 distinct sites of the process; waits from later sites are counted in `blocking_poll_sites_unnamed`, not named (ADR-4050) |
| `work` | The frame's own cost, not its interval (ADR-4947): per measured frame the larger of the CPU work (the display pacer's trace row: the frame's cost without the time blocked in the swapchain) and the GPU frame time, as `p50_ms`, `p99_ms`, `longest_ms`, with `cpu_p50_ms`/`cpu_p99_ms`, `frames` (frames with a pacer row) and `gpu_timed_frames`. On a vsync-paced panel `p99_ms` cannot drop under the refresh interval; `work.p99_ms` can, so it is what the Android `frame_p99` budget reads. `null` where no display pacer runs (desktop, headless) |
| `spikes` | The 32 worst frames over 2 × p50 with their CPU/GPU time, `bound` (the same class names, per frame) and creates |
| `streaming_waits` | Memory-pressure context over the measured window. The § 2.4 "no frame waits on a load" row has no numeric target, so it is reported here but **not judged** (`pass`/`failures` ignore it): `frames` (measured frames), `texture_held_frames` (frames the texture streamer held back mip uploads, within `MIP_HOLD` of its last out-of-memory signal) and `texture_backing_off_frames` (frames it backed off after a streamed texture failed to allocate), plus `render_residency` (`{ on, waits, timeouts, waiting_cells }`, deltas over the measured window; `null` without the render plugin). Nonzero values mean the streamer is under memory pressure: raise texture-memory headroom (pool size, quality) or prewarm. There is no per-frame upload-budget knob behind these counters |
| `pass`, `failures` | The verdict and every judged § 2.4 row missed, in words (the Streaming row is reported in `streaming_waits` but not judged) |

`creates` answers "what was created, and when" without a trace build. Ask for a short report
while the game does the thing that hitches (a cut, the first effect, a held camera), then look up
the labels in the table below:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"play.hitch_report","params":{"seconds":5,"warmup_s":2}}
```

```json
{"device_calls": {"bind_groups": 4, "pipelines": 0, "...": 0},
 "creates": [
   {"kind": "bind_group", "label": "hist bg", "count": 3, "first_frame": 212, "last_frame": 212},
   {"kind": "bind_group", "label": "post bg", "count": 1, "first_frame": 212, "last_frame": 212}],
 "creates_dropped": 0, "pass": false, "...": "..."}
```

The counters and `creates` see what the renderer creates through its tracked device
(`regia_render::TrackedDevice`). A crate that creates on a raw `wgpu::Device` is invisible here;
find it with the census build below.

`drive` names a scripted drive: the method inserts the `regia_agent::HitchDrive` resource for
the run and removes it after. A game that has scripted drives starts the named one when it sees the
resource. Only one report runs at a time (`F0017`).

## What causes a hitch, and the fix

| Signal in the report | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `bind_groups`/`buffers` > 0, labels `material bg`, `mesh vertex arena` (`mesh vb` before batch v020) | A material variant seen for the first time, or meshes that outgrew the mesh arenas (rocks streaming in) | `FrameRenderer::prewarm(device, variants, max_instances)` at level load; `ScatterField::prewarm_meshes()` lists every rock LOD × variant |
| `bind_groups` > 0, labels `gpu cull`, `instance objects`, `velocity objects` | A per-instance buffer grew past a power of two | The `max_instances` of `prewarm` |
| `inline_sky_bakes` > 0, 40–80 ms frames on sun moves or 10 m camera height changes | Atmosphere tables and the sky IBL integrated on the CPU inside the frame | `FrameRenderer::set_async_sky(true)` (on by default in `RuntimeRenderer`) |
| Long frames on camera cuts with `scatter update` time | A cut asks for a whole region's scatter tiles at once | `ScatterField::set_tile_budget(12)` (nearest tiles first) |
| One 50–300 ms frame about half a second after spawn, nearly all `scatter update`, only on CPUs with ≤ 12 threads and with the GPU probes on (Desktop High/Ultra) | Before ADR-176 (scatter stall): `ScatterField::update` waited for a needed tile's background placement, queued on the async pool (cpus / 4 threads) behind the probes' brick bakes | Fixed: a needed tile still queued is placed on the caller (`ScatterStreamStats::replaced_tiles`); `update` never waits for the pool. If it comes back, look for a new `block_on` of pool work on the frame thread |
| 100–600 ms frames with CPU ≈ normal, no creates, no run-queue wait, and one or two **major** page faults (`do27_chase` CSV `major_faults`, `spawn_major_faults`), on spawns; only on a box short of memory | The spawn read data nothing else read for seconds (the terrain heights where the effect lands) and the OS had swapped it out | Data a frame may read at any point registers a `regia_core::residency::ResidentRegion` (`TerrainMap` does); `regia_app::ResidencyPlugin` (in `DefaultPlugins`) keeps it paged in. Reproduce on a loaded box, or with `do27_chase --memory-squeeze MB[:MS][:file]` / `SPAWN_SOAK_SQUEEZE` (mind: a few MiB/s already thrashes) |
| `bind_groups`/`buffers` > 0 on spawn frames in the runtime, labels `gpu cull`, `instance objects`, `velocity objects` | Spawned objects pushed the per-instance buffers past a power of two | `RuntimeRenderer` reserves 1024 draws (`RUNTIME_INSTANCE_RESERVE`); call `RuntimeRenderer::reserve_instances(n)` at level load for more |
| Every ~20 s a burst of `sssr *`, `spd depth`, `spd params`, `spd unused level` creates (≈ 70 MB of textures at 1440p), with an `sssr probe` bind group ~150 frames before it | Before ADR-168: the stochastic SSR pass went dormant when nothing glossy was in view, freed its targets, and re-allocated them on the wake | Fixed: dormant keeps the targets (≈ 185 MiB at 1440p, ≈ 416 MiB at 4K) and zeroes them on the wake. If these labels come back, something freed them: `FrameRenderer::trim_memory()` / `regia_render::signal_memory_pressure()` (the OS low-memory event) do on purpose, a resize or quality change does too |
| `pipelines`/`bind_groups`/`buffers` = 1 each on the first dust or smoke spawn, labels `vfx soft composite`, `vfx soft composite bg`, `vfx soft composite params` | Before midplay-creates: the soft-particle layer built its composite pipeline and bind group on its first soft particle | Fixed: built on the first HDR frame that enables the layer (warm-up), whether or not soft particles are alive |

`residency` (present when the keeper runs): `data_bytes` and `code_bytes` swept, `pages` per sweep,
`sweeps` and `restored_pages` during the run (pages found paged out and read back by the keeper's
thread, each a major fault a frame did not take), `last_sweep_us`/`max_sweep_us`. `sweeps`,
`restored_pages` and `max_sweep_us` accumulate across suspends: a suspend stops the sweep thread and
a resume starts a new one, and the totals add up (so the `end - start` window above stays correct
when the app suspends and resumes inside it).
`REGIA_KEEP_RESIDENT=0` turns the keeper off for an A/B; `=code` also sweeps the code.

## Spawning without hitches (`drive: "spawns"`)

`samples/arena` maps `HitchDrive { name: "spawns" }` onto its `SpawnDrive`: every 0.25 s a crate
(shared mesh and material, a dynamic body, a box collider), a showcase effect, a scorch decal and a
positional sound, the oldest crates despawned. Through the runtime frame (a texture-target camera)
`samples/arena/tests/spawn_hitch.rs` asks for the report over a real connection (wall-clock time:
`enable_fixed_step` would make every frame a synthetic 16.7 ms) and requires zero device calls after
the warm-up and, on a hardware GPU, no frame that spawned over 50 ms; it prints the spawn frames'
p99 and worst, and the long frames without a spawn (the machine's, on a shared box):

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"play.hitch_report","params":{"seconds":60,"warmup_s":3,"drive":"spawns","timeout_ms":63000}}
```

The spawn path carries spans for a profiler or `do27_chase --slow-spans`: `vfx_spawn`,
`vfx_schedule`, `vfx_upload`, `decal_spawn`/`decal_update`, `scene_spawn`, `prefab_instantiate`,
`cooked_scene_spawn`, `level_spawn`, `asset_load` (with `kind`), `mesh_upload` and `material_upload`
(the renderer's first sight of a mesh or material), `audio_drain`, `audio_start_voice`,
`audio_start_emitter`, and the existing `sync_added_bodies` (physics) and `ScatterField::update`
(scatter re-tile). In `do27_chase` the soak's spawn step is the top-level `soak_spawn` span and the
`spawn_ms` column.

`SPAWN_SOAK_SPANS=1` on the arena test times every span per frame and prints, per span, the mean
time and entries on spawn frames against other frames, and the span breakdown of the five slowest
spawn frames with the frame before each. Read the entries before blaming the spawn: a time-driven
spawn lands on the frame after a long one, which also runs more fixed physics steps (2026-10-08 on
a loaded 5090: 1.5 steps against 0.87, every span ≈ 25 % slower; `spawn_drive` itself 0.06 ms).

## The DO27 soak (look-dev)

`do27_chase --soak long|minute` drives every region of both DO27 maps through the full runtime
frame (a boustrophedon over 84 % of each map after the road), cuts to the UE plate cameras and to
teleports every 12 s, jumps the time of day every 20 s, and spawns VFX plus a decal every 4 s (`--spawn-every-s S` for a spawn burst). It
prints this same report per map; `--timeline-dir DIR` writes `<map>.csv` (one row per frame:
wall, CPU phases, GPU, run-queue wait, every counter, events), `<map>.png` (the plot, legend in
`soak_plot.rs`) and `<map>-report.txt` (creates by label, the worst frames and what happened in
them). `--bare` reproduces the frame path of 2026-10-07 (no prewarm, no tile budget, inline sky).
`--submit-probe N` measures the box itself: `queue.submit` of an empty frame and a fixed CPU
workload. On a shared machine, read that floor before blaming the engine for CPU-side spikes.

To find creates the counters cannot see (a crate holding a raw `wgpu::Device`), build with
`cargo run -p lookdev --features wgpu-spans --bin do27_chase -- --census ...`. Every
`Device::create_*` inside a frame is printed with its call chain. `--slow-spans MS` prints the span
breakdown of every frame longer than `MS`.

## Soak on a DO27 bundle (lookdev harness)

This is a developer harness, not an agent method. `do27_chase --soak minute --content <bundle>` runs the hitch soak on a
DO27 content bundle named on the command line (read-only; `REGIA_DO27_CONTENT` is the fallback).
`--hitch-csv <path>` writes one row per measured frame (`frame,t_s,wall_ms,ratio,hitch,events`); `hitch` is 1 when the
frame took more than twice the run's median. `--camera-path orbit|line|figure8` replaces the plate-camera cuts with a
deterministic path. An output path inside the bundle is refused.

## Held views and plate cameras (ADR-2585)

A held camera freezes after 32 frames on a TAAU tier: the screen-space passes stop and post reads the resolve's last
output. A hitch after a cut to a plate camera is checked with a drive like the soak's, without DO27 content:
`cargo test -p regia_render --test warm_drive_creates` (a warm-up, a held camera until it freezes, a cut back to moving
frames, a second held camera; it asserts zero bind groups and pipelines after the warm-up, by label). On lavapipe the
same drive reproduced the soak's `hist bg` ×3 + `post bg` on the second hold before the fix. The fade overlay, HDR
display stage, fullscreen video, HW-RT shadow passes and outdoor targets now appear in `play.hitch_report` `creates`
when they create after the warm-up, as every other frame-path create does.

An empty VFX layer leaves the frame after its first 8 frames: an agent comparing `play.hitch_report` or the frame
timings with and without the layer should see no difference until an effect spawns.

## Counter ledger (integer caps, ADR-3943)

Frame-time milliseconds stay on the report above (`p50_ms`, `over_50ms`, `over_2x_p50`, the percentile
ratios). The create gate is also a named integer ledger, `regia_render::budget_ledger::BudgetLedger`.
A test records deltas and reads `misses(warm)`. `warm` is the first measured frame, the same index the
hitch recorder's report takes. A sum greater than the cap is a miss. A sum equal to the cap is not.

| Name | Default cap after `warm` | Where an agent reads the same integer |
|---|---|---|
| `pipeline_creates` | 0 | `play.hitch_report` `device_calls.pipelines`; `render.frame_work` `frame.pipelines_created` |
| `bind_group_creates` | 0 | `device_calls.bind_groups`; `frame.bind_groups_created` |
| `allocations` | none, until a caller sets one | `device_calls.buffers` and `device_calls.textures`; `frame.heap_allocations`, `buffers_created`, `textures_created` |
| `idle_frames` | none, until a caller sets one | recorded by the caller; this report leaves the name empty |
| `probe_prepares` | none, until a caller sets one | recorded by the caller; this report leaves the name empty |

`play.hitch_report` and `render.frame_work` already return these integers, so the protocol has no
separate ledger method. A pipeline-create delta of 1 on a measured frame is a miss. A delta of 0 is
not. An allocation under a cap the caller installed is not a miss. The ledger does not read a clock.

The hitch-frame feeder copies only pipeline and bind-group creations. For `allocations`, the caller
chooses a heap or device allocation count and records it explicitly; the fields above describe
available inputs. Use one consistent allocation metric when installing its cap. A `null`
`heap_allocations` value means that measurement is unavailable.

A newly accepted capture excludes the frame interval that ended before the request.
Warm-up and measurement count subsequent clock intervals, including their full unclamped
durations; a long startup interval cannot complete a capture before its drive has run.

## Hitches in player logs (v0.5.1)

`play.hitch_report` attributes one frame on request. The always-on `regia::hitch` telemetry event
classifies hitches the same way since v0.5.1 (ADR-7898): a frame spent waiting on the swapchain is
a `present_wait`, not a hitch; a frame under 1.5 pacing periods (frame cap or vsync) is never one;
the `cause` comes from the main and render threads only (worker spans are `background_spans`);
and `unaccounted_ms` with cause `outside_frame` marks time the engine did not measure at all. The
thresholds an agent can read are in `telemetry.live` (`thresholds.hitch_floor_ms`,
`pacing_period_ms`, `present_wait_share`). See [Telemetry](book/agents/telemetry.md#hitch-truth-v051-adr-7898).

<!-- source: book/agents/instant-load.md -->
# Instant load (boot splash, pipeline warm-up, load sets, memory budget)

DO27's "feels instant" budget — branding < 1 s, menu interactive < 1 s, Ready → in control < 1 s with no
loading screen — is checked through four methods registered as read-only. Specs: `docs/specs/13-renderer.md` § 2b–2c,
`docs/specs/12-assets.md` § 5b; cooked content layout: `docs/formats/cooked-pack-guide.md`.

## Boot timeline

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"render.boot_timeline","params":{}}
```

Returns `{ now_ms, marks: [{ mark, ms }] }`, milliseconds since the process started (Linux/Android read the
process start from `/proc`; elsewhere the clock starts at the first mark). Engine marks: `plugin_build`,
`resumed`, `device`, `surface`, `first_present`, `boot_tier_ready`, `menu_tier_ready`, `game_warm_start`,
`game_warm_done`, `first_game_frame`, `splash_done`, `splash_capped` (the 1.5 s cap ended the splash while a
game-frame warm still ran) and `boot_background_idle` (warm, deferred variants and quality probe all done).
Games add their own with `regia_render::boot::mark_named("menu_interactive")`. Check: `first_present` ≤ 500 ms
warm, `splash_done` ≤ 1500 ms on every launch (cold or warm, first launch included) when the host has called
`finish()` by then and `first_present` came before 1.25 s (the cap minus the 250 ms fade; a splash shown later
still fades in full).

## Splash cap and background boot (ADR-173)

The splash is gone 1.5 s after process start at the latest, fade-out included (`BootSplash::max_duration`,
default `regia_render::SPLASH_MAX_DURATION`; `REGIA_SPLASH_MAX_MS` overrides it, `0` = no cap). Once the host
has called `finish()`, the cap overrides every engine hold: a running game-frame warm, `min_duration`. It
never fades a splash the host has not finished. What is not done by then continues behind the host's first
scene:

- the game-frame warm stays on its warm worker. The window draws no scene until it is back, only the clear
  color plus the UI overlay (the loading path), so nothing compiles on the frame path;
- deferred variants build in the background after the first game frame (ADR-161); a draw whose variant is not
  ready is skipped;
- the splash's own pipeline is the boot tier's first job when the queue exists (`BootSplash::set_warm_queue`, which
  the renderer does itself, ADR-5131): the first present clears to the splash background and the image and text fade
  in once the job is done, so not even the splash compiles on the presenting thread. A host that calls
  `set_warm_queue(None)` keeps the splash pipeline on the presenting thread (ADR-5620);
- the overlay layers (lobby UI) are the boot tier's next job, so they are built before the cap; a layer installed
  after the queue started (the runtime UI sets its layer in `Startup`, after the first resume), or one that replaces
  a layer under the same name, gets its own boot-tier job (ADR-5131, ADR-5620);
- the first-launch quality probe runs on a warm worker after the splash and the warm: its own renderer draws
  the scene offscreen at the window's size back to back for ~3–4 s and holds nothing (a level load aborts it;
  `quality_probe_start` / `quality_probe_done` marks).

`regia_render::BootBackground` (resource, refreshed each `PreUpdate`) tells hosts where this stands:
`splash_done`, `splash_capped`, `game_warm_pending`, `game_warm_running`, `deferred_pending`, `probe_active`, and
`warm_done()`, `probe_done()`, `is_idle()`. Agents read the same under `render.pipeline_warm` →
`boot_background` (`splash_done`, `splash_capped`, `game_warm_pending`, `game_warm_running`, `deferred_pending`,
`probe_active`, `idle`).

## Pipeline warm-up and the persistent cache

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"render.pipeline_warm","params":{}}
```

The method stays `Read` (`mutating: false`). On a headless host, `offscreen: { width, height }` starts a warm that moves the live renderer onto its own thread and leaves a stand-in in its place until the warm is put back. `render.out_start` answers `F0018` until then. A host that already has a window does not start that warm.

Per tier (`boot`, `menu`, `lobby`, `map`, `optional`): jobs done/total/failed, pipelines built, worker time and
`ready_after_ms`; `pipelines_outside` counts pipelines created outside the warm workers (the frame path, load
code) — after warm-up a steady frame adds none. `cache.load` is `missing` (first launch on this adapter/driver),
`loaded` with its bytes, `discarded` with the reason (driver update, shader change, corruption), or `seeded`
(no usable local file; a shipped cache for this exact GPU and driver was used, see below). `cache.shipped` says
what the package's caches gave when they were consulted: `no_match`, `seeded` with the file, or `discarded` with
the file and the reason. The cache is saved once on a background thread right after the first game frame, so a
first launch closed before the warm queue drains keeps the first frame's pipelines (ADR-5857), and again when the
queue drains (`cache.saves`, `saved_bytes`). `cache.skipped`
names a driver rule that left the device without the engine cache (`null` otherwise): Intel's Windows Vulkan driver
since v0.2.15 (ADR-3288; `platform.paths` shows `driver_skipped`). `deferred`
counts the rarely used pipeline variants waiting for a background build (`pending`), built so far (`built`),
and whether the first game frame released them (`released`).

## Install prepare

`regia prepare --cache-dir <game pipeline cache>` (or `regia_render::prepare::run`) warms the splash and the
canonical lit frame headless, on the Boot thread budget, and writes `prepare-stamp.json` next to the `.fpc`.
A later launch with the same cache key and the same unit list skips. Progress is one JSON object per line on
stdout; `prepare-status.json` is what a launcher polls (`running` older than 45 s is `stale`). The command
never presents, so the queue stays in Boot. `--profile` adds that preset's frame to the unit list. Background
priority is on unless `--no-nice`. See the DO27 host checklist, "Install prepare (batch v020)".

## One device holds the cache

One device per process holds the persistent cache. A headless device opened while a live device holds it compiles
without a cache and leaves the file alone; a window's device takes the cache over from a headless one, and the
headless device keeps working uncached. `pipeline_cache::status` reports the device that holds it.

## Shipped pipeline caches

A Vulkan pipeline cache only helps on the GPU and driver that wrote it, so a package carries one per GPU × driver
it was warmed on. Build them on each test machine by running the game (or `boot_gpu --game --profile <tier>`
for each render profile the game ships) with `REGIA_PIPELINE_CACHE_DIR=<dir>`: every tier accumulates in one
`pipelines-vulkan-<vendor>-<device>.fpc` per GPU. Collect the files into `<project>/pipeline-caches/` (or pass
`--pipeline-caches DIR`) and `regia package --platform linux|windows` validates each one (header, key,
checksum: a broken file fails the package), renames it to its key's shipped name
(`pipelines-vulkan-<vendor>-<device>-<key hash>.fpc`, so two drivers of one GPU sit side by side) and puts it in
`content/pipelines/`. `build_info.json` lists them (`pipeline_caches`: vendor, device, driver, wgpu, shader hash).

At runtime the shipped directory (`<exe dir>/content/pipelines`; `REGIA_SHIPPED_PIPELINE_CACHE_DIR` or
`pipeline_cache::set_shipped_directory` override it) is read only when the local cache is missing or unusable,
and only a file whose whole key matches (backend, vendor, device, driver name and version, wgpu, shader hash)
is used. It passes the same checks as a local file, then wgpu's header check (adapter, driver pipeline-cache
UUID) and the driver's own; any rejection means an empty cache and a normal compile behind the splash, never a
crash (`tests/shipped_pipeline_cache.rs` feeds another driver's key, garbage, and payloads with a corrupted
wgpu or driver header). The first save writes the local cache, so later launches do not read the shipped one.

The checksum catches corruption, not forgery: a cache payload goes to the GPU driver, so the local cache
directory and the shipped directory are trusted like the executable. Never point
`REGIA_SHIPPED_PIPELINE_CACHE_DIR` or `REGIA_PIPELINE_CACHE_DIR` at a directory that other users or
downloaded content can write.

Measured with `boot_gpu --game` (headless; the `boot_probe --game` frame warmed like `GameFrameWarm`, both
caches empty for cold), game-frame warm on the worker:

| GPU (driver) | before: cold / seeded / warm | after: cold / seeded / warm |
|---|---|---|
| RTX 5090 (615.71.09; loaded farm host, 48 niced cores) | 12.9–14.3 s / 3.4–4.2 s / 1.14–1.20 s | 6.1–7.6 s / 1.31–1.41 s / 1.01–1.18 s |
| RTX 3080 Ti (615.78.08) | 7.6–7.7 s / 2.08–2.11 s / 1.05–1.06 s | 3.71–3.74 s / 1.05–1.06 s / 0.96–0.98 s |
| GTX 1080 (580.173.02) | 8.5–8.9 s / 2.72–3.07 s / 1.42–1.49 s | 3.84–3.92 s / 1.37–1.40 s / 1.29–1.32 s |
| RTX 5080 (615.71.09) | 5.6–6.8 s / — / 0.63 s ¹ | 2.24–2.34 s / 0.60–0.63 s / 0.52–0.57 s |

¹ boot-fast's windowed `boot_probe --game` numbers (47 pipelines then); the rig's GPU queue was too long to rerun
the old code headless.

cold = first launch, both caches empty; seeded = first launch with the package's cache for this GPU (driver disk
cache still empty); warm = second launch. "Before" seeded is the shipped cache on the old pipeline set, where 20
uncached sites still compiled. Desktop High and Ultra build the same 59 pipelines for this frame. The first
1920×1080 frame after the warm creates 0 pipelines in every run; the deferred variants then build in the
background (1–4 s of worker time cold, none once cached).
No GPU in the set (an AMD card, another NVIDIA driver): the launch compiles, which the cold column covers.

## Cold compile: only what the game frame draws

`warm_site_costs(n)` (and `boot_gpu`'s `slowest_sites`) lists the creation sites a warm spent its time in. A cold
NVIDIA driver spends 0.4–1.4 s per variant of the forward uber shader, so:

- **Deferred variants.** The forward set's blend, premultiplied, additive and five glass transmission pipelines
  (per format and cull mode) are `pipeline_warm::DeferredPipeline`s. The warm (`warm_scene` / `warm_extracted`,
  hence `GameFrameWarm` and `BootSplash::finish()`) builds every variant a material of its frame can draw, visible
  or not, so the level's glass and blended materials are ready when the splash fades. Variants no loaded material
  uses build on the warm workers after the first game frame (`release_deferred`; `GameFrameWarm` and
  `RendererWarm::take` call it). A material that appears later, before its variant is ready, is skipped for that
  frame and its build jumps the queue (`DeferredPipeline::try_get`): the frame path never compiles or waits.
  `pipeline_warm::blocking_scope()` lets a loading screen wait instead. Without warm workers the variants are
  built eagerly.
- **Side by side.** Independent compiles run on helper threads (`pipeline_warm::join` / `join_all`, which keep
  the warm tier and the frame counters of the calling thread): the opaque forward pipeline beside depth, shadow and
  sky; the culled and cull-none forward sets; the GPU-driven forward variants; DDGI's eight and SSSR's seven compute
  pipelines.
- **Every pipeline is cached and counted.** Twenty creation sites (TAA sharpen, DDGI, SSSR, SMAA, depth pyramid,
  contact shadows, visibility-buffer shadows, lens, display stage, gizmos, immediate mode, terrain VT, VFX sort,
  2D) passed no pipeline cache, so a cache never covered them and `pipelines_outside` never saw them. They go
  through `pipeline_cache::cache_for` now.

`game_frame` is the runtime renderer's own warm (`regia_render::GameFrameWarm`): `pending`, `warming`,
`last { ms, pipelines, error }` and `first_frame_ms`, the CPU time of the first scene frame after it. With a
`BootSplash`, the splash's `finish()` requests it: the runtime renderer moves onto a warm worker, renders the
extracted frame at 64×64 and once at the window's size (so the first visible frame allocates no targets
either: the 28–36 ms first-frame hitch on an RTX 5080 moves onto the worker), and comes back while the splash
holds (up to the cap); the first game frame then creates no pipeline (`pipelines_outside` does not move). A later level load calls `GameFrameWarm::request()` once the level
is spawned. Check: `game_frame.first_frame_ms` < 50 and `pipelines_outside` unchanged after `game_warm_done`.

A large new scene on a window that showed none (a map spawned behind a UI-only menu: 32 MiB or 256 meshes the
runtime renderer has not uploaded) is warmed the same way without a call (v0.1.8, ADR-190): `game_frame.on_new_scene`
(default `true`, `REGIA_SCENE_WARM=0` turns it off) and `game_frame.scene_warms` (how many ran; boot mark
`scene_warm_request`). The window keeps presenting the clear color and the UI meanwhile. Check after a map loads
behind the menu: `scene_warms` moved, and `pipelines_outside` did not move on the map's first frame.
`boot_probe --exit --late-scene-s 3 [--map-mb 1024]` reproduces that order (its `late_scene` block: longest
main-loop interval after the spawn, intervals over 250 ms and over 5 s); `boot_gpu --late-map MB --mode inline|warm
--game` measures the same first frame headless (NVIDIA on a farm).

A game queues its own tiers (DO27: the menu backdrop, then both alpha maps behind the menu):

<!-- ignore-reason: names `wgpu::TextureFormat`, and wgpu is not a dependency of the book's snippet crate -->
```rust,ignore
let format = surfaces.primary_format().unwrap_or(wgpu::TextureFormat::Bgra8UnormSrgb);
queue.push(WarmTier::Map, "map:switchbacks frame", pipeline_warm::frame_job(map_frame.clone(), format));
```

## Load sets

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"assets.load_progress","params":{"set":"map:switchbacks"}}
```

Returns `{ sets: [{ name, resident, items_resident, items_total, fraction, kinds: [...], failed }] }`. `resident`
is the answer to "can Ready switch to this map now?". Kinds: `texture`, `mesh`, `material`, `terrain_tile`,
`audio_bank`, `pipeline` (warm job labels), `other`. Omit `set` for every defined set.

## Memory budget and admission

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"method":"render.memory_budget","params":{"tier":"minimum","set":"map:bore_twelve"}}
```

Returns the tier's budget (`minimum` = RTX 2080 class: 6.5 GiB VRAM, 10 GiB RSS; `deck`; `desktop_high`;
`integrated_low` = the integrated-GPU floor Very Low is sized for: 1.5 GiB GPU memory, 2.5 GiB RSS, ADR-8878), the
measured GPU bytes by category and RSS, every load set's estimated and still-pending bytes, and with `set` the
admission check `{ fits, vram_after, ram_after, reason }` — whether that set can be preloaded now. A side
that is not measured (`use.vram_measured` false: GL, Metal and WebGPU have no allocator report; `use.ram` 0: no
resident-set sample on this OS) gives `fits: false` with a reason that names it, never an approval against an
empty baseline. Byte totals saturate at the largest u64 instead of wrapping.

Nothing picks the budget tier for you: `tier` defaults to `minimum`, and a host that runs the Very Low quality tier
asks with `{"tier":"integrated_low"}`. An unknown tier is an invalid-params error (`F0002`) whose message lists every
tier name.

## Probe

`cargo run -p boot_probe -- --exit [--game]` shows a splash, warms the boot tier, finishes the splash when its
scene is spawned (the engine then warms the runtime renderer on it), fades into the lit scene and, once the
splash is gone and the scene has drawn, prints `BOOT_PROBE {json}` (timeline, warm report, `game_warm`,
`first_game_frame_ms`, `max_frame_ms_after_splash`, `pipelines_outside_after_warm`, `splash_capped`). `--game` uses Desktop Ultra with sky, clouds and volumetric fog. Run it twice with `REGIA_PIPELINE_CACHE_DIR` set to
compare a cold and a warm pipeline cache; set `__GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE=0` (NVIDIA) or
`MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DISABLE=true` (Mesa) for a cold driver cache.

On a GPU that cannot present to the machine's display (NVIDIA under a farm's Xvfb), `boot_gpu --cache-dir DIR
--game [--profile ultra|high|low|deck]` runs the same warm headless and prints `BOOT_GPU {json}`: `game { ms,
pipelines, after_warm_pipelines, first_frame_ms }` (the first 1920×1080 frame after the warm; `after_warm_pipelines`
must be 0), `deferred_ms`, `slowest_sites`, and `cache.shipped`.
`docs/evidence/perf/shipped-shader-cache-20261009/cold_warm.sh` runs cold, warm and seeded per profile and writes
the GPU's shipped cache (`SHIP_OUT`).

## Scene ready

`render.scene_ready` (ADR-7883) is the host's scene prepare: one state with a single ready edge, instead of
polling the warm counters. The host spawns its map behind its loading page and calls
`SceneReadiness::prepare(map_id)` (resource `regia_render::SceneReadiness`). From that call until ready the window
keeps presenting the host's UI and does not draw the scene, while `GameFrameWarm` warms the runtime renderer on the
extracted frame on a warm worker: every mesh and texture the frame references is uploaded (all of them, not the
first 32 MiB) and the pipelines of every draw key are created. When a warm round returns and the frame holds a mesh
or material the round did not see (a spawn that landed after it started), it warms again, up to
`SCENE_PREPARE_MAX_ROUNDS` (8) rounds; the new-scene warm's once-per-stretch lock-out does not apply while a
prepare is open. Hosts that never prepare keep the size-threshold warm. A warm that started with nothing to upload
(a backdrop already resident) no longer uses up the scene-less stretch either: the map that arrives while it runs is
warmed after it (DO27 tester A2's order).

```text
{ "method": "render.scene_ready", "params": {} }
→ { "state": "presented", "map_id": "switchbacks", "prepare": 1, "uploaded_mb": 340.2, "meshes": 183,
    "pipelines": 85, "warms": 2, "ms": 41012.5, "timed_out": false, "error": null, "complete": true,
    "first_present_frame": 912, "first_present_ms": 41230.1, "presented_to_window": true }
```

`state` walks `idle` (no prepare yet) → `preparing` (warming; the scene is held) → `resident` (warmed; the first
scene frame is being drawn and presented) → `presented`. `wait_until` on `render.scene_ready` with `state ==
"presented"` is the agent's "the map is on screen". At the `presented` edge the engine sends the ECS message
`regia_render::SceneReady` once per prepare: after `queue.present` returned for the first frame that drew the scene
(on the frame generation path, after its present thread presented that frame's rendered image; a suspend that drops
the image re-arms it), never on CPU time. Gate audio, player control and the loading page on it.

- `timed_out`: a warm round was cancelled or abandoned by the watchdog (`GameFrameWarm::timeout`), the warm queue ran
  on another device, or no renderable frame came within `GameFrameWarm::request_grace` (10 s). The prepare still
  ends in `presented` (late): a host never waits forever. `error` says why.
- `complete`: whether the first scene frame found every mesh resident and created no pipeline on the frame thread.
- `presented_to_window: false`: headless apps and hidden windows present nothing. A hidden window reaches `presented`
  on the first tick the scene is resident and renderable. A headless app with a render device and a started
  `PipelineWarmQueue` runs the same warm rounds as the window (a frame with no window view warms its render-to-texture
  views) and reaches `presented` once the frame thread submitted a texture-view frame of the resident scene (the tick
  after it turned resident), or right after its warm when the frame has no texture view (the warm drew and submitted
  it). Its texture views are held, like the window's scene, while the prepare warms. A resident headless prepare that
  sees no submitted frame within `request_grace` ends with `timed_out`. Without a render device nothing warms or
  draws: `presented` on the first renderable tick (ADR-8122).
- On the frame generation path only the present of the scene's own image counts: when the real image's acquire
  fails after the generated image was queued, the prepare stays `resident` and the next drawn frame is its first
  (ADR-8122).
- A new `prepare` before the last one was presented replaces it; only the newest sends `SceneReady`.
- Hosts that draw into their own targets (benchmarks) drive the same logic with `GameFrameWarm::host_tick` and
  `GameFrameWarm::host_presented`. `boot_gpu --late-map 340 --mode prepare --game` and `boot_gpu
  --late-map-split 40,300 --mode prepare|auto --game` measure the map's first frame (pipelines, upload MB) with and
  without the prepare.

Telemetry: `scene_load_end` gains `map` (the prepare's map id) and `complete` (false when the first scene frame after
the warm still uploaded or compiled, or another warm was needed); it is sent once that is known. A `scene_ready`
phase goes out at the `presented` edge with `first_present_ms`, `frame`, the warm totals, `complete`, `presented`
and `timed_out`.

Error codes: `F0011` (no scene readiness: the render plugin was not added).


## Load budget

A warm covers what the scene held when it ran. What lands after it (a late spawn, a streaming LOD swap, a warm the
watchdog gave up on) used to upload and compile on the frame that first drew it: one frame of 200-500 ms on a
tester's map (ADR-7884). `FrameRenderer::set_load_budget(FrameLoadBudget { .. })` bounds that frame.

| Field | Default | Under `late: Defer` |
|---|---|---|
| `upload_bytes_per_frame` | `None` | Meshes the frame references but has not uploaded are taken nearest first (squared distance from the eye to the instance's origin, ties in submission order) while the frame's mesh bytes are under the cap. The mesh that crosses it still lands, so a frame uploads at most the cap plus one mesh; the rest wait for the next frames and their draws are skipped meanwhile. |
| `new_pipelines_per_frame` | `None` | A material graph whose pipeline set would take the frame thread past this many pipelines in the frame builds on the material-graph worker threads; its draws are skipped until the set lands. The set size is the largest set built so far (32 before the first). |
| `late` | `Block` | `Block` ignores both caps: every frame uploads and builds what it draws, as before. |

`FrameLoadBudget::RECOMMENDED_60FPS` is 64 MiB, 8 pipelines, `Defer`. The trade: a late object appears a few frames
later instead of costing one long frame. Ephemeral meshes (`mesh_key` 0) are never deferred. Warm jobs and blocking
scopes are never budgeted. The budget is per `render_into` call (one view). The engine's deferred blended,
transmissive, mask-decal and thin-film variants already skip their draw and build on the warm workers when a
`PipelineWarmQueue` runs. When the material-graph workers cannot take a set (they cannot start, or were shut
down), `Defer` builds it on the frame thread only as the frame's first pipeline work (one set past the cap, like the
mesh that crosses the upload cap) and the other draws wait for the next frames (ADR-8122).

**What `Defer` does not bound.** A frame-level forward set (`lab forward`, `lab depth`, `lab shadow`, `lab sky` and the
GPU-driven colour variants of one `PipelineKey`: target format, sample count, sun trace, many-light, double-sided) is
still built on the frame that first needs it, whatever the budget: without its set the frame cannot draw any of its
scene, so there is nothing to draw "a few frames later". That is the stall class of DO27 tester A2's first gameplay
frame (79 pipelines). Cover it with the warm instead: `SceneReadiness::prepare` warms the map's frame (its key at the
window's size) before the scene is shown, and `pipeline_warm::register_warm_target` covers every other target the
host renders into (see Targets and late pipelines below). A settings change that makes a new key mid-play (MSAA, the
sun trace) builds the set on the frame that applies it.

`FrameRenderer::load_budget_report()` has the last frame's counters: `deferred_meshes`, `deferred_bytes`,
`deferred_draws`, `async_pipelines_pending` (graph sets on their workers plus the deferred variants, process-wide),
`admitted_meshes`, `admitted_bytes`, `async_graph_sets` and `bursts`. A `debug` line on target `regia_render` marks the
start and the end of each deferral burst, never every frame.

| Method | Params | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `render.load_budget` | none | `{ budget: { upload_bytes_per_frame, new_pipelines_per_frame, late, active }, last_frame: { deferred_meshes, deferred_bytes, deferred_draws, async_pipelines_pending, admitted_meshes, admitted_bytes, async_graph_sets, bursts } }` |
| `render.set_load_budget` | `upload_bytes_per_frame?`, `new_pipelines_per_frame?` (positive integers, or null for no cap), `late?` (`block`, `defer`), `recommended?`, `reset?` | `{ before, after }` (each a `budget` object) |

Absent fields keep their value; `recommended: true` starts from the recommended budget, `reset: true` from the
default. Applies from the next frame; not persisted.

Errors: `load_budget_renderer_missing` (no `RuntimeRenderer`), `load_budget_bad_param` (a cap that is not a positive
integer or null, `new_pipelines_per_frame` past 32 bits, `late` not `block` or `defer`, a flag that is not a boolean,
or `recommended` and `reset` together; the budget is unchanged).

Check: `cargo test -p regia_render --test load_budget` (lavapipe): a 300 MiB burst under 64 MiB uploads at most 64 MiB
plus one mesh per frame and draws what the `Block` run draws once resident; 40 new graph keys under 8 pipelines create
at most 8 pipelines and no blocking poll per frame on the frame thread; the default and `Block` with caps match.
Measure: `boot_gpu --late-map 340 --mode inline --game --load-budget 64,8` (report `late_map.load_budget`).

## Targets and late pipelines

A renderer that draws into a colour format or MSAA sample count the warm never rendered (a render-to-texture camera, a
second window, an offscreen capture) builds its forward set (`lab forward`, `lab depth`, `lab shadow`, `lab sky`), the
