<!-- capture:nav.remove_obstacle -->

## Workflow: path around a temporary obstacle

1. `nav.get_mesh`. `F0003` means this world has no nav mesh yet.
2. `nav.find_nearest` for the start and the goal. A point far from the mesh comes back with no polygon.
3. `nav.find_path` between those points and keep the corridor.
4. `nav.add_obstacle` on the box that should block the corridor. The id comes back in the answer.
5. `nav.find_path` again and compare the corridor.
6. `nav.remove_obstacle` with that id when the blocker is gone.

<!-- /depth-2:method-reference -->

## Deterministic layered plans

`nav.plan` plans on the deterministic layered bake of the app's `NavMesh` (`regia_nav::det::layers`,
ADR-8486). The bake is integer millimeters with a layer index per polygon (0 is the top surface of
its column), so the same request gives the same bits on every machine. Build the mesh with
`NavMeshBuilder::build_layered` to get more than one layer. It needs a `NavMesh` resource; without
one it returns `NOT_FOUND` (`F0003`).

```json
{ "from": [-3, 0, -3], "to": [3, 15, 3], "tunnel_pct": 75 }
→ { "plan": { "waypoints": [[-3, 0, -3], [0, 0, 0], [0, 15, 0], [3, 15, 3]],
              "waypoint_layers": [1, 1, 0, 0], "layer": 0, "polys": [0, 1],
              "cost_mm": 21485, "length": 23.48, "expansions": 2 },
    "bake_hash": "4f0c2b8e7d1a9c35", "bits_version": 1, "layers": 2 }
```

(The numbers above are an example; the reply carries the mesh's own.)

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `tunnel_pct`, `flank_pct` | What a meter in a tunnel (area 60) or flank (area 61) polygon costs, in percent of an open meter, 10 to 100. Defaults 75 and 20. |
| `passing_gap` | Meters a passage lane leaves free for a body coming the other way. Default: one body diameter of the mesh's agent; 0 turns lanes off. Inside a passage, a plan follows the right-hand wall (it moves onto it at most one gap from the shortest path and drifts outward slowly, so it does not turn into a side opening), so two bodies that meet head-on take opposite walls. |
| `layer` | The goal waypoint's layer; `waypoint_layers` has one entry per waypoint. |
| `bake_hash` | FNV-1a 64 of the bake's bytes, hex. Two peers with the same mesh report the same value. |

When there is no route the reply is `{ "plan": null, "reason": <code> }` beside `bake_hash`,
`bits_version` and `layers`:

| `reason` | When |
|---|---|
| `plan_start_off_mesh` | `from` is more than 3 m from every polygon. |
| `plan_goal_off_mesh` | `to` is more than 3 m from every polygon. |
| `plan_start_closed`, `plan_goal_closed` | The endpoint's polygon is closed by a blocker (a host's `LayerState`; `nav.plan` itself plans on an open state). |
| `plan_unreachable` | No open route joins them. |
| `plan_budget` | The search expanded more polygons than its budget. |

A lockstep host keeps a `LayerState` beside the bake. With the `stage_b` feature,
`regia_nav::layered::geom::cook_layered` bakes a world-geometry map (`regia_world_geom::WorldGeom`)
and `sync_layers` feeds each generation's closed sections (blockers) and ground-edit rectangles into
it, in that order. A dirty tile stays walkable until the host re-bakes it; a plan that crosses one
reports `crosses_dirty`.

<!-- source: book/agents/smart-objects.md -->
# Smart objects: interaction slots agents can discover, claim and use

A **smart object** is a world entity that advertises *interaction slots* — places an AI agent (or a
player) can stand, sit or operate — so agents can find and use a chair, terminal, door or cover point
without bespoke per-object code. The feature lives in `regia_ai` (`SmartObject`, `SmartObjectSlot`,
`SmartObjectPlugin`); without the plugin the lists are empty and claim/release answer `NOT_FOUND`
(`F0003`).

Authoring: an entity carries `SmartObject` (tags + an `enabled` flag, and optionally a `definition` that names a
`.smartobject.ron`; see *Definitions* below); each slot is a **child** entity
carrying `SmartObjectSlot { role, enabled }`, placed and rotated in the editor. The slot's world pose
is its `Transform`/`GlobalTransform`; its facing is its local −Z axis. A slot is *available* when it is
enabled, its object is enabled, and it is not claimed.

## List

`smartobject.list` reports every object and slot:

```json
{}
→ { "total": 2,
    "objects": [ { "entity": 4294967301, "tags": ["cover"], "enabled": true,
                   "definition": null, "definition_path": null, "definition_cooked": false,
                   "definition_error": null } ],
    "slots": [
      { "entity": 4294967302, "object": 4294967301, "role": "cover",
        "enabled": true, "claimed": false, "claimed_by": null,
        "position": [3.0, 1.5, -2.0], "forward": [0.0, 0.0, -1.0] }
    ],
    "index_rebuilds": 3 }
```

`object` is `null` for a slot with no `SmartObject` ancestor (still a valid slot, but it cannot be
disabled through an object). `claimed_by` is the holding entity's bits or `null`.

`index_rebuilds` counts how many times the slot index was rebuilt (`null` without
`SmartObjectPlugin`). A frame where no slot, object, parent link or slot transform changed adds
nothing, so two reads over quiet frames that differ point at something touching those components
every frame.

## Claim

`smartobject.claim` claims `slot` for `agent`. Claiming the same slot again for the same agent is
idempotent. A slot held by another agent, or a disabled slot, answers `claimed: false` with the current
holder and a `reason`; a missing slot answers `NOT_FOUND` (`F0003`):

```json
{ "slot": 4294967302, "agent": 4294967303 }
→ { "claimed": true, "held_by": 4294967303 }

{ "slot": 4294967302, "agent": 4294967304 }
→ { "claimed": false, "held_by": 4294967303, "reason": "claimed" }
```

## Release

`smartobject.release` releases `slot` held by `agent`. Releasing a slot the agent does not hold answers
`released: false` with the current holder; releasing an unclaimed slot is a no-op (`released: true`):

```json
{ "slot": 4294967302, "agent": 4294967303 }   → { "released": true }
{ "slot": 4294967302, "agent": 4294967304 }   → { "released": false, "held_by": 4294967303 }
```

## Working with the results

- Slots are the claimable unit; `object` groups them. Query by `role` (e.g. `"sit"`, `"operate"`,
  `"cover"`) to find the affordance you want, then `claim` the nearest available one.
- `debug.set_gizmos { "group": "smart_object", "enabled": true }` draws every slot as a wire sphere
  and a facing ray, green when available, amber when claimed, grey when disabled. With v2 a claimed
  slot also gets a ring colored by the holder's priority (cool blue for `background`/`low`, amber for
  `normal`, orange for `high`, red for `urgent`), an in-use slot a second inner ring with spokes, and
  every entrance an arrow pointing at its slot (needs the `debug_draw` feature).
- The runtime API (`regia_ai::SmartObjectIndex`, `claim_slot`, `release_slot`) is the same surface a
  behavior-tree leaf task or a script uses; the agent methods are thin wrappers over it.

## v2: priorities, handles and the claim life cycle

Version 2 (`docs/specs/39-smart-objects-v2.md`) keeps everything above and adds a claim life cycle. A slot is in
one of four states, derived from its components: `free`, `claimed`, `in_use` and `disabled`.

`smartobject.claim` takes an optional `priority` (`background`, `low`, `normal` (default), `high`, `urgent`) and
`use: true` to begin using the slot in the same call. A successful claim returns a `handle`:

```json
{ "slot": 4294967302, "agent": 4294967303, "priority": "low" }
→ { "claimed": true, "held_by": 4294967303, "handle": { "slot": 4294967302, "generation": 0 } }

{ "slot": 4294967302, "agent": 4294967304, "priority": "low" }
→ { "claimed": false, "held_by": 4294967303, "reason": "claimed" }

{ "slot": 4294967302, "agent": 4294967304, "priority": "urgent" }
→ { "claimed": true, "held_by": 4294967304, "handle": { "slot": 4294967302, "generation": 1 } }
```

- A claim on a held slot succeeds only at a **strictly higher** priority than the holder's. The old holder gets a
  `lost` message with reason `preempted` and its handle goes stale.
- The same agent claiming again gets the same handle and may raise the held priority.
- `smartobject.begin_use { handle }` moves `claimed` to `in_use` (answer `{ "state": "in_use" }`). An in-use slot
  cannot be preempted: claims on it answer `claimed: false` with `reason: "in_use"`.
- `smartobject.release` accepts `{ "handle": { slot, generation } }` instead of `slot` and `agent`. A stale handle
  is an `F0002` error with reason `stale_handle`. With `agent` as well as `handle`, only that agent's claim is
  released; another agent gets `F0002` with reason `not_holder`.
- A claim is released automatically (one `lost` message each) when the holder is despawned (`holder_gone`), the slot
  or its object is despawned (`slot_gone`), the slot or its object becomes disabled (`disabled`) or a definition
  reload removes the slot (`slot_removed`). Behavior tasks read `lost` messages and clean up their own state.

## Search

`smartobject.search` filters slots in a region and returns them nearest first:

```json
{ "region": { "center": [0, 0, 0], "radius": 20 },
  "activity": "Has(\"Activity.Sit\")", "user_tags": ["Role.Guard"],
  "priority": "high", "allow_preempt": true, "explain": true }
→ { "hits": [ { "slot": 4294967302, "object": 4294967301, "distance": 3.2, "status": "free" },
              { "slot": 4294967310, "object": 4294967309, "distance": 7.9, "status": "preemptable",
                "holder": 4294967311 } ],
    "rejections": [ { "object": 4294967301, "slot": 4294967306, "stage": "activity",
                      "detail": "activity query failed" } ],
    "rejections_total": 1 }
```

- `region` is `{ center, radius }` (a sphere) or `{ min, max }` (a box). Distance is measured from the sphere's
  center or the box's center to the slot. Hits sort by `(distance, slot entity)`; `limit` applies after sorting. A `limit` that is not a
  non-negative integer, or a `user` that is not entity bits, is `bad_query`; a `user` that is well-formed but names no
  live entity is `entity_not_found` (ADR-1769, ADR-1809; they used to mean "no limit" and "no user").
- Stages run in order and the first failure is the recorded rejection: `region`, `enabled`, `state`, `family`,
  `activity`, `user`, `condition`. When one object-level check rejects every slot of an object alike, a single
  entry with `slot: null` is reported. `rejections` is capped at 256 entries (`rejections_total` is the count).
- `activity` is a tag query as RON text (`Has("A.B")`, `AnyOf([...])`) tested against the slot's effective activity
  set: the definition's and the slot's tags (`Union`, or the slot's own first with `SlotFirst`) plus the runtime tags.
- `user_tags` are the requester's tags, tested against the definition's and the slot's user rules.
- `families` keeps slots that offer one of the behavior families. `check_conditions` (default true) runs the
  registered slot conditions; an unregistered condition counts as failing (one warning in the log).
- A `claimed` slot is a hit only with `allow_preempt` and a `priority` above the holder's (`status: "preemptable"`,
  with the `holder`); an `in_use` slot never; a `disabled` slot only with `include_disabled`.

## Enabling, tags and messages

- `smartobject.set_enabled { entity, enabled, reason? }` adds (`enabled: false`) or removes (`true`) an off-reason on
  a slot or object (default reason `gameplay`). The target is enabled only when its own `enabled` flag is set (and, for a slot, its object's) and it has no
  off-reason left, so two disables need two enables; `enabled: true` never sets a cleared flag. The answer is the target's own effective value.
- `smartobject.tags { entity, add?, remove? }` adds and removes runtime tags on a slot or object and answers the
  runtime tags it holds. Runtime tags join the activity set of the slot (an object's join every slot of it).
- `smartobject.messages { last? }` returns the most recent records, oldest first (at most 256), ordered by object
  and then slot:
  - `{ "kind": "changed", "object", "slot", "what", "tag" }` with `what` one of `claimed`, `in_use`, `released`,
    `tag_added`, `tag_removed`, `enabled`, `disabled`, `custom` (written only when the effective value changed;
    `slot` is `null` for an object-scope change);
  - `{ "kind": "lost", "handle", "holder", "reason" }` with `reason` one of `preempted`, `disabled`, `holder_gone`,
    `slot_gone`, `slot_removed`.

## Definitions

A scene names a definition with `SmartObject::definition`, a persisted asset reference. The id comes from the cook, so a
project needs a `regia cook` first. On the next `PostUpdate` the definition is read (the source text when there is one,
else the pak entry) and the slots appear as children. Objects naming one id share one load.

`smartobject.set_definition { entity, path }` (or `{ entity, id }`) points an object at a definition from a tool. `path` is
under `assets/` and must already be a cooked asset id. It reads the definition at once, so the answer already says how that went:

```json
{ "entity": 4294967301, "path": "props/chair.smartobject.ron" }
→ { "definition": "67e55044-10b1-426f-9247-bb680e5fe0c8", "path": "props/chair.smartobject.ron",
    "loaded": true, "cooked": false, "error": null }
```

An unknown `path` (nothing cooked at `assets/<path>`) is `F0002` with `data.reason` `definition_not_found`. The call
returns before `SmartObject.definition` is written, so the object stays unpointed and saving the file afterward does
not fill it. Run `regia cook`, then call again.

An `id` that does not load is an `error` in the answer, not a protocol error: the object is pointed at that id anyway, so
fixing the file and saving is enough. `error.reason` is `definition_not_found` (the id resolves to nothing, or the file
is gone), `bad_definition` (it does not parse or validate) or `unsupported_version` (a newer `format_version`). `smartobject.list`
shows the same thing per object as `definition_error`, with `definition_path` and `definition_cooked`. A changed file is
read again in dev builds; if the new text does not load, the old definition stays in use, its slots are not touched, and
`definition_error` says why. Check the result with `play.wait_until` on `smartobject.list`.

## Errors

All new failures are `F0002` with `data.reason`:

| Reason | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `missing_param` | A required parameter is absent (also a handle without `generation`). |
| `slot_not_found` | The entity (or the handle's slot) is not a smart-object slot. |
| `stale_handle` | The claim was released, preempted or invalidated since the handle was issued. |
| `not_holder` | `release` with both `handle` and `agent`: that agent does not hold the claim. |
| `slot_claimed`, `slot_in_use`, `slot_disabled` | A runtime claim error mapped from the library (`claim` itself answers `claimed: false` with a `reason` instead). |
| `entity_not_found` | `set_enabled` / `tags` target is neither a slot nor an object, or a `search` `user` is not a live entity. |
| `bad_region` | `region` is neither a sphere nor a box, or has a negative radius, non-finite numbers or `min > max`. |
| `bad_priority` | Not one of `background`, `low`, `normal`, `high`, `urgent`. |
| `bad_query` | `activity` does not parse, or a tag name is not a valid tag name, or a list has the wrong shape, or a `search` `limit` is not a non-negative integer. |
| `tag_unknown` | The tag is valid but not declared in the loaded project tag table. |
| `definition_not_found` | `set_definition`: no cooked asset at `path`; run `regia cook`. |
| `bad_id` | `set_definition`: `id` is not an asset id string. |

## Runtime API

`claim_with(world, slot, user, priority) -> Result<ClaimHandle, SmartObjectError>`, `begin_use`, `release_handle`, `slot_state`,
`SmartObjectIndex::{search, find_first, availability}`, `add_runtime_tag` / `remove_runtime_tag`, `set_enabled`,
`entrance_for` and `slot_behavior::<T>` are in `regia_ai::smart_object_v2`. `claim_slot` / `release_slot` keep their
signatures and delegate at `Normal`. A handle packs into a `u64` with `ClaimHandle::to_bits` for a blackboard `Int`.
Read `smartobject.list` (`claimed_by`) or `smartobject.messages` to see the outcome of a claim.

## In the editor

The Smart Objects panel lists every object and slot with its claim state, holder and priority, and marks the slots in the
viewport. `smartobject.*` reach the world that serves the agent, which in the editor is the edit world;
`editor.smart_object_panel_*` reach the play world. See [gameplay panels](book/agents/editor-gameplay-panels.md). A changed
`.smartobject.ron` now reaches its objects through the editor's watcher (ADR-2030).

<!-- source: book/agents/functional-tests.md -->
# Functional tests: place a test in a level, run it, read the verdict

A **functional test** is an entity with a `FunctionalTest` component placed in a level. Playing the level can run it; `regia test` runs
every test of a level and exits with a code CI understands, so a team tests gameplay with the level data the game ships, without an
outside script holding the connection. The desktop game still opens its window: `regia test` sets `REGIA_SESSION_RENDER=0`, and that
variable does not choose a renderer (spec 41 § 2.8). Everything is counted in fixed-step frames: no limit, wait or order depends on a clock.

Without `regia_framework::functional::FunctionalTestPlugin` (dev and test builds only) every `functest.*` method answers `F0002` with
`data.reason: "no_runner"`. Formats: `FunctionalTest` (`docs/formats/functional-test.md`), `.functest.ron` (`docs/formats/functest-ron.md`),
`<level>.expected.ron` (`docs/formats/expected-ron.md`), `TestReport` (`docs/formats/test-report.md`).

## Lifecycle

| Step | When | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| Setup | once, when the run opens | settings overrides apply first |
| Ready gate | each frame until `ready` returns true | past `ready_limit` the run ends `Aborted` with `ready_timeout` and the body never begins |
| Begin | once per pass | ticks begin next frame |
| Tick | each frame while active | the body may conclude at any time |
| Conclude | once per pass | a verdict and a message; a second conclude in the same pass is ignored |
| Next pass | if passes are queued | labels run in sorted order; at most 32 passes (`too_many_passes`) |
| Teardown | once after the last pass, always | body hook, scoped entities, restored settings, restored viewpoint |

Verdicts: `Pending`, `Active`, `Passed`, `Failed`, `Aborted` (could not run to a decision: ready timeout, panic, bad setting or body, too many
passes), `Undecided` (the pass ended without a verdict). A run's verdict is its worst pass. Assertions never panic: they record a failure
(deterministic text, with the step name in brackets) and the pass ends `Failed` even if the body concluded `Passed`. A panicking body ends `Aborted`
with `panic: <text>` and still tears down.

## The recipe

```json
functest.create { "name": "doomed", "body": "script:tests/doomed.functest.ron", "tags": ["demo"],
                  "script": "(format_version: 1, steps: [(name: \"never\", wait_until: Some((condition: (resource: \"Score\", path: \"n\", op: \"gte\", value: 999), within_frames: 30)))])" }
→ { "entity": 4294967301 }
functest.run { "tags": ["demo"] }         → { "started": 1 }
play.wait_until { "condition": ... }       // or poll functest.status until "finished": true
functest.status {}                         → { "state": "done", "done": 1, "total": 1, "finished": true }
functest.results {}                        → { "tests": [ { "name": "doomed", "verdict": "Failed",
                                                "message": "step `never` failed; [never] wait_until not satisfied within 30 frames: ...",
                                                "steps": [ { "name": "never", "verdict": "Failed" } ] } ], "exit_code": 1 }
```

Make the test fail on purpose and confirm `Failed` with the step name and the failure text before trusting a green run.

## Methods

| Method | Class | Params | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `functest.list` | read | `{ filter?, tags? }` | `{ tests: [{ name, level, entity, tags, enabled, description, body }] }` |
| `functest.run` | play | `{ filter?, tags?, seed?, params?, update_expected?, looped?, level? }` | `{ started }` |
| `functest.status` | read | `{}` | `{ state, test?, pass?, frame?, done, total, finished }` |
| `functest.results` | read | `{ since? }` | the `TestReport` so far plus `exit_code`. The test that is running is not in the report until it closes. While the run is in progress and no finished test has a verdict (the report is empty, or holds only skipped tests), `exit_code` is 3 even though `functest.status` has `state: "running"` and `finished: false`. 3 means no verdicts yet, the same code as a selection that ran nothing. |
| `functest.abort` | play | `{ reason? }` | `{ aborted }` |
| `functest.create` | edit scene | `{ name, body, script?, tags?, frame_limit?, at? }` | `{ entity }` |
| `functest.bless` | edit scene | `{ test, key?, confirm }` | `{ written }` |

`filter` is a name glob (`*`, `?`) or an array (any-of); `tags` must all be present. Disabled tests are listed and skipped; a skipped test is not a pass.
`level` is a project-relative path (`levels/a.level.ron`); `regia test --level` sends that path. An empty `level` runs the tests already in the world. A `.expected.ron` this build cannot read aborts the run and is not rewritten.
`functest.bless` writes the values a test observed in the last run into its `.expected.ron`; without `confirm: true` (given after the owner reviewed the
diff) it answers `needs_confirmation`.

## Errors

`F0002` with `data.reason`: `no_runner` (plugin absent), `no_tests` (nothing enabled matches), `already_running`, `not_running`, `test_not_found`,
`script_invalid` (the `.functest.ron` does not parse), `needs_confirmation`, `bad_params`, and `not_playing` (reserved for editor hosts whose world is not
in play mode; the in-game agent never raises it). `body_not_found`, `setting_unknown`, `ready_timeout` and `too_many_passes` end a run `Aborted` and appear
as the test's `message` in `functest.results` (the message starts with the reason).

## Writing the body

**Script** (`.functest.ron`): steps with `do` (input injection), `wait_until` (the `play.wait_until` condition and a `within_frames` count) and `expect`
(`play.expect` conditions evaluated in one frame). A failed expectation, or a `do` action the input service refuses, fails the pass at
the end of its step with "step `<name>` failed". See the format page.

**Rust**: implement `regia_framework::functional::TestBody` (`setup`, `ready`, `begin`, `tick`, `conclude`, `teardown`, `wants_pass_now`, `summary`),
register it with `app.register_functional_test::<MyTest>()`, and select it with `body: Rust("my_game::MyTest")`. Through `TestContext`: assertions
(tolerance equality for floats, vectors, quaternions, transforms and matrices; facing equality; exact; the six relations; entity checks;
`condition`), `begin_step`/`end_step`, `spawn_scoped`, `override_setting`, `add_pass`, `param`, a seeded `rng`, and `expect_value` against the
level's expected-value file.

## The command line

```
regia test [PROJECT] --level L [--filter G]... [--tag T]... [--seed N] [--param k=v]... [--report FILE] [--junit FILE] [--update-expected] [--loop] [--exe PATH]
regia test [PROJECT] --platform android [--address attached|127.0.0.1:PORT] [--filter G]... [--tag T]... [--seed N] [--param k=v]... [--report FILE] [--junit FILE]
regia test session FILE [--recover] [--keep-artifacts] [--param k=v]... [--exe PATH]
```

Exit codes of both: **0** all passed, **1** at least one `Failed`, **2** at least one `Aborted` or `Undecided` (or a session aborted),
**3** no tests ran (an empty run is not a pass), **4** harness or launch failure. `regia test` starts the project's game on the level
(`REGIA_START_LEVEL`) with `REGIA_SESSION_RENDER=0`. A desktop build still opens its window: the variable does not select a renderer
(spec 41 § 2.8). The command runs the tests through `functest.*` and writes the JSON report and JUnit XML.

`--platform android` (ADR-2137) starts nothing: it runs the tests of the game already running on the attached device, through the
endpoint `regia install-android --attach` wrote (`--address attached`, the default) or a port you forwarded (`127.0.0.1:<port>`), with
the same report files and exit codes. The device runs the level it was started with, so `--level`, `--exe` and `--loop` are refused there.
Without the agent files the command says to run `regia install-android --attach` first and exits 4.

```sh
regia install-android --attach            # forward the agent port, write .regia/agent/endpoint.json and token
regia test --platform android --filter "smoke*" --junit device.xml
```

## Sessions

`<name>.session.ron` (format `Session`, v2; v1 files read unchanged) names the roles of a playthrough: `build` (`Cargo`, `Packaged` or `Remote`),
`roles` (name, kind `Server`/`Client`/`Game`, count, args, driver, render, env, and since v2 `remote`), the `tests` each role runs, optional harness `script` calls, `limit_frames`,
`max_restarts` (default 2), `allow_errors` and `keep`. The harness starts roles in listed order, each with its own agent directory
(`REGIA_AGENT_DIR=<artifacts>/<session>/<role>-<n>/agent`), waits for the agent, runs the tests, then stops each process (stdin closes; a process that
ignores that is killed). In role arguments `{server}` is the first server's address, `{port}` the instance's own OS-assigned port and `{param:key}` a
`--param`.

The session **passes** only if every process exited 0 (or was stopped by the harness at the end), every reported test is `Passed`, no log `ERROR` line outside
`allow_errors` appears, no panic/assert/fatal marker appears (`panicked at`, `assertion failed`, `FATAL`, `fatal runtime error`) and no crash bundle
(a `crash/` folder with files, or a `.dmp`) was written. Artifacts are `<artifacts>/<session>/<role>-<n>/` (stdout and stderr logs, the agent folder) and either
`session-result.json` (clean run only) or `session-failure.json`. With `--recover` the harness writes `session-progress.json`, restarts a role whose process
died and skips tests recorded as complete; after `max_restarts` the session ends `Aborted` with `too_many_restarts`.

`limit_frames` reaches every role as `REGIA_SESSION_LIMIT_FRAMES` (only when above 0; a role's own `env` entry wins); the harness itself does not enforce it.

**`keep.screenshots_on_failure`** (ADR-2755). When true, each failed step of a rendering role (`render: true`) saves a screenshot through `seeing.screenshot` while the process still runs: a test whose verdict is not `Passed` (`test:<name>`) or a failed `script` call (`script:<method>`). The PNG is `<artifacts>/<session>/<role>-<n>/failure-<k>.png` next to the logs, and the outcome (`session-failure.json`, the `processes[].screenshots` list) names it: `{ step, file, reason }`. A role that does not render, no display, or a failed screenshot call saves nothing and records the `reason`; it never fails the run by itself (the session's `reasons` stay the test's own). `false` (the default) asks for no screenshot. A passing session takes none.

**The arena smoke session** (spec 41 test 19, ADR-2755): `samples/arena/smoke.session.ron` starts `arena --smoke --bots 3 --seed 7` (the binary installs the functional-test runner and one placed test, `arena_smoke`, tagged `smoke`: the match is in warm-up or the round, its clock advances and pawns exist after 90 frames). `render` is unset, so the harness sets `REGIA_SESSION_RENDER=0`, and the arena binary still opens a window (`regia::run_with`). The in-process test `samples/arena/tests/smoke_test.rs` uses `MinimalPlugins` and opens none:

```sh
regia test session samples/arena/smoke.session.ron        # Linux (lavapipe or no GPU) and Windows alike
```

The device half is spec 41 test 20 (`regia test --platform android`, above).

A game picks up its driver from `REGIA_SESSION_DRIVER` (`regia_framework::functional::SessionDriverPlugin`; hooks `on_launch`, `before_level_load`,
`after_level_load`, `on_step`, `finish(code)`).

## The viewpoint

A test's `viewpoint` is the guid of an entity. At the first Begin the local camera takes that entity's world pose; teardown
puts it back however the run ended. The local camera is the window camera with the lowest `order`, else the lowest-order
camera of any target. A camera driven by a rig or a driver stays at the viewpoint during the run; another camera stays where
the test moves it. A guid nothing resolves, a world without a camera or a target without a transform ends the test `Aborted`
with `bad_params`, and the body never begins. A project may replace the service with `TestHooks::viewpoint`.

## Shipping builds

`FunctionalTestPlugin`, `functest.*` and `regia test` exist with the cargo feature `functional-tests` of `regia`. It is on by
default and with `agent`, so a named shipping profile with `no_default_features` leaves it out, and `ship_check` refuses a
game that turns it on there unless the profile says `allow_agent`. A body's panic cannot be caught under `panic = "abort"`.

`regia package --profile shipping` leaves the `FunctionalTest` entities and their descendants out of every level, with a
warning count, and the `.functest.ron`, `.expected.ron` and `.session.ron` files out of the package. Other profiles keep them.

## The Tests panel

The editor's Tests panel lists the open level's tests with tags, owner and last verdict, ticks a selection, runs it in
play-in-editor (starting play when stopped) and shows the report with its step names. A click selects the placed entity.
Placed tests draw a box with the name and a line to the viewpoint. The `functest.*` methods stay the primary surface; these
read and drive the panel a human sees:

| Method | Class | Params | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `editor.tests_panel_state` | read | none | `{ tests: [{ name, tags, owner, description, enabled, entity, verdict, chosen }], running, queued, status, report }` |
| `editor.tests_panel_run` | play, mutating | `tests?` | the state, plus `started` |
| `editor.tests_panel_open` | edit_scene, mutating | `test` | `{ entity }` |

`no_tests` when nothing enabled is selected, `already_running` during a run, `test_not_found` for an unknown name, and a
`status` starting `no_runner` when the play session has none. A run ends with the play session: the status says so.

## Device instances

`build: Remote(address: "attached")` drives the one game already running on a device. First run
`regia install-android --attach`: it forwards a port and writes `.regia/agent/endpoint.json` and `token`. `attached` uses that
endpoint; `127.0.0.1:<port>` connects to a port you forwarded yourself, with the same token. Any other address is refused, because
the token only goes to the loopback address. The session lists one role with `count: 1`.

The harness runs the session's script calls and tests over that connection. The process appears in the outcome with `remote: true`
and `exit_code: null`. A lost connection fails the session; there is no restart.

**A device role in a local session** (format v2, ADR-2137). With a local build (`Cargo` or `Packaged`), one role may carry
`remote: Some("attached")` (or `Some("127.0.0.1:<port>")`): that role is the game on the device, the others start on this machine as
usual. Roles still start in listed order, so a desktop server comes up before the device client is reached. The device role has
`count: 1`, gets no arguments and no agent directory (it is already running), is never restarted, and appears in the outcome with
`remote: true`; script calls address it by name like any role. A session file that uses `remote` must say `format_version: 2`; a v1
harness refuses v2 files, so it can never start the device role as a local process.

```ron
Session(
    format_version: 2,
    build: Cargo(package: "my_game", profile: "dev"),
    roles: [
        (name: "server", kind: Server, args: ["--server", "--port", "{port}"]),
        (name: "phone", kind: Client, remote: Some("attached")),
    ],
    tests: (filter: ["smoke*"], tags: []),
    script: [ (role: "phone", call: "play.pause") ],
)
```

The device does not learn the desktop server's address from the harness: connect it from the game (a menu, a saved address) or with a
script call to a method of your game. With `adb reverse tcp:<port> tcp:<port>` the phone reaches a desktop port as its own loopback.

## Limits of this build

A `Remote` build or role starts, stops and restarts nothing and reads no device logs. At most one role per session is a device (the token
comes from the one attached device). Server-plus-client tests wait for `regia_net`; until then `count: 4` of a non-networked role proves launch, folders and order only.

Cargo builds must identify one distinct binary executable of the exact package. Build-script artifacts and package-name substrings in unrelated paths never qualify; multiple binary paths are refused. A reported `Aborted` or `Undecided` test makes the session status `aborted` and exits 2, including when other results failed.

A nonzero session `limit_frames` is forwarded as `REGIA_SESSION_LIMIT_FRAMES` for local roles and as the string parameter `regia_session_limit_frames` in `functest.run` for local and remote roles. This is an informational hint, not an enforced cap; an explicit role environment entry or functional-test parameter can override its copy.

With `keep.screenshots_on_failure: true`, the harness asks live roles with `render: true` for `seeing.screenshot` before stopping them and atomically writes `<artifacts>/<session>/<role>-<index>/failure.png`. Remote roles are captured without being stopped. A capture failure logs `session_screenshot_failed` and preserves the original verdict and exit code.

<!-- source: book/agents/gizmos.md -->
# Gizmos: debug overlays

Turn the engine's debug overlays on and off, and restyle any gizmo group, to see what the game
cannot show: collider shapes, the nav mesh, audio emitter ranges and AI senses. Pair it with
`seeing.screenshot` to check placement. Groups are listed by `debug.gizmos`; the overlays ship
disabled.

| Group | Draws |
|---|---|
| `physics` | Collider wireframes (green; sensors yellow). Convex hulls, height fields and very large trimeshes draw their bounds. |
| `nav_mesh` | Nav-mesh polygon outlines (cyan, lifted 5 cm) and off-mesh links (pink arrows). |
| `audio` | Emitter full-volume sphere (orange), silence sphere (brown), inner/outer cones and facing arrow. |
| `ai_perception` | Sight fan at eye height (red) and hearing ring (blue) for every `Perception`. |
| `smart_object` | Smart-object slots: available, claimed and disabled markers and facing rays ([Smart objects](book/agents/smart-objects.md)). |
| `camera_rig` | Data-driven camera rigs: pose frustums tinted by weight, boom line, collision probe, aim point, layer markers. |
| `motion_matching` | Motion matching: the desired trajectory with facing ticks, the matched frame's own trajectory in gray, foot positions. |
| `post_volumes` | Post volumes: each volume's shape and blend band. |
| `default` | Whatever game code draws with `Gizmos`, and the `DebugDraw` queue: lines and world-space labels, each kept for its `duration` in frames ([Render lights](book/agents/render-lights.md#debugdraw-durations-and-labels)). |
| `paths` | Current agent position through unvisited navigation waypoints; registered by `DebugGizmosPlugin`, off by default, with the project path color. |

## List groups

`debug.gizmos`:

```json
{}
→ { "groups": [
      { "name": "ai_perception", "enabled": false, "line_width": 2.0, "perspective": false,
        "style": "solid", "joints": "none", "depth_bias": 0.0, "on_top": false },
      { "name": "default", "enabled": true, ... },
      { "name": "nav_mesh", "enabled": false, "depth_bias": -0.01, ... },
      ... ] }
```

## Toggle and style a group

`debug.set_gizmos` needs `group` and at least one of `enabled`, `line_width` (0..=64 px),
`depth_bias` (-1..=1), `on_top`, `perspective`:

```json
{ "group": "physics", "enabled": true, "on_top": true }
→ { "before": { "name": "physics", "enabled": false, ... },
    "after":  { "name": "physics", "enabled": true, "on_top": true, ... } }
```

An unknown group is `NOT_FOUND` with the list of groups in the hint. The call is mutating and
needs the `edit_scene` permission (it is audited like other edits).

## Recipes

- **Is the trigger where the designer thinks?** Enable `physics` with `on_top: true`, take a
  screenshot from the player camera, look for the yellow sensor box.
- **Why does the bot walk around this ramp?** Enable `nav_mesh`; a missing outline over the ramp
  means it is not walkable at the current agent slope/climb.
- **Can the guard see the door?** Enable `ai_perception`; the red fan is exactly the cone
  `in_sight_cone` tests (horizontal, `sight_half_angle` either side of the facing).
- **Is the alarm audible from the spawn?** Enable `audio`; the brown sphere is `max_distance`.

The overlays draw after the scene and before the UI, so a screenshot includes them; turn them off
again before capturing reference images.

The `paths` group omits completed paths and non-finite edges and caps work per frame. It uses
`DebugColors.path` in a client build; the editor's **Show ▸ Paths** is a separate view flag
([Project debug colors and remaining paths](book/agents/viewport-flags.md#project-debug-colors-and-remaining-paths-w12)).

## Sub-toggles: the locomotion group

The `locomotion` group (ADR-8729, off by default) draws walkers (`GaitRig`), foot planters
(`FootPlacement`) and their leg IK. It has three sub-toggles, all on by default: `gait`,
`foot_placement` and `ik`. `debug.gizmos` lists them as `toggles` on that group's entry, and
`debug.set_gizmos` takes `toggles` (an object of name to boolean; the names it leaves out keep their
value), alone or with the other fields:

```json
{ "group": "locomotion", "enabled": true, "toggles": { "ik": false } }
→ { "before": { "name": "locomotion", "enabled": false, ...,
                "toggles": { "gait": true, "foot_placement": true, "ik": true } },
    "after":  { "name": "locomotion", "enabled": true, ...,
                "toggles": { "gait": true, "foot_placement": true, "ik": false } } }
```

`toggles` that is not an object, an unknown sub-toggle, a non-boolean value, or `toggles` on any other
group is `invalid_params` and changes nothing.

A crowd cannot grow the overlay without bound: a frame stops starting new draws once it holds
`MAX_LOCOMOTION_SEGMENTS` (20 000, the paths overlay's budget) segments, counted conservatively, and
`LocomotionGizmoStats::skipped` counts the walker gaits, IK chains and foot planters it left out
(ADR-8800). A frame passes the budget by at most the one draw in progress. What each sub-toggle draws: [Procedural
gait](book/agents/procedural-gait.md#see-it-the-locomotion-overlay) and [Foot
planting](book/agents/foot-planting.md#see-it-the-locomotion-overlay).

<!-- source: book/agents/gltf-hierarchy.md -->
# glTF hierarchy and wireframe

## `editor.spawn_gltf_hierarchy`

Spawns a glTF/GLB as a named entity tree. Params: `path` (project-relative, required),
`editor_only`, `keep_sockets` (default true), `skins` (default true), `root_name`,
`show_collision` (default false), `lights` (default true).

```json
{ "method": "editor.spawn_gltf_hierarchy", "params": { "path": "models/tank.glb", "root_name": "Tank" } }
```

Returns `root`, `nodes[]` (`name`, `gltf_index`, `entity`, `parent`, `triangles`, `materials`,
`socket`, `collision`, `skin`) and a `report` (`nodes`, `mesh_entities`, `skinned_meshes`,
`sockets`, `collision_nodes`, `hidden_collision_meshes`, `skeletons`, `joints`, `triangles`,
`duplicate_names`, `warnings`). Use `entity` with
`scene.get_entity` / `editor.set_transform`. Not undoable: delete `root` to remove the model.
Names are not unique in glTF; check `duplicate_names`. Skins become `SkinnedMesh`; meshes with
morph targets get weights you can set with `anim.set_morph_weights`.

Nodes named `collision_*` (collision hulls such as `collision_turret_0`) keep their entity, name
and transform and carry `GltfCollisionNode`, but their meshes are not drawn and their triangles
are not counted (ADR-1622): `collision` is `true` and `triangles` 0 on their rows, and
`hidden_collision_meshes` counts them. `show_collision: true` draws them for debugging. Check it
worked: `editor.capture_viewport` with and without `show_collision` and compare.

## The collision layer: `editor.collision_layer`

By default the loaders drop `collision_*` meshes. A tool that wants them as a marked layer sets
the loader option `keep_collision_nodes` (ADR-1658):

```rust,ignore
use regia_editor::mesh_source::{GltfLoadOptions, load_gltf_model_with_options};
let model = load_gltf_model_with_options(
    &path, &default_material, &|_| true,
    GltfLoadOptions { keep_collision_nodes: true },
)?;
// model.parts: what renders (unchanged). model.collision_parts: the hulls, one merged part.
```

`LoadedModel::collision_parts` is empty by default. A renderer draws `parts` only, so the hulls
never show unless a tool draws `collision_parts` itself as an overlay (for example with a
wireframe or translucent material). The cook is unchanged: it still skips `collision_*` meshes,
and no stored format changes.

`editor.collision_layer { path }` (read-only) loads with the option on and returns
`has_collision`, `collision_triangles`, `collision_vertices`, `collision_bounds` (`{min, max}` or
`null`) and `render_triangles`. A missing or unreadable file is `not_found`. To look at the
hulls in the viewport, spawn the model with `show_collision: true` and capture it.

## `editor.capture_viewport { debug_view: "wireframe" }`

Adds the meshes' edges (linear green) over the lit frame. `lit` is the default. Check it
worked: capture with and without and compare, or count the wire colour in the PNG.

## Surface debug views: `uv_checker`, `texel_density`, `material_id`

`editor.capture_viewport { debug_view }` also takes these modes. They replace the shading with
exact (unlit, display-referred) colors; capture `lit` afterwards to compare.

| `debug_view` | Extra params | Reads as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `uv_checker` | `tile_m` (default 0.25; `0` = UV space) | A 4 x 4 checker; one cell is `tile_m` meters of surface. Equal square cells = even UVs; stretched cells = stretch. Red grows along U, green along V. |
| `texel_density` | `target_px_per_m` (512), `tolerance` (0.1) | Per triangle: blue below the target, green within `tolerance` (0.1 = 10 percent), red above. No base-colour texture counts as 1024 px. |
| `material_id` | none | One stable color per material name. The legend is `info.debug_legend`: `[{ name, color, hex }]`. |

```json
{ "method": "editor.capture_viewport", "params": { "debug_view": "texel_density", "target_px_per_m": 1024, "tolerance": 0.1 } }
```

Check it worked: count blue, green and red pixels in the PNG (a model at its budget is mostly
green), or compare with the `lit` capture. Material names come from the `MaterialLabel`
component, which `spawn_gltf_hierarchy` sets from the glTF material name; an unlabeled mesh
shows as `unnamed #rrggbb` (its base color).

<!-- source: book/agents/render-override-pick.md -->
# Render overrides and surface picks

## `editor.set_render_override`

Tints, ghosts, x-rays or unlights one entity without touching its material. Params: `entity`
(bits, required), `tint` `[r, g, b, a]` (linear 0-1, `a` multiplies the coverage), `emissive`
`[r, g, b]` (display-referred 0-1, added on top), `alpha` (coverage 0-1; below 1 draws blended),
`xray` (drawn through whatever is in front), `unlit`, `clear` (remove it). A non-finite number (or
one outside the `f32` range, `1e39`) is refused with `F0002` and stores nothing.

```json
{ "method": "editor.set_render_override", "params": { "entity": 4294967301, "tint": [1, 0.2, 0.2, 1] } }
{ "method": "editor.set_render_override", "params": { "entity": 4294967301, "alpha": 0.3 } }
{ "method": "editor.set_render_override", "params": { "entity": 4294967301, "xray": true, "alpha": 0.6 } }
{ "method": "editor.set_render_override", "params": { "entity": 4294967301, "clear": true } }
```

Returns `{ entity, name, override: { tint, emissive, alpha, xray, unlit, blends } | null,
undoable: false }`. An override on a node also covers its children and a model's parts that have
none of their own; an override with no fields set on a child stops that. Ghosts and x-ray draw in
the blend pass: they cast no shadow. Material-graph surfaces take tint, alpha, unlit and emissive,
but not x-ray. Check it worked: `editor.capture_viewport` before and after, and compare.

## `editor.pick_hit`

The surface under a capture pixel: which mesh, which triangle, where and which way it faces.
Params: `x`, `y` (required), `width`, `height`, `view` (as `editor.capture_viewport`), `cull`
(`none` = both faces, the default; `back` = front faces only).

```json
{ "method": "editor.pick_hit", "params": { "x": 160, "y": 120, "width": 320, "height": 240 } }
```

Returns `entity` and `name` (the mesh entity hit; a model part, not its owner), `owner` and
`owner_name` (what a click selects), `position` (world), `normal` (world, unit, the triangle's
front side as drawn), `smooth_normal` (interpolated vertex normal), `triangle` (index into the
mesh's index list), `indices` (its three vertices), `barycentric` (their weights), `distance`
(metres from the near plane) and `front_face`; `{ entity: null }` on background. Skinned meshes
are hit where they are drawn (current palette). Terrain is not returned (use `editor.pick`), but it hides: where terrain is nearer than the mesh, or a proxy cube covers the pixel in front of it, the result is `null`, not the mesh behind.

To place something on a surface: `pick_hit`, then `editor.set_transform` at `position`, oriented
along `normal`.

<!-- source: book/agents/scalar-overlay.md -->
# Scalar overlay (per-vertex heatmaps)

## `editor.set_scalar_overlay`

Colors one mesh entity by one number per vertex, drawn unlit over the lit viewport: skin-weight
heatmaps, deformation heatmaps, damage brushes. The material and the lighting are untouched.
Params: `entity` (bits of the mesh entity, required: the `entity` of `editor.pick_hit`, not a
model's owner), then at most one value source:

- `values`: one number per vertex, in vertex order;
- `constant`: every vertex gets this number;
- `axis` (`x`, `y`, `z`): each vertex's object-space coordinate on that axis;

and any of `paint` (`{ "vertices": [i, ...], "value": v }`: set those vertices on top of the given or
current values, zeros for a new overlay; an index that is negative, not a whole number (`1.9`), or
at or above the vertex count is skipped and paints nothing), `ramp` (`viridis`,
`diverging`, `grayscale`, or stops `[{ "at": 0..1, "color": [r, g, b] }]` in sRGB 0-1), `range`
(`[lo, hi]`, default `[0, 1]`: the values at the start and end of the ramp, clamped outside; a
reversed range flips the ramp; `lo == hi` is a step), `opacity` (0-1, default 1), `clear` (remove it).
Ramp, range and opacity can change alone on an existing overlay without resending values.

```json
{ "method": "editor.set_scalar_overlay", "params": { "entity": 4294967301, "axis": "y", "range": [-0.5, 0.5] } }
{ "method": "editor.set_scalar_overlay", "params": { "entity": 4294967301, "values": [0, 0.2, 1.0], "ramp": "diverging", "range": [-1, 1], "opacity": 0.8 } }
{ "method": "editor.set_scalar_overlay", "params": { "entity": 4294967301, "paint": { "vertices": [10, 11, 12], "value": 1.0 } } }
{ "method": "editor.set_scalar_overlay", "params": { "entity": 4294967301, "clear": true } }
```

Returns `{ entity, name, overlay: { vertices, values, fit, min, max, ramp, range, opacity } | null,
undoable: false }`. **`fit` must be `"exact"`**: a values count that differs from the vertex count
returns `{ mismatch: "short" | "long", values, vertices }` and the overlay draws nothing (never an
error, never a crash). NaN values read as 0. Infinities saturate at ±1e30 and then go through
the same range division as a finite value, so a range wider than 1e30 can place `+inf` inside the ramp.

Works on rigid, skinned (it follows the joint palette) and instanced meshes (entities sharing one
mesh each get their own overlay or none). It draws after the post stack, so the colors are exactly
the ramp's: no exposure, tonemap or bloom. Surfaces behind nearer geometry stay hidden.

Check it worked: `editor.capture_viewport` before and after; only the targeted entity's pixels
change, and `clear` restores them exactly.

## Rust API (for tools linking the crates)

`regia_render::{ScalarOverlay, Ramp, RampStop, ramp_position}` (component and data),
`VertexAdjacency::new(indices, vertex_count).neighborhood(vertices, &BrushSeed, radius)` and
`apply_brush(values, &neighborhood, radius, BrushFalloff, BrushMode, strength)` for brushes: a pick
hit's `indices` and `barycentric` fill the `BrushSeed`.

Invalid/missing entity bits, non-mesh entities, multiple value sources, or malformed ramps/ranges
return `F0002`. A length mismatch in `values` is a successful response whose `fit` is the object
`{ "mismatch": "short" | "long", "values", "vertices" }` instead of the string `"exact"`, as described above. Workflow: get the mesh entity from
`editor.pick_hit`, set values or an axis ramp, capture the viewport to review, then send `clear: true`
when finished.

Failing call (lavapipe; the entity bits name no entity in the editor world, so the existence check fails
before the mesh check):

```console
$ regia agent call editor.set_scalar_overlay '{"entity":4294967295,"constant":0.5}' --project samples/arena
error: method call failed: no entity 4294967295 (-32602): {"code":"F0002","hint":"check the method's parameters in the agent guide"}
```

<!-- source: book/agents/model-report.md -->
# Model map and node report

## `editor.model_report`

Read-only, CPU only. Params: `path` (project-relative glTF/GLB, required), `class` (`prop` default,
`character`, `vehicle`, `building`, `hero`), `limits` (object overriding the class limits), `root` (entity
id of a hierarchy from `editor.spawn_gltf_hierarchy`), `text` (also return the log rendering).

```json
{ "method": "editor.model_report",
  "params": { "path": "models/tank.glb", "class": "vehicle",
              "limits": { "max_texture_dimension": 2048, "require_normal_maps": true },
              "text": true } }
```

Returns `{ path, report, clean, text? }`. `report` has `nodes[]` (`gltf_index`, `name`, `parent`,
`children`, `depth`, `triangles`, `vertices`, `materials`, `skin`, `joints`, `is_socket`,
`is_collision`, `is_joint`, `in_scene`), `roots`, `skins[]`, `materials[]` (also `glass`), `lods[]` (`level`, `triangles`, `mesh_nodes`; empty without
`_LOD<n>` node names), `maps[]` (`material`, `slot`, `bound`,
`size`, `used`), `totals`, `flags[]` (`kind`, `subject`, `value`, `limit`, `message`),
`duplicate_names[]` and `orphans[]` (`gltf_index`, `name`, `reason`). `clean` is true with no flag,
duplicate or orphan.

Limit names: `max_triangles`, `max_node_triangles`, `max_nodes`, `max_materials`,
`max_materials_per_node`, `max_joints_per_skin`, `max_texture_dimension`, `max_texture_bytes`,
`require_normal_maps`, `lod1_permille`, `lod2_permille`, `lod3_permille`, `lod_ratio_tolerance_percent`,
`max_lod2_triangles`, `max_lod3_triangles`, `max_glass_materials`. An unknown name is an `invalid_params` error. 0 disables a check.

Nodes named `collision_*` are physics proxies (`regia_asset::is_collision_node_name`): they have
`is_collision: true`, stay out of `totals.triangles`, `totals.vertices`, `lods[]`, the material tables and
the per-node triangle budget, and are counted in `totals.collision_nodes`, `collision_triangles` and
`collision_vertices` instead.

How to check a result: "normal map not bound" is a `maps[]` row with `slot: "normal"`, `bound:
false`, `used: true`; a node over budget is a `flags[]` entry with `kind: "node_triangles"` and the
node name as `subject`. With `root`, a missing or extra entity is an `orphans[]` entry; a
`gltf_index` of null means the entity is not in the file.

For the `hero` class, `flags[]` also carries `lod_triangles` (subject `LOD2` or `LOD3` over its hard
ceiling), `lod_ratio` (a level above its expected share of LOD0) and `glass_materials` (subject `model`).
See [Model map and node report](book/user-guide/model-report.md) for the numbers.

## `editor.model_extensions`

Read-only, CPU only. Params: `path` (project-relative glTF/GLB, required), `include_json` (also return
the raw JSON of unknown extension blocks, default false).

```json
{ "method": "editor.model_extensions", "params": { "path": "models/car.glb" } }
```

Returns `{ path, extensions }`; `extensions` has `used`, `required`, `materials[]` (`index`,
`clearcoat`, `sheen`, `specular`, `anisotropy`, `emissive_strength`, `textures` by slot with `image`,
`tex_coord` and `transform`), `unknown[]` (`scope`, `index`, `sub_index`, `extension`, `json` only with
`include_json`), `dropped_unknown` and `unknown_names`. A file with `unknown_names` empty uses only
extensions Regia Engine reads. See [glTF extensions](book/user-guide/gltf-extensions.md) for which of them
render.

<!-- source: book/agents/open-kit.md -->
# Open kit

## `editor.open_kit`

Read-only. Opens a Tincal kit folder in the editor's Kit panel (the same state **File ▸ Open kit…**
uses) and returns what is in it. Params: `path` (the kit folder, absolute or relative to the open
project, required), `clip` (play this clip in the animation preview), `render` (also render the kit,
default false), and for the render `lod`, `width`, `height` (default 320×240, clamped to
64..=2048), `yaw`, `pitch` and `sockets` (paint socket marks, default true).

```json
{ "method": "editor.open_kit",
  "params": { "path": "/home/me/kits/jmc_hauler_v3", "clip": "idle", "render": true } }
```

Returns:

- `kit_id`, `path` (the canonical folder), `manifest` (`kit_id`, `kind`, `class`, `faction`,
  `replaces`, `stats_from`, `contract`, `version`), `character_kit` (the skeleton root's
  `{"tincal_kit": 1}` extras).
- `model` and `cockpit` (or null): `file`, `bytes`, `nodes`, `mesh_nodes`, `skins`,
  `skeleton_root`, `lod_levels`; the cockpit also has `attached_to`: `"socket_cockpit"` or
  `"origin"`.
- `lods[]`: `level`, `authored` (from `_LOD<n>` nodes, else generated), `triangles`.
- `clips[]`: `name`, `duration` (seconds), `source` (`model` or `rig`), `rig_secs`, `joint`.
- `sockets[]`: `name`, `position`, `parent`, `in_model`, `in_sockets_json`.
- `checksums`: `verdict` (`verified`, `failed`, `absent`, `unreadable`), `entries[]` (`file`,
  `expected`, `status`: `ok`, `mismatch` with `actual`, `missing`, `refused` with `reason`),
  `unlisted`, `malformed_lines`, `error`.
- `warnings[]`: `file`, `message`.
- `preview_rig` (the model is the animation preview rig), `clip_played` (null without `clip`).
- `budget`: the kit's budget against its class's default limits, the same object as
  `editor.budget { "source": "kit" }` returns ([budget meters](book/agents/editor-budget.md)); null when the
  model was not measured.
- With `render`: `render` = `{ width, height, lod, mime, png_base64, socket_marks: [{name, x, y}] }`.

A folder without `kit.json` or its model, or with either unsafe, too large or malformed, is an
error whose `data.kit_error` is one of `not_a_folder`, `missing_manifest`, `bad_manifest`,
`invalid_kit_id`, `missing_model`, `unsafe_path`, `too_large`, `io`, `bad_model`. Everything else
(a bad sidecar, a checksum mismatch, a symlink out of the folder) is a `warnings[]` entry.

`checksums.entries[].file` is the name as listed in `SHA256SUMS`: a flat name or an in-folder
subpath such as `textures/x.png`. A listed name with `..`, a leading `/`, a backslash, a colon, NUL,
an empty component, or a symlink out of the folder is `status: "refused"` and the verdict `failed`.
`manifest.faction` may be `generic` (no warning). With a cockpit glb at `socket_cockpit`, the hull
glb must not also hold the cockpit geometry: the editor draws both and hides no nodes.

How to check a result: a tampered file is a `checksums.entries[]` row with `status: "mismatch"`
and a warning `"<file>: checksum mismatch: ..."`; a cockpit at the wrong place is
`cockpit.attached_to: "origin"` with a warning naming `socket_cockpit`. After `clip`, see the
clip play with `editor.capture_panel { "panel": "clip" }`, or step it with `editor.anim_clip`.
See [Open kit](book/user-guide/open-kit.md) for the folder layout and the limits.

`path` is required. `clip` is optional; `render` defaults false. When rendering, `lod` defaults to 0
and must index an available LOD; `width`/`height` default to 320×240 and clamp to 64–2048, `yaw` and
`pitch` default to 0.6 and 0.35 radians, and `sockets` defaults true. Missing folder/manifest/model
uses `F0003`; refused or malformed kit data uses `F0002`, with the specific `data.kit_error` values
listed above. Workflow: open the folder, inspect warnings/checksums and available clips, request a
render at a selected LOD, then capture the clip panel if animation needs review.

Captured failing call (lavapipe; required `path` missing):

```console
$ regia agent call editor.open_kit '{}' --project samples/arena
error: method call failed: `path` is required (-32602): {"code":"F0002","hint":"check the method's parameters in the agent guide"}
```

<!-- source: book/agents/animation-robustness.md -->
# Animation robustness: clip reports and playback rules

`anim.clip_report` checks the clips a rig plays before they show up as a wrong pose: broken
key data, notifies that can never fire, root motion that drifts per lap, and how far the
cook's compression moves the joints. This page also lists the playback rules the evaluator
follows (ADR-871), so an agent knows what a graph should do and can verify it with
`anim.get_state`, `play.step` and screenshots.

## Report a rig's clips

```json
{ "entity": 4294967310 }
→ { "entity": 4294967310, "skeleton": 52,
    "tolerances": { "position": 0.005, "rotation": 0.005, "scale": 0.005, "propagated": 0.01 },
    "issue_count": 1,
    "clips": [
      { "name": "walk", "duration": 1.0, "tracks": 52, "notifies": 2,
        "root_motion": { "mode": "XZ", "joint": 0, "per_lap": [0.0, 0.0, -1.38], "yaw_per_lap": 0.0 },
        "loop_seam": { "max_rotation": 0.004, "max_translation": 0.0, "joint": 12, "joint_name": "spine_02" },
        "issues": [],
        "compression": { "max_position": 0.0041, "max_rotation": 0.0047, "max_scale": 0.0,
                         "max_object_position": 0.012, "worst_joint": 31, "worst_joint_name": "hand_l",
                         "worst_time": 0.48, "samples": 121, "within_tolerance": true,
                         "raw_bytes": 61224, "compressed_bytes": 9310, "ratio": 0.152 } },
      { "name": "wave", ...,
        "issues": [ { "code": "notify_outside_clip",
                      "detail": "notify \"wave_end\" at 2.4 s is outside 0..=2 s" } ], ... } ] }
```

Parameters (all optional except `entity`):

| Param | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `clip` | Report only this clip. An unknown name is `NOT_FOUND`. |
| `compression` | `false` skips the compression pass (cheaper on large libraries). |
| `position_tolerance`, `rotation_tolerance`, `scale_tolerance`, `propagated_tolerance` | Cook tolerances to measure against (meters, radians, scale, meters). Each must be a finite number from the smallest positive `f32` through 1000, else `INVALID_PARAMS`. Zero is refused. |

Clips are sorted by name. `skeleton` is the rig's joint count (`null` without a
`SkinnedMesh`; then the compression error is local only and `max_object_position` is 0).

### Loop seam

`loop_seam` says how far each clip's last frame is from its first, per joint in local space:
`max_rotation` (radians), `max_translation` (meters) and the joint with the largest seam. A
looping clip pops by that much at every loop point, so a clean loop reads close to 0. The
root-motion axes the clip extracts are left out, because the character controller carries them
across the loop. A walk without root-motion extraction shows its whole stride as a translation
seam: the rig snaps back every loop.

### Issue codes

Every `issues[].code` is one of these stable strings:

| Code | Meaning | What plays wrong |
|---|---|---|
| `bad_duration` | The clip duration is not a finite positive number. | The clip is stuck at time 0. |
| `non_finite_key` | A key time or value is NaN or infinite. | A sample is NaN when the segment it interpolates, or the endpoint it clamps to, contains that key. |
| `unsorted_times` | Key times do not strictly increase. | Keys play out of order. |
| `key_count_mismatch` | A curve has more times than values (or the reverse). | An unequal joint channel is skipped, so the joint keeps the pose's current value (the bind pose, when the evaluator just copied it). A morph track or a named curve with the same mismatch plays the paired prefix. |
| `key_outside_clip` | A key lies before 0 or after the clip end. | The outside key is still an interpolation endpoint. Playback clamps the clock to the clip; sampling clamps the clock to the key range. Neither drops the key. |
| `non_unit_rotation` | A rotation key is more than 1 % off unit length. | Skinning scales the mesh. |
| `notify_outside_clip` | A notify lies outside `0..=duration`. | It never fires. |
| `joint_out_of_range` | A track animates a joint the rig's skeleton does not have. | The track is skipped. |
| `duplicate_track` | Two tracks animate the same joint. | The later sampleable channel wins. A later channel that is not sampleable is skipped, so the earlier value remains. |
| `root_motion_track_missing` | Root motion names a joint the clip has no track for. | No root motion is extracted. |

### Compression error

`compression` cooks the clip with the given tolerances and samples the cooked clip against the
source at every key time of either and every midpoint between them. `max_position`,
`max_rotation` and `max_scale` are local joint errors; `max_object_position` is the
object-space joint error with every ancestor's error added up (what a viewer sees on a hand
or a foot). `within_tolerance` says whether the local errors respect the tolerances.

Key reduction quantises each key first and measures the reconstructed chord against the full
tolerance, so `within_tolerance` holds for ordinary clips. It is `false` when a track spans a
range too large for 16-bit keys at that tolerance: half a step of a 2 km root track is about
15 mm, more than 5 mm. Split such a clip, or cook it with a looser `position_tolerance` on
purpose.

## Playback rules the evaluator follows

These hold for every graph (ADR-871):

- **Root motion blends like the pose.** A blend space at 50/50 between walk (1 m/s) and run
  (3 m/s) moves the character at 2 m/s. A cross-fade weights the source by `1 − alpha` and the
  target by `alpha`; a clip without root motion counts as standing still. A masked layer
  contributes root motion only where its mask covers the skeleton root.
- **Long frames count every lap.** A frame that covers several loops of a clip (a hitch, a far
  LOD animator updating a few times a second) adds each lap's root motion and fires each
  notify once per lap (at most 16 times per notify per frame).
- **Reverse playback** (`speed < 0`, or a negative animator speed) plays from the end, wraps at
  the start when looping, moves root motion backwards and fires notifies in reverse order. A
  one-shot played in reverse finishes at its start (`ClipFinished`).
- **A notify at time 0 fires** on the first frame of a clip and on every loop.
- **A clip under half weight is silent.** Notifies fire only when the clip's effective weight is at
  least one half (`0.5 - 1e-4`). A 50/50 blend fires both sides. A blend at alpha 0.4 (parent weight 1)
  fires only the heavy side. A synced blend space gives each sample `weight × sample weight`, so a
  dominant sample under one half is silent too, even when it is the loudest sample. Entering a state
  uses the machine's audible weight: an enter under one half fires no start notify. A clip at weight 0
  (the far input of a blend pinned to one side, a cross-fade source on its last frame) is the same
  rule. `Notify` transition conditions still see every notify name, so a machine in a hidden branch
  keeps following them.
- **Entering a state restarts it.** The second jump plays the jump clip from the start again.
  An any-state transition (`from: None`) never re-enters the state that is already current, so
  a condition that stays true (`IsDead`) enters once instead of restarting every frame.
  An explicit self-transition (`from: Some("Hit"), to: "Hit"`) restarts the state.
- **Synced blend spaces** advance on one clock at the weighted average of the active samples'
  durations, so the cadence changes smoothly with the parameter, and keep that phase when the
  parameter jumps (sprint from a walk keeps the same foot forward). A sample fading in starts at
  the shared phase (no root-motion spike). Only the dominant sample fires notifies, and only when
  its effective weight is at least one half, so footsteps are not doubled and a dominant sample
  under half is silent.
- **Morph weights blend like the pose.** A target one side of a blend lacks counts as 0, so a smile
  fades out over a cross-fade instead of popping at its end. A face layer at weight 0.5 shows half
  the expression. An additive clip adds its morphs to the base.
- **Named curves** sampled by several clips are blended by the same weights.
- **Bad numbers do not reach the pose.** A NaN or infinite blend weight reads as 0, a NaN
  blend-space input as 0, and an IK node whose target is non-finite, or a socket that has not
  been placed yet, leaves the pose alone. Graph files with NaN or infinite speeds, sample
  positions, look-at limits or layer easing times, or a negative transition duration, fail to
  load with a message naming the field.
- **IK settings never panic.** Look-at limits and pelvis ranges are magnitudes (their sign is
  ignored, NaN means no limit for look-at and 0 for pelvis ranges); joint limits may come in
  either order; very short bones are solved.

## Verifying a fix

1. `anim.clip_report { entity }`: no `issues`, `within_tolerance: true`.
2. `anim.set_param` to the blend you want to see, `play.step`, and read `root_motion.delta`
   from `anim.get_state`: it changes smoothly as you sweep the parameter.
3. `seeing.screenshot` to judge the pose by eye.
