# Resource inspector: list and dump GPU targets

When a frame looks wrong, the useful question is what an intermediate target holds: the HDR
color before tonemapping, the depth, the velocity, the ambient-occlusion result, a shadow atlas,
the terrain virtual-texture atlas, the cloud history. Two read-only calls answer it.

## List

```json
seeing.list_resources { "label": "bloom", "category": "render_targets" }
→ { "debug_readback": true, "count": 12, "total_bytes": 3407872,
    "resources": [ { "label": "bloom down 0", "kind": "texture_2d", "format": "Rgba16Float",
                     "width": 640, "height": 360, "layers": 1, "mips": 1, "samples": 1,
                     "bytes": 1843200, "category": "render_targets",
                     "copyable": true, "dump_format": "exr" } ] }
```

Both filters are optional. `label` is a case-insensitive substring; `category` is one of the
[`seeing.memory_report`](book/agents/seeing.md) categories. Fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `texture_2d`, `texture_2d_array`, `texture_3d` or `texture_1d` |
| `layers` | Array layers (2D) or depth slices (3D) |
| `bytes` | All mips, layers and samples |
| `category` | The memory category of the label (same rules as `seeing.memory_report`) |
| `copyable` | The GPU can copy it out now and the inspector holds its handle |
| `dump_format` | The file `seeing.dump_resource` writes: `exr`, `png`, or `null` (no writer) |

The list shows each target as it was last created under its label. A target the renderer
released later (a resize replaces `frame hdr`) stays listed until the label is created again.
It lists textures only; buffers (for example the GI screen lookup, which is a storage buffer)
are not in it.

Registered today: `frame hdr`, `frame depth`, `shadow atlas`, `velocity`, `ssao`, `ssao raw`,
the TAAU `taau display` and `taau history` targets, `bloom down N` / `bloom up N`, `exposed`,
`tonemap`, `fxaa`, `terrain vt atlas N` and the outdoor passes' render targets (cloud and fog
history).

## Dump

```json
seeing.dump_resource { "label": "frame hdr", "mip": 0, "layer": 0, "format": "exr" }
→ { "path": ".../.regia/agent/resources/frame_hdr_m0_l0.exr", "label": "frame hdr",
    "format": "exr", "width": 1280, "height": 720, "mip": 0, "layer": 0, "bytes": 7372928 }
```

- `mip` and `layer` default to 0. `layer` is the array layer or the 3D slice.
- `format` is optional and must suit the texture: `exr` for float formats, `png` for 8-bit
  ones. Anything else is `format_unsupported`.
- `out_dir` is confined like `render.out_start`'s `out` (no `..`; inside the project or the
  system temp directory). The default is `<agent dir>/resources`, else the system temp directory.
- The file is written through a temp file and a rename, so a reader never sees half a file.
- The call waits for the GPU (it is a tool call, not a per-frame cost).

EXR files are uncompressed scanline files. `Rgba16Float`, `Rg16Float` and `R16Float` are
written as `HALF` channels from the raw bits, so the file holds exactly what the texture holds.
`R32Float`, `Rg32Float`, `Rgba32Float` and `Depth32Float` are `FLOAT`; `Rg11b10Ufloat` is
widened to three `FLOAT` channels. Channels are `R G B A`, or `Y` for one channel. 8-bit formats
(`Rgba8Unorm[Srgb]`, `Bgra8Unorm[Srgb]`, `Rg8Unorm`, `R8Unorm`) are written as PNG; BGRA is
swapped to RGBA. sRGB-encoded texels stay as stored.

### Error codes

Codes are lowercase and stable (`data.code`).

| Code | JSON-RPC class | When |
|---|---|---|
| `resource_not_found` | not found | No target has that label. List first. |
| `resource_not_copyable` | unsupported | The GPU cannot copy it (`Depth24Plus`, multisampled without a resolve), or it was created while debug readback was off. |
| `format_unsupported` | unsupported | No writer for the format (for example `Rgb10a2Unorm`), or the requested `format` does not suit it. |
| `subresource_out_of_range` | invalid params | `mip` or `layer` is outside the target. |
| `readback_failed` | internal | The copy or the map failed. |

Bad parameters (a missing `label`, a negative `mip`) are `F0002`; no render device yet is `F0011`.

## Debug readback

Targets need `COPY_SRC` to be copied. The agent plugin turns on **debug readback** before the
renderer creates any target (`regia_render::set_debug_readback`), which adds `COPY_SRC` to the
targets that lack it and keeps their handles for dumping. Without the agent plugin the switch is
off: shipping usage flags are unchanged, and the registry keeps only metadata, so `seeing.list_resources`
still works but every target reports `copyable: false`. A host that is not using the agent can
call `set_debug_readback(true)` itself, before the first frame.

## Rust API

`regia_render::list_resources()` and `regia_render::dump_resource(&device, label, mip, layer,
format)` are the same two calls without the protocol; `regia_render::resource_inspector::track`
registers a target of your own.

<!-- source: book/agents/thumbnails.md -->
# Batch thumbnails

## `editor.thumbnails`

Many small renders of models or entities in one call, on one warm renderer. For candidate cards,
library cards, feed tiles and multi-view proofs. Params: `jobs` (required, 1 to 256) and `size`
(default picture size, 128).

A job is `{ path | entity, view?, yaw?, pitch?, size?, debug? }`:

- `path` (project-relative or `builtin:cube`) loads a model; `entity` (bits) draws that entity and
  its descendants (and model parts) from the open world. Give exactly one.
- `view` is `perspective` (default, three-quarter), `top`, `front` or `side`. `yaw` and `pitch`
  (radians) win over `view`; yaw 0, pitch 0 is the front.
- `size` is the square picture's side in pixels, clamped to 16..=2048.
- `debug` is `lit` (default) or `wireframe` (green triangle edges over the lit picture).

```json
{ "method": "editor.thumbnails", "params": { "size": 96, "jobs": [
  { "path": "assets/chair.glb" },
  { "path": "assets/chair.glb", "view": "side" },
  { "path": "assets/chair.glb", "yaw": 2.4, "pitch": 0.3, "debug": "wireframe" },
  { "entity": 4294967301, "size": 64 } ] } }
```

Returns `images`, one per job in order: `{ index, width, height, mime, png_base64 }`, and `stats`:
`jobs`, `rendered`, `failed`, `sizes` (distinct sizes drawn), `cpu_ms`, and the frame-path counters
the call caused (`pipelines_created`, `bind_groups_created`, `textures_created`, `buffers_created`).

Every job is framed by its own bounds on the asset viewer's stage, so a picture depends only on
its job: equal jobs give equal pixels, in any batch. Jobs run grouped by size, so each render
target is allocated once per size. A job with nothing to draw (an entity without meshes) comes
back as a blank (transparent) picture of its size and counts in `failed`.

Check it worked: call twice; the second call's `stats.pipelines_created` is 0 and equal jobs have
equal `png_base64`. Compare a `lit` and a `wireframe` job of the same model: they differ.

The Rust API is `regia_editor::thumbnails::ThumbnailRenderer` (`new(&device)`, `render(&jobs)`,
`render_in(&mut world, &jobs)`).

The request limits are 1–256 nonempty `jobs`; top-level `size` defaults to 128, per-job `size` inherits
it, and both clamp to 16–2048 pixels. `path` must be a string project path (or `builtin:cube`); `entity`
is an unsigned entity-bits integer. Exactly one subject is required. `view` defaults to `perspective`
and accepts `top`, `front`, or `side`; numeric `yaw`/`pitch` override it and each missing angle defaults
to zero. `debug` defaults to `lit` and also accepts `wireframe`. Invalid request shape/view/debug uses
`F0002`; an asset that cannot be loaded returns `F0003` (`not_found`). Workflow: submit a small batch,
inspect each returned PNG, adjust view/size, then repeat the same batch to confirm reuse via the stats.

Captured failing call (lavapipe; `jobs` cannot be empty):

```console
$ regia agent call editor.thumbnails '{"jobs":[]}' --project samples/arena
error: method call failed: `jobs` (a non-empty array) is required (-32602): {"code":"F0002","hint":"check the method's parameters in the agent guide"}
```

<!-- source: book/agents/shading-models.md -->
# Shading models: skin, eye, fabric sheen

Character materials (Tincal B3, B4, B6). The model belongs to a mesh entity's material: every
entity that shares the same material `Arc` draws with the first one's model. User guide:
[Shading models](book/user-guide/shading-models.md).

## `material.shading`

One mesh entity's model, or (no `entity`) every entity that has one.

```json
{ "method": "material.shading", "params": { "entity": 4294967301 } }
{ "method": "material.shading", "params": {} }
```

With `entity`: `{ entity, model: "standard" | "skin" | "eye", skin? | eye?, sheen: { color,
roughness } | null, material_key, shares_material_with: [entity] }`. Without: `{ entities: [...],
table: { materials, shaded_draws, conflicts } | null, renderer: { materials } | null }`. `table`
is the last extracted frame: `conflicts` counts draws whose entity disagrees with an earlier
entity on the same material (that entity's model is drawn, not theirs). `renderer.materials` is
how many materials the runtime renderer shades with a non-standard model.

## `material.set_shading`

Params: `entity` (required); `model` (`standard`, `skin`, `eye`; default: the one a `skin` or `eye`
object implies, else unchanged); `skin` and `eye` objects with any of the fields below (omitted
fields keep their value; switching model starts from that model's defaults); `sheen`
`{ color?, roughness? }` (linear `[r, g, b]` or `"#RRGGBB"`, or `null` to remove the lobe);
`remove: true` deletes the component.

```json
{ "method": "material.set_shading", "params": { "entity": 4294967301, "model": "skin" } }
{ "method": "material.set_shading", "params": { "entity": 4294967301, "skin": { "scatter_scale": 2.0, "transmission": 0.6 } } }
{ "method": "material.set_shading", "params": { "entity": 4294967302, "model": "eye", "eye": { "iris_radius": 0.15, "iris_depth": 0.03 } } }
{ "method": "material.set_shading", "params": { "entity": 4294967303, "sheen": { "color": "#C08090", "roughness": 0.4 } } }
{ "method": "material.set_shading", "params": { "entity": 4294967303, "remove": true } }
```

Returns `{ before, after }`.

| `skin` field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `scatter_scale` | 1 | Multiplies the measured skin profile's scattering distances (above 1 is softer). |
| `curvature_radius_mm` | 0 | Fixed curvature radius in mm (0 = estimated per pixel from the surface). |
| `normal_blur` | 0.5 | How far red (green half, blue a quarter) diffuse leans back to the geometric normal. |
| `transmission` | 1 | Weight of light passing through thin skin from behind. |
| `thickness_scale` | 1 | Thickness per mm of curvature radius for the transmission. |
| `secondary_roughness` | 0.75 | Second specular lobe's roughness. |
| `secondary_weight` | 0.15 | Second lobe's share (0 = one lobe). |
| `mm_per_unit` | 1000 | Millimetres per world unit. |

| `eye` field | Default | Meaning (UV units of the eyeball map) |
|---|---|---|
| `iris_center` | [0.5, 0.5] | Pupil centre. |
| `iris_radius` | 0.16 | Iris (limbus) radius. |
| `limbus_width`, `limbus_darkening` | 0.025, 0.6 | The dark ring at the iris edge. |
| `iris_depth` | 0.04 | Depth of the iris under the cornea at the pupil (0 = no refraction). |
| `cornea_ior`, `cornea_roughness` | 1.376, 0.05 | Refraction index and the wet cornea's specular roughness. |
| `socket_occlusion`, `occlusion_start`, `occlusion_end` | 0.35, 0.3, 0.5 | Darkening toward the eyeball's edge. |

Check it worked: `seeing.screenshot` before and after the edit and compare; the entity's material
must not be shared with an entity that should stay standard (`shares_material_with`), and
`material.shading {}` should show `conflicts: 0`.

Errors: `F0003` (`-32001`, not found) when `entity` is not a mesh entity; `F0002` (`-32602`,
invalid params) for an unknown model or malformed `skin`, `eye` or `sheen` value.

Captured on lavapipe (llvmpipe Vulkan): the ephemeral cuboid entity had no `MeshRenderer`, so the
handler returned `F0003` before it validated `model`.

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":5,"method":"material.set_shading","params":{"entity":4294967094,"model":"Skin"}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":5,"error":{"code":-32001,"message":"entity 4294967094 has no MeshRenderer","data":{"code":"F0003","hint":"a shading model goes on a mesh entity: pick one from scene.query_entities"}}}
```

For light that spreads over a whole shadow edge, turn on [screen-space subsurface scattering](book/agents/subsurface.md). A skin material then swaps its pre-integrated falloff for the blur.

<!-- source: book/agents/handles.md -->
# Handles and snap targets

## `editor.snap_targets`

The snap points of an entity subtree. Params: `entity` (required), `kinds` (array of `face_center`,
`edge_midpoint`, `bounds_center`, `connector`, `all`; default all), `max_points` (default 1024, cap 8192).
Add `x`, `y` (pixels of a `width`×`height` pane, `view` as in `editor.pick`) and `radius` (default 10) to also get
`nearest`.

```json
{ "method": "editor.snap_targets", "params": { "entity": 4294967297, "kinds": ["face_center"], "x": 320, "y": 200 } }
```

Returns `count`, `truncated`, `points[]` (`kind`, `position`, `entity`, `normal` or null) and, with `x`/`y`,
`nearest` (a point or null). Check it worked: a box gives 6 `face_center` and 12 `edge_midpoint` points.

## `editor.handle_drag`

Replays a synthetic pointer drag through the handle state machine with no UI, so an agent can check handle math.
Params: `handles` (required; `{type: point, pos}`, `{type: arrow, origin, dir}`,
`{type: arc, center, axis, from, to, radius}`, `{type: plane, origin, normal, size}`; world space), `from` and `to`
(`[x, y]` pixels; the button goes down at `from`, moves in `steps` (default 8) and releases at `to`),
`snap_entity` + `kinds` (snap to that subtree), `radius`, `width`, `height`, `view`.

Returns `hovered` (handle under `from`), `grabbed`, `events[]` (`handle`, `phase` hover/begin/drag/end, `delta`,
`total`, `position`, `angle`, `angle_delta`, `snapped`) and `result` (the last event). `grabbed: false` means `from`
was not within the pick radius of any handle: aim at `handle.anchor` projected to the pane. Mutates nothing.
The interactive widget (`regia_editor::handles::handles`) is not reachable from the protocol; use
`editor.capture_viewport` to see the editor, and this method to test the math.

<!-- depth-2:method-reference -->

## Call reference

Parameters, results and error codes for every method on this page. Types and defaults come from the schema and handlers; limits include the contract. Error codes are in `data.code`; names explicitly labeled `data.reason` are additional handler reasons. Every method can also return `F0001`, `F0002`, `F0004`, `F0007` and `F0012`. The server can return `F0005`, `F0006`, `request_too_large`, or `F0008` when the method is not registered; see [protocol](book/agents/protocol.md).

Unless a lower or explicit method limit is listed, the dispatcher accepts at most 65,536 items in a top-level array parameter and 1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes in a string parameter. A limit violation returns `F0002`.

The request in each fence is the call that was sent with `regia agent call`.
The line under it is the host's answer.
A second fence tagged `json,ignore` is an error answer. Large fields are elided with `...`. A fence tagged `json,ignore` is a real call on a host or plugin method that the runtime schema does not list.


### `editor.handle_drag`

Replay a synthetic pointer drag through the custom-handle state machine (editor::handles) without a UI: press at `from` on a handle, move to `to`, release. Handles are {type: point, pos} | {type: arrow, origin, dir} | {type: arc, center, axis, from, to, radius} | {type: plane, origin, normal, size}, in world space. Returns the hovered handle, every begin/drag/end event (world delta, total, position, arc angle, snapped point) and the final result. Mutates nothing.

*Read, does not mutate.*

| Param | Type | Required | Default and limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `handles` | array | yes | Handle descriptions (see above). |
| `from` | array | yes | [x, y] pixel where the button goes down. |
| `to` | array | yes | [x, y] pixel where it is released. |
| `steps` | number | no | Interpolated pointer moves between from and to. Default 8; clamped to 1..=240. |
| `snap_entity` | number | no | Snap to the points of this entity's subtree while dragging. |
| `kinds` | array | no | Snap kinds (as editor.snap_targets). Default all. |
| `radius` | number | no | Pick and snap radius in pixels. Default 10. |
| `width` | number | no | Pane width in pixels. Default 640; clamped to 64..=4096. |
| `height` | number | no | Pane height in pixels. Default 480; clamped to 64..=4096. |
| `view` | string | no | Pane camera: perspective (default, the editor camera), top, front or side. |

Omitted snap_entity uses no snap targets. Handle positions are three-number world vectors; arc angles and deltas are radians. From and to each require two pixel coordinates.

Result: `{ hovered, grabbed, result, events: [{ handle, phase, delta, total, position, angle, angle_delta, snapped }] }`.

Errors: `F0002` for malformed handles, coordinates, view or snap arguments.

editor.handle_drag {"handles": [{"type": "point", "pos": [0, 1, 0]}], "from": [320, 240], "to": [360, 240], "steps": 2, "width": 640, "height": 480}

### `editor.snap_targets`

The snap points of an entity and its descendants: face centers (coplanar triangles merged), feature-edge midpoints, bounding-box centers and SnapConnector contact faces. With x and y (pixels of the width×height pane) also returns the nearest point within radius pixels.

*Read, does not mutate.*

| Param | Type | Required | Default and limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | number | yes | Entity id of the subtree root. |
| `kinds` | array | no | Any of face_center, edge_midpoint, bounds_center, connector, all. Default all. |
| `max_points` | number | no | Points returned at most (default 1024, cap 8192); truncated says if cut. |
| `x` | number | no | Pointer pixel x: with y, also return the nearest point. |
| `y` | number | no | Pointer pixel y. |
| `radius` | number | no | Snap radius in pixels. Default 10. |
| `width` | number | no | Pane width in pixels for x/y. Default 640; clamped to 64..=4096. |
| `height` | number | no | Pane height in pixels for x/y. Default 480; clamped to 64..=4096. |
| `view` | string | no | Pane camera: perspective (default, the editor camera), top, front or side. |

Only supplying both x and y requests nearest-point picking; otherwise the nearest field is omitted.

Result: `{ entity, count, truncated, points: [{ kind, position, entity, normal }], nearest? }`.

Errors besides the universal codes: `F0002`, `F0003`.

```json
editor.snap_targets {"entity": 1, "max_points": 4}
```

```json,ignore
→ { "message": "entity 1 does not exist", "code": -32001, "data": { "code": "F0003", "hint": "use scene.query_entities" } }
```

The host returned this error. `code` is the JSON-RPC code and `data` is the protocol object.

<!-- capture:editor.snap_targets -->

## Workflow: snap a drag to a mesh face

1. `editor.snap_targets` with the `entity` id. Add `x`, `y`, `width` and `height` when you also want `nearest` under the pointer. An unknown entity is `F0003`.
2. Pick a point from `points` (a `face_center` or a `connector`).
3. `editor.handle_drag` with one handle (`type` `point` at that position), `from` and `to` in pixels, and `snap_entity` set to the same entity so the drag reports `snapped`.
4. Read `events` in order: begin, drag, end. `result` is the handle's final world value. The call does not move the entity.

<!-- source: book/agents/skinning.md -->
# Skinning

Skinned meshes are drawn one of two ways. The default **vertex-shader path** skins each vertex
in every pass that draws it (sun shadow cascades, depth prepass, motion vectors, colour), with
four influences and linear blending. The **compute path** skins each instance once per frame in
a compute pass, and every pass draws that result. It also reads up to eight influences per
vertex and can blend with dual quaternions, so a twisted forearm or shoulder keeps its volume.
Nothing moves to the compute path unless you ask for it.

## `render.skinning`

Reports the compute path. No params.

```json
{ "method": "render.skinning" }
```

Returns `compute_all` (every skinned mesh on the compute path), `supported` (`false` on a
device without compute shaders; `unsupported` says why), `last_frame` (`instances` drawn from
the compute path, `dispatched` (the rest held a settled pose and were not skinned again),
`vertices`, `dual_quaternion`, `eight_influences`, `influence_mismatch` (an eight-influence
table whose length is not the mesh's vertex count: drawn with four), `resident`, `options`,
`counted` (instances skinned from a counted mesh's upload: the kernel reads the adopted vertex
buffer, or a GPU copy of it, ADR-7721)),
`gpu_bytes` (what the compute path holds on the GPU: source copies, two output buffers per
instance, palettes and tables; outside the mesh cache budget, freed after about 240 idle frames
or under memory pressure), and `entities` (every entity with options: `method`, `compute`,
`influences8` (table length or `null`), `on_compute_path`). `last_frame` and `gpu_bytes` are
`null` without a runtime renderer.

## `render.set_skinning`

Params: `compute_all` (boolean: every skinned mesh), or `entity` with any of `method`
(`"linear"` or `"dual_quaternion"`), `compute` (linear skinning on the compute path) and
`clear` (remove the entity's options).

```json
{ "method": "render.set_skinning", "params": { "compute_all": true } }
{ "method": "render.set_skinning", "params": { "entity": 4294967301, "method": "dual_quaternion" } }
{ "method": "render.set_skinning", "params": { "entity": 4294967301, "clear": true } }
```

Returns `{ before, after, note }` (both are `render.skinning` results). Changes apply from the
next extracted frame. Options on a character's root cover its skinned children. Eight-influence
tables come from code (`SkinInfluences8::from_cpu_skin`), not from this method.

Check it worked:

1. `render.skinning` after a frame: `last_frame.instances` counts the meshes you moved, and
   `dual_quaternion` counts the entities you set.
2. Twist test: pose a forearm 150° or more about its own axis. Capture a screenshot with
   `"linear"` and one with `"dual_quaternion"` and compare: the linear wrist pinches, the dual
   quaternion one stays round.
3. On a device where `supported` is `false`, everything draws linear with four influences.
   That is the fallback, not a bug.

## Eight influences from the cook (ADR-1622)

A mesh draws eight influences per vertex only when its asset opted in: the glTF's `.meta`
settings say `skin_influences: 8` and the skin has a second set (`JOINTS_1`/`WEIGHTS_1`). The
cook then writes `skin_influences` 8 (cooked mesh v3); everything else is the same bytes as the
default cook. The default is 4 influences, the vertex-shader path's four strongest, exactly as
before. The host attaches the table with `SkinningOptions::for_cooked_skin(&skin)` on the mesh
entity (it returns nothing for a default mesh).

Check it worked:

1. `assets.skin_check` on the cooked mesh: `stored_influences` 8 and `draw_influences` 8 (the
   default cook answers `draw_influences` 4).
2. `render.skinning` after a frame: the entity lists `influences8` (the vertex count) and
   `on_compute_path: true`, and `last_frame.eight_influences` counts it. A table of the wrong
   length shows in `influence_mismatch` and draws with four.

<!-- source: book/agents/radial-menu.md -->
# Radial menu

`regia_ui` has no per-widget protocol methods; an agent drives the wheel through the same input paths a
player uses, and reads the result from the wheel's component and its messages. User guide:
[Radial menu](book/user-guide/radial-menu.md).

## Drive it

- **Open.** `RadialMenu::open()`, `set_held(true)` (hold mode), `toggle()` (toggle mode) or the `open_action`
  entry of `VirtualButtons`. In a running app, `play.inject_input` of the bound action does the last one.
- **Point.** Stick: `GamepadAxisChanged` for `RightStickX` / `RightStickY` (or write `RadialSticks`). Mouse:
  `UiPointer::cursor` (the wheel needs two cursor samples; the first only records the resting position). Touch:
  `UiPointer::touches` and `active_touch` (the drag is measured from the first sample).
- **Confirm or cancel.** Release the open control, lift the finger or button, or `UiNavActions` `submit`
  and `cancel` (gamepad `A` and `B`).

## Read it

`RadialMenu::selection` (`None`, `Center`, `Sector(n)`), `open`, `progress` (`0..=1`), `phase()`; the
`RadialEvent` message stream (`Opened`, `Hover(selection)`, `Select { selection, id }`, `Cancel`, `Closed`); and the sector chips,
which are `RadialChip` nodes under the wheel (count = shown sectors + centre).

To see it: open the `ui_gallery` sample's Wheel page (key `4`) and `seeing.screenshot` while the wheel is
held. Check it worked: with eight sectors and the stick at `(1, 0)` the selection is `Sector(2)`; at `(0, 0)`
it is `None` (or `Center` with a centre action); jittering across a boundary by less than 12 % of a sector never
changes it.

The pure math (`RadialGeometry::select`) needs no app: `select(current, [x, y])` returns the sector or `None`.

This UI has no dedicated agent method, so there are no protocol parameters or error codes to list.
Workflow: open the Wheel page in `ui_gallery`, inject the configured open action with
`play.inject_input`, inject the pointing input, then inspect the selection/message stream and capture
the open wheel.

Captured failing input call (lavapipe; `actions` must be an array):

```console
$ regia agent call play.inject_input '{"actions":"bad"}' --project samples/arena
error: method call failed: `actions` must be an array (-32602): {"code":"F0002","expected":"an array","hint":"check the method's parameters in the agent guide","param":"actions"}
```

<!-- source: book/agents/quick-draw.md -->
# Quick draw: what the immediate layer drew

Games, prototypes and examples built on `regia_quick` draw every frame through two resources:
`Draw` (2D shapes, paths, meshes and text over the frame) and `Draw3d` (lit cubes, spheres,
cylinders, cones, planes, grids and lines in the world). Nothing they draw is an entity, so the
scene methods do not see it. Use `quick.draw_list` and the `QuickDraw` predicate resource
instead, and `seeing.screenshot` to look at it.

## What was drawn last frame

`quick.draw_list`:

```json
{}
→ { "frame": 240, "primitives": 14,
    "by_kind": { "ellipse": 6, "rect": 5, "text": 3 },
    "texts": ["SCORE 12", "LIVES 3", "PAUSED"],
    "background": [0.01, 0.01, 0.02, 1.0],
    "bounds": [-640.0, -360.0, 640.0, 360.0],
    "vertices": 412, "triangles": 380, "draw_calls": 3,
    "primitives_3d": 0, "lines_3d": 0, "frozen": false, "samples": 4 }
```

- `by_kind` counts 2D drawings: `rect`, `ellipse`, `line`, `arrow`, `tri`, `quad`, `polygon`,
  `path`, `mesh`, `text`.
- `texts` lists the strings of the text drawings in drawing order (at most 64). This is the
  cheapest way to read a HUD: the score, a prompt, a menu label.
- `bounds` is the box around every 2D vertex in logical units. The origin is the window center
  and +Y is up, so `[-w/2, -h/2, w/2, h/2]` is the whole window.
- `primitives_3d` / `lines_3d` count `Draw3d` drawings.
- `frozen` is `true` while the app holds its last frame (`DrawFrozen`). The numbers then describe
  that held frame.

An app without `QuickPlugin` answers `NOT_FOUND` (`F0003`).

## Assert on it

The same object is the `QuickDraw` resource of `play.wait_until` and `play.expect`
([testing](book/agents/testing.md)):

```json
{ "assertions": [
  { "name": "HUD shows the score",
    "condition": { "resource": "QuickDraw", "path": "by_kind.text", "op": "gte", "value": 1 } },
  { "name": "ten bricks left",
    "condition": { "resource": "QuickDraw", "path": "by_kind.rect", "op": "eq", "value": 10 } }
] }
```

Text equality uses `path: "texts.0"` (the first string).

## See it

The 2D layer draws after tonemapping, over the 3D frame and under the runtime UI, with 4×
anti-aliasing. `seeing.screenshot` includes it, from a visible or a hidden window; a headless
`target: "offscreen"` capture includes it with `window_layers: true`. `Draw3d`
primitives go through the normal forward path with a default lit material, so they take the
level's sun, shadows and exposure. Their lines are gizmo group `quick`, which `debug.set_gizmos`
can restyle or hide.

## Recipes

- **Did the game-over text appear?** `play.wait_until` on
  `{ "resource": "QuickDraw", "path": "texts.0", "op": "eq", "value": "GAME OVER" }`.
- **Is something drawn off-screen?** Compare `bounds` with the window's half size.
- **Why does the frame look cleared?** A `background` color in the list means the game fills
  the window every frame, which covers the 3D scene.

<!-- source: book/agents/ui-widget-style.md -->
# UI widget style: states, sizes and density

How a `regia_ui` widget decides what it looks like. This page is the model behind the `ui.theme_*`
methods ([UI themes](book/agents/ui-theme.md); lane D7 of `docs/specs/ui-default-design.md`, § 6.6): `ui.theme_get`
with `type`, `state` and `size` returns the look the resolver gives such a node, and the `Themed`
component on a live UI node holds its resolved style.

## State order

For one property of one node, states compose in a fixed order and the later one wins:

`normal → size (sm / lg) → selected → hover → pressed → error → focused → disabled`

- `focused` adds the ring and nothing else by default, so focus never hides other state.
- `disabled` wins a contested property and suppresses hover and pressed. The focused ring still applies. Disabled applies last.
- Hover is skipped for touch input.
- `md` is the base; only `sm` and `lg` add a layer.

## What drives each state

| State | Source on the node |
|---|---|
| hover / pressed / focused | `Hovered` / `Pressed` / `Focused` markers (written by the input systems) |
| disabled | `Disabled` marker |
| selected | `Selected` marker (checked, open, current tab or row) |
| error | `Invalid` marker |
| size | `WidgetSize` component (`Sm`, `Md`, `Lg`); absent = the node keeps its authored size |

`UiDensity` (resource, `Comfortable` default, `Compact`) picks the size table: control height
32 / 44 / 56 vs 22 / 28 / 36, padding 12 / 16 / 24 vs 6 / 8 / 12 (`sm` / `md` / `lg`).

## Style properties

`VisualOverrides` carries `background`, `border_color`, `border_width`, `radius`, `text_color`,
`focus_ring`, `focus_ring_width`, `focus_ring_offset`, `padding_x`, `height`, `min_width`, `gap`,
`text_px`, `icon_color`, `elevation`, `opacity`, `translate`, `scale`. A `StyleClass` holds one set
per state (`base`, `sm`, `lg`, `selected`, `hover`, `pressed`, `error`, `focused`, `disabled`) plus
`parts`: named sub-elements (`thumb`, `track`, `fill`, `knob`, `indicator`, `row`, `item`) that each
have their own states. `ThemeClasses::resolve_part` resolves one part for a node.

## Reading the result

`apply_themes` writes `Themed` each frame: `background`, `border_color`, `border_width`, `radius`,
`text_color`, `focus_ring`, plus `opacity`, `height`, `padding_x`, `translate`, `scale`,
`focus_ring_width`, `focus_ring_offset`. A `wait_until` on the colour or opacity of a node is the
check that a state took effect.

## The disabled rule

Disabled widgets draw at `UiThemes::disabled_opacity` over their normal look (the spec value is
0.45, `DISABLED_OPACITY`) with the dimmed text colour. The field defaults to `DISABLED_OPACITY`;
1.0 turns the rule off.

## Not yet wired

`translate` and `scale` are resolved into `Themed` but not yet read by layout or extract (D6, D8). A theme's own
`height`, `padding_x` and `gap` reach layout (ADR-9340, [UI themes](book/agents/ui-theme.md)); the `WidgetSize` token values in
`height` and `padding_x` stay resolved only. The focus ring colour, width and offset are drawn since D9: see
[UI focus ring](book/agents/ui-focus-ring.md). `opacity` is read by extract today.

## Inspecting a resolved style

`ui.theme_get` accepts `theme` (defaults to the UI's resolved theme), `keys` (a token-key glob or list of globs, default
all tokens), and `resolved` (include resolved token values, default `true`). It can also take `type` (widget type or
variation, such as `Button.primary`), `state` (one or more of `normal`, `hovered`, `pressed`, `focused`, `disabled`,
`selected`, `error` or `touch`), `size` (`sm`, `md` or `lg`) and `density` (`comfortable` or `compact`). Its
`resolved.props` contains the values to compare with the state rules above. The handler reports `ui_theme_unknown` or
`ui_theme_type_unknown` with `F0003`, `ui_bad_param` or
`ui_unknown_state` with `F0002`, and `ui_not_installed` with `F0013` when runtime UI is unavailable.

Workflow: query `ui.theme_get` for `Button.primary` in `hovered` state at `md` size, focus or hover the matching node
through the registered UI input method, then call `seeing.screenshot {}` to review the rendered state.

Captured failure on lavapipe:

Request:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"ui.theme_get","params":{"type":"__capture_missing_widget_type__"}}
```

Response:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"error":{"code":-32001,"message":"theme `regia-dark` defines no widget type or variation `__capture_missing_widget_type__`","data":{"code":"F0003","hint":"ui.theme_get without `type` lists the theme; types live under `types` and `variations` in the file","reason":"ui_theme_type_unknown"}}}
```

<!-- source: book/agents/quick-app.md -->
# Quick apps: the model, the loop, and driving a one-file game

A quick app (`regia::quick::app(model).update(update).view(view)`, `examples/quick/*.rs`, projects
from `regia new --template quick`) keeps its whole game state in one reflected resource,
`regia_quick::app::Model<crate::YourModel>`. Its drawing is not made of entities. So for a quick
app, `scene.query_entities` shows little: read the **model** and the **draw list** instead, and
look with `seeing.screenshot`.

## Read the model

The `QuickModel` predicate resource is the model as JSON: struct fields by name, `Vec2`/`Vec3` and
tuples as arrays, so `head.1` is the y of a `(i16, i16)` and `vel.1` the y of a `Vec2`.

```json
play.expect { "assertions": [
  { "condition": { "resource": "QuickModel", "path": "game_over", "op": "eq", "value": false } }
] }
→ { "pass": true, "results": [ { "detail": "QuickModel.game_over = false, eq false", ... } ] }
```

`resources.list` shows the model's full type (`regia_quick::app::Model<snake::Snake>`) and its
docs. Fields marked `#[reflect(ignore)]` (random generators, caches) are not in the JSON.

## The loop

`QuickLoop` is the run mode and the loop counters:

```json
{ "run_mode": { "mode": "LoopNTimes", "n": 1 }, "runs": 1, "ran_this_frame": false, "frozen": true }
```

- `Loop`: `update`/`view` every frame. `runs` counts them.
- `Wait`: they run on the first frame, then on input, a resize, or a scale-factor change. `ran_this_frame` is false while idle.
- `LoopNTimes(n)`: after `n` runs, `frozen` is true. The last drawing stays on screen
  (`quick.draw_list` reports `"frozen": true`) and the window still closes normally.

## Drive and check a quick game

Inject input, wait for the model to react, then look:

```json
play.inject_input { "events": [ { "type": "key", "key": "ArrowDown", "text": "", "state": "pressed" } ] }
play.wait_until { "condition": { "resource": "QuickModel", "path": "head.1", "op": "gte", "value": 2 },
                  "timeout_ms": 8000 }
seeing.screenshot { "timeout_ms": 30000 }
```

Keys are physical names (`ArrowLeft`, `Space`, `Enter`, `KeyW`). Touches are
`{ "type": "touch", "id": 0, "phase": "started", "x": 400, "y": 300 }` in window pixels; the game
sees them through `q.touches()` in drawing coordinates (center origin, +Y up).

The HUD text a quick app draws is in `quick.draw_list` → `texts` ([quick draw](book/agents/quick-draw.md)).
That is the cheapest way to read a score or a prompt without a screenshot.

## Running the examples headless

The examples are windowed apps. On a machine without a display, run one under Xvfb with lavapipe
and point the agent at a project directory of your choice:

```console
$ VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_SELECT='*lvp*' REGIA_PROJECT_DIR=/tmp/snake \
    xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1280x800x24" target/debug/examples/snake &
$ regia agent call seeing.screenshot '{"timeout_ms":30000}' --project /tmp/snake
```

## Hot reload

The model survives a game-library reload: it is snapshotted, the builder's `model` runs again in
the new library, and the snapshot is applied over it. Fields added since the last load start at
their `Default`. Check it after a reload with the same `QuickModel` predicate you used before.

## Limits

- A `draw_3d` frame needs at least one mesh (a cube, plane, …) for the 3D view to render. Lines
  alone (`grid`, `line`, `cube_wires`) draw nothing on their own.
- `QuickModel` reads one model. An app with two quick apps reports the first one found.

<!-- source: book/agents/decals.md -->
# Decals: scorch, pad markings, ruts

Project a prefab onto a hit, lay a strip along a path, or read how many decals the last view kept.
These need `regia_vfx::VfxPlugin` (a `DecalPool`). Without it every call returns `UNSUPPORTED`
(`F0016`) and does not enqueue a spawn.

Prefabs are `.decal.ron` version 3 (v1/v2 migrate) (`docs/formats/decal-ron.md`). The built-in names are `scorch`,
`pad_marking`, `rut` and `grime`. Each one's receiver mask is terrain and static meshes, so a
character layer is left clean when the host supplies a receiver buffer. The frame renderer
writes that buffer: it clears to terrain (layer 0, world up), stamps meshes, then lets native
terrain overwrite uncovered pixels with layer 0 and the heightfield normal
(`SharedPass::Receiver`). A rigid mesh stamps as static (layer 1) and a skinned mesh as a
character (layer 2), unless `receiver_layer` on the frame mesh or `MeshRenderer::decal_layer`
is non-zero — that value is the layer, so a rigid prop can be masked without a joint palette.
The depth those passes attach is `depth_for_output` (the scene depth, or a nearest copy at
the output size on a scaled frame). The LDR color is copied when the target allows
`COPY_SRC`. The stamp, the terrain receiver, the copy and the decal draw share the frame's
one command encoder.
Each survivor is one screen quad over the 16 px tiles it touched.

## Spawn on a hit

`vfx.spawn_decal` places one prefab. `position` is required. `normal` defaults to `[0, 1, 0]`
(a zero vector is rejected). `yaw` is radians. It spins a seed around world +Y and projects that
onto the plane: on a floor the decal turns, and on a vertical wall it does not make a 90° turn
around the normal. In-plane heading is `align_along`. `prefab` defaults to `scorch`.
`lifetime` overrides the prefab; omit it to keep the prefab's own lifetime.

```json
{ "position": [1.0, 0.0, 2.0], "normal": [0, 1, 0], "prefab": "scorch" }
→ { "index": 0, "slot": 0, "generation": 0, "live": 1, "capacity": 32, "prefab": "scorch", "normal": [0, 1, 0], "texture": null, "atlas_layer": 0 }
```

`normal` in the result is the decal's local +Z after alignment, not a copy of the input when the
input was un-normalized. `index` is the decal's current position in the pool's draw list, which
shifts as other decals retire. `slot` + `generation` is its stable id: it stays valid while the
decal lives and goes stale when it retires or the full pool recycles it. An unknown prefab is
`INVALID_PARAMS`.

## Rut strip

`vfx.place_rut` stamps overlapping decals along `points` (at least two). Defaults: prefab `rut`,
spacing `0.45` m, half-width `0.18` m, half-depth `0.15` m. Spacing below `0.05` m is raised to
`0.05` (the error text quotes that raised spacing). `half_width` and `half_depth` below `0.01` m
are raised to `0.01`; they are not rejected. `curve: true` with at least three points follows the
quadratic of the first three (12 samples). Extra points are not stamped, but the length check
sums every supplied segment first, so a far unused tail is `INVALID_PARAMS`. A rut is at most
4096 stamps, and every point must be finite; otherwise the call is `INVALID_PARAMS`.

```json
{ "points": [[-4, 0, 2], [0, 0, -2], [4, 0, 2]], "curve": true }
→ { "placed": 21, "live": 21, "capacity": 32 }
```

`placed` is how many stamps were built, before the pool's capacity drops the oldest. The curve
above is sampled at 13 points and stamped every 0.45 m, which is 21 stamps. `capacity` is the
pool's own size: 32 here is a small pool, and Desktop High reports 256. `placed` stays 21 while
the pool can hold them.

## Budget

`vfx.decal_budget` is read-only.

```json
{}
→ { "capacity": 32, "live": 12, "culled": 0, "tiles_touched": 0 }
```

The reply also carries `shading`: the path that shades each live decal (`post`, `forward` or
`split`) under the forward-decal switch, and the forward pass's tile counts for the view. See
[Forward decals](book/agents/forward-decals.md) (ADR-3255).

`culled` and `tiles_touched` are computed on the call when a `VfxView` is present. Without one
they stay 0, or the last figures a renderer stored. The `capacity: 32` answers above are a small
pool. Desktop High keeps 256 decals; Desktop Ultra keeps 512. The upload sorts by priority and
keeps the highest when the visible set exceeds the profile budget.

## Layering order

Decals draw lowest `priority` first, so the highest lies on top. Decals of equal priority draw
in spawn order: the newest lies over the older one. A full pool recycles its oldest slot in
place, so `DecalPool::decals()` is in slot order, not spawn order; hosts stage
`DecalPool::in_spawn_order()` instead (the VFX runtime and `vfx.decal_budget` do). When the
visible set exceeds the profile budget the lowest-ranked decals are dropped first, so among
equal priorities the oldest go.

## Static markings

Pad paint and grime that never move are a `StaticDecal` component on a level entity (`prefab`,
`yaw`, optional `receiver_mask`). The plugin copies them into the pool when the component is
added, and once more at startup for entities that already exist. Identity rotation projects
along world +Y.

### More `vfx.place_rut` parameters

The schema (`agent.schema`) also lists these optional parameters:

- `half_width` (number): Half-width across the path. Default 0.18.
- `half_depth` (number): Half-depth of the projection. Default 0.15.

## Decals in the reference trace and in the AOVs (ADR-2951)

The reference path tracer draws the same projected decal: `regia_pt::PtScene::decals` holds one
`regia_pt::PtDecal` per decal, with the fields of `Decal` and `DecalSurface` the decal shader reads. The tracer has
no `regia_vfx` dependency, so a host copies them. Use `PtDecal::from_box(position, rotation, half_size, color)` and
then set `roughness`, `normal_xy`, `normal_strength`, `emissive`, `angle_fade`, `distance_fade`, `priority`,
`receiver_mask`, `channels`, `edge_softness` and `blend`. Fold the lifetime fade into `opacity`. An atlas cell is a
`PtScene::textures` index (`atlas`): sRGB colour with coverage in alpha, sampled clamped like the frame's atlas
sampler.

The tracer uses the frame's projection and weights: the box test, receiver mask, grazing fade, edge feather,
distance fade and atlas coverage. It applies the decal to the hit's material inputs:

- **Albedo**: modulated (`blend` 0) or replaced (`blend` 1), weighted by the decal's weight.
- **Normal**: the atlas luma read as a height along the decal's axes, then the authored tangent-space normal
  blended in by whiteout. `normal_strength` weights both.
- **Roughness**: the decal's roughness, mixed in by the weight.
- **Emission**: added, weighted, as scene radiance. The frame's decal pass adds `DecalSurface::emissive` in exposed
  light, so to match a frame, divide it by that frame's exposure when you copy it into `PtDecal::emissive`.

`pack` leaves out a decal that is not `PtDecal::is_well_formed`: a non-finite number, a zero-length rotation or a
box of zero size. Such a decal would otherwise apply everywhere with a NaN weight and black out the trace.

So the trace lights the decal with the BRDF, and its `normal` AOV and `PtImage::roughness` hold the decal's values.

A scene without decals traces the base kernels, and its image is unchanged bit for bit. A scene with decals
composes the decal code into its own kernel set, cached like the material-graph sets
(`PathTracer::graph_kernel_compiles` counts both). Probe and lightmap bakes do not apply decals.

The frame is different. Its decal pass relights the composited colour after the forward pass, so the frame's
normal and roughness AOV (`seeing.frame_aov`, [Frame AOVs](book/agents/frame-aov.md)) holds the receiver's values on a decal's
footprint, not the decal's. The spec 27 suite's `decal_aovs` row records this as a fail with the numbers
([Spec 27 calibration](book/agents/spec27-calibration.md)).

Custom images and the `texture` / `atlas_layer` spawn result fields are covered in
[Custom decal textures](book/agents/custom-decal-textures.md).

<!-- source: book/agents/glass.md -->
# Glass: own canopy and damage

Per-instance glass control for transmissive meshes (`regia_render::glass`). Two components on a
glass mesh entity; entities without either draw exactly as before.

- `GlassView` — `exterior` (default) or `viewer_inside`: the pilot's own canopy or visor. That
  instance does not refract and its specular is scaled down to an anti-glare level
  (`inside_specular`, default 0.15). Crack shading stays on. Glass seen *through* it (another
  unit's canopy, a building window) still refracts: the refraction copy is taken before any glass
  draws, and the canopy only composites over it.
- `GlassDamage` — a crack set, a level D0–D3 and a list of impacts in mesh-local space. Each impact
  stamps one variant of the level's stamps into the instance's crack page at the hit point, so the
  cracks move with the vehicle or building. Saves keep the impact list; loading re-stamps it,
  byte-identical.

Crack sets are `.glasscrack.ron` v1 (`docs/formats/glass-crack.md`). Built-ins: `laminate` (unit
canopies: bullseyes and spall chips, then spiderweb with crazing and a milky halo, then heavy
crazing with small punched holes at the worst hits only; never sheds sheets or shards) and
`pressure_pane` (buildings: outer-pane star cracks, then a spiderwebbed outer pane over a clear
inner pane with parallax, then failure into chunky fragments and a decompression breach).

Refraction is on in Desktop High and Ultra (exterior glass), off on Low, Mobile and Deck.

## View mode

`render.glass_view { entity }` reads, `render.set_glass_view` writes:

```json
{ "entity": 4294967321, "mode": "viewer_inside", "inside_specular": 0.12 }
→ { "before": { "entity": 4294967321, "mode": "exterior", "inside_specular": 0.15 },
    "after":  { "entity": 4294967321, "mode": "viewer_inside", "inside_specular": 0.12 } }
```

`mode` must be `exterior` or `viewer_inside`; `inside_specular` is 0..=1.

## Own-canopy shading (v0.1.17)

Viewer-inside glass covers most of the screen, so its own light is shaded with a cheap shader by
default: the environment reflection with Fresnel, the sun (specular and diffuse, one cascade-0
shadow compare), the planet-shine fill, tint and absorption (the multiply pass is unchanged),
crack shading and the material's emission. It skips the clustered local lights, the fitted
emitters, probe GI and its reflection occlusion, the terrain and large-mesh occlusion terms, the
ground bounce, fog and multi-scatter. The visible difference: local lights and emissive panels
no longer put highlights on the own canopy. Exterior glass (windows, other ships' canopies) keeps
the full shader.

`render.canopy_glass` reads the process-wide setting, `render.set_canopy_glass` writes it from
the next frame (not persisted; one atomic change, so two callers setting different fields at once
both keep theirs):

```json
{ "shading": "full" }
→ { "before": { "shading": "cheap", "nearest_layer_only": false,
                "stored": { "shading": "cheap", "nearest_layer_only": false },
                "env_full": false, "env": "REGIA_CANOPY_FULL" },
    "after":  { "shading": "full", "nearest_layer_only": false,
                "stored": { "shading": "full", "nearest_layer_only": false },
                "env_full": false, "env": "REGIA_CANOPY_FULL" } }
```

- `shading`: `cheap` (default) or `full` (the forward shader, the look before v0.1.17).
- `nearest_layer_only` (cheap path only, default false): on frames with the glass front layer
  (screen-space refraction on), a canopy layer behind the nearest transmissive one adds no light
  of its own. Its tint still applies. A two-sheet canopy then loses the inner sheet's reflection.
- `REGIA_CANOPY_FULL=1` in the environment forces `full` over every setting (`env_full`
  true; `stored` shows what the host set).

The cheap path is for a camera inside the glass. A camera more than `eye_margin_m` (1 m) outside
the instance's bounding sphere (a chase, replay or texture-view camera while the instance keeps
`viewer_inside`) draws it with the full shader, so fog and every sun cascade apply. `render.canopy_glass`
counts the last frame's viewer-inside draws by the shader they took:

<!-- not-a-request -->
```json
{ "shading": "cheap", "nearest_layer_only": false, "eye_margin_m": 1.0,
  "last_frame": { "cheap": 0, "full": 0, "eye_outside": 1 }, … }
```

`last_frame` is `null` without a renderer. `cheap` 0 and `eye_outside` above 0 from the cockpit
means the glass's bounds do not hold the eye (a windscreen far from the pilot): the frame pays
for the full shader there.

Host code: `regia_render::set_canopy_glass(CanopyGlass { shading: CanopyShading::Full,
..CanopyGlass::default() })`, or `FrameRenderer::set_canopy_glass(Some(..))` for one renderer.
To compare, take a `seeing.screenshot` from the cockpit with each setting. The GPU cost of the
translucent section is `gpu_pass_ms.forward_glass` in `regia::frame_summary` (`telemetry.live`).

## Damage

`render.glass_damage { entity, set?, level?, stamp?, clear? }`:

- `stamp: { point, size?, energy? }` — `point` is the world hit (a ray hit on the mesh). It is
  moved into mesh-local space, mapped to the page (planar projection along the mesh's thinnest
  axis, or UV0 when the set says `damage_space: uv0`) and stamped now. `size` overrides the
  stamp's authored footprint in meters; `energy` feeds the set's escalation (default 1). With
  `level`, the stamp uses that level's stamps and raises the instance to it.
- `level` alone raises the level with one impact at the mesh center; `level: 0` clears.
- `set` switches the crack set (the impacts re-stamp with it). An unknown set is `NOT_FOUND`
  with the loaded names.

```json
{ "entity": 4294967321, "set": "pressure_pane", "level": 2,
  "stamp": { "point": [3.1, 1.4, -6.0], "size": 1.0 } }
→ { "entity": 4294967321, "set": "pressure_pane", "glass_type": "pressure_pane", "level": 2,
    "energy": 1.0, "impacts": 1, "applied": 1, "page_size": 512, "metres_per_uv": 2.0,
    "stamp": { "impact": 0, "local": [0.3, 0.005, -0.2], "uv": [0.65, 0.4], "texel": [332, 204] } }
```

Check the result with `seeing.screenshot`: cracks are frosted white lines (rough, scattering,
bending what is behind them), holes are cut out with jagged edges and cast no shadow.

## Breaches and fragments

When a `pressure_pane` reaches D3 (`GlassLevelChanged`), `regia_vfx::glass` bursts
`glass_chunks` (mesh fragments, 6–25 cm) and sends `GlassBreach { position, normal, atmosphere,
pressure }` keyed to the level's atmosphere. Each atmosphere plays its preset once
`(inside_kpa − outside)` is at least `min_pressure` (default 1 kPa): airless →
`glass_breach_airless` (vent plume of flash-frozen ice crystals and debris; with
`regia_framework::glass_breach::GlassBreachAudioPlugin` the breach sound emitter gets a
ground-coupled `AudioPropagation`, so it is felt, not heard), Mars → `glass_breach_mars`
(dust puff), Earth → `glass_breach_earth` (a faint gust). Earth outside is 101.3 kPa, so a pane
at 101.3 plays nothing. A pane at 200 kPa plays the gust, a shake clamped to 0.6 and a sound
emitter. A missing `GlassPressure` is treated as 101.3 kPa. `GlassPressure { outward, inside_kpa }`
on the pane sets the vent direction and the inside pressure. Games can send `GlassBreach`
themselves and override the presets in `GlassEffectSettings`; `GlassBreachFired` reports what
played and the sound emitter entity. `audio.propagation` on that emitter shows the paths.

<!-- source: book/agents/mask-decals.md -->
# Mask recolor and decal slots

Per-instance recolor and decals on a mesh (`regia_render::mask_decals`, Tincal B7): one material
and one set of textures, many looks. DO27 uses it for faction colors, chest numbers, callsigns,
faction marks and visor tint. An entity without a `MaskDecals` component draws exactly as before.

- **Palette**: `primary`, `secondary`, `trim` multiply the base color where the instance's mask
  texture has R, G, B; `emissive` × `emissive_intensity` glows where it has A.
- **Decal slots** (up to 8): an atlas `cell` (or none: a solid rectangle) placed over `uv_rect`
  (`[min_u, min_v, max_u, max_v]` in the mesh's base UV set), rotated by `rotation` radians about
  its center, tinted by `color` (`[r, g, b, a]`, a = opacity), blended by `blend`:
  `alpha` (paint over; metallic goes to 0 under it), `multiply` (tints, visor tint) or
  `emissive` (adds light × `emissive_intensity`).

Colors are linear `[r, g, b]`, or `"#RRGGBB"` strings (sRGB, decoded). The mask and atlas textures
come from the game; the agent edits values only. An instance the agent creates has no textures, so
its palette does nothing and its decals draw as solid rectangles until the game supplies them.

## Read

`render.mask_decals { entity }` reads one instance:

```json
{ "entity": 4294967321 }
→ { "entity": 4294967321,
    "palette": { "primary": [0.6, 0.01, 0.03], "secondary": [0.02, 0.03, 0.35], "trim": [0.8, 0.6, 0.02],
                 "emissive": [1.0, 0.26, 0.0], "emissive_intensity": 2.0 },
    "decals": [ { "cell": 7, "uv_rect": [0.42, 0.30, 0.58, 0.46], "rotation": 0.0,
                  "color": [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0], "blend": "alpha", "emissive_intensity": 0.0 } ],
    "drawn_slots": 1, "mask": [1024, 1024], "atlas": [512, 512], "atlas_grid": [8, 8] }
```

Without `entity` it lists every masked instance and the renderer's counters for its last frame:

```json
{}
→ { "instances": [ … ],
    "renderer": { "instances": 12, "masked_draws": 12, "fallback_draws": 0, "unsupported_draws": 0,
                  "gpu_entries": 12, "blocks_created": 12, "block_writes": 1, "block_bytes": 464 } }
```

- `fallback_draws` > 0: the instances' shader variant was still building in the background
  (mid-play, first frames after they appeared); they draw with the plain material meanwhile.
- `unsupported_draws` > 0: the material is a material graph, transmissive, premultiplied or
  additive; those draw without the feature.
- `blocks_created` grows by one per new instance, never per frame. `block_writes` counts the
  instances whose values changed last frame.

## Edit

`render.set_mask_decals { entity, palette?, decals?, remove? }`. Omitted palette entries keep their
value; `decals` replaces the whole list; `remove: true` drops the component.

```json
{ "entity": 4294967321,
  "palette": { "primary": "#1E3A8A", "trim": [0.9, 0.9, 0.9] },
  "decals": [ { "cell": 3, "uv_rect": [0.42, 0.30, 0.58, 0.46] },
              { "uv_rect": [0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0], "color": [0.55, 0.42, 0.1, 0.6], "blend": "multiply" } ] }
→ { "before": { … }, "after": { … } }
```

Errors: no `MeshRenderer` on the entity (`NOT_FOUND`), a color that is not three numbers or a hex
string, a slot without `uv_rect`, an unknown `blend`, more than 8 slots (`INVALID_PARAMS`).

Check the result with `seeing.screenshot`: each faction region takes its palette color over the
albedo's shading, decals sit where their rectangles are on the UV layout.

<!-- source: book/agents/draw-integrity.md -->
# Draw integrity and skinned bounds

Two renderer health readings on one page (`FrameRenderer::draw_integrity`, W2.2):

- **Render-world entries.** Every draw of a frame refers to a mesh, an object and a material entry
  in the renderer's caches. From the start of draw collection to the last encoded pass each of
  those entries stays (removals are deferred to the frame's end, the eviction sweep only takes
  entries idle before the frame). If one is gone anyway, the object is rebuilt on demand, or the
  draw is skipped with a once-per-id `warn` (`draw skipped: its … entry is gone`) instead of
  panicking. The counters tell you whether that last resort ever ran.
- **Draws the GPU cull missed.** On the GPU-driven path, collection sends a rigid opaque draw with
  a cull bound to the instanced batches, and it gets no per-object uniform. If the GPU cull then
  does not take it (its mesh lost the bound after collection), the draw is drawn per object
  instead: the renderer builds its object entry after the cull, counts it and warns once per
  object (`opaque draw missed by the GPU cull`). This was the v0.1.13 `object entry` panic, seen
  when DO27 drew one pilot mesh rigid for a hand-built pilot and skinned for another pilot in the
  same frame. Later versions skipped the draw instead, so the pilot vanished. ADR-4577 fixed that
  cause (the cache keeps the bound); ADR-8028 makes any other cause draw the pilot.
- **Skinned bounds.** A skinned mesh (characters, mechs) is frustum-culled by a conservative bound
  computed from its joint palette: each joint's bind-pose box of the vertices it weights, moved by
  that joint's matrix, unioned. A pose that throws an arm far outside the bind pose keeps the mesh
  visible; a character behind the camera is culled from the color passes and still casts its
  shadow. A mesh whose weights cannot be bounded (negative weights, a weight sum off by more than
  1 %, joint indices past its palette) has no bound and always draws, as before batch v020.

## Read

`render.draw_integrity` (no parameters):

```json
{}
→ { "skipped_draws": 0, "skipped_draws_total": 0,
    "objects_rebuilt": 0, "objects_rebuilt_total": 0,
    "cull_missed_draws": 0, "cull_missed_draws_total": 0,
    "deferred_removals": 0, "deferred_removals_total": 3,
    "skinned": { "bounds": true, "bounded": 10, "unbounded": 0, "culled": 4, "refused": 0 },
    "healthy": true }
```

- `skipped_draws` / `objects_rebuilt` are the last main-view frame's; the `_total` values count
  since the renderer was created, texture views included. Both should stay 0. Anything else is a
  renderer bug: capture the log lines `draw skipped` / `object entry rebuilt` (they name the kind
  and key) and the steps that led there.
- `cull_missed_draws` counts the last main-view frame's opaque draws the GPU cull did not take
  after collection sent them to the instanced batches; `cull_missed_draws_total` counts since the
  renderer was created. They were drawn per object, so nothing vanished, but the count should
  stay 0. A non-zero count is a renderer bug: capture the `opaque draw missed by the GPU cull`
  log lines (they name the object and mesh keys) and what the host submits for that mesh.
- `deferred_removals` counts mesh entries whose removal waited for the frame's end (a morph
  instance's deformed copy dropped while an earlier pass window of the frame may still draw it).
  Non-zero is fine; an object drawn under two mesh keys keeps a copy per key and defers nothing.
- `skinned.bounded` / `unbounded` split the last frame's skinned draws; `culled` is how many of the
  bounded ones were outside the view. `unbounded` > 0 with `bounds: true` means some skinned mesh
  has weights the bound does not cover (they draw every frame; check the asset's weights).
- `skinned.refused` counts the last frame's skinned draws that weight a joint at or past their
  palette's length, or at or past the 256-joint cap (`MAX_JOINTS_PER_SKIN`, ADR-5418). Drawn, they
  would skin from another unit's joints, so no pass draws them (and they cast no shadow). It
  should be 0: a non-zero count means the palette the host submits is shorter than the skeleton
  the mesh was skinned to, or the skin has more joints than the cap (split it; the cooked path
  refuses such a skin at load with `CookedSkinError::TooManyJoints`). A palette longer than the
  cap whose vertices stay under it draws with its first 256 joints and is not refused.

Telemetry summaries carry the same reading: `draws.skipped` (window total) and
`draws.skinned_culled_mean` ([telemetry](book/user-guide/telemetry.md)).

## Switch the skinned bounds

`render.set_skinned_bounds { enabled }` turns the skinned-mesh culling off (every skinned mesh
draws whatever the view, the pre-batch-v020 behavior) or back on. Use it to rule the bound out when a
character seems to vanish at a screen edge:

```json
{ "enabled": false }
→ { "before": { …, "skinned": { "bounds": true, … } }, "after": { …, "skinned": { "bounds": false, … } } }
```

The bound is conservative by construction, so a mesh that disappears with bounds on and stays with
them off is a bug worth reporting (the mesh, its pose, the camera). Hosts call
`FrameRenderer::set_skinned_bounds` directly.

The setter returns `F0002` when `enabled` is missing or is not a boolean, and `F0003` when there is
no runtime renderer.

Captured on lavapipe: calling `render.set_skinned_bounds` with `{}` fails with `F0002`. The CLI's
JSON `data` value is:

```json
{"code":"F0002","hint":"check the method's parameters in the agent guide"}
```

## Check it

Call `render.draw_integrity` after a long play session (DO27: several minutes with AI wingmen) and
after memory-pressure events: `healthy` must still be `true` (`skipped_draws_total`,
`objects_rebuilt_total` and `cull_missed_draws_total` 0).

<!-- source: book/agents/audio.md -->
# Audio: emitters, listeners, reverb, propagation

Inspect and tune entity sound without code. Both methods need `regia_audio::AudioPlugin`
(`regia::DefaultPlugins` installs it); without it they return `UNSUPPORTED` (`F0013`).

## List what is playing

`audio.list_emitters` (read-only) returns every `AudioEmitter` with its configuration and live
state, the listeners, the registered sound and cue names and the reverb-zone mix.

```json
{}
→ { "emitters": [{ "entity": 4294967301, "sound": "generator_hum", "cue": null, "autoplay": true,
      "looping": true, "volume_db": 0.0, "min_distance": 2.0, "max_distance": 40.0,
      "bus": "World", "occlusion": true, "voices": 1, "occlusion_amount": 0.62,
      "binaural": false, "hrtf_rate": null, "position": [4.0, 0.0, -10.0], … }],
    "listeners": [{ "entity": 4294967298, "position": [0, 1.7, 0], "forward": [0, 0, -1],
      "velocity": [0, 0, 0], "hrtf": false, "hrtf_rate": null }],
    "sounds": ["generator_hum", "rain"], "cues": ["footsteps", "impacts"],
    "reverb": { "weight": 1.0, "send_db": -4.0, … },
    "real_voices": 3, "virtual_voices": 0, "rejected_values": 0,
    "streams": { "playing": 1, "starved": 0, "underruns": 0, "starved_secs": 0.0 } }
```

`cue` is the name of the `SoundCue` the emitter plays (one of its variations, picked when it starts) when
no `sound` is set, else `null` (spec 16 § 3). `cues` lists the registered cue names. The buses
`audio.mix` reports are the tree a project's `config/audio.ron` defines (spec 16 § 1), falling back
to the default tree when the file is absent or invalid.

`hrtf_rate` is the sample rate of the HRIR table binaural voices convolve with: on an emitter,
its own track's table (`null` when it is not binaural); on a listener with `hrtf` on, the table
rate of the binaural voices (they share the one mixer; `null` for speakers or before a binaural
voice runs). It equals the mixer's rate (44.1, 48, 96 kHz, …): tables are built per mixer rate
on first need, at most six per sphere, so the interaural delay keeps its length in time on a
96 kHz device (ADR-7461). A value different from the device rate means the table set was full
and the nearest table is in use (the log says `HRIR tables are full` once).

`voices` 0 on an autoplaying emitter means its sound is not registered (check `sounds`) or it is
a one-shot that finished. `occlusion_amount` is the smoothed value the mix uses (0 clear, 1 fully
behind walls). `reverb` is `null` when the level has no reverb zones.

`rejected_values` counts the values the mixer refused since the process started: NaN or infinite
volumes, playback rates, pans and filter cutoffs (replaced by silence, the original speed, the
centre and an open filter), and loop regions kira cannot wrap (zero length, inverted or past the
end: the whole sound loops instead). It never goes down. If it grows across a `play.step`, a
transform, an emitter field, an occlusion tuning or a tool call is producing bad numbers: an
emitter at a NaN position is silent (its voice goes virtual) until it has a real place again. The
first refusal is also logged (`audio refused a bad …`).

`streams` watches the streaming voices and music stems: `playing` streams now, `starved` ones (held
silent because their decoder thread is behind), `underruns` since the start (one per starved
stretch of one stream) and `starved_secs` (rendered time spent starved, summed). A stream counts as
starved after it had been playing and stood still for 0.1 s of rendered audio; paused streams, a
headless run that does not render, and a non-looping stream at its end do not count. Underruns on a
device mean slow storage or a starved machine (the music plays late after each one); in an offline
render they mean the render outran the decoder: decode the sound with `SoundAsset::decode_to_memory`
for a reproducible render ([Audio](book/user-guide/audio.md)).

## Change an emitter

`audio.set_emitter` (`EditScene`) sets the given fields on `entity`'s emitter; omitted fields keep
their value. An entity without an emitter gets a default one first (`created: true`). A sound
with `autoplay` starts on the next frame; changing `sound` restarts it; `""` clears it.

```json
{ "entity": 4294967301, "sound": "rain", "volume_db": -6, "max_distance": 25 }
→ { "created": false, "before": { … }, "after": { "sound": "rain", "volume_db": -6.0, … } }
```

Fields: `sound`, `cue`, `autoplay`, `looping`, `volume_db` (−100..=24), `min_distance`, `max_distance`
(≥ `min_distance`), `fade_start` (0..1, a fraction of `max_distance` where the inverse and log curves
begin a smooth fade to 0; `null` for none), `spatial_blend` (0..=1), `cone_inner_degrees`, `cone_outer_degrees`
(0..=360), `cone_outer_gain` (0..=1), `air_absorption`, `doppler_factor` (0..=10),
`occlusion`, `bus`. `cue` names a registered sound cue: the emitter picks one of its variations on
start instead of repeating one fixed sound (a looping emitter loops that variation; `looping: false`
plays it once, like a sound). A `sound` and a `cue` are mutually exclusive: setting one clears the
other, and naming both in one call returns `INVALID_PARAMS`. Unknown sounds or cues return `NOT_FOUND` listing the
registered names; out-of-range numbers and unknown buses return `INVALID_PARAMS` and change nothing.

A one-shot cue at a position with no entity is game code: `Audio::play_cue_at(cue, position, emitter)`
plays it there through the medium, and `Audio::play_cue_on(cue, entity, emitter)` attaches it to an
entity's emitter so it follows (spec 16 § 3). Both apply the cue's authored low-pass, as `play_cue` and a
cue emitter do; on an attached voice the emitter's occlusion muffling stacks on top.

## Verify by ear, offline

Pair `play.step` with `audio.list_emitters`: after a step, `voices` and `occlusion_amount` show
whether the emitter is heard and how muffled. Reverb zones and listener `hrtf` are components:
edit them with `scene.add_component` and `scene.set_property` (`AudioReverbZone`, `AudioListener.hrtf`), or use
`audio.set_zone` for tunnels and mines ([Audio zones](book/agents/audio-zones.md)).

Audio that cuts out and restarts its loops is the engine's output gate. Grep the log for
`audio output paused`: it says whether every window was hidden or N slow frames in a row tripped
the throttle. The slow-frame pause follows the reflected `AudioThrottle` resource: `Auto` (the
default) arms it only on a software adapter (lavapipe), `On` always, `Off` never.
`Audio::throttle_suspend_count()` counts those pauses.

## Propagation media

Sound in Regia Engine travels through the level's **medium** (`docs/specs/16-audio.md` § 3c). Two
read-only methods let an agent check what a player would hear, and why.

### `audio.medium`

```json
{ "method": "audio.medium" }
→ { "kind": "airless", "airborne": false, "speed_of_sound": 0.0, "level_offset_db": -100.0,
    "ground": { "name": "ice", "wave_speed_mps": 3800.0, "q": 200.0, "coda_s": 4.4 },
    "listener": { "contact": "boots", "coupling_weight": 1.0, "vehicle": null, "structure": [] },
    "interiors": 1, "haptics": { "strength": 0.0, "last_event_strength": 0.31, "events_fired": 2, "pending": 0 },
    "path_voices": { "airborne": 0, "ground": 1 } }
```

- `kind`: `earth` (343 m/s), `mars` (240 m/s, −20 dB, strong high-frequency loss) or `airless`
  (no airborne path). It follows `LevelSettings.atmosphere.preset`, refined by
  `LevelSettings.audio_medium` (scene format v6).
- `listener.contact`: `boots`, `vehicle`, `structure` or `none` (jumping, flying, floating), from
  the listener's `ListenerCoupling` component. `coupling_weight` is the 50 ms fade of the ground
  path after leaving the ground.
- `haptics`: the rumble the ground path sends to the gamepads (through `regia_input`).

### `audio.propagation`

```json
{ "method": "audio.propagation", "params": { "position": [500, 0, 0], "category": "explosion" } }
→ { "paths": [ { "path": "ground", "delay_ms": 131.6, "gain_db": -31.9, "cutoff_hz": 167.7,
                 "coupling_cutoff_hz": 500.0, "coda_s": 4.4, "felt": 0.13, "audible": true } ],
    "bypass": false, "air": null, "ground_material": "ice", "coupled": true, "distance": 500.0,
    "audible": true }
```

Pass `entity` (an emitter with `AudioEmitter`; its `AudioPropagation` is used) or a hypothetical
`position` with a `category` (`impact`, `explosion`, `collapse`, `footstep`, `landing`,
`machinery`, `hull_landing`, `hull_scrape`, `hull_hover`, `planted_weapon`, `projectile`, `radio`,
`ui`, `cockpit`, `body`). Each path is:

- `airborne`: through the air (or a pressurised interior's own air, `air: "interior"`), delay
  `r / c`; through a wall it is muffled (`coupling_cutoff_hz` 400).
- `ground`: through the ground, delay `r / v`, low-passed by the material's Q (`absorption_cutoff_hz`)
  and by the listener's boots/hull/floor (`coupling_cutoff_hz`), with a ringing coda (`coda_s`).
- `direct`: the medium is bypassed (radio and UI buses, the listener's own body, the cockpit of the
  vehicle the listener sits in).

### Propagation recipes

- *Airless pilot jumping hears nothing*: set the listener's `ListenerCoupling.contact` to `None`
  (`scene.set_property`), `play.step` 4 frames, then `audio.propagation` → `paths: []`.
- *An explosion is felt before it is heard (Earth)*: the `ground` path's `delay_ms` is smaller than
  the `airborne` one, and `audio.medium.haptics.events_fired` increments when it arrives.
- *Mars is darker*: compare `cutoff_hz` and `gain_db` of the same `position` after switching the
  level's preset with `scene.set_property` on `LevelSettings.atmosphere.preset`.

## Procedural loops

A `.loopgen.ron` (`docs/formats/loopgen-ron.md`) renders a seamless loop from a noise and
filter graph. `audio.loopgen_render` renders one without playing it, so an agent can check a
file before a patch uses it. It needs the `play` permission and counts as a mutating call: with
`wav: true` it writes a file (ADR-3285), so a `read_only` client cannot reach it.

```json
{ "method": "audio.loopgen_render", "params": { "path": "audio/wind.loopgen.ron", "wav": true } }
→ { "name": "wind", "sample_rate": 48000, "channels": 1, "cached": false,
    "content_hash": "9c1f0e52a7d34b18",
    "stats": { "frames": 144000, "duration_secs": 3.0, "rms": 0.21, "peak": 0.64,
               "seam_jump": 0.0021, "max_step": 0.0187, "hash": "5be0a1f3c2d49e77" },
    "wav": "/tmp/regia_loopgen/wind-5be0a1f3c2d49e77.wav" }
```

Give exactly one of `ron` (inline text) or `path` (project-relative, ending `.loopgen.ron`, no
`..`). `wav: true` also writes a 16-bit WAV to `out_dir` (default `<temp>/regia_loopgen` on
desktop, the app cache dir's `regia_loopgen` on Android, where the system temp dir is
shell-owned; the file name carries the sample hash). `out_dir` must be relative to the project, or absolute inside the project, the
system temp directory or an `output_roots` entry of `.regia/agent.toml`, with no `..` and no symlink that leads out of them (checked on the deepest existing
directory, ADR-1816); anything else is `invalid_params` (`data.reason` `path_outside_project`). It works without the audio plugin; with it, the render
goes through the `SoundAssets` cache, and `cached: true` means the same file text had already
been rendered.

How to read the result:

- `hash` is the FNV-1a hash of the samples: the same file gives the same hash on every
  platform; a different `seed` gives a different one.
- `seam_jump` is `|first - last|` sample (the step when the loop wraps) and `max_step` the
  largest step inside the loop. A seamless loop has `seam_jump <= 1.1 x max_step + 0.0002`. A
  bigger value means `crossfade_secs` is 0 or too short for the content.
- `rms` near 0 is a silent graph (a mix with all gains 0, a `Gain` of -96 dB).

**Errors.** A bad file returns `INVALID_PARAMS` (`F0002`) whose `data.key_path` names the
offending value, e.g. `nodes[1].node.Filter.cutoff_hz` (above Nyquist), `output` (unknown id),
`nodes[0].id` (a cycle), `version` (newer than this engine) or `(file)` (RON syntax). Missing
or non-`.loopgen.ron` paths return `INVALID_PARAMS` / `NOT_FOUND` (`F0003`). No new error codes.

`audio.list_emitters` gains a `loopgens` object: `registered` (sound names made from a loop
generator, with the file's `content_hash`), `loops` (the cached loops with the same `stats`)
and `cache` (`entries`, `hits`, `misses`).

**Verify a patch layer by ear, offline.** Build the patch with `from_def_with_loopgen`, then
`play.step` a few frames and read `audio.list_emitters`; for a layer under test render the
loop with `audio.loopgen_render` and check `rms`, `peak` and `seam_jump` before listening.

## Cue points stored in a WAV file

`audio.cues` reads the cue points already stored in a WAV file: the RIFF `cue ` chunk and the
names in a `LIST` / `adtl` / `labl` list. These points are not a sound cue. A sound cue picks a
variation when it plays. This method does not play audio, does not decode PCM, does not
resample, and does not need the audio plugin.

```json
{ "path": "audio/marks.wav" }
→ { "count": 2,
    "cues": [
      { "order": 0, "id": 10, "sample_offset": 100, "name": "intro" },
      { "order": 1, "id": 11, "sample_offset": 200, "name": "loop" } ] }
```

`path` is project-relative. `..` and a symlink that leaves the project are `F0002`. A missing
file is `F0003`.

- `sample_offset` is `dwSampleOffset` as stored, in the file's own sample layout.
- `order` is the zero-based index of the point in file order across every `cue ` chunk. It is
  not `dwPosition`.
- `id` is `dwName`. Two points may share an id; both rows are returned.
- `name` is the first `labl` with that id, or null when none matches. An empty label is `""`.
  Label bytes are Latin-1: each byte is the Unicode scalar U+0000 through U+00FF, cut at the
  first NUL. The playback decoder does not read these strings.

A file with no `cue ` chunk returns `count` 0 and an empty `cues` list. That is not an error.
A cue chunk that claims more points than its bytes hold, and a label list that is cut short,
return `wav_cue_truncated` and no partial list.

**Errors.** `wav_cue_not_riff` when the file does not start with `RIFF`. `wav_cue_not_wave`
when the RIFF form is not `WAVE`. `wav_cue_truncated` when a cue or label chunk overruns.
`wav_cue_unreadable` when the path is not a regular file, the read fails, or the file is above
256 MiB. `F0003` when the file or project root cannot be resolved. `F0002` when `path` is
missing, not a string, or escapes the project.

Binding these points to a sequence is not part of this method.
