# Audio zones

Reverb volumes with presets, a per-zone distance scale, rock-thickness occlusion and mouth routing
(`docs/specs/16-audio.md` § 3d). Three methods; all need `regia_audio::AudioPlugin`.

## `audio.list_zones`

No params. Returns `{ zones, reverb, rock_field, count }`. Each zone: `entity`, `name`, `shape`
(`{kind: box|capsule|sphere|global, ...}`), `preset`, `wet_db`, `decay`, `damping`, `stereo_width`,
`distance_scale`, `blend_distance`, `cavity`, `priority`, `centre`, `portals[]` (world space).
`reverb` is the mix applied to player 0 (`weight` 0..1 is how far into the blend the listener is);
`rock_field` is true once the host installed an `AudioRockField`.

## `audio.set_zone`

Creates or edits an entity's `AudioReverbZone`. A `preset` (`tube`, `mine_gallery`, `open`, `custom`)
is applied first and keeps the entity's shape and priority; explicit fields then override it.

```json
{ "method": "audio.set_zone",
  "params": { "entity": 4294967310, "preset": "tube",
              "shape": { "kind": "capsule", "radius": 3.0, "half_length": 100.0 },
              "portals": [{ "position": [0.0, 100.0, 0.0], "radius": 5.0 }] } }
```

Fields: `shape`, `preset`, `wet_db` (-80..12), `decay` (0..1), `damping`, `stereo_width`,
`distance_scale` (0.1..10), `blend_distance` (m), `priority`, `cavity`, `portals`. Out-of-range values and
unknown presets are `invalid_params`; a failed call changes nothing.

## `audio.probe_zones`

Moves nothing. `listener` and `emitter` are `[x, y, z]`; `min_distance` (default 1) and `max_distance`
(default 50) describe the emitter's range.

```json
{ "method": "audio.probe_zones",
  "params": { "listener": [100, 1.7, 0], "emitter": [70, -10, 0], "max_distance": 400 } }
```

Returns `distance`, `distance_scale`, `effective_max_distance`, `in_cavity { listener, emitter }`,
`route` (`mouth`, `path_length`, `virtual_position`, or null), `rock_thickness_m` (null without a rock
field), `rock_gain`, `cutoff_hz`, `gain`, `gain_db`, `audible` (gain above 0.003) and `reverb`.

How to check a tunnel: probe with the listener on the surface above the emitter (`rock_thickness_m` is
the cover, `audible` false), at the mouth (`route` set, `rock_thickness_m` near 0), and inside the tube
(`distance_scale` 1.5, `effective_max_distance` 1.5 times the emitter's). `audio.list_emitters` reports
the live values per emitter: `rock_m`, `zone_scale`, `routed`.

## Example calls

Example calls (`regia agent call <method> '<params json>'`; entity ids come from `scene.query_entities`):

```text
audio.list_zones {}             # { zones, reverb, rock_field, count }
```

## A tunnel

A box zone with the `tube` preset over a tunnel's covered section is the whole setup; the tunnel
acceptance scene places one over its tube and checks that every corner of the tube is inside the zone,
that the listener is fully wet anywhere in the tube and dry once further out than the zone's fade
(`reverb_zone_covers_the_tube`, [Tunnel acceptance scene](book/agents/tunnel-scene.md)).

## Portal sound

Over cooked world geometry (a loaded `<map>.meshlayers`, plan row W-25, ADR-8416) install
`regia_audio::GeomSoundField::new(Arc<WorldGeom>)` on `AudioRockField`. It reads only the cooked
sections, portals, zones and blocker plugs, plus the core's segment test, so every answer is a pure
function of the file and the two points (no wall clock):

- **Path through the portals.** A source the listener cannot reach in a straight line is heard from the
  last portal before the listener (the mouth, for a listener outside), at the length of the shortest
  path through the portal centres. The emitter update moves the voice to that apparent source, so the
  distance curve attenuates by the path length and the pan points at the mouth.
- **Rock occlusion.** With no portal path (a source in the rock beside a passage, a buried source, a
  ridge) the sound stays on the straight line and `RockTuning` attenuates it by the rock on it: the span
  between the first roof or covered wall (`WorldGeom::rock_between`) or uncut ground seen from each end;
  an end inside the rock counts from itself.
- **Section reverb.** The section player 0 stands in arms its cooked preset (`tube`, `gallery`, `open`)
  as a global zone with priority 1 (an authored finite zone still wins); leaving every section disarms it.
- **Hearing range.** A listener in a covered section hears twice as far (the underground rule,
  `PortalSoundSettings::underground_hear_mult`).

Cells: a point inside a section zone is in that section (the smallest zone wins), a point under uncut
ground is in the rock (no portal reaches it), anything else is outdoors.

Agent reads (both null or false without a geometry field):

- `audio.list_zones` adds `geom_field` (true when the rock field is a `GeomSoundField`) and
  `armed_reverb` (`section`, `preset`, `decay`, `wet_db`) at player 0.
- `audio.probe_zones` adds `portal_path` (`kind`: `direct`, `portal` or `occluded`; `source_cell` and
  `listener_cell` as `{kind: outdoor|rock|section, section}`; `portals` crossed, source side first;
  `points`; `length_m`; `direct_m`; `arrival` unit vector; `apparent` source; `occlusion_m`;
  `range_scale`) and `armed_reverb` at the probe's listener. `distance` is the path length when routed.

```text
audio.probe_zones {"listener": [x, y, z], "emitter": [x, y, z], "max_distance": 600}
# portal_path.kind "portal", portal_path.portals [..], route.virtual_position toward the mouth
```

No new error codes: the methods keep their `F0013` (no audio) and `invalid_params` errors.

<!-- source: book/agents/voice.md -->
# Voice capture and loopback

Inspect and drive the voice capture stream and the voice loopback (specs/16 § 3b). All seven
methods need `regia_audio::AudioPlugin` (`regia::DefaultPlugins` installs it); without it they
return `UNSUPPORTED` (`F0013`). The method-specific codes are `capture_headless` and
`no_loopback` (below).

Regia Engine captures and plays voice back; it does not encode or transport it — that is the
game's job. The game drains captured frames to send to other players, and pushes decoded remote
frames into the loopback to hear them.

## Read the state

`audio.voice` (read-only) reports the capture stream and the loopback, if any.

```json
{ "method": "audio.voice" }
→ { "capturing": true, "device": "Built-in Microphone", "sample_rate": 48000, "channels": 2,
    "level_db": { "rms": -38.1, "peak": -12.4 }, "voice_active": true, "talking": true,
    "dropped_frames": 0,
    "loopback": { "running": true, "buffered_frames": 1240, "last_latency_ms": 34,
                  "max_latency_ms": 41, "chunks_pushed": 122, "chunks_dropped": 0 } }
```

- `level_db` is `null` when nothing is capturing; `rms` and `peak` are dBFS amplitudes.
- `voice_active` is the energy-based voice-activity detector (ITU-T P.56 style: short-term RMS
  threshold with hysteresis and a hangover).
- `talking` is the push-to-talk gate; `dropped_frames` counts frames the capture ring dropped
  because the game drained them too slowly.
- `loopback` is `null` when no loopback is running. `last_latency_ms` / `max_latency_ms` measure
  capture (or push) to first render; keep `max_latency_ms` under 60 ms for the § 3b loopback
  acceptance.

## Start and stop capture

`audio.capture_start` (`play` permission) opens the microphone; `audio.capture_stop` releases it.

```json
{ "method": "audio.capture_start", "params": { "sample_rate": 48000, "buffer_secs": 2 } }
→ { "capturing": true, "device": "Built-in Microphone", "sample_rate": 48000, "channels": 2 }
```

- `device` is a substring to prefer (default input device when omitted); `sample_rate`
  8000..=192000; `buffer_secs` 0.05..=30; `on_threshold_db` / `off_threshold_db` -90..=0
  (default -40 / -50; `off` must stay below `on`, checked against the other's default when only one
  is given); `hangover_ms` 0..=5000 (default 250); `window_ms` 1..=2000 (default 20).
- The device may open at a different rate than requested; the answer reports what opened.
- On Android the `RECORD_AUDIO` permission must already be granted by the platform layer —
  Regia Engine never prompts on its own. With no input device it answers with an error. In a
  headless run (`Audio::is_headless`) it answers `capture_headless` (`UNSUPPORTED`) and does not
  open a device. A threshold pair that breaks hysteresis is reported before that refusal.

```json
{ "method": "audio.capture_stop" }
→ { "capturing": false }
```

## Push-to-talk

`audio.set_talking` (`play` permission) replies with the requested flag. The gate is written only
when a capture exists, so with no capture `audio.voice` stays `talking: false` and a later
`audio.capture_start` opens the gate. With the gate closed, the level meter and the
voice-activity detector still update, then the samples are discarded: `Audio::tick_voice` returns
an empty list and nothing is pushed to the loopback.

```json
{ "method": "audio.set_talking", "params": { "talking": true } }
→ { "talking": true }
```

## The loopback

`audio.voice_loopback_start` (`play` permission) starts (or restarts) the loopback on the Voice
bus; `audio.voice_loopback_stop` stops it. The game pushes decoded remote frames into the running
loopback with `regia_audio::Audio::push_voice_frames` (or `Audio::tick_voice`, which drains the
capture straight into it for a local loopback test).

```json
{ "method": "audio.voice_loopback_start", "params": { "prebuffer_ms": 40 } }
→ { "loopback": { "running": true, "buffered_frames": 0, "last_latency_ms": 0,
                  "max_latency_ms": 0, "chunks_pushed": 0, "chunks_dropped": 0 } }
```

- `prebuffer_ms` is the jitter-buffer target before playback starts (0..=2000, default 40). Remote
  voice is untrusted data: non-finite samples are silenced and the rest clamped to -1..1 at the
  mixer boundary.

```json
{ "method": "audio.voice_loopback_stop" }
→ { "loopback": null }
```

## Placing the loopback (3D positioning)

`audio.voice_place` (`play` permission) places the running loopback in the stereo field
(specs/16 § 3b): distance gain, pan and an optional air-absorption low-pass, or the flat
center default. Refused with `no_loopback` (`INVALID_REQUEST`) when no loopback is running;
starting a new loopback resets the placement to center.

```json
{ "method": "audio.voice_place", "params": { "mode": "spatial", "gain": 0.8, "pan": -0.5 } }
→ { "placement": { "mode": "spatial", "gain": 0.8, "pan": -0.5, "cutoff_hz": null } }
```

- `mode`: `"center"` restores the flat default; `"spatial"` takes `gain` 0..=1 (default 1),
  `pan` -1..=1 (default 0) and `cutoff_hz` 1..=20000 (air-absorption low-pass, omitted = none).
- The gains ramp to a new placement over one audio batch and hold it exactly from the next, so
  per-frame updates from a moving anchor never click.
- A game places the stream from the world instead by putting a `VoiceStreamAnchor` component
  (distances, rolloff, air absorption) on the speaking entity: the AudioSync pass then pans and
  attenuates the stream like an emitter at that entity's position against the nearest listener.
  When the last anchor disappears (the entity despawns or is parked), the pass resets the stream
  to the flat center on that frame — an anchor that went away past `max_distance` left the
  placement at gain 0 and the loopback would otherwise stay muted. With no anchor at all, a
  placement set by `audio.voice_place` (or the game) is kept.
- `audio.voice` reports the live placement inside `loopback` as
  `{ mode: center | unresolved | spatial, gain?, pan?, cutoff_hz? }` (`mode` only when a
  stream runs).

## Recipes

- *Is the microphone live?* `audio.voice`: `capturing` true, `device` non-empty, and after a
  moment of speech `level_db.rms` rises and `voice_active` turns true.
- *Does the loopback meet the latency budget?* Start a loopback (`audio.voice_loopback_start`),
  feed a ramp, then read `audio.voice`: `loopback.max_latency_ms` must stay under 60 ms.
- *Did the game keep up?* `audio.voice` `dropped_frames` above 0 means the game drained the
  capture ring too slowly; drain every frame or raise `buffer_secs`.

# Gameplay: players, possession and save games

The M20 gameplay surface lets an agent see who is playing, switch what a controller drives, and
save or restore the running world. All of it works on the same entity ids `scene.query_entities`
reports.

## Players

`players.list` shows every active player — index, kind (`Local` until v0.4.0 networking), the
controller entity, and what it currently possesses:

```json
→ { "players": [{ "index": 0, "entity": 4294967296, "kind": "Local",
                  "controller": 4294967297, "possessed": 4294967304,
                  "viewport": [0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0], "cameras": [] }],
    "count": 1, "max_local": 4 }
```

`viewport` is the player's split-screen rect (`null` for a player without a local view) and `cameras`
lists the cameras tagged `SplitScreenCamera` for that player, with the viewport each one has now. The
player plugin writes the rect onto those cameras ([display settings](book/agents/display-settings.md), ADR-7880).

`players.get` takes either `index` or `entity` and adds the camera view target and the active
input context of the controller:

```json
{ "index": 0 }
→ { "entity": 4294967296, "index": 0, "kind": "Local", "controller": 4294967297,
    "possessed": 4294967304, "view_target": 4294967304, "context": "Gameplay" }
```

If the app has no `PlayerManager` (no `regia_framework::player::PlayerPlugin`), both calls answer
`F0003` with a hint naming the missing plugin.

## Possession

`scene.possess` makes a `PlayerController` drive an entity — the character the player's input and
camera should follow:

```json
{ "controller": 4294967297, "entity": 4294967304 }
→ { "controller": 4294967297, "before": 4294967304, "after": 4294967304 }
```

Both ids are required. The controller's `view_target` follows the possessed entity. Possessing a
new entity automatically unpossesses the old one; `before` reports the previous pawn.

This is the quickest way to test gameplay scripts on a specific character: spawn or find a
character, possess it, inject input (`play.inject_input`), and assert the results (`play.expect`).

## Save games

`save.save` serializes every entity marked `Saveable` and every resource the game registered as
saveable, then writes the slot atomically (temp file + rename, CRC-32 checked):

```json
{ "slot": "Chapter1" }
→ { "slot": "Chapter1", "entity_count": 42, "resource_count": 3, "bytes_written": 12345 }
```

`slot` defaults to `"Auto"`. `save.load` restores a slot into the running world — current
saveable entities are despawned, saved entities spawn back with their reflected component values,
and registered resources are replaced. The game's migration hooks run automatically when the file
is older than the current format. `save.load` needs `slot` (no default) and also reports which copy it
read (`"current"` or `"previous"`):

```json
{ "slot": "Chapter1" }
→ { "slot": "Chapter1", "entity_count": 42, "resource_count": 3, "bytes_written": 12345,
    "copy": "current" }
```

`save.list_slots` lists the slots on disk with their header metadata (versions, timestamp, whether
a screenshot thumbnail is embedded). Slots whose header fails validation (bad magic, CRC
mismatch) are listed with `null` metadata — treat them as damaged — unless their previous good
generation (`<slot>.prev`, ADR-3102) is valid: then the metadata is the previous copy's and
`has_previous` is `true`. `save.load` of such a slot loads the previous copy and reports
`"copy": "previous"` ([Player data](book/user-guide/player-data.md)).

```json
→ { "slots": [{ "name": "Auto", "game_version": "0.1.0", "engine_version": "0.1.0",
                "timestamp": 1760000000.0, "has_thumbnail": false, "has_previous": true }], "count": 1 }
```

Errors: `F0003` when the slot does not exist (`save.load`) or the save subsystem is missing, and
`F0001` when serialization fails (details in `logs.read`, target `regia_framework`).

### What an agent can rely on

- **Components**: every reflected component on a `Saveable` entity is stored by short type name and
  restored by value. A component that is not in the type registry is skipped with no warning. A
  postcard encode that fails logs a warning and is skipped. An entity left with no serialisable
  component is omitted from the file; load despawns every current `Saveable` entity and spawns
  only the file's rows, so that entity is deleted.
- **Resources**: only types the game opted in via `register_saveable_resource` — an agent cannot
  discover them generically; `resources.list` shows which reflected resources exist.
- **Entity ids inside component values** (e.g. a pawn reference) are process-local: do not expect
  them to survive a save/load round trip until stable entity remapping ships.

### Testing a save round trip

```json
save.save   { "slot": "T" }
scene.set_property { "entity": 4294967301, "component": "Health", "path": "hp", "value": 0.0 }
save.load   { "slot": "T" }
play.expect { "assertions": [ { "condition": { "entity": 4294967301, "component": "Health",
              "path": "hp", "op": "eq", "value": 73.5 } } ] }
```

On every platform the engine autosaves to the `"Auto"` slot once when the app enters `Suspended` (the Lifecycle edge, not every frame of the suspension). `Resumed` arms the next edge.

## Driving `samples/third_person` (M20)

The M20 sample exposes its gameplay through the generic surface plus one reflected
component. Every acceptance feature has an `expect`-able anchor:

| Feature | How to drive and assert |
|---|---|
| Move + jump | `play.inject_input` (or set `CharacterInput.move_dir` via `scene.set_property`), then `play.expect` on the character `Transform.translation` having changed / `CharacterState.grounded` flipping to `true` on landing. |
| Boom camera | Query the camera rig entity (`scene.query_entities` for `CameraRig`), read `Camera/Transform` — near a wall the camera sits closer than `boom_length`; `play.expect` `translation` within bounds. |
| Collectibles | The singleton `third_person::SampleState` component holds `collected`/`total`. Walk the character into a coin (inject input towards it), then `play.expect` `collected` to be `>= 1`. |
| HUD counter | The entity named `hud-counter` carries reflected `HudLabel.text`, the same string the HUD draws (`Coins: 1 / 8`). `play.expect` that string. `SampleState.collected` is the counter's source, not the HUD. |
| Pause menu | Trigger the pause key (`play.inject_input`), assert `SampleState.paused` is `true` and `play.step` does not advance the character. The pause-menu node's `NodeStyle` display becomes `Flex` (the style type is not reflected; the headless test reads it directly). |
| Save/load | `save.save { "slot": "Chapter1" }`, collect or wait, `save.load`, assert `SampleState.collected` is the stored value and despawned coins stayed gone. |
| Foot IK | Walk onto the stairs (the fox's length along +X). `fox-rig-0` (player 1: `fox-rig-1`) carries reflected `SolvedFoot.span`: the world-Y gap between solved foot tips that sit within 8 cm of the ground probe. On the flight that span is at least one step (~0.2 m). It stays ~0 if the rig's `FootPlacement` (graph output, which plans with `FootPlanter`) or the graph's `TwoBoneIK` nodes are removed, because the span is read from `JointGlobals`, not from the weight parameter. |
| Split-screen | Join a second player (F2, or a gamepad button through `play.inject_input`), then `players.list` shows two players. Each camera's `Camera.viewport` is half the window; the reflected `third_person::camera::SplitViewport` (`x`, `y`, `w`, `h`) is the `play.expect` anchor because `Camera` itself is not a reflected type. |

The headless equivalents of these checks live in `samples/third_person/tests/gameplay.rs`
— run `cargo test -p third_person` for the same assertions without a window.

## The third-person car and gameplay tags

`samples/third_person` parks a ray-cast car (`regia_physics::vehicle`) at `(-12, 1, -10)`, west of
the start (ADR-2134). A player within 3.5 m of the chassis presses `E` to get in and `E` again to
get out on the driver's side. While a player drives, `W`/`S` are throttle and reverse, `A`/`D`
steer and `Space` brakes; the keys write the car's `VehicleInput` only when they change, so an
agent's `physics.vehicle_input` holds until the player touches them. The player's camera runs the
camera-driver asset `vehicle_chase` (`samples/third_person/assets/camera/vehicle.camera.ron`) while
driving; getting out removes the `CameraDriver`, and the on-foot boom rig (`CameraRig`, the
`CameraRuntime.boom` the M20 checks read) takes over again. The car's tuning is the `.vehicle.ron`
`samples/third_person/assets/car.vehicle.ron` (the default car; `docs/formats/vehicle.md`); check an
edit to it with `physics.vehicle_config_check` before running the game.

| What | How to drive and assert |
|---|---|
| Find the car | `scene.query_entities { "component": "Car" }` (marker on the chassis). |
| Get in / out | `play.inject_input` key `KeyE` (pressed, then released) next to the car. The character gets the reflected `Driving { car, keys }` component; `scene.get_entity` with `components: ["Driving"]` reads `car`. |
| Drive | `physics.vehicle_input { entity, throttle, steer, brake }`, `play.step`, then `physics.vehicles { entity }` (`forward_speed`, `grounded_wheels`). See [Vehicles](book/agents/vehicles.md). |
| Chase camera | `camera.inspect { entity }` on the `PlayerCamera` entity names the `vehicle_chase` asset and its `chase` rig while driving; `camera.validate` checks the asset. See [Camera framework](book/agents/camera-framework.md). |
| Tags | The project tag table (`samples/third_person/assets/game.tags.ron`) declares `Role.Player` (the characters), `Pickup.Coin` (the coins), `Vehicle.Car` (the car) and `State.Driving` (added while a character drives). `tags.list`, `tags.get { entity }`, `tags.query { entity, query: { "Has": "State.Driving" } }`. See [Gameplay tags](book/agents/gameplay-tags.md). |

```json
{ "method": "play.inject_input", "params": { "events": [{ "type": "key", "key": "KeyE", "state": "pressed" }] } }
{ "method": "play.step", "params": { "frames": 2 } }
{ "method": "scene.get_entity", "params": { "entity": 4294967304, "components": ["Driving"] } }
{ "method": "physics.vehicle_input", "params": { "entity": 4294967157, "throttle": 1.0 } }
{ "method": "play.step", "params": { "frames": 120 } }
{ "method": "physics.vehicles", "params": { "entity": 4294967157 } }
```

`samples/third_person/tests/agent_expect.rs` (`agent_drives_the_car_and_reads_the_tags`) runs this
script; `tests/gameplay.rs` (`the_car_is_entered_driven_with_its_chase_camera_and_left`) checks the
same behavior without the protocol. `tests/car_render_agent.rs`
(`an_agent_drives_the_car_and_sees_it_through_the_chase_camera`) runs the sample with the headless
renderer: `play.wait_until` (level presented, character grounded), `play.expect` on `Driving.car`, and
an offscreen `seeing.screenshot` on foot and again through the chase camera after driving off (pixel
checks only, no golden; skipped with a message on a machine without any Vulkan device):

```json
{ "method": "seeing.screenshot", "params": { "target": "offscreen", "width": 320, "height": 180, "hud": false } }
→ { "width": 320, "height": 180, "mime": "image/png", "png_base64": "iVBORw0KGgo..." }
```

Out-of-reach `E` does nothing. A refused car spawn (no physics world) is logged and the level plays
without it. The Fox still plays the locomotion graph, not motion matching: its clips carry no root
motion, so a motion-matching database built from them has all-zero trajectory features.

<!-- source: book/agents/coroutines.md -->
# Coroutines

Gameplay coroutines (`regia_framework::coroutine`) are `async` sequences — cutscenes, tutorials,
spawn waves — polled once per frame. Use `coroutines.list` to see which are running and what each is
waiting for, for example to wait until an intro sequence finishes before taking a screenshot.

```json
{}
→ { "count": 2, "running": 2, "coroutines": [
      { "id": 0, "generation": 0, "label": "intro", "owner": 4294967301, "started_frame": 12,
        "waiting": "seconds", "seconds_left": 1.25, "frames_left": null, "finished": false },
      { "id": 1, "generation": 3, "label": "", "owner": null, "started_frame": 40,
        "waiting": "condition", "seconds_left": null, "frames_left": null, "finished": false } ] }
```

- `waiting` is `seconds` (game time; frozen while paused), `frames`, `condition` (a `wait_until`
  predicate), `world` (a `with_world` closure) or `nothing`.
- `owner`: the coroutine is canceled on the first frame that entity no longer exists. Despawning it
  with `scene.despawn` is how to stop an owned sequence from the protocol.
- `finished`: done, holding a result the game has not taken yet.
- Coroutines are polled in start order, after timers and before scripts. `F0003` (numeric `-32001`) means
  the app has no `CoroutinePlugin`.

Coroutines are **not saved** by save games and do not survive a game-library hot reload: after
`save.load` the game restarts any sequence from saved state.

Recipe — wait for a sequence: `play.wait_until` with a condition the sequence sets (a resource field
or component), or poll `coroutines.list` until the labeled coroutine is gone.

`coroutines.list` takes no parameters. It returns `F0003` (numeric `-32001`) when the app has no
`Coroutines` resource; add `CoroutinePlugin` to make the method available. Workflow: start the named
coroutine in gameplay code, call `coroutines.list`, then wait on its observable completion condition
with `play.wait_until` (or poll the list) before capturing the result.

Captured failing call (lavapipe; this editor has no coroutine plugin):

```console
$ regia agent call coroutines.list '{}' --project samples/arena
error: method call failed: no Coroutines resource in this app (-32001): {"code":"F0003","hint":"add regia_framework::coroutine::CoroutinePlugin and start coroutines with start_coroutine"}
```

<!-- source: book/agents/replay.md -->
# DO27 replay and Moments

`regia_framework::replay_sim::ReplaySim` plays a Direct Order 27 `.do27replay` (version 2, 3 or 4,
`spec/replay/do27-replay-v3.md` in the DO27 repo) for rendering and camera work. It is an
`ExternalSim`, so `SimBridgePlugin::<ReplaySim>` turns a replay into entities, and it is also a plain
resource the protocol drives without a window. These methods work on the world's `ReplaySim`;
`replay.load` creates one (with the opaque codec) when the app has none.

Playback never re-simulates. Between two fulls the entity set is the last full's (unless
`replay.play` blends between ticks, below), and nav beacons
(kind `"beacon"`, ids `2^32 | beacon_id`) come from the last nav record. The snapshot inside a full is
opaque to an outside reader (its layout and state hash belong to the sim build that wrote it), so a game
that links the matching sim installs a `FullCodec` (`ReplaySim::with_codec`) to get its entities and to
recompute the state hashes. Without one the entity list holds only beacons.

## `replay.load`

Params: `path` (required). Reads the file (at most 512 MiB), replaces any loaded replay, rewinds to
tick 0 paused. `path` is confined like `render.out_start`'s `out` (ADR-1769): relative to the project root, or absolute
under the project root, the system temp dir, an `output_roots` or `replay_roots` entry of
`.regia/agent.toml`, or a root the host added with the `regia_agent::ReplayRoots` resource (ADR-1965; the
showcase host's `--replay-root DIR`); `..` and a symlink leading out of them are `F0002` before anything is read,
with `data.allowed_roots` listing those kinds. List a replay store outside the project in `replay_roots`, not
`output_roots` (that one also allows writes). Needs the `assets` permission; `replay.seek` and `replay.step` need `play`;
`moments.list` and `moments.get` are read-only.

```json
{ "method": "replay.load", "params": { "path": "saved/replays/1760000000000-ironreach-tdm.do27replay" } }
```

Returns `path`, `bytes` (the file size), `header` (`version`, `protocol`, `tick_rate`, `lobby_preset`, `seed` as a string, `bootstrap`,
`map`, `mode`, `teams`, `input_delay`, `sim_git_sha`, `sim_abi`, `content_hash`, `config_hash`,
`players[]` with `peer_id`, `account_id`, `callsign`, `role`, `team`, and `peers[]`), `end_tick`,
`duration_secs`, `counts` (`inputs`, `fulls`, `navs`, `salvage`, `command_records`, `moments`,
`moment_ticks`), `abort` (`{tick, reason}` or null), `verify` (`ok`, `fulls`, `hash_checked`,
`hash_unchecked`, `mismatches`, `defects`, `moment_ticks`, `aborted`) and `position`.

`verify` is the audit `ironreach_replay --verify` does, as far as an outside reader can: at least one
full, non-decreasing input ticks, an applied-inputs record on every full's tick, no duplicate `peer_id`
(`defects[]`), and, when the player's codec can recompute a full's state hash, a bit-exact comparison
(`mismatches[]` lists the ticks). **`hash_unchecked` counts fulls nothing could check: skipped, not
passed.** `ok` is true when there is no mismatch and no defect; `aborted` only reports the trailer.

Errors (`INVALID_PARAMS`, `data.code` `F0002`, the message ends in a bracketed code): `truncated`, `bad_magic`, `unsupported_version`,
`bad_string`, `unknown_tag` (the record boundary is not defined), `v2_full` (a version 2 full has no length), `full_without_tick`,
`bad_moment`, `bad_nav`, `too_large`, `io`. A malformed file is always an error, never a crash.

**Version 2 files with fulls.** A version 2 full has no length prefix and no state hash: where it ends is
known only to the sim build that wrote it. An outside rule (looking for the next tag byte, assuming a size)
would split it in the wrong place without noticing, because snapshot bytes can hold any value, and every
later record would then be read as garbage. So the default player refuses such a file with `v2_full`
(ADR-1519). A game that links the writing build can load them: its `FullCodec` implements
`v2_full_len(body)` (how many bytes of `body` are the snapshot), and `replay.load` reads the file with the
codec of the world's `ReplaySim`. Those fulls have no hash, so `verify` counts them in `hash_unchecked`.
Otherwise convert the file to version 3 with DO27's own tools. Version 2 files without fulls load as before.

**Version 4 files.** Load the original file directly (ADR-8191); no v4-to-v3 rewrite is
needed. Extra player/team label strings are validated and discarded. Map-extent (`0x08`,
16-byte body) and training (`0x09`, tick plus length-prefixed body) records are skipped without
changing the last applied-input tick, snapshot hashes, events or duration. Their payload bytes
are never interpreted as record tags. Empty training bodies are safe; truncated bodies return
`truncated`. An unrecognized tag still returns `unknown_tag`: this format has no universal
record length. Versions above 4 return `unsupported_version`. V2/v3 behavior is unchanged.
The header response retains its existing fields and reports `version: 4`.

## `replay.seek`

Params: `tick` or `seconds` (at the header's tick rate). Clamped to `end_tick`. **Fires no events**, forwards or back, so
seeking over a Moment never plays it. Seeking is a pure function of the tick: the same tick gives the same
snapshot whatever came before. Returns `position` (`tick`, `end_tick`, `seconds`, `at_end`) and
`snapshot` (`tick`, `full_tick`, `nav_tick`, `entity_count`, `entities[]` capped at 100 with `id`, `kind`, `team`,
`position`, `rotation` as `[x,y,z,w]`, `truncated`, `decode_error`).
`decode_error` is `null` when the snapshot decoded; a player without a codec for full snapshots (the default
`OpaqueCodec`) reports a message starting with `no_full_codec` and an empty `entities[]`.

```json
{ "method": "replay.seek", "params": { "tick": 4280 } }
{ "method": "replay.seek", "params": { "seconds": 71.5 } }
```

`tick` and `seconds` must be non-negative; `tick` wins when both are given; a tick above `u32::MAX` or a
non-numeric value is `INVALID_PARAMS`.

## `replay.step`

Params: `ticks` (default 1) and `presented` (default false: the exact snapshot; true: the pose a bridge
presents, blended between ticks when `replay.play` turned `interpolate` on). Stops at the end. Returns
`from`, `advanced`, `clamped`, `position`, `snapshot`, `events_total`, `events_truncated` and
`events[]`: Moments (`type: "moment"`), peer commands (`type: "command"`: `peer_id`, `ok`, `kind`,
`text`) and aborts (`type: "abort"`) whose tick was crossed, each exactly once, in tick order.
`ticks` above 36000 is clamped (`clamped: true`; `advanced` is the ticks actually moved). The
response lists at most 1000 events; `events_total` is the count crossed and `events_truncated` is
true when the list is shorter. A later step does not repeat the events this response omitted.
Playing from the
frame clock (`ReplaySim::set_playing`) uses integer arithmetic, so the same frame times always land on the
same ticks at 30 fps or uncapped.

```json
{ "method": "replay.step", "params": { "ticks": 30 } }
{ "method": "replay.step", "params": {} }
```

`ticks: 0` is a valid probe: it advances nothing and reports the position. A negative, fractional or
non-numeric `ticks` is `INVALID_PARAMS`. Stepping past the end answers `advanced: 0` and no events.

## `replay.play`

Params, all optional: `from_tick` (seek there first, firing no events; default the current tick),
`speed` (0.001..=64, default 1 = real time), `interpolate` (default true), `max_gap_ticks` (1..=600,
default 1), `start` (`"now"`, the default, or `"render_out"`). Needs `play`.

Plays the replay on the **simulation clock**: each frame advances it by the frame's simulation delta
(`Time::sim_delta`, which is the frame delta unless a render-out `time_map` sets it apart) times `speed`
(exact integer arithmetic, so the same frame times land on the same ticks). With a
`SimBridgePlugin::<ReplaySim>` the bridge advances it; a player that is only a resource is advanced by the
agent (`driver` says which). Events are delivered as playback crosses their ticks, once each, as with
`replay.step`; playback stops at the end.

- **Slow motion.** With `interpolate` on, the pose a bridge presents between two fulls at most
  `max_gap_ticks` apart moves each entity present in both from the first pose toward the second by the
  playback time's fraction of the gap (linear position, normalized linear rotation on the shorter arc).
  This is presentation only: the tick, the events, the state hashes and every `replay.seek` /
  `replay.step` snapshot stay exact, with blending on or off. `replay.step { ticks: 0, presented: true }`
  returns the presented pose to check it. At a tick that holds a full nothing is blended. With the
  default gap of 1 the blend is between consecutive ticks only (a replay with a full every tick); a larger
  gap blends across sparser fulls, which is a straight line between them. An entity only in the later
  full appears when playback reaches it. Answers show `position.tick_fraction`, and a presented snapshot
  `snapshot.blend` (`{ next_full_tick, alpha }`; `null` in exact snapshots).
- **On a render-out.** Under `render.out_start` with a `time_map` the simulation delta is the job's
  simulation step, so the replay's `speed` composes with the map: a 2x replay under a 0.25 map plays at
  half the video's speed. `start: "render_out"` seeks to `from_tick` and waits there (not playing); the
  next render-out, or the running one if it has not reached frame 0, starts it on its frame 0. Frame 0
  then shows exactly `from_tick`, and frame `i` shows `from_tick + tick_rate · speed · sim_time(i)`
  (`render.out_progress` and the manifest report `replay_from_tick`; the manifest's `frame_times` has
  `sim_time_ns` per frame). `armed_for` says which job (`running_job` or `next_job`; `null` for `start: "now"`).
  After the job the replay keeps playing on the normal clock until `replay.pause`.

Returns `position` (with `tick_fraction`, `playing`, `speed`), `snapshot`, `interpolate`,
`max_gap_ticks`, `start`, `driver` (`sim_bridge` or `agent`) and `armed_for`.

```json
{ "method": "replay.play", "params": { "from_tick": 4280, "speed": 0.25 } }
{ "method": "replay.play", "params": { "from_tick": 4280, "speed": 1, "start": "render_out" } }
```

Recipe: a slow-motion kill cam.

```text
moments.get       { index: 12 }                                    -> seek_tick: 4310
replay.play       { from_tick: 4250, speed: 1, start: "render_out" }
render.out_start  { out: "renders/kill12", frames: 240, fps: 60,
                    time_map: [{frame: 50, scale: 1}, {frame: 80, scale: 0.2},
                               {frame: 200, scale: 0.2}, {frame: 230, scale: 1}] }
render.out_progress { }                                             -> replay_from_tick: 4250
```

## `replay.pause`

No params. Stops frame-clock playback where it is and drops a `start: "render_out"` arm. Returns
`position` and `disarmed` (true when an arm was dropped). Needs `play`.

## `moments.list` and `moments.get`

Moments are the sim's derived combat observations (kind `hit`, `down`, `kill`), in emission order. The
index is the Moment's id. Positions are Regia Engine metres: the replay stores sim metres and DO27's frame is
metres, +Y up, forward −Z, so the conversion (`replay_sim::sim_to_regia`) is the identity on axes.

`moments.list` params, all optional: `kind` (`"hit"`, `"down"`, `"kill"`, or a wire number as a string such as `"7"`), `from_tick`/`to_tick` (the stored tick), `entity` (attacker,
victim or either participant slot), `attacker`, `victim`, `fight`, `round`, `weapon`, `min_importance`,
`limit` (default 50, at most 1000), `offset`. Returns `total`, `matched`, `offset`, `returned`, `moments[]` with
`index`, `tick`, `drained_tick`, `kind`, `kind_wire`, `span` (`match`, `round`, `fight`), `participants`
(`[{role, entity_id}]`), `position`,
`damage`, `weapon`, `attacker`, `victim`, `importance`.

`moments.get { index }` returns one Moment plus `fight_moments` (indexes in the same fight and round) and
`seek_tick`, the Moment's event tick (`drained_tick`). `replay.seek` to that tick does not play it: a seek
sets the cursor on the tick and clears the fresh flag, and the next `replay.step` delivers events in
`(cursor, through]`. Seek strictly before `seek_tick`. A Moment at tick 0 is delivered on the first step
after load, not after a seek.

```json
{ "method": "moments.list", "params": { "kind": "kill", "min_importance": 80, "limit": 20, "offset": 0 } }
{ "method": "moments.get",  "params": { "index": 12 } }
```

`limit` above 1000 is clamped to 1000 and `offset` past the end returns an empty page (`returned: 0`);
`min_importance` above 255 saturates. An unknown `kind`, a non-string `kind` or `weapon`, or a negative,
fractional or non-numeric number is `INVALID_PARAMS`. `moments.get` without `index` is `INVALID_PARAMS`.

Recipe: find the kills, put the camera on one, and check the frame.

```text
replay.load   { path }
moments.list  { kind: "kill", min_importance: 80 }      -> pick index 12
moments.get   { index: 12 }                              -> position, seek_tick: 4310
replay.seek   { tick: 4280 }                             -> snapshot half a second early
camera / seeing.screenshot ...                           -> look at position
replay.step   { ticks: 30 }                              -> the kill's event, once
```

`NOT_FOUND` before a replay is loaded, or for a Moment index past the end.

## Errors at a glance

| Call | Condition | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `replay.load` | no `path`, non-string `path`, malformed or unsupported file, unreadable file | `INVALID_PARAMS` (message ends in `[code]`) |
| `replay.load` | `path` outside the allowed roots, with `..`, or through a symlink leading out | `INVALID_PARAMS` `F0002`, `data.reason` `path_outside_project`, `data.path_reason`, `data.allowed_roots` |
| `replay.load` | a failure leaves the previously loaded replay and its position untouched | n/a |
| `replay.seek`, `replay.step`, `replay.play`, `replay.pause`, `moments.list`, `moments.get` | no replay loaded | `NOT_FOUND` |
| `replay.seek` | neither `tick` nor `seconds`; negative or non-finite values | `INVALID_PARAMS` |
| `replay.step` | `presented` not a boolean | `INVALID_PARAMS` |
| `replay.play` | `speed` outside 0.001..=64 or not a number; `from_tick` negative, fractional or above `u32::MAX`; `interpolate` not a boolean; `max_gap_ticks` outside 1..=600; `start` not `"now"` or `"render_out"` | `INVALID_PARAMS` (nothing changes) |
| `moments.get` | `index` at or past the Moment count | `NOT_FOUND` |

`replay.seek` and `replay.step` are repeatable: seeking to the same tick twice, or loading the same
file twice, gives byte-identical answers. The player crosses the same events in the same order for
any step size. Each `replay.step` response includes at most 1000 of the events that step crossed
and at most 36000 ticks.

## Format compatibility

Files DO27 has already written keep loading. `crates/regia_framework/tests/fixtures/replay/` holds
frozen files written from the byte layout by an encoder that shares no code with the reader
(ADR-1378), and `tests/replay_format_compat.rs` pins every field they parse to:

| Fixture | What it pins |
|---|---|
| `v3_every_record.do27replay` | a version 3 file with every record tag, a non-ASCII callsign, input extremes, an empty full, an unnamed Moment kind (reported as `other`) and a 32-byte weapon stem |
| `v2_no_fulls.do27replay` | a version 2 file: the short header loads with the version 3 fields empty, and `verify` reports `no full record` |
| `v4_future.do27replay` | historical v3 layout stamped v4 remains malformed: `truncated`; a separate v5 mutation pins `unsupported_version` |
| `v3_unknown_tag.do27replay` | a record tag this reader does not know is refused where it starts: `unknown_tag` |
| `v4_extensions.do27replay` | non-empty player/team labels and bounded extension records preserve the known records and playback; misleading tag bytes inside skipped payloads are ignored |

A test checks each file's length and hash, so an edited fixture fails first. A new layout adds a fixture; the old ones keep passing. Any prefix of a fixture loads as a shorter
file or is a structured error, never a crash.

Game-side API (`ReplaySim`, `FullCodec`, `MomentQuery`): [Replay playback](book/user-guide/replay-sim.md).

<!-- source: book/agents/loop.md -->
# Frame loop and quitting

Control how the running app steps frames, and ask it to quit, without touching game code. The loop
settings are one view over the frame cap (`FramePacing`), the fixed-step rate (`FixedTime`) and the
runner's throttling (`regia_app::LoopSettings`).

| Mode | What runs | Input |
|---|---|---|
| `continuous` | One frame per redraw, capped by `max_fps` (the default). | Delivered. |
| `bench` | Frames back to back: no frame cap, no sleeping, no redraw round trip. Use it to measure throughput. | **Ignored** by the window runner (agent `play.inject_input` still works). |
| `lazy` | A frame when input or a window event arrives (or the game calls `LoopControl::request_redraw`), otherwise one every `1 / throttled_fps` s so the protocol stays responsive. | Delivered. |
| `run_frames` | `frames` frames from the moment it is set, then **frozen**: game time pauses and frames run at `throttled_fps`. Any other mode thaws it (a pause the game set itself is kept). | Delivered. |

The headless runner (tests, servers) has no OS events and treats `lazy` like `continuous`.

## Read the loop

`loop.get`:

```json
{}
→ { "mode": "continuous", "frames": null, "frames_in_mode": 0, "frozen": false, "accepts_input": true,
    "max_fps": null, "fixed_hz": 60.0, "max_substeps": 5, "throttled_fps": 10.0 }
```

## Change it

`loop.set` takes any of `mode` (+ `frames` for `run_frames`), `max_fps` (`1..=10000`, `null` =
no agent cap), `fixed_hz` (`1..=1000000000`), `max_substeps` (the catch-up limit, `1..=64`) and
`throttled_fps` (`1..=1000`), and returns `{ before, after }`. Those are the rates the engine
runs (`MIN_PACING_FPS`/`MAX_PACING_FPS`, `MAX_FIXED_HZ`, `MAX_SUBSTEPS_LIMIT`,
`MIN_THROTTLED_FPS`/`MAX_THROTTLED_FPS`). A value outside them is `INVALID_PARAMS` and changes
nothing: `loop.set` does not clamp. A direct `LoopSettings::apply` from Rust still clamps into
the same ranges, so `loop.get` after a protocol call matches the request.

`max_fps: null` clears the cap you set, and the loop then runs uncapped (or at vsync) **unless the render profile
has a frame cap of its own**: the `Deck` preset's 40 fps cap is copied into pacing again on the next frame whenever no
cap is set, so a later `loop.get` reports `max_fps` 40 there (found on the Steam Deck pass, ADR-5565). To measure headroom on
such a profile, set a large cap instead (`{"max_fps": 10000}`); the panel's vsync still limits a window.

```json
{ "mode": "run_frames", "frames": 120 }
→ { "before": { "mode": "continuous", ... }, "after": { "mode": "run_frames", "frames": 120, "frozen": false, ... } }
```

A reproducible still: `loop.set { "mode": "run_frames", "frames": 120 }`, then
`play.wait_until` on `loop.get`'s `frozen`, or wait, then `seeing.screenshot`. A throughput
number: `loop.set { "mode": "bench" }`, `play.get_diagnostics` after a few seconds, then
`loop.set { "mode": "continuous" }`.

## Quit

`quit.request` asks the app to quit the way closing its primary window does, so the game's
`ClosePolicy` decides:

```json
{}
→ { "window": 4294967297, "will_exit": true, "handled_by": "engine" }
```

With `ClosePolicy.exit_on_primary_close` off (a game with a "quit?" dialog) `will_exit` is `false`:
the game receives `WindowCloseRequested` and may cancel. Headless apps without a window exit directly
when the policy allows. The connection closes when the app exits.

`quit.request { "mode": "fast" }` skips the teardown: the windows are hidden at once, and a frame
later a bounded flush runs and the process ends (see [fast quit and single
instance](book/agents/process-guards.md)).

Every quit (this request, a closed window, `AppExit`, `regia::request_clean_exit`) runs the engine's
clean exit: stop the pipeline warm, leave fullscreen, wait for the GPU (at most 1 s), drop the
surfaces, the world and the device, then write the pipeline cache. The connection closes when the
world drops, in the middle of it. To check a quit, read the app's log: one `regia exit: <step> took
<ms> ms` line per step, a warning for any step over its budget, `regia exit: GPU device destroyed;
no wgpu objects left`, and `regia exit: done in <ms> ms` (ADR-188).

## Input timestamps

Every raw input event (`KeyboardInput`, `MouseButtonInput`, `CursorMoved`, `MouseMotion`,
`MouseWheel`, `TouchInput`) carries `timestamp`, when it reached the engine (winit exposes no OS
event time, so this is the receipt time in the event loop). `InputTiming.max_latency()` gives the
oldest input of the frame to frame start, and input recordings store each step's stamps for
analysis; replays are indexed by step and never use them. Game code reads
`regia_platform::InputTiming`; there is no protocol method for it.

<!-- source: book/agents/states.md -->
# Game states: GameFlow, sub-states and computed states

Games built on Regia Engine describe their flow (title screen, loading, play, pause) as **game states**
(`regia_ecs::state`, adopted from `bevy_state`). Every state is reflected, so you can read and
drive any game's flow without knowing its code: `state.list` shows what exists, `state.get` reads
one, `state.set` requests a change, and the `{ "state": … }` predicate waits for it.

## The model in one paragraph

A state type has one current value (`State<S>`). A change is a *request* (`NextState<S>`), applied
once per frame by the `StateTransition` schedule, which runs right after `PreUpdate` (and once
before `Startup`). A transition runs `OnExit(old)`, then `OnTransition { old → new }`, then
`OnEnter(new)`, and despawns entities tagged `DespawnOnExit(old)`. **Sub-states** exist only while
their source state has a given value (a pause-menu page exists only while paused) and start at
their default each time. **Computed states** are derived from other states (`InGame` = playing or
paused) and cannot be set; set their source instead.

## GameFlow

`regia_framework::flow::GameFlowPlugin` gives a game the standard flow:

```
Boot → MainMenu → Loading → Playing ⇄ Paused
```

| State | Kind | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `GameFlow` | settable | `Boot` (one frame), `MainMenu`, `Loading` (until `LoadingTasks` is empty), `Playing`, `Paused` (freezes `Time`) |
| `InGame` | computed from `GameFlow` | exists while `Playing` or `Paused`; level content uses `DespawnOnExit(InGame)` |
| `PausePage` | sub-state of `GameFlow::Paused` | `Main`, `Options` |

`GameFlowSettings { skip_main_menu, pause_time }` controls the automatic steps. The
`third_person` sample uses it with `skip_main_menu` (Boot → Loading → Playing in three frames) and
keeps it in step with its Esc pause menu.

## state.list

```json
state.list {}
→ { "count": 3, "states": [
    { "state": "regia_framework::flow::GameFlow", "name": "GameFlow", "exists": true,
      "current": "Playing", "settable": true, "pending": "Unchanged",
      "variants": ["Boot", "MainMenu", "Loading", "Playing", "Paused"] },
    { "state": "regia_framework::flow::InGame", "name": "InGame", "exists": true,
      "current": null, "settable": false, "pending": null, "variants": [] },
    { "state": "regia_framework::flow::PausePage", "name": "PausePage", "exists": false,
      "current": null, "settable": true, "pending": "Unchanged", "variants": ["Main", "Options"] } ] }
```

`exists` tells absent apart from a unit value (`InGame` is a unit struct, so its `current` is
`null` even while it exists). `pending` is the queued request: `"Unchanged"`,
`{ "Pending": v }` (forced) or `{ "PendingIfDifferent": v }`.

## state.get

```json
state.get { "state": "GameFlow" }
→ { "state": "regia_framework::flow::GameFlow", "name": "GameFlow", "exists": true,
    "current": "Playing", "settable": true, "pending": "Unchanged", "variants": [ … ] }
```

`state` accepts the short name or the full type path; an ambiguous short name answers with the
candidates (`F0002`). An unknown state type is `F0003`.

## state.set

```json
state.set { "state": "GameFlow", "value": "Paused" }
→ { "state": "regia_framework::flow::GameFlow", "before": "Playing", "requested": "Paused",
    "force": false, "applies": "on the next StateTransition (after the next PreUpdate); …" }
```

Needs the `play` permission. The change is applied on the **next frame**, not during the call:
follow it with `play.wait_until { "condition": { "state": "GameFlow", "value": "Paused" } }` (or,
with the app held by `play.pause`, advance one frame with `play.step`). Setting the current value does nothing unless
`"force": true`, which re-runs `OnExit`/`OnEnter`. A value that is not a variant fails with the
variant list; a computed state fails (set its source); both are `F0002`; a sub-state that does not exist right now
answers with a `warning`; the pending value is consumed by the next `StateTransition` and is
applied only if the source state at that transition makes the sub-state exist, otherwise it is dropped.

## Waiting on a state

```json
play.wait_until { "condition": { "state": "GameFlow", "op": "eq", "value": "Playing" }, "timeout_ms": 5000 }
play.expect { "assertions": [ { "name": "pause page", "condition": { "state": "PausePage", "value": "Main" } } ] }
```

The state atom compares the current value (`null` while the state does not exist).

## Recipes

- **Skip the menu in a test:** `state.set { "state": "GameFlow", "value": "Loading" }`, then wait
  for `Playing`.
- **Check pause really freezes the game:** set `Paused`, wait for it, read a moving entity's
  `Transform` twice; it must not change, and `{ "resource": "Time", "path": "paused", "value": true }`
  holds.

<!-- source: book/agents/arena.md -->
# Arena: driving and verifying the first-person bot arena

`samples/arena` is a first-person arena shooter against script-driven bots (`docs/specs/14` M20).
It covers what `third_person` does not: a `GameRules` match flow (warm-up → round → match over,
score limit + timer, respawn at `PlayerStart`s), `AiController` bots (a state tree with abilities,
a weapon chooser and resupply stations by default, or steering + line-of-sight raycasts; see
[Gameplay systems](#gameplay-systems-state-tree-bots-abilities-choosers-smart-objects-tags-spectator)), hitscan and pooled-projectile weapons, dynamic props with joints and explosion
impulses, VFX/decals/spatial audio, and a gamepad/touch HUD. No networking.

## Run it headless

The arena supports the offscreen capture path (`book/agents/headless-capture.md`): build the
sample with `MinimalPlugins` + `RenderPlugin { headless: true }` + `ArenaSample`, pin the fixed
step, and drive it with the agent protocol.

```
cargo run -p arena -- --exit-after-frames 300
```

Launcher flags (also used by `cargo xtask soak`):

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--seed N` | Match RNG seed (determinism) |
| `--bots N` | Number of AI bots (default 7, plus the local player) |
| `--no-local-player` | Pure bot-vs-bot match (soak hook: `--bots 16 --no-local-player` = 16 simulated players) |
| `--bench` | Budget probe (8 bots, 200 crates, ~20k particles) |
| `--brain state-tree\|steering` | Bot brain without a navmesh (default `state-tree`, ADR-2134) |

## What an agent can see

The arena registers its reflected types, so `scene.query_entities`, `resources.list` and
`play.expect` can inspect the match (`ArenaState` is a component, found with
`scene.query_entities`'s `component` filter):

| Type | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Pawn` | component | `slot` (0 = local player, 1.. = bots) and `is_bot` |
| `Health` | component | `current` / `max` hit points |
| `ArenaState` | component (on the `"match"` entity) | `phase` (`Warmup`/`Round`/`MatchOver`), `scores` by slot, `match_secs` |

The bot brain (`BotBrain`) and pooled projectile (`Projectile`) are also reflected. The match
RNG is seeded from the launcher's `--seed` flag (`arena::MatchRng`), so two runs with the same
seed replay to the same final score.

## Assertions

`play.expect` conditions use the short component names `scene.get_entity` and `resources.list`
report. Health is a component on each pawn; the match state is a singleton `ArenaState` component
on the `"match"` entity (a component, not a resource, so the field atom can read it — the
engine's resource predicate is a closed set of typed handlers). `samples/arena/tests/agent_expect.rs`
executes exactly these assertions:

```json
{ "assertions": [
  { "name": "a bot is alive",
    "condition": { "entity": { "component": "Pawn" }, "component": "Health", "path": "current", "op": "gt", "value": 0.0 } },
  { "name": "the match is in the round",
    "condition": { "entity": { "component": "ArenaState" }, "component": "ArenaState", "path": "phase", "op": "eq", "value": "Round" } },
  { "name": "scores start at zero",
    "condition": { "entity": { "component": "ArenaState" }, "component": "ArenaState", "path": "scores", "op": "eq", "value": [0, 0, 0] } }
] }
```

A good headless smoke: pause, `play.step` 120 frames (two seconds), then assert every pawn is
above the floor and at least one bot has taken damage, and take a `seeing.screenshot` with
`target: "offscreen"` (the frame must not be black and must show bot bodies).

## Determinism

`samples/arena/tests/determinism.rs` records a three-minute bot match with `InputRecording`
(`regia_framework::input_recording`): the RNG seed plus every fixed-step action value.
Playback feeds each step's values through `InputInjection` before that frame's action evaluation
(`PreUpdate`), so a replayed step sees what the recorded step saw (ADR-537). The test asserts the
replayed `Actions` contain the recorded non-zero `Move`, and that `ArenaState.scores` matches.
`tests/repro_check.rs` goes further: 20 seeds of the match (steering and navmesh bots, a local player
on seeded input) are recorded and replayed, and every reflected component must hash the same at each
checkpoint ([Determinism](book/agents/determinism.md)).

## Touch and pause

The HUD draws a virtual stick (`Move`) and a fire button (`Fire`). A bridge copies
`VirtualAxes` / `VirtualButtons` into `InputInjection`. Gamepad Start opens the pause menu
(`Display::Flex`); the Resume button's click sets it back to `Display::None`.

## Weapons

Bots fire a pooled rocket (`PrefabPool` key `rocket`) every fourth shot. An explosion overlap
writes `ExternalImpulse` on dynamic crates. A static wall between two bots blocks the
line-of-sight raycast, so the shot does not land until the wall is gone.

## Budget probe

```
cargo run -p arena -- --bench
```

Prints p50/p95/p99 over 300 frames and the live counts: 8 bots, at least 200 rigid bodies, at
least 20,000 particles (`VfxScene::estimated_live`). Lavapipe timings are not representative.

## Gameplay systems: state-tree bots, abilities, choosers, smart objects, tags, spectator

Without a navmesh the default bot brain is a state tree (`ArenaConfig::brain`,
`BotBrainKind::StateTree`, ADR-2134); `BotBrainKind::Steering` keeps the plain steering loop that
the determinism, replay, budget and evidence tests pin. The data ships in `samples/arena/assets/`
and is embedded in the binary, so the agent methods see it under these paths:

| Data | Path | System |
|---|---|---|
| Bot behavior | `ai/bot.statetree.ron` | `regia_ai` state tree: `Bot` → `Idle` (warm-up and match over), `Fight` (task `arena::brain::Engage`), `Resupply` (task `arena::brain::Restock`); ambient task `arena::brain::Sense`; `state_key: "state"`. See [State trees](book/agents/state-tree.md). |
| Ammunition | `abilities/pawn.attrs.ron` | Attributes `ammo_max` 6, `ammo` 6. |
| Weapons | `abilities/rifle.ability.ron`, `abilities/rocket.ability.ron` | Abilities: rifle costs 1 round and starts a 0.6 s cadence (`Cooldown.Rifle`); rocket costs 4 rounds, cools 2.4 s (`Cooldown.Rocket`), chains the rifle cadence and waits for it. See [Abilities](book/agents/abilities.md). |
| Effects | `effects/*.effect.ron` | Costs, cooldowns and `resupply` (instant refill, cue `Cue.Resupply`). |
| Weapon choice | `choosers/weapon.chooser.ron` | Chooser, mode `First`: `rocket` (ready, 5 to 30 m, 4+ rounds), `rifle` (ready, up to 30 m, 1+ round), catch-all `none`. See [Choosers](book/agents/choosers.md). |
| Tags | `game.tags.ron` | `Team.Bot`, `Team.Player`, weapons, cooldowns, `Effect.Ammo.*`, `Cue.Resupply`. See [Gameplay tags](book/agents/gameplay-tags.md). |
| Station choice | `ai/resupply.spatialquery.ron` | Spatial query `resupply_stations` (entity items, `NearbyEntities(tag: "resupply_slot")`, scored by planar distance to the bot, pick `All`). See [Spatial queries](book/agents/spatial-queries.md). |

A bot fights while it has rounds: `Engage` closes to 6 m, and with a clear line of sight asks the
chooser (inputs `distance`, `ammo`, `rifle_ready`, `rocket_ready`; the readiness comes from the
ability activation check) and starts the picked ability. When `ammo` drops below 1 the tree enters
`Resupply`: `Restock` runs the station query for the bot (nearest slot first, ties to the lower
entity id) and claims the first free slot of role `resupply` in that ranking, on one of the two
yellow stations (smart objects at `(-6, 0, 3)` and `(6, 0, -3)`), walks there, uses it for 0.5 s, applies
the refill and succeeds once the new `ammo` reads back. A respawn also refills. A claim left behind
when the round ends is released by `Sense`. A bot-only match (`--no-local-player`) is watched
through the spectator camera following bot 1; `SpectatorFocus { enabled, slot }` on `main_camera`
switches the view and the followed slot.

| What | How to drive and assert |
|---|---|
| Which brain runs | `ArenaBrainStatus` on the `"match"` entity: `brain` (`state_tree`, `steering`, `navmesh`), `trees`, `stations`, `errors`. A tree that fails to compile falls back to steering and lists the error. |
| A bot's state | `StateTreeStatus.active_path` on the pawn (`["Bot", "Fight"]`), `trace`; `Blackboard` keys `in_round`, `ammo`, `has_target`, `target`, `target_pos`, `target_dist`, `state`. |
| Validate or swap the tree | `statetree.compile { text }`, `statetree.reload { entity, text }`, `statetree.control`, `statetree.debug`. |
| Ammunition and weapons | `abilities.list { entity }` (two grants), `abilities.check { entity, grant }` (`on_cooldown`, `cannot_afford`), `abilities.inspect`, `abilities.set_base { entity, attribute: "ammo", base }`, `abilities.cues` (`Cue.Resupply`). The reflected `Loadout { rifle, rocket }` holds the grant ids. |
| Weapon choice | `chooser.evaluate { path: "choosers/weapon.chooser.ron", context: { distance, ammo, rifle_ready, rocket_ready }, trace: "full" }` answers `row` and why every other row failed. |
| Stations | `smartobject.list` (two slots, role `resupply`, `claimed_by`), `smartobject.search`, `smartobject.set_enabled` (a disabled station sends a restocking bot to the other one). |
| Tags | `tags.get { entity }`, `tags.query { entity, query: { "Has": "Team.Bot" } }`. |
| Station ranking | `ai.query_list` (lists `resupply_stations`), `ai.query_run { template: "resupply_stations", owner, pick: "all" }` (both slots, nearest first, with `score` and the `near` contribution). Only the state-tree brain installs `SpatialQueryPlugin`; in the other modes the methods answer `ai_query_unavailable`. |
| Spectator | `spectator.get`, `spectator.set { mode, target }`, `spectator.step`; `scene.set_property` on `SpectatorFocus.enabled` / `.slot`. |

```json
{ "method": "abilities.set_base", "params": { "entity": 4294967310, "attribute": "ammo", "base": 0.0 } }
{ "method": "play.step", "params": { "frames": 15 } }
{ "method": "scene.get_entity", "params": { "entity": 4294967310, "components": ["StateTreeStatus"] } }
→ { "components": { "StateTreeStatus": { "value": { "active_path": ["Bot", "Resupply"], ... } } } }
```

```json
{ "method": "ai.query_run", "params": { "template": "resupply_stations", "owner": 4294967310, "pick": "all" } }
→ { "status": "success", "item_count": 2, "units": 4,
    "items": [ { "entity": 4294967340, "score": 0.0, "passed": true, "contributions": { "near": 0.0 }, ... },
               { "entity": 4294967339, "score": -1.0, "passed": true, "contributions": { "near": -1.0 }, ... } ],
    "tests": [ { "id": "near", "kind": "Distance", "in": 2, "out": 2 } ] }
```

`samples/arena/tests/wc_systems.rs` holds the headless checks and the agent script
(`an_agent_drives_the_gameplay_systems_of_the_arena`: compile, tags, abilities, chooser, smart
objects, the station query, an emptied magazine restocked at a station, the spectator). `tests/wc_render_agent.rs`
(`an_agent_watches_the_state_tree_match_through_the_spectator_camera`) runs the match with the
headless renderer: `play.wait_until` (a bot in `Fight`), `play.expect` (brain, trees, stations,
`SpectatorFocus`), an offscreen `seeing.screenshot` through the spectator camera, then
`scene.set_property` `SpectatorFocus.slot` to 3 and a second shot that must differ (pixel checks only,
no golden). `tests/repro_check.rs` records
and replays 20 seeds of the state-tree match (`arena_state_tree`) next to the steering and navmesh
scenes. The `agent` feature (default) installs the `abilities.*` and `chooser.*` methods; without it
they are absent.

## Evidence

`docs/evidence/m20/arena/arena_first_person.png` is the pawn's eye view.
`arena_overhead.png` looks down on the floor, crates and distinctly colored bots. Both
composite the HUD. `cargo test -p arena --test offscreen` regenerates them on lavapipe.

# Safety: permissions, read-only mode, audit and provenance

The owner stays in control (specs/23 § 5). The project gates the protocol with
`<project>/.regia/agent.toml`; every call lands in an audit log; every authored change is stamped
with provenance and listed for review.

## Permission profiles

```toml
# .regia/agent.toml
read_only = false                     # true: every mutating call is denied (F0012)
permissions = ["read", "edit_scene", "assets", "play"]
rate_limit_per_second = 50            # mutating calls (1..=10000)
heavy_rate_limit_per_second = 60      # cost "heavy" calls, read-only ones too (1..=10000)
output_roots = ["/srv/capture"]       # extra directories render.out_start may write under
replay_roots = ["/srv/replay-store"]  # extra directories replay.load may read from (never written)
```

- `read` — every query method (always allowed).
- `edit_scene` — scene edits and live settings writes.
- `assets` — loading and reloading assets.
- `play` — pause/step/resume, time scale, input injection.

Default (no file): the full working set above. A file that exists but does not parse or cannot be read fails closed (logged as an error, never fatal): `read_only` with the `read` permission only. A denied call
answers `PERMISSION_DENIED` with `error.data.code = "F0012"` and a hint that names the permission.
`output_roots` lists absolute directories that `render.out_start` may write under, in addition to the project root, the
system temp dir (see [Render-out](book/agents/render-out.md)). The same roots bound the files `demo.inspect`,
`demo.seek_plan` and `replay.load` read (ADR-1769). `replay_roots` lists absolute directories `replay.load` may
read from on top of those (ADR-1965): a replay store kept outside the project goes here, not in `output_roots`,
because `output_roots` also says where the engine may write. A host adds replay roots of its own with the
`regia_agent::ReplayRoots` resource (the showcase host's `--replay-root DIR` flag). Unknown keys are ignored for forward compatibility. The editor-side confirmations (`package`,
`delete`, `bless`) arrive with the editor surface.

## Request paths

Since v0.5.1 (ADR-7871), the process's working directory is **not** an additional allowed root.
Starting a game from a home directory therefore does not grant access to that directory when a
project root is supplied. Configure `output_roots` or `replay_roots` explicitly for folders outside
the project and temp roots. With neither an asset-server root nor `AgentSettings::project_dir`,
the working directory still serves as the project root itself. Every agent method resolves a
project-relative path against that one root, in that order (ADR-8798: `ai.bt_edit`, `ai.statetree_edit`,
`anim.montage_edit`, `anim.montage_slot_edit`, `audio.loopgen_render`, `level.export_bake` and the project reads of
`logic.*`, `statetree.*`, `vfx` systems and `fuzz.run` used to fall back to the working directory when only
`project_dir` was set). A write path whose deepest existing part cannot be resolved (the project root itself, or
a dangling symlink) is refused, not let through. The temporary file of every atomic write beside a project file
(`x.bt.ron.new`, `.x.<pid>.tmp` and the like) is created fresh: a file or symbolic link already at that predictable
name is removed (a link itself, never its target) and the temp is opened with exclusive create, so a link planted
there in a cloned project never receives the bytes (ADR-10066; `audio.loopgen_render` did this since ADR-3206).

File paths in requests are confined (ADR-1816). No method, under any rule, reaches a path under a directory named
`goldens` (`golden_path_denied`, [Golden images](book/agents/goldens.md)). Two rules, named in each method's page:

- **Project-relative** (levels for `level.storage`/`level.convert`, `functest` levels and scripts, prefabs and
  materials under `assets/`, `editor.create_asset`, the import folder, procedural graphs, `configurator.contract_check`
  `package_dir`): no absolute path, no
  drive or UNC prefix (`C:x`, `\\server\share`), no `:`, no `..` (nor a segment of only dots and spaces, such as
  `.. ` or `...`), no NUL, no device name (`CON`, `NUL`, `COM1`, ...), and the file (or its deepest existing parent) may not
  lead out of the project through a symlink.
- **Allowed roots** (the `render.out_start` rule): a relative path joins the project root and keeps the lexical rules
  above (no drive or UNC prefix, no `:`, no `..`, no NUL, no device name); an absolute one must lie under the project
  root, the system temp dir or an `output_roots` entry, with no `..` and no NUL; the deepest existing
  parent is checked with symlinks resolved. Used by `render.out_start` `out`, `render.out_job`'s paths, `abilities.validate`,
  `abilities.add_attributes`, `content.set_source`, every `out_dir`, `editor.save_level`, `editor.set_reference`,
  `editor.view_asset`, `editor.thumbnails`, `editor.spawn_gltf_hierarchy`, `editor.collision_layer`,
  `editor.play_sound`, `editor.model_report`, `editor.model_extensions`, `editor.theme_panel_open`/`_save`, the animation editor's paths,
  `editor.bake_set`/`bake_gi` `out`, `editor.procgen_capture` `out`, and `photo.capture` `directory` (also under the
  session pictures folder; ADR-8795). `demo.inspect`, `demo.seek_plan` and
  `replay.load` read under the same roots; `replay.load` also under `replay_roots` and the host's `ReplayRoots`.
- **Documents** (ADR-7388): the project-relative rule for a relative path; an absolute one must lie under the project
  root or the system temp dir (not `output_roots`, which widen outputs only); the deepest existing
  parent is checked with symlinks resolved, and a network or device form outside both is refused before the filesystem
  is touched. Used by every path an editor tool opens, reads or saves: `editor.save_level` `path`,
  `editor.set_reference` `path`, `editor.ui_designer_open`/`_save`, `editor.ui_anim_open`/`_save`,
  `editor.conversation_open` (`path`, `project`)/`_save`, `editor.mode2d_set` `map`/`rules`, `editor.tilemap_save`,
  `editor.bt_*`, `editor.statetree_*`, `editor.matgraph_*` (and an instance's `parent`), `editor.theme_panel_open`/`_save`,
  the animation editor's paths, the mesh-source paths, `editor.lightmap_*` `source`, and the read-only inspectors
  `editor.usd_inspect`, `ply_inspect`, `stl_inspect`, `psd_inspect`, `fbx_inspect`, `obj_inspect`, `bvh_inspect` and
  `svg_report`, and `net.sim_clients` `recording`. Saves also check the document's suffix (`.ui.ron`, `.uianim.ron`, `.conv.ron`, `.tilemap.ron`, ...). A
  refusal lists `allowed_roots: ["project", "temp_dir"]`. Paths a level or UI document holds (a `TileMap` map, a UI
  component's `use`) follow the project-relative rule.

A refused path answers `F0002` with `data.reason = "path_outside_project"` and `data.path_reason` naming the rule:
`path_absolute`, `path_prefix`, `path_parent`, `path_nul`, `path_device`, `path_trailing` (a segment ends in a dot
or a space, which Windows can drop when it opens the file), `path_remote` (a network or device form outside every root, refused before the
filesystem is touched), `path_empty`, `path_escapes` (outside every root, or through a symlink) or `path_io` (the root
cannot be resolved). An allowed-roots refusal also lists
the kinds of root the parameter may lie under in `data.allowed_roots` (`project`, `temp_dir`,
`output_roots`, and `replay_roots` for `replay.load`); it never names a host path. Methods with their own reason code
keep it (`procgen_bad_path`). `editor.import` `sources`, `editor.new_project` and `editor.open_project` take paths
from anywhere by design, and so does `editor.open_kit` (inspect a Tincal kit folder before
importing it; the kit reader confines its reads to the folder; `editor.fbx_inspect`/`obj_inspect` did too before
ADR-7388: a `Read` method no longer reaches outside the project and the temp dir, so import a model or copy it there first), `editor.bake_gi` `scene` (a
flag-like `-...` is refused), and `configurator.open_product` `root` (a content directory, never a network or device form; every path below it is checked lexically, see
[the configurator page](book/agents/configurator.md)). `replay.load` and `demo.*` are not among them: since ADR-1769 (v0.2.8) they read only
under the allowed roots above (before, they took a path from anywhere).

## Audit log

Every call — success, error or deferred — appends one JSON line to
`<project>/.regia/agent/audit.jsonl`:

```json
{ "seq": 1, "frame": 621, "unix_ms": 1730000000621, "method": "scene.spawn",
  "params_hash": "9e107d9d372bb682", "outcome": "ok", "error_code": null,
  "duration_us": 412, "client": "claude" }
```

The params hash is FNV-1a over the params (compact — params can be huge). Where the log lives is in
`project.info` → `audit_log`. `outcome` is `ok`, `error`, `deferred`, `expired` (the caller already got `F0006`,
so the call was not run) or `board` (a `render.out_progress` the connection answered from the render-out
progress board while the app thread was inside a render-out step, so the app did not run it; ADR-2582).

The log is owner-only on Unix and on Windows (an owner-only DACL; a log an earlier version left readable by other
accounts is rewritten owner-only on open, ADR-5489), and at 64 MiB it moves to `audit.1.jsonl` and starts over; one previous file is kept. A
project is often a cloned repository, so a symbolic link planted at `audit.jsonl` is replaced, never appended through,
and a linked agent folder turns the log off (also at rotation: if the new log cannot be opened after the move, the log
stops rather than growing `audit.1.jsonl`). The token and `endpoint.json` get the same care: a linked agent folder is
refused, and a client reads the token only from a small regular file of token characters.

## Provenance of agent-made changes

Every successful authored edit (scene edits, settings writes) is stamped and readable through
`agent.changes` — oldest first, one page at a time. `since` is exclusive (records with a greater `seq`);
`limit` caps the page (default 200; `0` counts as 1 and anything over 1000 as 1000, ADR-7454). `next` is the
`since` of the following page: the last returned `seq`, or the newest `seq` in the log when the page is empty.
Walk the whole log with `since: 0`, then `since: next`, until a page comes back empty:

```json
agent.changes {}
→ { "records": [{ "seq": 1, "frame": 700, "utc_unix_ms": 1730000000700,
    "method": "scene.set_property", "target": "entity 17 Transform.translation.y",
    "summary": { "before": 0.0, "after": 2.0, "applied": true },
    "tool": "agent", "client": "claude", "model": "sonnet", "session": "pid-4242",
    "reviewer": "pending" }], "next": 1 }
```

The log keeps the newest 10,000 records (`seq` keeps increasing). `dry_run` previews and failed calls are not changes and are not stamped. The dispatcher skips that stamp for an `edit_scene` call with `dry_run: true`. A method in another permission class does not preview unless its own handler reads `dry_run`; `nav.add_obstacle` inserts the box either way. Asset-file provenance
(`.meta` records, staged review, owner confirmation before shipping) is the editor surface's half of
this rule.

## Trust model

The token is the outer gate, and `build`/`play` amount to code execution (specs/23 § 5): grant them
only to agents you would trust with a shell on the machine, or run the app in a container. Mutating
calls are rate-limited per second (`F0007`).
