# Theme panel (editor)

The editor's **Theme** tab edits a runtime UI `.theme.ron` (the files described in [UI themes](book/agents/ui-theme.md)). It
holds a *draft*: a working copy of one theme that you change token by token, lint, and save. It never touches the
running game's theme; the file you save is what a game loads (`[ui] theme = "my-game"`).

The editor window itself stays on the [editor theme](book/agents/theme.md) tokens. This panel is for the theme your game ships.

## What the panel shows

- **Open / New child.** Open a built-in or loaded theme, or start an empty child of one (the re-skin workflow: the
  child inherits every token and you set only what differs).
- **Token rows**, grouped by section (Color, Spacing, Shape, Type, Motion, Size, Other). Colors have a color picker,
  numbers a drag value, other tokens a text box. A row you have set shows a `reset` button; an inherited row says so
  on hover. Changing `color.accent` restyles every derived token (hover, pressed, selection) because those are
  expressions of it.
- **Density** (comfortable or compact): which size tokens the rows and the lint resolve for.
- **Swatches**: the main color roles drawn as foreground on background, so a change is visible at once. This is not
  the full widget sheet, and the panel does not embed it: render the sheet with `ui.theme_preview` ([UI
  themes](book/agents/ui-theme.md)), passing the same token edits as `tokens` overrides.
- **Lint**: contrast pairs against WCAG 2.x, touch target size, unknown token keys, resolve errors.
- **Save**: writes the draft through a temp file and a rename. Built-in names (`regia-dark`, `regia-light`,
  `regia-high-contrast`, `regia-light-high-contrast`) are refused; copy a built-in by renaming the draft first.

An edit is checked against the whole `extends` chain before it is accepted. A value that does not parse, a missing
reference, or a type mismatch (a duration where a color is expected) is rejected and the draft stays as it was.

## Methods

Mutations need `edit_scene`; opening a file and saving need `assets`. Relative paths are relative to the project
root; `..` is refused.

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `editor.theme_panel_state { filter?, group?, limit? }` | Draft name, `extends`, density, `dirty`, `revision`, the openable `themes`, and token rows `{ key, group, kind, value, raw, inherited }`. `value` is resolved (colors `#rrggbb`, or `#rrggbbaa` when the color is not opaque, durations in ms); `raw` is the draft's own expression, `null` when inherited. `limit` defaults to 200; `truncated` says more exist. |
| `editor.theme_panel_open { theme? \| path? \| new?, density? }` | Make a loaded theme, a `.theme.ron` file or `new: { name, extends }` the draft. Give exactly one of the three. |
| `editor.theme_panel_set { tokens?, rename?, density? }` | `tokens` is `{ key: value }` with a number or an expression string (`"#e8793a"`, `"80ms"`, `"@color.accent"`, `"lighten(@color.accent, 0.06)"`); `null` resets a key. `tokens` and `rename` are restored together when either fails (the draft text and `revision` go back). `density` is applied first and is not restored, including when no draft is open (`theme_panel_no_draft`). Returns `changed` and lint `warnings`. |
| `editor.theme_panel_lint {}` | `{ clean, findings: [{ code, severity, key, message }] }`. Codes: `contrast`, `touch_target`, `unknown_key`, `resolve_error`. |
| `editor.theme_panel_save { path? }` | Writes the draft. Without `path`, saves back to the file it was opened from. |

`revision` increases on every accepted change; a client can poll `editor.theme_panel_state` until it passes the value
it saw before.

## Errors

Error `data.code` values are lowercase and stable:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `theme_panel_no_draft` | No theme is open; call `editor.theme_panel_open`. |
| `theme_panel_unknown_theme` | No loaded theme has that name (`themes` in the state lists them). |
| `theme_panel_invalid_token` | A token value failed to parse or resolve; the message carries the key path. Nothing changed. |
| `theme_panel_unknown_token` | `null` reset of a key the draft does not set. |
| `theme_panel_invalid_name` / `theme_panel_name_taken` | A new or renamed theme name is not letters, digits, `-`, `_`, or already exists. |
| `theme_panel_builtin_name` | The draft still has a built-in name; rename it before saving. |
| `theme_panel_parse_error` | A file failed to load, or the text to save did not parse back. |
| `theme_panel_io_error` | A file could not be read or written. |
| `theme_panel_no_path` | `editor.theme_panel_save` without `path` and the draft has no file yet. |

## Example

```json
{ "method": "editor.theme_panel_open", "params": { "new": { "name": "my-game", "extends": "regia-dark" } } }
{ "method": "editor.theme_panel_set", "params": { "tokens": { "color.accent": "#e8793a", "color.on-accent": "#140a04", "radius.md": 3 } } }
{ "method": "editor.theme_panel_lint", "params": {} }
{ "method": "editor.theme_panel_save", "params": { "path": "assets/ui/themes/my-game.theme.ron" } }
```

Check it worked: `editor.theme_panel_state { "filter": "color.accent" }` shows the new value with `inherited: false`
and `dirty: true`; after the save, `dirty` is `false` and the file loads again with `editor.theme_panel_open { path }`.

## Types, states and variations (v0.6 UI parity)

The **Widget styles** tree selects a type or variation, then a state. Its typed property rows show inherited
expressions and highlight local overrides. Numbers can be typed or adjusted; colors have both an expression
field and a picker; lists use JSON arrays. **Reset override** removes just the draft's key. **New variation**
takes a dotted name such as `Button.alert` and an existing base such as `Button` or `Button.primary`. The
root-first variation chain is shown below the selection. **Pin style** remembers a type/state; **Apply to all
states** copies that effective property box to each supported state in one undo step.

`editor.theme_panel_set` additionally accepts `types` and `variations`, using the runtime theme patch shape:

```json
{ "variations": { "Button.danger": { "extends": "Button", "props": { "background": "#ca1234" } } } }
{ "types": { "Button": { "hover": { "radius": 12 }, "sizes": { "sm": { "height": 30 } } } } }
{ "types": { "Button": { "hover": { "radius": null } } } }
```

Definitions merge per key. `null` removes a draft definition or property, exposing inheritance again. Supported
layers are `props` (normal), `hover`, `pressed`, `focused`, `disabled`, `selected` (checked), `error`, and
`sizes.<name>`. `extends` is a type/variation name or `null` to use the implicit base. Cycles and invalid references
reject the whole operation. Existing inherited variations retain their other inherited properties when edited.

Additional `editor.theme_panel_set` parameters:

| Parameter | Contract |
|---|---|
| `selection` | `{ "type": "Button.danger", "state": "pressed" }`; view selection only. State aliases: normal/props, hovered/hover, checked/selected, plus the other layers above. |
| `apply_all_states` | A `{ type, state }` selection; copy its effective property box to every supported state, one undo entry. Must be the only parameter. |
| `history` | `"undo"` or `"redo"`, restoring a whole draft operation. Must be the only parameter. Opening another theme clears this history. Saving does not clear it. |
| `preview_page` | Built-in gallery kind or a loaded document page name. Must be the only parameter. |
| `preview_document` | Project-relative or permitted absolute `.ui.ron` path; add/reload and select that preview page. Must be the only parameter. |

A successful call with tokens, types, variations and/or rename creates one undo entry and one draft revision.
A rejected call preserves draft, selection, history and theme collection. Density keeps the older behavior
described above: it applies before validation. View-only operations do not dirty the theme.
`editor.theme_panel_state` additionally returns merged `types`, `variations`, current `selection`, root-first
`chain`, effective `properties`, `gallery` page names and `preview` (current `page`, `pages`, `error`, and the
last rendered `picks` with accessible labels, type/state selections and pixel rectangles).

## Live gallery

Expand **Live widget gallery** to preview runtime widgets in normal, hovered, pressed, focused, disabled,
checked and error states. Choose a widget page or add a user `.ui.ron` document. The runtime UI renderer uses
the unsaved draft and selected density. The selected variation is applied to compatible built-in samples.
Hovering or pressing a sample updates its runtime state styling. Clicking selects the sample's runtime class
and state in the style editor. The focusable sample list supplies the same selection with Up/Down and
Enter/Space. Text fields, property actions and import controls also work from the keyboard and use the editor's
UI scale and theme colors.

The gallery demonstrates styling; it does not execute a user's game bindings. It requires an available render
device (lavapipe is supported). The existing token swatches still work without a GPU. `focus_visible` is not a
separate layer at this base; the focused sample shows the runtime navigation focus ring. Gallery view state
and added documents are not written into `.theme.ron`.

## Selective import

`editor.theme_panel_import { from, items, with_values? }` needs `assets`. `from` is a loaded or built-in theme name,
a theme file path, or `"editor"`. File paths obey the same project/temp confinement as other theme file methods.
`items` is a nonempty array of `{ type, state?, kind? }` selectors. Omitted state selects all states and size
layers. `kind` defaults to `all`; other kinds are `colors`, `sizes`, `fonts`, `borders`, `paddings` and `other`.

```json
{ "method": "editor.theme_panel_import", "params": {
  "from": "regia-light",
  "items": [{ "type": "Button", "state": "normal", "kind": "colors" }]
} }
```

This copies exactly `types.Button.props.background`, `types.Button.props.border_color` and
`types.Button.props.text_color`. It copies no tokens, sizes, sibling types or other states. The response includes
sorted `copied` paths. Expressions resolve against the source before copying, so missing source-only token
names cannot leak into the destination. A compound `border` or `focus_ring` is a whole `borders` item, never a
partial colors import; padding fields are `paddings`; font family/text role/size properties are `fonts`.

Use `type: "tokens"` for global tokens, filtered by kind (colors, sizes, fonts/text, other); use `type: "fonts"`
for font family definitions. Neither accepts a state. `with_values` defaults to true. False creates selected
keys with their current destination values, falling back to the built-in default; if neither exists the whole
import is rejected. Imports copy property keys, not variation ancestry; an existing destination variation
keeps its base, and a new one uses its implicit base. Every successful import is one undo step. Failed selectors,
invalid sources or missing references leave the entire draft and its history unchanged.

The editor source maps the documented UI-role bridge's ten unambiguous color roles and Button normal/hover/
pressed colors into a sparse runtime theme. Unmapped keys are absent; requesting only unmapped items fails
without editing the draft. It does not import editor-only gizmo colors, font files or chrome layout. In the panel, choose a source, type (blank uses the selection), state (`all` selects all),
kind, and **Copy values**, then **Import items**.

Additional stable error codes (prefixed with `theme_panel_` in protocol replies):

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `theme_panel_invalid_state` | The selected state is not supported by the current theme format. |
| `theme_panel_unknown_type` | The selected or imported type/variation does not exist. |
| `theme_panel_invalid_import` | Invalid selector kind, no matches, invalid source, or a names-only item has no destination/default value. |
| `theme_panel_empty_history` | There is no undo/redo entry. |
| `theme_panel_unknown_page` | The requested gallery/document page is not loaded. |
| `theme_panel_preview_failed` | Runtime preview creation, layout or readback failed. |

Malformed JSON parameter shapes use the standard JSON-RPC invalid-parameters response (`F0002`). File read/parse failures use the existing
`theme_panel_io_error` / `theme_panel_parse_error` codes. No format migration is needed.

For a headless acceptance screenshot, call `editor.theme_panel_state { "preview": true }`. The response's
`preview` includes `width`, `height`, `mime: "image/png"`, `png_base64` and fresh `picks` from the exact same
runtime render path as the panel. This read does not edit the draft or its revision. Without `preview` (or false),
state reads do not create a GPU device.

**Add type** creates an empty widget type or part (for example `Slider.thumb`), equivalent to
`editor.theme_panel_set { "types": { "Slider.thumb": { "props": {} } } }`. Adding a type describes a style;
it does not register a new runtime widget implementation.

The import host-extension contract is synchronous: success commits one draft/history operation and returns
the exact sorted copied paths; rejection commits nothing. It uses the dispatcher’s default rate class and
host-extension parameter caps (65,536 array items and 1 MiB per string), plus the schema’s `assets` permission.
The runtime contract table intentionally covers built-in methods; editor extensions use these default caps.

<!-- source: book/agents/shot-panel.md -->
# Shots panel (editor)

The editor's **Shots** tab is a small curve editor for the shot sequence that is loaded in the app
([camera paths and shot sequences](book/agents/camera-paths.md)). It edits one scalar track of one shot at a time:
**fov**, **roll**, and, for a shot with depth of field, **focus_distance** and **aperture**. Every edit goes
straight into the loaded sequence (the clock and play state stay), so the camera preview follows.

## In the panel

- Pick the **Shot** and the **Track** from the two drop-downs.
- Drag a key to move it in time and value. Double-click empty space to add a key. Right-click a key for its
  menu: delete it, or set the ease of the segment that starts there (a constant key is `Step`, a linear key
  `Linear`, a cubic key `Smooth`). The grid pans with the secondary button and zooms with the wheel.
- The playhead shows the current time of the shot; scrubbing it moves the sequence clock.
- A refused edit (a time outside the shot, a value outside the track's range, two keys at one time) shows its
  message under the curve and changes nothing.

## The shot list as a document

The loaded list is a document (ADR-8730): the path row at the top of the panel opens a project `.shots.ron`
(**Open**) and saves the list (**Save**, or Ctrl+S / Cmd+S while the pointer is over the panel and no text field has
focus). A `● unsaved` mark shows while the list differs from what its file holds. Every edit counts, whether it
came from this panel, the Sequence Curves timeline's cut row (Add cut, move, trim, delete, fades: it edits this list
when the sequence player has no shot list of its own), undo or redo, or an agent call; undoing back to the saved list
is clean again. A list loaded without a file (`render.sequence`, the timeline's first Add cut) is unsaved and has no
path until a save gives it one. Saving an unchanged list again writes the same bytes. Opening is refused while the
loaded list has unsaved edits (pass `discard: true` to drop them). After an Open, undoing a cut edit made on the
previous list does nothing to the new one. Content Browser **New ▸ Shot list** makes a new `.shots.ron` (one still
shot, 5 s at 30 fps; see [Editor creators](book/agents/editor-creators.md)).

A dirty list with a file autosaves with the editor's documents (kind `shots`,
[editor autosave](book/agents/editor-autosave.md)): the autosave holds the text a save writes (the current format version,
whatever number the list carries in memory), and Restore loads it back at its path, unsaved until you save it.

**Closing the editor.** The close prompt lists a dirty shot list. **Save and exit** writes a list that has a file. A
list with no file (detached, or adopted and never saved) is listed as "an untitled shot list (not saved by Save and
exit: save it from the Shots panel first)": Save and exit goes ahead without it, as Discard would, so Cancel and
Save with a path if you want to keep it.

**Another list in its place (ADR-8940).** When something other than the panel loads a list into the shot player
(`render.sequence { action: "load" }`, `camera.set_path` on an empty player, a host calling `load` or `clear`), the
document is detached from its file: the path is cleared, the path row stops naming the old file, the new list shows
`● unsaved`, and undoing a cut edit made on the old list does nothing to the new one. **Save** then needs a path:
without one it answers `shot_panel_detached`, so the opened file is never overwritten with the other list. Saving to a
path gives the new list its own file.

**A sequence player's own shot list (ADR-8940).** A list the host set on a sequence player
(`SequencePlayer::set_shots`) is not loaded in the shot player. **Edit player's shots** (shown when the Sequence
Curves panel's player, or any player, has its own list) takes it into the panel as an unsaved document with no path:
the curve here and the timeline's cut row then both edit the player's list. Save with a path (Save As) writes it as
`.shots.ron` at the current format version, whatever version number the list carries in memory; after that it is a
document like an opened one (a second save writes the same bytes, edits mark it unsaved). If the player is despawned
the panel goes back to the shot player's list. A crash-recovered adopted list (one saved to a file, then edited) is
restored into the shot player at its file's path, not back into the sequence player: the recovery row keeps the file,
not the host.

**Camera position and rotation keys (ADR-7726).** The Track drop-down also lists **position** (the shot camera's
path keys, `camera.path.keys`) and **rotation** (its orientation keys, `camera.rotation`). With one of them picked
the panel draws the path from above (X to the right, Z down) with its keys, a ring at the playhead's eye and, for
rotation, each rotation key's view direction; below it a key list with each key's time and value (x, y, z metres for
a position; yaw and pitch degrees for a rotation, which is the orientation before the roll track). Dragging a field
moves the key (one undo entry for the whole drag; a typed value is one entry). **Add key at playhead** keys the
preview's own pose at the playhead (so the preview does not jump), and **Delete key** removes the selected key; each
is one undo entry. The path keeps at least one key (`shot_panel_last_key`). Rotation keys are stored as unit
quaternions; a moved rotation key keeps its ease. With no rotation keys the look-at rule orients the camera; the
look-at rule itself (`Heading`, `Point`, `Track`) is edited with `camera.set_path` or in the file. The curve draws
`Smooth` segments as straight lines; the playback still eases them.

## Agent methods

- `editor.shot_panel_state { shot?, track? }` (read-only) selects the shot (by name) and track if given and
  returns `{ loaded, shots, shot, shot_name, duration, track, tracks, range, has_track, selected, keys:
  [{ time, value, ease }], error, path, dirty, host }`. With nothing loaded it returns `loaded: false` (with `path`,
  `host` and `dirty: false`). `path` is the document's project-relative file (`null` before a save, and after another
  list replaced the opened one); `dirty` is true while the list differs from that file. `host` is `"shot_player"`, or
  `{ "player": <entity> }` for an adopted sequence player's own list. It is a read: it reports a pending detach
  (`path: null`, `dirty: true`) without committing it; the next mutating Shots method or panel draw commits it.
- `editor.shot_panel_open { path, discard? }` (needs `edit_scene`) opens a project `.shots.ron` into the shot
  player, stopped at zero, and returns `{ path, shots, dirty }`.
- `editor.shot_panel_save { path? }` (needs `assets`) writes the list atomically to `path`, else to its document's
  file, makes that the document's path and returns `{ path, bytes, dirty }`. The file always carries the current
  format version. A failed save changes nothing and the list stays dirty. A read-only destination file is replaced
  (as level saves do); a folder that cannot be written answers `shot_panel_io`. With no `path` after another list
  replaced the opened one, it answers `shot_panel_detached`.
- `editor.shot_panel_adopt { player?, discard? }` (needs `edit_scene`) takes the sequence player's own shot list as
  the document (unsaved, no path; the panel's **Edit player's shots**) and returns `{ player, shots, path, dirty }`.
  `player` is an entity id (default: the Sequence Curves panel's player when it has a shot list, else the first player
  that has one). Refused while the loaded list has unsaved edits unless `discard: true`.
- `editor.shot_panel_edit { op, shot?, track?, index?, time?, value?, ease? }` (needs `edit_scene`) does one
  edit and returns `{ applied, selected, keys }`:
  - `op: "add"` with `time` and `value` inserts a `Linear` key.
  - `op: "move"` with `index`, `time`, `value` moves a key; its ease travels with it and the keys re-sort.
  - `op: "remove"` with `index`.
  - `op: "ease"` with `index` and `ease` (`Linear`, `Step` or `Smooth`).
  The whole sequence is validated before it is swapped in.
  With `track: "position"` or `"rotation"` the same ops `add`, `move` and `remove` edit the shot camera's path or
  rotation keys, with `value` `[x, y, z]` (metres) or a quaternion `[x, y, z, w]` (stored normalized); each call is
  one undo entry, and the keys come back as `[{ time, value }]` (rotation keys also carry `ease`). The panel's
  buttons and fields run the same code, so the same calls write the same file bytes.

Parameter details: `shot` is an optional string (default: the panel's selected shot); `track` is an
optional string, `fov` by default, with `roll`, `focus_distance`, `aperture`, `position` and `rotation` also
accepted (a state call with `position` or `rotation` returns that track's keys and `range: null`). `op`
is a required string. `index` is a zero-based non-negative integer key index for `move`, `remove` and `ease`;
`time` and `value` are finite numbers required for `add` and `move`; `ease` is `Linear`, `Step` or
`Smooth` for `ease`. Time is limited to `0..=duration`; values are `fov` 1..=170 degrees, `roll`
−3600..=3600 degrees, `focus_distance` 0.001..=1,000,000 meters, or `aperture` 0.1..=128 f-stops.
An absent state `shot` or `track` keeps the current selection.

## Errors

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `shot_panel_no_sequence` | no sequence is loaded (`render.sequence { action: "load" }` or `camera.set_path` first) |
| `shot_panel_bad_shot` | `shot` names no shot |
| `shot_panel_bad_track` | `track` is not `fov`, `roll`, `focus_distance`, `aperture`, `position` or `rotation` |
| `shot_panel_no_dof` | the shot has no depth of field and the track is `focus_distance` or `aperture` |
| `shot_panel_bad_key` | `index` is past the last key |
| `shot_panel_out_of_range` | `time` outside `0..=duration`, or `value` outside the track's `range`, or not finite |
| `shot_panel_key_time_taken` | another key already sits at that time |
| `shot_panel_bad_value` | a rotation value on the position track or a position value on the rotation track |
| `shot_panel_last_key` | removing the position path's only key |
| `shot_panel_invalid` | the edited sequence failed validation (also refuses a save) |
| `shot_panel_unsaved` | `editor.shot_panel_open` or `editor.shot_panel_adopt` while the loaded list has unsaved edits and `discard` is not true |
| `shot_panel_detached` | `editor.shot_panel_save` with no `path` after another list replaced the opened one (give a path) |
| `shot_panel_no_player` | `editor.shot_panel_adopt`: `player` is not a sequence player, or no player has a shot list |
| `shot_panel_bad_path` | the path does not end in `.shots.ron`, is not relative, leads out of the project, or a save has no path |
| `shot_panel_no_project` | no project is open |
| `shot_panel_io` | the file cannot be read (open) or its folder cannot be written (save) |
| `shot_panel_bad_file` | the file is not a valid `.shots.ron` (parse, version or validation error) |
| `F0002` | invalid or missing parameters, including a missing/unknown `op`, a missing field for the chosen op, or a wrong parameter type |

```json
{"method": "editor.shot_panel_state", "params": {"shot": "wide", "track": "fov"}}
{"method": "editor.shot_panel_edit", "params": {"op": "add", "time": 1.5, "value": 35}}
{"method": "editor.shot_panel_edit", "params": {"op": "ease", "index": 1, "ease": "Smooth"}}
{"method": "editor.shot_panel_edit", "params": {"track": "position", "op": "add", "time": 1.0, "value": [1.25, 1.75, 4.5]}}
{"method": "editor.shot_panel_edit", "params": {"track": "rotation", "op": "add", "time": 3.0, "value": [0.0, 0.3, 0.0, 0.954]}}
{"method": "editor.shot_panel_open", "params": {"path": "assets/cine/intro.shots.ron"}}
{"method": "editor.shot_panel_save", "params": {}}
{"method": "editor.shot_panel_adopt", "params": {"player": 4294967301}}
{"method": "editor.shot_panel_save", "params": {"path": "assets/cine/own.shots.ron"}}
```

## Workflow

1. Open a project `.shots.ron` with `editor.shot_panel_open` (or load one with
   `render.sequence {"action":"load", "ron":"..."}`).
2. Read `editor.shot_panel_state` for the selected shot, track, range and existing keys.
3. Call `editor.shot_panel_edit` with one add, move, remove or ease operation.
4. Read state again and capture the updated camera with `seeing.screenshot`.
5. `editor.shot_panel_save` writes it; `editor.shot_panel_state` then reports `dirty: false`.

## Failing call

With no sequence loaded, this captured call returns the handler error and changes nothing:

```text
$ regia agent call editor.shot_panel_edit '{"op":"add","time":0,"value":50}' --project samples/boot_probe
error: method call failed: no shot sequence is loaded (-32001): {"code":"shot_panel_no_sequence","hint":"render.sequence { action: \"load\", ... } or camera.set_path first"}
```

<!-- source: book/agents/viewports.md -->
# Independent viewports

One world can have several viewports open at once: the editor's main viewport, plus any number
of `ViewportInstance`s that a tool draws (a review lightbox, a before/after toggle, a
side-by-side concept compare, a candidates grid). Each instance has its own camera, quality
preset, single/quad layout, show flags and game view. Instances in one *link group* orbit
together.

These methods see and drive the instances. The main viewport keeps its own methods
(`editor.capture_viewport`, `editor.set_viewport`, `editor.focus`; see [Editor surface](book/agents/editor.md)).
The selection, gizmo mode, bookmarks and undo stack belong to the world, so every viewport
shares them.

## Methods

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `editor.viewport_instances {}` | Lists every instance: `id`, `live` (a panel drew it this frame or the last), `camera` (`target`, `distance`, `yaw`, `pitch`, `fov_deg`, `eye`), `quality`, `layout` (`single`/`quad`), `active` pane, `game_view`, `possessed`, `show` flags, `settings` (`grid`, `labels`, `realtime`, `audio`), `link` (group id or null), the `panes` of its last draw (`index`, `kind`, `eye`, `target`, `width`, `height`) and `fps`. |
| `editor.viewport_instance_set { id, create?, target?, distance?, yaw?, pitch?, fov_deg?, quality?, layout?, grid?, labels?, realtime?, audio?, icons?, bounds?, outline?, proxies?, stats?, preview_light?, game_view? }` | Edits one instance. The panel applies the edit on its next draw; captures see it at once. On a linked instance, a camera edit moves the whole group. `create: true` registers an unknown id, seeded from the main viewport, for headless captures. |
| `editor.viewport_link { id, group? }` | Links the instance's camera to group `group`. If another instance already holds that group it joins it and adopts the group's camera; otherwise it starts the group with its own camera. `group: null` (or absent) unlinks; the camera stays where it is. |
| `editor.capture_viewport_instance { id, view?, width?, height?, quality?, game_view?, warm_frames? }` | Renders the instance headless with its own camera, preset and show flags, overlays painted in, and returns `png_base64`, the `eye` and `target` it used, the viewport measurements (`sky_luminance`, `lit_peak`, `shading_range`, `selection_highlight`, `grid_pixels`, `gizmo_axes`), `quality` and `info` (as in `editor.capture_viewport`). `quality` and `game_view` apply to this call only. A linked instance first follows its group. |
| `editor.viewport_instance_remove { id }` | Forgets the instance: its registry entry, link membership and the renderers it owns. A panel that draws it again registers it afresh. |

Errors: an unknown `id` is `not_found` on `editor.viewport_instance_set` (unless `create: true`),
`editor.viewport_link` and `editor.capture_viewport_instance`. `editor.viewport_instance_remove` of an id
that was never registered returns success `{ "id", "removed": false }` and does not change the registry.
An unknown `quality`, `layout` or `view` name is `invalid_params`. `editor.viewport_instance_set`,
`editor.viewport_link` and `editor.viewport_instance_remove` need `edit_scene` and are mutating
(ADR-3285): they change the registry a later `editor.viewport_instances` reads.

## Recipes

**A/B compare at one camera.**

```
editor.viewport_instance_set {"id": 1, "create": true, "yaw": 0.6, "distance": 4}
editor.viewport_instance_set {"id": 2, "create": true, "quality": "game"}
editor.viewport_link {"id": 1, "group": 7}
editor.viewport_link {"id": 2, "group": 7}        # 2 adopts 1's camera
editor.capture_viewport_instance {"id": 1}
editor.capture_viewport_instance {"id": 2}        # same eye, different preset
```

**Orbit both.** `editor.viewport_instance_set {"id": 2, "yaw": 1.2}` moves 2 and, through the
group, 1. Check with `editor.viewport_instances`: both `camera.yaw` values match.

**Split them.** `editor.viewport_link {"id": 2, "group": null}`, then move 2 alone.

**Per-view show flags.** `editor.viewport_instance_set {"id": 2, "game_view": true}` hides the
helpers in 2 only. A capture of 1 still has the grid (`grid_pixels` > 0).

## Notes

- Instance ids are chosen by the tool that draws them. Keep them unique per world.
- Linking copies the whole perspective camera (target, distance, yaw, pitch, field of view, fly
  speed). Orthographic panes of a quad layout keep their own cameras.
- In the live panel, a pane drawn earlier in the frame follows a later pane's move on the next
  frame (one frame of lag). When two linked panes move in the same frame, the first one drawn
  wins.
- When several viewports draw through a world's shared `RuntimeRenderer` in the same frame,
  temporal upscaling (TAAU) is off for all of them, so one view's history never leaks into
  another's. `info.taau` reports it.

## Idle repaint

With realtime disabled, a viewport does not request another egui frame simply because it was
drawn. Pointer, keyboard, SpaceMouse, linked-camera synchronization, and other editor changes
still trigger redraws as needed. The stats overlay also stays idle when its displayed values are
unchanged; a changed displayed value can request a redraw.

<!-- depth-2:method-reference -->

## Call reference

Parameters, results and error codes for every method on this page. Types and defaults come from the schema and handlers; limits include the contract. Error codes are in `data.code`; names explicitly labeled `data.reason` are additional handler reasons. Every method can also return `F0001`, `F0002`, `F0004`, `F0007` and `F0012`. The server can return `F0005`, `F0006`, `request_too_large`, or `F0008` when the method is not registered; see [protocol](book/agents/protocol.md).

Unless a lower or explicit method limit is listed, the dispatcher accepts at most 65,536 items in a top-level array parameter and 1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes in a string parameter. A limit violation returns `F0002`.

The request in each fence is the call that was sent with `regia agent call`.
The line under it is the host's answer.
A second fence tagged `json,ignore` is an error answer. Large fields are elided with `...`. A fence tagged `json,ignore` is a real call on a host or plugin method that the runtime schema does not list.


### `editor.capture_viewport_instance`

Render one viewport instance headless with its own camera, quality preset and show flags (overlays painted in) and return a PNG, the eye it used, measurements and frame statistics.

*Read, does not mutate.*

| Param | Type | Required | Default and limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | number | yes | Viewport instance id. |
| `view` | string | no | Pane: perspective (default), top, front or side. |
| `width` | number | no | Frame width in pixels. Default 320, clamped to 64..=2048. |
| `height` | number | no | Frame height in pixels. Default 240, clamped to 64..=2048. |
| `quality` | string | no | Preset for this call only. Default: the instance's. |
| `game_view` | boolean | no | Hide every editor helper for this call. Omitted uses the instance’s game_view. |
| `warm_frames` | number | no | Frames rendered before the kept one. Default 0; capped at 16. |

Result: `{ id, width, height, mime, png_base64, view, eye, target, sky_luminance, lit_peak, shading_range, selection_highlight, grid_pixels, gizmo_axes, quality, info }`.

Errors besides the universal codes: `F0002`, `F0003`, `F0011`.

`F0011` when the adapter returns no image. Width and height default to 320 and 240 and clamp to 64..=2048. `warm_frames` clamps to 0..=16.

### `editor.viewport_instance_remove`

Forget a viewport instance: its registry entry, link membership and viewport-owned renderers. A panel that draws it again registers it afresh.

*EditScene, mutating. Changes the editor viewport registry.*

| Param | Type | Required | Default and limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | number | yes | Viewport instance id. |

Result: `{ id, removed }`. `removed` is false when that id was never registered; that call is not `not_found`.

Errors besides the universal codes: `F0002`, `F0003`.

```json
editor.viewport_instance_remove {"id": 7}
→ { "id": 7, "removed": true }
```

### `editor.viewport_instance_set`

Edit one viewport instance: perspective camera, quality preset, single/quad layout, show flags and game view. The panel applies it on its next draw; a linked camera that moves leads its group. `create` registers a new instance (seeded from the main viewport) for headless captures.

*EditScene, mutating. Changes the editor viewport registry.*

| Param | Type | Required | Default and limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | number | yes | Viewport instance id. |
| `create` | boolean | no | Default false. Create the instance when the id is unknown; seed it from the main viewport. Omitted edit fields keep the instance’s values. |
| `target` | array | no | Orbit target [x, y, z]. |
| `distance` | number | no | Orbit distance, meters; clamped to 0.2..=5000. |
| `yaw` | number | no | Yaw around +Y, radians. |
| `pitch` | number | no | Pitch above the horizon, radians (clamped to ±1.45). |
| `fov_deg` | number | no | Vertical field of view, degrees; clamped to 5..=150. |
| `quality` | string | no | Quality preset name (editor, game, mobile_low, ..., deck). |
| `layout` | string | no | single or quad. |
| `grid` | boolean | no | Reference grid. |
| `labels` | boolean | no | Selection name labels. |
| `realtime` | boolean | no | Render every frame. |
| `audio` | boolean | no | Audio gizmos. |
| `icons` | boolean | no | Light/camera/decal/audio icons. |
| `bounds` | boolean | no | Selection bounds, light ranges, frustums. |
| `outline` | boolean | no | Selection outline. |
| `proxies` | boolean | no | Proxy cubes for entities with nothing to draw. |
| `stats` | boolean | no | Stats overlay. |
| `preview_light` | boolean | no | Preview sun when the level has none. |
| `game_view` | boolean | no | Hide every editor helper. |

Result: `the instance, as in editor.viewport_instances`.

Errors besides the universal codes: `F0002`, `F0003`.

`create: true` registers an id the list does not have yet, seeded from the main viewport. Without it an unknown id is `F0003`.

### `editor.viewport_instances`

List the world's independent viewports (lightbox, before/after, compare panes): each one's camera, quality preset, layout, show flags, link group, the panes of its last draw and whether it is live (drawn this frame or the last).

*Read, does not mutate.*

No parameters.

Result: `{ instances: [{ id, live, frame, camera, quality, layout, active, game_view, possessed, show, settings, link, panes: [{index, kind, eye, target, width, height}], fps }] }`.

Errors besides the universal codes: `F0002`.

```json
editor.viewport_instances {}

```

## Workflow: open a second view and capture it

1. `editor.viewport_instances` to see ids already registered.
2. `editor.viewport_instance_set` with a new `id` and `create` true, plus the orbit (`target`, `distance`, `yaw`, `pitch`) and a `quality` name.
3. `editor.viewport_link` with that `id` and a `group` when a second pane should orbit with it. `group` null unlinks.
4. `editor.capture_viewport_instance` with the `id`, a small `width` and `height`, and `warm_frames` 0 to capture without warm-up frames. The answer carries `png_base64`. `F0011` means the adapter produced no image.
5. `editor.viewport_instance_remove` when the pane is done. A panel that draws the id again registers it afresh.

<!-- /depth-2:method-reference -->

## Clip planes and 2- and 3-pane layouts (ADR-7755)

`editor.viewport_instance_set` also takes `near` and `far` (meters; near 0.001 to 100, far 1 to 100000 and at least ten
times near, checked together against the instance's current planes; a bad pair is `bad_clip` and changes nothing), and
`layout` takes `single`, `quad`, `side_by_side`, `stacked` or `one_large_two`. `editor.viewport_instances` reports each
instance's `near`, `far` and `layout` name. Every pane of a 2-, 3- or 4-pane layout keeps its own camera and view kind;
the main viewport's layout is `editor.viewport_layout` (see [Viewport tools](book/agents/viewport-tools.md)).

```json
{ "method": "editor.viewport_instance_set", "params": { "id": 7, "create": true, "near": 1.0, "far": 50.0, "layout": "side_by_side" } }
```

Check it worked: `editor.viewport_instances` lists instance 7 with `near: 1.0`, `far: 50.0`, `layout: "side_by_side"`.

<!-- source: book/agents/headless-capture.md -->
# Headless deterministic capture

Run any Regia Engine app **offscreen** (no window, no compositor) with a fixed timestep, step exact
frames through the agent protocol, then screenshot. Two lavapipe runs of the same script produce
**byte-identical** PNGs — the path DO27 and CI use for goldens.

## Setup

```rust
use regia::prelude::*;
use regia_app::enable_fixed_step;
use regia_render::RenderPlugin;

fn main() {
    let mut app = App::new();
    app.add_plugins((
        MinimalPlugins,
        RenderPlugin { headless: true },
        regia_agent::AgentPlugin,
    ));
    enable_fixed_step(&mut app, 60.0); // ManualDuration + one FixedUpdate per App::update
}
```

- `RenderPlugin { headless: true }` skips surfaces but still runs `extract_frame`, so
  `seeing.screenshot` with `target: "offscreen"` draws the extracted runtime frame
  (`MeshRenderer` + `Camera` via `RuntimeRenderer::render_offscreen`). There is no window and
  no compositor.
- `enable_fixed_step(app, hz)` pins `TimeUpdateStrategy::ManualDuration` and `FixedTime` so wall
  clock never enters the sim. Start the app paused (`play.pause`) so the connection delay does
  not advance the clock before the first `play.step`.

## Agent script

For offscreen capture, `seeing.screenshot` accepts `target`, `width`, `height`, `window_layers`,
`hud`, `layout`, and `calibration`. Width and height default to 256×144 and must each be in
1..=4096; layout is `auto`, `landscape`, or `portrait`; calibration is `applied` or `neutral`.
Invalid values return `F0002`; unsupported view modes or overlays return `F0013`; failure to
create the headless renderer returns `F0011`.

```json
play.pause {}
play.step { "frames": 8 }
seeing.screenshot {
  "target": "offscreen",
  "width": 64,
  "height": 64,
  "timeout_ms": 30000
}
→ { "width": 64, "height": 64, "mime": "image/png", "png_base64": "..." }
```

On lavapipe, a zero-sized request fails parameter validation before rendering:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":10,"method":"seeing.screenshot","params":{"target":"offscreen","width":0,"height":64}}
→ {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":10,"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"`width`/`height` must be in 1..=4096 for target \"offscreen\"","data":{"code":"F0002","hint":"check the method's parameters in the agent guide"}}}
```

Offscreen capture needs a `Camera` and at least one `MeshRenderer`. It answers immediately
(no present wait). A mesh that rotates in `FixedUpdate` makes frame N differ from frame N+10;
two runs of the same step counts are byte-identical on lavapipe. Pin `Camera.exposure_ev` and
turn auto-exposure off so the exposure does not drift between runs.

## Determinism checklist

Workflow: start paused with a fixed timestep, add a camera and mesh, step the chosen frame count,
capture offscreen, and repeat from a fresh app with the same inputs. Compare PNG bytes; then
change the step count and confirm the moving object changes the image.

1. Use lavapipe for goldens (`VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_SELECT=*lvp*` — already set in this repo’s cargo
   env). Never bless a golden on the real GPU.
2. Call `enable_fixed_step` before the first `App::update`.
3. Pin exposure (`Camera.exposure_ev` and `PostSettings::golden_deterministic()`). Auto
   exposure adapts and breaks byte identity.
4. Disable film grain, TAA, and bloom for goldens.
5. Re-run the same script twice; PNG bytes must match. The agent test
   `two_headless_runs_match_and_the_clock_moves_the_mesh` renders a mesh that spins with the fixed
   clock: the frame is not blank, frame N differs from frame N+10, and both runs match.

See also [seeing](book/agents/seeing.md) and [testing](book/agents/testing.md).

<!-- source: book/agents/fog.md -->
# Distance and height fog

Outdoor haze on the runtime path: fog gets stronger with distance and with depth below a
base height. It runs in linear color, before AgX.

## Formula

Optical depth for the flat-color mode (`sky_inscatter = false`) is evaluated at the point.
`regia::fog::fog_factor` returns the fog amount `1 − exp(−τ)`, not `τ` itself:

```text
τ = distance · density · exp(−height_falloff · (y − base_height))
amount = 1 − exp(−τ)
color = lerp(scene, fog_colour, amount)
```

That is the exponential height fog from Hoffman & Preetham, "Rendering Outdoor Light Scattering"
(GDC 2002). `regia_render::fog` is the CPU copy of this point formula, and the flat branch of
`lab_forward.wgsl` and the terrain shaders (`terrain.wgsl`, scatter, water) use it.

The default aerial mode (`sky_inscatter = true`) instead integrates along the camera-to-surface
segment (`height_fog_optical_depth` in `aerial.wgsl`):

```text
start = density · exp(−height_falloff · (camera.y − base_height))
dh    = surface.y − camera.y
τ     = start · distance · (1 − exp(−height_falloff · dh)) / (height_falloff · dh)
```

(the last factor is 1 when `height_falloff · dh` is near 0). A hand-computed golden for a mesh
must use this form.

## Runtime

Put settings on `RenderSettings.fog` (`FogSettings`). When the LUT sky runs, the frame forces
`FogSettings` off for meshes and terrain and the atmosphere's aerial LUT supplies the haze; use
`VolumetricFogSettings` there. On Earth the LUT sky is `physical_atmosphere` (Desktop High and
Ultra, and only when no studio environment owns the frame). On Mars or an airless world an HDR
single-sample frame uses the LUT sky on every preset. An airless world also forces `FogSettings`
off. On Earth, `FogSettings` applies when that LUT sky is off (Desktop Low, Deck, Mobile, lab).
Extraction copies them onto
`ExtractedFrame` and `FrameScene`, so `MeshRenderer` + `Camera` see them. The default
(`RenderSettings::default().fog`) is `FogSettings::aerial()`: aerial perspective that
in-scatters the horizon sky radiance (`sky_inscatter = true`, optical depth integrated along
the ray; see [The default look](book/user-guide/default-look.md)). `FogSettings::default()` is
off, and lab/golden scenes built from `LabScene` stay fog-free. `FogSettings::outdoor_haze()`
is a dense blue-gray flat-color preset.

```rust
use regia::prelude::*;
use regia_render::{FogSettings, RenderProfilePreset, RenderSettings};

fn configure(app: &mut App) {
    // Desktop Low keeps the analytic fog. Desktop High's LUT sky forces `FogSettings` off;
    // use `VolumetricFogSettings` on that preset.
    let mut settings = RenderSettings::from_profile(RenderProfilePreset::DesktopLow);
    settings.fog = FogSettings::outdoor_haze();
    app.insert_resource(settings);
}
```

`params_vec4()` packs `(density, height_falloff, base_height, enabled)` for the GPU.

## What a good frame looks like

Far terrain shifts toward the fog color more than near terrain. A uniform tint is not fog.
Tests reject a near-black frame, a blown-out frame, and a frame where far pixels did not move
more than near ones. Evidence for the heightfield (scatter, one sun cascade, three sun angles,
fog on and off) lives in `docs/evidence/do27-gaps/`. The noon fog-on PNG is the lavapipe golden.

<!-- source: book/agents/atmosphere.md -->
# Atmosphere

Desktop High and Ultra sample a physically based sky. The tables are integrated on the CPU
once per sun elevation, camera height and planet, then uploaded. A change of azimuth only
rotates the sample. On Earth, Mobile, Desktop Low and Deck keep the analytic gradient; Mars and
airless maps use the tables on every HDR frame (there is no cheap stand-in for them).

## What is in the tables

- Transmittance to space.
- One multiple-scattering estimate (Hillaire 2020, building on Bruneton 2017).
- A sky-view table relative to the sun.
- Aerial perspective: in-scatter and transmittance over 32 km, sixteen bilinear slices.

The sun disk is drawn analytically, at least a pixel wide, with limb darkening. It is smaller
than one sky-view texel, so it is not baked into the table. Stars are added on top of the
lookup: at night on a planet with air, at any hour on an airless one. A sky body (Jupiter seen
from Europa, 14° in the DO27 preset) and up to two `moons` are spheres lit by the sun, so they show the right phase; `OutdoorParams::sky_body_albedo` takes an equirectangular albedo map for
the body, and `OutdoorParams::moon_albedo` (`[Option<Arc<SkyBodyTexture>>; 2]`, one per moon in
order) does the same for the moons. A `None` slot keeps that moon's tint, byte-identical to the
untextured look; a `Some` map is sampled on the same path (equirectangular, longitude across,
north pole at the top, sRGB RGBA8) and lit with the same sun-driven phase. Airless daylight stars carry their physical radiance, so they vanish next to sunlit ice and show at night exposure. Indirect light uses the
table without the disk, plus a ground bounce below the horizon, written into the existing IBL
textures, so a diffuse surface matches the sky; on an airless moon that ambient is the ground
bounce alone.

A view ray below the geometric horizon that no geometry covers (past a platform edge, past the
far edge of a map) shows the planet's surface: one Lambertian color behind the air in front of
it. That is on by default under air and off on an airless world, where nothing fades it into a
horizon and it would read as a flat band at the map's edge; `OutdoorParams::planet_surface`
(`Some(true)` / `Some(false)`) overrides it per sky (ADR-162).

## Planets

`AtmosphereParameters::{earth, mars, airless}` (or `from_preset`) set the medium; maps choose
one with `LevelSettings.atmosphere.preset` (`Earth`, `Mars`, `Airless`), see the
[rendering guide](book/user-guide/rendering.md#planet-presets-per-map). In code,
`OutdoorParams { planet, sky_body, .. }` on `FrameRenderer::set_outdoor` does the same.

| Preset | Sky | Haze | Clouds | Ambient |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Earth | blue, orange at sunset | Rayleigh + Mie | yes | sky + ground |
| Mars | butterscotch, blue around a low sun | dust | yes | dusty sky + ground |
| Airless | black, stars | none | none | ground bounce |

Agents: the protocol has no dedicated sky command. Read the level's settings with
`scene.serialize` (the `LevelSettings` resource) and change the planet by editing the
`.level.ron` (canonical RON, format v3); the map's exposure and grade are `level.get_look` / `level.set_look` ([look](book/agents/look.md)). `render_lab planets` renders the reference shots.

## Time of day

Insert a `TimeOfDay` resource (`hour`, `day_of_year`, `latitude_deg`). When the physical
atmosphere is on, that sun replaces the directional light, including the transmitted color
and illuminance, before the shadow cascades are fitted. With no `TimeOfDay`, the authored
directional light still drives the sky.

```rust
use regia::prelude::*;
use regia::render::TimeOfDay;

fn configure(app: &mut App) {
    app.insert_resource(TimeOfDay::noon());
}
```

`TimeOfDay::dawn`, `dusk` and `night` are the equinox, 45°N samples the goldens use. A map
can set the clock instead with `LevelSettings.atmosphere.time_of_day`; a `TimeOfDay`
resource wins.

## Checks

`sky_four_times_of_day_have_the_right_hue` renders dawn and dusk as one fixed panorama: the
glow sits over the sun's azimuth (east at dawn, west at dusk) and a dusk frame fails the dawn
golden. `planet_presets_have_their_own_sky_haze_and_ambient`,
`mars_sunset_is_blue_around_the_sun` and `airless_sky_body_is_lit_on_the_sun_side` check the
presets on whole Desktop High frames.

<!-- source: book/agents/look.md -->
# Map look: exposure meter and color grade

Every map can carry its own exposure and grade in `LevelSettings.look` (scene format v3). The
runtime applies it to every view's post stack; a field left `None` keeps the view's
`RenderSettings.post`, so a level that says nothing looks like the engine default.

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| `exposure_bias_ev` | Added to the metered (or fixed) exposure; positive brightens. |
| `min_ev100`, `max_ev100` | The auto-exposure clamp (the snow ceiling, the night floor). |
| `meter` | `low_percentile` / `high_percentile` trim the dark and bright ends of the histogram; `center_weight` 0 meters evenly, 1 weights the frame center up to 9×. |
| `contrast`, `saturation` | The display look after AgX (engine default 1.2 / 1.4). |
| `grade` | `white_balance_kelvin` (6500 neutral; higher warms the print), `tint`, then `lift` / `gamma` / `gain` per channel on the display image. |
| `lut` | A project-relative `.cube` (Adobe Cube LUT, 3D) or PNG strip (N slices of N×N side by side, x = r + b·N, y = g) applied after the grade; `None` is the identity. `\` is accepted as a separator. A `.cube` the asset manifest holds loads from the paks or the cooked cache first (a packaged Android client has nothing else), then a loose file under the project root. Loaded once per path (`LevelColorLut`); a failed load warns and keeps the identity. |
| `local_exposure` | Scene format v9, off by default. `shadow_contrast` / `highlight_contrast` (0–1, 1 = unchanged) pull dark / bright regions toward middle grey, `detail_strength` (1 = unchanged) scales the texture on top; an edge-aware bilateral grid in post, so a dark hull lifts as a whole beside sunlit snow. DO27's `local_exposure_shadows 0.75` is `{"shadow_contrast": 0.75}`. |

`LevelAtmosphere.haze` gives the map a dust or mist layer near the floor (`density` 1/m,
`scale_height_m`, `base_height_m`); on Mars it scatters like the planet's butterscotch dust.
`LevelAtmosphere.moons` adds up to two lit moons beside `sky_body`.

## Agent methods

- `level.get_look` returns `{ look }` for the open level.
- `level.set_look` deep-merges a partial object and returns `{ before, after }`:
  `{"look": {"exposure_bias_ev": 0.5, "grade": {"white_balance_kelvin": 6900}}}`. A `null`
  block (`meter`, `grade`) starts from its neutral value. The next frame uses the new look.

The view's own tonemap operator, auto-exposure switch, fixed EV, physical camera, bloom, vignette and
grain are `render.get_exposure_settings` / `render.set_exposure_settings` ([Exposure and tonemap](book/agents/exposure.md)); the look
is applied on top of them.

Judge a change by eye: `seeing.screenshot` (target `offscreen`) after a few frames for auto
exposure to settle, side by side with the reference plate, then save the level.

## Reference presets

`samples/lookdev` (`lookdev::look_r2`) holds the DO27 presets tuned against the UE v13 plates:
`switchbacks_look` + `switchbacks_haze` (Mars: EV100 held at 10.25–10.75, contrast 1.8, 5800 K +
magenta tint 0.45, a thin 1.2e-5 /m haze) and `bore_twelve_look` (Europa: EV100 held at 11.5–11.7 for
≈ 0.5-reflectance ice, contrast 1.15). Render them with
`cargo run -p lookdev --bin look_r2 -- --out <dir>`.

Hold daylight exposure in a narrow `min_ev100`/`max_ev100` band rather than letting the meter
average the frame. An averaging meter darkens any frame with a bright sky in it by about 2 EV, and
it prints ice at the same brightness whatever its albedo. Put the sun ahead of and to the side of the
camera, not behind it: a sun behind the lens hides every shadow behind the object that casts it.

A warm white balance is not the same as a red print: for an orange (red > green > blue) the hue
angle is 60·(g − b)/(r − b), so cutting blue moves it toward yellow and olive. To push Mars rock
toward red-brown, add magenta `tint` (it removes green) rather than raising the kelvin.

## Frame problems

`render.problems` returns `{ ok, problems: [{ code, message }] }` for the last frame the runtime
renderer drew. `msaa_skips_terrain` means the quality asks for MSAA (`msaa_samples` ≥ 4) while a
shared terrain draw or a planet sky is set: the renderer draws neither on multisampled frames, and
auto exposure then meters what is left (often black, which blows every mesh out). Use
`msaa_samples` 1; anti-aliasing is TAA in post. A host that drives `FrameRenderer` itself reads
`FrameRenderer::frame_problems()`, and `host_checklist_report` lists the same item as an `ERROR`
([Host look checklist](book/user-guide/host-look-checklist.md)).

`texture_budget_exceeded` (the material textures resident exceed the tier's texture budget, or
2 GiB with streaming off) and `uncompressed_textures` (more than 64 RGBA8 material textures: a
level of PNG/JPEG instead of cooked BC7/ASTC) name the five largest offenders; the host checklist
lists them as differences, not errors. `assets.texture_memory` has the per-texture detail
([Assets](book/agents/assets.md#texture-memory-and-the-budget)).

Two GPU health codes (ADR-171) are process-wide, not about one frame:

- `gpu_errors`: wgpu reported uncaptured errors since start (validation, internal, out of
  memory). Release builds log them under `regia::gpu_error` and keep drawing, so a garbled
  frame may follow. The perf overlay shows "GPU errors: N" and `perf_overlay.get` returns
  `stats.gpu_errors`; feedback bundles carry `gpu_errors` in `feedback.json`. Read the log for
  the pass that failed.
- `vram_pressure`: GPU memory ran short (a wgpu out-of-memory error, live allocations above
  85 % of the adapter's VRAM in the telemetry probe, or the OS low-memory event). Every renderer
  freed its idle GPU memory (a dormant stochastic SSR pass's targets). Only out-of-memory errors
  lower the texture streaming budget: since v0.1.16 the first halves it, and each later one
  within 60 s of the previous one halves it again, at most three times and never below 256 MiB.
  One less than 60 s after a trim also holds the streamed textures a mip lower for a minute. The
  message gives the count of trims, budget steps and caught out-of-memory errors, and whether the
  mips are held; [`render.memory_pressure`](book/agents/low-memory-gpus.md) has the detail.

A lost GPU device has no code: the game stops drawing, writes a crash bundle whose `crash.txt`
starts with `device_lost:`, and exits with code 3 within about 2 s. A window surface
that cannot be created (after one retry) or stays lost for 120 frames does the same with
`surface_unavailable` and exit code 4.

## Large-mesh proxies

`render.mesh_occluders` returns `{ in_use, bands: { near, far, dropped, near_max, far_max },
occluders: [{ center, axes, half_extents, albedo, ground_y, far_band }] }`: the oriented boxes of the entities with `OcclusionProxy` (parked hulls, vehicles,
containers). Each box's sun shadow darkens the ground that meshes beside and on it see, in both
diffuse light and reflections. Each box also replaces the sky it hides from the ground with its
own faces' light, and shadows the sky body's fill. `in_use` is how many the last frame shaded
with; it is 0 on frames not lit by the planet atmosphere's IBL. A hull whose skirt or belly glows
like sunlit ground, or that sits on its shadow without a dark contact, is missing its proxy:
add `OcclusionProxy::default()` to the entity
([Host look checklist](book/user-guide/host-look-checklist.md) § 9).

`bands` splits the last frame's proxies (ADR-7970). `near` (at most `near_max`, 32) get the full
shade above. `far` (at most `far_max`, 128) are the next nearest proxies with `far_band` true
(`OcclusionProxy { far_band: true, .. }`): each is a coarse ground-contact blob that darkens the sky
and fill under its footprint, with no sun shadow. A near proxy whose distance comes within 5 m of
the nearest far one fades into its blob, so a hull crossing the boundary does not pop. `dropped`
are the rest: past 32 without `far_band`, past both bands, or with a non-finite box. All three are 0
until a frame lit by the planet IBL packs them. A match with hundreds of hulls and `dropped` above
0 on hulls near the camera needs more of them opted in, or fewer proxies per hull.

## Example calls

Example calls (`regia agent call <method> '<params json>'`; entity ids come from `scene.query_entities`):

```text
level.get_look {}
level.set_look {"look": {"exposure_bias_ev": 0.5, "grade": {"white_balance_kelvin": 6900}}}
render.problems {}               # { ok, problems: [{ code, message }] }
render.mesh_occluders {}         # { in_use, bands: { near, far, dropped, ... }, occluders: [...] }
```

# Exposure and tonemap (agents)

The post stack's exposure and tonemap settings (`PostSettings`) are readable and settable on the
running app. A map's own look (`level.set_look`, [Map look](book/agents/look.md)) is applied on top of these
values every frame: its `exposure_bias_ev` adds to `exposure_compensation`, and its `min_ev100` /
`max_ev100`, `meter`, `contrast` and `saturation` replace the ones set here while the map sets them.
Guide topic: `agent.guide {"topic": "look"}`.
The exposure the eye actually applied (the meter, exposure zones, the exposure log) is
`render.get_exposure`: see [Exposure zones](book/agents/exposure-zones.md).

## Methods

- `render.get_exposure_settings` returns every setting in the table below, plus `tonemaps` (the operator
  names `tonemap` accepts) and `camera_ev100` (the EV100 the aperture, shutter and ISO give).
- `render.set_exposure_settings` takes any subset of the settings, validates all of them, and then applies
  them on the next frame. It returns `{ before, after }`. At least one field is required. The
  change is not persisted. Mutating; permission `edit_scene`.

| Setting | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `auto_exposure` | Histogram auto exposure on or off. Off holds `exposure_ev`. |
| `exposure_ev` | The fixed EV100 used when auto exposure is off (-20 to 30). |
| `exposure_compensation` | EV added on top of auto or fixed exposure; positive brightens (-16 to 16). |
| `min_ev100`, `max_ev100` | The EV100 range auto exposure may pick (-20 to 30). `min_ev100` must not exceed `max_ev100`. |
| `tonemap` | `agx` (default), `aces_fitted` or `neutral`. Case and `-` / `_` do not matter. |
| `use_physical_camera` | Derive EV100 from `aperture`, `shutter_seconds` and `iso` instead of `exposure_ev`. |
| `aperture` | Aperture in f-stops (0.5 to 128). |
| `shutter_seconds` | Shutter time in seconds (1e-6 to 3600). |
| `iso` | ISO sensitivity (1 to 1e6). |
| `contrast`, `saturation` | The display look after the tonemap (0.05 to 8 and 0 to 8; engine default 1.2 and 1.4). |
| `bloom` | Bloom on or off. |
| `bloom_intensity` | Blend toward the blurred image, 0 to 1 (default 0.04). |
| `vignette` | Vignette strength, 0 to 1. |
| `film_grain` | Film grain strength, 0 to 1. Keep 0 for deterministic goldens. |
| `meter` | A partial object of `low_percentile`, `high_percentile`, `center_weight` (all 0 to 1), `bright_threshold` (cd/m², 0 to 1,000,000) and `bright_bias_ev` (-4 to 4). A field left out keeps its value. |
| `band_bounds_final_exposure` | Off (default): the meter is clamped to `min_ev100`..`max_ev100`, then `exposure_compensation` and the meter's `bright_bias_ev` shift it, so a frame of sunlit snow can settle under the band floor. On: both shifts apply first and the band clamps last, so the band bounds the final auto exposure. A map's look does not change it. |

Errors: `F0002` (`-32602`, `invalid_params`) for an unknown field, a value out of range or of the
wrong type, an unknown tonemap name, `min_ev100` above `max_ev100`, or no field at all. Nothing is
applied when any value is refused. `F0003` (`-32001`, `not_found`) means this app has no
`RenderSettings` resource (usually it has no `RenderPlugin`).

`band_bounds_final_exposure` (ADR-7969) is for a map whose band was tuned as the range the frame
may print at: with a band of EV100 10.5 to 11.5, a +1 EV snow bias and +1 EV compensation, a frame
of sunlit ice metering EV100 12.5 or more prints at EV100 9.5 with the switch off (1 EV under the
floor, clipped highlights) and at 10.5 to 11.5 with it on. Inside the band the switch changes
nothing. A level file cannot set it yet (the scene format gains the field with its v0.6 bump): the
host sets it once with `render.set_exposure_settings` or on `PostSettings` in code.

```json
{"method": "render.set_exposure_settings", "params": {"band_bounds_final_exposure": true}}
```

Settings this method does not own, and where they live: the post stack switch and the anti-aliasing
mode (`render.set_profile`), the color grade, LUT and local exposure (`level.set_look`), and motion
blur and depth of field (the camera's `PhysicalCamera`).

```json
{"method": "render.set_exposure_settings", "params": {"tonemap": "aces_fitted", "auto_exposure": false, "exposure_ev": 12.5}}
```

Captured on lavapipe (llvmpipe Vulkan): an unsupported tonemap name is rejected before any settings change.

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"render.set_exposure_settings","params":{"tonemap":"film"}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"`tonemap` must be one of agx, aces_fitted, neutral","data":{"code":"F0002","hint":"check the method's parameters in the agent guide"}}}
```

Judge a change by eye with `seeing.screenshot` (target `offscreen`) after a few frames, and pin
`auto_exposure` off and `film_grain` to 0 for goldens.

<!-- source: book/agents/gi-probes.md -->
# Lighting option: Balanced or Depth

Players choose how indirect light (sky light and light bounced off the ground and walls) looks.
This choice is separate from the quality preset:

| Option | What lights a shadowed surface | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **Balanced** | The sky irradiance map with canyon occlusion, an estimate of light bounced off sunlit walls, and the mesh ground bounce (ADR-062/065/066). | Every platform. Default on Low, Medium, Deck and mobile. |
| **Depth** | GPU-traced irradiance probes: up to four camera-relative cascades of 20×10×20 probes, 2 m spacing ×3 per cascade, tracing the terrain heightfield and per-mesh distance fields. They gather sun, sky and emissive light over several bounces (emissive meshes of any size enter through an emitter list, not rays), and Chebyshev visibility keeps light from passing through closed walls. A half-resolution screen pass stores the probe light at the visible surfaces, and each pixel rebuilds it for its own normal. | Desktop only (not on Android). Default on Desktop High and Ultra. |

A map with a baked GI volume (`.fgiv`) uses it instead of the probes, under Depth and the preset
default alike. Only a chosen Balanced keeps the analytic terms. See [Baked GI volumes](book/agents/baked-gi.md).
The renderer-side look `GiLook::Baked` (`render.set_gi_mode {"mode": "baked"}`) forces it and is not
a menu choice.

## Settings

- `GameSettings::graphics.lighting` is the value a game's options menu binds:
  `Some(LightingMode::Balanced)`, `Some(LightingMode::Depth)`, or `None` (the quality preset's
  default). It is applied live and persisted with the other graphics settings.
- `RenderSettings::gi_look` is the renderer-side value the settings plugin writes.
  `RenderSettings::effective_gi_look()` resolves `None` to the preset default.
- Preset defaults: Desktop High and Ultra ship Depth; Low, Medium, Deck and Android ship
  Balanced (ADR-133 records the cost and tracer numbers; the hull plate passes since round 4).
- Ground albedo: the probes' rays need the terrain's albedo where they hit it. A host calls
  `TerrainSharedDraw::bake_gi_albedo_map(device)` once at load, before the first frame. It
  bakes the albedo the terrain shader shades with, at 2 m texels. Without it the probes see one
  albedo for the whole map, and the bounce color and strength follow that average.

## Agent methods

- `render.get_gi_mode` returns `{ mode, probes, setting, preset_default, depth_available, persisted }`.
  `mode` is the look in effect (`"balanced"`, `"depth"` or `"baked"`). `setting` is the player's choice
  (`"default"` when unset). `graphics.lighting` is never `"baked"`: that look is renderer-side only.
- `render.set_gi_mode {"mode": "depth"}` sets the option and returns `{ before, after, note }`.
  `mode` is `"balanced"`, `"depth"`, `"baked"` or `"default"`; `"terms"` and `"probes"` are aliases of
  balanced and depth, and `"static"` is an alias of baked. Balanced and depth write
  `RenderSettings::gi_look` and, when the app has `GameSettings`, also `graphics.lighting`.
  `"baked"` sets `GiLook::Baked` and leaves `graphics.lighting` as it was. It applies on the next
  extracted frame; without an installed volume (`FrameRenderer::set_baked_gi`) the frame shades as
  balanced. On Android, `"depth"` and `"baked"` are refused.

Depth needs the post stack (a linear-HDR frame), so an LDR lab frame always uses Balanced. After
a switch or a camera cut the probes take about 30 frames to settle. To compare the two:

1. Call `play.pause` and `render.set_gi_mode {"mode": "balanced"}`, then `play.step 30` and
   `seeing.screenshot` (target `offscreen`).
2. Call `render.set_gi_mode {"mode": "depth"}`, then `play.step 30` and `seeing.screenshot`.
3. Judge the pair by eye against the reference plate. To check against ground truth, run
   `seeing.reference_trace` and `seeing.compare` with `aov: "indirect_diffuse"` (guide topic
   `renderer-excellence`).

## What to look for

- **Shadowed ground and walls:** Depth lights a shadowed trench floor only from the walls and
  sky the probes actually see. Where the terrain is open it is close to the path tracer.
  Balanced over-lights Mars canyon shadows about 2× against the tracer.
- **Interiors:** with Depth, a sealed room stays dark (under 1 % light leak).
- **Close-ups on open ground:** under the probes, a layer's ORM occlusion only shades
  crevices against its own texture mean. Texture AO is not geometry the probes trace (a scanned
  dune sand averages 0.36). The heightfield cavity and the baked macro AO do not darken the
  probe light either: the probes trace that relief themselves (ADR-169). Terrain debug views
  14 and 15 print the occlusion inputs: cavity, macro AO, probe coverage, ORM and SSAO.
- **Which meshes the probes trace:** rigid, opaque, shadow-casting meshes at least 1 m in
  radius whose distance-field voxel stays within 8 m (meshes up to ~320 m long). A thin plate
  (no thicker than 1 m: a floor, a pad, a studio ground) is traced at any length.
- **Known limits:** a receiver inside a shadow smaller than a probe cell (2 m near the camera)
  still takes some light from probes that see the sunlit ground beyond it, so small shaded
  pockets read brighter than the path tracer. Terrain more than ~450 m from the camera lies
  outside the cascades and keeps the analytic sky and bounce light. Europa's shaded trench flats
  read above the path tracer for the same sub-cell reason. The screen-space GI bounce is added on
  top of the probes' own bounce (about 3 % too bright in shade).
- **Cost:** GPU timings report it as `gi_ms`: the probe update plus the screen pass. On the
  RTX 5090 at 1440p, with the clocks up, the Mars plates cost about 0.26–0.28 ms per frame.
  For a bench run, set `LOOK_R2_PERF_HEAT=1000000` with `look_r2 --perf`. Without it, an idle
  card sits in its low power state and every pass reads about 3× slower.

Look-dev: `LOOK_R2_PROBES=1 cargo run -p lookdev --bin look_r2 -- --out <dir>` renders the DO27
plates with Depth. `docs/evidence/gi-probes/sheet/` holds the UE | Balanced | Depth sheet.
`pt_plates` (with `LOOK_R2_PROBES=1`) writes `<shot>_probe_vs_pt_irradiance.png`: probe
irradiance on the left, the tracer's on the right, at one exposure.

## Example calls

Example calls (`regia agent call <method> '<params json>'`; entity ids come from `scene.query_entities`):

```text
render.get_gi_mode {}            # { mode, probes, uses_bake, baked, setting, ... }
```

<!-- source: book/agents/baked-gi.md -->
# Baked GI volumes

A map can ship its indirect light baked by the path tracer: a `.fgiv` volume made by
`regia bake-gi` (format: `docs/formats/baked-gi.md`). The volume holds probes at fixed
positions. Each probe stores four light components as L1 spherical harmonics: sun bounce, sky,
sky-body fill and emissive. It also stores distance moments for visibility. The probes sit on a
terrain-following layer, with optional fine detail bricks around set pieces.

At runtime the bake replaces the GPU probe update (DDGI). It gives path-traced bounce, sky and
fill light at a fixed cost: one half-resolution lookup pass, about one sample per four pixels. There
is no settling time, so the first frame after a load or a camera cut is final.

## What changes on a baked map

| | Without a bake | With a bake |
|---|---|---|
| Diffuse indirect | DDGI (Depth) or the analytic terms (Balanced) | the bake, where it covers |
| Sky-body fill | live, unshadowed | baked: shadowed, plus its bounce |
| DDGI probe update | on under Depth | off |
| SSGI | per preset | off (the bake already counts the bounce) |
| GTAO | per preset | full resolution drops to half (the bake holds long-range sky visibility) |
| Sun, shadows, paged cache, SSR, local lights | per preset | unchanged |

The bake lights every look except a chosen **Balanced**. That includes Depth, the preset default,
and the Low presets. Outside the volume, the frame keeps its analytic terms: more than one column
spacing past the outermost columns, or more than twice the top level above the ground.

## Host API

- `RuntimeRenderer::set_baked_gi(Some(Arc<BakedGiVolume>))` installs a volume (or
  `FrameRenderer::set_baked_gi`). `None` removes it. Install it once per map, like the GI field.
- `FrameRenderer::set_baked_gi_settings(BakedGiSettings)` sets the tunables: normal and view bias,
  intensity, `sky_scale` and `emissive_scale` (relative to the bake), `follow_sun`, `follow_fill`
  and `replace_live_fill`, the quality switches `deringing`, `leak_guard` and `sun_relight`
  ([Baked GI quality](book/agents/baked-gi-quality.md)), and the leak control `visibility_filter` and
  `leak_reduction` ([Baked GI leak control in the lookup](book/agents/baked-gi-visibility.md)).
- `FrameRenderer::set_baked_gi_enabled(Some(false))` keeps the volume installed but unused. Use it
  for comparisons against Depth.
- `FrameRenderer::baked_gi_status()` reports `installed`, `active`, probe count, GPU bytes, an
  error, the per-component light factors and the sun mismatch.
- `regia_render::sample_static_gi(volume, settings, scales, p, n, v)` is the same lookup on the
  CPU: a gameplay query, or a check against the GPU.
- `FrameRenderer::set_gi_occluders(&[GiCapsule])` (or `RuntimeRenderer::set_gi_occluders`) sets
  the capsule occluders of dynamic units. It returns how many it kept. See *Dynamic occluders*
  below.

Each component scales linearly with its light. The sun-bounce term follows the frame's sun, and the
fill term follows the frame's sky-body fill. Light-level changes after the bake still apply.
Changes to the sun's direction do not. A sun more than 3° from the baked one logs a warning once.

## Interiors

A volume in format v2 can flag a detail brick as `INTERIOR`: an enclosed room, a hangar, a tunnel.
The bake sets the flag on bricks whose centre lies inside an interior box. Inside an interior
brick:

- The terrain layer adds nothing, so outdoor sky and bounce light do not leak through the walls.
- The brick does not fade out over its last cell toward the outdoor probes. Its light ends at its
  box, so it does not leak out either.
- It wins over any other brick that holds the point, even a larger outdoor brick around it.
- The lookup tests the point pushed half a cell along its normal. An outer wall (normal pointing
  out of the box) reads the outdoor light. An inner wall reads the interior's.
- The test allows an eighth of a cell outside the probe box (ADR-1364). A floor pixel next to a
  wall, or a surface exactly on the box, can land a few ulps outside it; without this slack it
  read the outdoor light and drew a bright line along every room edge.
- Put the brick's probe lattice on the room's air box: the inner faces of the walls, floor and
  roof. `regia bake-gi --from-scene` does this with each `interiors.json` box. A lattice half a
  cell or more inside the air reads the outdoor light on the room's own surfaces. A box out to the
  wall centres puts probes inside the walls, and the walls come out blotchy.
- If every probe around the point failed the bake, the point reads black at full coverage instead
  of falling back to the outdoor terms.

An interior with an opening (a vehicle bay door) is flagged as a whole in v0.2.0. Light does not
enter through the opening yet. Version 1 files have no flags and light exactly as before.

## Emitters the bake holds

The bake's emissive component holds the light of every emissive surface it traced, seen directly
and bounced. Desktop High and Ultra also light the scene with area lights fitted to emissive
meshes (`emissive_lights`). Without care the same emitter would light a room twice: the Cornell
box in the v0.2.0 look review came out 13 to 57 % too bright on those tiers (ADR-1386).

- A volume in format v3 names the emitters it traced: per placed emissive mesh, its world bounds
  (`BakedGiVolume::emitters`, `BakedEmitter`). `regia bake-gi` writes the list.
- Each frame, the renderer matches the emissive meshes it draws against that list by their world
  bounds (2 cm plus 2 % of the emitter's size). The area lights of a matched emitter are tagged.
- The forward pass takes a tagged light's diffuse back out where the volume covers the pixel. It
  also takes out the light's specular as far as the probes stand in for the rough lobe. Outside the
  volume, and on surfaces the volume does not cover, the area light stays.
- An emitter the bake did not trace keeps its area light everywhere: one added or moved after the
  bake, a unit's lights, anything on the `structure` and `dynamic` layers.
- Over the area light budget, tagged lights go after the others.
- Desktop Low, Deck and Mobile draw no emissive area lights, so nothing changes there.
- `emissive_scale` 0 (the bake's emitter light off) or `intensity` 0 keeps every area light.
- A v1 or v2 volume does not name its emitters. It still loads, but every area light stays, so on
  High and Ultra its emitters are counted twice. The renderer logs a warning once. Rebake the map
  with this build: there is no other migration, because only the bake knows which emitters it
  traced.
- Change an emitter's material color or intensity after the bake and the tag still applies: the
  bake's emitter light follows `emissive_scale` only. Rebake after emitter changes, as after any
  scene change.

## Dynamic occluders

Units are not in the bake. To darken the baked light next to a vehicle or a character, the host
lists a few capsules per unit each frame:

```rust,wrap
# let renderer: &mut regia_render::FrameRenderer = todo!();
use regia_render::baked_gi::GiCapsule;
let hull = GiCapsule::new([10.0, 1.2, 4.0], [14.0, 1.2, 4.0], 1.1); // ends and radius, metres
renderer.set_gi_occluders(&[hull, GiCapsule::sphere([12.0, 2.6, 4.0], 0.8)]);
```

- Each capsule is the segment `a`–`b` swept by `radius`. `strength` (0 to 1, default 1) is how much
  of the blocked light it removes.
- At most `MAX_GI_OCCLUDERS` (64) are used per frame. The rest, and unusable ones (non-finite ends,
  radius or strength ≤ 0), are dropped and counted in `baked_gi_status().occluders_dropped`. There is
  no distance band here: with hundreds of units, list the 64 capsules nearest the eye, and give every
  unit's mesh proxy `OcclusionProxy::far_band` so the units past those still shade the ground under
  them (`render.mesh_occluders` `bands`, ADR-7970).
- The list stays until the next call. A host whose units move sets it every frame. An empty list
  clears it.
- They act only in the baked screen pass, so only where a volume lights the frame. Android has no
  volume, so they cost nothing there. With an empty list nothing is uploaded and the pass does no
  occluder work.
- Fit capsules inside the unit's hull. A capsule then darkens the ground and walls next to the unit
  but not the unit itself, because its surface faces away from the capsule.
- The occlusion is analytic: the light a sphere blocks from the hemisphere above a surface, with
  each capsule treated as its sphere nearest the surface. A long capsule is under-counted toward its
  ends; split a long body into two or three capsules.

## Agent methods

- `render.get_gi_mode` returns `uses_bake` (whether the current look would use an installed
  volume). It also returns `baked`, which is `null` without a runtime renderer, else `{ installed,
  active, probes, gpu_bytes, error, scales, sun_mismatch_deg, occluders, occluder_cap,
  occluders_dropped, interior_bricks, emitters }`. `scales` has one row per component, in the order
  sun bounce, sky, fill, emissive. Each row is per channel, and 1 is the baked level. `occluders` is
  the number of capsules in use, `occluder_cap` is 64, and `interior_bricks` counts the installed
  volume's interior bricks. `brick_grid` is `{ cells, entries }` of the brick lookup grid the screen
  pass walks instead of every brick (ADR-1835): `cells` 0 means no bricks, and `entries` over `cells`
  is how many bricks a texel's cell tests on average (keep it far below `interior_bricks` plus the
  plain brick count; a map where it approaches the brick count has bricks that span the whole level).
  `emitters` is the number of emitters the bake named, or `null` for a v1
