  resized during the job arms warm frames for the window's targets; they wait for the job's end (ADR-2808).
  A job that starts while the context still builds on a warm worker installs it first, so its early
  effects are drawn and it starts the way later jobs do; the compile only makes that job start later (ADR-2814).
- the effect instance slots (ADR-2814): with no instance live they start over at a job's start, so effects
  spawned in the same order take the same slots, whichever retired first in the job before.
  Before, Red-Rouge's first held pair on a software rasterizer differed from the crash's impact on (15 of
  24 color frames equal) while later pairs repeated.

| Two runs of one request | Hashes |
| --- | --- |
| Two fresh apps | equal |
| One app, the replay armed or seeked to the same tick before each job | equal, for a world posed from the replay |
| One app, the world did not move: a `time_map` of scale 0 holds the simulation, or the scene is posed from the clocks alone | equal |
| One app, the first job moved the world (the fixed loop ran a game or a host timeline) | differ: the second job continues the world. `clock.app_sim_time_at_start_ns` differs too, which is the tell |
| One app, the world held and a live effect running (a `vfx.crash`, its fires) | equal: the particles move on the render clock inside each job, and a held job puts them back when its frames end (ADR-2633) |
| One app, no hold, nothing alive at either start, the game spawns an effect (seeded or not) at the same job time | equal (ADR-2687) |
| One app, no hold and a live effect running | the color frames differ (the second job continues the effect); depth, id and motion can repeat, because the AOVs do not draw particles |
| Different GPUs or drivers | differ |

**Live effects under a hold (ADR-2633).** Red-Rouge's v0.2.13 retest (0 of 24 color frames equal between two
held jobs, depth, id and motion 24 of 24) came from a `vfx.crash` left running in the host. Live effects run on
the render clock (ADR-1524), so a held job still shows its smoke drifting and its fires flickering. When its frames end, however the job ended, these go
back to where the job found them: the effect instances (ages, spawn counters, random streams), the particle
pool on the GPU, `vfx.crash` sequences, the fires and their clock, the debris clock, the decal pool, the camera
shake, a weather transition with its clock and drift, surface wetness and snow, and the fall of rain and snow. A job with any other `time_map`, or none, leaves them where its last frame did: the manifest's
`clock.live_effects` says which (`restored` or `moved_on`). A paused app also holds the fire and debris clocks
between jobs, so the idle frames a host runs while clients talk to it do not reach a later job.
The camera director's shakes and every camera's received shakes (`regia_framework`) play on the same clock
and go back the same way (ADR-2687).

Give both jobs some `warmup_frames` when you compare them: a fresh host's first rendered frame can show a
world that is still arriving (in the showcase, frame 0 of a held shot differs from the rest without a
warm-up), which a later job never sees.

The showcase's director is a timeline of the scene (the track, the spawns, the weather changes), so a
second job in one showcase host renders later frames of it, the fourth row. To compare two takes of one
shot there, use a fresh host for each. The tests are
`crates/regia_agent/tests/render_out_deterministic.rs`, `render_out_replay_scene.rs` and
`samples/showcase/tests/render.rs` (`two_jobs_repeat_their_color_*`: where the AOVs of two jobs in one
showcase host repeat, the color frames must too; set `REGIA_GPU_UUID` to run them on a card).

## Exposure at a cut

Auto exposure reads a histogram of each frame two frames late (`FrameRenderer::EXPOSURE_READBACK_FRAMES`).
A cut restarts the meter, so in a game the two frames after a cut print at the meter's initial EV: the
camera's or the map's fixed EV when one is set, otherwise the top of the auto-exposure band (EV100 15, a
sunny day). Before ADR-1455 a render-out did the same: a one-frame still was that first frame, and on
the showcase's hazy morning it printed 1.26 EV darker than the meter's own reading (EV100 15.0 against
13.74). A render-out now meters every cut before delivering it. After the cut it renders the cut's game
frame two more times at the delivered size. These renders are not delivered, and the clock and the
particles stay still while they run. Then it cuts again with `CutExposure::Fade`, which restarts every
temporal history but keeps the meter's reading. The delivered frame is exactly the first frame after a
cut, exposed for itself. A job also makes auto exposure wait for its histogram readbacks
(`set_wait_for_exposure_readback`), so the meter reads the same histograms on the same frames in every
run, and the hashes stay deterministic. Cost: two renders per cut. A view with a fixed exposure (a
camera EV, a profile without auto exposure) cuts once, as before. The manifest and
`render.out_progress` report `exposure_metered_cuts`. `camera_cuts` counts a metered cut once.
`render.exposure_log` shows each frame's EV (`crates/regia_agent/tests/render_out_cut_exposure.rs`).

## Motion blur (`subframes` and `shutter_angle`)

With `subframes` N above 1, each delivered frame is the average, in linear light, of N renders taken
while a virtual film shutter is open. The shutter opens at the frame's own time and stays open for
`shutter_angle / 360` of a frame (180 = half a frame, the film default; 360 = the whole frame). Subframe
k is rendered at the middle of its slice of that interval. The game clock steps between the subframes
and closes the frame with the rest of the step, so every frame still advances the clock by exactly one
step, and the subframe times are whole nanoseconds computed from the frame number alone: the same
request gives the same hashes, and frame 100 has the same subframe times whether the job started at
frame 0 or not. A camera cut applies before the first subframe of its frame.

Everything that moves with the game clock blurs: transforms changed in `Update`, camera paths and shot
sequences, particles (the VFX step is each subframe's delta), physics bodies (interpolated poses). Things
moved only in `FixedUpdate` without interpolation step at the fixed rate and blur only when the fixed rate
is above the frame rate. The supersample blocks of all subframes are summed and quantized once, so
`supersample: 2, subframes: 8` is a 32-sample average per pixel. Cost: N full renders per delivered frame.
`subframes: 1` (the default) is the classic frame, byte for byte.

How many subframes: an edge moving S pixels per frame is smeared over `S · shutter_angle / 360` pixels and drawn as N
copies along that streak. Too few subframes show as separate steps instead of a smooth smear (16 subframes over an
80-pixel streak leave visible 5-pixel steps), so pick N near the streak length in pixels of the fastest thing you care
about, and add supersampling for the rest. A slow pan needs few; fast debris close to the camera needs many.

## 16-bit frames (`bit_depth: 16`)

With `bit_depth: 16` the frame is rendered into a half-float target instead of an 8-bit one; the post
stack keeps its tonemapped image in half floats too, so nothing is quantized to 8 bits before the file.
The frames are 16-bit RGBA PNGs (sRGB-encoded like the 8-bit ones). A half float holds 11 significant
bits, so a smooth sky or mist gradient has at least 8 distinct levels between two 8-bit codes instead of
one hard step; a 10-bit video master made from them keeps the extra depth. Limits: PNG only (the movie
formats take 8-bit frames), `calibration: "neutral"`, and no HUD (the UI overlay draws 8-bit; an app
with a HUD needs `hud: false`). On the SMAA tiers (Mobile High and the Deck's non-temporal fallback) the
SMAA pass blends in 8 bits, so the file has 8-bit precision there; the TAA, TSR and FXAA tiers are deep
end to end. The frame hash is FNV-1a over the 16-bit values as little-endian bytes.

The manifest and the echoed `request` carry `subframes`, `shutter_angle` and `bit_depth`.

## Slow motion and speed ramps (`time_map`)

The output timeline never changes: frame `i` is `i / fps` seconds into the video. `time_map` changes how
much *game* time each frame covers. It is a list of keys `{ "frame": F, "scale": S, "ease": E }` (frames
are the job's delivered frames, 0-based; `scale` 0..=100, 1 = real time, 0.25 = quarter speed, 0 = a
frozen frame; at most 4096 keys). Before the first key and after the last the scale holds. Between two
keys it ramps into the later key's scale with that key's `ease`: `smooth` (the default, smoothstep, so the
speed eases out of and into each key), `linear`, or `hold` (the earlier scale up to the key's frame, then
a jump). Frame `j` covers `round(step · scale(j + 0.5))` nanoseconds of game time (the scale at the
frame's middle), and frame `i` is at the sum of the steps before it. Warm-up and settle frames use the
scale before the first key. Everything is whole nanoseconds computed from the request, so the same
request gives the same game times and the same hashes. No `time_map` (or a map of ones) is the plain
timeline, byte for byte.

```json
{"method": "render.out_start", "params": {"out": "/tmp/kill_cam", "frames": 180, "fps": 60, "hud": false,
  "time_map": [{"frame": 30, "scale": 1}, {"frame": 60, "scale": 0.2}, {"frame": 120, "scale": 0.2}, {"frame": 150, "scale": 1}]}}
```

That is real time for half a second, a smooth half-second ramp down to one fifth speed, one second of slow
motion, and a ramp back. The echoed `request.time_map` lists the keys as parsed.

**Two clocks.** A job with a `time_map` runs two clocks:

| Clock | Step per frame | Read through | Who runs on it | Reported as |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| render | `step` (1 / fps), always | `Time::delta`, `Time::elapsed`, `RealTime` | VFX, shot players and `render.sequence`, HUD and UI animation, the material clock, `Update` systems, the shutter and TAA | `game_time_s`, `frame_times[].game_time_*` |
| simulation | `round(step · scale)` | `Time::sim_delta`, `Time::sim_elapsed`, `FixedUpdate`'s `Time` | the fixed loop (physics, gameplay), sim bridges (`read_snapshot`), replays | `sim_time_s`, `frame_times[].sim_time_*`, `sim_step_ns` |

The job drives the render clock exactly as without a map and sets the simulation clock through the
`regia_app::SimStep` resource each frame (it puts back a host's own one at the end). It never uses
`Time::time_scale`. At 0.25 a burst of particles plays at its normal speed while the ship that fired it
moves at a quarter.

- **It is not motion blur.** `subframes` and `shutter_angle` still sample inside each frame on the
  render clock; the simulation moves by the same share of the frame's simulation step between
  subframes, so in simulation time the blur shortens, as with a high-speed camera. The two parameters
  combine freely.
- **The simulation keeps its fixed rate.** A slowed frame runs fewer fixed steps (`FixedUpdate`), never a
  shorter one, so the game's results do not depend on the render's speed; what moves between fixed steps
  is presentation that interpolates (physics poses, `FixedTime::overstep_fraction`, a blending replay).
  A fast stretch can need more fixed steps per frame than the host's `max_substeps`: the job raises it for
  its own length and puts it back afterwards; above 64 the request is refused.
- **Replays follow the simulation clock.** `replay.play { from_tick, speed, start: "render_out" }` starts
  the replay on frame 0 at `from_tick`, so frame `i` shows tick `from_tick + tick_rate · speed ·
  sim_time(i)`: the replay's `speed` and the map multiply. Poses are blended between ticks for
  presentation only ([replay](book/agents/replay.md#replayplay)).
- **Gameplay in `Update`.** A system that moves gameplay in `Update` with `Time::delta` stays at render
  speed under a map. Move it to `FixedUpdate`, or read `Time::sim_delta`.

## AOVs: depth, ids and motion vectors (`aovs`, `aov_format`)

`aovs` writes control inputs for video tools (enhancement, relighting, rotoscoping) next to each
delivered frame: `<name>_depth_000000.exr`, `<name>_id_000000.exr`, `<name>_motion_000000.exr`
(`.raw` with `aov_format: "raw"`). They are drawn by their own pass, not read out of the frame
renderer: the frame's meshes and the terrain are drawn once more through the job's camera, with no
TAA jitter, one sample at each delivered pixel center (no supersampling: an id cannot be averaged),
at the middle subframe of a motion-blurred frame (`subframes / 2`). The HUD is never in an AOV.

| AOV | Channels (EXR names) | Type | Encoding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `depth` | `Z` | `f32` | Linear view depth in meters: the distance from the camera plane along the view direction (not the distance to the eye). Sky: `+inf`. |
| `id` | `id.instance`, `id.class` | `u32` | `instance`: one id per entity drawn (the terrain counts as one). An entity keeps its id for the whole job, through moves, LOD swaps, and leaving and coming back into view. New ids of a frame are numbered in a fixed order (the terrain first, then entities by their `Entity` bits), so the same project and request give the same ids. `class`: one id per mesh asset (every instance of one mesh shares it; the terrain has its own). Sky: 0. |
| `motion` | `motion.u`, `motion.v` | `f32` | Backward motion in delivered pixels, `+u` right, `+v` down: where the surface under the pixel was in the previous delivered frame, minus where it is now (the engine's TAA convention). The motion is between delivered frames, not between subframes. The sky gets the camera's rotation. 0 on frame 0 and on every `cuts` frame, and exactly 0 wherever the surface and the camera are bit-identical to the previous delivered frame (a held world, ADR-1965: no rounding noise from projecting one position twice). |

EXR files are single-layer scanline OpenEXR with ZIP compression (lossless), written by the
pure-Rust `exr` crate; `f32` and `u32` channels are stored as they are, never as half floats. Raw
files have no header: the channels interleaved per pixel in the order above, little-endian 32-bit,
rows top to bottom. A frame is written whole: a frame counts as `written` only when its image and
each of its AOV files are on disk, and a failed write removes all of that frame's files.

The manifest's `aov` block records everything a tool needs:

- `encodings`: format, size, sampling, file pattern, per AOV its channels, type, unit, meaning and
  background value, and for `raw` the byte order, layout and bytes per file.
- `ids`: the id tables, `instances: [{id, kind: "entity" | "terrain", entity_bits?, label}]` and
  `classes: [{id, label}]`.
- `motion_reset_frames`: the frames whose motion is 0 (frame 0 and the cuts).
- `frame_hashes`: per AOV, the FNV-1a hash of each frame's raw bytes (the same for `exr` and
  `raw`), so two runs can be compared without the files.
- `input_hashes`: per frame, the FNV-1a hash of everything the AOV pass uploaded (camera, last frame's
  camera, every instance's matrix, last matrix, ids and held flag; ADR-1965). Two jobs with equal
  `input_hashes` and unequal `frame_hashes` differ on the GPU; unequal `input_hashes` mean the world
  or the camera differed.
- `terrain`: `{ drawn, sample_stride }` when a terrain was drawn.

The manifest's `files.aov` lists the files: `[{ aov, files: [...] }]` per AOV in request order,
frame `i` at index `i`, the same index as `files.frames` and `frame_times`. AOV frame `i` is
delivered frame `i`, so its render and simulation times are `frame_times[i]`. Under a `time_map`
(ADR-1524) the motion AOV covers one delivered frame on each clock: the camera, shots and VFX move
by the render step, simulated motion (physics, gameplay in `FixedUpdate` or on `Time::sim_delta`,
replays) by the frame's simulation step, so at scale 0.5 a simulated object's motion vectors are
half as long (ADR-1554).

## Material AOVs: normal, roughness, metalness, base_color, material_id

`aovs` also takes six material AOVs (ADR-3256), written in the same frame sequence and under the same
naming scheme as the others (`<name>_normal_000000.exr`, `<name>_roughness_000000.png`, ...), sorted
into the request after `depth`, `id` and `motion`. They come from a material pass that draws the same
list of meshes and the terrain as the id pass, with the same camera, no jitter, one sample at each
delivered pixel center, and does not depend on the quality tier, TAA or the upscaler. Every material
AOV is 0 on the sky.

| AOV | Channels (EXR names) | Type | Encoding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `normal` | `normal.x`, `normal.y`, `normal.z` | `f32` | Unit surface normal in world space: the vertex normal carried through the entity's normal matrix (inverse transpose of the model's upper 3×3), interpolated, renormalized and flipped toward the camera on a back face. The terrain's normal comes from its heightfield. |
| `normal_view` | `normal_view.x`, `.y`, `.z` | `f32` | The same normal rotated into view space: `+x` right, `+y` up, the camera looks down `-z`. |
| `roughness` | `roughness` | `f32` | Perceptual roughness: the material's factor, times the green channel of a packed ORM map (`orm_packed`), clamped to 0..1. The terrain is 1. |
| `metalness` | `metalness` | `f32` | The material's factor, times the blue channel of a packed ORM map, clamped to 0..1. The terrain is 0. |
| `base_color` | `base_color.r`, `.g`, `.b` | `f32` | Linear albedo before lighting: the factor times the sRGB-decoded base-color texture. Vertex color is not applied. The terrain is a neutral 0.5 grey. |
| `material_id` | `material_id` | `u32` | One id per material asset drawn (the terrain has its own), assigned the first time it is seen in the frame's sorted draw order and kept for the whole job. The manifest's `aov.ids.materials` is `[{ id, label }]`. |

`aov_format` `"png"` (8-bit) and `"png16"` (16-bit) write `normal`, `normal_view`, `roughness`,
`metalness` and `base_color` as PNG (grayscale for one channel, RGB for three): normals as
`n * 0.5 + 0.5` (the sky stays 0), `base_color` sRGB-encoded, roughness and metalness as they are.
`depth`, `id`, `motion` and `material_id` need exact values and are refused with
`aov_format_unsupported`; use `exr` or `raw` for them. With `png` or `png16` every AOV of the job must be one of the five.

The pass reads a material's factors, base-color texture, packed ORM map and alpha-mask cutoff. It
does not read normal maps, material graphs, shared or dynamic image slots, vertex color, the
deformation of a skinned mesh's normal (the rest-pose normal is used) or morph targets; a
translucent material is not drawn, as in every AOV. The same job run twice writes byte-identical
files, and the manifest's `aov.frame_hashes` has a hash per material AOV. A `.render_job.ron`
takes the same names in its `output.aovs` (and `aov_format`); no field was added, so the job format
stays at version 2. The CLI path is `regia render --job` with such a job; there is no per-AOV flag.

A shot fade ([camera paths](book/agents/camera-paths.md), ADR-1522) is drawn by the compositor after the UI, on
8-bit display frames only, and never in an AOV: depth, ids and motion are the same with and without
a fade. Scene-linear (`exr`) and 16-bit frames are taken before the compositor and carry no fade.
The manifest's `fade` block, `{ in_frames, in_aovs: false, frames: [{ frame, amount, color }] }`,
lists the frames a fade was visible on, so a tool can apply it to a plate that does not carry it.

```json
{"method": "render.out_start", "params": {"out": "/tmp/plate", "frames": 96, "fps": 24, "format": "exr", "hud": false, "aovs": ["depth", "id", "motion"], "settle_frames": 16, "warmup_frames": 16}}
```

Known issues (AOV pass, ADR-1521):

- Alpha-masked materials (foliage cards) are tested against their cutoff with the base-colour
  texture's alpha, so a card has the shape of its leaves. The test samples the full-resolution
  texture without mipmaps, so far-away cards can shimmer between frames. A material graph's own
  alpha is not evaluated (its base-colour texture slot is used when there is one).
- Translucent materials (blend, premultiplied glass, additive), particles, water and decals have no
  AOV; the pixel shows what is behind.
- The terrain is a grid of its heightfield (at most 2048 samples per side; a larger map is drawn
  every `sample_stride`-th sample), built once per job: terrain holes and terrain edits during a
  job are not in the AOVs, and its depth can differ from the rendered terrain by its LOD.
- Skinned meshes are skinned on the CPU with the frame's four strongest influences; morph targets
  are ignored.

## Scene-linear EXR frames (`format: "exr"`)

`format: "exr"` writes each frame as `<name>_000000.exr` with `R`, `G`, `B` channels in `f32`:
the post stack's input, after TAA or the upscaler and before exposure, bloom, the tonemap and the
display encoding, in the frame's photometric units (cd/m², Rec. 709 primaries). A supersampled
frame is box-averaged in linear light; subframes are averaged. The manifest's `color` block names
the space and unit. Limits: `bit_depth` 8 (the default), `calibration: "neutral"`, and no HUD (an
app with a HUD needs `hud: false`). A view without the post stack has no scene-linear frame: the
job fails on its first frame with an error that says so. The frame hash is FNV-1a over the `f32`
values as little-endian bytes. Exposure is not applied: the EV each frame was shown at is in
`render.exposure_log`.

## Frame files, speed and `raw` (`format`, `png_compression`, `writers`)

Frame files (`format: "png"` or `"raw"`) are encoded and written by a pool of worker threads, not by
the thread that renders. The render thread renders, hashes and hands the frame over; it waits only when
the queue is full (back-pressure), so memory stays flat: at most `writers` frames wait and `writers`
more are being written. `writers` is 0..=16; 0 (the default) is automatic: half the cores, at most 8.
A file appears under its final name only when it is complete (it is written to `<file>.part` and
renamed). Progress reports `frame` (handed over) and `written` (the unbroken run on disk from frame 0).

- **`png_compression`**: `"fast"` (the default), `"balanced"` or `"best"`. Fast deflate is several times
  quicker than best and the files are somewhat larger; best is the smallest file the encoder makes.
  The level never changes the pixels or the hash.
- **`format: "raw"`**: no compression at all. One file per frame, `<name>_000000.raw`: tightly packed
  RGBA, rows top to bottom, no header. 8-bit frames are one byte per channel; with `bit_depth: 16` each
  channel is a 16-bit little-endian code. The manifest has a `raw` block with `pixel_format`
  (`rgba8` or `rgba16`), `width`, `height`, `channels` (4), `channel_order`, `bit_depth`, `byte_order`
  (`little` for 16-bit), `row_stride_bytes`, `frame_bytes` and `file_pattern`, so an external encoder
  can read the files without guessing. Alpha is always 255.
- **The hash does not depend on any of this.** It is FNV-1a over the delivered RGBA values before any
  encoding, so PNG at every level, raw, and any number of writers give the same hashes and the same
  decoded pixels (`crates/regia_agent/tests/render_out_frames.rs`).
- **Cancel and failure guarantee.** Every frame handed over before a cancel is written: after a cancel
  the files are exactly frames 0 to `frame - 1`, in order, none missing, none after, no `.part` file.
  If a write fails (disk full), the job fails and keeps only the unbroken run from frame 0 (a later
  file that finished first is removed); `frame`, `files` and the manifest's `frame_hashes` all stop at
  that run.
- **No GPL tool is required.** Only the `ffv1`, `prores` and `dnxhr` formats pipe to an `ffmpeg` found
  on `PATH`, and they are optional; the default needs nothing. A deliverable can be made from the PNG or
  raw frames with any external encoder whose licence you are happy with: read the PNG sequence, or read
  the raw files with the layout from the manifest.

## Rules

- Wait for loading to finish before starting (`assets.load_progress`); asynchronous builds that finish
  on different frames on different machines change early frames. Use `warmup_frames` for effects.
- `play.pause`, `play.resume`, `play.step` and `play.set_time_scale` are refused during a job (`F0018`):
  the job holds the clock, every frame, and a running step refuses the start (`F0009`).
- Pointer hover state does not reach the HUD during a job (open item from the ADR-202 audit).

Workflow and the HUD layouts from the game side: [Rendering a video](book/user-guide/render-out.md).

## Render jobs

To render takes of a shot list or a sequence (folders per take, an automatic cut list, a job file
that `regia render --job` runs headless), see [render jobs](book/agents/render-jobs.md) (`render.out_job`,
ADR-1616).

## WebM movies without ffmpeg (`format: "webm"`)

`format: "webm"` (alias `"av1"`) encodes the frames to AV1 and the audio mixdown to Opus in one
`<name>.webm`, in-process, with no external program (ADR-3369). It needs a build with the `media-encode`
feature (`regia/media-encode`); without it the job is refused with `data.reason`
`media_encode_unavailable`. The optional `encode` block sets `quality` or `bitrate_kbps`, `speed`,
`keyframe_interval`, `audio_kbps` and `threads`; `threads: 1` makes the file byte-identical run to run.
The picture must be even-sized, 16..=8192 pixels a side; the mixdown must be at a rate Opus takes
(48 kHz, the default). A cancelled job leaves a playable movie of every delivered frame. Settings, limits
and error codes: [Video encoding](book/agents/video-encode.md).

# Camera paths and shot sequences (agents)

A shot sequence is a camera move written as data: where the camera is, where it looks, its field of
view and depth of field, the cuts between shots and the fades at their edges. The same data plays in
a game, renders frame-exact for a video, and is what a person edits by hand (or, later, in an editor
panel). Guide topic: `agent.guide {"topic": "camera_paths"}`. Format: `docs/formats/shots-ron.md`.

Everything is a pure function of a time value. Seeking to 3.5 s gives the same pose on every machine
and every frame rate; there is no wall clock in it. Playing advances the clock by the game's time
step, so `play.pause`, `play.step` and the time scale all apply.

## The model

- A **sequence** is shots played back to back. Each **shot** has its own clock starting at zero.
- The boundary between two shots is a hard **cut**. A time exactly on a boundary belongs to the shot
  that starts there. The end of the sequence holds the last frame.
- A shot has a **path** (position keys with `Linear`, `Step` or `CatmullRom` interpolation), a
  **look-at** rule (`Heading` = along the direction of travel, `Point`, or a moving `Track`), and
  tracks for **fov** (degrees), **roll** (degrees) and optional **dof** (focus distance, aperture,
  `focus_on_target`, `bokeh`). `fade_in` and `fade_out` are seconds at the shot's edges.
- A shot may key its **rotation** (v2): `[{time, rotation: [x, y, z, w], ease?}]`, a unit quaternion
  per key, interpolated by spherical interpolation along the shortest arc (`Smooth` smoothsteps the
  parameter, `Step` holds). Keyed rotation replaces the look-at rule for the camera's orientation;
  `roll` still applies, and `look_at` still gives the sample's `target` (and the `focus_on_target`
  distance). Without keys the orientation comes from `look_at` as before.
- A **path** or `Track` **look-at** key may sit past its shot's end (v3, ADR-8640): a shortened
  Catmull-Rom shot keeps its tail keys as control keys, so the curve before the cut is unchanged; the
  shot's clock never reaches them. A v2 file loads as v3 (`regia upgrade-project` rewrites only the
  number); a build that reads v2 refuses a v3 file with `shot sequence version 3 is newer than
  supported version 2; upgrade the engine`.
- The **fade** is drawn: the compositor's `fade` layer blends `fade_color` over the finished frame, above
  the UI. It shows in windows, in `seeing.screenshot` with `window_layers: true`, in screenshots taken
  while a fade is visible, and in `render.out_start` frames, so a render-out fades like the preview.
- Every shot change, seek into another shot and loop wrap is counted as a camera cut and the renderer
  drops its temporal history ([camera cuts](book/agents/camera-cuts.md)), so no frame blends the old shot into the new.

## Methods

- `render.sequence { action?, ... }` runs the player. `action` is one of:
  - `load` with `ron` (the `.shots.ron` text) or `sequence` (the same data as JSON; enums are
    externally tagged: `"Heading"`, `{"Point": [0, 1, 0]}`). Also `play`, `loop`, `camera`.
  - `seek` with `time` (seconds) or `frame` (at the sequence's `fps`).
  - `sample` with `time` or `frame`: the pose at any instant without moving the clock.
  - `play` (optional `time`/`frame` to start from, `loop`, `camera`), `pause`, `stop` (back to zero).
  - `export`: the canonical RON, which loads back to the same sequence.
  - `query` (the default): the outline, the clock, the cut count and the current sample.
  - `clear`: unload.
- `camera.set_path { path, shot?, ... }` authors one shot. With `shot` it replaces that shot's path
  in the loaded sequence (the clock and play state stay); without it, it creates a one-shot sequence
  named `name` (default `adhoc`) and loads it. Optional `duration`, `fov`, `roll`, `rotation` (`null` clears the
  keys), `dof` (`null` removes it), `fade_in`, `fade_out`, `camera`, `play`. `preview: n` (0 to 64) returns `n` evenly spaced samples
  (eye, target, field of view) so a move can be checked without playing it, and `dry_run: true`
  validates and previews without applying. Everything is validated; an error names the shot and field. Without `duration` the new shot lasts
  until its last key (give `duration` when that key is at time zero). The reply has `shot`, `index`,
  `created`, `applied`, `duration`, `keys`, `preview` and, when applied, `state`.
  Errors: `INVALID_PARAMS` for a bad field or a path that fails validation; `NOT_FOUND` for a `shot`
  that is not in the loaded sequence (the hint lists the shot names) or when `shot` is given and no
  sequence is loaded.
- `camera.raycast { u, v | x, y, ... }` turns a point of the camera's image into a ray and casts it
  like [`world.pick`](book/agents/world-pick.md): `hit` (`entity`, `point`, `normal`, `distance`, `layer`) or, with
  `all_layers`, `hits`. `x`/`y` are pixels from the top-left corner (a pixel centre is at +0.5),
  `u`/`v` the same point as fractions; the image size is `width`/`height` or the primary window.
  `entity` names a camera (default: the `Camera` with the highest `order`); `ray_only` skips the cast.
  It uses the camera's pose, field of view or orthographic size. CPU only, no window needed.

Every `render.sequence` reply has `action`, `state` (`loaded`, `playing`, `time`, `cuts`,
`camera`, and the outline and current sample once loaded) and `fade_layer` (`installed`: the fade layer
has been added to the window overlay, which happens the first frame a sequence shows a fade; `amount` and
`color`: what it draws; it follows the sample from the next frame); `sample` adds `sample` and `export` adds
`ron`. `seek`, `sample` and `play` before anything is loaded fail with `NOT_FOUND`. `time` and
`frame` together are `INVALID_PARAMS`. A sample has `time`, `shot`, `shot_name`, `local_time`, `eye`,
`target`, `up`, `rotation`, `roll_degrees`, `fov_y_degrees`, `dof`, `fade`, `fade_color` and
`finished`.

`camera.raycast` returns `camera`, `origin`, `direction` and `screen` (`x`, `y`, `u`, `v`, `width`,
`height`, `aspect`) plus the pick result unless `ray_only`. It fails with `NOT_FOUND` when no `Camera`
exists or `entity` has none.

`render.sequence` and `camera.set_path` need the `edit_scene` permission (they move the camera);
`camera.raycast` is read-only.

```json
{"method": "camera.set_path", "params": {
  "path": {"interp": "CatmullRom",
           "keys": [{"time": 0, "position": [0, 2, 12]}, {"time": 2, "position": [4, 2, 7]}, {"time": 4, "position": [6, 2, 3]}],
           "look_at": {"Point": [0, 1.5, 0]}},
  "fov": [{"time": 0, "value": 40}, {"time": 4, "value": 28, "ease": "Smooth"}],
  "fade_in": 0.5, "preview": 5}}
{"method": "render.sequence", "params": {"action": "seek", "time": 2.0}}
{"method": "seeing.screenshot", "params": {}}
{"method": "camera.raycast", "params": {"u": 0.5, "v": 0.5}}
```

More calls, one per method and action:

```json
{"method": "render.sequence", "params": {"action": "load", "ron": "(version: 1, shots: [ ... ])", "loop": true, "play": true}}
{"method": "render.sequence", "params": {"action": "sample", "frame": 45}}
{"method": "render.sequence", "params": {"action": "export"}}
{"method": "camera.set_path", "params": {"shot": "b", "path": {"keys": [{"time": 0, "position": [0, 5, 0]}, {"time": 3, "position": [0, 5, 6]}]}, "dry_run": true, "preview": 3}}
{"method": "camera.raycast", "params": {"x": 960, "y": 540, "width": 1920, "height": 1080, "entity": 8589934592, "all_layers": true}}
```

## Errors

| Call | Condition | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `render.sequence` | `play`, `seek`, `sample`, `export` with no sequence loaded | `NOT_FOUND` |
| `render.sequence` | unknown `action`; `time` and `frame` together; negative or non-numeric `time`/`frame`; a sequence that fails validation (duplicate or empty shot names, `fps` outside (0, 1000], fades longer than the shot, keys before time zero or not increasing, keys past the shot's end on any track but the camera path and look-at (those are control keys, ADR-8640), a zero or non-finite rotation quaternion, values outside the track limits, unknown `version`); `ron` and `sequence` together, or `load` with neither; more than 256 shots or more than 4096 keys on one track | `INVALID_PARAMS` |
| `camera.set_path` | `shot` names no shot of the loaded sequence, or there is no sequence | `NOT_FOUND` |
| `camera.set_path` | missing or invalid `path`, `duration` not greater than zero (or the last key is at time zero with no `duration`), `preview` above 64, a track out of range or with more than 4096 keys | `INVALID_PARAMS` |
| `camera.raycast` | no `Camera` in the app, `entity` is not a camera | `NOT_FOUND` |
| `camera.raycast` | no point, a point outside the image (`u`/`v` outside 0..=1; the edges are inside), only one of `width`/`height`, a non-positive `aspect` | `INVALID_PARAMS` |

A rejected call changes nothing: the loaded sequence, the clock and the cut count are as before.
`seek` to the same time twice, replacing a shot with the same path twice, `pause`, `stop` and `clear`
are idempotent. `sample`, `export`, `camera.raycast` and a `dry_run` never change the player.

## Typical loop

1. Write the move: `camera.set_path` with `preview`, or `render.sequence {action: "load", ron: ...}`
   for several shots.
2. Check it without playing: `render.sequence {action: "sample", time}` at the keys, at each side of a
   cut and inside the fades.
3. Look at it: `render.sequence {action: "seek", time}`, then `seeing.screenshot` on a later call (a
   call lands at a frame boundary and the camera moves later in that frame). Screenshots of a seek
   are frame-exact; nothing needs stepping.
4. Verify what is in frame: `camera.raycast` at the image centre or at a thing that must be visible.
5. Keep it: `render.sequence {action: "export"}` returns the canonical text to save as `*.shots.ron`.
6. For motion: `render.sequence {action: "play"}`, then `play.step` for fixed steps.

## Notes

- For the file format, the game-side API and what is not included yet, see
  [Camera shot sequences](book/user-guide/shot-sequences.md).

- Depth of field needs a quality profile that allows it. The sequence sets the camera's
  `PhysicalCamera` focus distance, aperture and mode, and turns its motion blur off when it creates
  the component; an existing `PhysicalCamera` keeps its other settings.
- The fade is drawn when a `WindowOverlay` exists: the compositor blends `fade_color` over the
  finished frame, above the UI. With no overlay nothing is drawn, and the fade stays on the sample
  (`fade`, `fade_color`).
- Do not put a `CameraRig` on the camera a sequence drives: the rig would overwrite the pose.
- Paths kilometres from the world origin pan smoothly (ADR-1488): the renderer keeps the view
  direction to `f32` precision, and `Heading` shots take their direction of travel in `f64`. To
  check a slow pan for ticks, compare frame-to-frame image shifts of a distant region: the shift
  should change smoothly, not jump by a pixel at a fixed period. A camera's roll does not reach
  the image yet (main views render with +Y up).
- Game code uses the same player:

```rust,wrap
# use regia::prelude::*;
# use regia_core::math::{Vec3, Quat};
# use regia_scene::Transform;
# let mut commands: Commands = todo!();
# let world: &mut World = todo!();
# let app: &mut App = todo!();
# let frame: u64 = 0;
use regia_framework::shots::{ShotPlayer, ShotPlugin, ShotSequence};

app.add_plugins(ShotPlugin); // AgentPlugin adds it too
let sequence = ShotSequence::from_ron(&std::fs::read_to_string("intro.shots.ron")?)?;
app.world_mut().resource_mut::<ShotPlayer>().load(sequence.clone());
app.world_mut().resource_mut::<ShotPlayer>().play();
// Or sample by hand, e.g. per rendered video frame:
let pose = sequence.sample_frame(frame); // Option<ShotSample>: eye, target, rotation, fov_y_degrees, dof, fade
```

### More `camera.raycast` parameters

The schema (`agent.schema`) also lists these optional parameters:

- `max_distance` (number): Ray length cap, metres (world.pick filter).
- `layers` (array): Accepted MapLayer ids (world.pick filter).
- `cull` (string): "none" or "back" (world.pick filter).
- `terrain` (boolean): Cast against terrain (default true).
- `meshes` (boolean): Cast against meshes (default true).
- `include_hidden` (boolean): Also test hidden entities.
- `skip` (array): Entity ids to ignore.

# UI themes (agents)

A UI theme is a `.theme.ron` file of design tokens: colors, spacing, radius, type scale, sizes, elevation and
motion, plus per-widget looks. A theme can extend another, so a game re-skins the default by listing only what
changes. Format: `docs/formats/theme-ron.md`. Design: `docs/specs/ui-default-design.md`.

Built-in themes: `regia-dark` (default), `regia-light`, `regia-high-contrast`, `regia-light-high-contrast`
(`crates/regia_ui/assets/themes/`). Games put theme files in `assets/ui/themes/`; `UiPlugin` loads them at
startup (parents before children). `regia upgrade-project --write` rewrites old `UiTheme`-shaped `.theme.ron`
files as v1.

## Methods

Every method goes through the runtime UI's agent hook (`UiAgentHost`, the same one as [ui](book/agents/ui.md)), so an app
without `regia_ui` answers `ui_not_installed`. Reads need `read`; `ui.theme_set`, `ui.theme_select` and
`ui.theme_reload` need `edit_scene`; `ui.theme_set { persist: true }` also needs `assets` (it writes a file).
Writes land on the **next frame** as one theme generation, with the colors cross-fading over `motion.base` (instant
with reduced motion). Wait for them with `wait_until` (below).

When `theme` is omitted, a method uses the theme the UI resolves against (after the high-contrast and fallback
rules), as `ui.theme_list` reports in `resolved`.

### `ui.theme_list`

No parameters. Returns every loaded theme `{ name, extends, scheme, density, path, builtin, error }` (`path` is the
file it came from, `error` the last load error `{ key, message }`), then `active` (the selected name), `resolved`,
`density`, `high_contrast`, `reduced_motion`, `generation`, `error` (why the selected theme could not be resolved),
`files` (every watched file `{ path, theme, loads, error }`, including files that never loaded) and `watching`.
`slots` lists the named token slots widgets read (see "Token slots" below) as `{ key, kind, used_by, fallback,
value }`, `value` being the resolved theme's value or null when it leaves the slot to the engine fallback.

### `ui.theme_get`

| Param | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `theme` | string | Theme name. |
| `keys` | string or list | Globs over token keys (`*` any run, `?` one character), e.g. `"color.*"`. Default: every token. |
| `resolved` | bool | Include resolved values (default `true`). |
| `type` | string | A widget type or variation, e.g. `"Button.primary"`. |
| `state` | string or list | With `type`: `normal`, `hovered`, `pressed`, `focused`, `disabled`, `selected`, `error`, `touch`. |
| `size` | string | With `type`: `sm`, `md` (default), `lg`. |
| `density` | string | `comfortable` or `compact` (default: the active density). |

Returns `{ name, extends, format_version, scheme, density, chain, tokens, rules, types?, resolved? }`. `rules` lists
the chain's style rules (`.theme.ron` v2), root theme first, as `{ selector, specificity, state, props }`: `selector`
is display text that is never parsed back (`Toolbar Button`, `[danger-zone] :hover`, `Button.primary
:focus_visible`), `specificity` the `[variation + classes, widget + inside]` pair the resolver sorts by, `state` the
rule's state or null, `props` the raw properties. Each token is
`{ raw, from, density?, value }`: the expression as written (`"lighten(@color.accent, 0.06)"`), the theme in the chain
that defines it (`density` when a density overlay does), and the resolved value (colors as `#rrggbb[aa]`, durations
as `"80ms"`, easings as written). With `type`, `types` holds the authored definitions of the type's variation chain
root first, and `resolved` is `{ type, chain, state, size, props }`: the look the resolver gives a node of that
type in that state (background, border, radius, text color, focus ring, opacity, height, padding_x, `padding`
as `{ left, top, right, bottom }`, `min_width`, `min_height`, `max_width`, `max_height`, translate, scale, ...),
computed by the same resolver the live UI uses.

### `ui.theme_set`

| Param | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `theme` | string | Theme to change. |
| `tokens` | object | Token key to a number or a string expression; `null` removes the key so the parent's value applies. |
| `types` | object | Type name to `{ extends?, props?, hover?, pressed?, focused?, focus_visible?, disabled?, selected?, error?, sizes? }`; each layer merges per property (`null` removes a property, a `null` type removes the type). `focus_visible` (v2) applies over `focused` only for keyboard or gamepad focus. |
| `variations` | object | Variation name (`"Button.primary"`) to the same shape. |
| `reset` | bool | Start from the theme's original (its last good file, or the built-in) before the edits. |
| `persist` | bool | Also write the theme's `.theme.ron` (needs `assets`). |

The whole theme chain is checked before anything changes: a bad value fails with `ui_theme_invalid` and the key
path at the start of the message (`tokens.color.accent-hover: unknown reference ...`), and the live theme is
untouched. On success it returns `{ theme, changed, warnings, generation, applies_at_generation, persisted }`:
`changed` lists key paths (`tokens.color.accent`, `types.Button`), `warnings` the lint findings of the new theme
(same shape as `ui.theme_lint`), and `applies_at_generation` the generation that shows the change (equal to
`generation` when nothing changed). `persist` writes the file atomically (temporary file, then rename) through the
same serializer the format uses, so it reloads to the same theme; comments in the file are not kept. Only themes
loaded from a file can be persisted; built-ins are engine assets.

### `ui.theme_select`

| Param | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `theme` | string, required | Theme to select. |
| `density` | string or null | `comfortable`, `compact`, or `null` to follow `UiDensity` and the theme. |
| `high_contrast` | bool | Use `<theme>-high-contrast` when loaded, else `regia-high-contrast`. |
| `reduced_motion` | bool | Swap at once instead of cross-fading. |

Returns `{ previous, selected, generation, applies_at_generation }`; `previous` and `selected` are
`{ theme, density, high_contrast, reduced_motion }`.

### `ui.theme_preview`

| Param | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `theme` | string | Theme to show. |
| `tokens`, `types`, `variations` | object | Overrides for the preview only, same shape as `ui.theme_set`. |
| `page` | string | `"theme-sheet"` (default), an `assets://` path or a file path of a `.ui.ron`. |
| `size` | `[w, h]` | Pixels, 1 to 4096 each (default `[1280, 720]`). |
| `scheme` | string | `dark` or `light`: shows the theme's `-dark`/`-light` sibling, else the built-in of that scheme. |
| `density` | string | `comfortable` or `compact`. |
| `device` | string | Safe-area profile for `SafeAreaPadding` roots: `desktop` (default, no inset), `tv` (5 % title-safe), `phone` (the portrait or landscape render-out profile). |

The preview runs in a separate headless UI app: the overrides are never applied to the live UI and the theme
generation does not move. The page is laid out for `size` through the render-out path (ADR-202), drawn into an
offscreen target and returned as `{ width, height, theme, page, scheme, density, device, generation, mime,
png_base64, path }`; `path` is the PNG written under the scratch output directory — the system
temp directory (`regia-theme-preview/`) on desktop, the app-private data directory on Android
(the system temp directory is not writable for an app there).

The theme sheet shows every button variation (`button`, `primary`, `danger`, `ghost`) in every state (normal,
hovered, pressed, focused, selected, disabled), toggles off and on, a slider, a progress bar, list rows (normal,
hovered, selected) and body text on surfaces.

### `ui.theme_lint`

`{ theme? }`. Returns `{ theme, scheme, density, clean, findings }`; each finding is `{ kind, key, message, pair?,
ratio?, required?, value? }` with `key` the key path at fault:

| `kind` | What |
|---|---|
| `contrast` | A text or boundary pair below its WCAG 2.x contrast ratio, in the theme's scheme. `pair` is `[foreground, background]`, `ratio` the measured ratio, `required` 4.5 (text) or 3 (boundaries, slider fill, focus ring). Pairs: text, muted text (also on the overlay surface in dark themes and the sunken one in light themes), on-accent on accent, on-danger on danger, accent, danger, warning, success and border-strong on surface, focus ring on background. Translucent colors are composited first. Disabled text is exempt (WCAG 1.4.3). |
| `unknown_reference` | A reference no theme in the chain defines. |
| `reference_cycle` | References that loop. |
| `unreachable_reference` | References cut off by a missing `extends` parent, or a variation whose base does not exist. |
| `unknown_key` | A token key or widget property the engine does not define (kept in the file). |
| `touch_target` | `size.control.md`, `size.control.lg`, `size.row` or an interactive type's `height` under `size.touch-min` (`required`), checked in the `comfortable` density only: `compact` is pointer-only. |

### `ui.theme_reload`

`{ theme? }`: re-reads the file a theme came from, or every theme file. Returns `{ reloaded: [{ theme, path,
changed }], failed: [{ theme, path, key, message }], skipped: [{ theme, reason }], generation,
applies_at_generation }`. A built-in or a theme set in code is `skipped` with reason `built_in` or `no_file`.

## Waiting for a change

`play.wait_until` and `play.expect` take `{ "predicate": "ui.theme_generation", "at_least": n }` (or `op` and
`value`, with `op` one of `gte` (default), `gt`, `eq`, `lt`, `lte`). Take `n` from `applies_at_generation`:

```json
{"method": "ui.theme_set", "params": {"tokens": {"color.accent": "#e8793a"}}}
{"method": "play.wait_until", "params": {"condition": {"predicate": "ui.theme_generation", "at_least": 7}}}
```

## Hot reload

In the editor and dev builds (`regia run --dev`, whenever the asset watcher runs), a saved `.theme.ron` that a
theme was loaded from is re-read within the watcher's look interval (every 30 frames by default): a good file swaps
in with a cross-fade, and every theme that extends it follows. A file that does not parse or resolve keeps the last
good theme, logs one warning with the key path, shows in the editor's watch status line and is reported by
`ui.theme_list` and `ui.theme_reload`. Shipping builds run no watcher and read themes once. Rust hosts and tests
control it through the `ThemeFiles` resource (`watch: Auto | On | Off`, `poll_frames`) and load extra files with
`regia_ui::theme_agent::load_theme_file`.

## Error reasons

Errors carry `data.reason`:

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `ui_not_installed` | The app has no runtime UI hooked to the agent. |
| `ui_bad_param` | A parameter has the wrong type or value (the message names it). |
| `ui_unknown_state` | `state` names no widget state. |
| `ui_theme_unknown` | No theme of that name is loaded (the hint lists the loaded ones). |
| `ui_theme_required` | `ui.theme_select` without `theme`. |
| `ui_theme_invalid` | The change would not load: the message starts with the key path; nothing was applied. |
| `ui_theme_type_unknown` | `ui.theme_get` `type` names no type or variation of the theme. |
| `ui_theme_resolve_failed` | The resolver could not run for `ui.theme_get` (a bug; report it). |
| `ui_theme_no_original` | `reset` on a theme that came from neither a file nor the built-ins. |
| `ui_theme_not_persistable` | `persist` on a theme without a file (built-ins, themes set in code). |
| `ui_theme_write_failed` | The file could not be written; nothing was applied. |
| `ui_theme_page_not_found` | `ui.theme_preview` `page` cannot be read. |
| `ui_theme_page_invalid` | The page is not a loadable `.ui.ron`. |
| `ui_theme_preview_no_gpu` | No GPU adapter for the offscreen preview (install lavapipe). |
| `ui_theme_preview_failed` | The offscreen readback failed. |
| `editor_headless` | `ui.theme_preview` on a host that opened no GPU on purpose (the headless editor's `--no-gpu`, or none found there): the host's own code, and no preview device is opened (ADR-5180). The other `ui.theme_*` methods still answer. |

A `persist` without the `assets` permission is the protocol's permission error (`F0012`).

## Re-skinning in a file

```ron
(
    format_version: 1,
    name: "my-game",
    extends: Some("regia-dark"),
    tokens: { "color.accent": "#e8793a", "color.on-accent": "#140a04", "radius.md": 3 },
)
```

Hover, pressed, selection and focus colors follow the accent because the parent derives them from it. A bad value
is reported as `theme "my-game": tokens.color.accent: ...` with the key path, and the previous theme stays active.
The same edit through the agent: `ui.theme_preview { tokens: { "color.accent": "#e8793a" } }` to look,
`ui.theme_lint` to check, then `ui.theme_set { theme: "my-game", tokens: {...}, persist: true }`.

## Runtime resolution (lane D6)

The running UI resolves every classed node from the active theme (ADR-289):

- `ActiveTheme` (resource) selects the theme by name, plus `density`, `high_contrast` and `reduced_motion`. A write
  swaps the theme next frame and cross-fades colors over `motion.base`. `ui.theme_select` writes it.
- A node's classes pick widget types and variations: `button` is `Button`, `primary` is `Button.primary`, `surface`
  is `Panel.surface`; a class may name a type directly (`"Button.ghost"`). For each property the first hit wins: the
  node's `ThemeOverride`, the matching style rules (most specific first), the variation chain nearest first, the
  type, the theme defaults. Disabled applies last at 0.45 opacity. A `.ui.ron` button widget puts its own `button`
  class first, so an authored `classes: ["primary"]` shows `Button.primary` (ADR-8303).
- Style rules (`.theme.ron` v2, ADR-8105 (e), ADR-8303) are structured selectors: `inside` (an ancestor's widget
  type, any depth), `widget`, `variation` (needs `widget`), `classes` (all of them) and `state`. They apply in
  ascending specificity `(variation + classes, widget + inside)`, then parent before child theme and file order.
  `ui.inspect` names a winning rule as `rule <selector>` and lists the node's matching rules under `theme.rules`;
  the UI designer's Style section shows the same list. Format: `docs/formats/theme-ron.md`.
- `focus_visible` layers (v2) show only while the focus came from the keyboard or a gamepad (`FocusRingPolicy`, by
  default `navigation_only`): Tab shows them, a click hides them and keeps the focus, in the running game and in the
  UI designer's live preview.
- `ThemeScope { theme }` on a node themes its subtree with another loaded theme.
- `ThemeResolver::stats()` reports the theme generation and how many nodes and styles were resolved last frame; an
  idle frame reports zero. `ui.theme_generation` reads the same generation.

## Motion (lane D8)

A widget type's `transition` names a duration and an easing, both usually tokens:
`"transition": ["@motion.fast", "@ease.standard"]`. The resolver animates the fill over that duration and shapes the
progress with the easing curve (`cubic-bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2)` as in CSS, or `linear`; an entry that is not an easing
means linear). A theme swap cross-fades every color over `motion.base` on a linear curve.

**Reduced motion.** `ActiveTheme { reduced_motion: true, .. }` makes state transitions (hover, press, focus, selected)
jump to their end value and a theme swap apply at once. Opacity fades, when a widget has them, cap at `motion.fast`
instead of being removed (`regia_ui::theme_motion::reduced_duration`). The pressed nudge (`translate: [0, 1]` in a
`pressed` layer) is a state change, so it is instant either way.

`regia_ui::theme_motion::sample(easing, t)` gives the eased progress for tests and tools; `exit_duration` is the
0.75 x rule for `ease.exit`. `Themed::anim_ease` holds the control points of the transition now running, so an agent
reading a node mid-fade can tell which curve drives it.

## Layout box and token slots (ADR-7208)

**Padding and min/max size.** A widget type, variation or `ThemeOverride` may set `padding` (one number for every
edge, two for vertical then horizontal, four for top, right, bottom, left as in CSS), `min_width`, `min_height`,
`max_width` and `max_height` (UI px). Unlike the other properties they reach layout: where the theme sets one, it
replaces the node's own `Style` value (padding mirrors in right-to-left layout like the style's own padding), and a
theme change relayouts only the nodes whose box moved. Where the theme sets none, the node's style is used as is.
**Height, inline padding and gap (ADR-9340).** A theme's own `height` (UI px) becomes the node's height,
`padding_x` its left and right padding (a full `padding` wins over it), and `gap` the row and column gap between its
children. The `size.control.*` and `size.pad-x.*` values a node with a `WidgetSize` resolves in `height` and
`padding_x` without a theme property do not move layout: widgets size themselves from `UiDensity`. `ui.theme_get`
reports what reaches layout under `resolved.props.layout` (`{ height, padding_x, gap }`, `null` where the theme sets
nothing).

```ron
types: { "Card": (props: { "padding": [12, 16], "min_width": 240, "max_width": 480 }),
         "Toolbar": (props: { "height": 40, "padding_x": 8, "gap": 4 }) }
```

**Token slots.** Widgets read these tokens by name; `ui.theme_list` lists them with the resolved values:

| Slot | Kind | Read by | When unset |
|---|---|---|---|
| `color.scrollbar-track` | color | `Scrollbars` presets with a track (classic) | `color.text` at the preset alpha |
| `color.scrollbar-thumb` | color | the scroll view's built-in thumb; `Scrollbars` preset thumbs | white at 35 % (built-in); `color.text` tint |
| `color.scrollbar-thumb-hover` | color | preset thumb under the pointer | `color.text` tint |
| `color.scrollbar-thumb-active` | color | preset thumb while pressed or dragged | `color.text` tint |
| `subtitle.text` | color | caption text while the player keeps the default color (white) | white |
| `subtitle.plate` | color | the caption box plate; its alpha multiplies the player's box opacity | black |
| `subtitle.plate-opacity` | number | the lowest caption box opacity | the player's opacity |
| `subtitle.font` | text | the caption font family (rows are measured and drawn in it) | the UI font |
| `subtitle.size` | number | multiplies the caption text size on top of the player's text scale (0.25 to 4) | 1 |
| `subtitle.outline` | color | the stroke around caption glyphs with the `Outline` background | black |
| `subtitle.outline-width` | number | the outline width in UI px (at most 8 physical px) | 2 |

The scrollbar slots are optional: no built-in theme sets them, so the default look is unchanged, and a custom
`Scrollbars` config (not a preset) is painted as stored. `regia-dark` (and so every built-in theme) sets
`subtitle.text` white and `subtitle.plate` black; the high-contrast themes set `subtitle.plate-opacity` to 1, so
turning high contrast on swaps captions to an opaque plate (a player who turned the box off keeps it off, and a text
color the player picked wins over `subtitle.text`). `regia-dark` also sets `subtitle.size` 1, `subtitle.outline` black
and `subtitle.outline-width` 2 (the previous size; the `Outline` background used to draw nothing and now strokes the
glyphs); `subtitle.font` is unset. `ui.theme_get` returns the theme's caption style as
`caption: { text, plate, plate_opacity, font, size, outline, outline_width }`. The linter treats the slot keys as
known.

```json
{"method": "ui.theme_set", "params": {"tokens": {"subtitle.size": 1.25, "subtitle.outline": "#202020"}}}
{"method": "ui.theme_get", "params": {"keys": ["subtitle.*"]}}
```
