# UI input events and layers (agents)

Guide topic: `agent.guide {"topic": "ui_input"}`. ADR-273 lane 4, ADR-293.

## Events

Every `UiEvent` carries `button` (`primary`, `secondary`, `middle`), `modifiers` (shift, ctrl, alt, meta, tracked from
keyboard messages) and `click_count`. New kinds:

| Kind | When |
|---|---|
| `DoubleClick` | The second press-release on the same node within 0.4 s and 8 px. Sent after the second `Click`, which keeps its old meaning (`click_count` 2). |
| `ContextClick` | Secondary button released over the node it went down on. No `Click` is sent for it. |
| `MiddleClick` | The same for the middle button. |
| `Scroll([dx, dy])` | Wheel or trackpad over a node (physical px). Scroll views still consume the wheel as before. |
| `LongPress` | A node with `LongPressable { delay }` held for `delay` seconds; once per press. |
| `Repeat(n)` | A node with `RepeatOnHold { delay, interval }` still held; `n` counts from 1. |

When a long press or repeat fired, the release sends no `Click`. Click, long-press and key-repeat
timers step on `RealTime`. Pause and `time_scale` change `Time` only, so they do not freeze or stretch
these timers. A manual `play.step` still moves them: that step is applied to `RealTime` before `Time`
scales it. `UiInputConfig` holds the double-click window and slop, in seconds of `RealTime`.

## Bubbling and scripts (ADR-7070)

A `UiEvent` is about its `target` only. After the UI passes, `bubble_ui_events` writes a `UiBubbledEvent { current,
event, depth }` for each ancestor of the target, nearest first (`depth` 1 is the parent), for every kind except
`PointerEnter` and `PointerLeave`. The walk stops after a node that carries `UiStopBubble`. A panel reads the copies
whose `current` is itself to handle its children's clicks in one place.

Scripts (`regia_framework::script`) receive `ScriptEvent::Ui { entity, origin, event }`: on the target's scripts with
`entity == origin`, then on each ancestor's scripts with `entity` = that ancestor. `event` is a `ScriptUiEvent`
(`Click { click_count }`, `ValueChanged(ScriptUiValue)`, `FocusChanged(bool)`, ...); text payloads stay on the widget.
Delivery can trail the UI pass by one frame.

## Gameplay gating (ADR-7070)

While the UI holds the pointer (`UiPointer.consumed_pointer`: over an interactable node, or pressing one),
`regia_input::UiPointerGate.ui_consumed` is set and mouse-button bindings of every input context except the exempt
ones (`Menu` by default) read as released. A click on a button does not also fire the gameplay `Fire` action; the
same click on empty space does. The flag follows the interaction pass, so evaluation sees the previous frame's
hover. Keys, mouse motion and gamepads are not gated. While pointer claims are on (the default with `UiPlugin`,
ADR-8786), the flag is set only while a press that started on a node lasts, not on hover: a press that started on the
world stays the game's when it moves over UI, and the first press after the pointer leaves UI is the game's on its
own frame. With claims off (`input.pointer_claims {enabled: false}`) the hover reading above applies.

To check it: hover a button with `play.inject_input` `cursor`, press `mouse_button` `left`, and `play.expect` that the
gameplay effect did not happen; repeat over empty space.

## Navigation from the `Menu` input context (ADR-7070)

When the project's `InputConfig` declares the `Menu` context (`InputConfig::with_menu_context()` adds the default
bindings) and player 0 has it enabled (`InputContexts::push(0, "Menu")`), focus navigation reads its actions
`Up`, `Down`, `Left`, `Right`, `Next`, `Prev`, `Submit`, `Cancel` and the `Navigate` stick, and the raw arrow-key and
gamepad paths stand down. Rebinding a `Menu` action with `input.rebind {context: "Menu", action: "Up"}` therefore
changes how the UI moves. Held directions repeat with `GamepadNavConfig`; `Next` with Shift held is `Prev`; while a
text input has focus, left/right and `Submit` belong to the editor. Without the context enabled, nothing changes.

## Script-field bindings (ADR-7070)

`Bind::script_field("Hud.score", Some("Score: {:03}"))` (`BindSource::ScriptField`) shows the field `score` of the
script `Hud` on the bound node or its nearest ancestor that carries one. The script exposes its fields by
implementing `Script::reflect_fields` (`Some(self)` on a `Reflect` script). The binding is one way and is read every
frame; the label changes only when the text does. An unknown script or field reports `binding_unresolved` in
`ui.inspect`'s binding `error`, and `source_kind` is `script_field`. `.ui.ron` layouts cannot name a script field yet.

## Runtime settings

`Regia.toml` may carry a `[runtime]` table (`docs/formats/regia-toml-runtime.md`): `pause_on_focus_loss = true`
pauses gameplay `Time` while the window is out of focus, and `keep_screen_on = true` keeps an Android display awake.
`settings.get` (no `path`) reports the live values under `runtime`:

```json
{"method": "settings.get", "params": {}}
{"settings": {"...": "..."}, "runtime": {"pause_on_focus_loss": false, "keep_screen_on": false}}
```

## Input layers

A node with `InputLayer { mode }` is a layer root. Only the top layer's subtree is hit-tested and navigable; the rest
of the screen gets no hover, click or focus movement. An open `Modal` becomes a layer by itself (mode `ui_and_game`)
and stops being one when it closes.

| Mode | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ui_only` | Gameplay should not act on input. Read `UiInputState::layer_mode`. |
| `ui_and_game` | The layer and the game both get input. Also the mode with no layer. |
| `game_only` | The UI ignores the pointer and navigation. |

Push focuses the layer's `DefaultFocus` (else its first focusable in reading order). Pop focuses what had focus before
the push and restores the previous input mode. `UiInputState::pointer_consumed` keeps its meaning.

## Methods

- `ui.layers { action?, entity?, mode? }`. `action` is `list` (default; the list result carries `applied: false`, so it is not written to the change log), `push` or `pop`. `push` needs `entity` (entity
  bits) and takes `mode` (default `ui_and_game`). `pop` takes the top layer, or `entity` to pop a specific layer (a
  modal is closed). Returns `{ layers: [{ entity, mode, previous_mode, restore_focus }], depth, mode, focused }`, bottom
  layer first, plus `popped` after a pop. Changes apply at once. Mutating; permission `edit_scene`.

```json
{"method": "ui.layers", "params": {}}
{"method": "ui.layers", "params": {"action": "push", "entity": 4294967301, "mode": "ui_only"}}
{"method": "ui.layers", "params": {"action": "pop"}}
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `no_layers` | `pop` with an empty stack. |
| `not_a_layer` | `pop` of an entity that is not a layer root. |
| `already_layer` | `push` of a node that already is a layer. |
| `unknown_entity` | The entity does not exist. |

`ui.click { button?, count?, modifiers? }` synthesizes the same pointer fields (`button` is `left`, `right` or `middle`, `count` is 1 to 8 and
raises `click_count`, `modifiers` is a list of `shift`, `ctrl`, `alt` and `meta` sent as real key messages around the click,
so the click's `UiEvent::modifiers` reports them; ADR-5665).

`ui.layers` places its lower-case reason in `error.data.code`: `unknown_entity`, `not_a_layer` and `no_layers` use
JSON-RPC `-32001`, while `already_layer` uses `-32602`. `ui.click` takes the selectors in [Runtime UI](book/agents/ui.md), plus
`button`, `count` and `modifiers` above. Its selectors are `node`, `name`, `text`, `text_contains`, `class`, `type` and `state`. It
can return `F0002` for an
invalid or refused node, `F0003` for no matching node, and `F0013` (`ui_not_installed`) without the runtime UI hook.

Workflow: query the modal or layer root, push it as `ui_only`, check `ui.layers` reports it at the top, then pop it
and check the prior mode and focused node were restored.

Captured failure on lavapipe:

Request:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"ui.layers","params":{"action":"pop","entity":0}}
```

Response:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"`entity` must be entity bits from ui.layers list","data":{"code":"F0002","hint":"check the method's parameters in the agent guide"}}}
```


## Recursive disabled input

`Disabled` keeps its local-only meaning. Insert `Disabled::recursive()` (a `DisabledSubtree`
component) to disable pointer and keyboard/gamepad focus for a node and its current or future
descendants. Removing that marker restores inherited input without removing any descendant's
local `Disabled` marker. Reparenting takes effect immediately; no copied flags need repair.
`regia_ui::node::is_disabled` and `ui.inspect` / `ui.query` report the effective state.
This is a runtime API; its `.ui.ron` representation belongs to the format lane.

`ui.set_disabled {entity, disabled, recursive?}` requires `edit_scene`; `entity` is the numeric
entity bits from `ui.query`, `disabled` is required, and `recursive` defaults to false.
The call changes only the selected local or recursive flag and releases newly disabled focus.
The result is `{entity, disabled, local, recursive}`: `disabled` is effective, the other two
booleans are the node's own markers. Clearing a local flag cannot override a disabled ancestor.

```json
{"method":"ui.set_disabled","params":{"entity":4294967310,"disabled":true,"recursive":true}}
{"method":"ui.set_disabled","params":{"entity":4294967310,"disabled":false,"recursive":true}}
```

Errors: `bad_entity` (missing/invalid entity bits), `unknown_entity` (absent entity or not a UI
node), `bad_flag` (missing disabled boolean). Wrong parameter types may be refused by the
shared schema gate with `F0002`. The runtime function `set_disabled(world, entity, disabled,
recursive)` returns false for an absent entity.

## Pointer claims

Guide topic: `agent.guide {"topic": "ui-pointer-claims"}`. ADR-7976.

A mouse press whose press edge lands on a hit-testable UI node (the node `ui_interaction` would press: the top layer's
subtree only, nothing under a `game_only` layer) belongs to the UI until that button is released. While a button is
claimed, action evaluation reads it as up for every binding that names it, whatever the trigger (down, pressed,
released, hold, tap, pulse, chord). So a click on a loadout tile never fires the gun bound to the left button: not on
the press frame, not while held, not on the release.

| Case | Who gets the button |
|---|---|
| Press starts on a widget | The UI, until the release, even if the pointer leaves the widget. |
| Press starts on empty screen | Gameplay, until the release, even if the pointer moves over a widget. |
| Press and release in one frame's batch on a widget | The UI, for that frame. |
| Another button pressed while a widget is pressed | The UI. |
| A `game_only` layer is on top | Gameplay (the UI takes no pointer input). |

The claim is written in `PreUpdate` (`regia_ui::interaction::claim_pointer_buttons`, after `update_pointer` and
`regia_input::InputSet::Devices`, before `InputSet::Evaluation`), so it applies in the press frame. It is on whenever
`UiPlugin` is installed. `regia_input::PointerClaims` holds the claimed buttons; `set_enabled(false)` turns claims off
and gameplay reads the mouse as it is. Claims are derived state: input recordings and replays do not store them.
Keyboard and gamepad are not claimed (focus navigation and input layers route them). Touch, the wheel, mouse motion and
gameplay systems that read `regia_input::Mouse` directly are not gated.

### `input.pointer_claims`

`input.pointer_claims { enabled?, watch?, expect_untriggered? }`. With no parameters it only reports. Order: `enabled`
changes, then `watch` arms, then `expect_untriggered` checks. Mutating; permission `edit_scene`.

- `enabled` (boolean): turn claims on or off.
- `watch` (list of declared action names): arm a fresh watch. From then on, each frame (in `Last`) counts, per action,
  the frames gameplay saw it: any phase but idle, a press edge, or held. Replaces any earlier watch.
- `expect_untriggered` (list of watched action names): add `check { passed, triggered: { <action>: frames } }`;
  `passed` is true when every named action stayed at 0 frames.

Returns `{ enabled, ui_claimed_buttons, claimed_presses, watch: { frames, actions: { <action>: { triggered_frames } } }
| null, check? }`. Button names are `left`, `right`, `middle`, `back`, `forward` and `other_<code>`, in that order.
`claimed_presses` counts presses claimed since start-up.

Workflow (a click on a node must not fire `Fire`):

```json
{"method": "input.pointer_claims", "params": {"watch": ["Fire"]}}
{"method": "ui.click", "params": {"name": "loadout_tile"}}
{"method": "play.step", "params": {"frames": 4}}
{"method": "input.pointer_claims", "params": {"expect_untriggered": ["Fire"]}}
```

The last answer has `check.passed: true` and `claimed_presses` one higher. A press on empty screen in the watch window
makes `check.passed` false with `triggered.Fire` above 0.

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pointer_claims_bad_params` | Parameters are not `{ enabled?, watch?, expect_untriggered? }`, or a list is empty. JSON-RPC `-32602`. |
| `pointer_claims_not_installed` | No `PointerClaims` resource: the app has no `InputPlugin`. JSON-RPC `-32001`. |
| `pointer_claims_not_watched` | `expect_untriggered` names an action with no armed watch. JSON-RPC `-32602`. |
| `pointer_claims_unknown_action` | `watch` names an action the input config does not declare. JSON-RPC `-32602`. |

## Host navigation keys

`UiNavActions` (`regia_ui::focus`) is the one input the focus pass reads. The built-in keyboard path maps the arrows,
Tab, Shift-Tab, Enter, Space and Escape, and `ui_gamepad_navigation` maps the gamepad. A host adds its own keys, such as
h/j/k/l, with a system ordered before `regia_ui::focus::ui_focus_navigation` that sets the flags. The flags are
cleared after each focus pass. Skip the map while a text field has focus so typing stays text:

<!-- ignore-reason: a host system fragment; its imports and the app that registers it are the host's -->
```rust,ignore
fn vi_nav_keys(
    mut keys: MessageReader<regia_platform::KeyboardInput>,
    mut nav: ResMut<UiNavActions>,
    focus: Res<FocusState>,
    text_inputs: Query<(), With<TextInput>>,
) {
    let typing = focus.focused.is_some_and(|f| text_inputs.contains(f));
    for e in keys.read() {
        if e.state != ButtonState::Pressed || typing {
            continue;
        }
        match e.logical_key.as_str() {
            "h" => nav.left = true,
            "j" => nav.down = true,
            "k" => nav.up = true,
            "l" => nav.right = true,
            _ => {}
        }
    }
}

app.add_systems(Update, vi_nav_keys.before(regia_ui::focus::ui_focus_navigation));
```

The arrows and Enter keep working beside it. Reading the `Menu` input context for navigation is a later item. Tested by
`crates/regia_ui/tests/nav_keymap.rs`.

<!-- source: book/agents/ui-accessibility.md -->
# UI accessibility settings and right-to-left layout (agents)

ADR-273 lane 2, ADR-341.

## Settings

`GameSettings.accessibility` has three UI fields; the framework copies them into the `regia_ui::UiAccessibility`
resource whenever the settings change.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `text_scale` | Multiplier on every text size (`1.0` = as authored). The UI limits it to 0.5 through 3.0. The device text floor (`UiDevicePolicy::min_text_px`, 12 px on the Deck) still applies afterwards. |
| `reduced_motion` | Animations jump to their end value: tweens, theme cross-fades (a theme swap applies at once; copied into `ActiveTheme`, UI D15) and [motion presets](book/agents/ui-motion.md) (presets keep a short fade). The same flag also stops framework camera shake, handheld sway and walk bob, and forces motion blur off (ADR-3464, [accessibility](book/user-guide/accessibility.md)). |
| `high_contrast` | The theme switches to its high-contrast variant (`<theme>-high-contrast`, else `regia-high-contrast`; UI D15, [theme switch](book/agents/ui-theme-switch.md)). `regia-light` has `regia-light-high-contrast`, so a light-scheme player stays light. |
| `color_scheme` | `GameSettings` only: `None` (default) leaves the theme to the game; `Some(Dark)`, `Some(Light)` or `Some(System)` sets `ThemeMode::follow` ([theme switch](book/agents/ui-theme-switch.md)). |

`reduced_motion`, `high_contrast` and `color_scheme` are missing in older settings files and load as `false` /
`None`. Changing `text_scale` re-shapes all text and re-runs layout on the next frame.

Set them with `settings.set` (`accessibility.text_scale`, `accessibility.reduced_motion`,
`accessibility.high_contrast`, `accessibility.color_scheme`) or with `ui.accessibility` (all but `color_scheme`).

## Right-to-left layout

A node's `text_dir` (`auto`, `ltr`, `rtl`) now decides its layout direction. `rtl` always mirrors, `ltr` never does,
and `auto` inherits its parent's direction; a root with `auto` mirrors when the active locale is a right-to-left
language (ar, he, fa, ur, ps, sd, yi, dv, ug, ckb). A mirrored node lays out with CSS `direction: rtl` (rows run from
the right, `start` is the right edge, grid columns run right to left) and the left and right edges of `margin`,
`padding`, `border` and `inset` swap (ADR-518). Switching the locale re-lays out the tree. `ui.query` reports each
node's direction as `layout_dir`. The details are in [UI layout edge cases](book/agents/ui-layout.md).

## Methods

- `ui.accessibility { text_scale?, reduced_motion?, high_contrast? }`. With no parameters it reports. With any of them it
  changes those fields in the live resource, and in `GameSettings` only when that resource is already in the world
  (`persisted` is false otherwise), then reports.
  Returns `{ text_scale, effective_text_scale, reduced_motion, high_contrast, locale, locale_rtl, persisted }`.
  Mutating; permission `edit_scene`.

A partial update starts from `GameSettings.accessibility` when settings are installed, preserving
omitted fields, and writes the same three values to settings and the live resource. Without settings,
it starts from the live resource, or the defaults when the live resource is absent.

```json
{"method": "ui.accessibility", "params": {}}
{"method": "ui.accessibility", "params": {"text_scale": 1.5, "reduced_motion": true}}
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ui_bad_text_scale` | `text_scale` is not a number from 0.5 to 3.0 |
| `ui_bad_flag` | `reduced_motion` or `high_contrast` is not a boolean |

<!-- source: book/agents/ui-animation.md -->
# UI tweens and the visual transform (agents)

Guide topic: `agent.guide {"topic": "ui_animation"}`. ADR-273 lane 3, ADR-343.

## Tweens

A tween animates one property of a node from a start value to an end value over a duration, after an optional delay,
through an easing curve. Time comes from the game clock (`Time`): `play.step`, a paused game and a fixed step
reproduce a tween exactly, and nothing reads a wall clock. With reduced motion on (`ActiveTheme::reduced_motion` or the
player's `reduced_motion` setting, see [UI accessibility](book/agents/ui-accessibility.md)) a tween jumps to its end value on the
next frame. Motion presets ([UI motion presets](book/agents/ui-motion.md)) follow the spec's rule instead: transforms jump, fades
are capped at `motion.fast`.

| Property | Kind | Writes |
|---|---|---|
| `opacity` | number `0..1` | `Opacity` |
| `background` | colour | A solid `Background` |
| `border_color` | colour | `Border` colour |
| `text_color` | colour | The shaped glyphs while it runs, every span at the end |
| `inset_left`, `inset_top`, `inset_right`, `inset_bottom` | number, UI px | `Style::inset` |
| `width`, `height` | number, UI px | `Style::size` |
| `translate_x`, `translate_y` | number, UI px | `UiTransform::translate` |
| `scale` | number | `UiTransform::scale` |

A start value that is left out is the property's value when the tween starts (for a `width` or `height` that is `auto`,
the laid-out size). Components the node does not have yet (`Opacity`, `Background`, `Border`, `UiTransform`) are added
with neutral values. Several tweens run as a **parallel** group (the default) or a **sequence**; in a sequence a tween
with no start value begins where the previous step on the same property ended. When two tweens in a group write the
same property, the later one wins.

Easing curves: `linear`, and `quad`, `cubic`, `expo`, `back`, `bounce`, `elastic` each as `_in`, `_out` and `_in_out`
(for example `back_out`). A cubic bezier is `[x1, y1, x2, y2]` with the CSS meaning. `back` and `elastic` overshoot
the end value on the way.

Sampling is a pure function (`TweenPlan::sample`): the same time gives the same values. When a tween ends it sends a
`UiTweenFinished { entity }` message and removes itself; replacing it with a new `UiTween` or stopping it sends
nothing. A node with no `UiTween` costs nothing per frame.

Game code starts one by inserting the component:

```text
commands.entity(button).insert(UiTween::new(
    Tween::to(TweenProperty::Scale, TweenValue::Number(1.1), 0.15).ease(Ease::BackOut),
));
commands.entity(panel).insert(UiTween::show(Reveal::Slide([0.0, 24.0]), 0.3, Ease::CubicOut));
```

`UiTween::show` takes a node out of `Display::None` and fades (and slides) it in; `UiTween::hide` fades it out and sets
`Display::None` at the end.

A themed node's colours are written by the theme system when its state changes (hover, press); a colour tween on the
same channel and a theme change fight, and the later write wins. Use tweens for colours the theme does not drive, or
tween a different channel (opacity, scale).

## Visual transform

`UiTransform { translate, scale, pivot_ratio, hit_test }` moves and scales a node and its subtree without layout
knowing: siblings do not shift and the layout result is kept in `UiLayoutBox`. After layout each frame, the computed
rects of the node and every descendant are mapped on the CPU (scale about the pivot, then translate), so the draw list
is built from the transformed rects with no change to the overlay shader. `translate` is in UI px; `pivot_ratio` is a
fraction of the node's own rect (`[0.5, 0.5]` is the centre, the default). A transform on a parent also moves its
children, and a child's own transform applies first.

Limits of this first cut: no rotation (it needs the overlay shader); the scale applies to the boxes, so border width,
corner radius, shadow blur and glyph size keep their size; wrapped text inside a scaled node is shaped again at the new
width.

Hit testing uses the transformed rect by default, so a button is hit where it is drawn. A button that grows or moves
away on hover can lose the hover it just got; set `hit_test: "layout"` on it to keep pointer hit testing on the layout
rect. Focus navigation, `ui.query` bounds and `ui.click` use the transformed rect.

## Methods

`ui.tween { action?, entity?, ... }`. `action` is `query` (default), `start`, `show`, `hide`, `stop` or
`set_transform`. All but `query` need `entity` (entity bits from `ui.query`). Mutating; permission `edit_scene`.

- `start`: one tween `{ property, to, from?, duration?, delay?, ease? }` (duration defaults to 0.25 s), or
  `{ tweens: [ ... ], mode?: "parallel" | "sequence" }` with at most 32. Colours are `"#RRGGBB"`, `"#RRGGBBAA"` or
  `[r, g, b, a]` (linear floats). Starting replaces a running tween on the node.
- `show`, `hide`: `{ kind?: "fade" | "slide", offset?: [x, y], duration?, ease? }`. The default offset is `[0, 24]`.
- `stop`: cancels the node's tween and leaves the values where they are. Answers `stopped: true | false`.
- `set_transform`: any of `translate`, `scale`, `pivot_ratio`, `hit_test` (`"transformed"` or `"layout"`); fields left
  out keep their value. `reset: true` removes the transform.
- `query`: with `entity` the node's state, without it every running tween: `{ count, tweens }`.

Every answer except the list form is `{ entity, tweening, tween, transform, opacity }`; `tween` is `{ elapsed,
duration, progress, properties, shows, hides }` while one runs, else `null`.

Wait for a tween with the `ui.tweening` atom in `play.wait_until` and `play.expect`: `{ predicate: "ui.tweening", entity?,
is? }` holds when the node (without `entity`, any node) is tweening equals `is` (default `true`).

```json
{"method": "ui.tween", "params": {"action": "start", "entity": 4294967301, "property": "opacity", "from": 0, "to": 1, "duration": 0.5, "ease": "quad_out"}}
{"method": "ui.tween", "params": {"action": "start", "entity": 4294967301, "mode": "sequence", "tweens": [{"property": "scale", "to": 1.2, "duration": 0.1}, {"property": "scale", "to": 1.0, "duration": 0.2, "ease": "back_out"}]}}
{"method": "ui.tween", "params": {"action": "hide", "entity": 4294967301, "kind": "slide", "offset": [0, 30]}}
{"method": "ui.tween", "params": {"action": "set_transform", "entity": 4294967301, "translate": [40, 0], "hit_test": "layout"}}
{"method": "play.wait_until", "params": {"condition": {"predicate": "ui.tweening", "entity": 4294967301, "is": false}}}
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `missing_entity` | The action needs `entity`. |
| `bad_entity` | `entity` is not entity bits. |
| `unknown_entity` | The entity does not exist. |
| `missing_property` | A tween has no `property`. |
| `unknown_property` | The property name is not one of the table above. |
| `bad_value` | `to`, `from`, `offset`, `translate`, `pivot_ratio`, `scale` or `hit_test` has the wrong type or range. |
| `bad_duration` | `duration` or `delay` is not between 0 and 3600 seconds. |
| `bad_ease` | The curve name is unknown or the bezier is not four numbers. |
| `no_tweens` | `tweens` is empty or not an array. |
| `too_many_tweens` | More than 32 tweens in one call. |
| `bad_mode` | `mode` is not `parallel` or `sequence`. |
| `bad_kind` | `kind` is not `fade` or `slide`. |
| `bad_action` | Unknown `action`. |

<!-- source: book/agents/ui-shortcuts.md -->
# UI shortcuts (agents)

Guide topic: `agent.guide {"topic": "ui_shortcuts"}`. ADR-273 lane 7 (gap I02), ADR-374.

The shortcut registry (`regia_ui::shortcuts::UiShortcuts`) binds key chords to named actions. A chord is modifiers
plus one key, written `Ctrl+Shift+S`, `Alt+F4`, `Escape`. A shortcut lives in a scope: `global`, or a named context
the game switches on (`editor`, `pause_menu`). A context shortcut wins over a global one on the same chord. Pressing
the keys writes a `ShortcutTriggered { action, chord, scope }` message; game and menu code react to the action name.

- Letters match case-insensitively; Shift is an explicit modifier (`Shift+1`, not `!`).
- Auto-repeat does not fire. While a text input has focus, only chords with Ctrl, Alt or Meta fire.
- Two actions on one chord in the same scope are a conflict: registering is allowed, the chord triggers nothing, and
  `ui.shortcuts` lists it. An exact duplicate (same chord, scope and action) is refused at registration.
- `UiShortcuts::chord_label(action)` gives the text a menu shows (`Ctrl+S`, or `⌘S` style on macOS).

## Methods

- `ui.shortcuts {}`. Read-only. Returns `{ shortcuts: [{ action, chord, display, scope, label, active }], conflicts:
  [{ chord, kind, actions, scopes }], contexts }`. `active` is whether the action would fire now. Conflict `kind` is
  `same_scope` (nothing fires), `shadow` (a context shortcut hides a global one while its context is on) or `overlap`
  (the same chord in two contexts; ambiguous only when both are on).
- `ui.shortcut_trigger { action }`. Fires the action as if its keys were pressed, with the same scope and conflict
  rules. Returns `{ action, chord, scope }`. Mutating; permission `edit_scene`.
- `ui.shortcut_contexts { contexts }`. Replaces the active contexts (an empty array turns all off). Returns
  `{ contexts }`. Mutating; permission `edit_scene`.

```json
{"method": "ui.shortcuts", "params": {}}
{"method": "ui.shortcut_contexts", "params": {"contexts": ["editor"]}}
{"method": "ui.shortcut_trigger", "params": {"action": "bold"}}
```

Registration is done in game code (`UiShortcuts::register`); there is no agent method for it yet.

## Errors

The code is in `data.code`. The protocol code beside it is `F0003` for `unknown_action`, `F0013` for
`shortcuts_not_installed` and `F0002` for the rest.

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `unknown_action` | No shortcut has this action name. |
| `shortcut_inactive` | Every shortcut of the action is out of scope (context off) or shadowed by another action. |
| `shortcut_ambiguous` | Another action shares the chord in the same scope. |
| `shortcuts_not_installed` | The app has no `UiShortcuts` resource (no `UiPlugin`). |
| `bad_chord` | A chord string could not be parsed (Rust API only). |
| `duplicate_shortcut` | Same chord, scope and action already registered (Rust API only). |

`ui.shortcuts` takes no parameters. `ui.shortcut_trigger` requires an `action` string from its results. Context
switching requires `contexts`, an array of context name strings (a name no shortcut uses is accepted and matches
nothing); an empty array turns all contexts off. The
`shortcuts_not_installed` protocol error is returned when the app has no shortcut registry.

## Failure example

Captured CLI output from `regia agent call ui.shortcut_trigger '{"action":"missing-action"}'`:

```text
error: method call failed: the shortcut registry is not installed (-32004): {"code":"shortcuts_not_installed","hint":"the app needs regia_ui::UiPlugin"}
```

## Workflow

List shortcuts and their conflicts, enable the context needed by the action, then trigger the action by its registered
name. If it does not fire, inspect `active` and `conflicts` in the list response; same-scope conflicts make a chord
ambiguous.

<!-- source: book/agents/ui-drag-drop.md -->
# UI drag and drop (agents)

Guide topic: `agent.guide {"topic": "ui_drag_drop"}`. ADR-517.

## Model

A node with `DragSource { payload: { kind, data } }` starts an operation when it is dragged past the interaction
system's threshold (the same `DragStart` the sliders use). The payload `kind` is a type tag (`"item"`, `"tab"`); `data`
is a `UiValue`. A node with `DropTarget { accepts }` receives drops: an empty `accepts` takes every kind, otherwise only
the listed kinds. A target also receives drops that land on its `Interactable` descendants (the nearest target above
the node under the pointer wins). Nodes inside the dragged source's own subtree are never drop sites.

While an operation runs the source carries `DragActive` and the hovered target carries `DropHover { accepted }`
(`accepted: false` means "show a no-drop cue"). Game code reacts to `DragDropEvent` messages: `Started`, `HoverEnter`,
`HoverLeave`, `Dropped { source, target, payload }` and `Cancelled { source, reason }`. The engine moves nothing, so a
cancel needs no undo. `DragOperation::ghost_origin()` gives where a ghost belongs (pointer minus the grab offset).

An operation ends with a drop only when the button is released over a target that accepts the kind. Everything else
cancels:

| Cancel `reason` | When |
|---|---|
| `escape` | Escape was pressed. |
| `no_target` | Released over no drop target. |
| `rejected` | Released over a target that does not accept the kind. |
| `source_gone` | The source node was despawned or lost its layout. |
| `layer_changed` | An input layer opened that excludes the source. |
| `requested` | `cancel_drag` (or the agent's `cancel`). |

While an input layer is active only its subtree can be hovered.

## Methods

- `ui.drag_drop { action? }` with `action` `state` (default), `drag`, `drop` or `cancel`. Mutating (permission
  `edit_scene`), like the other `ui.*` writes.
  - `state` returns `{ active, source, kind, data, position, grab_offset, hover: { node, accepted } | null, sources:
    [{ node, kind }], targets: [{ node, accepts }] }` (the middle fields only while `active`).
  - `drag { from, to | at, release? }` queues five frames of real input: move onto `from`, press, move 6 px (starts the
    operation), move onto `to` (a node, as `ui.query` filters) or `at` (`[x, y]` physical px), release. With
    `release: false` the button stays down and the operation stays open for `state`, `drop` or `cancel`. `from` needs a
    `DragSource`; `to` needs a `DropTarget`. Returns `{ from, start, end, released, queued_frames }`.
  - `drop { to? }` moves onto `to` when given, then releases. Returns `{ queued_frames }`.
  - `cancel` cancels the running operation and releases the button. Returns `{ cancelled, queued_frames }`.
- `ui.query` nodes carry `drag_kind` (the payload kind or `null`) and `drop_accepts` (the list or `null`).

Effects show after the frames run: use `play.step` or `play.wait_until`.

```json
{"method": "ui.drag_drop", "params": {"action": "drag", "from": {"name": "sword"}, "to": {"name": "slot_3"}}}
{"method": "ui.drag_drop", "params": {"action": "drag", "from": {"name": "sword"}, "to": {"name": "slot_3"}, "release": false}}
{"method": "ui.drag_drop", "params": {}}
{"method": "ui.drag_drop", "params": {"action": "cancel"}}
```

## Errors

| `reason` | `data.code` | When |
|---|---|---|
| `ui_drag_active` | `F0002` | `drag` while an operation runs. |
| `ui_no_drag` | `F0002` | `drop` or `cancel` with no operation. |
| `ui_not_draggable` | `F0002` | `from` has no `DragSource`. |
| `ui_not_drop_target` | `F0002` | `to` has no `DropTarget`. |
| `ui_drag_target_required` | `F0002` | `drag` without `to` or `at`. |
| `ui_node_off_window` | `F0002` | `from` or `to` draws into a camera texture or a world panel; the window pointer cannot press it (use `ui.world_click`). |
| `ui_node_required` | `F0002` | `drag` without `from`. |
| `ui_bad_param` | `F0002` | Wrong type for `action`, `from`, `to` or `at`. |

Node lookup, disabled and invisible nodes answer with the codes in the [UI](book/agents/ui.md) page (`ui_node_not_found`,
`ui_node_ambiguous`, `ui_node_disabled`, `ui_node_not_visible`).

Not covered yet: hover-to-switch (a tab bar activating a tab while a payload hovers it) and a built-in ghost node.

<!-- source: book/agents/volumetric-fog.md -->
# Volumetric fog

Desktop High and Ultra march a froxel grid (Wronski, SIGGRAPH 2014). Each cell stores
in-scatter and extinction. The sun is multiplied by cascade 0 of the shadow map (the paged
sun atlas when paging is on, otherwise the CSM slice), and up to
four local lights add inverse-square light. Slices are integrated front to back and blended
with the previous frame after reprojection.

This is separate from `RenderSettings.fog`, the analytic height fog. That fog runs in the
forward shader only when the LUT sky is off and the world has air. On Earth the LUT sky is off
for Desktop Low, Deck, Mobile and the lab. Desktop High and Ultra draw the LUT sky on an Earth
frame with no studio environment, and that frame forces `FogSettings` off for meshes and
terrain. An airless world forces it off on every preset. The haze on a LUT-sky frame is the
atmosphere LUT and this froxel pass, not `FogSettings`.

## Controls

`VolumetricFogSettings` is the height component (density, falloff, albedo, anisotropy,
history weight). `FogVolumes` adds boxes and spheres. Both are resources. Density zero and
an empty volume list skip the pass.

```rust
use regia::prelude::*;
use regia::render::{FogVolume, FogVolumes, VolumetricFogSettings};

fn configure(app: &mut App) {
    app.insert_resource(VolumetricFogSettings {
        density: 0.02,
        ..VolumetricFogSettings::default()
    });
    app.insert_resource(FogVolumes {
        volumes: vec![FogVolume::Sphere {
            center: [0.0, 2.0, 0.0],
            radius: 6.0,
            density: 0.2,
        }],
    });
}
```

Fog that belongs to a tunnel or a cave goes in its `InteriorVolume`:
`FogVolume::interior(volume, density)` is a box with the interior's centre and half extents, so the
fog exists exactly where the interior contains the point (ADR-3257). An interior that contains
nothing (a non-positive or non-finite axis) or a negative density adds no fog. The sky does not
light air inside an interior volume, so the interior's fog glows only where the sun or a fog light
reaches it: under a tunnel portal that is the sunlit wedge below the cut; deeper in, the headlight.
The tunnel acceptance scene (`crates/regia_terrain/tests/tunnel_scene`) checks both by readback:
`interior_fog_stays_in_the_tube` (no pixel outside the interior's screen box moves) and
`light_shafts_fall_through_the_cut` (with the `calibrated` sun-shadow rule, air the roof shadows
does not glow like the shaft).

Point lights extracted from the world are converted from lumens to candela (`lm / 4π`) before
the fog march, matching the forward shader. Spot lights are already candela and pass through
as is (before v0.2.0 they were divided by 4π too, 12.6× too dim). Paged shadows are not in
this tree; the shaft uses the cascaded shadow map.

## Surfaces, low sun and planets (look-r2)

- A froxel is sampled no deeper than the farthest surface its sub-rays hit, and a pixel reads
  the fog up to its own depth: height fog below the ground no longer leaks onto terrain seen
  downhill (the old Mars "fog wall").
- Sunlight and skylight in the fog are dimmed by the fog layer they cross
  (`fog_layer_optical_depth`): a dusk sun barely lights a valley haze.
- `planet_medium` (default on): on Mars the fog scatters like the planet's dust (butterscotch,
  forward lobe), not like white water fog. Earth keeps `albedo` / `anisotropy`.
- Fog inside an `InteriorVolume` sees no sky. A map can author its dust with
  `LevelAtmosphere.haze` instead of a `VolumetricFogSettings` resource.

## Local lights in the fog (v0.2.0, ADR-1365)

The fog has four local-light slots (`FOG_LIGHT_SLOTS`). Each frame, `extract_frame` scores
every point and spot light from the primary camera (the window view drawn first) and keeps
the four best:

```text
score = candela × max(color) × window(gap) / max(d², r²)
gap   = max(d − r, 0)            distance from the eye to the light's sphere
window(x) = (1 − (x / far)⁴)₊    far = the view's far plane (the froxel range)
```

`d` is the eye-to-light distance and `r` the light's radius (a spot's range). Inside its
radius every position scores as if it were at `r`. A light outside its own radius still
scores, so a muzzle flash 20 m ahead keeps its slot. A light picked the frame before ranks
with its score × 1.25 (`FOG_PICK_HYSTERESIS`), so two lights of about equal strength do not
swap every frame. Lights that stay keep their slot, and a new light takes a freed slot.

A spot lights only the air inside its cone. The ramp is the forward pass's: full inside the
inner half-angle, zero past the outer one, linear between. The distance falloff is the forward
pass's too, `saturate(1 − (d / r)⁴)² / (d² + 1)` (`fog_light_falloff`). A lamp at the eye, such
as a headlight, does not flood the slices next to the camera.

On Desktop High and Ultra a spot that casts shadows (`SpotLight.cast_shadows`) and has a tile
in the local shadow atlas is also shadowed in the fog: a floodlight through a doorway throws a
shaft, and the wall beside the door stops the beam. The fog takes one unfiltered atlas tap per
sample. Point lights are not shadowed in the fog.

Hosts that fill `OutdoorParams::lights` themselves (lab scenes, `FrameRenderer` without the
ECS) build each light with `FogLight::point(position, color, candela, radius)`,
`FogLight::spot(position, direction, color, candela, range, inner, outer)` or
`FogLight::from_local(&lab_local_light)`. `from_local` applies the same units as the
forward pass. Struct literals no longer compile: `FogLight` gained `cone`.

### Agent surface

`render.fog_lights` returns the pick for the last extracted frame:

```json
{ "slots": 4, "hysteresis": 1.25, "candidates": 6, "eye": [0, 1.8, 0],
  "lights": [ { "entity": 4294967301, "kind": "spot", "position": [0, 2, 0],
                "color": [1, 0.95, 0.85], "intensity_cd": 40000, "radius": 70,
                "score": 8.16, "held": true, "shadowed": false,
                "direction": [0, 0, -1], "cos_inner": 0.989, "cos_outer": 0.900 } ] }
```

`lights` is in slot order. `held` is true when the light was also picked the frame before.
`shadowed` is true when the last drawn frame shadowed the light from its atlas tile (false
without a `RuntimeRenderer`).
`direction`, `cos_inner` and `cos_outer` are present only for spots. The method fails with
the not-found error (`F0003`) when the app has no `FogLightPick` resource (no `RenderPlugin`).

Use it when a light is missing from the haze. A fifth light is not picked: its score is
lower than the four in `lights`. A light whose sphere lies past the far plane scores 0.

### What a good frame looks like

A spot aimed across the frame lights a wedge of haze on its side and leaves the other side
dark. A point light of the same candela lights both sides evenly
(`regia_render/tests/fog_local_lights.rs`). With a wall over the upper half of a shadowed
spot's cone, the haze above the axis goes dark and the haze below it stays lit. The per-sample in-scatter of a spot on its
axis equals that of a point light of the same candela (`fog_lights` unit tests).

## Sun shadow in the fog (ADR-3122)

The froxel fog reads one sun cascade: the first whose split reaches 150 m (cascade 0 is too
short for light shafts on a long view), with the same light matrix the shadow pass just drew.
`VolumetricFogSettings::sun_shadow` chooses how it reads it:

| Rule | Depth bias of the compare | Outer 15 % of the cascade's square | A froxel slice that holds a surface |
|---|---|---|---|
| `legacy` (default) | 0.002 of the cascade's depth extent: about 0.4 m along the sun on a 200 m view, metres on a long one | a shadowed sample fades to lit toward the edge | samples beyond the surface are pulled onto it |
| `calibrated` | half a texel plus half a texel per unit of level-ground slope seen from the sun (`fog_sun_shadow_bias_m`; ADR-4199 reduces the constant margin) | the compare decides up to the edge | every sub-ray's samples are spread over the air in front of its own surface (`fog_sample_depth`), weighted by the share of the slice that air fills (`fog_sample_weight`) |

Outside the square both rules read the sun as unshadowed: the fog has no other cascade, and past
the shadow distance the forward pass reads lit too. Under `legacy` the air within the bias under
a roof, the samples on a roof's underside and the shadowed air near the square's edge read the
sun; in the spec 27 fog room this lights the room's upper air and makes the raster fog 1.43
times as bright as the path tracer's. `calibrated` keeps that air dark. It changes every fogged
frame with sun shadows, so it is opt-in until the owner decides the default (the default frames,
`studio_frame_pin` and the shipped goldens, are `legacy`).

```rust
use regia_render::{FogSunShadowRule, VolumetricFogSettings};

fn calibrated_fog() -> VolumetricFogSettings {
    VolumetricFogSettings {
        density: 0.02,
        sun_shadow: FogSunShadowRule::Calibrated,
        ..VolumetricFogSettings::default()
    }
}
```

### Agent surface: `render.fog_shadow`

`render.fog_shadow { point? }` reports how the last drawn fog pass read the sun shadow (the
render plugin's `FogSunShadowProbe`, filled by every fog pass). The shape (the values are
illustrative):

```json
{ "recorded": true, "rule": "calibrated", "configured_rule": "calibrated",
  "rules": ["legacy", "calibrated"], "fade_band": 0.0,
  "cascade_index": 3, "cascade_count": 4, "sun_travel": [0.5, -0.866, 0.0],
  "bias_ndc": 0.000186, "bias_m": 0.126,
  "cascade": { "resolution": 2048, "texel_m": 0.16, "depth_m": 680.0 },
  "lookup": { "point": [-4.0, 5.7, 0.0], "reads": "compare", "why": "covered",
              "state": "covered", "edge": 0.03, "fade": 0.0, "texel": [1031, 1010],
              "ndc_z": 0.297, "bias_ndc": 0.000186,
              "cascades": [ { "index": 0, "read": false, "state": "not_read" },
                            { "index": 1, "read": false, "state": "not_read" },
                            { "index": 2, "read": false, "state": "not_read" },
                            { "index": 3, "read": true, "state": "covered" } ] } }
```

- `recorded` is false until a fog pass has run; the reply then lists `rule` (the configured
  one), `rules` and `fade_band` only.
- `rule` is the rule the last pass ran, `configured_rule` the `VolumetricFogSettings` resource's.
- `cascade` is null when the fog ran without sun shadows (every sample reads the sun).
- `bias_m` is the compare's bias in metres along the sun: air nearer than that under a caster
  reads lit.
- `lookup` (with `point`) runs the shader's lookup on the CPU at that world point. `state` is
  `covered` (the compare decides), `faded` (`legacy` only: in the fade band, a shadowed sample
  still reads `fade` of the sun) or `outside` (read as lit). `reads` is `compare`,
  `compare_faded` or `lit`, and `why` says why: `covered`, `fade_band`, `outside_cascade` or
  `no_sun_shadow`. Per cascade, the one the fog read carries the state; the others are
  `not_read`. The stored depth is not read back: the compare's result needs the frame.

Errors: `F0003` (not found) when the app has no `FogSunShadowProbe` resource (no
`RenderPlugin`); `F0002` (invalid params) when `point` is not three finite numbers.

Use it when fog glows where the sun should be blocked: a `faded` or `outside` state, or a
`bias_m` larger than the gap between the caster and the air, explains the light; `calibrated`
fixes the first and the last.

### What a good frame looks like (sun shadow)

In a closed room with a slit in its roof, the shaft from the slit to the floor is the only lit
air: pixels whose rays never come near the shaft stay dark
(`regia_render/tests/fog_shadow_lookup.rs`, the room on lavapipe under `calibrated`). The CPU
tests check the lookup against an analytic shadow map: air under a roof slab deeper than the
cascade resolves reads no sun at five cascade sizes and five places in the square, air above it
keeps the sun, and lit level ground does not shadow itself.

<!-- source: book/agents/clouds.md -->
# Volumetric clouds

Desktop High and Ultra raymarch one cloud layer on Earth and Mars maps (an airless preset has
none). The method follows Schneider's public talks (SIGGRAPH 2015, and "Nubis", SIGGRAPH 2017):

- A **weather map**: R is coverage, G is cloud type. `CloudPattern::Coverage` thresholds a
  tiling cellular noise at the coverage percentile, so exactly that fraction of the map is at
  least half covered, with soft edges.
- A **shape** volume (32³ Perlin–Worley plus Worley FBM) eroded by a smaller **detail** volume.
  Both tile and are built once per process.
- A **height profile** per type: stratus (thin, low), cumulus, towering cumulus.
- **Light**: a six-step march toward the sun, Beer's law, the Beer–Powder edge term, a dual-lobe
  Henyey–Greenstein phase and three multiple-scattering octaves; ambient from the sky dome.
- **Cone light** (batch v020, `FrameQuality::cloud_cone_light`, on for Desktop High and Ultra, the
  presets with clouds): the light march takes five taps spread inside a ~10° cone toward the
  sun over half the layer thickness (the first three eroded by the detail noise, as in the
  straight march), rotated per sample, plus one long tap that catches shadow
  from cloud farther toward the sun (Schneider 2015). The two multiple-scattering octaves are
  weighted by an in-scatter probability (Schneider & Vos 2017) that is low in thin wisps and
  near the base and high in dense cores, so edges and undersides read darker and cores glow.
  The detail erosion is displaced by a tileable 2D curl-noise field, strongest at the bases,
  for swirled wisps. Off keeps the v0.1 straight march, octaves and detail.
- **Sun at altitude** (batch v020, always): the layer is lit by the sun as transmitted to its base
  and top (the atmosphere's transmittance table), not to the camera. At sunset the tops take
  a warmer, brighter sun than the bases, and the layer stays lit for a while after the sun has
  set for a camera on the ground (the horizon dips ~1.8° at 3 km).
- **Aerial perspective** (batch v020, with the physical sky): the air between the camera and the
  cloud comes from the same aerial LUT the terrain uses, at the cloud's scatter distance, so
  distant clouds take the haze colour of the sky around them. Past the table's 32 km they also
  fade out over the old 45 km scale.
- **Cost**: the march runs at half resolution (`resolution_divisor`) with jittered start
  positions. A big step is four times the small one; a hit steps back and walks small,
  and eight empty small steps return to the big step. The small step grows with
  distance. Inside the layer it starts at 20 m and grows so the 67.5 km fade span
  finishes in the step budget. The result is upsampled by nearest scene distance
  over the whole frame (tied distances blend bilinearly), so a cloud in front of a
  mountain draws over it and a closer peak stays in front. View rays use the unjittered
  camera; depth is still unprojected with the jittered matrix. Clouds fade into the sky
  with distance. Froxel fog still integrates through the same band.
- **Temporal** (batch v020, `FrameQuality::cloud_reprojection`, on for every preset): each frame
  marches one texel of every 4×4 block of the half-resolution target, in Bayer order, so a
  texel is refreshed every 16 frames. The other 15 are reprojected from the previous result:
  the texel's world point at its scatter distance, minus the wind drift since that frame, is
  projected with the previous unjittered view-projection and fetched with a Catmull-Rom
  filter, then clamped to the min/max of the 3×3 fresh texels around it. Off screen, or where
  the scene distance no longer matches the history (a disocclusion), the texel is filled from
  the fresh texels on its surface and keeps blending in new fills until it is marched. The
  clamp only applies where the block's fresh sample shows the history is stale, so a still
  sky keeps detail finer than a block. The marched texel blends half and half with its
  history when still, and replaces it when the texel moved or was resampled (a fast pan
  softens clouds by about a low-resolution texel until then). RTX 5080, 1440p, coverage 0.5:
  High 0.98 → 0.35 ms, Ultra 1.37 → 0.45 ms. A camera cut (`FrameRenderer::camera_cut`, or a detected one), the first
  frame and a resize march every texel. Desktop Ultra spends the time saved on 96 steps
  (`cloud_step_percent` 150). Texture views keep clouds off and never touch the history.

The composite leaves a surface alone when it is nearer than the point where its view ray enters the
layer (ADR-5792): no cloud can be in front of it, whatever the low-resolution texels around it
hold. Before that rule, trees and rooftops against a cloudy sky carried texel-sized specks of
cloud radiance, which the history fetch had spread from sky texels over the surface texels beside
them.

The same weather column, projected along the sun, darkens the terrain (cloud shadows). With the
cloud shadow map on (below), the 3D clouds themselves shadow the sun instead.

## Cloud shadow map, god rays and overcast sky light (batch B, ADR-320, ADR-321)

Three switches on `CloudSettings`, **all off by default** (frames with them off are unchanged):

- `shadow_map`: a top-down **cloud transmittance map** darkens the **sun term only** of meshes
  (`lab_forward.wgsl`) and of the terrain (the shared colour pass); sky and ambient light are
  untouched, so a surface under a cloud keeps its sky light. The old screen-space pass that
  multiplied the whole pixel with a 0.35 floor is not drawn while the map is on.
- `fog_coupling`: the froxel fog's sun in-scatter reads the same map, so sunlit air shows god
  rays through gaps in the layer. It builds the map even with `shadow_map` off.
- `overcast_ibl`: the sky light (the atmosphere IBL, the terrain's hemisphere sky and the fog's
  sky ambient) greys and dims with the layer's mean coverage and column depth, by up to 60 %
  under a full, thick overcast. Earth skies only: airless and Mars skies never change.

The map is `R16Float`, `shadow_map_size` texels a side (512 by default) over
`shadow_map_extent_m` (20 km, about 39 m a texel) around the camera. Each texel holds the sun's
transmittance along the line through where it crosses the layer base: 16 samples of the same 3D
density the clouds pass draws. It is world-anchored (a texel keeps its cell while the camera
moves) and snapped to whole texels, so shadows do not swim. Each frame marches one sixteenth of
it (a band of rows) plus the strips a camera move brings in; a camera cut, a weather cut, a new
sun, a changed layer shape (altitudes, noise scales, weather tile, resolution, seed or pattern) or
a wind-drift jump of a texel marches it whole. Coverage, type, density and wind changes smaller
than a weather cut are followed by the band refresh within 16 frames (ADR-429). It fades to unshadowed over the outer 15 % of the
window, and nothing reads it with the sun under about 0.6°. Texture views keep clouds off.

```rust
use regia::prelude::*;
use regia::render::CloudSettings;

fn configure(app: &mut App) {
    app.insert_resource(CloudSettings {
        shadow_map: true,
        fog_coupling: true,
        overcast_ibl: true,
        ..CloudSettings::coverage_layer(0.45)
    });
}
```

### The air under the layer (ADR-5944)

With `shadow_map` on, the air between the eye and a surface is shadowed with the surface. No extra
switch: it follows `shadow_map`, and a frame with `shadow_map` off draws its air as before, byte
for byte.

- **Aerial perspective** (the atmosphere tables, Desktop High and Ultra). The tables are built for
  a clear sky. They now keep the sun's single scattering apart (`AtmosphereLuts::aerial_sun`), and
  the composite takes that share out of the stretches of each view ray that lie in the layer's
  shadow: the cloud transmittance map is read at 8, 4, then 2 points per 2 km of the ray (nearest
  first), with the lookup the surfaces use, so one transmittance dims the sun on a surface and in
  the air in front of it. Under a clear part of the sky nothing is removed.
- **The rest of the in-scatter** is multiple scattering: the sky's light and the lit ground's
  bounce, scattered again (a quarter to more than half of the in-scatter, by the tables). It
  follows the light on the ground under the layer: where the ray's air is shadowed it loses the
  sun's share of the clear ground light, and with `overcast_ibl` on the sky's share grays and dims
  by the same rule as the sky light on surfaces. Under one cover the air and the ground behind it
  then fall by the same factor.
- **Analytic haze** (`FogSettings` aerial mode, on meshes, terrain, impostors and grass): the sun
  glow, and the horizon sky term down to a floor of 0.12 (the sky's share of the clear ground
  light), fall with the map's mean at 4 points of the view ray. Today this rule shows only
  through rain and snow (below): a frame that draws the atmosphere tables switches the forward
  fog off, so the fog's own haze and the cloud map do not meet.

Why it matters: before, the haze kept the full sun over ground that had lost it. From eye height
that hardly shows; from high up, under a closed cover, the exposure rises for the darker ground and
the whole view washed out to blue-gray (ADR-5792 measured it on the forest demo). Now a cover
leaves the contrast of a high view where a clear sky has it.

The planet's own surface beyond the terrain (the land a sky pixel shows where its ray meets the
planet) is under the layer too: it loses the sun's share of its light by the map's value where the
ray meets it, and the air in front of it is shadowed like the air in front of the terrain.

The image light follows as well when `overcast_ibl` is on too: below the horizon it shows the
ground, and that ground is then the shadowed one (the sun's share of its light times the layer's
mean transmittance, the sky's share under the overcast rule). A wall, a tree or a hillside under
the cover no longer takes the bounce of a sunlit ground. The terrain's hemisphere ambient (the
bounce its slopes, its grass and its tree impostors take) uses the same ground. With `shadow_map`
alone the image light is unchanged (a texture view lit by it renders as with the map off), so steep
faces keep that bounce: switch the overcast sky light on with the map.

The GI probes (the Depth lighting option, the default of Desktop High and Ultra) are under the
layer too, with `shadow_map` alone. A probe ray's hit is lit by the sun through the tracer's own
shadow rays, which meet the terrain and the meshes and not the clouds; with the map on, the hits
keep the share of the sun the layer leaves on the ground on average (one minus its mean cover).
Before, the probes kept a sunlit ground's bounce under any cover, and what they light (a tree, a
wall, a hillside) stood pale against the shadowed ground: on High and Ultra, not on the tiers
without probes. To check it, set `render.set_gi_mode {"mode": "depth"}` under a closed cover with
the three cloud switches on: a wall with its back to the sun should be no brighter than the
ground at its foot.

Without the probes (the Balanced option) the terrain estimates the bounce a sloped face takes from
the ground before it; that ground's sunlit share falls with the cloud map too, so a cliff under a
cover no longer outshines the ground it stands on.

Limits: the map fades to lit beyond about 8.5 km of the camera (its window), so far air and far
land keep their sun; the image light's ground and the probes' sun take the layer's mean cover, not
the cover over each place (in the shadow of one cloud of a broken layer the probes keep the mean
share of the sunlit bounce); a baked GI volume and the terrain's bounce grid for meshes (the
Balanced option) keep the frame's sun, and so do the effect layer's particles; the cloud layer's
own aerial perspective is not shadowed; the froxel fog needs `fog_coupling`, as before.

Rain and snow are under the layer too (frames without the table air). Each surface mixes toward
the precipitation's in-scatter over its distance; with `shadow_map` on that in-scatter takes the
map's mean along the view ray, by the haze's rule: in the fog's sky in-scatter mode the sun glow
goes and the sky term falls to its 0.12 floor, and in the flat mode the fog's color falls to 0.12
of its clear-day radiance under a closed cover (meshes, terrain and grass). The flat color on
meshes is display-referred at the scene's exposure setting, so this assumes the final exposure
adapts on its own (the auto exposure); a host that sets the exposure by hand for the cover gets a
weaker veil on meshes. The floor is a
constant: with `overcast_ibl` on as well the ground dims further than the veil, so the far ground
through rain stays paler than on a clear day. The table air's veil (`aerial_from_tables`,
ADR-3294) keeps its own deck rule.

`render.get_clouds` reports it under `shadow_map.air`: `shadowed` (the air reads the map: the
`shadow_map` switch), `steps` (`[8, 4, 2]`), `haze_steps` (4) and `overcast` (true when
`overcast_ibl` also dims the sky's share of the light the air's multiple scattering follows). In Rust,
`FrameRenderer::cloud_air_frames()` counts the frames whose aerial perspective read the map.

```json
{ "method": "render.set_clouds", "params": { "shadow_map": true, "overcast_ibl": true } }
{ "method": "render.get_clouds" }
```

The second call answers with `"shadow_map": { "enabled": true, ..., "air": { "shadowed": true,
"steps": [8, 4, 2], "haze_steps": 4, "overcast": true } }`.

Proposed preset defaults (ADR-320; not on yet): Desktop High and Ultra on, every other preset
off.

### Agent methods

- `render.get_clouds` → `{ source: "resource" | "level" | "default", coverage, cloud_type,
  density, altitude_bottom, altitude_top, wind_m_per_s, time_s, shadow_map: { enabled, built,
  size, extent_m, texel_m, refresh_fraction, steps, air: { shadowed, steps, haze_steps, overcast }
  }, fog_coupling, overcast_ibl }`. `built` is
  true when any switch that needs the map is on; `refresh_fraction` is 1/16; `air` is the air
  under the layer (ADR-5944, above).
- `render.set_clouds { coverage?, cloud_type?, density?, shadow_map?, shadow_map_size?,
  shadow_map_extent_m?, fog_coupling?, overcast_ibl? }` → `{ before, after }`. Changes only the
  fields given and writes the app's `CloudSettings` resource (starting from the level's clouds
  when there is no resource), which then wins over the level. An airless planet still forces the
  frame's coverage to 0 and skips the pass, including a cirrus sheet on the resource. `get_clouds`
  returns the stored resource and does not apply that zero. `shadow_map_size` is clamped to
  64..2048 and `shadow_map_extent_m` to 1000..200000. A wrong type (a string for a number, a
  number for a switch) answers error `F0002` (invalid parameters) and changes nothing. A number that
  is not finite, or that does not fit in `f32`, is the same `F0002` and changes nothing (it is not
  stored as a non-finite look override).
- `render.set_clouds` also takes the genus and look fields, documented on their pages: `genus`,
  `diffusion`, `erosion`, `breakup`, `breakup_scale_m`, `cirrus_coverage`, `cirrus_altitude_m`,
  `cirrus_optical_depth`, `cirrus_scale_m` and `cirrus_stretch` ([cloud types](book/agents/cloud-types.md));
  `cirrus_fiber`, `cirrus_fiber_scale_m`, `cirrus_shear_deg`, `cirrus_shear`, `cirrus_breakup` and
  `cirrus_hook` ([fibrous cirrus](book/agents/cirrus-fibrous.md)); `cirrus_crisp` ([crisp cirrus](book/agents/cirrus-crisp.md));
  and `clear_look_override` (below). Values are clamped to each field's range.
- **Look override** (ADR-1492). When a `Weather` drives the layer (a showcase scene always has one),
  the weather step rewrites the genus layer's look every fixed step. The look fields given to
  `render.set_clouds` (`diffusion`, `erosion`, `breakup`, `breakup_scale_m`, `cirrus_*`) are therefore
  also kept in the weather as an override applied over the genus look every step, so
  `render.get_clouds` right after returns what was set and it stays. `render.get_clouds` and
  `set_clouds` report `look_override: { active, fields }` (only the pinned fields). Later calls merge
  into the pins; `clear_look_override: true` drops them all (given together with look fields, the
  fields are pinned afresh) and the genus look returns on the next step. A scene can pin the same
  values with `cloud_look` in `sky.ron` ([showcase](book/agents/showcase.md)). Without a `Weather` nothing
  overwrites the resource and `look_override` is inactive. `genus`, `coverage`, `cloud_type` and
  `density` are still the weather's to set (`render.set_weather`).
- Debug view `cloud_shadow_map` (`DebugViewMode::CloudShadowMap` on the `DebugView` resource, or
  the editor viewport's `debug_view: "cloud_shadow_map"`): the frame is replaced by the map, grey
  by the sun's transmittance at every surface (white lit, black shadowed) and, on the sky, where
  the view ray meets the layer base. It builds the map even with the switches off.

```json
{ "method": "render.set_clouds", "params": { "shadow_map": true, "fog_coupling": true } }
{ "method": "render.get_clouds" }
```

`CloudSettings` is a resource; coverage zero skips the pass. Defaults are a cumulus layer from
1.5 km to 4 km. A map can instead set `cloud_coverage` / `cloud_type` in
`LevelSettings.atmosphere`; an explicit `CloudSettings` resource wins.

```rust
use regia::prelude::*;
use regia::render::CloudSettings;

fn configure(app: &mut App) {
    app.insert_resource(CloudSettings::coverage_layer(0.45));
}
```

Wind is `wind_m_per_s` times `time_s`, plus `drift_offset_m`; it moves the weather and the noise.
Nothing advances `time_s` on its own: a game does, or the [`Weather`](book/agents/weather.md) resource does
(it also integrates the drift, so a wind change does not jump the clouds). The map is re-packed
only when coverage, type, tile size, resolution, seed or pattern change, and a coverage or type
change re-thresholds a cached noise field into the same texture (ADR-429).

## Checks

- `cloud_coverage_matches_the_setting_within_ten_percent`: a top-down march of the full 3D
  density covers 25 %, 50 % and 75 % of the tile within ±10 % of the setting.
- `clouds_are_clear_at_zero_coverage_and_shaped_by_density`: coverage 0 leaves the sky
  byte-identical; moving the cloud field (wind) changes the sky, so cloud brightness comes from
  the density, not from the view direction; local contrast is far above the clear sky's.
- `clouds_horizon_shows_structure_along_the_shell`, `clouds_inside_the_layer_are_lit`,
  `clouds_above_the_layer_leave_gaps`, `clouds_occlude_a_far_peak_and_leave_a_near_one`:
  horizon curvature, a lit in-layer view, gaps when looking down, and occlusion of a far
  peak with a near peak left in front.
- `shell_matches_f64_on_a_planet_sphere`: the curved shell against the same expression in f64.
- `cloud_temporal.rs` (regia_test_utils): held-camera flicker at most half the full
  march's, converging to it, with nothing allocated per steady frame; a 45°/s pan at 120 m/s
  and a 40 m/s wind (60 fps) leave the clouds undisplaced, with an error a small part of the
  motion's own image change, and the pan settles back within 16 held frames; the frame
  after a camera cut has SSIM ≥ 0.95 against a full march; a texture
  view renders the same with and without clouds and leaves the main view's clouds unchanged.
  `cloud_temporal_cost_at_1440p` (ignored) times the pass continuously, full vs reprojected,
  64 and 96 steps, cone light on and off.
- `clouds_at_sunset_are_warm_and_lit` (golden `clouds_sunset`, the sun 2° up, found by
  bisection on the solar model, looking away from the sun): at least an eighth of the cloud
  pixels are warm (R > 1.15 B), and those sunlit faces are brighter than the shaded rest.
  `clouds_stay_lit_after_the_camera_sunset`: with the sun just below the camera's table horizon
  (found by bisection on the camera's table sun, ~−1.7° at 3 m), the camera has no sun, the
  layer top still has some, and far cloud rims toward the sun are redder than the clear sky
  (a smoke check: the soft table horizon leaves only the upper layer lit). `cone_light_changes_the_clouds_but_keeps_the_layer`: cone
  on vs off differ but keep the layer (SSIM > 0.6). The ignored
  `cloud_lighting_lookdev_dump` writes 640×360 noon, sunset and dusk views, cone on and off.
- `a_raised_layer_keeps_the_sun_after_the_camera_sunset` (`transmitted_sun_at`) and
  `curl_field_tiles_and_is_divergence_free` (unit tests).
- Cloud shadow map (ADR-320, unit tests in `regia_render::clouds`):
  `cloud_shadow_march_matches_an_f64_reference` (the f32 map march equals the same 16-step march
  in f64 within 5e-3 of transmittance near the origin and 75 km out, and a 4096-step f64
  integral within 0.02), `cloud_shadow_window_snaps_to_texels` (sub-texel camera moves keep the
  window and a world point's texel; a whole-texel move shifts the window one cell and the point
  keeps its texel), `cloud_shadow_refresh_covers_the_map_in_16_frames` (16 frames march every
  texel exactly once, counted; moved windows march the strips they bring in),
  `cloud_shadow_lookup_follows_the_sun_line` and `cloud_shadow_switches_are_off_by_default`.
- Overcast (ADR-321): `overcast_factor_grows_with_coverage`,
  `overcast_applies_only_to_earth_with_the_switch` (Mars, airless and switch-off measure 0),
  `overcast_zero_leaves_the_ibl_unchanged` (factor 0 is the clear bake bit for bit).
- Shaders: `cloud_shadow_lookup_composes_and_is_gated` (the lookup composes and validates; the
  forward and fog shaders read the map only under its switch; all composed variants validate),
  `terrain_cloud_lookup_matches_the_engine` (the terrain splices the same lookup text).
- Frames (`cloud_shadow.rs`, regia_test_utils): `switches_off_leave_the_frame_unchanged`,
  `shadow_map_shadows_the_sun_term_only` (shadowed ground darker, not black),
  `fog_coupling_shadows_the_sunlit_air` (the fog only loses light),
  `overcast_ibl_dims_earth_and_leaves_mars_and_airless`, `debug_view_shows_the_map`; ignored
  bench `cloud_shadow_cost_at_1440p` (map in `shadows_ms`, coupling in `fog_ms`).
- The air under the layer (ADR-5944). Frames (`cloud_shadow_haze.rs`, regia_test_utils):
  `the_air_under_the_cloudy_half_loses_its_sun` (over a black ground the frame is the air and
  little else: the half under a split sky's layer loses its sun, on the side where the ground is
  shadowed, and the clear half keeps what it has with no layer), `a_high_view_keeps_its_contrast_under_a_closed_cover` (dark and
  bright ground patches from 1.2 km up: under a closed cover, exposed to the clear frame's level,
  they keep at least 0.85 of the clear sky's contrast, with the map alone and with the overcast
  sky light), `the_cover_shadows_all_of_the_ground_in_view`,
  `the_planets_surface_beyond_the_terrain_is_shadowed_too`,
  `a_wall_under_the_cover_takes_no_sunlit_grounds_bounce`,
  `rain_under_the_cover_scatters_the_covers_light` (forward surfaces through rain in the fog's sky
  in-scatter mode keep at least 0.85 of the clear sky's contrast under the map),
  `rain_in_the_flat_fog_mode_under_the_cover_keeps_the_contrast` (the same in the flat mode, the
  final exposure adapting away from the scene's setting),
  `the_probes_under_the_cover_gather_no_sunlit_bounce` (a wall with its back to the sun on open
  ground under a closed cover: with the GI probes it reads at most 1.6 times what the image light
  alone gives it, and under a clear sky the probes' wall is more than twice as bright), and on the
  terrain
  `rain_under_a_closed_cover_scatters_the_covers_light` (`terrain_surface_weather.rs`,
  regia_terrain: exposed for the near ground, the far ground through rain is no brighter under the

  (the same file: a cliff's face is no brighter than the flat ground before it),
  `the_air_reads_the_map_only_with_the_switch_on` (the renderer's count of such frames: none with

  airless world). Unit tests:
  `the_sun_table_is_a_share_of_the_aerial_table`,

  (`regia_render::clouds`), `the_image_lights_ground_follows_the_cover_when_the_map_shadows_it`,

# Weather

The `Weather` resource (`regia_vfx::weather`, ADR-429) drives the [volumetric cloud
layer](book/agents/clouds.md): coverage, cloud type, density and wind, plus a precipitation value for games to
read. `VfxPlugin` installs the driver (`WeatherPlugin`); nothing happens until a `Weather` resource
exists. Each frame the driver steps it by the game's `Time` (so it pauses and scales with the game)
and writes the result into the `CloudSettings` resource. Coverage, type, density, wind, the
clock and the drift are always written. The genus presets `fair_cumulus`, `cumulus`,
`stratocumulus` and `cirrus` also write altitudes, `shape_scale_m`, `detail_scale_m` and look.
The other presets leave those fields alone. `shadow_map`, `fog_coupling` and `overcast_ibl`
stay as they are.

- **Presets**: `clear`, `fair`, `cloudy`, `overcast` (a low grey stratus deck) and `storm`
  (towering, dense cells in a strong wind), `rain`, `snow` and `blizzard`, and the genus presets
  `fair_cumulus`, `cumulus`, `stratocumulus` and `cirrus` (those four also rewrite the layer
  heights, noise tiles and look).
  `WeatherState::preset(name)`.
- **Transitions** ease with a smoothstep over a given number of seconds of game time. While one
  runs, coverage and cloud type are written in steps of 1/256 and density in 1/64-octave steps, so
  the CPU re-thresholds the weather map at most once per step (a cached noise field, written into
  the same texture: no texture or bind group is created). At rest the values are exact.
- **Wind** drift is integrated over the weather clock and handed to the renderer as
  `CloudSettings::drift_offset_m`: a wind change carries the clouds on from where they are and keeps
  the cloud history valid. (Setting `wind_m_per_s` on `CloudSettings` directly still moves the
  clouds by `wind × time_s`, so a change there jumps them.)
- **Weather cuts**: a change of more than 0.05 coverage, 0.1 cloud type or a 1.25× density ratio in
  one frame (for example `set_now` to another preset, or a `transition_s` of 0) is a cut. That frame
  marches the clouds and the cloud shadow map whole, like a camera cut. Smaller changes are followed
  by the reprojection: the history is clamped toward the fresh samples in proportion to how far
  the weather moved since it was marched, so a transition does not trail its old sky.
- **Precipitation** (`0..1`), with the temperature and the kind, gives what falls: `rain`, `snow` and
  `blizzard` are presets too. With the project's effects on it draws rain and snow, wets surfaces and
  moves the wind near the ground: see [Rain, snow and wet surfaces](book/agents/weather-precipitation.md). With
  them off (the default) it stays a value to read, `Weather::rates(&config)` or
  `Weather::current().precipitation`.

```rust
use regia::prelude::*;
use regia_vfx::{Weather, WeatherState};

fn start_storm(mut weather: ResMut<Weather>) {
    // Two minutes from whatever the sky shows now to a storm.
    weather.transition_to(WeatherState::STORM, 120.0);
}

fn configure(app: &mut App) {
    app.insert_resource(Weather::new(WeatherState::FAIR));
}
```

## Agent methods

- `render.get_weather` → `{ active, current: { coverage, cloud_type, density, wind_m_per_s,
  precipitation, genus, temperature_c, precipitation_kind, gustiness }, target, transitioning,
  progress, remaining_s, clock_s, drift_m, paused, cloud_layer: { coverage, cloud_type, density,
  wind_m_per_s, drift_m }, presets, rates: { snow_fraction, rain_mm_per_h, snow_we_mm_per_h,
  snow_depth_mm_per_h, drop_lambda_per_mm, visibility_m }, config: { path, format_version, error } }`.
  `visibility_m` is null when nothing falls. Without a
  `Weather` resource `active` is false and `current` is the weather the cloud layer shows (the
  transition fields are absent).
- `render.set_weather { preset?, coverage?, cloud_type?, density?, wind_m_per_s?: [x, z],
  precipitation?, temperature_c?, precipitation_kind?, gustiness?, transition_s?, paused? }` →
  `{ before, after }`. Builds the target from `preset` (a built-in one or one of the project's;
  else the current target) with the given fields replaced and eases to it over `transition_s`
  seconds of game time (0 or absent: at once, a weather cut). With no `Weather` resource it creates
  one from the current cloud layer first, so a call that changes nothing moves nothing. The cloud
  layer is written straight away (`render.get_clouds` shows it before the next frame). `paused`
  stops or resumes the clock, the transition and the wind drift.
- Errors: an unknown preset, a wrong type (a string for a number, `wind_m_per_s` that is not two
  finite numbers, a non-boolean `paused`) or a negative `transition_s` answers `F0002` (invalid
  parameters) and changes nothing.

```json
{ "method": "render.set_weather", "params": { "preset": "overcast", "transition_s": 30 } }
{ "method": "render.get_weather" }
```

To watch a transition, step frames (`playtest` frame stepping or `wait_until`) and poll
`render.get_weather` until `transitioning` is false; a screenshot per step shows the sky change.

## Cost

Per frame, a held camera marches one low-resolution texel in sixteen and one sixteenth of the cloud
shadow map whatever the weather does; `regia_render::cloud_steady_work` gives the count and
`CLOUD_FRAME_SAMPLE_BUDGET` (about 4 M density samples, Desktop High at 1440p with the map on) is
the budget it is tested against. `cloud_work_counters()` counts what the renderer actually did
(view frames marched whole or reprojected, texels marched, map texels, weather map packs, uploads,
textures and weather cuts).

## Checks

- Unit (`regia_vfx::weather`): presets in range; a transition eases monotonically to the exact
  target; turning the wind at t = 1000 s moves the drift by at most `wind × dt` a frame and equals
  the integrated drift; a 10 s clear-to-overcast transition has no weather-cut frame and changes the
  weather map at most once per 1/256 step; `set_now` is a cut and keeps the layer's switches;
  paused weather holds; taking over a layer moves nothing; in an app the plugin follows game time.
- Unit (`regia_render::clouds`): the wind row is unchanged without a drift offset; the CPU weather
  sample follows the integrated drift; the cached weather field gives byte-identical maps;
  weather cuts against transition steps; the weather motion is 0 when still and 1 at a cut; the
  Desktop High 1440p frame fits the sample budget and the full march does not.
- Agent (`regia_agent::weather`): get without weather, set a preset at once, a transition with
  overrides and partial follow-up sets, every bad parameter answers F0002.
- Frames (`regia_vfx/tests/cloud_weather.rs`, GPU): `wind_change_keeps_the_clouds_in_place`
  (no history reset, no displacement, a small error against the full march),
  `weather_cut_marches_the_whole_frame` (SSIM ≥ 0.95 against a fresh full march),
  `coverage_transition_tracks_the_full_march` (half way and after settling),
  `weather_transition_stays_inside_the_work_budget` (counted: exactly the steady-state texels a
  frame, no whole-map march, no texture, bind group or pipeline created); ignored bench
  `cloud_weather_cost_at_1440p` (clouds and map ms, held and in transition, against 0.7 ms).

## Haze and rain from the atmosphere tables (`aerial_from_tables`)

On a frame that draws the physical sky (the atmosphere tables: Desktop High and Ultra on Earth,
any HDR single-sample frame on another planet), the sky shades from the sky-view table and the
ground from the aerial-perspective table. By default two things still split them at the horizon:

- the aerial table ends at 32 km, so ground farther out keeps the 32 km haze while the sky's last
  row holds the whole path through the air;
- the falling rain's or snow's extinction (`Weather::rates(&config).visibility_m`) reaches only the
  ground (forward pass, lite pass, shared terrain), with the analytic stand-in sky as its colour,
  and the sky stays as clear as on a dry day.

`RenderProfile::aerial_from_tables` (off in every preset, ADR-3294) moves both onto the tables:
past 32 km the ground's haze keeps thickening toward the sky's first row above the horizon, and the
extinction becomes one full-screen veil after the clouds over the sky, the clouds and the ground
alike, mixing by `exp(−σ d)` (`d` is the pixel's distance, the far plane for the sky) toward the
light the drops scatter: the average over the whole sphere of the horizon sky above, the lit
ground below and the sun's share, with a drawn cloud deck greying and dimming all of it and
blocking the sun. So heavy rain under a deck dims the sky and the ground together. Every term is table radiance in cd/m² times the HDR target's pre-exposure,
the same units the forward pass writes. Frames without the physical sky do not change.

Cost per pixel, in texel loads: the full path reads two aerial slices (8 loads; 12 past 32 km);
the Mobile (lite) path reads one slice (4; 8 past 32 km); the veil adds 4 while something falls.
No froxel volume either way.

- `render.get_weather` adds `aerial_tables: { enabled, frame_mode, fetches_per_pixel: { aerial,
  aerial_past_range, veil }, seam: { off, on, far_m, extinction_per_m, sun_elevation_deg } }`.
  `enabled` is the profile switch (null without a `RenderSettings` resource); `frame_mode` is what
  an atmosphere frame of this profile draws (`off`, `full`, or `lite` on a lite-forward profile).
  `seam` is the horizon seam both modes give, from a CPU model of the tables for the current
  `TimeOfDay` (Earth's air, the eye 2 m up, the farthest ground 50 km out) and the current
