`8` is Hole: a click cuts a round hole of the brush's size, a drag cuts a slot along it as wide as the
brush, and Shift removes the named hole under the release point. Each is one undo step. The first
hole edit brings in the level's `<map>.holes.ron`; a file that cannot be read turns hole edits off
rather than being replaced. Agents cut the same holes with `terrain.set_hole`
([terrain runtime](book/agents/terrain-runtime.md)).
`9` is Scatter, the brush for mesh instances: see [painted scatter](book/agents/terrain-scatter-paint.md).

## Saving holes and paint

Every save a user asks for (Save, Save As, saving on close) and the agent's `editor.save_level` write
the same set: the level, the re-cooked tiles of a sculpted terrain, and next to the level the files
below, each only when it changed. The `editor.save_level` reply names them in `terrain_tiles_recooked`,
`terrain_holes_file` and `terrain_paint_file`. The autosave stays a recovery copy of the level alone.

| File | Holds | Agent |
|---|---|---|
| `<map>.holes.ron` | named and unnamed holes | `terrain.save_holes`, `terrain.load_holes` |
| `<map>.weights.bin` | painted layer weights (`LayerWeightMap`, versioned) | `terrain.save_paint`, `terrain.load_paint` |

`terrain.save_paint { path, entity? }` and `terrain.load_paint { path, entity? }` take a map or level
file (`maps/arena.level.ron` means `maps/arena.weights.bin`) or a name ending in `.weights.bin`, under
the project root. A save writes atomically and replaces the file; a load needs the terrain's grid.

- `terrain.save_paint` replies `{ entity, path, width, height, layers, bytes }`.
- `terrain.load_paint` replies `{ entity, path, width, height, layers }` and uploads the weights.
  A weights file over 1 GiB + 1 MiB (the largest weight map, 2^30 weights, plus its header) is
  refused before it is read (`height_io_decode`), so whatever `terrain.save_paint` wrote loads back.
- Errors: `F0002` (bad path), `F0003` (no terrain, or no paint to save), `height_io_write`,
  `height_io_read`, `height_io_decode`, `height_io_size_mismatch`.

Check it: `terrain.save_paint`, then `terrain.load_paint` in a fresh session and compare a
`seeing.screenshot` of the same camera.

A host that spawns the terrain loads these files itself, with `regia_terrain::load_holes_ron` and
`LayerWeightMap::from_bytes`. A level that names its terrain (scene v12, [Level terrain](book/agents/level-terrain.md))
brings it and its side files in on its own, and [New terrain](#new-terrain) creates one.

## Heightmap export and import

A save re-cooks only the cooked heightfield. To carry sculpted heights back into the terrain's
source file, export them:

```json
{ "method": "terrain.export_heights", "params": { "path": "terrain/island.r16" } }
```

```json
{ "entity": 4294967297, "path": "terrain/island.r16", "format": "r16", "width": 4097,
  "height": 4097, "bytes": 33570818, "clamped_low": 0, "clamped_high": 12 }
```

- `path` is relative to the project root (no `..`); parent folders are created; the file is
  written atomically.
- `format`: `png` (16-bit grayscale) or `r16` (headerless, `endian` `little` by default or `big`);
  by default taken from the extension (`.png`, `.r16`, `.raw`).
- The samples are the map's 16-bit grid, the encoding a save uses; row 0 is the −Z edge, the order
  the cooker's PNG import reads. `clamped_low` / `clamped_high` count samples sculpted below or
  above the map's height range (written as 0 or 65535).

`terrain.import_heights` reads a file back onto the terrain:

```json
{ "method": "terrain.import_heights", "params": { "path": "terrain/island.r16" } }
```

<!-- not-a-request -->
```json
{ "entity": 4294967297, "path": "terrain/island.r16", "format": "r16", "width": 4097,
  "height": 4097, "changed": 5210, "undoable": true,
  "dirty": { "col_start": 1201, "col_end": 1390, "row_start": 640, "row_end": 702 } }
```

The file's grid must be the terrain's (`terrain.get` reports it). A RAW file without `width` and
`height` is read as a square. Only changed samples are written; the GPU re-uploads the dirty
rectangle and a save re-cooks the touched tiles. In the editor the import is one undo step
(`undoable` is false only past 4 194 304 changed samples).

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `height_io_bad_format` | unknown `format` or `endian`, or no extension to tell the format |
| `height_io_write` | the file could not be written |
| `height_io_read` | the file could not be read |
| `height_io_decode` | not a 16-bit grayscale PNG, or a RAW of the wrong length |
| `height_io_size_mismatch` | the file's grid is not the terrain's |

Check a round trip: `terrain.export_heights` to `a.r16`, `terrain.import_heights` from it, and
`changed` is 0 on a terrain that was saved and reloaded.

The headless editor runs the same CPU terrain frame effects as the windowed editor:
opening a level loads its named terrain, and agent strokes enter the editor undo stack.
This path works with `--no-gpu`; rendering and screenshot evidence still require a device.

## New terrain

`editor.terrain_create` makes a terrain from nothing, as the Terrain panel's **New terrain…**
dialog (and **Content ▸ New ▸ Terrain…**) does (ADR-7727). It is an editor method because the cook
runs in the editor's asset pipeline.

```json
{ "method": "editor.terrain_create",
  "params": { "name": "hills", "size": 129, "cell_size": 1.0, "height_range": [-10.0, 90.0] } }
```

<!-- not-a-request -->
```json
{ "job": "terrain_create:1", "state": "done",
  "layers": "assets/maps/hills/hills.terrain.layers.ron", "folder": "assets/maps/hills",
  "files": ["assets/maps/hills/heightfield.json", "assets/maps/hills/heightfield.png",
            "assets/maps/hills/hills.terrain.layers.ron", "assets/maps/hills/hills.terrain.layers.ron.meta"],
  "map_id": "…", "cooked": 2, "warnings": ["…"], "size": 129, "cell_size": 1.0,
  "world_width_m": 128.0, "height_range": [-10.0, 90.0],
  "terrain": { "layers": "maps/hills/hills.terrain.layers.ron", "map": "maps/hills/hills",
               "world_width_m": 128.0, "height_scale_m": 100.0, "height_offset_m": -10.0 },
  "entity": 4294967310, "loaded": true }
```

- **Files.** The cook convention (`docs/formats/terrain.md` § 9) in `assets/<folder>/<name>/`:
  the layer file and its `.meta` (the map id), `heightfield.png` (16-bit gray, flat at the height
  nearest 0 m inside `height_range`, or the heightmap's samples) and `heightfield.json`
  (`size_m`). Layers are `layers` (names, bottom first; `grass`, `rock` and `dirt` get slope
  presets), else grass, rock and dirt when the project has `assets/starter/terrain/<layer>/`
  for each (their `albedo`, `normal`, `orm`, `height` PNGs are copied to `detail/<layer>/`), else
  one `ground` layer. No format changes: these are the existing layer and heightfield files.
- **Sizes.** `size` is samples a side: 129, 257, 513, 1025, 2049 or 4097. `cell_size` is 0.25,
  0.5, 1, 2 or 4 m; the world width is `(size − 1) · cell_size`.
- **Sample layout** (ADR-10079). `sample_layout` is `VertexCentered` (the default: samples on the
  edges, the width above) or `CellCentered`: each sample is the center of a `cell_size` cell, so
  the terrain is `size · cell_size` wide and the level's block names the layout (use it for a
  heightmap whose pixels are areas). `heightfield.json` keeps the samples' span
  `(size − 1) · cell_size`. The New terrain dialog's **Samples at cell centers** box sets it. Any
  other value is `terrain_create_bad_params`.
- **Import as new.** `heightmap` (a project-relative 16-bit `.png`, `.r16` or `.raw`; `endian`
  for RAW) starts from a file: its samples are kept, its size is the terrain's (`size`, if given,
  must match). Exporting terrain A with `terrain.export_heights` and creating B from that file
  gives B A's samples.
- **The job.** The files are written and cooked in a staging folder under the project's state
  directory, then moved into `assets/` in one rename. Without `async` the call waits and answers
  the terrain; `async: true` answers `{ job, state: "running" }` (poll `agent.job_status`).
  `editor.cancel_job { id }` cancels it: the staging folder and the cooked files of the new map id
  are removed, so nothing is left. A cancel after the rename is too late and the job ends `done`.
- **The level.** The open level's `LevelSettings::terrain` names the terrain (one undo step;
  `terrain.level_terrain` reports it), and the terrain is built with a cook target, so
  `terrain.stroke` and the terrain tool work on it at once. `loaded` is false for a level that was
  never saved; it is built once the level has a path. `editor.undo` removes the level's reference
  and the built terrain; the files stay.

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `terrain_create_bad_params` | a missing `name`, a parameter of the wrong kind, `height_range` not `[min, max]` with min < max, a bad layer list (none, more than 8, a name twice), or a `sample_layout` other than `VertexCentered` or `CellCentered` |
| `terrain_create_bad_name` | the terrain or a layer name is not 1..=64 ASCII letters, digits, `_` or `-` |
| `terrain_create_bad_path` | the folder is not under `assets/`, has `..`, or leads out of the project through a symlink; or the heightmap path does |
| `terrain_create_exists` | `assets/<folder>/<name>` exists |
| `terrain_create_bad_size` | `size` or `cell_size` is not an allowed value, or the heightmap is not square at an allowed size, or `size` differs from it |
| `terrain_create_bad_heightmap` | the heightmap is missing, over the size limit, not a `.png`/`.r16`/`.raw`, or does not decode |
| `terrain_create_no_project` | the editor has no project open |
| `terrain_create_busy` | another create runs |
| `terrain_create_failed` | a write, the cook or the move into `assets/` failed (nothing is left) |
| `terrain_create_cancelled` | the job was cancelled (nothing is left) |

## Brush shoulder controls

The Terrain panel has keyboard-focusable **Size**, **Strength**, **Falloff** and **Falloff curve**
sliders. Tab reaches a slider; arrow keys adjust it. Size is the circle radius in meters
(rectangles also expose Length). Falloff is hardness: 0 fades from the center, 1 keeps full
strength to the edge. The viewport's inner ring marks the full-strength interior. The existing
`[` / `]` and `-` / `=` shortcuts change these same size and strength values. In the existing
Grass density and Scatter modes, Strength follows those modes' target-density shortcuts.
The curve selector applies to height/layer strokes and is disabled for holes, scatter and grass density.

`terrain.stroke` accepts `falloff: "smooth" | "linear" | "sphere" | "tip"`. Omission preserves
the existing smooth curve and its deterministic output. For inward coverage `t` after hardness:
Smooth uses the existing raised cosine, Linear uses `t`, Sphere uses `sqrt(t*(2-t))`, and Tip
uses `1-sqrt(1-t*t)`. The curve affects height and layer-weight strokes, including threaded
viewport strokes. An unknown curve or a non-string `falloff` returns the standard invalid-params
error (`F0002`); no stroke is applied.

## Terrain regions: editor.terrain_region

Enable **Region mode** in the Terrain panel and drag a rectangle on the terrain. The panel's
Column, Row, Width and Height fields provide the same selection entirely from the keyboard.
The paste destination is the cursor's sample column/row, also editable in Paste column/row.
**Copy region**, **Paste region**, **Export region** and **Import region** are focusable buttons;
Tab then Enter operates them. Quarter turns and Height offset control paste placement.

```json
{"method":"editor.terrain_region","params":{"op":"copy","rect":[10,20,8,4]}}
{"method":"editor.terrain_region","params":{"op":"paste","at":[30,20],"rotation":90,"height_offset":2.5}}
{"method":"editor.terrain_region","params":{"op":"export","rect":[10,20,8,4],"path":"assets/maps/region.png"}}
{"method":"editor.terrain_region","params":{"op":"import","rect":[30,20,8,4],"path":"assets/maps/region.png"}}
```

Parameters:

- `op` (required): `copy`, `paste`, `export` or `import`.
- `entity`: terrain entity id; default the selected terrain, otherwise the first terrain.
- `rect`: `[column,row,width,height]` in samples; default the panel selection. Both ends of a
  pointer-selected rectangle are included. The rectangle must be wholly inside the terrain.
- `at`: paste's minimum `[column,row]`; default the cursor/panel destination.
- `rotation`: clockwise degrees, exactly 0, 90, 180 or 270; default the panel's Quarter turns.
  A 90/270-degree rotation swaps width and height. Rotation permutes samples without interpolation.
- `height_offset`: meters added to pasted heights; default the panel value (initially 0).
- `path`: project-relative `.png`, `.r16` or `.raw` interchange path; default the panel's Region file.
- `endian`: RAW byte order, `little` or `big`; default the panel's Region RAW big-endian setting (initially off).

Copy keeps the exact floating-point heights and every byte weight plane in session memory.
Paste requires a destination with the same weight-layer count and grid dimensions as its own
terrain. It writes all changes as **one shared undo entry**, including overlapping copies and
rotations. A zero height offset copies float bits verbatim. Undo and redo restore original/final
bits, including weights. A paste that changes nothing adds no undo entry. The clipboard is not
saved with the project.

Export uses the existing 16-bit heightmap interchange encoding (map scale/offset, row 0 at −Z),
with clamp counts. RAW defaults to little-endian; PNG always uses its standard byte order. Import requires the file dimensions to match `rect`,
changes heights only, and is one undo step. Interchange regions must be at least 2×2 samples.
Interchange quantizes heights to 16 bits; the in-memory
clipboard does not. No layer weights are stored in these interchange files.

Replies: copy `{width,height,layers}`; paste/import `{changed,undoable:true}` (changed counts height
and weight values); export `{width,height,bytes,clamped_low,clamped_high}`. The maximum is 2^22 values
across heights and weight planes. The tool refuses oversized or out-of-bounds transfers, a missing
clipboard/terrain, mismatched weights, invalid parameters, unsafe paths and decode/I/O failures
with `terrain_region_invalid`. An active terrain stroke must finish before any region operation.
Rejected edits leave terrain data and undo/redo history unchanged. Dispatcher limits and permission
errors also apply; these methods require scene-edit permission.

Verification: `terrain_region` unit tests cover each non-square rotation, overlapping copy,
all weight planes, exact undo/redo, overflow/bounds rejection, offsets, and PNG/RAW interchange.
`terrain_kit_tools` drives the real dispatcher and the keyboard controls without a display.

## Edit layers (non-destructive)

A terrain can stack named **edit layers** over its base heights (ADR-7825). The terrain you see,
draw, collide with and cook is the base folded through every shown layer, bottom first; the
cooked heightfield holds that flattened result, so nothing changes at run time. Two blends:

- **add** layers add `opacity × delta`. Their order among themselves never changes a bit (the
  deltas of a run of add layers are summed in a fixed order before they are added).
- **set** layers move the height below them toward their own height where they were painted, by
  `coverage × opacity`. Their order matters: a set layer on top replaces the add layers under it;
  moved to the bottom, the add layers raise it.

Strokes (the editor's terrain tool, `terrain.stroke`, height imports) write the **active** layer:
the newest layer, the one picked with `terrain.edit_layer_set { active: true }`, or the base. A
stroke that lands is moved into the layer and its samples are rewritten from the fold, so hiding a
layer gives back exactly what the other layers made, bit for bit. A hidden, fully transparent or
locked layer refuses strokes. Showing, hiding, reordering, deleting or changing the opacity of a
layer recomputes only the samples that layer covers (`recomputed` in the reply,
`recomputed_samples` in `terrain.edit_layers`). In the editor every change and every layered
stroke is one undo step and restores the map and the layer bit for bit.

```json
{ "method": "terrain.edit_layer_create", "params": { "name": "Hills" } }
```

<!-- not-a-request -->
```json
{ "entity": 4294967297, "layer": 1, "active": 1, "recomputed": 0, "merged": 0,
  "layers": [ { "id": 1, "name": "Hills", "index": 0, "blend": "add", "enabled": true,
                "locked": false, "opacity": 1.0, "procgen": null, "bounds": null } ],
  "recomputed_samples": 0, "unsaved": true }
```

```json
{ "method": "terrain.stroke",
  "params": { "mode": "raise", "center": [120.0, -40.0], "radius": 12.0, "strength": 4.0,
              "edit_layer": "Hills" } }
```

`edit_layer` is a layer id, a layer name or `"base"`; without it the stroke writes the active
layer. (`layer` stays the painted material-weight layer.) The reply's `edit_layer` names the layer
written (`null` on a terrain without edit layers).

```json
{ "method": "terrain.edit_layer_set", "params": { "layer": "Hills", "enabled": false } }
```

```json
{ "method": "terrain.edit_layer_reorder", "params": { "layer": "Hills", "index": 0 } }
```

```json
{ "method": "terrain.edit_layer_flatten", "params": {} }
```

| Method | Does |
|---|---|
| `terrain.edit_layers` | the stack, bottom first: id, name, index, blend, enabled, locked, opacity, procgen (`{ graph, output }` or null), bounds; the active layer |
| `terrain.edit_layer_create { name, blend? }` | a layer on top (`add` by default, or `set`), made active |
| `terrain.edit_layer_set { layer, name?, enabled?, locked?, opacity?, active? }` | rename, show or hide, lock, opacity `0..=1`; `active: true` makes it (or `"base"`) the stroke target |
| `terrain.edit_layer_delete { layer }` | removes an unlocked layer; its samples go back to the layers below |
| `terrain.edit_layer_reorder { layer, index }` | moves a layer, 0 is the bottom |
| `terrain.edit_layer_flatten` | bakes every shown layer into the base and removes them (hidden ones stay); the terrain does not change by a bit. Enabled weight deltas are baked into the base weights |
| `terrain.edit_layer_weights { col, row }` | the folded material weights at one sample: `weights` (eight numbers) and `sum` (1) |
| `terrain.edit_layer_paint_weights { layer?, col, row, channels }` | sets the base weights or one layer's signed delta. A short `channels` array is padded with 0. The reply's `weights` are the folded channels and sum to 1 |
| `terrain.edit_layer_procgen { layer, graph?, output?, detach? }` | attaches a procgen graph and output, or `detach: true` clears it. Undoable |

```json
{ "method": "terrain.edit_layer_paint_weights",
  "params": { "layer": "Hills", "col": 0, "row": 0, "channels": [0.0, 1.0] } }
```

```json
{ "method": "terrain.edit_layer_weights", "params": { "col": 0, "row": 0 } }
```

```json
{ "method": "terrain.edit_layer_procgen",
  "params": { "layer": "Hills", "graph": "assets/hills.pgraph.ron", "output": "height" } }
```

```json
{ "method": "terrain.edit_layer_procgen", "params": { "layer": "Hills", "detach": true } }
```

Weights fold like this (ADR-8381). Start from the base (a missing sample is channel 0 at weight 1). Each enabled
layer with opacity above 0 adds `opacity ×` its signed delta, per channel. Clamp every negative channel to 0, then
divide by the sum. A sum of 0 is channel 0 at weight 1, the base material. An explicit all-zero base paint is stored
and is not the same as a missing sample; the fold of that paint with no deltas is still channel 0 at weight 1.

A layer with a procgen target is owned by that graph. `terrain.stroke` and `terrain.edit_layer_paint_weights` on it
return `edit_layer_owned` until `terrain.edit_layer_procgen` detaches the target. Publish from that graph writes only
the owned layer. If two layers name the same graph and output, the topmost wins. A generator with no target still
writes the base, as before.

In the editor the Terrain panel's **Edit layers** section does the same: Add layer (with Set
height layer for a set layer), a row per layer (top of the stack first) with select, Hide/Show,
Lock/Unlock, Move up, Move down, Delete and Opacity, a Name field and Rename for the active layer,
Base, and Flatten into base. An owned layer shows `owned by <graph> · <output>` and **Detach procgen**.
The active layer that is not owned has Procgen graph and Output fields and **Attach procgen**.
**Paint weight** writes channel 1 at sample (0, 0) and is disabled while the active layer is owned.
The panel shows the folded weights at (0, 0). Every control is reachable with Tab and works with
Enter, Space or the arrow keys. A level save writes `<map>.terrain.editlayers` version 2 beside the
level (`docs/formats/terrain-editlayers.md`); opening the level reads it back, including a version 1
file through the migrator. A file whose height fold no longer matches the cooked terrain (the terrain
was changed outside the layers) is refused, left on disk untouched, and the panel says why.

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `edit_layer_not_found` | no layer with that id or name |
| `edit_layer_no_terrain` | the entity has no terrain |
| `edit_layer_locked` | the layer is locked (strokes, delete and flatten are refused) |
| `edit_layer_hidden` | the layer is hidden or at opacity 0, so a stroke would not show |
| `edit_layer_limit` | already 32 layers |
| `edit_layer_bad_name` | a name is 1 to 64 printable characters |
| `edit_layer_bad_opacity` | opacity is in `0..=1` |
| `edit_layer_size_mismatch` | the layers were made for another heightfield size |
| `edit_layer_file_invalid` | the `.terrain.editlayers` file is malformed (editor) |
| `edit_layer_file_version` | the file is from a newer engine (editor) |
| `edit_layer_file_stale` | the terrain changed outside its layers since the file was written (editor) |
| `edit_layer_owned` | the layer is owned by a procgen graph; detach the target before a brush or a weight paint |
| `edit_layer_bad_weight` | `channels` has more than 8 numbers, or a number is not finite |
| `edit_layer_bad_target` | `graph` is not 1 to 256 characters, or `output` is not 1 to 64, or either is blank or has a control character |

## Unlayered height writers

Height patches, procedural publications, imports and direct map deformations are retained in
the edit-layer base (ADR-8202). Their height change is measured against the last composed
height, so toggling an Add layer does not erase it. A Set layer can cover a base change until
that layer is hidden. The editor reconciles direct writes before saving the v2
sidecar; named-layer strokes still use `terrain.stroke { edit_layer }`.

A host using the low-level map API should recompute the affected rectangle through
`TerrainEditLayers::recompute_terrain` after the write. This absorbs the change, updates the
composite and notes the dirty region for drawing and collision. Reconcile before directly
calling `flatten_into_base` or `to_bytes`; the world-level layer operations and editor save
perform that step automatically. That preservation adds no method parameters of its own.
On reopening cooked terrain, the loader recognizes its exact 16-bit cook/decode heights and
keeps the sidecar's authored precision. Other height mismatches still refuse the stale sidecar.

Material weights and a persisted procgen target are version 2 of the sidecar (ADR-8381). Paint
them with `terrain.edit_layer_paint_weights` and read the fold with `terrain.edit_layer_weights`.
Attach a target with `terrain.edit_layer_procgen`. A generator that carries `ProcTerrainOutput`
publishes into the matching layer and restores only that layer. A generator without that component
still publishes into the base and restores by the composite-value check.

<!-- source: book/agents/terrain-vt.md -->
# Terrain virtual texture

The terrain virtual texture caches the photoreal terrain surface in pages of one atlas, baked by
the terrain shader's own surface function. Pixels whose pages are resident read them instead of
shading the surface. It is opt-in: it trades a little texture sharpness for terrain shading cost.

## Methods

- `terrain.vt` reports whether it is on, its settings, and last frame's counters:
  - `resident_pages`.
  - `stats.baked` and `stats.rebaked`.
  - `stats.missing` and `stats.oldest_miss_frames` (how far behind the bakes are).
  - `stats.hit_rate`.
  - `stats.bake_ms` and `stats.reduce_ms` (GPU).
  - `depth_test`: `early`, `late` (DX12, Metal: needs `late_depth_fallback`) or `unsupported`
    ([terrain virtual texture tiers](book/agents/terrain-vt-tiers.md)). `supported` is `true` on `early`,
    and on `late` only while the settings carry `late_depth_fallback`.
- `terrain.set_vt { enabled, settings }` switches it on, off, or to new settings on the next frame.
  `settings` is any subset of:
  - `cache`: `lighting`, `relief` or `surface`.
  - `lod0_texel_m`, `page_texels`, `atlas_slots`, `oversample`, `near_m`, `min_normal_y`.
    `near_m` is metres. The whole-surface cache never serves nearer than 24 m (the near-field
    detail has faded, and the atlas stores no frost). Lighting and relief use `near_m` as
    given, so a value under 24 serves those nearer pixels from the atlas when the slope
    passes `min_normal_y`.
  - `bakes_per_frame`, `rebakes_per_frame`, `stale_threshold`, `stochastic_lod`.
  - `late_depth_fallback`: also run on devices without forced early depth tests.

  Wait until `terrain.vt` shows `pending: false`. A refused request shows in `error`.

## What `cache` picks

| `cache` | Cached | Per pixel | Frames vs uncached (DO27 plates, SSIM) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lighting` | Cliff-relief normal, heightfield sun occlusion, cavity, horizon slopes, bounce | Layers, mid relief, strata, rock, talus, macro | 0.998–1.0 |
| `relief` | The above plus the strata/talus albedo factor and the fractured-rock normal | Layers, mid relief, macro | 0.995–1.0 |
| `surface` | The whole surface | Lighting only | 0.977–0.997, slightly softer texture detail |

## Behavior

- **A page miss never shows.** A pixel whose pages are not resident shades the surface in full.
  The counters only tell you the cost.
- **Pages need a few frames to arrive.** Pages are requested by the frame that needs them and
  baked two frames later. A camera cut therefore costs full shading for a few frames.
- **Changing what the surface depends on drops every page.** That covers the sun direction, the
  material and layers, the heights, the terrain budget, and the relief settings.
- **Moving cameras re-bake pages.** The re-bake budget is `rebakes_per_frame`. When the camera
  has moved far enough to change a page's distance-dependent terms, it is re-baked.
- **Stochastic LOD needs TAA.** `stochastic_lod` reads one of the two LODs per pixel, and the
  temporal filter averages them. Turn it off for frames without TAA.

## Checking it

1. Take `seeing.screenshot` with the texture off, then on.
2. Debug view 96 shows how far the bake's rebuilt geometry is from the rasterized one:
   - green: within 5 cm;
   - red: height off;
   - blue: pyramid level off.
3. `TerrainVtHandle::read_page` (Rust) reads a page back for tests.

## Example calls

Example calls (`regia agent call <method> '<params json>'`; entity ids come from `scene.query_entities`):

```text
terrain.vt {}
terrain.set_vt {"enabled": true, "settings": {"cache": "lighting"}}
```

<!-- source: book/agents/renderer.md -->
# Renderer: scale, culling and output

The frame path is `FrameRenderer`. Quality comes from `RenderSettings.profile`
(`RenderProfilePreset`: Mobile Low/High, Desktop Low/High/Ultra, Deck). The golden
harness pins `FrameQuality::LAB` and does not follow the desktop-high preset.

## What the profile turns on

- `render_scale` below 1 renders the HDR target smaller. It is upscaled by TAAU when
  anti-aliasing is TAA (Desktop High: native, or 0.67 as an opt-in performance budget; Deck: 0.7) and by a bilinear resolve
  otherwise (Desktop Low). Ultra stays at 1.0. Scale is ignored when both the post
  stack and TAAU are off, so a raw MSAA frame stays at the output size.
- The opt-in 0.67 Desktop High budget (`render_scale` 0.67 with a 2048² cascade)
  gathers screen-space GI at half resolution and joint-bilateral-upsamples
  it, uses 6+8 PCSS taps, and skips full-resolution SSR. Stock Desktop High (native
  scale) keeps the full-resolution SSGI gather, 12+16 taps and the full-resolution linear SSR march when stochastic SSR is not capable (Desktop High and Ultra normally use stochastic SSR, cutoff 0.55).
  A held camera (same unjittered view, sun, and draws) reuses the previous SSGI,
  SSR, and AO. Ultra's SSGI stays full resolution. SSAO on Desktop High is already
  half resolution and is sampled directly. Sun PCSS uses 12+16 taps except in the
  0.67 budget (6+8).
- `gpu_driven` (Desktop Low, Desktop High, Ultra and Deck) runs a compute frustum plus a Hi-Z test and
  draws with indirect commands. Shadow and depth-prepass draws of those meshes are
  instanced from one object buffer. Skinned color and blended materials stay on
  the CPU path. If the device cannot do indirect draws, the CPU loop is used.
- `ssao` darkens indirect light only. Off is a 1×1 white texture, which matches the
  lab goldens.
- `shadow_filter` selects hardware PCF, 3×3, 5×5, or a small PCSS kernel. Desktop
  High and Ultra use PCSS-lite.
- `max_lights_per_cluster` is the froxel cap. `max_reflection_probes` caps how many
  captured probes are blended into SSR misses. See [high-end lighting](book/agents/high-end-lighting.md).
- `horizontal_plus` keeps the 16:9 vertical FOV on wider aspects and the 16:9
  horizontal FOV on narrower ones. The lab leaves it off.
- Deck is 1280×800, `render_scale` 0.7, TAAU, and a 40 fps cap. The cap is applied
  only when pacing has no cap yet. It does not clear a cap you already set, and it
  does not replace a variable-refresh present mode.

## Lights and debug views

A frame draws up to four directional lights (the sun with its cascades and three unshadowed ones),
`AmbientVolume` fill boxes, and every `DebugViewMode`. See [Render lights](book/agents/render-lights.md) and
`render.lights`.

## Output

`OutputSettings` (a resource):

- `present`: `Vsync` (the default; same mapping as before), `Uncapped`, or `Vrr`
  (mailbox, else relaxed FIFO, else FIFO). On DX12, `Vrr` takes `Immediate` when the
  surface lists it, even if mailbox is listed too. See [swapchain](book/agents/swapchain.md).
- `hdr`: `Sdr` (default), `Hdr10`, or `ScRgb`. The swapchain changes only when the
  surface lists that format and color space. See ADR-021: the image is still the
  AgX 0..1 grade.
- `frame_cap_fps`: `None` leaves `FramePacing` alone.

## Timings

`FrameRenderer::set_gpu_timing(true)` then `gpu_timings()` reports every pass that ran,
by name (`GpuTimings::report` prints every pass, zeros included): `shadows`, `clusters`,
`gi probes` (the GPU probe update, `gi_ms`), `prepass`, `cull`, `ssao`, `contact shadows`,
`forward`, `ssgi`, `ssr`, `atmosphere`, `clouds`, `fog`, `taau`, `scene total`, `post` and
`frame`. A skipped pass reads 0.00 ms and its scalar field stays 0. `gi_cpu_ms()` is only the
host-set CPU trace time, not a GPU pass. `render_lab` and `sim_bridge --bench-frames` print the same
named list (render_lab also prints the CPU trace). The Sponza bench uses the desktop-high profile, so paging,
probes, screen-space GI and SSR run there when the depth prepass is on.
`spawn_lab_scene` itself stays on the lab baseline, which leaves all of those off.

<!-- source: book/agents/high-end-lighting.md -->
# High-end lighting

Desktop High and Ultra turn these on. Mobile Low, Desktop Low, and Deck leave most of
them off: ambient (or the existing IBL) instead of probe GI and no screen-space
reflections. Paged sun shadows (cached cascades) are on for Desktop Low, High, Ultra
and Deck, and off for both Mobile tiers and the lab baseline, which redraw every
shadow map every frame. The lab golden harness (`FrameQuality::LAB`)
matches that off state, so older screenshots stay put. Screen-space GI is the cheaper
tier (`GiMode::ScreenSpace`). It is not the Low preset.

## Local lights

`max_visible_lights` is how many point and spot lights a view uploads. Desktop High
is 256, Desktop Ultra 512, Deck 96, Mobile Low 32. The buffer holds 512. The lab
harness and the editor stay at 64, and under that cap the order is the authored
order, so a cached shadow tile does not move. Over the cap the dimmer lights (by
screen importance) are dropped and a warning is logged. A froxel still stops at
`max_lights_per_cluster`; that overflow is counted on `FrameRenderer::light_upload`
and warned. There is no engine constant of 48. The old lab path kept 64 and said
nothing.

Shadowed spots take one atlas tile, points take six. The atlas has 64 tiles.
When the casters fit, assignment stays in authored order. When they do not, a
near spot can take a tile a far point light cannot. `local_shadow_max_lights` is
the profile's count (Desktop High 32, the lab 16).

## Sun shadows

`paged_sun_shadows` caches each cascade as a 4×4 page grid. A caster that moves
dirties the pages its old and new bounds cover. A light-matrix change (a new sun
direction, or a camera move of a shadow texel or more) redraws that cascade. The
cascade center is snapped in light space, including depth, so a smaller camera move
keeps the matrix and the pages. Local lights remember which atlas tile a caster
overlaps. A warm atlas clears and redraws only those tiles. PCSS-lite is the
Desktop High / Ultra filter. The lab stays on 3×3 PCF and does not snap.

## Global illumination

The preset's probes (Desktop High and Ultra) are the GPU DDGI volume; see
[GI probes](book/agents/gi-probes.md). `FrameRenderer::set_gi_field` below is the optional,
separate CPU volume and stacks with it if both are on.

`GiMode::Probes` is a dynamic irradiance grid in the sense of Majercik et al. 2019,
reduced to an L1 spherical harmonic and a small octahedral depth. For the CPU field, rays are marched
on the CPU against SDFs (boxes, spheres, a mesh voxelization, the terrain
heightfield). Upload the field with `FrameRenderer::set_gi_field` before the frame.
The forward pass adds it on top of ambient when the grid is non-empty. A closed room
does not pick up the sky: probes inside the shell see the shell, and a hit is tested
against the sun. `set_gi_cpu_ms` / `gi_cpu_ms` is the trace time. It is not inside
`gpu_timings`.

`GiMode::ScreenSpace` is one depth-aware gather in a composite pass. It needs a
depth prepass, a single sample, and a linear HDR target (post or TAAU).

## Reflections

SSR is the same class of pass: a short screen march on the floor, then a reflection
probe if the march misses. On the linear march (lab, editor, probe capture) the mix is scaled by
roughness (`ssr_roughness_weight`): a floor at 0.35 stays a mirror, and roughness 0.7 and above
keeps the shaded color. Stock Desktop High and Ultra run stochastic SSR instead: cutoff 0.55,
fade from 0.40, and a probe on any downward-pointing reflection ray.
The forward HDR buffer carries that roughness in alpha; the post stack writes alpha 1.
`FrameRenderer::capture_reflection_probe` renders six 16² faces and packs them
with `equirect_from_faces`. Each face uses `cube_face_axes` for its look direction
and its camera up. World +Y is parallel to the ±Y looks, so those faces cannot be
shot with the ordinary camera up. Capture forces GI, screen-space GI, SSR, other
probes, and paging off, and it renders a native 90° square so the pack matches the
face basis. `max_reflection_probes` is how many of those probes are blended for a
pixel. Box projection uses the probe's center and half-extent.

## Interiors

A tunnel or a cockpit that only sees local lights is black at a sunny EV. AgX's
toe maps 40 lux at EV 15 to display 0. The same 40 lux at EV 8 (`INTERIOR_EXPOSURE_EV`),
under the corrected AgX and the default look, prints near luma 37 for an albedo
around one half. EV 6 prints that floor near luma 91, which reads as a wash. Put an `InteriorVolume` on the
room. When the camera eye is inside it, the extracted frame sets
`quality.interior_ambient`, drops sky IBL, and uses the volume's lux (0 means the
40 lux floor). Without a volume, insert an `EnclosureScene` (a hollow shell, not a
solid box) and extraction calls `detect_enclosure`: four of six cardinal traces
must hit. `build_interior_lighting` runs `plan_interior_coverage` and traces the
grid with the local lights. A miss stores black, so an open mouth is not painted
with the sky. The grid coarsens its longest axis before it exceeds `MAX_PROBES`,
which keeps a tunnel's cross-section. Bind the field with `GiMode::Probes` and
capture one reflection probe at the coverage center. Walls take their bounce from
the field. Outdoor probes replace the sky (ADR-031). An interior adds the bounce
on top of the 40 lux floor (`camera_pos.w`; `quality.w` is the shadow-noise index).
`INTERIOR_BOUNCE_GAIN` (2.5) is the rest of the diffuse series after
that one bounce, so a wall beside a light is not left at the 40 lux floor. On the linear march the probe only reaches floors that pass the reflection gate
(roughness under 0.7, normal.y at least 0.72); stochastic SSR has no `normal.y` test. Do not expect the floor to survive
an outdoor exposure. Pin EV 8, or leave auto-exposure on for a view that does not
also see the sun. The 40 lux term is a floor, not a wash: the lights still have to
read as pools.

## What an agent should expect

- Turning GI off removes the color bleed and leaves ambient.
- Turning SSR off leaves the probe color on reflective floors.
- `gpu_timings().ssgi_ms` and `ssr_ms` are the composite passes. A pass that ran
  reports a positive lavapipe timestamp; zero means that pass did not record.
  Those milliseconds are not a frame budget. The floor-tier number still needs a
  discrete GPU. The RTX 5080 on the build box did not enumerate.
- Do not add these fields to a scene extract. The renderer holds the grids.

<!-- source: book/agents/lookdev.md -->
# Look-dev compare

After a photoreal merge, render the shot list and diff it against the committed baseline.
The lead reads the `--compare` table. `docs/evidence/lookdev/baseline/` is the RTX 5080
capture (960-wide PNGs and `shots.json`). `cargo test -p lookdev` is the lavapipe check;
it does not bless those PNGs.

## Render

Headless. No window. Lavapipe is the test device; the evidence run pins the NVIDIA adapter:

```sh
flock /tmp/regia-gpu.lock flock /tmp/ferrite-gpu.lock env VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_SELECT='*nvidia*' \
  cargo run -p lookdev --release -- --shots /tmp/lookdev-nvidia \
  --width 1920 --height 1080 --heightfield 4096 --macro 2048 \
  --frames 30 --png-width 960
```

Tests use `LookdevConfig::tiny()` (48² heightfield, 64×36, both planets, 30 frames) through
`RenderDevice::headless()`. That is `cargo test -p lookdev`.

## Compare

```sh
cargo run -p lookdev -- --compare docs/evidence/lookdev/baseline /tmp/lookdev-nvidia
```

A directory means `shots.json` inside it. The first lines are the two adapters and any
feature flag that changed (`ssr_in_linked_crates`, `volumetric_atmosphere_in_linked_crates`,
`gpu_samples_macro_variation`, and the rest on `EngineFeatures`). Then one row per shot id
`{planet}/{camera}/{profile}`.

Read a row as `new − old`:

- `d_lum`, `d_con` — mean luminance and contrast on the 8-bit BT.709 plane
- `d_black`, `d_blow` — percentage-point change in near-black and blown pixels
- `d_sat`, `d_tile`, `d_sharp` — saturation, secondary tiling peak, Laplacian sharpness
- `d_stab` — temporal stability over the 30 frames. A static camera sits at 1, including a
  frozen blown or black frame, so stability is not a lighting check
- `d_gnd` — mean luminance of the bottom 45% (the ground band on horizon cameras)
- `d_gpu` — total GPU milliseconds (0 on a device without timestamp queries)

`missing_in_new` / `missing_in_old` list shot ids that do not pair. A profile rename shows
up there.

## What the numbers are measuring

The image is the terrain hook: sun cascade, height fog, CDLOD, six layers, scatter, hole,
plus the portal mesh the harness draws itself. `applied_terrain_cascades` stays 1.
`ssr_in_linked_crates` and `gi_probes_in_linked_crates` are true on this tree because
`fn ssr_roughness_weight`, `struct ReflectionProbe`, `struct GiField`, and `struct GpuGiGrid`
are linked. That is presence, not a second cascade and not an SSR or GI pass.
Ultra / High / Deck-Medium still change CDLOD range, fog density, scatter budget, and (Deck)
framebuffer scale. Deck-Medium is `RenderProfilePreset::Deck`.

Layer height maps and the macro map are authored and uploaded (`uploaded_*` and the byte
counts). `gpu_samples_macro_variation` flips when the terrain-photoreal symbols land; until
then the shader blends by slope and altitude only. Evidence macro is 2048 for that reason
and for the 10 minute GPU window. `--macro 8192` still allocates; the CPU test covers 8192
without rendering it. Rock scatter stays the terrain pyramid mesh.

<!-- source: book/agents/vfx.md -->
# VFX

`.vfx.ron` v7 is the particle asset (`docs/formats/vfx-ron.md`). v1 through v6 load and
migrate in memory. v3 adds `FireAnim`; v4 adds the `FireballAnim` body sheet and `heat_haze`;
v5 adds the `Planar` velocity mode (outward along the ground when local +Z is the ground normal);
v6 adds the scene wind and event spawns (below); v7 adds ribbons and mesh shapes.
Crash effects (fireball, dust ring, spray sheet, smoke column) are on the
[crash effects](book/agents/crash-fx.md) page.

## Author a system

```ron,vfx
(
    version: 7,
    name: "smoke",
    system: (budget: 1024),
    emitters: [
        (
            name: "puff",
            delay: 0.0,
            spawn: (mode: Rate(12.0), lifetime: (min: 1.0, max: 2.0)),
            init: (
                shape: Point,
                size: (min: 0.4, max: 0.8),
                color: [(t: 0.0, color: "#9a9288")],
            ),
            render: (
                mode: Billboard,
                sprite: PuffAnim,
                blend: Alpha,
                softness: 1.2,
                lit: true,
                emissive: 1.0,
                self_shadow: 0.7,
                screen_floor_px: 2.0,
                flipbook: Some((
                    cols: 8,
                    rows: 2,
                    frames: 16,
                    mode: Fps(10.0),
                    random_start: true,
                    blend_frames: true,
                )),
            ),
        ),
    ],
)
```

Fire stays in the orange/yellow/white family in linear light, before AgX. An HDR
`emissive` above 1 feeds bloom on a single-sample `Rgba16Float` frame (ADR-049). The
present pass adds that bloom and scales the peak. It does not repaint hue (ADR-049). A
pink core fails the hue test. Desktop High is exposure, `mix(base, bloom, 0.04)`, AgX
and `display_look(1.2, 1.4)`. Alpha emitters sort back to front; additive emitters do
not. Smoke is lit alpha puffs, not an additive disc. The muzzle flash uses the flare
sprite. The explosion is a flash, one fire body from the `FireballAnim` sheet (hot core, sooty rim,
flame tongues on top), its light on the ground, a heat-haze card, ember streaks, then a lit
smoke column.

## Check it

`samples/vfx_lab --evidence <dir>` writes the gallery. The GPU tests in
`crates/regia_vfx/tests/quality.rs` reject a hard ground cut, an unlit puff, a popping sort,
a pink core, a frozen flipbook and a sub-pixel spark. Plates live in
`docs/evidence/vfx-quality/`.

## Systems: list, describe, spawn, change

These work on any `.vfx.ron` system, whatever its effect.

- `vfx.systems` lists the loaded systems and every live instance: `live`, `active`, `age`, `origin`,
  `forward`, `scale`, `intensity`, `lod_scale` and `gpu_ms_estimate` (the live count at the 2 ms per
  100k budget rate of spec 26 § 6: a planning number, not a measurement). `wind` is what particles
  drift in. With `"gpu": true`, `gpu` holds the pool's counters read back from the device (it
  blocks on the GPU): `alive`, `dropped`, `events_fired`, `events_overflow`, `children_spawned`,
  `children_dropped` and the two capacities; it stays `null` without a GPU context. `live` counts
  scheduled particles; event children are only in `gpu.alive`.
- `vfx.describe` reads one system: a line per emitter (`spawn_mode`, `lifetime`, `wind_response`,
  `wind_drag`, `drag`, `events`, `event_tail_s`, and since `.vfx.ron` v7 `shape`, `kill` and
  `render`) and the whole `definition`. `shape.kind` is `point`, `sphere`, `box`, `cone`,
  `mesh_surface` or `skinned_mesh`; a mesh shape adds `mesh` and `mesh_status` (`ok` with
  `triangles`, `area` and `skinned`, or `missing_mesh` / `bad_mesh` with `error`). `kill` holds
  `below` (the `kill_below` plane), `volume` (`shape`, `half_extents` or `radius`, `center`, `kill`:
  `inside` or `outside`) and `depth_collision`. `render.mode` is `billboard`, `stretched`, `mesh`
  or `ribbon`; a ribbon adds `link`, `max_points` and `texture`. A mesh particle (`.vfx.ron` v8)
  adds `mesh` and `mesh_status`: `cube` (no `mesh`, the built-in cube, `indices` 36), `ok` (the
  registered mesh it draws, with `triangles` and `indices`), or `missing_mesh` / `bad_mesh` with
  `error` (it draws nothing), and `lit` (the mesh asset is shaded by the sun and ambient; the cube
  is always `false`). `mesh_draws` lists the GPU's mesh-asset draws of the last frame, one per
  registered render mesh: `mesh`, `slot`, `indices` and `instances` (that mesh's live particles,
  nothing else); it is `null` without a GPU context and empty with no registered mesh.
- `vfx.spawn_probe` plays a loaded `system` for `frames` frames (1..=600, default 1) with `seed`
  at `origin` along `forward` on a scratch instance and returns, per emitter, `spawned`, `refused`
  (spawns a mesh shape refused), `mesh_error` and the first `max` (1..=4096, default 256)
  `positions` with their `velocity`. Nothing is spawned; the same seed always gives the same
  positions, so it checks where a mesh shape puts particles before playing it.
- `vfx.spawn` plays a loaded `system`, or a project-relative `asset`, which it loads first (a loaded
  definition of the same name is replaced), at `origin` along `forward`, with optional `seed`,
  `scale` and `intensity`. It returns the instance `id` and what it `plays` in the level's medium.
- `vfx.set_param` changes a live `instance` (`scale`, `intensity`, `origin`, `forward`) or a loaded
  `system` + `emitter` (`wind_response`, `wind_drag`, `drag`, `count_scale`, `alpha_scale`,
  `emissive`; running instances follow on their next update). It returns `{ param, before, after }`.
  Changing an emitter validates the definition first, so a refused value changes nothing.

```json
{"method": "vfx.spawn", "params": {"asset": "fx/shell_impact.vfx.ron", "origin": [4.0, 1.0, 9.0]}}
{"method": "vfx.set_param", "params": {"system": "shell_impact", "emitter": "dust", "param": "wind_response", "value": 0.5}}
{"method": "vfx.systems", "params": {"gpu": true}}
```

Refusals are `F0002` with `data.reason`:

| `data.reason` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `missing_param` | A required parameter is absent. |
| `bad_source` | Not exactly one of `asset` and `system`, or of `instance` and `system`. |
| `path_escapes` | `asset` is absolute, holds `..`, or a link leads out of the project. |
| `asset_invalid` | `asset` does not parse or validate; the message says why. |
| `unknown_param` | `vfx.set_param` has no parameter of that name. |
| `value_out_of_range` | A value is not finite or fails the emitter's rules. |

A system, emitter, instance or file that does not exist is `F0003`; a world without `VfxPlugin` is
`F0016`.

## Wind and event spawns

An emitter with `wind_response` above 0 drifts in the scene wind (`render.set_foliage_wind`, the
weather or a host's `SceneWind`): the wind's velocity pulls it at `wind_response * wind_drag` per
second, so without other forces it ends up moving with the wind, and still-air `drag` holds it to
a fraction. Change it live: `vfx.set_param` `wind_response`, then watch `vfx.systems`
`wind` and a screenshot. The default of 0 keeps every older effect exactly as it was.

`events` spawn a child emitter (spawn mode `Event`) from a particle's `Spawn`, `Death` or `Collision`
(the depth-collision path) with `count`, `probability` and `inherit_velocity`: sparks when a shell
lands, dust when it dies. See the example and the rules in `docs/formats/vfx-ron.md`. Counts are
deterministic: a replay fires the same events.

To check one: `vfx.spawn` it, `wait_until` the parent's lifetime has passed, then `vfx.systems`
with `gpu: true`. `children_spawned` is the parents fired times `count` at probability 1. A rising
`events_overflow` or `children_dropped` means the frame asks for more than
`VfxProfile::event_capacity` or `child_capacity`: lower the rates or raise the profile's limits.
`events_overflow` counts an over-budget event one frame after it fired (the next frame's event
prepare drops it), so read it a frame after the burst.

## Mesh shapes, kill volumes and ribbons (`.vfx.ron` v7)

- **Mesh shapes.** `MeshSurface(mesh: "...")` spawns on the surface of a mesh the game registered
  under that name (`VfxLibrary::add_cpu_mesh`), by area; `SkinnedMesh(mesh, max_per_frame)` spawns
  on the deformed surface for the instance's current joint palette (`VfxScene::set_skin_palette`),
  at most `max_per_frame` per frame. `Normal(speed)` launches along the surface normal. A mesh that
  is not registered, has no triangles or no area spawns nothing: `vfx.describe` shows
  `mesh_status` and `vfx.spawn_probe` shows `refused` and `mesh_error`. Check one: `vfx.spawn_probe`
  with `frames: 1`, then compare the positions with the mesh.
- **Kill volumes.** `kill_volume: Some((shape: Box(half_extents: (...)) | Sphere(radius: r),
  center: (...), kill: Inside | Outside))` kills particles that enter (or leave) the volume. It
  follows the instance's rotation and scale. The GPU and the CPU reference use one rule.
- **Ribbons.** `render: (mode: Ribbon, ribbon: (...))` draws the emitter's particles as one strip per
  instance (`link: Emitter`) or per frame's spawns (`SpawnGroup`), width and colour over length,
  `texture: Stretch` or `Tile(metres)`, at most `max_points`. A strip of `n` points is `6 (n - 1)`
  vertices. Ribbon particles live on the CPU; they are not in the GPU pool counters.

| Code | Where | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `missing_mesh` | `shape.mesh_status`, `mesh_error` | No mesh is registered under the shape's name. |
| `bad_mesh` | `shape.mesh_status`, `mesh_error` | The mesh is empty, has no area, a bad index, or is rigid under `SkinnedMesh`. |
| `missing_mesh` | `render.mesh_status` | No mesh is registered under the mesh particle's `render.mesh` (v8); it draws nothing. |
| `bad_mesh` | `render.mesh_status` | The GPU refused the mesh particle's mesh at the last upload (more than 65 536 triangles, or 64 render meshes already in use); it draws nothing. |

## Mesh particles from mesh assets (`.vfx.ron` v8)

`render: (mode: Mesh, mesh: Some("name"))` draws each particle as the mesh registered under
`name` (`VfxLibrary::add_mesh` or `add_cpu_mesh`, the same registry the mesh shapes use) instead
of the built-in cube, scaled by the particle size and drawn instanced from the mesh's own vertex
and index buffers. Without `mesh` the particle is the cube, as in v7. Check one:
`vfx.describe` shows `render.mesh_status` `ok` and the mesh's `indices` (the cube is 36); a
`missing_mesh` or `bad_mesh` status means that emitter draws nothing while its particles still
simulate (they count in `vfx.stats` `live_mesh`). Register the mesh before the first frame that
draws the effect; a mesh registered later draws from the next upload.

`lit: true` on the render module shades a mesh asset with the scene sun and ambient on its face
normals and draws its front faces only (counter-clockwise, glTF's winding); a mesh wound the other
way shows its inside, so flip its winding at import. `vfx.describe` shows `render.lit`. Each
registered mesh is one instanced draw over only that mesh's particles: `mesh_draws[].instances`
is how many the last frame drew (a mesh whose emitters are all dead draws 0). The pipeline warm
compiles the mesh-asset pipeline with the other effect pipelines, so the first mesh particle does
not compile on the frame path.

```json
{"method": "vfx.describe", "params": {"system": "shard_burst"}}
```

Examples are `samples/vfx_lab/effects/mesh_sparks.vfx.ron`, `skinned_aura.vfx.ron`,
`kill_room.vfx.ron` and `ribbon_trail.vfx.ron` (the lab registers `lab/plane` and `lab/arm`).

```json
{"method": "vfx.describe", "params": {"system": "sample_mesh_sparks"}}
{"method": "vfx.spawn_probe", "params": {"system": "sample_mesh_sparks", "seed": 7, "frames": 2, "max": 16}}
```

## Atmosphere-aware effects

Explosions and smoke follow the level's air by default (`LevelSettings::atmosphere.preset` and
`gravity`, the same source as `audio.medium`). `vfx.medium` reports it:
`{ atmosphere, gravity, wind, variant_suffix, variants }`, where `variants` lists the effects that
play a medium variant, for example `{ "effect": "explosion", "plays": "explosion@airless" }`.

- **airless** (Europa, the Moon): a flash, a fireball of the explosive's own gases that is gone
  by about 0.35 s, then ice and regolith ejecta on ballistic arcs under the level's gravity
  (no drag), a thin low dust skirt, and nothing that rises or billows. Landed ejecta rest where
  they fell and fade. `smoke` becomes a thin vent fountain that falls back.
- **mars**: the fireball dies fast; butterscotch dust billows, lingers for 10 s or more, rises
  weakly and drifts with the wind; the soot is thin and disperses fast.
- **earth**: the reference look (lit smoke columns, sooty fireballs).

A game's own `.vfx.ron` named `explosion@airless` (or `@mars`) replaces the built-in variant.
Spawn effects with a horizontal forward (the default +Z): the effects' local up is the
instance's up axis, which is world up only when forward is horizontal.

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"method":"vfx.medium"}
```

## Hover washes

A hovering hull kicks up the ground under it. Give the hull a `regia_vfx::HoverWash` (gameplay
sets `ground`, `ground_normal` and `height` every frame) and the plugin keeps one effect on it:

- **surface**: `dust` (Mars: butterscotch fines), `ice` (Europa: bright grains that glint),
  `frost` (fine powder), or `auto` (airless → ice, Mars and Earth → dust).
- **height**: intensity is `(1 − h / 2R)²` for footprint radius `R`: full on the ground, a
  quarter at one radius up, nothing past one diameter. Fewer and fainter particles, same look.
- **footprint**: the effect is authored for a 3 m radius and scales to the hull (sizes and offsets
  by `R / 3`, speeds by `√(R / 3)`).
- **air**: as for explosions. In air a rolling, lit skirt drifts and settles (Mars: lingers several
  seconds and drifts downwind). Airless: only grains, on ballistic arcs under the level's gravity,
  that land, with no lingering cloud.
- **look**: the outflow sheet and the billows are soft puffs that grow as they slow, drawn at most
  three times longer than wide along their motion, never as long streaks. A small grit spray and,
  on ice, glints ride on top.
- **jumps**: a cruising hull lends a share of its speed to the dust. A ground point that moves
  faster than 200 m/s (a respawn or teleport) moves the wash without that push, so the sheet is
  not flung away as streaks for a frame.

`vfx.hover_washes` lists them: `{ entity, surface, resolved_surface, footprint_radius, height,
intensity, expected_intensity, playing }`. `vfx.set_hover_wash` adds or changes one; fields you
leave out keep their value.

```json
{"method": "vfx.set_hover_wash", "params": {"entity": 4294967310, "footprint_radius": 2.4, "height": 0.6, "ground": [12.0, -3.1, 40.0]}}
```

Check it: `wait_until` `vfx.hover_washes` shows `playing`, then screenshot the hull. Raise `height`
to `2 × footprint_radius` and the wash stops (`intensity` 0). From above, the ring under the hull
should read as a soft skirt; thin radial lines (a "hairy ring") mean the wash is streaking.

## Thruster plumes

Give a nozzle entity (a child at the unit's socket) a `regia_vfx::ThrusterPlume`. The plume
follows the entity's transform, with the exhaust along `exhaust` (local, default down), at
`throttle`. Each air shows something different:

- **earth:** heat shimmer (refraction cards, Desktop High), a faint exhaust haze and the nozzle
  glow.
- **mars:** no visible shimmer (the air is about 1.5 % of Earth's density). A thin plume that
  spreads wider and drifts, and the glow.
- **airless:** the exhaust is invisible. Only the nozzle glows, and its light makes a lit spot on
  the ground when the unit is low.

Kinds are `duct` (gleaner lift/thrust ducts, Kraken fans) and `jetpack` (pilots). `vfx.plumes`
lists the plumes and DO27's thruster table (unit, kind, sockets, exhaust direction).
`vfx.set_plume` adds or changes one; throttle 0 is idle, with no particles and no light.

```json
{"method": "vfx.set_plume", "params": {"entity": 4294967330, "kind": "duct", "throttle": 0.8}}
```

The hover wash in air is a brownout-style outflow. A flat, stretched sheet streams out along the
ground (soft against it), then rolls up at the jet's edge into round billows that lift and drift.

## Weapon hits, muzzles and tracers

`vfx.hit` plays one round landing (`regia_vfx::WeaponHit`, also a command games queue):

- **metal**: hot sparks, a short flash, molten droplets, a burnt-paint wisp (in air), and a scorch
  decal with a molten spot that cools from yellow-white through orange to dull red in about a
  second.
- **concrete**: chips, a fan of grit, a lit dust puff, and a chip decal (a dark pit in lighter,
  freshly exposed aggregate).
- **glass**: glitter fragments and powder. With `target` set to the glass entity, its
  `GlassDamage` takes the impact in its own frame (`render.glass_damage` shows the crack level).

Decals ride `target` (a moving hull keeps its marks) and retire with it. Airless hits fly drag-free
and nothing puffs; sparks stay hot longer (no air to cool them). The calibre (`light`, `medium`,
`heavy`, or a DO27 `weapon` id) scales the effect and the decal, and sets the glass energy.

```json
{"method": "vfx.hit", "params": {"position": [3.1, 1.2, 0.4], "normal": [1, 0, 0], "surface": "glass", "weapon": "rifle", "target": 4294967321}}
```

`vfx.weapons` lists DO27's weapons and what each plays: muzzles `muzzle_flash` (rifles, pistols,
spike and ricochet guns), `muzzle_cannon` (chaincannon, sentry, guntower) and `muzzle_launcher`
(thumpgun, arcmortar, quakeshell, heatseeker); tracers `tracer` and `tracer_heavy`; hits by
calibre, explosive rounds as the atmosphere-aware `explosion`.

Muzzle flashes and tracers draw their color *over* the scene, so they read as orange on Europa's
bright ice in full sun instead of clipping to white. Their additive cores are small. Airless and on
Mars a muzzle has no secondary flash (no oxygen), and airless there is no smoke wisp. Tracers carry
their own oxidiser and look the same everywhere.

## Soft-particle layer (cost)

Dust, smoke and billows (soft, low-frequency alpha particles) draw into an offscreen layer at a
fraction of the frame size, and are composited back with a depth-aware bilateral upsample, so
they never bleed across a hull's silhouette. Sparks, tracers, muzzle cores and fire stay full
resolution. Tiers:

| Tier | Soft layer |
|---|---|
| Desktop High | half (the default) |
| Desktop Ultra | full |
| Mobile | quarter, always |

`vfx.get_look` reports `soft_particle_res` (the override, or `null`) and
`soft_particle_res_profile`. `vfx.set_look` takes `"soft_particle_res": "full" | "half" |
"quarter" | null`. The layer applies to HDR frames and is skipped when no soft particle is alive.

The alpha sort and the particle update cover only what can be alive: the live alpha count and
the ring slots spawned within the longest lifetime. Frames are unchanged.

## Heat haze and fire light

`vfx.get_look` reads the fire look: `{ heat_haze, haze_scale, fire_light, fire_light_scale,
fire_lights_live, strongest_light }`. `strongest_light` is `{ position, color, radius }` of
this frame's brightest particle light, or `null`.

`vfx.set_look` changes it; fields you leave out keep their value. It returns `{ before, after }`.

- `heat_haze` (bool): haze cards bend the scene behind the fire. They draw on any HDR frame
  where a scene copy exists (the host refreshes it after decals); elsewhere they are skipped.
- `haze_scale` (0..=4): multiplies every card's `heat_haze` pixels.
- `fire_light` (bool): particle lights reach the renderer's local lights (the ground under the
  fireball glows) and the lit smoke.
- `fire_light_scale` (0..=8): multiplies every particle light. One unit of
  `ParticleLightDef::intensity`, with envelope 1, instance intensity at least 1 and a brightest
  linear channel of 1, is 5e5 lm. A dimmer peak scales that down. The gathered colour is the
  linear colour times intensity, the fire envelope and `min(instance intensity, 1)`.

```json
{"method": "vfx.set_look", "params": {"heat_haze": false, "fire_light_scale": 1.5}}
```

Check it with a screenshot before and after: the haze shows as a wobble behind the fire, the
light as a warm patch on the ground. The look is runtime state, not saved in the level.

## Example calls

Example calls (`regia agent call <method> '<params json>'`; entity ids come from `scene.query_entities`):

```text
vfx.get_look {}                  # { heat_haze, haze_scale, fire_light, ... }
vfx.weapons {}                   # each weapon with its muzzle, tracer and hit effect
```

### More `vfx.set_hover_wash` parameters

The schema (`agent.schema`) also lists these optional parameters:

- `enabled` (boolean): false: no new particles.

### More `vfx.hit` parameters

The schema (`agent.schema`) also lists these optional parameters:

- `seed` (integer): Variation seed.

### More `vfx.set_plume` parameters

The schema (`agent.schema`) also lists these optional parameters:

- `enabled` (boolean): false: no particles and no light.

## Particles under temporal upscalers

Effects draw after the temporal resolve (TAAU, TSR, FSR 3.1, a vendor upscaler), into a copy of its
output, so they never enter an upscaler's history: a spark or a smoke puff over a moving background leaves
no trail, at any render scale, and needs no reactive mask. `render.get_upscalers` reports this as
`reactive_mask.layers.placement: "after_resolve"`. The check is `cargo test -p regia_vfx --test
reactive_upscaler`; the design and the frame-generation follow-up are in ADR-3101 and the
[upscalers page](book/agents/upscalers.md#particles-and-the-reactive-mask).

## Particle budgets and order

`vfx.stats` reads the particle budgets this frame (read-only):

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":9,"method":"vfx.stats"}
```

It returns `{ capacity, smoke_budget, sorted, live, live_alpha, live_mesh, headroom,
smoke_headroom, last_scheduled, pending_jobs, instances }`:

- `capacity` is the pool size (the global budget) and `smoke_budget` the cap on live
  alpha-blended particles, both from the quality profile (Desktop High 100 000 and 8 192,
  Mobile 10 000 and 2 048). `headroom` and `smoke_headroom` are what is left of them.
- `live` counts every particle the scheduler has spawned and not yet retired, including the
  `pending_jobs` that wait for the next drawn frame. A spawn counts once. A particle that
  dies this frame frees its budget this frame.
- `instances` lists each live effect: `{ id, effect, live, budget, active, age }`, where
  `budget` is the system's `system.budget`. `live` never passes `budget`.
- `sorted` is `true` when the profile sorts. Alpha-blended and mesh particles then draw back
  to front. Two particles at the same depth keep a fixed order (by pool slot), so a column of
  smoke does not shimmer, and the same scene draws in the same order on every run. When it is
  `false` (the Mobile profile) the alpha-blended particles draw emitter by emitter, back to front
  for the current view: the CPU ranks the emitters by the depth of their effect's origin each
  frame, so of two overlapping smoke effects the nearer one is on top; inside one emitter the
  particles keep their gather order.

Particle simulation is deterministic: the same seed, the same timestep and the same spawns put
every particle in the same pool slot with the same position, on every run and with either
alpha sort (bitonic, the default, or the opt-in radix sort). Additive particles are not sorted;
they add in whatever order the GPU gathers them, which can change the last bit of a pixel.

Check it: spawn an effect, then `wait_until` `vfx.stats` shows `live` above 0 and each
instance's `live` at or below its `budget`. Stop it and `live` falls to 0 once its longest
lifetime has passed.

Errors: without `regia_vfx::VfxPlugin` the method answers `UNSUPPORTED` with data code `F0016`.

Sample effects for these checks live in `samples/vfx_lab/effects/`: `sample_smoke_stack` (lit
puffs at equal depths), `sample_debris_cubes` (overlapping mesh debris), `sample_budget_storm`
(sparks asked for at more than twice their budget) and `sample_ember_drift` (curl, vortex and attractor embers).
`cargo run -p vfx_lab -- --effects samples/vfx_lab/effects` runs the lab's format, determinism
and budget checks on them.

## VFX editor (`editor.vfx_*`)

The editor's **VFX Editor** dock tab edits a `.vfx.ron` effect: the emitter list,
each emitter's module stack with a palette, enable boxes (the A/B toggle) and parameter rows, the
curve and gradient editors, a live preview and a per-emitter cost table (spec 26 § 3, ADR-3171). The
four methods below drive the same code. Every change is one step on the editor's undo stack (shared
with every other panel; `editor.undo` works too) and is checked by the `.vfx.ron` validator: an edit it
refuses changes nothing, not the effect, the undo stack or the file.

**Modules.** `.vfx.ron` v7 has no module list; an emitter is a fixed spawn, init, update and render
block. The editor shows a module wherever a group of fields leaves its default: `spawn`, `init` and
`render` (always there, `required: true`), `init_color`, `gravity`, `drag`, `curl`, `vortex`,
`attractor`, `wind`, `size_over_life`, `color_over_life`, `alpha_over_life`, `rotation_over_life`,
`kill_below`, `kill_volume`, `depth_collision`, `events`, `flipbook`, `soft_particles`, `light` and
`heat_haze`, in that order. `palette` lists what `add_module` can add (everything optional except
`events`, which needs a child emitter: write the link in the file). Module order inside an emitter is
fixed by the format; `move_emitter` reorders emitters.

**Disable (A/B).** `disable_module` takes the module's values out of the effect into the editor (the
format has no "enabled" field and stays frozen); the preview, `sim` and a save see the effect without it.
`enable_module` puts the exact values back, so the `sim` hash returns to what it was. A disabled module
is listed with `enabled: false`, cannot be edited until it is enabled, and is not written by `save`
(`disabled_not_saved` counts them).

**Curves.** Curves interpolate linearly between keys and have no tangents. Keys stay sorted by `t`
(0..=1); a moved key that passes a neighbour is re-sorted. Scalar curves: `size_over_life`,
`alpha_over_life`, `rotation_over_life`, `ribbon_width`. Gradients (`#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`):
`init_color`, `color_over_life`, `ribbon_color`. Adding a key to an empty curve adds its module.

**Saving.** `save` writes atomically. An effect nobody edited is not rewritten; an effect undone back
to the state it was opened in saves the file's original bytes; anything else is written in the
canonical form (`VfxSystemDef::to_ron`, the form the loader round-trips).

`editor.vfx_open { path }` opens a project-relative `.vfx.ron` and returns the state:
`{ open, path, dirty, revision, name, version, budget, emitters: [{ index, name, draw_list, modules: [{
kind, stage, enabled, required, params: [{ name, kind, value, min?, max?, choices? }] }], curves: {
size_over_life: [[t, v]], ... }, gradients: { init_color: [[t, "#rrggbb"]], ... } }], disabled, palette,
undo_depth, redo_depth }`. A parameter's `kind` is `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `choice` or `color`;
numbers outside `min..=max` are refused. `keys` and `links` rows are read-only counts.

`editor.vfx_state { sim_steps?, cost_time?, seed? }` returns the same state. With `sim_steps` it also
runs the CPU reference simulation (`regia_vfx::probe::probe_steps`, events and kills included) for that
many 1/60 s steps from a fixed seed (default 1) and returns `sim: { steps, seed, particles, hash }`:
the hash covers every live particle's emitter, position, velocity, age and lifetime bits, so two effects
with the same hash simulate identically. With `cost_time` it returns the cost rows (below) at that time.

`editor.vfx_edit { op, ... }`, where `emitter` is a name or an index:

| `op` | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `add_module`, `remove_module`, `enable_module`, `disable_module` | `emitter`, `module` |
| `set_param` | `emitter`, `module`, `param`, `value` (number, boolean or string) |
| `curve_add_key` | `emitter`, `curve`, `t`, `v` |
| `curve_move_key` | `emitter`, `curve`, `index`, `t`, `v` |
| `curve_delete_key` | `emitter`, `curve`, `index` |
| `gradient_add_key` | `emitter`, `gradient`, `t`, `color` |
| `gradient_move_key` | `emitter`, `gradient`, `index`, `t`, `color` |
| `gradient_delete_key` | `emitter`, `gradient`, `index` |
| `add_emitter` | `name` (a 20/s point fountain to start from) |
| `remove_emitter` | `emitter` |
| `move_emitter` | `emitter`, `to` |
| `set_budget` | `value` |
| `set_fixed_bounds` | `min`, `max`: `[x, y, z]` each, metres in the effect's local space (`min <= max`) |
| `clear_fixed_bounds` | none (the computed bounds cull again) |
| `fixed_bounds_from_measured` | `time?` (default the preview time), `seed?` (default the preview seed) |
| `save`, `undo`, `redo` | none |

It returns the state plus `changed` (false when the edit was a no-op), `written` and
`disabled_not_saved` for `save`, `undone` / `redone` for `undo` / `redo`.

`editor.vfx_preview { time?, seed?, width?, height?, png?, bounds? }` renders the open effect through the
offscreen VFX harness (`regia_vfx::offscreen`: a sky, a lit ground and the full GPU simulation and
draw) at a fixed 1/60 s step, fired 0.5 m above the ground with local +Z up and framed by the CPU
probe's envelope. `time` is 0..=30 s (default 1), the size 32..=1024 per side (default 256×144). It
returns `{ path, revision, time, steps, seed, width, height, coverage, gpu_alive, counters: { additive,
alpha, mesh, alive }, gpu_ms, costs, png? }`. `coverage` is the fraction of pixels the effect changes
against the same backdrop without it. A later time steps the running preview on; an earlier time, a
new seed, a new size or any edit restarts it, so the same effect, seed and time always take the same
number of steps. With `png: true` the frame is written to a temp directory
(`<tmp>/regia-vfx-preview/`) and `png` is its path. With `bounds: true` it also returns `gpu_bounds`
(see "Fixed, measured and GPU bounds" below).

**Cost rows** (`costs`), one per emitter: `{ emitter, alive, spawned_per_sec, draw_list, draw_calls,
gpu_ms, gpu_source }`. `alive` comes from the CPU reference simulation at that time;
`spawned_per_sec` counts the scheduler's spawns in the one-second window that ends at that time (a
burst at t = 0 counts up to `cost_time` 1; `null` for an event-driven emitter). `draw_list` is the list the emitter feeds (`additive`, `alpha`, `mesh`, `ribbon` or `haze`);
each list is one indirect draw shared by its emitters, so `draw_calls` is 1 when any emitter of the list
has a live particle. `gpu_ms` is the emitter's share (by live particles) of the timed VFX simulate and
draw passes, when the device has timestamp queries and a preview frame was timed; otherwise it is
`null` and `gpu_source` is `cpu_counts`.

Check it: `editor.vfx_open`, then `editor.vfx_state { sim_steps: 90 }` and keep `sim.hash`;
`editor.vfx_edit { op: "disable_module", emitter: 0, module: "gravity" }` changes the hash and
`enable_module` brings it back; `editor.vfx_preview { png: true }` shows `coverage` above 0.

Errors (`data.reason`, with `data.hint` pointing here):

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `vfx_editor_no_project` | No project is open. |
| `vfx_editor_bad_path` | The path leaves the project or does not end in `.vfx.ron`. |
| `vfx_editor_io_failed` | The file (or the preview PNG) cannot be read or written. |
| `vfx_editor_parse_failed` | The loader refuses the file (the message is the loader's). |
| `vfx_editor_no_effect` | No effect is open. |
| `vfx_editor_unknown_emitter` | No emitter by that name or index. |
| `vfx_editor_unknown_module` | Not a module kind. |
| `vfx_editor_unknown_param` | The module has no such parameter in its current mode, or it is read-only. |
| `vfx_editor_unknown_curve` | Not a curve or gradient name. |
| `vfx_editor_bad_value` | A value outside its range, non-finite, of the wrong type, an unknown choice, a bad colour, a key `t` outside 0..=1, or a preview size or time out of range. |
| `vfx_editor_bad_index` | No key, or no emitter position, at that index. |
| `vfx_editor_too_many` | Past 64 keys on a curve or 64 emitters. |
| `vfx_editor_required_module` | `spawn`, `init` and `render` cannot be removed or disabled. |
| `vfx_editor_not_addable` | `events` cannot be added from the palette. |
| `vfx_editor_already_present` | The emitter has that module (enabled or disabled). |
| `vfx_editor_not_present` | The emitter does not have that module. |
| `vfx_editor_module_disabled` | The module is disabled: enable it before editing it. |
| `vfx_editor_invalid` | The `.vfx.ron` validator refuses the result (its message says why: `min > max`, a duplicate emitter name, a broken event link, ...). |
| `vfx_editor_serialize_failed` | The effect cannot be serialized. |
| `vfx_editor_no_gpu` | No GPU device for the preview. |
| `vfx_editor_preview_failed` | The harness or a preview frame failed on the GPU, or its GPU bounds could not be read back. |
| `vfx_editor_empty_bounds` | `fixed_bounds_from_measured`: nothing is alive at that time and seed to measure. |

`vfx.spawn_probe` requires only `read` (ADR-4760). It borrows the world immutably and uses
a scratch instance: live instances, loaded systems and entities remain unchanged. Repeated
calls with the same seed return the same positions. `vfx.spawn` still edits the live scene
and requires its existing permission.

## Scene budget and significance

Every system has its own `budget` and distance `lod`. The scene-wide budget ranks the live
instances of the whole scene, so a battle with 300 effects on a phone pays for the ones that
matter (ADR-3275). It is off until caps are set: without caps the scene schedules exactly as
before.

Each update scores every active instance: `priority × projected size × visibility × youth`.
Projected size is the bound of the system's particles over the distance (nearer and bigger
scores higher). Out of view scores a quarter. An effect that just started scores up to 1.5×,
fading over a second. Priority is 1 unless overridden per system or per instance. Instances
then take a state by rank:

| State | What it does |
|---|---|
| `full` | The first `full_instances`: spawns at its authored rate. |
| `reduced` | The rest up to `max_instances`: rate emitters at `reduced_rate` (bursts keep their counts). |
| `paused` | Out of view with `pause_offscreen`: spawns nothing; a burst due now is spent unseen. On re-entry it catches up at most `warmup_s` of its rate, never more than `warmup_max_particles`. Holds no rank slot. |
| `culled` | Past `max_instances`: spawns nothing; its live particles finish. |

Stopped or spent instances are `finishing` and not ranked. An incumbent ranks with a
`hysteresis` bonus (default 25 %) and keeps its state for `min_dwell_frames` (default 30), so
an effect at the cut does not flicker; instances coming back into view and demotions a lowered
cap needs are never held, and a new instance that outranks a held one (bonus included) takes its
slot on its first ranking while one that does not waits (ADR-7431). `max_spawns_per_frame` is shared in rank order,
`max_live` lowers the pool capacity. A per-system cap limits active instances of one system;
its `steal` policy decides what a spawn past it does: `reject` (refused), `oldest` (the oldest
is stopped), `least_significant` (the least significant is stopped, or the newcomer refused if it
scores lower).

Tier presets (`regia_vfx::quality::significance_caps`, design values):

| Tier | Instances | Full | Spawns / update | Live |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MobileLow | 16 | 6 | 256 | 4 000 |
| MobileHigh | 32 | 12 | 512 | 10 000 |
| Deck | 48 | 16 | 1 024 | 20 000 |
| Low | 32 | 12 | 512 | 20 000 |
| Medium | 96 | 32 | 2 048 | 60 000 |
| High | 160 | 64 | 4 096 | 100 000 |
| Ultra | 256 | 128 | 8 192 | 100 000 |

All tiers pause off screen with a 0.25 s warm-up. A host applies them with
`scene.significance_mut().set_caps(regia_vfx::quality::significance_caps(tier))`.

- `vfx.significance` (`limit`, 1..=1000, default 64) returns `{ enabled, caps, counts: { full,
  reduced, paused, culled, finishing }, rejected_spawns, rejected_total, stolen_total,
  transitions, transitions_total, spawned, warmup_particles, spawn_cap_reached, system_priority,
  instance_priority, instances, ranked }`. `ranked` lists live instances most significant first:
  `{ rank, id, system, state, finishing, score, distance, visible, priority, age, live,
  frames_in_state }`. Without caps `state` is null and the scores are computed now.
- `vfx.significance_set` applies, in this order: `tier` (a quality tier name, or `off` for no
  caps), `caps` (a patch: a null cap is cleared), `system_cap` (`{ system, max_instances,
  steal }`; a null `max_instances` removes it) and `priority` (`{ system | instance, value }`; a
  null value removes it). Returns `{ before, caps }`.

```json
{"method": "vfx.significance_set", "params": {"tier": "Low", "priority": {"system": "objective_flare", "value": 50}}}
{"method": "vfx.significance", "params": {"limit": 10}}
```

Check it: set a tier, spawn many effects, `wait_until` `vfx.significance` shows `counts.full +
counts.reduced` at or below `caps.max_instances`, and `ranked` with the nearest (or overridden)
instances on top. Turn the camera away: their state goes `paused` and `vfx.stats` shows no new
spawns from them.

| `data.reason` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `unknown_tier` | `tier` is not a quality tier name or `off`. |
| `unknown_cap` | `caps` holds a field that is not a cap. |
| `unknown_steal_policy` | `system_cap.steal` is not `reject`, `oldest` or `least_significant`. |
| `refused_by_cap` | `vfx.spawn` of a loaded system that its per-system cap refused. |
| `value_out_of_range` | A number out of its range, or a field of the wrong type. |
| `missing_param` | Nothing to apply, or a required field of `system_cap` / `priority` is absent. |
| `bad_source` | `priority` names both or neither of `system` and `instance`. |

All are `F0002`. A priority for a system that is not loaded or an instance that is not live is
`F0003`; a world without `regia_vfx::VfxPlugin` is `F0016`.

## System overview, emitter timeline and bounds (W12)

The System overview displays one card per emitter with a spawn summary and measured alive/draw
costs. **Enable preview** and **Solo preview** isolate emitters without editing the document,
changing the undo stack or changing saved content. Multiple soloed emitters play together;
