a disabled emitter stays disabled even when soloed. Reopening an effect clears isolation.

`editor.vfx_edit { "op": "preview_emitter", "emitter": "sparks", "enabled": true, "solo": true }`
uses the same operation. Both booleans are optional (omission keeps the current value).
`editor.vfx_edit { "op": "scrub", "time": 0.75 }` pauses and seeks the panel preview (0..=30 s).
These operations still require an open effect; invalid time is `vfx_editor_bad_value`.

`editor.vfx_state` adds `overview`, `preview_time` and `timeline`. Timeline rows contain
`name`, `start`, `spawn_end`, `alive_until`, `lifetime: [min, max]`, `burst_count`, `count_scale`
and `event_driven`. A burst ticks at its delay; a bar includes the maximum particle lifetime.
Unbounded rate emitters have null end times; event emitters have no invented start or duration.
The panel plots the first 30 seconds and provides a named scrub slider.

Pass `bounds_time` and optional `seed` to `editor.vfx_state` for `bounds` (see "Fixed, measured
and GPU bounds" below for what the boxes hold): `mode: "computed"` (or `"fixed"` when the effect has
fixed bounds), `fixed: { min, max } | null` (local space), `fixed_world: { min, max } | null` (the
fixed box at the preview instance), `kind: "particle_extents"`, `source: "cpu_reference"`,
`space: "preview_world"`, quantized `time`, `seed`, `system: { min, max } | null`, and
`emitters: [{ name, aabb: { min, max } | null }]`.
Empty emitters have null bounds; the system AABB is the union of the nonempty emitters.
The preview draws the emitter and system boxes with theme tokens at the measured fixed step.

Keyboard: Tab reaches card selection, Enable preview and Solo preview; Space toggles a focused
checkbox. Tab reaches Scrub preview; arrow keys move time. Controls follow `appearance.ui_scale`.
No new content format or golden is introduced. Tests: `w12_state_reports_emitter_timeline_and_computed_bounds`,
`w12_overview_enable_solo_and_scrub_are_view_only`, and
`w12_overview_and_timeline_operate_by_keyboard_at_two_scales`.

In the panel, expand **System overview** or **Emitter timeline** to show these controls.
The disclosure headers accept Tab and Space; collapsed sections keep the existing module
and curve editors visible in a small dock.
Preview isolation also applies to `vfx_state` simulation and cost diagnostics and to `vfx_preview`.

## Fixed, measured and GPU bounds (P-225)

**Measured bounds** are the CPU reference run with every motion module of the GPU update kernel
(gravity, drag, scene wind, curl noise, vortex, attractor, the kill plane and volume), each live
particle grown by its drawn extent: a camera-facing quad of width `s` reaches `s·√2/2` at any
rotation, a stretched quad half its diagonal (`max(velocity_scale·speed, min_length)` by `s`), a mesh
particle (the built-in cube of edge `s`) `s·√3/2`. Not included: the screen-size floor (a per-view
enlargement) and a registered render mesh larger than the unit cube. Depth collision uses the flat
ground stand-in of the reference.

**Fixed bounds** are `system.bounds` of the `.vfx.ron` (a v8 fold, `docs/formats/vfx-ron.md`): a box
in the effect's local space. When set, the box transformed by the instance culls the effect (the
scene significance ranking decides in view, distance and projected size by it) and the readout
reports `mode: "fixed"`. It never kills particles. `editor.vfx_edit` sets it (`set_fixed_bounds`),
clears it (`clear_fixed_bounds`) or sets it to the box holding the measured system bounds at a time
(`fixed_bounds_from_measured`); each is one undo step, validated like a hand edit (a non-finite
value or `min > max` is `vfx_editor_bad_value`). `editor.vfx_open` and `editor.vfx_state` report it
as `fixed_bounds: { min, max } | null`.

**GPU bounds** reduce the live GPU pool to one box per emitter: the same extent rule, `atomicMin` and
`atomicMax` on an order-preserving float key, read back once (`regia_vfx::VfxGpu::read_particle_bounds`).
The read blocks on the device, so it is opt-in: `editor.vfx_preview { bounds: true }` returns
`gpu_bounds: { source: "gpu_reduction", kind: "particle_extents", space: "preview_world",
system, emitters: [{ name, aabb }] }`, and the panel's **Read GPU bounds** checkbox reads it at most
once per half second of preview time. A game never runs it.

In the panel, under the bounds readout: **Read GPU bounds**, **Fixed bounds** (turns the box on, sized
from the measured bounds, or off), the six **Min** / **Max** fields and **Set fixed bounds from
measured**. The preview draws the fixed box with the gizmo ring token and a handle on each face in
the axis tokens; dragging a handle moves that face along its local axis (one undo step per drag).

Keyboard: Tab reaches each checkbox, field and the button; Space toggles a checkbox and presses the
button; ArrowUp and ArrowDown step a focused field. The handles are the mouse route of the fields.
Controls follow `appearance.ui_scale`.

Check it: `editor.vfx_open`, `editor.vfx_edit { op: "fixed_bounds_from_measured", time: 1.0 }`, then
`editor.vfx_state { bounds_time: 1.0 }` shows `mode: "fixed"` and a `fixed_world` box holding
`system`; `editor.vfx_preview { time: 1.0, bounds: true }` returns `gpu_bounds`.
Tests: `measured_bounds_include_particle_extent`, `an_effect_with_fixed_bounds_culls_by_them`,
`gpu_bounds_contain_every_particle`, `w13_fixed_bounds_set_from_measured_saved_and_reported`,
`w13_fixed_bounds_operate_by_keyboard_at_two_scales`, `w13_fixed_box_gizmo_drags_one_face_with_theme_tokens`.

# Entry streak

`regia_vfx::entry` draws a body entering the atmosphere along a timed track: a bright head, an
ionised trail, a long-lived dust and smoke train behind it, shed pieces, and, below 20 km, a dark
body with no glow at all. It is an engine feature for any game; nothing in it is specific to one
scene. Everything is a pure function of the track, the profile and the time (`frame / 60`), so two
runs draw the same frame.

## What it models

- **Heating** scales with air density times speed cubed (`heating_flux`), against an exponential
  atmosphere. The glow saturates in that flux.
- **Gates.** The glow is exactly 0 at or below `GLOW_CEILING_M` (20 km), whatever the speed, and
  also below the ablation speed (2 km/s, fully open at 4 km/s). A body falling at terminal speed
  (150 to 250 m/s) never glows, even high up.
- **Colour** follows gas temperature: `head_temperature_k` gives about 3000 K below 3 km/s up to
  about 9000 K at 11 km/s, and the gas cools exponentially toward 1300 K (`cooled_temperature_k`,
  0.45 s). `temperature_color` is the full ramp (deep red, orange, yellow-white, white, blue-white, with
  sodium, magnesium and iron line tints); what the streak shows is `glow_color`, the same ramp held to
  `VISIBLE_MIN_K..=VISIBLE_MAX_K` (3500 to 6000 K). A fireball's light is mostly a 4000 to 5000 K vapour
  and a day-adapted eye takes about 6000 K as white, so the head reads warm white, never blue; cooling
  gas goes yellow, then orange, and then fades out instead of turning deep red (which reads pink, or as
  a laser line, over a blue sky). `heat_color` is the older speed-only ramp.
- **Head**: a round, soft blob (Gaussian across, faded to nothing at both ends along the direction of
  travel as seen on screen, as long as it is wide plus the on-screen part of one exposure of travel)
  in three nested layers, so it has no outline at any range and stays round when the body comes
  straight at the camera.
- **Ionised wake**: about a second and a half of samples behind the head (dense next to it),
  brightness falling off in two exponentials (under half the head after 0.1 s, under a twentieth by a
  second) and gusting, the colour cooling. Its pixel floor narrows as it dims, so it tapers to a point
  instead of reading as a constant-width rod. No vertex emits more than `peak_radiance`.
- **Afterglow**: the young train keeps a faint, gusting glow (`ember` on the train points) that cools
  and fades within `EMBER_LIFE_S` (3 s): a few seconds after the head goes dark nothing glows.
- **Train**: deposited where the body ablates, pale grey-brown (`DUST_COLOR`). It emerges from behind
  the wake over 0.6 s, is thrown out by the hot wake to 0.3 of the cylindrical blast radius (Mach number
  times the body's diameter, about 100 to 180 m half-width at 11 km/s) within about a second, then
  widens by turbulent diffusion (40 m per square-root second, about a kilometre across after two
  minutes on the width formula), billows and meanders smoothly, thins as it widens and drifts with
  `EntryProfile::wind`. Glowing dust fades on `dust_life_s` (24 s by default), so the default profile
  does not show that two-minute width. `train_life_s` (240 s) fades the dark-flight damage smoke and
  is the sample window; `legacy_dust` sets `dust_life_s` to 240 s. Below the ceiling a faint dark
  train (`damage_smoke`, 0 turns it off) stands for on-board damage. The train is lit smoke; it never
  emits.
- **Shading**: every glowing ribbon is soft (Gaussian across, no flat core) and additive (it adds
  light and never dims the sky behind it); the dust is soft and hides the sky behind it. Both use the
  flag slots of `TrailVertex` (`_pad`: additive share, `_pad2[0]`: soft); other trails leave them at 0
  and draw exactly as before.
- **Shed pieces** are ablation debris (2 to 20 cm). They break off from `shed_altitude_m` on, spread
  over the glowing flight, and fall back behind the head along the flight path: a fragment has more
  area per mass than the body, so drag (`Cd A rho v^2 / 2m`, with `A / m` going as one over its radius)
  slows it faster. The smaller the piece, the faster it falls back. A small sideways push at break-up
  (Passey and Melosh 1980, damped by the same drag) keeps them within a few pixels of the train's line
  at 4K. Each glows from its own heating (`rho v^3` at its own speed), never more than `PIECE_MAX_SHARE`
  (0.6) of the head, bright while it ablates, then cools (yellow, then orange) and fades over the end of a short life (`PIECE_LIFE_MIN_S` to
  `PIECE_LIFE_MAX_S`, 2 to 4 s, the smallest first), flickering as it tumbles; every piece is gone before
  the head goes dark. It is drawn as a short streak along its own velocity: one exposure of motion
  (`speed * shutter`, as the head) plus its vapour cooling behind it over `PIECE_WAKE_S` (0.12 s), one
  soft core with no halo. Seen exactly head-on it is a round blob, as the head is.
- **Dark body**: a thin dark streak of `speed * shutter` at least `min_px` wide, so it reads at range.
- **Range fit**: a point beyond 90 % of the camera's far plane is pulled along its view ray to that
  distance and its width shrinks by the same factor, so a bolide 190 km away looks the same but is not
  clipped by a 20 km far plane. The train keeps at least half of `min_px`.

## Using it

Add `EntryStreakPlugin` next to `VfxRuntimePlugin` and put an `EntryStreak` component on an entity:

```rust,wrap
# use regia::prelude::*;
# use regia_core::math::Vec3;
# let app: &mut App = todo!();
# let world: &mut World = todo!();
use regia_vfx::entry::{EntryTrack, TrackPoint};
use regia_vfx::{EntryStreak, EntryStreakPlugin};

app.add_plugins(EntryStreakPlugin);
let track = EntryTrack::new(vec![
    TrackPoint { time: 0.0, position: Vec3::new(0.0, 60_000.0, -40_000.0) },
    TrackPoint { time: 8.0, position: Vec3::new(0.0, 30_000.0, 0.0) },
])?;
world.spawn(EntryStreak::new(track));
```

`frame` advances once per update while `playing`; set it to seek. Set `tier` to `EntryTier::Cheap` on
Low, Deck and Mobile: it keeps the head, a six-sample ion trail and a train at a quarter of the density,
and drops the pieces. `peak_radiance` is display-referred like every other VFX colour (above 1
blooms), so a host sets it against its exposure.

## Agent protocol

`vfx.entry_state` evaluates a track at a time and returns the head (position, altitude, speed, glow,
radiance, colour, `temperature_k`, `dark`), the counts of ion points, train points, glowing (`ember_points`)
train points and pieces, `ion_tail_temperature_k` (cooler than the head), `train_max_half_width_m` (the
widest train point), `glow_range_k` (the colour temperatures the glow shows, `[3500, 6000]`) and
`piece_streaks`: per glowing piece, `behind_m` (along the head's heading), `aside_m` (off the line
through the head along its heading), `speed`, `age_s`, `life_s`, `glow`, `glow_share` (its glow over
the head's) and `temperature_k`. It is read-only.

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"vfx.entry_state","params":{
  "track":[{"time":0,"position":[90000,80000,107000]},{"time":120,"position":[700,105.7,5]}],
  "time":60,"tier":"cheap"}}
```

Check it: at a `time` where the track is at or below 20 km, `head.dark` is `true`, `head.glow` and
`head.radiance` are 0, and `ion_points` and `pieces` are 0 (`piece_streaks` is empty); 3 s later `ember_points` is 0 too, while
`train_points` and `train_max_half_width_m` (hundreds of metres) show the dust train. A few seconds
after the shed altitude, every entry of `piece_streaks` has `behind_m` > 0, `aside_m` smaller than
`behind_m` once the piece is a second old, and `glow_share` at most 0.6. Parameters: `track` (required, at most 64
points, times strictly increasing), `time`, `tier` (`full` or `cheap`), `ground_y`, `wind`,
`shed_count`, `seed`, and the dust knobs `dust_opacity_scale` (default 0.5), `dust_life_s` (default 24)
and `legacy_dust` (true starts from the pre-look-5 dust: opacity 1, pale grey-brown, 240 s).

Errors: `F0002` (invalid params, JSON-RPC `-32602`) for a missing or malformed track, a
non-increasing time, a non-finite value or an unknown tier.

## Cost

Evaluation is a few hundred CPU samples (about 1000 train points at the full tier, 240 at cheap) and
at most a few thousand ribbon vertices through the existing trail pipeline. Measured numbers at 1440p
and 4K are in the lane report; the effect adds no GPU pass of its own.

# Hard-surface materials

Hulls and set pieces pick up detail, a clearcoat lobe, brushed-metal anisotropy, specular
occlusion, multi-scatter, parallax panel lines, and curvature edge wear from the standard
material. The factors default off on `LabMaterial::EMPTY`, so a lab scene that does not set
them keeps the previous shading. A `.material.ron` that migrates from v1 turns multi-scatter
and specular occlusion on.

The decision is ADR-043. The formulas and their papers are in `docs/provenance.md`.

## What is shaded

| Factor | Uniform | When it changes pixels |
|---|---|---|
| Detail albedo / normal / roughness | `detail`, `detail_fade` | Any strength above zero. Weight is fade × mask × strength |
| Clearcoat | `coat.x`, `coat.y` | Factor above zero. Dielectric F0 is 0.04. Uses the base normal |
| Anisotropy | `coat.z`, `coat.w` | Strength above zero and a non-zero tangent. Rotation is radians |
| Specular occlusion | `response.x` | Above 0.5. Multiplies the indirect specular (base, multi-scatter, coat), from AO |
| Multi-scatter | `response.y` | Above 0.5. Rough metals stay brighter |
| Parallax | `response.z`, `pom.x` | Scale above zero and `FrameQuality::parallax_occlusion` |
| Edge wear | `wear`, `wear_tint` | Intensity above zero and source 1 (curvature) or 2 (AO) |

`FrameQuality::parallax_occlusion` is on for Desktop High and Desktop Ultra and off for
Mobile, Desktop Low, Deck, the lab baseline, and the editor. The lab uploads it as
`LabFrame.pcss.z`. `quality.w` is the PCSS noise index. The view is normalized before the
step count. A height of 1 does not move the UV.

Six maps pack into three textures at upload: detail albedo (RGB) + roughness (A), detail
normal (RGB) + mask (A), height (R) + curvature (G). Missing channels stay neutral
(albedo 0.5, roughness 0.5, mask 1, height 1, curvature 0.5).

## Authoring

`docs/formats/material-v2.example.ron` is the v2 block. v1 files stay frozen;
`migrate_material_v1_to_v2` fills the defaults. `regia upgrade-project` writes them back.
The user-guide section is [Materials](book/user-guide/materials.md).

`LabMaterial::from_authored` copies the factors and leaves texture slots empty.
`LabMaterial::from_authored_with_maps` copies resolved detail, height, and curvature
images; the mesh bind group uploads those three packed textures. The lab scenes in
`regia_render::hard_surface` bind procedural maps themselves.

## Look-dev

```sh
cargo run -p lookdev -- --hull /tmp/hull-closeup.png
```

That is the hull close-up: painted metal, clearcoat spheres, 960×540 at EV 14.5, lab
quality plus the parallax gate.
The cost table (second-frame forward milliseconds, 1280×720, 12 hulls, one factor at a
time) is:

```sh
flock /tmp/regia-gpu.lock flock /tmp/ferrite-gpu.lock env VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_SELECT='*nvidia*' \
  cargo run -p lookdev --release -- --hull-cost docs/evidence/hard-surface/cost.md
```

## Goldens

`cargo test -p regia_render --test hard_surface` renders each feature on and off on
lavapipe at 960×540, EV 14.5. Mean luma must sit in 60..=180. A coat glint must be present
only when the lobe is on, specular occlusion must darken a cavity, and the hull close-up
must show those glints. The on frame must also match
`docs/evidence/hard-surface/<feature>.png` (luma SSIM ≥ 0.98). Bless only on lavapipe:

```sh
env VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_SELECT='*lvp*' REGIA_BLESS=1 \
  cargo test -p regia_render --test hard_surface
```

A parallax material with the profile gate off must match the feature-off frame.

<!-- source: book/agents/hair-cards.md -->
# Hair cards

Hair, eyebrows, lashes, fur and foliage drawn as alpha-tested cards get a strand shading model
from the standard material: two Kajiya-Kay highlight lobes, light through the strands, a
root-to-tip colour and alpha ramp, and an alpha strategy. The feature is `LabMaterial::hair`
(`HairFactors`). It defaults off, and a material without it shades exactly as before. The
decision is ADR-245; the papers are in `docs/provenance.md`.

## What is shaded

| Factor | Effect |
|---|---|
| `primary_shift`, `primary_exponent`, `primary_strength` | The first lobe: a tight line, takes the light's colour |
| `secondary_shift`, `secondary_exponent`, `secondary_strength` | The shifted, broader lobe, takes the hair colour |
| `shift_noise`, `streak_density` | Per-strand jitter of both shifts across the card's `u`, so the highlight breaks into streaks |
| `transmission` | Wraps the diffuse cosine, so a card lit from behind glows instead of going black |
| `root_color`, `tip_color`, `root_alpha`, `tip_alpha`, `ramp_start`, `ramp_end` | Multipliers on base colour and alpha, blended along the card's `v` (`ramp_start` above `ramp_end` flips it) |
| `alpha` | `Hashed`, `Sorted` or `Coverage` (below) |

The strand direction is the mesh **tangent** (glTF `TANGENT`), root to tip, and `v` runs root
(0) to tip (1) by default. Cards need tangents; a card with none shades its diffuse and ramp
but no highlight.

## Alpha strategies

- **`Hashed`** (default): the material is alpha tested. On a TSR frame the threshold is a
  per-pixel, per-frame hash, the same in the depth prepass and the colour pass, so TSR's
  accumulation turns it into fractional coverage. Without TSR it is the hard cutoff
  (`LabMaterial::alpha_cutoff`). Cards write depth, so they need no sorting.
- **`Sorted`**: the material draws in the sorted alpha-blend pass, back to front, with no depth
  writes. Soft tips, no TSR needed; overlapping cards need the draw order to be right. The
  order-independent pass excludes hair cards, so turning that pass on does not change them.
- **`Coverage`**: alpha-to-coverage on multisampled frames. This build has no coverage
  pipeline, so it draws as `Hashed` (ADR-245).

`HairFactors::apply_alpha_mode` writes the matching `alpha_mode` and cutoff on the material;
the renderer also derives the mode itself (`hair::effective_alpha_mode`).

## Shadows

A hair card casts its shadow through its alpha test, using the translucency maps (see
[Translucent shadows](book/agents/translucent-shadows.md)): the ramp alpha is tested against the cutoff, so
the shadow has the card's strands and not its square outline. Every preset but Mobile Low has
the maps (Mobile High one cascade, Desktop Low and up two or more plus local lights); Mobile Low
casts no hair shadow.

## Agent methods

`render.hair_get {entity}` reads the factors. `render.hair_set {entity, ...}` patches them; any
patch turns hair on, and `enabled: false` turns it off and keeps the tuning. Turning it off
also puts back the alpha mode and cutoff the material had before `render.hair_set` turned hair
on (an opaque mesh is opaque again). The entity gets its own copy of the material, so other
instances of the shared material keep their look.

```json
{"method": "render.hair_set", "params": {"entity": 4294967297, "tip_color": [0.3, 0.2, 0.1],
  "tip_alpha": 0.3, "ramp": [0.2, 0.9], "alpha": "hashed"}}
```

Then `seeing.screenshot` to look at it. Hair on a material graph surface is not supported: the
graph path skips the ramp and the alpha factor.

## Authoring in Rust

```rust,ignore
let mut material = LabMaterial::default();
material.hair = HairFactors {
    tip_color: [0.35, 0.28, 0.22],
    tip_alpha: 0.35,
    ..HairFactors::strands()
};
material
    .hair
    .apply_alpha_mode(&mut material.alpha_mode, &mut material.alpha_cutoff);
```

## Tests

`cargo test -p regia_render --test hair_cards` renders a card mesh: pixels change only for the
material that enables hair, the lobes add a highlight, the ramp darkens the tip, the strategies
draw, and the shadow follows the alpha test. `REGIA_PREVIEW=/tmp/hair` also writes the
look-dev fan (hair off and on). `--test hair_cards_warm` checks that no pipeline is created
after warm-up.

<!-- source: book/agents/material-graph.md -->
# Material graphs

A material graph (`.matgraph.ron`, format v4, `docs/formats/matgraph-ron.md`) is a node graph that
compiles to the forward pass's `material_surface` function. The graph decides the surface (base
color, normal, roughness, metallic, occlusion, emissive, alpha); the lighting (sun, local lights,
IBL, GI, clearcoat, multi-scatter) is the engine's one hand-written code path, so a graph material
lights exactly like a standard one. Instances (`.matinst.ron`) override a graph's parameters and
textures without new shader code: instances that override only parameters and textures share the
graph's pipelines (a static-switch override selects another permutation).

## Read and list

`material.graph_get` with no `name` lists the library (`{ graphs: [{ name, revision, nodes, params,
textures }], cache }`). With a `name` it returns the graph three ways: `ron` (the file text),
`graph` (JSON, the shape `material.graph_set` accepts) and a flat `nodes` list
(`{ name, kind, inputs, texture }`) that is the quickest way to see the wiring.

## Create and edit

`material.graph_set { name, ron }` (or `graph` as JSON) creates or replaces a graph. To edit in
place, send only what changes:

```json
{ "name": "paint",
  "nodes": { "vcol": "VertexColor",
             "rgb":  { "Swizzle": { "input": "vcol", "channels": "rgb" } },
             "base": { "Mul": ["tint", "rgb"] },
             "old_node": null },
  "output": { "base_color": "base" } }
```

`nodes` upserts by name (`null` deletes), `output` sets slots (`null` clears one); `params`,
`textures` and `shading` replace those blocks whole. Every call compiles and answers
`{ revision, ok, key, errors: [{ node, message }] }`; a graph that does not compile is still stored,
so you can fix a node error with the next edit. `ron` is migrated to format v4 before it is stored.
`graph` JSON is not: `format_version` must already be 4, or the compile error is
`format_version N (migrate to v4 first)` and a later `nodes` edit leaves that version in place.
Errors name the node (`"rgb"`), a declaration
(`"param:tint"`, `"texture:albedo"`) or an output (`"output:base_color"`).

## Compile

`material.compile { name, include_wgsl }` returns the layout the renderer binds:
`params: [{ name, slot, type }]` (uniform `vec4` slots 1–15; slot 0 is time),
`textures: [{ name, slot, binding, color_space }]` (seven slots), `node_types`, the pipeline `key`,
`graph_hash`, `cache_hit` and, with `include_wgsl: true`, the generated WGSL. Graphs with the same
structure and switch values share one compile (`graph_hash`, the hash of that permutation) and one
pipeline set (`key`); parameter values and texture paths never trigger a recompile. A switch
override is another permutation with its own `graph_hash`.

It also returns the expansion's size (ADR-4901): `lowered_nodes` (flat nodes and aliases after the
switches and functions resolve) and `function_calls` (every nesting level counted), with
`limits: { max_lowered_nodes, max_static_switches }`.

Every entry of `errors` (from `material.compile` and `material.graph_set`) is
`{ node, message, code, authored_node }`. `code` is one of `node`, `param`, `texture`, `switch`,
`function`, `output`, `graph` and `generated_code_invalid`. `authored_node` is the node of the graph
the error belongs to: for a node inside an expanded function (`node: "big/half"`) it is the call
node `big`. Only `code: "node"` has one. `generated_code_invalid` is the one failure no authored
node maps to: generated code a host shader rejects, an engine bug. The compile fails on it and the
cook fails with it, so it is never dropped.

```text
→ material.compile { "name": "f" }
← { "ok": false, "errors": [{ "node": "big/half", "message": "unknown node `missing`",
     "code": "node", "authored_node": "big" }], ... }
```

## A graph

```ron,matgraph
(
    format_version: 4,
    name: "dusty_metal",
    params: [
        (name: "tint", value: Color((0.55, 0.56, 0.58))),
        (name: "dust", value: Color((0.42, 0.27, 0.16))),
        (name: "tiles", value: Float(0.5)),
    ],
    textures: [(name: "grime", path: "textures/grime.png", color_space: Linear)],
    nodes: {
        "tint": Param("tint"),
        "dust": Param("dust"),
        "tiles": Param("tiles"),
        "grime": Triplanar(texture: "grime", scale: "tiles", sharpness: 4.0),
        "grime_r": Swizzle(input: "grime", channels: "r"),
        "n": WorldNormal,
        "up": Swizzle(input: "n", channels: "y"),
        "settle": Mul("up", "grime_r"),
        "mask": Saturate("settle"),
        "base": Lerp(a: "tint", b: "dust", t: "mask"),
        "metallic": OneMinus("mask"),
        "rough_lo": Float(0.35),
        "rough_hi": Float(0.95),
        "roughness": Lerp(a: "rough_lo", b: "rough_hi", t: "mask"),
    },
    output: (base_color: Some("base"), metallic: Some("metallic"), roughness: Some("roughness")),
)
```

Node kinds: inputs (`TexCoord`, `VertexColor`, `WorldPosition`, `WorldNormal`, `ViewDirection`,
`CameraDistance`, `Time`, `Wind`, `Param`, `Float`/`Vec2`/`Vec3`/`Vec4`), textures (`Sample` with an optional
`lod`, `Triplanar`, `UvTransform`, `Parallax`), math (`Add`, `Sub`, `Mul`, `Div`, `Min`, `Max`, `Pow`,
`Dot`, `Lerp`, `Smoothstep`, `Saturate`, `OneMinus`, `Abs`, `Normalize`, `Length`, `Swizzle`,
`Append`), noise (`Noise(input: "uv", octaves: 4)`, v4: fractal gradient noise in 0..1 at a `Float`, `Vec2`
or `Vec3` position, 1–8 octaves) and shading (`Fresnel`, `HeightBlend`, `UnpackNormal`, `NormalStrength`, `BlendNormals` with
`Rnm`, `Udn` or `Whiteout`). `Add`, `Sub`, `Mul`, `Div`, `Min`, `Max` and `Pow` accept a `Float` beside a
vector; other widths must match. `Lerp`'s `t` may be a `Float` or the same width as the edges. `Dot` needs
two vectors of one width (a `Float` is an error).
Surface outputs are typed: `base_color`, `emissive` and `normal` take `Vec3` (use `Swizzle` on a sample),
the rest (`alpha`, `metallic`, `roughness`, `occlusion`) `Float`; `normal` is tangent space unless
the `output` block sets `normal_space: World` (it is not a `shading` field).

`WorldPosition`, `Triplanar` (which projects the world position) and `ObjectPosition` are world positions, also
in a streamed world whose floating origin has moved (spec 78 § 12, ADR-2435): a triplanar rock, world noise or a
wind phase stays on the same world point across a rebase. The compiler's output does not add the origin itself; the
renderer adds it when it composes the graph, from the highest parameter slot the graph does not read
(`regia_render::surface_graph::graph_origin_slot`). A graph that reads a world or object position and also reads
all 15 parameter slots does not compile (`graph`): at most 14 parameters may be read together with a position, so
one slot stays free for the origin. A graph that reads no position may still declare 15 parameters. Far from the
world's zero (beyond about 16 km) these positions have under a millimeter of `f32` precision, as they had before a
rebase. A double-sided back face negates the tangent frame (`SurfaceInput.facing` is 1 on a front face and -1 on
a back face), the same rule as the hand-written normal map.

## Switches, functions, vertex offset (v2)

This sample is a v2 file. `MaterialGraph::from_ron` and `regia upgrade-project --write` migrate it to v4
(the step only moves the version).

```ron,matgraph
(
    format_version: 2,
    name: "swaying_panel",
    params: [
        (name: "tint", value: Color((0.6, 0.62, 0.65))),
        (name: "sway", value: Vec3((0.0, 0.0, 0.08))),
    ],
    switches: [(name: "weathered", default: true)],
    functions: {
        "weather": Inline((
            inputs: [(name: "c", ty: Vec3)],
            nodes: { "c": Input("c"), "rust": Vec3((0.45, 0.22, 0.1)), "k": Float(0.35),
                     "out": Lerp(a: "c", b: "rust", t: "k") },
            outputs: { "out": "out" },
        )),
    },
    nodes: {
        "tint": Param("tint"),
        "worn": Call(function: "weather", args: { "c": "tint" }),
        "base": Switch(switch: "weathered", on: "worn", off: "tint"),
        "t": Time,
        "obj": ObjectPosition,
        "phase_x": Swizzle(input: "obj", channels: "x"),
        "phase": Add("t", "phase_x"),
        "wave": Sin("phase"),
        "uv": TexCoord,
        "height": Swizzle(input: "uv", channels: "y"),
        "amount": Mul("wave", "height"),
        "sway": Param("sway"),
        "offset": Mul("sway", "amount"),
    },
    output: (base_color: Some("base"), world_position_offset: Some("offset")),
    shading: (max_vertex_offset: 0.1),
)
```

- **Static switches** pick a branch at compile time: an instance sets `switches: { "weathered":
  false }` and gets its own permutation (`material.compile` reports the `key`).
- **Functions** expand in place under the call node's name (a call node `worn` names an error inside
  it `worn/out`); they can live
  in a `.matfunc.ron` file (`functions: { "weather": File("assets/materials/weather.matfunc.ron") }`).
- **`world_position_offset`** moves vertices in every pass: the surface, its depth, its shadow and
  its motion vectors stay together. No eye-dependent nodes or `Parallax` may feed it. Set
  `shading.max_vertex_offset` so culling keeps the displaced mesh.
- **`TexCoord1`** reads the mesh's second UV set (`FrameMesh::uv1`, the `MeshUv1` component), or
  the first set when the mesh has none.

## Wind (v3)

`Wind` is the scene wind as a `Vec2`: meters per second on world X (`x`) and world Z (`y`). The
renderer writes it beside the material clock (graph parameter slot 0 `zw`, set by
`FrameRenderer::set_foliage_wind`; zero when nothing sets it), and it reads the same in the
surface and the vertex stage. A graph that reads `Wind` is time-reading (`material.compile`
answers `uses_time: true`), which is what makes the renderer write the slot. This plant bends
along the wind, more toward its top, with a gust that varies per instance:

```ron,matgraph
(
    format_version: 4,
    name: "reed_sway",
    nodes: {
        "wind": Wind,
        "t": Time,
        "op": ObjectPosition,
        "wp": WorldPosition,
        "opx": Swizzle(input: "op", channels: "x"),
        "freq": Float(3.1415927),
        "tw": Mul("t", "freq"),
        "arg": Add("tw", "opx"),
        "s": Sin("arg"),
        "gust_amp": Float(0.2),
        "gust_var": Mul("s", "gust_amp"),
        "gust_base": Float(0.8),
        "gust": Add("gust_base", "gust_var"),
        "wpy": Swizzle(input: "wp", channels: "y"),
        "opy": Swizzle(input: "op", channels: "y"),
        "rel": Sub("wpy", "opy"),
        "inv_height": Float(0.5),
        "h_lin": Mul("rel", "inv_height"),
        "h": Saturate("h_lin"),
        "h2": Mul("h", "h"),
        "wx": Swizzle(input: "wind", channels: "x"),
        "wz": Swizzle(input: "wind", channels: "y"),
        "zero": Float(0.0),
        "wxy": Append("wx", "zero"),
        "w3": Append("wxy", "wz"),
        "stiffness": Float(0.02),
        "bend": Mul("w3", "stiffness"),
        "gusty": Mul("bend", "gust"),
        "offset": Mul("gusty", "h2"),
        "leaf": Vec3((0.18, 0.32, 0.08)),
    },
    output: (base_color: Some("leaf"), world_position_offset: Some("offset")),
    shading: (max_vertex_offset: 0.8),
)
```

The offset is `wind · 0.02 · gust · h²` meters, with `h` the height above the object's origin over
2 m: at the renderer's 40 m/s wind limit and a full gust that is 0.8 m, so
`shading.max_vertex_offset` is 0.8. The gust's 2 s period divides the clock's lap, so it loops
without a seam ([Material clock and wind](book/agents/material-clock.md)). A surface output can read the wind
too, for example `Length("wind")` to tint leaves in a storm. `Wind` is the v3 node and `Noise` is the
v4 node. v2 and v3 graphs load with the same nodes at v4, and
`regia upgrade-project --write` rewrites `.matgraph.ron` files at v4 and `.matfunc.ron` files at
v3 (the function format holds the same node set).

## In a game

A `MaterialGraphRef { path }` component on an entity with a `MeshRenderer` draws it with the
cooked graph or instance at `path` (`MaterialGraphPlugin`; scene files:
`"regia_matgraph::runtime::MaterialGraphRef": (path: "assets/materials/hull.matinst.ron")`).
Cooked graphs load without a compile; a recook plus the dev cooked watcher hot-reloads every
entity using the asset. New graphs are prewarmed on the renderer's worker threads and a level
load waits for them, so the first frame of a level draws every graph with no pipeline built on
the frame thread (`FrameRenderer::material_graph_stats`: `built_on_frame_path` stays 0). A graph
met for the first time mid-level draws with the standard surface until its pipelines land
(`fallback_draws`). Graph draws use the GPU-driven instanced path like other materials
(`FrameRenderer::draw_stats`: `graph_instanced`).

## Check the result on screen

The renderer draws a graph material through the same frame as everything else, so the
`seeing.*` tools apply unchanged. The parity test renders two hand-written materials and their
graph rebuilds on lavapipe and requires every channel within 1/255 (they match exactly):
`cargo test -p regia_matgraph --test parity`. The runtime paths (instancing, prewarm, vertex
offset in every pass, the second UV set) are `cargo test -p regia_matgraph --test
runtime_paths`; the cook and hot reload are `cargo test -p regia_asset_pipeline --test
matgraph_cook`. Frames: `docs/evidence/material-graph/`, `docs/evidence/matgraph-runtime/`.

## Limits

At most 15 parameters (14 when the graph also reads a world or object position, so the floating origin keeps a
slot), 7 textures and 8 nested function calls per graph; two UV sets. At most
16 static switches per graph (`MAX_STATIC_SWITCHES`: up to 65,536 code permutations, of which the
cook compiles only the ones the graph and its instances pick), and at most 4096 flat nodes after the
functions expand (`MAX_LOWERED_NODES`). A function called many times, nested a few levels, grows
exponentially, so the expansion stops at the bound with one error on the authored call node
(ADR-4901). The vertex
offset does not bend normals. Decal receivers and the editor's material preview draw a
vertex-offset mesh at its rest position.

## Checking foreground emission across the sky

For an additive hologram, compare screenshots of the same fixed camera and
exposure with the emitting mesh visible and hidden. Keep any opaque backing
present in both frames. Check regions on both sides of the terrain/sky silhouette;
the holo must change pixels on each side. Repeat with an airless black sky and
with the backing hidden. A foreground opaque occluder must still hide the holo.
Use the existing material graph and scene-edit methods; no new protocol method
is needed (ADR-7963). The independent lavapipe regression is
`cargo test -p regia_render --test holo_over_sky -- --nocapture`.

`render.graph` continues to expose the existing `forward` and `atmosphere` steps.
The forward step includes the physical sky background before transparency;
`atmosphere` retains aerial perspective and its weather veil. Accordingly,
`forward_ms` includes the background and `atmosphere_ms` measures the remaining
late atmosphere work. See the [world-space holo contract](book/systems/material-graph.md#foreground-holograms-and-ui-in-world-space).

<!-- source: book/agents/animation-editor.md -->
# Animation editor

The editor's animation tooling has three panels — **Anim Graph**, **Clip** and **Skeleton** — and
an `editor.anim_*` agent surface that edits the same documents. Every mutating call is an undo
entry on the editor's shared stack (`editor.undo` / `editor.redo` revert it in order with level
edits).

Two documents are open at a time:

- the **graph** (`.animgraph.ron`, frozen format v3; v1 and v2 still load
  through the migrator) plus an editor-only `.animgraph.layout.ron` of canvas
  positions next to it (layout format v1);
- the **rig's authoring sidecar** (`<source>.animedit.ron`, format v1,
  `docs/formats/animedit-ron.md`): notifies, named curves, property tracks, the root-motion mode,
  sockets and IK chains authored on top of an imported glTF.

## Graph model

Nodes have numeric ids, a canvas `scope` and named input slots. The root canvas is `"root"`; a
state's sub-graph is `{ "machine": <state machine id>, "state": "Idle" }`. Slots are named like
the runtime's node paths: `a`/`b` (blend), `base`/`additive`, `base`/`layer0…` (layers), `inner`
(IK, look-at, root motion), `source` (montage slot). Each canvas has one **output**: `editor.anim_connect { child }`
without a `parent` makes `child` its canvas's output. Graphs are trees: connecting a node that
already feeds something moves it.

| Kind | `data` fields (serde JSON, shallow-merged) |
|---|---|
| `clip` | `clip`, `looping`, `speed`, `sync_group` |
| `blend_space_1d` | `space: { param, samples: [{ value, clip }] }`, `sync_group` |
| `blend_space_2d` | `space: { param_x, param_y, samples: [{ point: [x, y], clip }], triangles: [] }`, `sync_group` |
| `state_machine` | none — use `editor.anim_state` / `editor.anim_transition` (`set_node` accepts `{ initial }`) |
| `blend` | `alpha_param` |
| `additive` | `weight_param` |
| `layer` | `layers: [{ mask: { joints, include_children }, mode: "Override"\|"Additive", weight_param }]` |
| `two_bone_ik` | `chain: [root, mid, tip]`, `target: { "Param": name }\|{ "Socket": name }`, `pole`, `weight_param` |
| `look_at` | `joint`, `target`, `max_yaw`, `max_pitch`, `weight_param` |
| `root_motion` | `mode: "None"\|"XZ"\|"XYZ"\|"Yaw"` |
| `slot` | `name` (a slot of the skeleton's table), `eval_idle_source` (default `true`); input `source`. Plays that slot's montages inside the graph (`.animgraph.ron` v3, spec 34 M9): nodes above it (IK, layers) see the montage pose |
| `chain_ik` | `root`, `tip`, `solver: "Fabrik"\|"Ccd"`, `target`, `pole`, `limits: null\|{ "Uniform": limit }\|{ "PerJoint": [{ joint, limit }] }`, `iterations` (≤ 256), `tolerance` (meters), `weight_param`; input `inner`. FABRIK or CCD over a chain of any length (`.animgraph.ron` v4, ADR-8475) |
| `body_aim` | `joints: [[name, share], …]` (bottom first), `aim_joint`, `axis: [x, y, z]` (default `[0, 0, -1]`), `target`, `limits`, `passes` (1..=32, default 8), `weight_param`; input `inner`. Turns the stack so `aim_joint`'s axis points at the target (v4) |
| `stride_warp` | `ground_speed_param` (float, m/s), `settings: { strength, min_speed, ratio_min, ratio_max, response, mode: "Rate"\|"Pose" }` (default full strength, `Pose`), `legs: [[hip, knee, ankle], …]` and `pelvis` (needed in `Pose` mode), `stride_length` (meters, default 0.5); input `inner`. Matches the inner clips' speed to the ground speed by clock or stride IK (v4, ADR-8540) |
| `orientation_warp` | `heading_param` (float, radians, 0 = forward, counter-clockwise), `pelvis`, `spine: [[name, share], …]` (shares sum to 1), `strength` (default 1), `max_delta` (radians, default π/2); input `inner`. Turns the lower body toward the heading, the spine back (v4) |

## Build a graph

```json
{"method": "editor.anim_open", "params": {"create": true, "path": "anim/hero.animgraph.ron"}}
{"method": "editor.anim_param", "params": {"name": "Speed", "kind": "float"}}
{"method": "editor.anim_param", "params": {"name": "Grounded", "kind": "bool", "default": true}}
{"method": "editor.anim_add_node", "params": {"kind": "state_machine"}}
{"method": "editor.anim_state", "params": {"machine": 1, "op": "add", "name": "Idle"}}
{"method": "editor.anim_add_node", "params": {"kind": "clip", "scope": {"machine": 1, "state": "Idle"},
  "data": {"clip": "Survey", "sync_group": "gait"}}}
{"method": "editor.anim_connect", "params": {"child": 2}}
{"method": "editor.anim_transition", "params": {"machine": 1, "from": "Idle", "to": "Walk",
  "conditions": [{"Float": {"param": "Speed", "op": "Gt", "value": 0.5}}], "duration": 0.25}}
{"method": "editor.anim_connect", "params": {"child": 1}}
{"method": "editor.anim_save", "params": {}}
```

Conditions: `{"Float": {param, op, value}}`, `{"Int": …}`, `{"Bool": {param, value}}`,
`{"Trigger": {param}}`, `"ClipFinished"`, `{"Notify": "Land"}`; `op` is `Lt Le Gt Ge Eq Ne`.
`from: null` is "any state". `editor.anim_state` ops: `add remove rename initial move` (`rename` takes `new_name`).
`editor.anim_transition` takes `interruptible` (default true): whether a later transition may cut this one short.
`editor.anim_transition` ops: `add` (default), `set { index }`, `remove { index }`. `blend` is
`Crossfade` (default) | `Inertialize` | `InertializeSpring` (see
[Inertialized transitions](book/agents/inertialization.md)). `duration` is the cross-fade length or the
inertial decay time.

Editing nodes after the fact: `editor.anim_set_node { node, data?, pos? }` shallow-merges `data`
into the node's kind fields (a type mismatch is an error, nothing changes) and/or moves it;
`editor.anim_remove_node { node }` deletes it (a state machine takes its states' sub-graphs
with it); `editor.anim_disconnect { parent, slot }` clears one input, and
`editor.anim_disconnect { scope }` without `parent` clears that canvas's output.

`editor.anim_graph { ron: true }` returns every node (`id, kind, scope, pos, inputs, data`; state
machines list `states`, `initial`, `transitions`), `valid` / `error` (the same validation the
runtime loader runs), `unreachable` (nodes no output reaches — they are not saved), `paths`
(node id → runtime path) and the RON `anim_save` would write. `anim_save` refuses an invalid
graph and reports the unreachable nodes it dropped.

The end-to-end test builds `samples/third_person`'s locomotion graph (three states, five
transitions, four foot IK wrappers) with these calls only; the result is committed as
`samples/third_person/assets/locomotion.animgraph.ron` and equals the sample's code-built graph.

## Preview and PIE debugging

`editor.anim_rig { source: "demo" | "selected" | "gltf", path? }` picks the preview character:
a built-in biped (clips `Idle Survey Walk Run Wave Jump`, the sample's names), the selected
entity's `SkinnedMesh` + `Animator` clips, or a `.glb` (its `.animedit.ron` opens with it).

`editor.anim_preview { params: { "Speed": 3.0, "Jump": true }, advance: 0.5, speed?: 1.0 }` sets preview
parameters, advances at 60 Hz and returns `{ state, error, nodes: [{ path, node, active, weight,
state }], parameters, speed }` — the evaluator is the game's, with the rig's edits applied. `speed` (0 to 2)
is the panel's preview speed slider: it scales every preview step, an agent's `advance` included, so at 0 the
preview does not move (ADR-7747).

While PIE runs, the Anim Graph panel mirrors the play world's animator running the open graph
(or the first graph animator): `editor.anim_debug` returns the same snapshot for it, plus
`entity` and `name`; `null` when nothing runs. Node `state.kind` is `clip` (time, finished),
`blend_space` (input, per-clip weights), `state_machine` (current, transition `[from, to,
progress]`), `blend` (alpha), `layers` (weights) or `wrapper`.

## Clips and skeletons

`editor.anim_clip { clip, op, … }` edits one clip of the preview rig: `add_notify { time, name,
payload? }`, `set_notify { index, … }`, `remove_notify { index }`, `root_motion { mode }`,
`set_curve { name, keys: [[time, value, "linear"|"constant"|"cubic", slope?], …], property? }`,
`remove_curve { name, property? }`. `property: true` targets a property track (`name` is the
reflected path, e.g. `Transform.translation.y`). The first edit of a clip copies its imported
notifies into the sidecar, so they are kept.

`editor.anim_skeleton { op, name, … }`: `add_socket { joint, offset: [x, y, z], rotation?: [yaw, pitch, roll] }`
(`rotation` in degrees, Euler YXZ, the panel's Rotation° fields; absent = no rotation; ADR-7747),
`remove_socket`, `add_ik_chain { joints: [root, mid, tip], pole_param? }` (must be a
parent → child chain), `remove_ik_chain`. Graph IK nodes pick authored chains in the inspector.
`editor.anim_save_edits { path? }` writes the sidecar.

## The standalone timeline and pose sampling

Two reusable pieces that do not need the Clip panel or an `AnimEditor` document:

- **`regia_editor::anim::timeline::Timeline`** is an egui widget (`timeline.show(ui)`) with
  tracks of keys, a playhead, a loop range, a Loop toggle and a marker lane (foot contacts,
  notifies). It owns its data and returns `TimelineEvent`s (`Scrub`, `KeyMoved`, `KeyAdded`,
  `KeyRemoved`, `MarkerMoved`, `MarkerAdded`, `MarkerRemoved`, `RangeChanged`, `LoopChanged`,
  `Selected`); drags emit `finished: true` once on release, which is the one undo step.
  Click or drag the ruler to scrub, shift-drag it to draw the range (drag its ends, secondary
  click clears it), drag keys and markers, double click a track or the marker lane to add one,
  secondary click or Delete removes, Ctrl + wheel zooms. `Timeline::from_clip` fills it from a
  clip.
- **`regia_animation::sample_into(world, skeleton_root, &clip, time, SampleMode)`** writes the
  clip's joint TRS at `time` into the joint entities of any world, with the animation path's own
  sampling and additive math. Only joints the clip animates are written, so a clip over the first
  67 of 109 joints leaves the other 42 alone. Time clamps to the clip; wrap it first to loop.

The agent drives the widget headless, with the same logic the egui frame uses:

`editor.timeline_set { clip?, duration?, playhead?, range?, loop?, snap?, tracks?, markers?,
width?, zoom? }` fills it (`clip` loads one track per animated joint and a marker per notify;
`Foot…` notifies are foot contacts). `editor.timeline_state` reads it and drains the edit events
since the last call. `editor.timeline_input { op: "press"|"drag"|"release"|"delete", time, row:
"toolbar"|"ruler"|"markers"|<track index>, button?, shift?, double? }` is synthetic pointer input
and returns the events it caused:

```json
{"method": "editor.timeline_set", "params": {"clip": "Walk", "snap": 0.0333}}
{"method": "editor.timeline_input", "params": {"op": "press", "row": "ruler", "time": 0.5}}
{"method": "editor.timeline_input", "params": {"op": "press", "row": 0, "time": 0.4}}
{"method": "editor.timeline_input", "params": {"op": "release", "row": 0, "time": 0.6}}
{"method": "editor.timeline_state", "params": {}}
```

`editor.sample_into { clip, time, mode?: "replace"|"additive", joints? }` samples a preview-rig
clip into a scratch copy of the rig and returns `{ written, untouched, joints: [{ name,
translation, rotation, scale }] }` for the animated joints (or the named ones).

## Seeing the panels

`editor.capture_panel { panel: "anim_graph" | "anim_clip" | "anim_skeleton", width?, height? }`
(default 1024 x 640, clamped to 64..=4096) renders a panel offscreen and returns `{ width, height,
mime: "image/png", png_base64 }`. The panel shows
whatever the editor state selects (canvas, selected node/state/transition, clip, curve, joint).

## Live parameters, the recorder and the clip preview

These are view and debug tools: none of them edits a saved document or adds an undo entry.

**Live parameters.** While play-in-editor runs and the Anim Graph panel watches an animator, the
Parameters section shows a **Live** badge and its fields write to that animator (a debug write: not
saved, forgotten when play stops). The agent writes the same way:

```json
{"method": "editor.anim_param", "params": {"name": "Speed", "live_value": 2.5}}
```

returns `{ parameters, live: { name, value, queued } }`; the write reaches the animator at the
panel's next frame. `live_value` takes a number, a bool, `[x, y]` / `[x, y, z]`, or anything for a
trigger, converted to the declared kind.

**The recorder.** The Recorder section above the parameters records the watched animator while
play runs: per play frame its current state, transition, parameter values, node blend weights and
evaluated pose (with a 64-bit pose hash). The ring keeps `capacity` frames (default 600, at most
36 000) and never more than 64 MiB; the oldest frames go first and are counted. A paused session
records nothing. After pause or stop, the frame slider (arrow keys step one frame) replays a
frame: the graph canvases highlight its states and nodes, `editor.anim_debug` returns it, and the
graph preview takes its pose. **Live** follows the session again.

- `editor.anim_record { op: "start", capacity? }`, `{ op: "stop" }`, `{ op: "state" }` return
  `{ recording, frames, capacity, bytes, dropped, scrub, first, last }`.
- `editor.anim_scrub { frame }` (0 = the oldest kept frame) returns `{ frame, index, play_frame,
  entity, name, state, transition: { from, to, progress }, parameters, weights: [{ path, weight }],
  pose_hash }`; `frame: null` goes back to live.

**The clip preview.** The Clip panel's playback row sets the speed (0.1 to 4x), **Once**, **Loop**
or **Ping-pong**, and a preview range (the two range fields, or drag the bright end line on the
timeline; the shaded part is not played; **Whole clip** clears it). The range trims only what the
preview plays, never the clip. **Onion skins** draws ghost poses before (z-axis color) and after
(ok color) the playhead: count, step in seconds and opacity. **Root-motion floor** scrolls a floor
grid under the in-place rig by the clip's extracted root motion and draws the root's path on it.
The clip picker has a search field and sorts by import order, name, length or recent use.

```json
{"method": "editor.anim_clip", "params": {"op": "preview", "clip": "Walk", "speed": 0.5,
  "loop": "ping_pong", "range": [0.2, 0.8], "onion": {"enabled": true, "before": 2, "after": 2,
  "step": 0.1, "opacity": 0.5}, "root_floor": true, "time": 0.2, "advance": 0.5}}
{"method": "editor.anim_clip", "params": {"op": "list", "filter": "run", "sort": "length"}}
```

`preview` returns `{ clip, time, playing, speed, loop, reverse, range, trimmed, onion,
onion_times: [[offset, time], …], root_floor, root: { position, yaw } }` (`root` is the root's
travel from the range start to `time`); `list` returns `{ clips: [{ name, duration }], filter,
sort }`.

**Several curves at once.** The Clip panel's curve list and the Sequence Curves panel's curve list
show every curve in a palette color (theme tokens), each with a show checkbox and a lock checkbox;
**Frame all** fits the view to every visible curve. Hidden curves are not drawn; the other visible
curves are drawn behind the edited one; a locked curve still scrubs but refuses edits. The agent
reads and sets the same state:

```json
{"method": "editor.curve_view", "params": {"panel": "seq_curve", "curve": "track:1:2", "locked": true}}
```

returns `{ panel, curves: [{ key, label, palette_index, visible, locked, edited }] }`. Keys are
`curve:<name>` and `property:<path>` (Clip panel) and `track:<index>:<component>` (Sequence
Curves).

**Keyboard.** Every control above is a focusable widget: Tab reaches it, arrow keys change sliders
and number fields, Space or Enter toggles checkboxes and presses buttons, and the clip picker opens
with Enter and takes typed search text.

**Error codes** (in `error.data.code`):

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `not_playing` | `live_value` without a watched play animator, or while a recording is replayed |
| `unknown_parameter` | `live_value` for a parameter the graph does not declare |
| `nothing_recorded` | `editor.anim_scrub` before anything was recorded |
| `frame_out_of_range` | `editor.anim_scrub` past the last recorded frame |
| `bad_range` | `editor.anim_clip { op: "preview", range }` that is not `0 <= start < end` |
| `unknown_curve` | `editor.curve_view` with a key the panel does not list |

## Chain IK and body aim nodes

`chain_ik` and `body_aim` (`.animgraph.ron` v4, ADR-8475) are node kinds of `editor.anim_add_node` and
`editor.anim_set_node` like the rest; there is no new method. A joint limit in `data` is `"Free"`,
`{ "Cone": { "max_swing", "min_twist", "max_twist" } }` or `{ "Hinge": { "axis": [x, y, z], "min", "max" } }`
(radians, relative to the joint's bind rotation). A solver or limit name the format does not know fails the
call with nothing changed. A `body_aim` joint with an empty name is refused when the graph is saved (validation,
ADR-8732), and the inspector's "Add joint" appends a rig joint, never an empty name. In a `.animgraph.ron` file the
two nodes and a `PerJoint` entry refuse unknown fields (a misspelled field is a load error). Every add, edit and connection is one undo step.

```json
{"method": "editor.anim_add_node", "params": {"kind": "chain_ik", "data": {
  "root": "tail_01", "tip": "tail_06", "solver": "Ccd", "target": {"Param": "TailTarget"},
  "limits": {"Uniform": {"Cone": {"max_swing": 0.6, "min_twist": -0.2, "max_twist": 0.2}}}}}}
{"method": "editor.anim_add_node", "params": {"kind": "body_aim", "data": {
  "joints": [["turret_yaw", 1.0], ["turret_pitch", 1.0]], "aim_joint": "muzzle", "target": {"Param": "Aim"}}}}
```

At run time the nodes log, once per rig and name: `animgraph_chain_invalid` (the root and tip do not form a
parent chain; the node passes the pose through), `animgraph_limit_joint_not_in_chain` (a per-joint limit names
a joint the node does not turn; ignored) and `animgraph_aim_joint_not_under_chain` (the aim joint is neither a
turning joint nor below the last one). An unknown joint name stops the graph's evaluation with the same
"joint not found" error `two_bone_ik` gives. Residuals (the last chain node's tip distance and iterations, the last aim node's angle) are kept per rig in
`EvalReuse::ik_node_residuals` for `anim.ik_report`.

## Stride and orientation warp nodes

`stride_warp` and `orientation_warp` (`.animgraph.ron` v4, ADR-8540) are node kinds of `editor.anim_add_node` and
`editor.anim_set_node`; there is no new method. A `Pose`-mode stride warp without legs or a pelvis, settings out of
range (strength outside `[0, 1]`, `ratio_min` above 1, `ratio_max` below 1) or spine shares that do not sum to 1 fail
graph validation when the graph compiles, with nothing changed. Every add, edit and connection is one undo step.

```json
{"method": "editor.anim_add_node", "params": {"kind": "stride_warp", "data": {
  "ground_speed_param": "GroundSpeed",
  "settings": {"strength": 1.0, "min_speed": 0.1, "ratio_min": 0.8, "ratio_max": 1.4, "response": 12.0, "mode": "Pose"},
  "legs": [["thigh_l", "calf_l", "foot_l"], ["thigh_r", "calf_r", "foot_r"]], "pelvis": "pelvis"}}}
{"method": "editor.anim_add_node", "params": {"kind": "orientation_warp", "data": {
  "heading_param": "MoveHeading", "pelvis": "pelvis", "spine": [["spine_01", 0.5], ["spine_02", 0.5]], "max_delta": 1.0}}}
```

At run time an inner graph without root motion makes the node pass the pose and log `animgraph_warp_no_root_motion`
once per node and parameter; an unknown joint name stops the evaluation with the "joint not found" error
`two_bone_ik` gives. What each node did on the latest frame is in `anim.get_state`'s `warps` (see
[Animation](book/agents/animation.md#locomotion-warp-nodes)) and in the editor preview's debug snapshot.

## Locomotion test bed

`editor.anim_locomotion_preview` walks a gait in the animation preview's locomotion test bed (ADR-8806): the
stepper of `regia_animation::gait` in driven mode, at fixed 1/60 s steps, over a ground preset, with a driven body
that starts at the origin heading −Z and moves at `speed` while turning at `turn_rate`. It answers the run's quality
metrics, puts the run in the panel's test bed (Anim Graph tab, right column, "Locomotion test bed"), and with
`screenshot` renders that panel offscreen (locomotion gizmos on) and writes it as a PNG. The run is not an edit:
nothing goes on the undo stack. Results are deterministic for identical parameters on one machine.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `entity` | number | Entity id whose `GaitRig.params` are walked (hip offsets measured from the bind pose when the rig's `auto_hips` is on and it has a skeleton). Not with `asset`. |
| `asset` | string | Project-relative `.gait.ron`, read through the format's loader. Not with `entity`. Neither: the built-in six-leg tripod (the settings `anim.gait_simulate` uses without `params`). |
| `ground` | string or object | A preset name, or `{kind, ...}` overriding the preset's fields: `flat`; `slope {degrees}` (0 to 60, default 10); `stairs {rise, run}` (rise 0 to 1 m, default 0.15; run 0.05 to 10 m, default 0.3); `rubble {amplitude, cell, seed}` (0 to 2 m, default 0.1; 0.05 to 10 m, default 0.4; seed default 7); `tunnel {depth}` (the floor at 0 and a second layer `depth` meters above it, 0.5 to 50, default 3). Default flat. Slopes and stairs climb along −Z. |
| `speed` | number | Driver ground speed, 0 to 20 m/s (default 1). |
| `turn_rate` | number | Driver turn rate, −6.283 to 6.283 rad/s, positive turns left (default 0). |
| `seconds` | number | Simulated time, above 0 and at most 300 (default 5); `steps` is `seconds × 60` rounded. |
| `screenshot` | string | Project-relative `.png` path to write the test bed panel to (640 × 480). |

The result is `{ source, ground, speed, turn_rate, seconds, steps, dt, legs, metrics, final: { position, yaw },
screenshot }`. `source` is `"default"`, `{entity}` or `{asset}`; `screenshot` is `{path, width, height, bytes}` or
null. `metrics` uses the definitions of [`anim.gait_simulate`](book/agents/locomotion-quality.md), and a straight run on flat,
slope, stairs and rubble gives that method's numbers bit for bit (`slope {degrees}` is its `slope {rise_z:
-tan(degrees)}`, `stairs {rise, run}` its `steps {rise: -rise, run, axis: "z"}`, the driver its `body_path
[[0, 0], [0, -4096]]`):

| Metric | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `max_slide` | Largest XZ move of a foot planted and not swinging before and after one step, meters (`max_planted_slip` there). |
| `max_foot_jump` | Largest 3D move of any foot in one step, meters. |
| `forced_steps` | Feet the reach limit forced to step. |
| `refused` | Footsteps refused (slope too steep, no ground). |
| `replants` | Feet moved to a better foothold. |
| `min_planted` | Fewest planted feet after any step. |
| `stability_margin` | The last step's margin of the body over the support polygon, meters; null when there is no polygon. |
| `min_stability_margin` | The smallest finite margin seen; null when none was finite. |
| `settled` | The walker is idle with every foot at neutral. |

```json
{"method": "editor.anim_locomotion_preview", "params": {"entity": 4294967321,
  "ground": {"kind": "stairs", "rise": 0.12, "run": 0.35}, "speed": 0.8, "turn_rate": 0.2, "seconds": 6,
  "screenshot": "captures/stairs.png"}}
```

| Error code | When |
|---|---|
| `F0002` | `entity` and `asset` together; `seconds` not a number above 0; a parameter of the wrong type. |
| `no_such_entity` | `entity` names no entity. |
| `no_gait_rig` | The entity has no `GaitRig`. |
| `gait_settings`, `gait_pattern` | The rig's settings fail the stepper's checks. |
| `gait_io`, `gait_parse`, `gait_version`, `gait_legs` | The `.gait.ron` cannot be read, is not a gait document, has a newer `format_version`, or its legs do not match its patterns (an asset's settings can also answer `gait_settings` or `gait_pattern`). |
| `F0002` with `reason: path_outside_project` | `asset` or `screenshot` leads outside the project (`data.path_reason` names the rule). |
| `bad_ground` | An unknown `ground.kind`, a field the kind does not have, or a value out of range. |
| `bad_driver` | `speed` or `turn_rate` not a finite number in range. |
| `simulate_too_long` | `seconds` above 300. |
| `gait_input`, `gait_state`, `gait_floor`, `gait_step_too_large` | The stepper stopped the walk mid-run (the message names the step). |
| `editor_headless` | `screenshot` on an editor without a GPU adapter. |
| `capture_failed` | Rendering, encoding or writing the screenshot failed. |

`editor.capture_panel {panel: "anim_locomotion"}` captures the panel as it stands. In the Inspector, a `GaitRig` or
`FootPlacement` shows an authoring section (settings with their ranges, leg chain pickers, pattern presets, the
`.gait.ron` picker). The field, joint and preset edits are ordinary component edits, so `editor.undo` reverts them and
agents make them with `editor.set_property` and inspect them with `scene.get_entity`. The picker's buttons have their
own methods:

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `editor.anim_gait_load { entity, path }` | Load a project `.gait.ron` into one entity's `GaitRig` (params, legs and body) as one undoable component edit. Returns `{ entity, path, loaded, legs, body, auto_hips }`. |
| `editor.anim_gait_save { entity, path }` | Write one entity's `GaitRig` to a project `.gait.ron` file with the format writer's own validation and atomic write. Returns `{ entity, path, written, legs, body, auto_hips }`. |

Both methods refuse a dead `entity` as `no_such_entity`, an entity without a `GaitRig` as `no_gait_rig`, a path outside
the project with `path_outside_project`, and a bad gait file or settings with the same `gait_*` codes
`anim.gait_validate` / `anim.gait_simulate` use.

# 2D

Methods for the 2D toolkit (`specs/22` § T2.10, `specs/86`). They need `regia_2d::Sprite2dPlugin`
in the app; use `seeing.screenshot` for the picture itself. The first five read; the `tilemap.*`
writes below change the loaded map (see [Tile writes and auto-tiling](#tile-writes-and-auto-tiling)).

| Method | Params | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `sprite.list` | `limit?` (500) | `{ total, sprites: [...] }` in entity order |
| `sprite.get` | `entity` | one sprite |
| `tilemap.list` | — | `{ tilemaps: [{ entity, map, loaded, visible, position, detail }] }` |
| `tilemap.get_tile` | `entity?`, `x` + `y` **or** `world: [x, y]`, `layer?` | hit: `{ cell, layer, tile, map_rect, orientation, outline }`; empty in-range cell: `{ cell, tile: null }`; world outside the map: `{ tile: null, reason }` |
| `view2d.get` | — | `{ camera, pixel_perfect, snap, clear, last_frame }` |
| `tilemap.set_tile` | `entity?`, `layer`, `x`, `y`, `gid` (0 = erase), `flip? { x, y, diagonal }` | `{ cell, layer, before, after }` |
| `tilemap.autotile_register` | `name`, `ron` (`.autotile.ron` text) **or** `path` (a cooked `.autotile.ron`) | `{ name, terrains, replaced, path? }` |
| `tilemap.autotile_list` | — | `{ rule_sets: [{ name, tileset, seed, border, terrains }] }` |
| `tilemap.paint` | `entity?`, `layer`, `rules`, `terrain` **or** `erase: true`, `cells: [[x, y], …]` **or** `rect: [x0, y0, x1, y1]` | `{ count, truncated, changed: [{ cell, before, after }] }` |
| `tilemap.autotile` | `entity?`, `layer`, `rules` | `{ changed }` |
| `tilemap.stamp_copy` | `entity?`, `layer`, `rect: [x0, y0, x1, y1]` | `{ width, height, cells }` |
| `tilemap.stamp_paste` | `entity?`, `layer`, `x`, `y`, `stamp`, `op?` **or** `ops?`, `skip_empty?` | `{ stamp, count, truncated, changed: [{ cell, before, after }] }` |

A sprite entry: `entity`, `atlas` (path), `loaded`, `source` (`{name}` or `{rect}`), `region`
(`page`, `rect`, `source_size`, `pivot`, `nine_slice`; the last three are `null` for a rect source), `position` `[x, y, z]` (z = draw order),
`size`, `color`, `flip` `[x, y]`, `visible`, and `animation` (`animation`, `index`, `frame`,
`playing`, `finished`, `animations`) when it has an `AnimatedSprite`.

`tilemap.list` `detail`: `size` (tiles), `tile_size`, `orientation` (`orthogonal`, `isometric`,
`staggered` or `hexagonal`), `tilesets`, and `layers` — tile layers with
their non-empty `tiles` count, object layers with every object's `id`, `name`, `class`, `position`
and `size` (Tiled coordinates). Spawn points and triggers authored in Tiled show up here.

`tilemap.get_tile` addresses a cell with `x`, `y` (row 0 = **top**, as in Tiled) or a world point
(`world: [x, y]`, through the map entity's transform; its origin is the map's bottom-left). Without
`layer` it returns the topmost tile layer that has a tile there.

A cell that holds a tile returns `cell`, `layer` (`index`, `name`), `tile`, `map_rect`,
`orientation` and `outline`. `tile` is `gid`, `tileset`, `local_id`, `flip { x, y, diagonal }`,
`collision` (`empty` / `solid` / `one_way`), `class` (`""` when the tile has no data), `animated`
and `properties` (`{}` when none). `map_rect` is the bounding box of that cell and `outline` its
shape (4 points, 6 for a hexagon) in map pixels, +Y up; `orientation` names the map's layout.

An in-range cell with no tile returns `{ cell, tile: null }` and omits `layer`, `map_rect`,
`outline` and `orientation`. An `x`/`y` past the map takes that same result (it is not an error).
A world point outside the map returns `{ tile: null, reason: "outside the map" }` and omits `cell`.

On isometric, staggered and hexagonal maps `world` picks the cell whose diamond or hexagon holds
the point ([map orientations](docs/formats/tilemap-ron.md)).

`map_rect` retains double precision, including on wide maps. Use integer `x`, `y` cell addresses
for such queries: `world` input and `outline` coordinates still use single precision. Rendering
also uses single-precision GPU instances; translate/rebase far map cells near the world origin
to preserve pixel detail.

`view2d.get` `last_frame` counts the sprites and tiles drawn last frame, the sorted instances and the
texture batches (draw calls).

## Tile writes and auto-tiling

The writes change the map loaded in the running app (copy-on-write; the sprite pass draws the new
tiles the next frame). They are runtime edits: a hot reload of the map's source file replaces them.
To edit the source itself, use the editor's 2D mode ([Editor 2D mode](book/agents/editor-2d.md)). The editor also
creates new maps, edits their tileset binding and layer order, and edits `.autotile.ron` rule sets
with a preview painted by the same auto-tiler ([Auto-tile rule editor](book/agents/editor-2d.md#auto-tile-rule-editor)).

- `tilemap.set_tile` writes one tile. `gid` is the bare id (`first_gid + local id`, 0 = empty);
  flips go in `flip`. `gid` 0 ignores `flip` and stores 0. `before` and `after` are raw GIDs with Tiled's flag bits.
- `tilemap.autotile_register` parses `.autotile.ron` text (`docs/formats/autotile-ron.md`, at most
  1 MiB; a longer `ron` is refused with `F0002` before the method runs) and registers it under
  `name`. Games register rule sets in code with `regia_2d::AutoTiles::insert`.
- `tilemap.autotile_list` lists the rule sets: `tileset`, `seed`, `border` (`same` / `empty`) and each
  terrain's `name`, `layout` (`edge16` / `blob47` / `rules`), `rules` (count), `members` (local tile
  ids that count as the terrain) and `variants` (entries).
- `tilemap.paint` paints a terrain, or erases, over `cells` or an inclusive `rect` (at most 65 536
  cells). The painted cells and their 8 neighbours re-resolve, so edges and corners appear by
  themselves. Every cell is checked before anything is written. `changed` lists at most 1 000 cells
  sorted by row then column; `count` is the total and `truncated` says whether the list was cut.
  The result does not depend on the order of cells or calls.
- `tilemap.autotile` re-resolves every terrain cell of a layer: after `tilemap.set_tile` placed member
  tiles by hand, or on an imported map.
- `tilemap.autotile_register` also takes `path`: a `.autotile.ron` cooked with the project's other
  2D assets (`regia cook`, stored in the pak) is loaded instead of parsing text, and equals the raw
  file's rule set. `layout` is also `wang_corner` (16 tiles indexed by which cell corners lie inside
  the terrain). Rules work on the cell grid, so on staggered and hexagonal maps the 8 neighbours are
  the grid neighbours, not the geometric ones.
- `tilemap.stamp_copy` returns a rectangle of a layer as a stamp (`width`, `height`, `cells`: raw gids
  with flip bits, row 0 on top). `tilemap.stamp_paste` puts it back with its top-left cell at `x`, `y`
  (negative is fine; the part off the map is clipped), after the optional `op` / `ops`
  (`rotate_cw`, `rotate_ccw`, `rotate_180`, `flip_x`, `flip_y`, at most 16): the tiles' flip bits turn
  with the stamp, so a rotated stamp looks like the rotated picture. Empty stamp cells leave the map
  alone unless `skip_empty: false`. Every check happens before the first write.
  The transformed stamp's last cell must fit signed 64-bit coordinates; an overflowing extent
  answers `tile_bad_params` and leaves the map and its revision alone.

Error codes (`data.code`; `errors.explain` gives the long form). The JSON-RPC error code is
`-32602` (invalid params) for every one of them except `tile_unknown_rules`, which is `-32001`
(not found):

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `tile_bad_params` | A parameter is missing or has the wrong shape (`terrain` and `erase` together, `cells` and `rect` together, a cell that is not `[x, y]`). |
| `tile_bad_gid` | `gid` carries flag bits, or no tileset holds it. |
| `tile_not_tile_layer` | The layer does not exist or is an object layer. |
| `tile_outside_map` | A cell is outside the map; nothing was written. |
| `tile_too_many_cells` | More than 65 536 cells in one `tilemap.paint` or one `tilemap.stamp_paste`. |
| `tile_unknown_rules` | No rule set has that name. |
| `tile_unknown_terrain` | The rule set has no terrain of that name. |
| `tile_bind_failed` | The rule set's `tileset` is not in this map, a tile id is past its `tile_count`, or the layer's data is not `width × height` cells long (nothing was written). |
| `tile_bad_rules` | The `.autotile.ron` text does not parse or validate, or is a newer version, or the cooked `path` is not in the manifest. |
| `tile_bad_stamp` | The stamp is empty, over its size limit (`1 << 20` cells, including a `tilemap.stamp_copy` rectangle), has the wrong cell count, or the rectangle is empty. |

`F0003` means no tilemap entity exists or its map is not loaded.

## Recipes

- **Did the player land on the platform?** `sprite.get` the player, then `tilemap.get_tile` with
  `world: [x, y - 1]` under its feet: `collision` should be `solid` or `one_way`.
- **Is the animation playing?** `sprite.get` → `animation.frame` changes between two calls with
  `play.step` frames in between; `finished` turns true for play-once animations.
- **Build a wall and check its corners.** `tilemap.paint` a `rect` with the wall terrain, then
  `tilemap.get_tile` at its ends: the `local_id`s are the end-cap tiles, the middle cells the
  straight piece. `tilemap.paint` with `erase: true` on one cell splits it into two walls.
- **Is the map loaded and visible?** `tilemap.list` → `loaded: true` and `visible: true`. Then
  `view2d.get` → `last_frame.tiles > 0` tells you whether any of its quads fall inside the camera
  (a visible map that sits off camera reports `0`).

## Example calls

Example calls (`regia agent call <method> '<params json>'`; entity ids come from `scene.query_entities`):

```text
sprite.list {"limit": 20}
sprite.get {"entity": 4294967310}
tilemap.list {}
tilemap.get_tile {"x": 3, "y": 2}               # row 0 is the top row
tilemap.get_tile {"world": [48.0, 32.0]}
view2d.get {}
tilemap.set_tile {"layer": "ground", "x": 3, "y": 2, "gid": 5, "flip": {"x": true}}
tilemap.autotile_list {}
tilemap.paint {"layer": "ground", "rules": "walls", "terrain": "wall", "rect": [0, 4, 9, 4]}
tilemap.paint {"layer": "ground", "rules": "walls", "erase": true, "cells": [[4, 4]]}
tilemap.autotile {"layer": "ground", "rules": "walls"}
tilemap.autotile_register {"name": "walls", "path": "assets/maps/walls.autotile.ron"}   # cooked, from the pak
tilemap.stamp_copy {"layer": "ground", "rect": [0, 0, 3, 2]}
tilemap.stamp_paste {"layer": "ground", "x": 10, "y": 4, "op": "rotate_cw",
                     "stamp": {"width": 2, "height": 1, "cells": [5, 6]}}
```
