# Steam

Methods for the shared Steam connection and the Steam Input bridge: all read-only except `steam.set_deck_preset`, which
changes the Deck performance preset (permission `play`). It needs `regia_steam::SteamPlugin` in the app;
the plugin registers it on the `AgentExtension`.

| Method | Params | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `steam.status` | — | `{ plugin, state, running, offline, user_id, app_id, overlay_open, steam_deck }` |
| `steam.input` | — | `{ plugin, enabled, active, controllers, action_set, driven_actions, ui_down }` |
| `steam.input_manifest` | — | `{ plugin, ok, manifest?, error? }` |
| `steam.deck` | — | `{ plugin, detected, cap_fps, power_cap_fps, power_reason, render_scale_factor, controller, glyph_family, keyboard_open, keyboard_failures }` |
| `steam.glyphs` | `family?`, `action?`, `context?` | `{ plugin, family, controller, buttons: [{ button, label, texture_key }], context?, action?, prompts? }` |
| `steam.deck_perf` | — | `{ plugin, detected, preset, presets, panel, frame_cap_fps, render_scale, upscaler, csm_cascade_count, csm_resolution, ssao, contact_shadows, bloom_mip_count, local_shadow_max_lights, max_visible_lights, tdp_hint_watts, game_resolution, gamescope, output, compositor_upscales, output_16_10 }` |
| `steam.set_deck_preset` | `preset` | `{ plugin, preset, previous }` |
| `steam.layout` | `family?`, `context?`, `keyboard_only_ok?` | `{ plugin, ok, family, sheets: [{ context, rows: [{ control, label, texture_key, actions }], keyboard_only }], issues: [{ severity, code, context, action, control, message }], errors, error? }` |

- `plugin` is `false` (and nothing else is present) when the app has no `SteamPlugin`.
- `state` is `Ready`, `Unavailable` (Steam not running, feature off, Android) or `Restarting`.
- `running` is `state == Ready`. `offline` means Steam runs in offline mode (not logged on).
- `user_id` is the 64-bit Steam id as a string, or `null` when not signed in.
- `overlay_open` tells you why gameplay input is suspended: the Steam overlay is up.

On a CI box without Steam, `steam.status` answers `running: false`; tests that need a connected
state inject `MockSteam` (see [Steam](book/user-guide/steam.md)).

## Steam Input

- `steam.input`: `enabled` is `SteamInputSettings::enabled`. `active` is true once Steam Input
  initialized with Steam ready. `controllers` is what Steam Input reports. `action_set` is the
  upper-case set chosen from the player's top-priority context, `driven_actions` the Regia Engine
  actions currently held from Steam, `ui_down` the UI actions (`ui_up`, `ui_accept`, ...) down.
  With the bridge off the result is `enabled: false, active: false`.
- `steam.input_manifest`: the generated in-game actions file for the live `InputConfig`.
  `ok: false` with an `error` text when the config cannot be expressed (a 3D action, or two actions
  mapping to one Steam name); a missing `InputConfig` is also reported there. Neither is a protocol
  error.
- Check a Deck run: `steam.input` should show `controllers >= 1` and the expected `action_set`;
  press A and read `ui_down`.

## Deck readiness (`steam.deck`)

`steam.deck` is read-only and reports what the Deck-specific systems decided (ADR-368):

- `detected` is the Deck flag. Off a Deck every system below is idle and the fields keep their defaults.
- `cap_fps` is the player's chosen cap; `power_cap_fps` is the ceiling the thermal governor allows (60 means no
  limit). The frame loop paces at the lower of the two.
- `power_reason` is `none`, `low_battery` or `thermal`. `render_scale_factor` is a multiplier the host applies to
  the render scale (1.0 means unchanged).
- `controller` is the controller kind the UI last saw (`Unknown`, `SteamDeck`, `SteamController`, `Xbox`,
  `PlayStation`, `Switch`, `Generic`). `glyph_family` is the glyph directory to draw: `xbox`, `playstation`,
  `switch` or `deck`.
- `keyboard_open` tells you whether the floating keyboard is up; `keyboard_failures` counts refused show requests.

`plugin` is `false` (and nothing else is present) when the app has no `SteamPlugin`. There are no error codes.

## Prompts, presets and FSR 1 (ADR-526)

- `steam.glyphs` lists the label and texture key of all 17 standard buttons for a glyph family
  (`xbox`, `playstation`, `switch`, `deck`; default: the family the UI shows now). With `action`
  it also returns `prompts`: one entry per distinct gamepad control bound to the action in
  `context` (default: the player's top enabled context, else `Gameplay`), in binding order.
  Keyboard and mouse bindings have no prompt; an unknown action or context gives `prompts: []`.
  A stick axis shares the stick's glyph (`glyphs/<family>/left_stick`), a trigger axis the trigger's.
  An unknown `family` is a protocol error (`F0002`, invalid params). A present `family`,
  `action` or `context` that is not a string is the same error. Omit the field, or pass JSON
  null, to take the default.
- `steam.deck_perf` reports the performance preset in force and its effective budget: the preset's
  knobs after the thermal and battery governor, fitted to the output size. `tdp_hint_watts` is the
  SteamOS power limit the preset is meant to hold its cap under (`null` = the default limit). It is
  a hint and is never applied. `gamescope` is true under gamescope. `output` is the game's window
  size (`null` until the first resize). `compositor_upscales` is true when gamescope scales a
  smaller output up to the panel (the FSR 1 profile). Off a Deck, `detected` is false and the
  knobs stay at Balanced.
- `steam.set_deck_preset` switches the preset (`battery`, `balanced`, `performance`, `fsr1`;
  permission `play`). On a Deck the new budget applies on the next frame; off a Deck only the stored `preset` changes and the knobs stay at Balanced. The preset's frame cap is written
  into the player's cap; the player can still pick another cap afterwards. An unknown or missing
  `preset` is `F0002`.

Check a Deck run:

1. Call `steam.set_deck_preset {"preset":"battery"}`, step a frame, then read `steam.deck_perf`:
   `frame_cap_fps` is 30 and `render_scale` is 0.6.
2. For the FSR 1 profile, start the game at 960×600 with gamescope's FSR filter on, then read
   `steam.deck_perf`: `compositor_upscales` is true, `output_16_10` is true, and with `fsr1` the
   `render_scale` is 1.
3. Plug in a DualSense, then call `steam.glyphs {"action":"Jump"}`: `family` is `playstation`.
   On the Deck's own controls it is `deck`.

There are no new error codes.

<!-- depth-2:method-reference -->

These calls were sent to a headless editor, which does not register the steam methods, so each answer is unknown method (`F0008`). A process that registers them and has no Steam resource answers success with `plugin` false instead.


## Call reference

Parameters, results and error codes for every method on this page. Types and defaults come from the schema and handlers; limits include the contract. Error codes are in `data.code`; names explicitly labeled `data.reason` are additional handler reasons. Every method can also return `F0001`, `F0002`, `F0004`, `F0007` and `F0012`. The server can return `F0005`, `F0006`, `request_too_large`, or `F0008` when the method is not registered; see [protocol](book/agents/protocol.md).

Unless a lower or explicit method limit is listed, the dispatcher accepts at most 65,536 items in a top-level array parameter and 1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes in a string parameter. A limit violation returns `F0002`.

The request in each fence is the call that was sent with `regia agent call`.
The line under it is the host's answer.
A second fence tagged `json,ignore` is an error answer. Large fields are elided with `...`. A fence tagged `json,ignore` is a real call on a host or plugin method that the runtime schema does not list.


### `steam.deck`

Deck readiness: detection, frame cap, power policy, controller glyph family, keyboard state.

*Read, does not mutate.*

No parameters.

Result: `{ plugin, detected, cap_fps, power_cap_fps, power_reason, render_scale_factor, controller, glyph_family, keyboard_open, keyboard_failures }`.

No error codes beyond the universal set.

With the extension handler registered but its Steam resource absent, the call succeeds with `plugin` false. A host that never registered the extension returns `F0008`, as in this capture.

```json,ignore
steam.deck {}
→ { "message": "unknown method steam.deck", "code": -32601, "data": { "code": "F0008", "hint": ... } }
```

The host returned this error. `code` is the JSON-RPC code and `data` is the protocol object.
Elided: `data.hint` (string 19099 chars).

### `steam.glyphs`

Controller prompt glyphs: every button's label and texture key for a family, and the prompts of an action.

*Read, does not mutate.*

| Param | Type | Required | Default and limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `family` | string | no | xbox, playstation, switch or deck; default the family the UI shows now |
| `action` | string | no | an input action; its gamepad bindings become `prompts` |
| `context` | string | no | the input context of `action`; default the player's top enabled context, else Gameplay |

Omitting action returns the button list without action prompts; context only applies when action is supplied.

Result: `{ plugin, family, controller, buttons: [{ button, label, texture_key }], context?, action?, prompts? }`.

No error codes beyond the universal set.

With the extension handler registered but its Steam resource absent, the call succeeds with `plugin` false. A host that never registered the extension returns `F0008`, as in this capture.

```json,ignore
steam.glyphs {}
→ { "message": "unknown method steam.glyphs", "code": -32601, "data": { "code": "F0008", "hint": ... } }
```

The host returned this error. `code` is the JSON-RPC code and `data` is the protocol object.
Elided: `data.hint` (string 19099 chars).

### `steam.input`

The Steam Input bridge: enabled, active, controllers, chosen action set, held actions, UI actions down.

*Read, does not mutate.*

No parameters.

No error codes beyond the universal set.

With the extension handler registered but its Steam resource absent, the call succeeds with `plugin` false. A host that never registered the extension returns `F0008`, as in this capture.

```json,ignore
steam.input {}
→ { "message": "unknown method steam.input", "code": -32601, "data": { "code": "F0008", "hint": ... } }
```

The host returned this error. `code` is the JSON-RPC code and `data` is the protocol object.
Elided: `data.hint` (string 19099 chars).

### `steam.input_manifest`

The Steam Input in-game actions file generated from the live InputConfig.

*Read, does not mutate.*

No parameters.

Result: `{ plugin, ok, manifest?, error? }`.

No error codes beyond the universal set.

With the extension handler registered but its Steam resource absent, the call succeeds with `plugin` false. A host that never registered the extension returns `F0008`, as in this capture.

## Workflow: see whether Steam input and the Deck preset are live

1. `steam.status`. `F0008` means this host did not register the Steam extension. If its handler is registered but the Steam resource is absent, it succeeds with plugin false. A present resource with running false means Steam is unavailable; offline mode is reported separately by offline.
2. When `plugin` is true, `steam.input` for the actions the manifest bound, and `steam.glyphs` with `family` and an `action` for the prompt labels.
3. `steam.deck` says whether the process is on a Deck. `steam.deck_perf` is the preset in force.
4. `steam.set_deck_preset` with `battery`, `balanced`, `performance` or `fsr1`. Off a Deck only the stored preset changes. An unknown name is `F0002`.
5. `steam.input_manifest` checks the manifest file the game ships. `ok` false carries the manifest error in the success object.

<!-- /depth-2:method-reference -->

## Controller layout (`steam.layout`, ADR-1332)

`steam.layout` is read-only. It shows what a "Controls" screen shows, and checks that the game can be played on a
controller alone (the controller part of Valve's Deck Verified review).

- `family` is the glyph family the labels are for (`xbox`, `playstation`, `switch`, `deck`; default: the family the UI
  shows now, which is `deck` on a Deck before any other pad reports in).
- `sheets` has one entry per input context, highest priority first, or only `context` when you pass it. Each `rows`
  entry is one bound control, in the layout order (face buttons, shoulders, triggers, each stick before its click, the
  D-pad, Start, Select, the system button). `control` is the family-neutral id (`south`, `left_trigger`, `left_stick`,
  `left_stick_click`, `dpad_up`, `dpad`, `start`, `mode`, ...). `actions` are the actions on it, in binding order.
  `keyboard_only` lists the actions this context binds to keys or the mouse but to no usable gamepad control.
- `issues` are sorted errors first. `errors` counts them. The issue codes:

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `no_gamepad_binding` | error | The action has key or mouse bindings in the context and no gamepad binding: a Deck player cannot do it. Pass the action in `keyboard_only_ok` when that is deliberate (a debug console key). |
| `reserved_control` | warning | The action is on the system button (Steam on the Deck, Guide, PS, Home). The system menu takes that button, so it does not count as the action's gamepad binding. |
| `control_conflict` | warning | Two or more actions share one control with plain triggers (no hold, tap, pulse or chord). One press fires all of them. |
| `missing_glyphs` | warning | Only from `regia steam layout --glyphs <dir>`: a family's glyph textures are incomplete. |

- A missing `InputConfig` is `ok: false` with an `error` text, not a protocol error. An unknown `family` or `context`,
  or a `keyboard_only_ok` that is not a list of strings, is `F0002` (invalid params). There are no new error codes.
- The same report from the command line: `regia steam layout [--family deck] [--context NAME] [--glyphs assets]
  [--allow-keyboard-only ACTION]... [--check]`. `--check` makes an error fail the command, for CI.

Check a build:

1. Call `steam.layout {"family":"deck"}`. `errors` must be 0 before the game goes to the Deck review.
2. Read the `Gameplay` sheet: every action you expect on the pad has a row, and `keyboard_only` is empty or holds only
   your debug keys.
3. Connect a DualSense and call `steam.layout` without `family`: the labels change to Cross, Circle, L1, ...

## The net_game client's Steam line (overlay check)

The `net_game` sample's windowed client built with `--features steamworks` (or `--features steam` on the mock
backend) runs `SteamPlugin` and shows a HUD text node named `steam_overlay` (ADR-7317,
`book/user-guide/steam-real-run.md` § 3). No new method: read the state with `steam.status` and the line with
`ui.query`.

1. `steam.status {}`: `overlay_open` is true while the Steam overlay is up; `running` false means no Steam client.
2. `ui.query {"name": "steam_overlay"}`: the one node's `text` holds `Steam (<backend>): running, app <id>`,
   `overlay OPEN` or `overlay closed (Shift+Tab opens it)`, `last: OverlayOpened (opened N, closed M)` (or
   `OverlayClosed`, or `no overlay message yet`), and `gpu: <adapter> (<backend>)` once the window has a device.

The mock test `cargo test -p net_game --features steam --test steam_overlay` injects `OverlayActivated` and checks
both reads.

## The overlay trace and the cursor hold (ADR-7349)

No new method. Two engine behaviors for the overlay check:

- **Cursor hold.** While the overlay is open, `SteamPlugin` sets `regia_platform::CursorRelease`: the window layer
  shows a free cursor and passes no game grab to the OS until `OverlayClosed` (or a shutdown), then applies the
  game's current `Window::cursor_grab` / `cursor_visible` once. `SteamSettings::release_cursor_on_overlay = false`
  turns it off. `regia_platform::CursorCalls` counts the `set_cursor_grab` / `set_cursor_visible` calls the window
  layer made.
- **Trace.** `REGIA_STEAM_OVERLAY_TRACE=<file>` writes a line per `GameOverlayActivated` callback (repeats included),
  `OverlayOpened`/`OverlayClosed`, window focus change, Shift/Tab key event, cursor wish/hold/OS call, and a
  heartbeat once a second; the header names the overlay injection facts (`overlay_renderer_preloaded`,
  `vk_overlay_layer`). Format and how to read it: `book/user-guide/steam-real-run.md` § 3.

The `net_game` client's line now starts with `STEAM OVERLAY: OPEN (opened N, closed M)` or
`STEAM OVERLAY: closed (...)`; read it with `ui.query {"name": "steam_overlay"}` as before.

Tests: `cargo test -p regia_steam --test plugin the_overlay` (hold through re-grabs and focus churn, opt-out, trace
contents), `cargo test -p regia_platform --features window --lib a_cursor_hold` (no grab call while held),
`cargo test -p net_game --features steam --test steam_overlay` (headline row, Shift+Tab never shows the scoreboard).

<!-- source: book/agents/schedule-shuffle.md -->
# Schedule shuffle and ambiguity checks

Systems that have no `.before`, `.after` or `.chain()` path between them run in an order nobody chose. Two checks find
code that depends on that order. Both are developer tools (a command and a test helper), not runtime features, so there
is no agent-protocol method: an agent runs the command and reads the report.

## Run it

```sh
cargo xtask shuffle-check                 # the smoke scene under 8 seeded orders
cargo xtask shuffle-check --seeds 32 --frames 180
cargo xtask shuffle-check --ambiguities   # only the ambiguity report
cargo xtask shuffle-check --ambiguities --report target/ambiguities.md
```

On the workstation run it through the build wrapper (`localbuild.sh <lane> -- cargo xtask shuffle-check`). It runs
`cargo test -p regia_test_utils --test shuffle_check`, so it needs only lavapipe-free CPU: no GPU is touched.

Reading the output:

- `repeat of the reference seed: identical` — the scene gives the same state twice in a row. If it says `DIFFERS`, the
  scene or a plugin is nondeterministic by itself (a wall clock, a thread race), and the seed comparison means nothing.
- `N of M other seeds diverge` with `seed S hash H: <entity>/<Component>, ...` — the components, by entity `Name`, whose
  value differs from the reference seed. The systems that write those components are the pair that needs an edge.
- The ambiguity table lists each schedule's system count and unordered conflicting pairs, then the top pairs by score:
  a pair that both write the same component or resource scores 3 per shared item, read/write 1, a whole-world
  (`&mut World`) system 1.

## In your own tests

```rust,ignore
use regia_app::prelude::*;

let mut app = build_my_app();
let report = app.ambiguity_report();          // builds every schedule, runs nothing
println!("{}", report.to_markdown(20));

let mut app = build_my_app();
app.shuffle_schedules(7);                      // before the first update
for _ in 0..120 { app.update(); }
```

`regia_test_utils::shuffle::shuffle_check(build, frames, seeds)` does the per-seed comparison for any `App`:
`snapshot(world)` is every reflected component of every entity as debug text, keyed by `Name`, with entity references
printed as those names. Name every entity a test spawns; an unnamed entity is keyed by its component types and content.

## What to do with a finding

An ambiguity is a candidate. Two unordered systems that only push to a list, or that touch unrelated fields of one
resource, are fine. Add an explicit edge only for a pair that a shuffle run shows changing the result, and add a test that
fails without it. Seeds run single-threaded; the real executor can order differently still, so a clean run proves the
listed pairs are not the cause, not that no race exists.

`App::shuffle_schedules` needs the `debug_names` feature (on by default; the same feature that keeps system names).

<!-- source: book/agents/baked-gi-bake.md -->
# Baking GI from meshes

`regia bake-gi` bakes a map's indirect light into a `.fgiv` volume with the reference path tracer
(using the volume at runtime: [Baked GI volumes](book/agents/baked-gi.md)). This page covers the bake side: the
`.bake.ron` description with static meshes, interiors and automatic detail bricks, the dry run, the summary
and the error codes. Format reference: `docs/formats/bake-ron.md`. Design: ADR-279 and ADR-280.

## Commands

```text
regia bake-gi <scene> [--out FILE] [--rays N] [--samples N] [--bounces N] [--seed N]
                        [--probes-per-batch N] [--no-filter] [--dry-run] [--check-volume FILE.fgiv]
                        [--rr-start N] [--clamp-direct L] [--clamp-indirect L]
                        [--sample-groups N] [--firefly-threshold K]
```

The last line's quality controls (bounces, clamps, sample groups, firefly suppression, the noise estimate) are
covered in [Bake quality controls](book/agents/baked-gi-bake-quality.md).

- `<scene>` is a built-in (`cornell`, `furnace`, `rolling-hills`) or a description (`.ron`, usually
  `<map>.bake.ron`).
- `--dry-run` validates the description, loads every mesh, checks the manifest and lays out the probes. It
  prints the layout and does not trace. It needs no GPU.
- `--check-volume FILE.fgiv` builds the job as `--dry-run` does and compares it with a baked volume instead of
  baking. It needs no GPU. See [Is the bake stale?](#is-the-bake-stale).
- Without `--dry-run` or `--check-volume`, the command bakes on the first GPU adapter and writes `--out` (default
  `<map>.fgiv`). `--cpu` bakes on the CPU instead (no GPU; for checks and small scenes): [Checking a bake end
  to end](book/agents/baked-gi-bake-check.md).

Both print one JSON object on stdout. Progress goes to stderr.

## Describing a map

A v1 description adds static meshes to the terrain, sun and sky of v0:

```ron
(
    format_version: 1,
    root: Some("<build-dir>"),
    manifest: Some("MANIFEST.sha256"),
    terrain_mesh: Some((source: "terrain/terrain.gltf", spacing: 1.25)),
    static_meshes: Some("static_meshes.json"),
    interiors_file: Some("interiors.json"),
    sun: Some((toward: (0.3, 0.5, 0.2), illuminance: 50000.0)),
    layout: (
        terrain_spacing: Some((8.0, 8.0)),
        auto_bricks: Some((spacing: 1.0, margin: 2.0, layers: ["setpiece"])),
    ),
)
```

- **Meshes** are occluders and bounce surfaces with their base color. Emissive parts become lights. Sources
  are glTF (`.gltf`, `.glb`, every primitive with its node transforms, LOD0) or cooked meshes (`.fckd`).
  Transforms are column-major 4x4 in Regia Engine's frame. A mirrored transform (negative determinant) flips the
  winding, so the faces stay front-facing. `instances` places one source many times (rock hints). The bake
  does not sample textures: a textured part without a `material: Some((albedo: ...))` override bakes with
  `default_albedo` (0.5) times its base color factor. The summary counts these parts as `default_albedo_parts`.
- **`static_meshes`** reads DO27's `static_meshes.json` as it is. It loads `source`, never `mesh`. It skips
  non-static entries, `structure`/`dynamic` layers, and scatter classes whose instances Regia Engine generates
  (`instances: null` with a `placement`). The summary lists them under `plan.skipped`.
- **`terrain_mesh`** turns the terrain grid mesh into the traced heightfield. The terrain layer follows it, and
  uncovered samples (an open borehole) are holes. The same source in `static_meshes` is not placed again.
- **`interiors`** / **`interiors_file`**: a brick inside an interior's box is tagged with it. The tag asks for
  INTERIOR (no sky through the walls) unless the interior is `sky_open`. The flag is written into the brick in
  the `.fgiv`. It needs the brick's whole box inside the interior, so a cluster brick that reaches out of the room
  stays outdoor. An interior with `openings` is INTERIOR as a whole in v0.2.0.
- **`auto_bricks`** places one brick over each interior, then one per cluster of mesh placements. Each
  placement's box grows by `margin`, and overlapping boxes merge. When these bricks (interiors included)
  would hold more than `max_probes`, the cluster bricks coarsen first so the interiors keep their spacing. Only
  when the interiors alone leave fewer than 8 probes per cluster does every spacing coarsen by one factor.
  `plan.auto_bricks.scale`, `plan.auto_bricks.interior_scale` and `plan.auto_bricks.spacing` report the factors
  and the cluster spacing used. With thousands of small placements (rock hints), restrict `layers` to the set pieces.
- **Leak control**: probes inside mesh geometry are moved out by relocation or marked invalid
  (`INSIDE_GEOMETRY`), as for any bake. A sealed room's probes see no sky. Walls between neighboring probes and the
  INTERIOR bricks the bake writes: [Baked GI leak control](book/agents/baked-gi-leak-control.md).

## Output

`--dry-run`:

```text
{
  "ok": true, "dry_run": true, "scene": "bore.bake.ron",
  "layers": {
    "terrain": { "origin": [..], "spacing": [8.0, 8.0], "counts": [160, 160], "levels": [..], "probes": 128000, "validity": null },
    "bricks": [ { "index": 0, "first_probe": 128000, "origin": [..], "spacing": [..], "counts": [..], "probes": 4096,
                  "plan": { "source": { "interior": { "id": "hangar" } }, "interior": "hangar", "interior_flag": true, "sky_open": false },
                  "validity": null } ],
    "probes": 140000, "valid": null, "invalid": null
  },
  "plan": { "format_version": 1, "terrain_from_mesh": true,
            "meshes": { "entries": 21, "sources": 14, "placements": 4030, "triangles": 2600000, "mirrored": 12, "skipped": 6, "default_albedo_parts": 9 },
            "skipped": [["scatter_rocks", "generated_placement"], ..], "interiors": 3,
            "bricks": [..], "auto_bricks": { "requested_spacing": 1.0, "spacing": 1.0, "scale": 1.0, "interior_scale": 1.0, "placements": 12, "clusters": 5, "probes": 9000, "interiors": 3 },
            "manifest_verified": 40, "volume_bytes": 19040000 },
  "settings": { .. }, "seconds": 12.5
}
```

The numbers above are illustrative. A bake prints the same object without `dry_run`, plus `out`, `bytes`,
`device`, `report` (probes, valid, under terrain, inside geometry, relocated, rays, `borderline_back_face`,
`dead_interior_cells`) and `build_seconds`. `dead_interior_cells` counts interior-brick cells whose eight probes
are all invalid: they read black at runtime, so a non-zero value asks for a finer brick or a looser interior box.
`borderline_back_face` counts probes within 1 % of the inside-geometry threshold. Their validity can differ on
another GPU, so compare bakes from one device. In a
bake, every terrain and brick entry has `validity`: `{ valid, invalid, under_terrain, inside_geometry,
relocated }`, and the totals `valid` / `invalid` are filled.

Brick `plan.source` is `"builtin"`, `{ "explicit": { "index" } }`, `{ "interior": { "id" } }` or
`{ "cluster": { "meshes": [ids], "placements" } }`.

## Is the bake stale?

Nothing rebakes a volume when a mesh, an interior or the sun moves. `--check-volume` tells you whether a volume still
matches its description (with the same command-line overrides as the bake):

```text
{
  "ok": false, "check": "bore.fgiv", "scene": "bore.bake.ron", "stale": true,
  "reasons": ["scene", "layout"], "code": "bake_volume_stale",
  "volume": { "probes": 140000, "interior_bricks": 0, "scene_hash": "6a1f..." },
  "description": { "probes": 140000, "interior_bricks": 2, "scene_hash": "93c0..." }
}
```

`reasons` lists what changed since the bake, in this order:

| Reason | What changed |
|---|---|
| `scene` | The traced scene: a mesh, its transform or material, the terrain, the sun or the sky (the scene hash). |
| `layout` | The probe layout: the terrain layer, a brick's box or spacing, a brick's INTERIOR flag, the moment resolution or the distance clamp. A volume baked before v0.1.28 wrote interior flags is stale here. |
| `lights` | The light levels the components were baked for (sun, sky, fill). |
| `settings` | Seed, rays, samples, bounces or the filter. The relocation rounds and thresholds are not recorded in the volume, so a change there is not reported. |
| `emitters` | The scene has emissive surfaces but the volume does not name them: a format v1 or v2 bake. On Desktop High and Ultra its emitters are counted twice (ADR-1386, `baked-gi.md` "Emitters the bake holds"). |

A fresh volume prints `"ok": true, "stale": false, "reasons": [], "code": null` and exits 0. A stale one exits
non-zero. Rebake it with the same command without `--check-volume`. The runtime also reports the sun drift live:
`render.get_gi_mode` `baked.sun_mismatch_deg` (above 3°, the baked bounce light is for another sun).

## Errors

A description error prints `{"ok": false, "code", "path", "message"}` on stdout and exits non-zero. `path` is
the key in the description, or in the file it names (`static_meshes.json: meshes[3].layer`).

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `bake_scene_unknown` | Neither a built-in nor a `.ron` file. |
| `bake_desc_parse` | RON (or JSON) syntax error, wrong shape, or unknown field. |
| `bake_desc_newer` | `format_version` above this engine's. Upgrade the engine. |
| `bake_desc_invalid` | A value serde cannot check: non-positive spacing, inverted box, albedo outside 0..1, `terrain` together with `terrain_mesh`, a bad DO27 header or entry, a degenerate transform, a bake control out of range (`bake.*`, also from a flag: [Bake quality controls](book/agents/baked-gi-bake-quality.md)). |
| `bake_source_missing` | A file the description names cannot be read. |
| `bake_mesh_load` | A mesh source does not load (missing, not glTF or `.fckd`, import error). |
| `bake_manifest_missing_entry` | A file read under `root` is not in the manifest, or a mesh `source` lies outside `root` while a manifest is given. |
| `bake_manifest_mismatch` | A file's SHA-256 differs from the manifest. |
| `bake_layout` | The layout is empty or inconsistent, or `auto_bricks` cannot fit `max_probes` (8 probes per brick at least). |
| `bake_volume_stale` | `--check-volume`: the volume does not match the description (`reasons`). |
| `bake_volume_unreadable` | `--check-volume`: the volume file cannot be read or is not a valid `.fgiv`. |
| `bake_volume_too_large` | The volume would need more than 128 MiB in the renderer's one GPU storage binding (`plan.volume_bytes`). Coarsen `terrain_spacing` or `auto_bricks.spacing`, lower `max_probes`, or lower `moment_resolution`. |

## Upgrading descriptions

v0 descriptions (no `format_version`) still load. `regia upgrade-project` lists them as `bake` v0. With
`--write`, it adds `format_version: 2` and keeps the original as `<file>.bak`. v1 descriptions load too; `--write`
rewrites their version number to 2. v2 adds `sky_hdri` and `emitters` ([Bake light inputs](book/agents/baked-gi-light-inputs.md),
whose page also lists the `bake_hdri_decode` and `bake_hdri_sun` errors) and the bake quality controls
([Bake quality controls](book/agents/baked-gi-bake-quality.md)).

## Resumable bakes

**Since ADR-3095.** `regia bake-gi <scene> --checkpoint` (and `--from-scene <level> --bake --checkpoint`) checkpoints the
relocation's outcome and the main trace's probes beside the volume; run again, it continues and writes the same volume
byte for byte, on the CPU tracer and on the GPU. `level.export_bake` reports a resumable checkpoint of the level's
volume. See [Resumable bakes (checkpoints)](book/agents/bake-checkpoints.md).

<!-- source: book/agents/ui.md -->
# Runtime UI (agents)

An agent can see and drive the game UI (`regia_ui`) the way a person does: find a node, click it, move
focus, type, and wait for a state. Guide topic: `agent.guide {"topic": "ui"}`.

Reads come straight from the world. Writes become input: a click is a pointer move, a button press and a
release fed to the same path a mouse uses, so hover, press, `UiEvent::Click` and every widget reaction run
as they would for a player. Nothing happens in the call itself; the effect shows on the next frame, so
step the game (`play.step`) or use `play.wait_until`.

The `ui.*` methods need the app to have the UI and the agent hooked together. `regia::DefaultPlugins` does
that when the `ui` and `agent` features are on. A host that builds its own app inserts
`regia::agent::UiAgentHost::new(regia::ui::agent_bridge::host_call)`; without it every `ui.*` method
answers `ui_not_installed`.

## Finding nodes

Most methods take the same node filters. Every filter you give must match.

- `node`: the node id (the `id` field of a `ui.query` result).
- `name`: the exact `NodeName`.
- `text`: the exact node text; `text_contains`: part of it, ignoring case. A node's text is its own `Text`
  (localized keys are resolved in the active locale), or, for a button and similar widgets, the text of its
  label children. A label child that only repeats its parent's text is not returned by a `text` filter on its
  own (ask for `type: Text` to find it).
- `class`: a theme class the node carries.
- `type`: `Root`, `Button`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `ProgressBar`, `TextInput`, `Dropdown`, `TabBar`, `Modal`,
  `ListView`, `ScrollView`, `Text`, `Image` or `Node` (case does not matter).
- `state`: one state name or a list that must all hold: `hovered`, `pressed`, `focused`, `disabled`,
  `selected`, `invalid` (case does not matter).

Methods that act on a node (`ui.click`, `ui.focus`, `ui.set_value`) need the filters to match exactly one.

## Methods

- `ui.query { ...filters, limit? }` lists matching nodes (default 100, at most 1000), in node id order. The
  reply is `{ count, truncated, nodes }`. Each node has `id`, `name`, `type`, `classes`, `rect` and `clip_rect`
  (`[x, y, width, height]` in physical pixels from the root's top-left), `center`, `visible` (the rect and clip
  have an area), `text`, `states`, `value`, `interactable`, `focusable`, `focus_visible` (the node draws its focus ring),
  `layout_dir` (`ltr` or `rtl`, see [UI layout edge cases](book/agents/ui-layout.md)) and `parent`. `value` is a bool for a
  Toggle, a number for a Slider or ProgressBar, the displayed text for a TextInput (masked when it is a
  password field), the selected index for a Dropdown, the active index for a TabBar, and whether a Modal is
  open.
- `ui.state` reports `focus` (node id or null), `input_mode` (`pointer` or `navigation`), `focus_ring`
  (whether it shows, the policy, and its node, outer rect, width and colour; see
  [UI focus ring](book/agents/ui-focus-ring.md)), `scale`
  (`window_size`, `scale_factor`, and the scale of each root), `locale` (`selected`, `available`), the `pointer`
  (cursor, hovered and pressed node), the open `tooltip` and the `hints` for the last device (see
  [Tooltips and hints](book/agents/ui-tooltips.md)), the `nodes` count and `pending_frames` (agent input not yet fed to the UI).
- `ui.click { ...filters, button?, count?, modifiers? }` moves the pointer to the node's center and presses and releases
  the button, `count` times (1 to 8, default 1). `button` is `left` (default), `right` or `middle`; only the left
  button activates widgets today. `modifiers` is a list of `shift`, `ctrl`, `alt` and `meta` held through the
  click (real key messages: down with the first press, up one frame after the last release, so each `UiEvent`
  of the click reports them); a bad entry is `ui_bad_param`. A click takes two frames, plus one when
  `modifiers` is given. The reply has `node`, `at` (the pixel), `top_hit`
  (the node a click at that pixel reaches) and `occluded` (true when another node covers the center), and
  `queued_frames`. Clicking does not move focus: use `ui.focus`.
- `ui.focus { ...filters }` gives the node focus as navigation would: the `Focused` marker and
  `FocusChanged` events. It must be focusable and not disabled. Like a Tab press it also switches the input
  mode to `navigation`, so the focus ring shows; a later `ui.click` switches back to `pointer` and hides it.
- `ui.type { node?, name?, label?, class?, type?, text?, keys? }` types into a node. With a target it focuses
  that node first; without one it uses the focused node. `text` is committed as input-method text (it lands
  in a focused TextInput); then each of `keys` is pressed and released: `Enter`, `Backspace`, `Delete`,
  `Tab`, `Left`, `Right`, `Home`, `End`, a single character, or `Shift+Tab`. Here `label` is the target's exact
  text (the `text` field is the text to type).
- `ui.set_value { ...filters, value }` sets a widget's value: a boolean for a Toggle, a number for a Slider
  (clamped and stepped) or ProgressBar, a string for a TextInput, an index for a
  Dropdown or TabBar. A number must fit the widget's `f32` (`ui_value_out_of_range` past ±3.4e38). A TextInput
  string is sanitized like typed text (line breaks become spaces in a single-line field), cut to its `max_chars` on
  grapheme clusters, and a read-only field or a value the field's filter refuses is left unchanged; the field's undo
  history is cleared, as by `TextInput::set_text` from code. A Toggle, Slider, TextInput, Dropdown or TabBar also
  emits its `ValueChanged` event.

- `ui.set_locale { locale }` switches the active locale (one of `ui.state` `locale.available`). Every
  localized text re-resolves and the layout reflows on the next frame. The reply is `locale`, `previous`,
  `changed` (false when it was already active) and `generation` (moves on every switch).
- `ui.resolve { key, args?, locale? }` formats one message without touching a node. `args` is an object of
  strings and numbers; a number (or a string that is a canonical number such as `"3"`) selects plural forms by
  the locale's rules, so `{ $count -> [one] ... *[other] ... }` works in every language. Without `locale` it
  uses the active locale and falls back to the project fallback; with `locale` it uses exactly that locale. The
  reply is `key`, `locale`, `found` and `text` (`⟦key⟧` in dev builds when nothing has the key). Use it to audit
  a translation: `found: false` for a locale means that locale lacks the key.

`ui.click`, `ui.focus`, `ui.type`, `ui.set_value` and `ui.set_locale` change state: they need the `edit_scene` permission and
are refused with `F0012` in a read-only session before anything is queued. `ui.query` and `ui.state` are
always allowed.

## Waiting

`play.wait_until` and `play.expect` take two node atoms next to the usual ones. They combine with `all`,
`any` and `not`.

- `{ "predicate": "ui.node_exists", ...filters, "exists": true }` holds when at least one node matches
  (`exists: false` waits for none).
- `{ "predicate": "ui.node_state", ...filters, "state": "focused", "is": true }` holds when the one matching
  node has the state (`is: false` waits for it to be gone). No match, or more than one, does not hold.

The other `ui.*` atoms are `ui.theme_generation` ([UI themes](book/agents/ui-theme.md)), `ui.tweening`
([UI animation](book/agents/ui-animation.md)) and `ui.theme_fading` ([UI theme switch](book/agents/ui-theme-switch.md)). `play.expect` and
`play.wait_until` are read-only, so any other `ui.` name (such as `ui.click` or `ui.set_value`) is a broken
condition (`ui_bad_predicate`) and never reaches the UI.

```text
ui.focus {"name": "settings"}
play.wait_until {"condition": {"predicate": "ui.node_state", "name": "settings", "state": "focused"}}
```

## Errors

Errors keep the protocol's code in `data.code` and add a stable `data.reason`. A `ui.*` call can answer:

| `reason` | `data.code` | When |
|---|---|---|
| `ui_not_installed` | `F0013` | the app has no `UiAgentHost` (no UI hooked to the agent) |
| `ui_node_required` | `F0002` | a node-acting call named no node |
| `ui_node_not_found` | `F0003` | no node matches the filters |
| `ui_node_ambiguous` | `F0002` | more than one node matches; add `name`, `type` or `class`, or pass `node` |
| `ui_node_disabled` | `F0002` | clicking, focusing or setting the value of a disabled node |
| `ui_node_not_visible` | `F0002` | clicking a node with no visible area (not laid out, hidden or clipped away) |
| `ui_node_blocked_by_layer` | `F0002` | clicking or focusing a node outside the top input layer, or any node while that layer is `game_only` |
| `ui_node_not_focusable` | `F0002` | focusing a node without focus support |
| `ui_node_not_settable` | `F0002` | `ui.set_value` on a node with no value |
| `ui_value_required` | `F0002` | `ui.set_value` without `value` |
| `ui_value_type_mismatch` | `F0002` | the value type does not fit the widget |
| `ui_value_out_of_range` | `F0002` | a Dropdown or TabBar index past the last entry, or a number outside the f32 range |
| `ui_type_empty` | `F0002` | `ui.type` with neither `text` nor `keys` |
| `ui_no_focus` | `F0002` | `ui.type` with no target and nothing focused |
| `ui_locale_required` | `F0002` | `ui.set_locale` without `locale` |
| `ui_locale_unknown` | `F0003` | `ui.set_locale` or `ui.resolve` with a locale that is not available |
| `ui_key_required` | `F0002` | `ui.resolve` without `key` |
| `ui_unknown_state` | `F0002` | a `state` that is not one of the six names |
| `ui_bad_param` | `F0002` | a parameter of the wrong type or range |
| `ui_unknown_method` | `F0003` | a method the UI does not implement |
| `ui_node_off_window` | `F0002` | `ui.click` or `ui.drag_drop` on a node of a camera-texture or world-panel root (use `ui.world_click`) |
| `ui_world_miss` | `F0003` | `ui.world_click`'s ray hits no world panel |
| `ui_not_world_panel` | `F0002` | `ui.world_click` `entity` is not a world-space root |
| `ui_not_a_root` | `F0002` | `ui.set_target` on a node that is not a `UiRoot` |
| `ui_bad_target` | `F0002` | `ui.set_target` without a valid `target` (window, camera or world with `size` 1..=4096 and `ppm` > 0) |
| `ui_not_a_camera` | `F0002` | `ui.set_target` `{camera}` names an entity without a `Camera` |
| `ui_bad_predicate` | (none: a broken condition) | a `play.expect` / `wait_until` atom names a `ui.*` predicate other than `ui.node_exists`, `ui.node_state` or `ui.theme_generation`; the condition reports broken and its detail ends with `(ui_bad_predicate)` |

## Notes

- The UI and the agent meet through `UiAgentHost`, so the UI crate never names an agent type (ADR-291).
  The agent crate does depend on the UI crate, through `regia_framework` and directly for `ui.layers` and the
  typed `ui.*` helpers (ADR-5665 corrects the earlier note here, which cited ADR-202, the render-out HUD record).
- Queued input is fed one frame at a time, oldest first, before the pointer is read. `ui.state`
  `pending_frames` tells you when it has all been delivered.
- A click leaves the pointer parked on the node, so it stays hovered until the next move.
- Accessibility settings (text scale, reduced motion, high contrast) and right-to-left layout have their own page and
  the `ui.accessibility` method: [UI accessibility](book/agents/ui-accessibility.md). `ui.state` itself does not report them.

## Camera-target and world-space UI

A `UiRoot`'s `target` decides where its tree draws (ADR-2406):

- `UiTarget::Window` (the default): the window overlay, as before.
- `UiTarget::Camera(camera)`: for a `RenderTarget::Texture` camera, the tree is laid out at the camera's
  texture size (`TextureViewSettings::size`) and drawn into that texture after the view's own passes (the
  frame's `overlay` slot): an in-world monitor that shows a menu, which a material or a `UiImage` then shows.
  For a window camera it is laid out at the camera's viewport rect and drawn over that rect (split-screen
  HUDs); the window pointer reaches it at the offset.
- `UiTarget::WorldSpace { size, ppm }`: the tree is laid out at `size` UI px (`UiRoot::world_space` sets one
  UI px per texel) into an offscreen texture of that many pixels, which the frame draws as a quad
  `size / ppm` metres large at the root entity's `GlobalTransform`: centred (by default) on the origin,
  spanning local X right and Y up and facing +Z, hidden where scene geometry is nearer. It is composited after
  the post stack (`after_post`), so its colours are the authored ones: no exposure, tonemap or bloom. A
  `WorldPanel` component on the root sets `billboard` (`none`, `full`: faces the eye, `axis_y`: turns about
  world up), `pivot`, `fade` (`[start, end]` metres: opaque before `start`, gone after `end`), `depth_test`,
  `opacity` and `live` (redraw the texture every frame, for a panel that shows a live image).

The frame passes `ui_world_panels` (`after_post`) and `ui_camera_targets` (`overlay`) are registered only
while a world or camera-texture root exists, so a frame without such UI does exactly what it did before;
`render.graph` lists them while they exist. Both faces of a panel draw (the back shows the texture mirrored).

The window pointer never hits texture or world UI (their layout rects are target pixels). Focus and gamepad
navigation are unchanged.

- `ui.targets {}` lists every root with its `target` (`window`, `camera`, `world`), layout `size`, and for
  world panels `ppm`, `size_m`, `position`, `billboard`, `pivot`, `fade`, `depth_test`, `opacity`, `live`;
  the offscreen lists the renderer holds (`surfaces`: `kind` `camera_texture` or `world`, `id`, `size`,
  `quads`, `draws`, `composites`); and which of the two passes are registered (`passes`).
- `ui.set_target {root, target}` moves a root. `root` is an entity id or a node name (or the usual filters);
  `target` is `"window"`, `{"camera": <entity>}` or `{"world": {"size": [w, h], "ppm": n, "billboard"?,
  "pivot"?, "fade"?, "depth_test"?, "opacity"?, "live"?}}`. A world target writes the root's `WorldPanel` and
  switches its scale mode to one UI px per texel. The reply is the root's `ui.targets` entry; the change shows
  on the next frame.
- `ui.world_click` clicks a world panel. Give a ray (`origin` and `direction`, or `ray: {origin, direction}`),
  a screen point of a camera (`x`/`y` pixels or `u`/`v` fractions with an optional `camera`, as
  `camera.raycast`), or a panel root `entity` with an optional `uv` (default the centre). A ray is tested
  against every panel (both faces; billboards turn toward the ray origin) and the closest hit wins. The agent
  then casts the same ray with `world.pick`'s scene query: a surface nearer than the panel (by more than 1 cm,
  so a panel mounted on a mesh still clicks) makes the reply `occluded: true` and nothing is clicked.
  `occlusion: false` skips that test. Otherwise the panel pixel goes through that root's own hit test and a
  `Click` is delivered to the interactable node there on the next frame. The reply is `{root, uv, px,
  distance, node, clicked, occluded, occluder_distance}`.

`ui.world_click` and `ui.set_target` need the `edit_scene` permission; `ui.targets` is read-only.

```text
ui.set_target {"root": "shop_sign", "target": {"world": {"size": [512, 256], "ppm": 256, "billboard": "axis_y", "fade": [8, 12]}}}
ui.targets {}
ui.world_click {"x": 640, "y": 360}
ui.world_click {"entity": 4294967321, "uv": [0.25, 0.5]}
```

## Example calls

Example calls (`regia agent call <method> '<params json>'`; entity ids come from `scene.query_entities`):

```text
ui.query {"type": "Button", "text_contains": "play", "limit": 10}
ui.state {}
ui.click {"name": "play_button"}
ui.set_value {"name": "volume", "value": 0.5}
ui.type {"name": "player_name", "text": "Ada", "keys": ["Enter"]}
```

# UI agent map

Every `ui.*` and `editor.theme_panel_*` method of the runtime UI in one place: what it does, the permission it
needs, and the page with the full parameters and error codes. Read [Runtime UI](book/agents/ui.md) first for the node
filters (`node`, `name`, `text`, `class`, `type`, `state`) that most methods share. The same map for people is
[Runtime UI: a tour](book/user-guide/ui-tour.md).

Guide topic: `agent.guide {"topic": "ui"}`.

## Waiting

`play.wait_until` and `play.expect` take these UI atoms; combine them with `all`, `any` and `not`.

| Atom | Holds when | Page |
|---|---|---|
| `ui.node_exists` | at least one node matches (or none, with `exists: false`) | [Runtime UI](book/agents/ui.md) |
| `ui.node_state` | the one matching node has the state | [Runtime UI](book/agents/ui.md) |
| `ui.tweening` | a node (or any node) is tweening | [Tweens](book/agents/ui-animation.md) |
| `ui.theme_generation` | the theme generation reached a value | [Themes](book/agents/ui-theme.md) |
| `ui.theme_fading` | nodes are (or, with `is: false`, are no longer) cross-fading after a theme swap | [Theme switching](book/agents/ui-theme-switch.md) |

## Widgets with no method of their own

The radio button, spin box, foldable, split pane and toast (D11) are read with `ui.query`, driven with
`ui.click` and `ui.set_value` and awaited with the atoms above: [Default widgets](book/agents/ui-default-widgets.md). The
theme sheet page of the gallery sample gives each widget in each state a node name `sheet.<widget>.<size>.<state>`:
[Theme sheet](book/agents/ui-theme-sheet.md).

## Errors

Error codes are lowercase ascii, digits and `_`, and each page lists its own. Two rules hold for the whole
family:

- A missing or wrongly typed parameter answers `F0002`.
- `ui_not_installed` means the app has no `UiAgentHost`; `regia::DefaultPlugins` inserts one when the `ui`
  and `agent` features are on.

## A worked check

Open a menu, pick an item, and read that the menu closed:

```text
ui.open_popup {"anchor": {"name": "file_menu"}}
play.step {"frames": 2}
ui.menu_activate {"name": "file_menu", "path": ["save"]}
ui.menu {"name": "file_menu"}
```

# Baked GI from the level

A map can name its own baked GI volume. The framework loads the `.fgiv` when the level opens and
installs it in the renderer, so a host no longer calls `set_baked_gi` itself. The volume and its
lookup are in [Baked GI volumes](book/agents/baked-gi.md); this page is about how a level carries one.

## The level names its bake

`LevelSettings.look.baked_gi` (scene format v10, `docs/formats/scene-files.md`):

```ron
look: (
    baked_gi: Some((
        volume: "maps/bore_twelve.fgiv",      // under assets/
        settings: (sky_scale: Some(0.8)),     // optional per-map overrides
    )),
),
```

- `volume` is a path under `assets/`. `assets://` and `assets/` prefixes are accepted. An empty
  path names no bake.
- `settings` overrides the renderer's baked-GI settings for this map. Each field is optional, and
  an unset one keeps the host's value: `intensity`, `sky_scale`, `emissive_scale`,
  `replace_live_fill`. Biases and sun/fill following stay with the host.
- Levels older than v10 migrate with `baked_gi: None` and light as before.

## What the framework does

`regia_framework::baked_gi_level::BakedGiLevelPlugin` is part of `DefaultPlugins`.

- **Level loads:** reads the volume (the cooked asset from a pak or the dev cache; in a dev run
  without a cook, the file `assets/<path>`), installs it, and applies `settings` on top of the
  settings the host had.
- **Hot reload:** a recooked `.fgiv`, a changed file, or an edited path or override installs the
  new volume without reopening the level. A file that appears later (a bake finishing) is picked up
  too.
- **Level unloads:** the volume is removed and the host's settings come back. Only the volume the
  level installed is removed. A volume the host installed itself stays, and a level that names a
  volume replaces it.
- **Failure:** a missing file or one that does not load logs one warning and installs nothing. The
  frame keeps its other GI (Balanced or Depth). Nothing panics. A split volume with a part lost lights
  the others ([Split baked GI volumes](book/agents/baked-gi-split.md#a-missing-or-damaged-part-adr-3006)).

## Entities: baked or dynamic

`GiMobility` is a component with two values: `Static` (the bake reads this entity) and `Dynamic`
(the default: lit from the volume at runtime, not part of it). An entity without it is `Dynamic`,
so existing scenes are unchanged. It is separate from the `Static` marker used for batching. The
export that builds a bake description from a level's `Static` entities is a follow-up
(ADR-284); until then the description is written by hand (`regia bake-gi`).

## Agent method

`level.get_baked_gi` (read only) returns:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `plugin` | the framework plugin is installed |
| `level` | the level's `baked_gi` (`volume`, `settings`), or `null` |
| `volume` | the path the plugin is working on, or `null` |
| `installed_by_level` | the level's volume is the one in the renderer |
| `source` | `level`, `host` (the host installed another volume) or `none` |
| `error`, `error_code` | why it could not load, and a stable code |
| `probes` | probes in the level's installed volume |
| `renderer` | `{ installed, active, probes, gpu_bytes, error }` from the renderer, or `null` |
| `parts` | the split set: `{ count, lit, failed: [{ index, path, code, error }], installed: [{ index, bytes, bricks, cropped_bricks }] }`, `null` before a volume was read; a whole volume has `count` 1 (ADR-3006). `installed` lists each lit part, with the bricks it holds cropped at a cut ([cropped bricks](book/agents/baked-gi-split.md#cropped-bricks-adr-3237), ADR-3237) |
| `host_layers` | layers in the renderer that are neither the level's parts nor a streamed level's (ADR-3006) |
| `memory` | the volumes' bytes against every tier, what is over and what fixes it ([details](book/agents/baked-gi-split.md#memory-before-a-bake)), `null` with none installed (ADR-3006) |

Error codes: `volume_not_found` (no cooked asset and no file under `assets/`) and
`volume_unreadable`. That second code is a damaged or newer-version file, a split part whose group
does not match part 0, or a path that names a split part other than 0. Read `error`: when it says
`name part 0`, point `level` at the file without a `.part` suffix. Rebaking writes another good part
file and the same code comes back until the path is part 0.

## Checking a map

1. `level.get_baked_gi`: `source` is `level`, `error` is `null`, `probes` matches the bake.
2. `play.step 2`, then `render.get_gi_mode`: `baked.active` is `true`
   ([Baked GI volumes](book/agents/baked-gi.md)).
3. If `error_code` is `volume_not_found`, check the path against `assets/` and run `regia cook`;
   if `volume_unreadable`, read `error`. A split part other than 0 needs the part-0 path; a damaged
   or newer-version file is rebaked with the same engine version.
4. `level.set_look {"look": {"baked_gi": null}}` removes the bake on the next frame, to compare.

## Example calls

Example calls (`regia agent call <method> '<params json>'`; entity ids come from `scene.query_entities`):

```text
level.get_baked_gi {}          # { plugin, level, volume, source, error, probes, renderer }
```

## Tunnels

A tube lights well from a ground-following layer along its floor: the sun that falls through the mouth
bounces down the tube (the tunnel acceptance scene's volume reads 440 lux/π on the floor 6 m in and 64 at
18 m). The volume lights single-sample frames only, so a tunnel view with MSAA shows no bake. Inside an
`InteriorVolume` that holds the camera the forward pass takes the interior shade, and since ADR-7975 that
shade reads the baked volume too: where the volume covers a surface inside the interior box, its baked
irradiance (and its probe light in the reflection) replaces the interior's neutral floor and the legacy
probe-grid bounce, so a baked tunnel keeps its light gradient on every desktop tier (Low included) instead
of a flat floor. Where no volume covers the surface (a tube without a bake, a stretch the bake missed),
the interior shade is the floor and probe bounce as before, bit for bit. Before ADR-7975 the interior shade
ignored the volume (ADR-3257), so a baked tunnel had to be lit without an `InteriorVolume`
(`probe_volume_lifts_the_tube_interior`, [Tunnel acceptance scene](book/agents/tunnel-scene.md)). The Mobile tiers'
lite forward shader on a tile GPU reads no baked volume anywhere, inside or out (ADR-1874).
`cargo test -p regia_render --test interior_baked_gi` (lavapipe) holds the interior floor to the bake's
gradient on Desktop Low and High and the tube without a covering volume to the flat floor.

# UI lists and scrollbars (agents)

Guide topic: `agent.guide {"topic": "ui_list"}`. ADR-273 lane 8, ADR-344.

## Lists

A list (`ListView` with `ListItems` or `ItemCount`) owns its data. Only the visible rows exist as entities, plus
the overscan, so 10 000 items cost a few dozen nodes. Row `i` always lives in pool slot `i % pool_len`: scrolling by
one row rebinds one entry and spawns nothing. Each rebind writes a `ListEntryBind { list, row, index }` message, so a
game can fill custom entries (mark the list `CustomEntries` to switch the default label off).

Optional components on the list entity:

| Component | Effect |
|---|---|
| `ListHeights(Vec<f32>)` | Per-item row heights (UI px); items past the end use `ListView::item_height`. A prefix-sum table makes the row at an offset a binary search. |
| `ListTiles { tile_size, gap, columns }` | Tile mode: items wrap into columns (`columns: None` fits as many whole tiles as the width allows). |
| `ListSelection::new(mode)` | `none`, `single` or `multi`. Click selects, Ctrl toggles, Shift extends from the anchor. Rows of selected items carry the `Selected` marker. |
| `ListHeaders(Vec<usize>)` | Items that are section headers (ascending). The header of the section at the top sticks there until the next header pushes it out. Rows only; not in tile mode. |
| `ScrollToItem { index, align }` | A one-shot request; `ui.list`/`ui.scroll_to` insert it. |

Keyboard and gamepad: arrow keys and the d-pad move focus between rows as before and the list cursor follows (with
Shift held in a multi list the selection extends). Home, End, PageUp and PageDown jump (the page is the number of
items in the viewport), Ctrl+A selects all in a multi list, and typing letters jumps to the next item whose label
starts with them (case-insensitive; the typed prefix expires after one second of game time). Repeating one letter
cycles through the matches.

Messages: `ListSelectionChanged { list, selected }`, `ListActivated { list, index }` (double-click).

## Scrollbars

Add `Scrollbars` to a scroll view (or list). It draws a track and a draggable thumb on the vertical edge (and the
horizontal edge with `horizontal: true`) when the content overflows. Dragging the thumb scrolls; a click on the track
centers the thumb on the click. `auto_hide: Some(seconds)` hides the bars after that long without scrolling or
pointer contact. The bars are siblings of the scroll view, so the view needs a parent node that does not scroll
itself. They carry the theme classes `scrollbar-track` and `scrollbar-thumb`; set `track_color` / `thumb_color` to
`None` to leave the colors to the theme. A scroll view without `Scrollbars` keeps its thin, non-interactive thumb.

Focus moving to a node inside a scroll view scrolls the node into view on both axes, once per focus move.

## Methods

- `ui.list { entity, action?, ... }` where `entity` is the node id from `ui.query` (`node` works as an alias).
  - `action: "info"` (default): `{ entity, count, range: [start, end], live_rows, spawned_rows, rebinds, total_height,
    offset, layout, selection: { mode, selected, cursor }, headers }`. `count` is the current item count
    (`ListItems`, or `ItemCount` when there are no items) and `total_height` is that count's content height,
    including before the first virtualise pass. `layout` is `rows`, `variable_rows` or `tiles`;
    `range` is the half-open range of items with live rows, and it stays empty until a virtualise pass
    lays the list out.
  - `action: "items"` with `start` (default 0) and `limit` (default 100, at most 500): `{ entity, start, items: [{ index,
    label, selected }] }`.
  - `action: "select"` with optional `mode` (`none`, `single`, `multi`: adds a selection model when the list has none),
    `op` (`set` default, `add`, `toggle`, `range` from the first to the last index, `all`, `clear`) and `indices`
    (or one `index`). Returns the same shape as `info`. Applies at once. A call with only `mode` changes the mode and
    keeps the selection.
  - `action: "scroll_to"` with `index` and `align` (`nearest` default, `start`, `center`, `end`): `{ entity, index,
    queued: true }`. The scroll applies in the next frame's layout pass.
- `ui.scroll_to { entity, index? | reveal? | x?, y? | fraction?, align? }` scrolls a list or any scroll view. `index`
  is a list item (queued, as above). `reveal` is a node id to bring into view. `x` and `y` are absolute offsets in
  physical pixels; `fraction` is the vertical position from 0 (top) to 1 (end). Offsets clamp to the content. Returns
  `{ entity, offset: [x, y], max: [x, y] }` and applies at once.

Both are mutating (permission `edit_scene`).

```json
{"method": "ui.list", "params": {"entity": 4294967301}}
{"method": "ui.list", "params": {"entity": 4294967301, "action": "select", "mode": "multi", "op": "range", "indices": [3, 9]}}
{"method": "ui.list", "params": {"entity": 4294967301, "action": "items", "start": 100, "limit": 20}}
{"method": "ui.scroll_to", "params": {"entity": 4294967301, "index": 5000, "align": "center"}}
{"method": "ui.scroll_to", "params": {"entity": 4294967310, "fraction": 1.0}}
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `not_a_list` | The entity exists but is not a `ListView`. |
| `unknown_entity` | The entity (or `reveal` node) does not exist. |
| `index_out_of_range` | An item index is past the last item. |
| `no_selection` | `select` on a list without a selection model (or with mode `none`); pass `mode`. |
| `not_scrollable` | `ui.scroll_to` on an entity without a scroll offset. |

Bad or missing parameters answer `F0002` as for the other `ui.*` methods.

`unknown_entity`, `not_a_list` and `not_scrollable` are the listed `error.data.code` reasons on JSON-RPC `-32001`;
`index_out_of_range` and `no_selection` are `error.data.code` reasons on `-32602`. `indices` is limited to 4096
entries, and `align` is `nearest`, `start`, `center` or `end`.

Workflow: find a `ListView` with `ui.query`, read its `count` and `range` with `ui.list`, fetch a short item window,
then call `ui.scroll_to` for an item using `align:"center"` and inspect the next frame.

Captured failure on lavapipe:

Request:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"method":"ui.list","params":{"entity":0}}
```

Response:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"`entity` (or `node`) must be the node id from ui.query","data":{"code":"F0002","hint":"check the method's parameters in the agent guide"}}}
```

# Visibility buffer and cooked meshlets

The visibility buffer is the opt-in geometry path for dense scenes (`docs/specs/27` § 4.2 stage 3):
rigid opaque meshes and eligible masked foliage are split into clusters (meshlets), culled and LOD-cut on the GPU, written into
an ID target, and shaded by a per-material resolve with the forward shader's lighting. This page is
about how a game's cooked meshes get onto it, how its memory behaves under streaming, and how an
agent checks both.

## Turning it on

The path runs when the active render profile has `visibility_buffer: true` (off on every preset; a
game sets it on a custom profile) and the device has the storage buffers the resolve needs. The
frame must also have a depth prepass, a post stack (linear HDR) and no MSAA, and some mesh must have
meshlets. Meshes without meshlets, and every mesh while the path is off, draw on the forward path.

An agent switches it with `render.set_visbuffer { enabled: true }` (below). A preset change
(`render.set_profile`) replaces the whole profile, and with it the switch.

## Dense scenes: selecting the path

`RenderProfile::visibility_path` says which frames take the path and how its resolve shades. The
default is what the switch has always meant: every frame the path can draw, one draw per material.
**No preset changes this.** A game picks the selectable profile, or an agent the same settings:

```rust,wrap
# use regia_render::{RenderProfile, RenderProfilePreset};
// Desktop High or Ultra; `None` on every other preset, none of which has been measured.
let profile = RenderProfile::dense_scenes(RenderProfilePreset::DesktopUltra).ok_or("no dense-scenes profile")?;
```

| `select` | Which frames take the path |
|---|---|
| `always` | Every frame the switch allows (the default) |
| `dense` | Only while the frame's rigid opaque meshes reach `enter_triangles` triangles or `enter_instances` meshes |

The count is the whole submitted list, in view or not, with or without meshlets, so turning the camera
does not flip the path. Entering takes `enter_frames` frames in a row over a threshold (default 4) and
leaving takes `leave_frames` frames in a row under half of both (default 120), so a scene near a threshold
never flaps. A sparse level draws the classic forward frame, byte for byte. A frame with persistent
instance sets (`FrameRenderer::set_instance_set`) always takes the path, because they draw nowhere else.

The default thresholds (2,000,000 triangles, 4096 meshes) are a starting point, not a measured
crossover. The switch itself costs one pop in LOD selection: the first path frame draws chains as
before, and clusters pick the detail from the next one (see "Mesh LOD chains").

A game-frame warm of a profile on `dense` builds the path's cull, raster, shadow and resolve pipelines
(warm key `visbuffer_path`), and draws two window-size frames through the path, so its targets, lists
and bind groups exist too. While a profile selects `dense`, the lists keep a reserve from its
thresholds: four times `enter_instances` meshes (1024 to 65,536) and the larger of
`enter_triangles / 32` and 16 per reserved mesh in clusters (at most 2^20). The frames a scene turns dense compile nothing and create no
target, list, buffer or bind group: `creates.last_frame.objects` stays 0, switch after switch, and a
new renderer-wide bind epoch in play does not touch the path's groups. A scene past the reserve grows a list once, on the frame it
passes it, and the count is flat again from the next frame. The dense scene's own meshes still become
resident on their first path frame, and if they overflow the cluster arena it doubles once ("Cluster
memory"), which replaces its buffers and the groups over them. A worker warm that is handed over
(`adopt_warm_pipelines`) moves the pipelines only; that renderer creates its lists and targets on its
first dense frame.

### Choosing the thresholds

Pick the thresholds in density units, not raw counts: the classic path's cost grows with the
triangles it submits per pixel, the path's with the clusters it draws per screen tile, so one
density holds at 1080p and at 4K where a triangle count does not. `DensityMetrics::of_frame`
gives a frame's `triangles_per_pixel` (the gate's triangle count over the frame's pixels),
`instances_per_megapixel` and `clusters_per_tile` (clusters drawn per 16 px tile, from
`FrameRenderer::visbuffer_counters`). The bench prints all three on every row ("Measuring a
machine"). To choose a default from a card's rows:

1. Run the bench at the target resolution. For each scene, compare the classic row's `gpu` time
   with the path's.
2. Take the lowest `tri/px` where the path's time is at or under the classic one, on both cards.
   That density, with a margin, is the triangle threshold. Do the same with `inst/Mpx` for the
   instance threshold (a many-small-props scene).
3. `DenseSceneSelect::at_density(tri_per_px, inst_per_mpx, width, height)` turns them into the
   gate's counts for a frame size. Write them into `RenderProfile::dense_scenes`.
4. Note the rows' `clusters/tile` next to the choice: that is the path's load at the
   crossover, and a scene far above it costs more on the path than the bench measured.

The current defaults (2,000,000 triangles, 4096 meshes) are about 1 triangle per pixel and 1,975
meshes per million pixels at 1080p. Lavapipe rows show the numbers are counted right, not where
the crossover is.

The bench does steps 1 to 3 itself (ADR-3149): after the scenes of each size it prints one
`crossover <resolve>:` line per resolve, from `DenseCrossover::of_rows`. That is the sparsest scene
from which the path wins every denser scene by at least 3 % (`DENSE_CROSSOVER_MARGIN`), with the
gate's counts at 1080p, 1440p and 4K. `bracketed false` means the path won down to the sparsest
scene run, so add sparser scenes until a row loses. `crossover <resolve>: none` means the path lost
the densest scene, and no threshold is safe on that card. For two cards, `DenseCrossover::stricter`
takes the denser of each column, so a routed scene wins on both.

## The dense-scene default

`RenderSettings::visibility_default` is the switch that routes dense scenes to the path by default
(ADR-3149). It is off (`preset`) in every preset, so nothing changes unless a game or an agent turns
it on:

```rust,wrap
# use regia_render::{RenderProfilePreset, RenderSettings, VisibilityDefault, VisibilityDefaultState};
let mut settings = RenderSettings::from_profile(RenderProfilePreset::DesktopHigh);
let state = settings.set_visibility_default(VisibilityDefault::Dense);
assert_eq!(state, VisibilityDefaultState::Applied);
assert_eq!(settings.preset(), Some(RenderProfilePreset::DesktopHigh)); // the same tier for every other system
```

On, a Desktop High or Ultra profile that still has its preset's path columns (path off, `always`)
gets `VisibilityPath::DENSE_DEFAULT`: the path on, `select` `dense` at `DenseSceneSelect::MEASURED`
(4,000,000 triangles or 4096 meshes), and the per-material resolve. Those thresholds come from the only
card rows recorded (a 5090 at 1440p, `docs/perf-log.md`). The sparsest scene the path won there has
3,999,744 triangles, and the single pass lost two of the four scenes, so it stays off. The 5080 and
7900 crossovers replace these numbers. The switch is kept across `apply_preset` (`render.set_profile`)
and leaves alone:

| `default.state` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `applied` | The switch is on and the profile holds the default's path |
| `switch_off` | The switch is off (`preset`) |
| `preset_unmeasured` | The profile is not Desktop High or Ultra, or not a preset's row at all: unmeasured, untouched |
| `profile_choice` | The game set its own path (`enabled`, `select`, the single pass): the default neither writes nor reverts it |

Turning it off restores the preset's columns only when the profile still holds exactly what the default
wrote. With the switch on, no golden moves. The lab goldens draw at `FrameQuality::LAB`, which has the
path off whatever the settings say. The default-look goldens (`samples/lookdev/goldens`, drawn from
`RenderSettings`) stay byte-identical because their scenes are far below the thresholds:
`default_look_dense_default` renders each shot both ways with clusters available and fails on one
moved pixel. The same test prints what `select: always` would move instead.

Stage 3's acceptance on the floor tier (1080p, Desktop High, the default on) is
`samples/lookdev/tests/visbuffer_default_plates.rs`. In the gate, `the_floor_tier_routes_ten_times_the_rocks_to_the_path`
checks that 410 rocks stay classic and 4100 take the path. On a card, `stage3_scatter_plates` times
the base scatter, ten times the rocks on the classic path, and ten times with the default, and prints
`stage3 verdict: ... holds true|false` (ten times with the default within 5 % of the base).
`dense_default_owner_plates` writes the classic and default frames with their difference times eight
for the owner:

```sh
REGIA_STAGE3_OUT=/tmp/stage3 REGIA_STAGE3_SIZE=1920x1080 \
cargo test --release -p lookdev --test visbuffer_default_plates -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1
```

## The single-pass resolve

With `single_pass_resolve` on, one full-screen draw shades every material. Group 2 binds the whole
material arena and a map from the frame's material slots to arena records, each pixel finds its record
through its instance, and the textures come from the texture table by per-pixel index. There is no
material-depth pass. The frames equal the per-material resolve byte for byte, on any adapter where both
run.

It needs a device on the texture table ([bindless](book/agents/bindless.md)), which is decided when the device is
created: `RenderProfile::dense_scenes` and any profile with the knob on ask the first window's device for
it, and `REGIA_BINDLESS_LEVEL=3` does the same for any device. Where it cannot run, the per-material
resolve shades the same pixels and `resolve.fallback` says why:

| Code | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `vis_no_texture_table` | The device is off the texture table (`render.bindless_report` says why) | Set the profile before the first window's device, or `REGIA_BINDLESS_LEVEL=3`; a device that cannot carry the table keeps the per-material resolve |
| `vis_storage_limits` | Fewer than 13 storage buffers per fragment stage (14 with residency feedback) | A device with higher limits |
| `vis_lightmap_receivers` | An instance this frame is a lightmap receiver; the per-material resolve has the variant that reads the lightmap | Nothing to fix: the frame is right, it costs the per-material draws |

To check it: `render.get_visbuffer` `resolve.single_pass` is `true`, `resolve.draws` is 1 and
`resolve.materials` counts the materials; off it, `draws` is 1 + the materials.

## Mesh LOD chains

A cooked mesh usually carries a `MeshLodChain` too (its generated LOD 1..3 index lists). On the
visibility buffer the clusters are the LOD: each cluster of the simplification hierarchy is cut per
pixel at every distance. So while the path draws, the mesh LOD selector leaves a chained mesh at
LOD 0 when that mesh has meshlets (ADR-1148). Without that, its coarser levels would draw on the
forward path from the first switch distance on, which is most of a dense scatter.

- **When.** The profile has the path on, the runtime renderer's last frame took it
  (`FrameRenderer::visbuffer_active`), and the mesh has meshlets that were not declined (cooked for
  other mesh data) and not refused at the arena's cap (`FrameRenderer::visbuffer_cluster_lod`).
  The entity must also be one the path draws: opaque, not transmissive, no material graph, no morph
  targets (skinned meshes never take a chain's selection). Otherwise the chain picks the level as
  before, so a glass or morphing user of a shared mesh keeps its levels. The first visibility frame after the path turns on
  still uses the chain, and the hand-off starts on the next one.
- **Shadows.** With `cluster_shadows` on (the default), the clusters cast with their own per-texel
  cut, so the mesh is one draw. With it off, the chain's shadow LOD still draws the shadow on the
  forward shadow passes.
- **Switching back.** When the path stops drawing, or the meshlets are removed, the chain picks the
  level for the distance at once, with no cross-fade from LOD 0. Turning the path on is likewise
  one switch with no fade.
- **Hosts that drive `FrameRenderer` themselves** (not through `RuntimeRenderer`) keep their own
  LOD selection. A meshlet builder (`set_meshlet_builder`) clusters each LOD's index list as its
  own mesh, as before.

## Software raster

With `software_raster` on (`render.set_visbuffer`, off by default), clusters that span at most
`software_raster_max_px` pixels rasterize in compute instead of through the hardware rasterizer. A
cluster stays in hardware when it reaches the near plane or the software list is full. A
double-sided material's clusters take the compute path too, with their back faces drawn, as the
hardware's cull-none raster draws them; when the software list is full they fall back to that raster,
so their back faces stay. Shadow clusters always rasterize in hardware: a shadow job
writes depth only, with the shadow pipelines' slope bias, and its LOD cut is already per shadow
texel. The pixels merge into the same ID target and depth, so the resolve, motion vectors, SSAO and
decals do not change.

To check it, read `render.get_visbuffer` `settings` after the call, then compare screenshots with
the switch off and on: they match except for a few edge pixels. Tests and benches read how many
clusters took the path with `FrameRenderer::visbuffer_counters` (`software_clusters`), which blocks
on the GPU. Whether it is faster than the hardware rasterizer depends on the GPU, so no preset
turns it on.

## Cooking meshlets

Set `meshlets: true` in a glTF's `.meta` settings. `regia cook` then writes one `.fmlt` sub-asset
per mesh primitive, `meshlets/<node>/primitive_<i>`, next to `mesh/<node>/primitive_<i>`. The
clusters are built over LOD 0 of the cooked mesh exactly as the runtime decodes it, so they index
the vertex buffer the game uploads.

## The framework bridge

`regia_framework::meshlet_bridge::MeshletBridgePlugin` is part of `DefaultPlugins`. It is idle
until the profile turns the path on.

A host marks each entity that draws a cooked primitive with `MeshletSource`, the `.fmlt` sibling's
asset id:

```rust,wrap
# use regia::prelude::*;
# let mut commands: Commands = todo!();
# let world: &mut World = todo!();
# let app: &mut App = todo!();
# let (gltf_id, rock): (regia_asset::AssetId, Entity) = todo!();
# let server: regia_asset::AssetServer = todo!();
use regia_framework::meshlet_bridge::MeshletSource;

// From the glTF's asset id and the mesh's sub-asset path:
let source = MeshletSource::for_mesh(gltf_id, "mesh/Rock/primitive_0");
// Or from the manifest path of the cooked mesh:
let source = MeshletSource::for_mesh_path(&server, "assets/rock.gltf#mesh/Rock/primitive_0");
commands.entity(rock).insert(source.expect("a cooked mesh primitive"));
```

Each frame (`PostUpdate`) the bridge:

- **Inserts.** It loads the payload through the asset server (the latest pak that holds it, else
  the cooked cache) and calls `FrameRenderer::insert_meshlets` under the entity's mesh key. Several
  entities that share one mesh share one insert.
- **Registers masked foliage.** Rigid `ALPHA_MASK` meshes without hair or parallax receive their cooked meshlets
  too. The frame uses the alpha-tested cluster raster on texture-table devices; elsewhere they keep their forward
  draws. Material changes to blended, hair, parallax, transmissive or graph shading remove that entity from the bridge.
- **Keeps the forward path where it must.** Skinned meshes (`SkinJoints`), morphing meshes
  (`MeshMorphTargets`), translucent ones (blended, hair drawn blended or masked, transmissive) and
  material-graph meshes are never inserted.
- **Leaves a lightmap receiver alone.** It draws its entry's unwrap, which the source's clusters do not fit, so the bridge gives
  them back while it is one and inserts them again when it gets its own mesh back. Its clusters come from a
  `regia bake-lightmaps --meshlets` bake ([Lightmaps](book/agents/lightmaps.md)).
- **Removes and inserts again.** This happens when the entity's mesh or `MeshletSource` changes,
  when the entity is despawned or loses either component (the last user of a mesh removes it), and
  when the `.fmlt` is hot-reloaded (`regia run --dev`, the editor's live cook).
- **Removes everything** when the profile turns the path off, and inserts again when it comes back
  on.
- **Fails safe.** A missing, damaged or old payload, or one cooked for other mesh data, logs one
  warning (per payload version) and the mesh draws forward. Nothing panics. Recooking the asset
  retries it.

Hosts that drive the renderer directly call `FrameRenderer::insert_meshlets`,
`FrameRenderer::remove_meshlets` and `FrameRenderer::has_meshlets` themselves.

## Cluster memory

Every resident mesh's cluster records and geometry words (vertices, cluster vertex lists,
triangles) are ranges of one GPU buffer per stream, taken from a best-fit free list that merges
