| `foam_width` | Width of the foam band, horizontal meters from the waterline | 1.6 |
| `max_depth` | Path length at which the body color reaches `deep_color`, meters. Body opacity is 95 % of `alpha` at half of it | 12.0 |
| `alpha` | Opacity of deep water (0..1) | 0.75 |
| `wave_amplitude` | Ripple amplitude, meters | 0.05 |
| `wave_frequency` | Ripple wave number, radians per meter | 0.9 |

## Errors

- `F0003`: the world has no `Terrain`.
- `F0002`:
  - an unknown field, or a value that fails validation (colors outside 0..1, a negative width,
    `alpha` outside 0..1, a non-finite level);
  - more than 64 points, or a point that is not `[x, z]`;
  - `enabled: false` together with `water`.

## How it looks

- **Reflection.** The surface reflects the sky by Fresnel. Looking straight down, about 2 %
  of what shows is reflected sky. At grazing angles almost all of it is. The reflected sky is
  the frame's uniform sky light, the same light the terrain is lit with. There is no
  screen-space reflection yet.
- **Transmission.** The view ray bends into the water (Snell's law). The bed shows through
  in proportion to the water crossed along that bent ray, so shallow water is clear and deep
  water shows its own color. The offscreen renderer also refracts the picture: the bed shows
  from where the bent ray meets it (screen-space refraction). Where something above the water
  stands in front of that spot, the water shows what is straight behind it instead.
  `TerrainGpu::set_water_refraction(false)` turns the refraction off.
- **Waterline.** The water's opacity fades in from zero over the last 0.2 m of depth, so the
  shoreline shows no hard edge.
- **Foam.** The band is `foam_width` meters wide measured across the beach, whatever the
  beach's slope.
- **Ripples.** The ripple normals shade every pixel. The water grid has 64 cells per side
  over the whole map, so it drops a ripple it cannot resolve: on a large map the drawn surface
  is flat and only the shading ripples.
- **From below.** Past the critical angle (about 48.6° from straight up) the surface is a
  mirror of the water body. Inside that cone it shows the sky.

## Checking it

1. Call `terrain.water { at: [[x, z]] }` at a beach point. `wet` should be true and `depth`
   small, and `shore_distance` should be about `depth / slope`.
2. Raise `max_depth` with `terrain.set_water`, then probe the same point again.
   `opacity_from_above` should drop: the same water is clearer.
3. Edits change the `Terrain` component only. An offscreen `TerrainGpu` keeps the plane it
   was built with until the host passes the new plane to `TerrainGpu::set_water`; the runtime
   water body (with `WaterPlugin`) follows on the next frame.
4. Look at the pictures in `samples/terrain_lab`: compare a frame looking
   straight down with one at a grazing angle. The grazing water should take the sky's color.

## Caustics and sun shafts (`water.set_caustics`, `water.caustics_stats`)

Light focused by the ripples falls on whatever lies below a water surface, and under a surface
the sun makes shafts in the water (ADR-2432). Both are **off by default**: a body has
`look.caustics.enabled = false`, no pass is built and default frames are byte-identical.

The setting is `WaterCaustics` on the water look: `enabled`, `strength` (0..=4, 1 is physical),
`scale` (pattern size against the ripple tile), `speed` (the pattern's change; the first enabled
body drives the frame's tile), `chromatic` (0..=1 colour spread of the focus), `shaft_steps` (0 for
no shafts, else 8..=16) and `tier_cost` (`high` or `ultra`). It is saved with the look and left
out of a save while it is the default; older files load unchanged.

`water.set_caustics { entity?, body?, enabled?, strength?, scale?, speed?, chromatic?,
shaft_steps?, tier_cost? }` patches those fields on one body (`entity`, alias `body`, default the
first). It returns `{ entity, before, caustics, tier, active, compiled_out }`: `active` says
whether the pass draws at the effective tier, `compiled_out` is true on Low, which never draws it.

`water.caustics_stats { depth? }` reports `{ tier, compiled_out, enabled_bodies, active_bodies,
passes: { bodies, tile_size, tile_passes, shaft_passes, shaft_texels, shaft_steps, shafts_drawn },
tile }`. `tile` is the tile read back from the GPU and summarized at `depth` metres (default 1):
`mean_density` stays near 1 (the focusing moves light, it does not add any) and `max_density` is the
focus. It is `null` until a tile pass has run, and the read blocks until the GPU is done.

| Code | Raised by |
|---|---|
| `F0002` | `water.set_caustics` on an unknown or out-of-range field, a `tier_cost` of `low`, or `shaft_steps` outside 0 and 8..=16; `water.caustics_stats` on a `depth` outside 0..=20. |
| `F0003` | `water.set_caustics` without `WaterPlugin` or without the body; `water.caustics_stats` with no water renderer. |

Checking it:

1. `water.set { tier: "high" }`, then `water.set_caustics { enabled: true }` and wait a frame
   (`wait_until` on `water.caustics_stats.passes.tile_passes >= 1`). With the sun above the horizon
   the tile exists: `tile.max_density` above 1.5 at 1 m, `tile.mean_density` near 1.
2. Take a screenshot looking down at a shallow bed, enable, take another: bright lines move over
   the bed and fade with depth (to the plain lighting by about 6 m). Pick a body with
   `normal_strength` 0 and nothing changes: calm water focuses nothing.
3. Dive under (`water.set { underwater: true }`, camera below the surface) with `shaft_steps: 12`:
   `passes.shafts_drawn` is true and bright shafts run toward the surface. `water.set { tier: "low" }`
   makes `compiled_out` true and both effects vanish.

The pattern is sharpest at about a quarter of the tile length below the surface (the tile is
`look.ripple_scale` times `caustics.scale`): a 1.5 m stream tile focuses near 0.4 m, the sea's 18 m tile
near 5 m, where the fade has all but ended it, so use a smaller `scale` for shallow beds under big
ripples.

Limits: the pattern follows the ripple map, not a swell's or ocean's long waves; frames that only
blend (no scene copy) draw no receiver caustics.

### Shafts with occluders, accumulation and the view from above (ADR-3251)

- **Occluders.** With a sun shadow map bound, a pier, a hull or a cave roof cuts the shafts:
  `passes.shadow_bound` is true. The engine frame hands its sun cascade over once its hookup is in
  (the frame patch named in ADR-3251); a host can bind its own map with `WaterRenderer::set_sun_shadow`.
  No map bound draws exactly what it did before.
- **Accumulation.** `water.set_caustics { shaft_accumulate: true }` averages the half-resolution march
  over up to 16 frames (`passes.resolves`, `passes.history_frames`), reprojected as the camera turns and
  restarted on a camera cut (`passes.history_resets`). Off by default; two more half-resolution targets.
- **From above.** `water.set_caustics { shafts_from_above: true }` draws a plane's shafts with the eye
  above its surface, behind the surface only (`passes.from_above`). Off by default.

Checking it: dive under a body with shafts next to a pier (`passes.shadow_bound` true): a dark slab
runs down from the pier's shadow on the surface along the refracted sun; with `shaft_accumulate` on and
the camera still, `passes.history_frames` reaches 16 and the shafts stop crawling; a camera cut (a
teleport the frame renderer detects) brings `history_frames` back to 1. Above the water with `shafts_from_above` on, shafts show
in the water in front of the camera and nowhere above it.

<!-- source: book/agents/sky-lab.md -->
# Sky Lab: a day cycle with weather presets

`samples/sky_lab` renders the physical sky and the volumetric cloud layer for a fixed number of
frames while the sun moves from a start hour to an end hour and the weather blends from one preset
to another. It runs headless (a GPU adapter is needed; lavapipe works), writes PNG frames and a
JSON report, and has no window and no network. Use it to check a sky or cloud change over a whole
day instead of one pose, or as the smallest example of driving `TimeOfDay` and `CloudSettings` per
frame. For how clouds and the sky work see [Clouds](book/agents/clouds.md) and [Atmosphere](book/agents/atmosphere.md); the
walk-through for people is [Sky Lab (user guide)](book/user-guide/sky-lab.md).

The sample has no agent-protocol methods of its own. It is driven from the command line, and its
output (`report.json`, PNG files) is what an agent reads back.

## Run it

```sh
cargo run -p sky_lab -- --out /tmp/sky_lab_run
cargo run -p sky_lab -- --frames 60 --size 640x360 --from clear --to overcast --start-hour 9 --end-hour 15
cargo run -p sky_lab -- --list
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--frames N` | 120 | Frames to render, at least 1. |
| `--size WxH` | 320x180 | Image size, up to 4096 on a side. |
| `--from NAME`, `--to NAME` | `fair`, `storm` | Weather at the first and the last frame. |
| `--start-hour H`, `--end-hour H` | 5.5, 18.5 | Hour of day at the first and the last frame, wrapped into 0..24. |
| `--out DIR` | none | Write `frame_NNNN.png` and `report.json` under `DIR`. |
| `--every N` | 20 | A PNG every `N` frames; frame 0 and the last frame are always written when `--out` is set. |
| `--list` | | Print the preset names and exit. |

Exit codes: 0 done, 1 a frame failed to render or a file could not be written, 2 bad arguments (the
usage line is printed), 3 no GPU adapter.

## Presets

| Name | Coverage | Type | Layer (m) | Wind (m/s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clear` | 0 | cumulus | 1500 - 4000 | 6, 2 |
| `fair` | 0.3 | cumulus | 1500 - 4000 | 6, 2 |
| `broken` | 0.6 | cumulus | 1500 - 4000 | 9, 3 |
| `overcast` | 0.9 | stratus | 900 - 2400 | 4, 1 |
| `storm` | 0.85 | towering | 1200 - 6000 | 18, 6 |

`clear` has coverage zero, so the cloud pass is skipped. Between two presets, coverage, cloud type,
density, layer altitudes and wind interpolate with a smoothstep over the run. The renderer rebuilds
its weather map whenever coverage or type change, so a blend in progress rebuilds it every frame.

## The report

`report.json` has `width`, `height` and a `frames` array with one entry per frame:

```text
{ "frame": 60, "hour": 12.05, "sun_elevation_deg": 44.9, "coverage": 0.58, "mean_luma": 91.3 }
```

`mean_luma` is the mean of `0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B` over the 8-bit image. The scene has a
fixed exposure, so luma follows the sun: it is lowest while the sun is below the horizon and highest
near midday. Everything is a function of the frame number, so two runs with the same flags give the
same hours, elevations and coverages. The luma values depend on the GPU driver.

## Checks

- `tests/smoke.rs` `a_day_of_120_frames_renders_and_the_sky_follows_the_sun`: 120 frames at 160x90
  render, every luma is finite, midday is brighter than the first and the last frame, the coverage
  ends higher than it starts, and consecutive frames differ.
- `tests/smoke.rs` `a_run_writes_frames_and_a_report`: PNG files appear every 40th frame and on the
  last, `report.json` parses, and no temp file is left behind.
- Unit tests in `src/lib.rs` and `src/lab.rs` (no GPU): preset names and ranges, blend end points,
  the hour wrap, the sun rising and setting over the default day, command-line parsing.

Both smoke tests print a note and pass when there is no GPU adapter, so a green run on a machine
without one proves nothing; run them on a lavapipe or a hardware machine.

<!-- source: book/agents/shadow-stability.md -->
# Shadow stability (sun shadows that hold still)

A sun shadow should not crawl when the camera turns. Each sun cascade is an orthographic sun
view fitted to a sphere around a slice of the camera frustum. The sphere's size depends only on
the slice's distances, the field of view and the aspect, so turning the camera keeps it. Its
center moves with the camera.

Every preset keeps that center on the cascade's own texel grid in light space
(`FrameQuality::stable_sun_cascades`, ADR-1236). All placements then share one world-fixed texel
lattice, so a static pole, rail or leaf covers the same shadow texels in every frame. Without the
snap, the lattice slides by part of a texel each frame, and thin shadows widen, thin out and
break up as the camera turns: shimmer.

Before ADR-1236 only paged sun shadows (Desktop High and Ultra) snapped. Mobile Low, Mobile High,
Desktop Low, Deck and the editor viewport shimmered. The lab baseline (`FrameQuality::LAB`) still
uses the free-sliding fit, because its goldens were blessed with it.

## Check it

`render.shadow_stability` places the active profile's cascades on the CPU, the same way the
renderer does, for every frame of a camera sweep. No frame needs to run.

```json
{ "method": "render.shadow_stability",
  "params": { "eye": [0, 1.7, 0], "target": [0, 1.45, -1], "sweep": "yaw", "amount": 30, "frames": 60 } }
```

All parameters are optional:

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `eye`, `target` | `[0, 1.7, 0]`, 1 m ahead and 0.25 m down along −Z | The camera at the start of the sweep. |
| `sun` | `[-0.45, -0.72, -0.53]` | The sun's travel direction. |
| `sweep` | `"yaw"` | `yaw` (turn about the vertical), `pitch` (tilt) or `strafe` (move sideways). |
| `amount` | 30° (5 m for `strafe`) | The total turn in degrees, or the total move in meters. |
| `frames` | 60 | The number of frames along the sweep (2–1000). |
| `fov_y_deg`, `aspect`, `near`, `far` | 60, 16/9, 0.1, 2000 | The camera's lens. |
| `stable` | the profile's | What-if only: overrides `stable_sun_cascades` for this report. The renderer is not changed. |

Vector coordinates must remain finite as `f32`. The camera's target-minus-eye and the sun direction
must also have finite, nonzero squared lengths. Invalid vectors answer `F0002` before the sweep.

It returns, for example (the numbers are illustrative):

<!-- not-a-request -->
```json
{ "preset": "DesktopLow", "stable": true, "paged": false, "snap_texels": 2048, "resolution": 2048,
  "sweep": "yaw", "amount": 30.0, "frames": 60, "still": true, "still_threshold_texels": 0.02,
  "cascades": [ { "cascade": 0, "texel_m": 0.07, "max_drift_texels": 0.0004,
                  "mean_drift_texels": 0.0001, "moves": 59, "pairs": 59 } ] }
```

- **Drift** is how far a fixed world point slides inside its shadow texel from one frame to the
  next, in texels. 0 means static shadows stay put.
- **Moves** counts the frames in which the cascade moved. A stable cascade still moves, but only
  in whole texels, which a viewer cannot see.
- **Still** is true when every cascade stays under `still_threshold_texels` (0.02). The leftover
  is float rounding of the matrices: about a hundredth of a texel on Ultra's 1 cm cascade-0 texels.

## Compare before and after

1. Run `render.shadow_stability { "sweep": "yaw", "amount": 12, "frames": 48 }`. `still` should
   be `true`.
2. Run it again with `"stable": false`. Every cascade now drifts by tenths of a texel per frame,
   and `still` is `false`. That is the shimmer the snap removes.
3. To see it on screen, put the camera over thin casters (a fence, poles, scatter). Turn it slowly
   with a few `play.step` calls and take a `seeing.screenshot` after each one. On a stable profile
   the shadows do not change between shots.

**What is a bug.** `still: false` on any preset without `"stable": false` is a bug. So is a
`texel_m` that changes during a `yaw` or `pitch` sweep (the cascade radius must not depend on
where the camera looks). Report the parameters and the response.

## Limits

- The report covers the sun cascades only. The near sun tile (ADR-164) is always snapped to its own grid.
- Paged sun shadows (Desktop High and Ultra) may keep an older placement on the same lattice
  while it still covers the view. The report shows the fresh placement of each frame, which has the
  same drift.
- World coordinates far from the origin round more coarsely. At about 2 km out, rounding reaches
  about a hundredth of a 1 cm texel.

<!-- source: book/agents/material-clock.md -->
# Material clock and wind

Wind on foliage, scrolling water, a pulsing light panel: a material graph animates its surface by
reading the `Time` node. The value it reads is the **material clock**, which the runtime renderer
writes into every graph that reads `Time` (`params[0].x`, with the previous frame's value in
`params[0].y` for motion vectors). `regia_matgraph::drive_material_clock` sets it each
`PostUpdate` from gameplay [`Time`](book/user-guide/gameplay.md) (ADR-1238).

## Read

`render.material_clock` (no parameters):

```json
{}
→ { "set": true, "now": 12.5, "prev": 12.483333, "delta": 0.016667,
    "period_secs": 3600, "gameplay_secs": 3612.5 }
```

- `now` is the clock this frame, `prev` the clock one frame earlier, `delta` their difference
  (the frame's gameplay delta). `null` until the clock system has run once.
- `period_secs` is the lap length: the clock is gameplay time modulo 3600 s.
- `gameplay_secs` is the unwrapped gameplay time the clock follows (`null` without a `Time`
  resource).

Without a `RuntimeRenderer` the call fails with `F0003` (not found) and a hint. A host that drives
`FrameRenderer` itself sets the clock with `FrameRenderer::set_material_clock(now, prev)`, usually
from `regia_render::material_clock(elapsed, delta)`, and reads it with
`FrameRenderer::material_clock`.

## What the clock guarantees

- **Deterministic.** The clock is a function of gameplay time and the frame's delta, computed in
  integer nanoseconds. Two runs that step the same gameplay time (fixed-step captures, replays,
  `loop.set` stepping) write the same clock and draw the same frames.
- **Smooth in long sessions.** Plain `f32` seconds lose resolution as a session grows: after
  9 hours neighboring values are 3.9 ms apart, after 30 days 0.25 s, so wind would move in
  visible steps and its motion vectors would come out wrong. The wrapped clock never passes 3600,
  so it keeps sub-millisecond resolution whatever the session length.
- **Follows gameplay time.** A paused game holds the wind (`delta` 0, no motion blur or TAA
  smear on still leaves); `Time::time_scale` slows it with everything else.
- **The wrap.** Once an hour the clock jumps back to 0. `prev` is measured on the new lap
  (slightly negative), so motion vectors stay right. A sway whose period divides 3600 s loops
  across the wrap without a seam: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15 s and so on, and 0.5, 0.75,
  1.5, 2.5 s. With `sin(time * k)`, the period is 2π / k: pick `k` so it is one of those (for a
  2 s sway, `k` = π).

## Authoring wind

A per-instance sway uses the instance's origin as the phase, so neighbors do not move in step:

```text
"t": Time,
"op": ObjectPosition,
"opx": Swizzle(input: "op", channels: "x"),
"phase": Add("t", "opx"),
"s": Sin("phase"),
"sway": Mul("gust", "s"),
...
output: (world_position_offset: Some("sway")),
shading: (max_vertex_offset: 0.5),
```

Set `shading.max_vertex_offset` to the largest offset the graph can produce. The renderer grows
every culling bound by it: the frustum test on the CPU, the GPU cull's spheres, and the shadow
casters' boxes. An offset larger than the bound can carry a surface out of its bound and get it
culled at a screen edge.

Swaying instances batch like any other mesh: the GPU-driven path draws a field of them in one
instanced draw per mesh and material, with the same pixels as drawing them one by one
(`crates/regia_matgraph/tests/wind_sway.rs`).

## Occlusion culling of instances

On the GPU-driven path, instances that the depth prepass hides are dropped from the color pass by
a Hi-Z test (`gpu_cull.wgsl`). The test is conservative: it bounds each sphere on screen from the
view-projection, reads every pyramid texel under that bound (up to 3×3), and draws anything that
reaches pixels the pyramid's coarser levels do not cover (the last row or column of an odd-sized
level). A visible instance is never dropped, so there are no holes of clear color at a narrow
field of view (a scope), at the bottom or right edge of the screen, or behind a one-pixel gap.

## Check it

- Step the game a few frames (`loop.set`) and call `render.material_clock` after each:
  `prev` of each frame equals `now` of the frame before, and `delta` equals the step.
- Pause gameplay: `now` holds and `delta` is 0.
- Take two screenshots at the same gameplay time in two runs: they match.

<!-- source: book/agents/baked-gi-export.md -->
# Exporting a map's bake input

A map's bake input is a `.bake.ron` description ([Baking GI from meshes](book/agents/baked-gi-bake.md)). You no longer write
it by hand: `regia bake-gi --from-scene <level>` and the agent's `level.export_bake` build it from the level.
A stamp next to it tells you when the level has changed since the export. Design: ADR-310 and ADR-311.

## What the export reads

| From the level | Becomes |
|---|---|
| Every entity with `GiMobility::Static` and a `MeshSource` | One `meshes` entry: `id` = the entity's guid, `source` = the mesh path, `transform` = the world transform (parents included), `layer` = `scatter` if the entity is tagged `scatter`, else `setpiece`. |
| The `Static` mesh entity tagged `terrain` | `terrain_mesh` (`source`, `transform`, `spacing` from `--terrain-spacing`, default 1 m). At most one. |
| `<map>.holes.ron` next to the level (CLI only) | `terrain_mesh.holes`. |
| `LevelSettings.atmosphere` | `sun`, `sky`, `sky_bodies` (below). |
| The first `DirectionalLight` (by guid) | The sun when the atmosphere has no `time_of_day`. |

Skipped and counted in the summary (`skipped`, `skipped_by`, `skipped_entities`):

- `dynamic`: an entity with a mesh and `GiMobility::Dynamic` (or no `GiMobility`: the default is `Dynamic`).
- `no_mesh`: a `Static` entity without a mesh.
- `builtin_mesh`: a `Static` entity whose mesh is a built-in primitive (`builtin:cube`, ...). The bake only reads
  mesh files. Use a glTF instead.

Entities without a mesh that are not `Static` (cameras, groups, lights) are not counted. Prefab instances whose
template is not loaded are not expanded; the CLI summary lists them under `warnings`.

### Lights

- **Sun direction**: `--sun` when given, else the level's sun clock (`atmosphere.time_of_day`), else the
  authored directional light, else no sun. A sun below the horizon is dropped.
- **Sun strength**: on a planet with air, the illuminance and color the atmosphere passes to the ground. When the
  planet is airless, the top-of-atmosphere value (`sun_illuminance_lux` or the preset's). An authored light
  without a clock keeps its own color and illuminance. The sun's angular radius follows the distance its
  illuminance implies (0.00465 rad at 128 klx).
- **Sky**: none when airless. Otherwise one uniform radiance: the atmosphere's cosine-weighted sky radiance, so
  an upward-facing surface gets the same irradiance as under the real sky. The bake does not trace the sky's
  gradient.
- **Sky bodies** (`sky_body`, `moons`): a disc whose radiance times its solid angle is the body's planet-shine
  fill, tinted by its albedo.

Light values are rounded to 5 significant digits so the text is the same on every machine.

### Layout

- With a terrain: the terrain layer, 8 m columns, levels 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 m.
- Without a terrain: one brick over the statics' bounds plus 4 m, at 4 m spacing (coarser if an axis would hold
  more than 64 probes). `--bounds minx,miny,minz,maxx,maxy,maxz` replaces those bounds. The level format has no
  bounds field (scene v10), so the override is a command-line option only.
- Automatic detail bricks over the `setpiece` placements and the interiors: 1 m spacing, 2 m margin, at most
  262,144 probes.

## Command line

```text
regia bake-gi --from-scene <LEVEL> [--from-static-meshes FILE] [--interiors FILE]
                [--project DIR] [--desc FILE] [--terrain-spacing M] [--bounds minx,miny,minz,maxx,maxy,maxz]
                [--sun elevation_deg,azimuth_deg,lux]
                [--check | --bake | --write-level] [--dry-run] [--out FILE]
                [--rays N] [--samples N] [--bounces N] [--seed N] [--probes-per-batch N] [--no-filter]
```

- The project root is the nearest folder above the level with a `Regia.toml`, else the folder above its
  `assets/` (`--project` sets it). Mesh paths are relative to it.
- The description goes to `<project>/bake/<stem>.bake.ron` (`--desc` sets it). `<stem>` is the name of the
  level's `look.baked_gi.volume` up to its first dot, else the level file's. It stays outside `assets/`, so it
  never ships. The stamp is `<stem>.bake.stamp.json` next to it.
- `--sun el,az,lux` replaces the level's sun: degrees above the horizon, degrees clockwise from north (+Z, with
  +X east, as the sun clock uses), top-of-atmosphere lux. It is stored with the stamp's options, so the agent
  uses it too.
- The default writes the description and the stamp only when something changed, then prints one JSON line:

```json
{"ok":true,"desc":"/p/bake/yard.bake.ron","stale":true,"statics":2,"skipped":2,
 "skipped_by":{"dynamic":1,"no_mesh":1},"skipped_entities":[...],"terrain":"assets/meshes/ground.gltf",
 "triangles":24,"bounds":{"min":[-0.5,0.5,-0.5],"max":[5.5,1.5,0.5]},"bounds_override":false,
 "sun_source":"time_of_day","sun":true,"sky":false,"sky_bodies":0,"bundle":null,"hash":"…","warnings":[]}
```

  `stale` is true when this run wrote a new description. `triangles` and `bounds` come from loading each mesh
  through the bake's loader.
- `--check` writes nothing. It prints `{"ok", "check", "desc", "hash", "stale", "reason"}` and exits **0** when the
  description is current, **2** when it is stale, **1** on an error (the same codes as `regia prepare --check`).
  `reason`: `desc_missing`, `stamp_missing`, `inputs_changed`, `desc_changed` (the file was edited by hand).
- `--dry-run` exports in memory, then validates and lays out the description with the bake's own reader. It
  writes nothing and needs no GPU. The line adds `layers` and `plan` as in `regia bake-gi --dry-run`.
- `--bake` bakes right after the export, the same code as `regia bake-gi <file>`, and writes `--out`, else
  `assets/<look.baked_gi.volume>`, else `assets/maps/<stem>.fgiv`. The line adds `volume` and `bake` (the bake
  summary), and the stamp records which input hash the volume was baked from.
- `--write-level` names the volume in the level's `look.baked_gi.volume` and keeps its overrides. The level is
  read and written back through the scene loader and writer, atomically. The file comes back in canonical form:
  its comments are not kept, and an older scene version is saved at the current one. Nothing is written when
  the level already names that volume.

### What makes it stale

The input hash covers the export rules' version, the options (terrain spacing, bounds, bundle, holes), every
exported entity's guid, mesh path, material path, layer and world transform (bit for bit), the content of every
mesh file (and a `.gltf`'s external buffers), the hole mask, the atmosphere settings and the authored sun. Moving
a static entity, editing a mesh or changing the time of day makes the description stale. Renaming the volume
(`--write-level`) does not.

## DO27 bake bundles

`--from-static-meshes <bundle>/static_meshes.json` adds a DO27 bundle, with or without a level. With a level the
map's look comes from the level, and without one there is no sun or sky (a warning says so).

- The bundle folder is the description's `root`. The description names `static_meshes.json`, `interiors.json`
  (next to it, or `--interiors`) and `MANIFEST.sha256` when present. The bake reads them itself: `source`
  glTFs, mirrored transforms with flipped winding, rock hints, skipped generated scatter and interiors
  (see [Baking GI from meshes](book/agents/baked-gi-bake.md)).
- The exporter checks the files it reads first, with the bake's readers: the manifest hash of
  `static_meshes.json` and `interiors.json`, the header (`version`, `units`, `up`, `handedness`) and the required
  entry fields. Errors use the bake's codes and name the field (`static_meshes.json: header.version`).
- The terrain is the `terrain`-layer entry whose source is `terrain.*`, else the first `terrain` entry. Use
  `--terrain-spacing 1.25` for DO27's 1.25 m grid.
- A DO27 map keeps its sun in `map_look.json` (`atmosphere.sun`: elevation, azimuth, lux) in the sim frame. The
  bundle is in Regia Engine's frame (x negated), so pass `--sun <elevation>,<360 - azimuth>,<lux>`.
- Scene meshes are written with absolute paths when a bundle is the root. They lie outside the bundle, so the
  manifest does not check them.
- The summary adds `bundle_entries`, `bundle_placed`, `bundle_skipped`, `bundle_interiors` and
  `bundle_manifest_verified`. With a manifest, the input hash covers the manifest instead of every bundle file.

Export and bake Bore Twelve with the sky body from its level and a sun given on the command line (24° up,
azimuth 175° in Regia Engine's frame, 4.4 klx):

```bash
regia bake-gi --from-scene maps/bore_twelve.level.ron \
    --from-static-meshes <build-dir> \
    --terrain-spacing 1.25 --sun 24,175,4400 --dry-run      # check the layout first
regia bake-gi --from-scene maps/bore_twelve.level.ron \
    --from-static-meshes <build-dir> \
    --terrain-spacing 1.25 --sun 24,175,4400 --bake --write-level
```

## Agent methods

| Method | Params | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `level.export_bake` | `path?` (project-relative, no `..`, ends in `.bake.ron`) | The summary above plus `ok`, `desc`, `stale`. |
| `level.get_baked_gi` | none | Also `bake_input_stale`, `bake_input_hash` and `bake_input: { desc, hash, stale, reason }`. |

- `level.export_bake` exports the running game's open level (its live entities) to `path`, default
  `bake/<volume stem>.bake.ron` under the project root. It needs the `assets` permission. The options of an
  existing stamp at that path (terrain spacing, bounds, a bundle the CLI named) are kept, so the agent and the
  CLI agree on the hash. The agent loads no meshes, so `triangles` and `bounds` are `null`. Without a terrain,
  the description then has no volume brick. Export from the CLI for one.
- `level.get_baked_gi` computes the open level's input hash and compares it with the stamp at the default path.
  It reports `null` when the level names no volume. With no stamp it reports `stale: true` with
  `reason: "stamp_missing"`. When the export itself fails, `reason` is the error code. It reads every mesh file
  to hash it, so call it after an edit, not every frame.

Errors carry `data.reason`:

| `data.reason` | When |
|---|---|
| `export_no_level` | No level is open (no `LevelSettings`). |
| `export_path_invalid` | `path` is absolute, has `..` or `:`, names a Windows reserved device (`NUL`, `CON`, …), does not end in `.bake.ron` or leads out of the project, or the level names no volume and no `path` was given. Also a mesh, material, holes or glTF buffer path the level names outside the project, or a bundle file name that leaves the bundle (`data.entity` names it). |
| `export_mesh_missing` | A static entity's mesh file cannot be read. `data.entity` is `name (guid)`. |
| `export_terrain_ambiguous` | Two static meshes are tagged `terrain`, or the level has one and the bundle names a terrain. |
| `export_no_input` | No static mesh, no terrain and no bundle. |
| `export_read_failed` | A bundle file or the level file cannot be read. |
| `export_write_failed` | The description, the stamp or the level cannot be written. |

The CLI prints the same codes as `{"ok": false, "code", "entity", "message"}` and adds:

| `code` | When |
|---|---|
| `export_path_invalid` | The description would be written inside the bundle (read-only). Give `--desc` or `--project`. Without a level, the project defaults to the working directory. Also: the level's `look.baked_gi.volume` is absolute, has `..` or a drive prefix, or leads out of `assets/` through a symlink (ADR-1816; `--out` may name any path). |
| `export_level_parse` | The level does not load, or a rewritten level does not load back. |
| `export_mesh_load` | A mesh does not load through the bake's loader (bounds). |
| `export_bake_failed` | `--bake` failed (no GPU, a trace error, the volume could not be written). |
| `bake_*` | A bundle check failed: `bake_desc_invalid`, `bake_desc_parse`, `bake_manifest_mismatch`, `bake_manifest_missing_entry`, `bake_source_missing` ([Baking GI from meshes](book/agents/baked-gi-bake.md)). |

## Workflow

1. Tag the map's set pieces, rocks and terrain `GiMobility::Static` and give the terrain the `terrain` tag.
2. `regia bake-gi --from-scene maps/x.level.ron --dry-run` and read `statics`, `skipped_entities` and the
   brick plan.
3. `regia bake-gi --from-scene maps/x.level.ron --bake --write-level`.
4. In CI or before a release: `regia bake-gi --from-scene maps/x.level.ron --check` fails with exit 2 when the
   map changed since its bake input was exported.
5. In a running game: `level.get_baked_gi` → `bake_input_stale`; `level.export_bake` to refresh the description.

<!-- source: book/agents/baked-gi-bake-check.md -->
# Checking a bake end to end

A baked GI volume passes through five tools before it lights a frame: the level, its exported `.bake.ron`
([Exporting a map's bake input](book/agents/baked-gi-export.md)), the bake ([Baking GI from meshes](book/agents/baked-gi-bake.md)), the
level naming the volume, and the runtime install ([Baked GI from the level](book/agents/baked-gi-maps.md)). This page covers
the tools that check that chain without a GPU: the CPU bake (`--cpu`), reading a volume back (`--sample`), and
`cargo xtask bake-check`, which runs the whole chain on a fixture project. Design: ADR-365.

## Bake on the CPU

```text
regia bake-gi <scene> --cpu [--rays N] [--samples N] [--bounces N] [--out FILE]
regia bake-gi --from-scene <level> --bake --cpu [--write-level]
```

`--cpu` traces the probes on the CPU probe tracer instead of the GPU path tracer. Everything else is the same
bake: relocation, validity, the 3×3×3 filter and the `.fgiv` encode. The summary gains `"backend": "cpu"`, and
`device` reads `cpu (N threads)`.

Use it for checks, CI and small scenes (thousands of probes, thousands of triangles). Bake maps on the GPU. The
CPU tracer:

- traces the same ray sets and folds them the same way (L1 SH per component, distance moments);
- refuses a description that sets `clamp_direct`, `clamp_indirect`, `firefly_threshold` or `sample_groups` above 1
  (the quality controls are GPU-only; the bake fails instead of returning an unclamped mean with no noise
  estimate), and caps `samples × rays_per_probe` at 2^24 as the GPU does;
- treats every surface as diffuse (base color × (1 − metallic)) and samples no textures;
- takes a uniform sky or none (`bake_desc` descriptions always give one). A sky table, an equirect
  map or a cloud field is refused with a message (bake those on the GPU);
- refuses a heightfield whose sample count, spacing or origin the GPU packer would refuse, with the
  same message, instead of baking a scene with no ground;
- lights vertices with the sun and with each sky body as a direction. Emitters light the volume when bounce rays
  hit them;
- does not apply `clamp_direct`, `clamp_indirect`, `sample_groups` or `firefly_threshold` (ADR-1096 is the GPU
  kernels). The summary still prints those fields from the file. The volume is the uncapped trace, and each
  probe's `clamped`, `clamp_loss`, `suppressed_groups`, `firefly_loss` and `noise` stay at their defaults;
- does not cap `samples` so that `samples × rays_per_probe` stays within 2^24 (the GPU tracer does, because its
  ray counter is an f32). `rays_per_probe` above 4096 is traced as 4096, the same as the GPU;
- ends a path at a back face, so a probe inside geometry sees nothing.

Its result does not depend on the thread count. It agrees with a GPU bake in expectation, not bit for bit.

## Read a volume back

```text
regia bake-gi --sample <volume.fgiv> --at x,y,z [--at x,y,z ...] [--normal x,y,z]
```

This prints the irradiance the runtime lights each point with. The lookup is the renderer's CPU mirror of the
shader (`regia_render::sample_static_gi`), with the default lookup settings and every component at its baked
light. The viewer is taken along the normal (default `0,1,0`). It needs no GPU and no running game.

```json
{"ok": true, "volume": "assets/maps/courtyard.fgiv", "probes": 1924, "valid": 1924, "bricks": 3,
 "interior_bricks": 0, "terrain": false,
 "baked": {"sun_illuminance": 98213.0, "sun_direction": [0.0, 0.96, -0.28], "sky_scale": 3891.2, "fill_lux": 0.0},
 "samples": [
   {"at": [14.8, 0.0, 0.0], "normal": [0.0, 1.0, 0.0], "irradiance": [10521.4, 12088.7, 15110.2],
    "components": {"sun_bounce": [3.1, 3.4, 3.9], "sky": [10518.3, 12085.3, 15106.3], "fill": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
                   "emissive": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]},
    "coverage": 1.0}]}
```

The numbers above only show the shape.

- `irradiance` and every `components` entry are in lux (irradiance, not irradiance / π), per channel.
- `coverage` is 0 outside the volume and 1 well inside it. With every corner probe rejected it is 0 as well.
- A point inside an INTERIOR brick reads only that brick.

Errors print `{"ok": false, "code", "message"}` and exit non-zero:

| `code` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `volume_not_found` | No file at the path. |
| `volume_unreadable` | Not a `.fgiv`, another format version, damaged, or unreadable. |
| `sample_normal_invalid` | `--normal` is the zero vector. |

A malformed `--at` or `--normal` is a usage error (exit 2, before anything runs).

## The whole chain: `cargo xtask bake-check`

```text
cargo xtask bake-check [--gpu] [--release] [--keep] [--rays N] [--samples N]
```

It copies the fixture project `crates/regia_cli/tests/fixtures/bake_e2e` to a new temporary directory. Then it
runs each step through the real `regia` binary (`cargo run -p regia_cli`) and prints one line per step:

1. `bake-gi --from-scene assets/levels/courtyard.level.ron --bake --cpu --write-level`: two static entities
   export (the dynamic one is skipped). The bake writes `assets/maps/courtyard.fgiv`, and the level now names
   `maps/courtyard.fgiv`.
2. `bake-gi --from-scene … --check` exits 0 (the input is current).
3. `bake-gi --sample` at the open cell (14.8, 0, 0) and at the sealed room's centre (0, 0, 0):
   - the open cell's sky component is 0.94 to 1.02 of π × the exported sky radiance;
   - the room's centre is exactly 0.
4. The level opens in a headless app. `BakedGiLevelPlugin` installs the volume through the asset server, and the
   lookup on the installed volume must equal step 3's.
5. Moving a static entity makes `--check` exit 2 (stale).

The last line is a JSON summary:
- `backend`, `device`, the bake `report`, the exported `sky`;
- the open cell's `irradiance`, `sky` and `sky_ratio`;
- the sealed cell's `irradiance`.

The exit code is 0 when every step passes. A failed step prints `FAIL` lines and a JSON line with the step's
name.

- `--gpu` bakes on the GPU path tracer against the same expectations: the GPU vs CPU check. It needs a GPU
  (lavapipe works).
- `--keep` keeps the temporary project and prints its path, so you can inspect it with `--sample`, or by opening
  the level.
- `cargo test -p regia_cli --test bake_e2e` runs the same chain as a test. It needs no GPU.

## The fixture

`assets/levels/courtyard.level.ron` (scene v10) holds:
- `Room` at the origin: a sealed room with 0.3 m walls (inner box ±2.5 m facing in, outer box ±2.8 m facing out);
- `Marker`: a 0.2-scale static copy 24 m east;
- `Rover`: a 0.2-scale `GiMobility::Dynamic` copy.

The sky is Earth's at noon (day 172, 40° N), and there is no ground. The two cells have exact expectations:
- The open cell sees the uniform sky in every direction except where the rooms are. The rooms hide about 3 %, and
  their walls bounce back a quarter of it.
- No light reaches the room's inside. The lookup corners there, and every neighbor the filter mixes into them,
  are inside probes.

The export's volume brick (4 m) and the automatic bricks (1 m, one per room) place no probe inside a wall.

## Interiors reach the volume

The bake now writes the INTERIOR flag into the `.fgiv` (`.fgiv` v2 brick flags). The bake plan's `interior_flag`
decides which bricks get it: a brick inside an interior that is not `sky_open`. `--sample`'s `interior_bricks`
and `render.get_gi_mode`'s `interior_bricks` count them. A description without interiors bakes the same bytes
as before.

<!-- source: book/agents/baked-gi-incremental.md -->
# Incremental GI bakes

A map bake traces every probe. After an edit (a moved crate, a new wall, a raised hill), most probes see nothing
new. `--incremental` keeps a state file between bakes. The next bake traces only the probes near what changed and
reuses the rest from the state. Design: ADR-1094.

## Bake incrementally

```text
regia bake-gi <scene> --incremental <state> [--influence METERS] [--tile-columns N] [--cpu] [--out FILE]
regia bake-gi --from-scene <level> --bake --incremental <state> [--write-level]
```

`<state>` is a file path. The first bake finds no state, traces everything and writes the state there. Each later
bake reads it, traces what changed, writes the volume, and writes the new state back. The state is a build cache,
not content: keep it out of `assets/` (for example `bake/state/<map>.fgis`). Deleting it only makes the next bake
a full one.

The bake splits the volume into cells:

- one cell per detail brick;
- one cell per tile of `N × N` terrain-layer columns (`--tile-columns`, default 8).

A cell is traced again when:

- **`layout`**: the state has no cell with the same probes. It is a new or moved brick, or a terrain tile whose
  ground changed. Adding or removing a brick does not touch the others, even though their probe indices move.
- **`scene`**: something within the influence margin of the cell changed. That covers a placed mesh's geometry,
  material, textures or transform, a local light, or a heightfield sample. The margin defaults to the layout's
  `max_distance` and is set with `--influence`.
- **`state`**: the stored cell does not fit the layout (a damaged state).

Every cell is traced again (`full`) when there is no state, or when something that lights every probe changed:

| `full` | What changed |
|---|---|
| `no_state` | The state file does not exist yet. |
| `state_unreadable` | The state file is damaged, truncated or from another version (warning `bake_state_unreadable`). |
| `tracer` | Regia Engine version, `--cpu` or GPU, or the GPU and its driver. |
| `settings` | Rays, samples, bounces, seed, relocation, filter, moment resolution, distance clamp, or `--influence`. The batching (`--probes-per-batch`, samples per GPU submission) is not compared. |
| `sky` | The sun, the sky, sky bodies, stars or media. |
| `terrain` | The heightfield's size, spacing or material, or the terrain view albedo. |
| `camera` | The description's camera (texture detail fades with the distance to it). |

The volume is rebuilt from all probes. The 3×3×3 filter and the encode run over the whole volume, so:

- a rebake of an unchanged scene traces nothing and writes the same bytes;
- a reused cell's probes are the previous bake's, bit for bit;
- an incremental bake with no state is the normal bake, bit for bit.

### What is approximate

An edit farther than the margin from a cell does not rebake that cell, so the cell keeps the old scene's light.
The summary says so with `"approximate": true`, which means cells were reused although the scene changed
somewhere. A cell that is traced again gets other random noise than in a full bake. It matches a full bake in
expectation, not bit for bit. For a volume you ship, run one bake without a state, or delete the state first.

## The summary

The summary is the normal bake summary ([Baking GI from meshes](book/agents/baked-gi-bake.md)) with three more keys:

```json
{"ok": true, "out": "assets/maps/courtyard.fgiv", "report": {"probes": 1924, "valid": 1924},
 "incremental": {"full": null, "cells": 12, "cells_reused": 11, "cells_baked": 1,
                 "probes_reused": 1860, "probes_baked": 64, "scene_changed": true, "approximate": true,
                 "influence_margin": 32.0,
                 "baked": [{"cell": {"brick": 3}, "probes": 64, "reason": "scene"}]},
 "state": {"path": "bake/state/courtyard.fgis", "written": true, "bytes": 512344},
 "warnings": []}
```

The numbers above only show the shape.

- `incremental.baked` lists the traced cells and why (`layout`, `scene`, `state`). It is empty when `full` is set.
  A cell is `{"brick": index}` or `{"terrain": [i, j]}` (tile column `i` along X, row `j` along Z).
- `state.written` is false when the state could not be written (warning `bake_state_write_failed`). The volume is
  written anyway, and the next bake traces everything.

## Plan without tracing

```text
regia bake-gi <scene> --incremental <state> --plan-incremental [--cpu]
```

This prints which cells a bake would reuse and trace, and why. It traces nothing and writes nothing. It returns
`{"ok": true, "plan_incremental": true, "state": {"path", "exists"}, "incremental": {...}, "warnings", "layers"}`.
With `--cpu` it needs no GPU. Without it, the GPU adapter is opened to compare the device, but nothing is traced. It
does not combine with `--from-scene --bake`: export first, then plan on the exported `.bake.ron`.

Use it before a long bake to see how much will be traced. Use it after an edit to check that the edit reaches the
cells you expect.

## Errors and warnings

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `bake_incremental_invalid` | In the error message when the options are built in code with a negative or non-finite margin or 0 columns per tile. On the command line, `--influence` (a finite distance, 0 or more) and `--tile-columns` (1 or more) are checked by the parser first: a usage error, exit 2. |
| `bake_state_unreadable` | Warning: the state could not be read or used. Every cell is traced and a new state is written. |
| `bake_state_write_failed` | Warning: the volume is written but the state is not. The next bake is a full one. |

`--incremental` does not combine with `--dry-run`, `--sample`, `--check-volume` or `--from-scene --check`. With
`--from-scene` it needs `--bake`: an export alone reads no state. `--check-volume` passes on an
incremental bake's volume. It compares the recorded scene hash, layout, lights and settings, and an incremental
bake records them like a full bake.

## Library

`regia_pt::bake_incremental`: `bake_cells`, `cell_scene_hashes`, `global_hashes`, `plan_incremental`,
`bake_gi_volume_incremental`, `BakeState` (`read`, `write`, `to_bytes`, `from_bytes`). The trace and the finish of a
bake are split into `regia_pt::probe::bake_probes` (any subset of probes) and `regia_pt::probe::finish_bake`.

<!-- source: book/agents/baked-gi-leak-control.md -->
# Baked GI leak control

A baked GI volume (`.fgiv`, [Baked GI volumes](book/agents/baked-gi.md)) stores light at probes on a grid, and the
runtime interpolates between them. Where a wall stands between two probes, the light of one side must not
reach the other. This page covers what the bake and the lookup do about it (ADR-366, on top of ADR-206,
ADR-279 and ADR-281) and how an agent checks it.

## What keeps light where it belongs

- **Probes inside geometry** are moved out by relocation or marked invalid (`INSIDE_GEOMETRY`), and probes
  under the terrain are invalid (`UNDER_TERRAIN`). The lookup skips invalid probes.
- **Walls between probes.** After the trace, `regia bake-gi` tests the straight segment between every pair of
  neighboring probes against the map's meshes and terrain. Where a segment crosses geometry:
  - the 3×3×3 smoothing filter does not average the two probes;
  - the probe at the low end stores where the wall is on the segment (a 4-bit code per axis in its flags).
  At runtime, a lookup cell whose corners carry such a code uses only the corners on the receiver's side of
  the wall. A doorway leaves some segments open, so the two sides stay joined there and light comes in through
  the door only.
- **Interiors.** A brick inside a DO27 interior that is not `sky_open` (the hangar, the hab) is written with the
  INTERIOR flag: inside it the terrain layer's outdoor light is skipped (ADR-281). The borehole shaft is
  `sky_open` and gets sky from above. An interior with `openings` is INTERIOR as a whole in v0.2.0.
- **Sealed rooms see no sky** in the trace itself: their rays hit the walls.

The distance moments of each probe still weight the corners as before. The wall test covers the case they miss:
a coarse moment map averages a thin wall with the open space beside it.

## Checking a bake

`regia bake-gi <map>.bake.ron` prints a summary whose `report` holds:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `wall_pairs_tested` | Neighbor segments tested (0 when the wall test is off). |
| `wall_pairs_blocked` | Segments that cross geometry; the filter skips them. |
| `wall_probes` | Probes whose flags carry a wall code. |
| `interior_bricks` | Bricks written with the INTERIOR flag. |
| `interior_sky_probes` | Valid probes inside INTERIOR bricks that saw the sky (more than 1 % of their rays escaped). Probes on a brick's faces do not count: they may stand outside the walls. A sealed room reports 0; a room with an opening reports the probes that see out of it. A sealed room with a non-zero count has a hole in its walls. |

The bake reports a `walls` progress stage between the trace and the encoding.

Checks an agent can make after a bake:

1. `report.interior_bricks` equals the number of `plan.bricks` with `interior_flag: true`.
2. `report.wall_probes > 0` on any map with set pieces (a map of terrain only may report 0).
3. For each sealed interior, `report.interior_sky_probes == 0`. If not, look for a gap in the walls.

## Checking the installed volume

`render.get_gi_mode` returns `baked.wall_probes`: the installed volume's probes with a wall code. It is 0 for a
volume baked before the wall test (v0.1.27 and older bakes): those still load and look up exactly as before, but
without wall control. Rebake to get it.

Screenshots for a look check: one inside each interior near a wall, one outside along the same wall, with
`render.set_gi_mode {mode: "baked"}`, then with `{mode: "balanced"}` for comparison.

## Limits

- One wall position per segment: two partitions inside one cell read as one wall at their middle.
- The wall test sees triangles and the terrain. Glass blocks like a wall; alpha-tested foliage counts as solid.
- No light passes through an opening of an INTERIOR brick (the brick ignores the outdoor layer as a whole).
- A segment that runs to a probe under the floor or inside geometry crosses that surface, not a wall, so its code
  says little about where the wall is. The ADR-861 leak guard (`BakedGiSettings::leak_guard`, on by default)
  ignores such codes when it places the wall. `render.sample_baked_gi` shows the lookup at a point with the guard
  on and off. See [Baked GI quality](book/agents/baked-gi-quality.md).

<!-- source: book/agents/gi-validation.md -->
# GI validation

Every real-time diffuse GI technique is scored against the reference path tracer (`regia_pt`) on three
standard scenes, and a test fails when a technique's error grows past the value recorded for it (ADR-423,
`docs/specs/27-renderer-excellence.md` § 2.2). This page says what is measured, how to read the table, how to
re-record after an intended change, and how an agent gets the same numbers on a live frame.

## The scenes

`regia_test_utils::gi_scenes`, 160 × 96, opaque rough dielectrics under the sun and a uniform sky (`ibl` off;
`ambient_lux` is the sky's illuminance, which the tracer traces as a uniform sky of radiance `ambient_lux / π`):

| Scene | What it tests |
|---|---|
| `trench` | A sunlit orange wall bounces onto a floor in the other wall's shadow (outdoor bounce). |
| `color_room` | A room open at the front with red and green walls. The sun comes in through the opening; the ceiling and back corners get indirect light only (color bleeding, multi-bounce). |
| `sealed_box` | The § 2.2 leak case: a closed box under the sun and the sky, camera inside. The reference is black, so any light inside is a leak. Its numbers are relative to the lit exterior ground's luminance, which makes them leak fractions. |

## The techniques

| Row | Frame |
|---|---|
| `direct` | The direct-only frame (sun and its shadows, nothing else) against the tracer's `direct` AOV. This is the plumbing floor: if it is off, every GI row is off too. |
| `ambient` | The flat sky term with AO. This is the balanced look in a lab scene. |
| `ssgi` | Screen-space GI. |
| `probes` | GPU-traced irradiance probes after 64 frames (hysteresis 0.9: a bounce chain settles by about 64; `sweep_the_gather` reads the colour room at 1.033 of the tracer's energy at 32 frames and 1.062 at 64). |
| `probes_ssgi` | Probes and screen-space GI together (the Desktop High default). |
| `baked` | A volume baked by `regia_pt::probe` from the same scene, rendered with Desktop High settings and the bake installed. |

The reference is the tracer's `indirect_diffuse + indirect_specular`: everything after the first hit, the sky
included. A frame's indirect light is its linear HDR minus the direct-only frame, kept signed, so over-darkening
counts as error too.

## The numbers

These are measured over the pixels that see a surface, away from silhouettes:

- **Rel. RMSE**: per-channel RMSE divided by the mean reference luminance.
- **Shadow bias**: (test − reference) mean luminance in sun shadow, divided by the reference's. Negative means the
  technique is too dark where only indirect light reaches. Spec 27 § 2.0's "GI in sun shadow" ratio is 1 + bias.
- **Energy ratio**: total test luminance over total reference luminance. Above 1, the technique adds light;
  below 1, it loses light.
- **FLIP**: mean FLIP on both planes through the runtime's display transform at the scene's exposure, and the 95th
  percentile of the same map (`flip_p95`). The § 2.2 targets are mean ≤ 0.08 and p95 ≤ 0.20 (ADR-2951); for
  `sealed_box` the target is a leak ≤ 0.5 %. All are printed per scene and technique as met or not met, not
  asserted. The spec 27 suite harvests the `probes_ssgi` rows (`<scene> / probes_ssgi: FLIP`, `p95 FLIP`,
  `leak`) into its GI (diffuse) rows.

## Running, reading, re-recording

```sh
cargo test -p regia_pt --test gi_validation -- --nocapture          # check against the records
REGIA_GI_TABLE=/tmp/gi cargo test -p regia_pt --test gi_validation  # also write <scene>.md and <scene>.png
REGIA_GI_RECORD=1 cargo test -p regia_pt --test gi_validation       # write the records (lavapipe only)
```

- The records are plain text in `crates/regia_test_utils/gi_thresholds/<scene>.txt`. Each line holds `scene
  technique rel_rmse shadow_bias energy_ratio`, with `-` for a value the scene has none of.
- A check fails when one of these grows past `record · (1 + r) + a`:
  - relative RMSE;
  - the shadow bias's distance from 0;
  - the energy ratio's distance from 1.

  On lavapipe, r = 10 % and a = 0.02. On a hardware GPU, r = 50 % and a = 0.10, because the records are taken on
  lavapipe.
- A missing record fails the check. A clearly better result is printed with "re-record to tighten it".
- The real-GPU non-golden pass (`REGIA_SKIP_GOLDENS=1` on a hardware GPU) prints regressions instead of
  failing, the same way it skips the lavapipe-blessed goldens.
- Record only on lavapipe (the test refuses other adapters), and only for an intended change. Say why in the
  commit message, as for a re-blessed golden. Never re-record to make a regression pass.
- `<scene>.png` puts the reference and every technique side by side, in table order, at the scene's exposure
  plus 2 EV.

## On a live frame (agents)

The same comparison on whatever a running app draws uses the existing methods
([Renderer excellence](book/agents/renderer-excellence.md), "Scoring GI"):

```json
seeing.reference_trace { "scene": "current", "width": 640, "height": 360, "spp": 1024 }
seeing.reference_trace { "job": 1, "wait": true }
seeing.compare { "a": { "job": 1 }, "b": "/tmp/frame_indirect.exr", "aov": "indirect_diffuse", "ev100": 12.5 }
```

Here `b` is the frame's indirect light: its HDR capture minus the same frame with every indirect term off.
`lookdev`'s `pt_plates` writes that for the DO27 parity plates. `seeing.compare` reports FLIP mean and p95
(`flip_mean`, `flip_p95`), RMSE and `rel_rmse` over the whole image. The shadow bias and energy ratio above are
test-side numbers: run the test, or mask the two EXRs yourself. There is no separate agent method for the table,
and this page adds no error codes.

## Attribution (lane sprint-gi-leak-plates-p95, ADR-3701)

When a GI plate row misses its § 2.2 target, `crates/regia_pt/tests/gi_attribution.rs` attributes the miss to a
term. One renderer settles the probes once at the baseline row's quality (64 frames); each row then flips one
`FrameQuality` field (or one renderer switch) at that settled state and reads the same number of frames, so the
probe hysteresis, the SSGI temporal state and the static-screen cache start every row identical — a fresh renderer
per row would leave each row's state at a different age, which is the confound that made the gather's sign flip
across renderers. Every row is scored against the path tracer with the same masks and direct floor as
`gi_validation`:

```sh
REGIA_GI_TABLE=/tmp/gi cargo test -p regia_pt --test gi_attribution -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1
```

Rows: `probes_ssgi` (the Desktop High default), `probes` (the screen gather off), `ssgi` (the probes off),
`probes_ssgi_no_ao` (SSAO off), `probes_ssgi_no_reuse` (the static-screen cache off, `paged_sun_shadows` off) and
`probes_ssgi_cache` (the radiance cache on, hits only). The sealed-box variant prints the leak with the
static-screen cache on and off (`sealed_box_leak_with_and_without_the_static_screen_cache`). Both tests are
measurements (`--ignored`): they assert only what the attribution itself proves (every probe row beats the flat
sky term; a switch-off row that moves the score by more than 0.05 FLIP fails as an attribution change).

**Settled reading (re-measured 2026-11-10, lane sprint-fixrev-24-k, ADR-5455; supersedes the 2026-11-07 paragraph,
which read rows built on separate renderers).** One renderer settles the probes once; each row toggles one term at
that state, so the settled rows are directly comparable (FLIP, energy):

| row | trench | colour room |
|---|---|---|
| `probes_ssgi` (held cache, the default) | 0.112 (0.947) | 0.109 (0.986) |
| `probes` | 0.112 (0.961) | 0.139 (1.064) |
| `probes_ssgi_no_ao` | 0.104 (0.980) | 0.156 (1.121) |
| `probes_ssgi_no_reuse` (settled) | 0.113 (0.967) | 0.144 (1.093) |
| `probes_ssgi_cache` | 0.118 (0.955) | 0.144 (1.077) |

The probes carry the plates: `probes` alone scores trench 0.112 and colour room 0.139, and every other row stands
on them. The screen gather at the settled frame does **not** correct the colour room (0.139 → 0.144, energy
+0.029) and leaves the trench alone (+0.001). The 0.109 a held view reports is the early gather the static-screen
cache keeps — a cache artifact, not a gather correction. SSAO is scene-dependent: it helps the colour room
(0.156 off → 0.144 on) and hurts the trench (0.104 off → 0.113 on, within cross-renderer noise). The radiance cache
ties the settled plain gather. The residual miss is the probes' own irradiance error (DDGI, job 1010).

## Acceptance table (v0.5 J06, ADR-4948)

`crates/regia_pt/tests/gi_acceptance.rs` turns the dynamic GI acceptance into one numbered table on any adapter:
metric, `specs/27` bar, measured value, verdict (`pass`, `FAIL`, `report` for rows without a bar) and the likely
cause of a miss. It adds three interiors to the standard plates: `door_room` (a 6 × 3 × 6 m room the sun enters
through a door), `tunnel` (open at both ends) and `shaft` (8 m deep under an open top), and scores each at four
probe configurations: `fine` (the plate's own layout), `fine_held` (the same with the static-screen cache on, the
held view a standing player sees), and the shipped `low` and `high` tier layouts, settled with the cache off.

```sh
# lavapipe (set VK_ICD_FILENAMES to lvp_icd.json) or a card (REGIA_GPU_UUID=<uuid> REGIA_GPU_STRICT=1)
REGIA_GI_ACCEPT_OUT=/path/out cargo test -p regia_pt --test gi_acceptance -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1
# one part: acceptance_scenes | energy_decomposition | tier_leak | stability_split | tier_cost | owner_plates
# attribution: layout_sweep | ground_sweep | ground_thickness_sweep | sun_elevation_sweep | ray_census
# by term (ADR-5290): error_attribution | reference_depth
REGIA_GI_PLATE_SCALE=6 REGIA_GI_ACCEPT_OUT=/path/out cargo test -p regia_pt --test gi_acceptance -- --ignored --nocapture owner_plates
```

Filters for slow adapters: `REGIA_GI_SCENES=trench,door_room`, `REGIA_GI_CONFIGS=fine,high`,
`REGIA_GI_TIER_FRAMES=96` (default 192; fewer frames leave the tiers' 0.97 hysteresis short of settled, so the
table states the count). `tier_cost` holds the `specs/79` § 7 bars only on the adapters they name (RX 7900 and
RTX 5080 for High at 1440p, the Deck for Low at 800p); every other card reports its numbers without a verdict.

Reading it: a FLIP miss with energy near 1 is spatial error (probe spacing, screen-gather noise); energy under 0.95
is a probe deficit, which `energy_decomposition` splits by light (sun only, sky only) and by the tracer's bounce
depth (1, 2, 6). A stability miss counts against GI only when the no-GI control frame passes. `tier_leak` reads the sealed box at
96 to 1536 frames per tier, at every-probe-each-frame, at the shipped update divisor and kept awake (a negligible sun
nudge each frame that stops the renderer's 600-frame probe freeze), so a frozen field is told from a converged one.
`ground_thickness_sweep` and `sun_elevation_sweep` tell a sun-bounce deficit that comes from the probe trace's own
hit self-shadowing (it follows the floor's brick epsilon) from one that comes from the probe layout. These are
measurements (`--ignored`); the regression gates stay `gi_validation`'s records, `gi_radiance_cache` and
`regia_render`'s `dynamic_gi`. There is no agent method for the table and this section adds no error codes; on a
live frame use `seeing.compare` as above.

### After the J06 fix (ADR-5001)

The probe freeze now counts 512 updates of a finest probe (4096 frames on High), so `tier_leak` reads to 4160 frames
and its `high_shipped` / `low_shipped` rows run past their own freeze. The probes' sun shadow ray no longer shadows
its own floor, and High and Ultra space their finest probes 1 m apart with the ADR-2605 options; the `high_2m`
config and `tier_leak`'s "2 m layout (before ADR-5001)" rows keep the old High layout as the control. The two
`target_` tests are green on the RTX 5080 and 5090. Still missing the § 2.2 mean-FLIP bar on every plate: the door
room reads about 1.3 × the tracer on High, the tunnel about 0.86 ×.

### The reference's depth and the error by term (ADR-5290)

The acceptance reference traces 32 bounces (`REFERENCE_BOUNCES`): the probes carry every bounce, and at 6 the tracer
missed 9.8 % of the door room's converged indirect light, so the probes read over it. `reference_depth` prints each
scene's indirect energy at 12 and 32 bounces over 6 and the fine and High scores against both. `error_attribution`
changes one term at a time (SSAO, the screen-space pass, the exact lookup instead of the ambient cube, a 16-frame
mean) and prints the tracer's own noise (a second seed): on an RTX 5090 every term moves a scene's mean FLIP by
0.015 or less and the tracer's noise is 0.03–0.06, so what is left is the probe irradiance itself.

### Terms by frame size, reference and light (ADR-5374)

`term_table` prints one row per scene, light and probe layout: mean and p95 FLIP, energy, GI in sun shadow over the
tracer's, and both mean luminances. `REGIA_GI_LIGHTS=both,sun,sky` splits a row by light, `REGIA_GI_SCALE=4` scores
640 × 384 frames instead of 160 × 96, `REGIA_GI_REF_SPP=8192` raises the reference's samples, and `REGIA_GI_NOISE=1`
adds the reference's own floor (a second seed against the first: 0.03–0.06 at 1024 spp, 0.015–0.029 at 8192).
`REGIA_GI_SCENES` and `REGIA_GI_CONFIGS` select as in `acceptance_scenes`. It measures (`--ignored`), it has no agent
method and adds no error codes.

```sh
REGIA_GI_ACCEPT_OUT=out REGIA_GI_CONFIGS=fine,high REGIA_GI_LIGHTS=both,sun,sky \
  cargo test -p regia_pt --test gi_acceptance -- --ignored --nocapture --exact term_table
```

Since ADR-5374 every tier weights the probes at the surface point (the bias only moves the visibility test) and
holds each axis's exact lobe in the irradiance texels next to it; both ride `DdgiSettings::visibility_blend`. Probe
rays continue past their cascade's mesh reach on every layout. The plates' own layouts keep the default lookup, so the
`fine_surface` configuration scores each plate's layout with the tiers' lookup. On an RTX 5080 Desktop High reads
door room 0.080, trench 0.098, color room 0.140, tunnel 0.150 and shaft 0.154 (1024 spp); the door room meets the
0.08 bar against an 8192-spp reference (0.073). What is left is listed in the ADR: walls between probe planes, the
brick march's hit band at openings, the shaft over the finest window, and the Low tier's 2 m probes across a doorway.

### Update noise and per-row images (ADR-5457)

`term_table` also prints each row's frame-to-frame FLIP while every probe updates (the stability bar, 0.01), and
with `REGIA_GI_DUMP=1` writes one PNG strip per row into `REGIA_GI_ACCEPT_OUT`
(`<scene>_<light>_<config>.png`): the tracer's indirect light, the probes', their signed luminance ratio (white
equal, blue darker, red brighter, full color at a factor of √2) and the FLIP map. `REGIA_GI_SCALE=3` makes the
strips large enough to read. `material_model` scores the probes against a Lambertian reference and the material
one (the tracer with every material Lambertian reads the tunnel 0.947 and the shaft 0.972 times the material
tracer, the door room 1.024: the probes' ray hits are Lambertian). `high_head47` is Desktop High with 4.7 m of the
finest cascade over the eye. They measure (`--ignored`), have no agent method and add no error codes.

```sh
REGIA_GI_ACCEPT_OUT=out REGIA_GI_CONFIGS=high REGIA_GI_DUMP=1 REGIA_GI_SCALE=3 \
  cargo test -p regia_pt --test gi_acceptance -- --ignored --nocapture --exact term_table
```

Since ADR-5457 a tier's probes also hold the irradiance at the surface behind them, and the probes' update noise is
lower on every layout (a second short filter on the shading copy).
On an RTX 5090 Desktop High reads door room 0.076, trench 0.098, tunnel 0.097, shaft 0.102 and color room 0.111
(1024 spp), with frame-to-frame FLIP at 0.0073 or less. What is left is listed in the ADR: creases inside a probe
cell, the first metre inside an opening, the probes' Lambertian hits, and the Low tier's 2 m probes across a
doorway.

### One lookup, lightness blending, material hits (ADR-5506)

Since ADR-5506 every layout has the tiers' lookup (the `fine` and `fine_surface` configurations differ only by
the blend between cascades), the probes are blended as cube roots, and a probe ray's hit reflects as the forward
pass's dielectric, at the point where the ray crosses the surface. On an RTX 5080 Desktop High reads trench 0.070,
tunnel 0.075, door room 0.066, shaft 0.088 and color room 0.092 (1024 spp), the Low door room 0.259; the plates'
own layouts read trench 0.062, door room 0.070, shaft 0.078, color room 0.079 and tunnel 0.104. What is left is
listed in the ADR: creases inside a probe cell (the color room's and the shaft's p95), the shaft's and the
tunnel's energy, the Low tier's doorway.

### Crease texels (ADR-5552)

Since ADR-5552 a probe holds the light at the crease points of its faces and the lookups scale a face toward its
creases. On an RTX 5080 Desktop High reads shaft 0.0794 (p95 0.194), tunnel 0.0699, trench 0.0705, door room
0.0668 and color room 0.0911 (p95 0.195; 1024 spp): every p95 is under 0.20 and every mean but the color room's
under 0.08. The Low tier reads door room 0.240 (0.259 before), color room 0.181, trench 0.087, shaft 0.169 and
tunnel 0.100. To see where a row's error lies, run `term_table` with `REGIA_GI_DUMP=1 REGIA_GI_SCALE=3`: the
third panel of each strip is the signed ratio (red: the probes brighter, blue: darker, full color at a factor of
√2). What is left is listed in the ADR: a sun edge between two probe columns in the color room, the shaft's
walls' level, the tunnel's inside.

<!-- source: book/agents/baked-gi-quality.md -->
# Baked GI quality

The baked GI lookup (`regia_render::baked_gi`, `shaders/baked_gi.wgsl`) has three quality switches on
`BakedGiSettings` (ADR-861). All three are on by default, and each can be turned off on its own to compare:

| Switch | What it does | Where it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `deringing` | Some probes see light from a narrow solid angle: a window, a sunlit patch, an emitter, a sky body. There the L1 irradiance is evaluated as a non-negative lobe with the same mean and first moment over the sphere. The old evaluation was the linear form clamped at 0, which reads light beside and behind the source and adds energy through the clamp. Light as smooth as a hemisphere (the sky, the ground) evaluates exactly as before. | Surfaces beside or facing away from a small bright source. |
| `leak_guard` | Refines the ADR-366 wall split in a lookup cell with wall codes. An edge with a rejected probe at either end (under the floor, inside geometry) joins nothing, and its code does not move the wall's position: that segment crossed the floor or the solid, not the wall. Where every wall along an axis sits on such edges, the wall's position is unknown, and a receiver whose normal points along the axis takes the side its normal faces. | Inner walls and floors of rooms whose probe grid has a layer under the floor. |
| `sun_relight` | The sun-bounce component of a probe lit from below follows the sun's elevation: sun light bounced off level ground scales with `sin h`. The factor is `(max(sin h_now, 0) + 0.02) / (max(sin h_baked, 0) + 0.02)`. A probe takes it in proportion to how much of its L1 points down and how directional it is. Light from the side or above keeps the baked factor. Needs `follow_sun`. | Time of day after the bake, on terrain. |

`sample_static_gi` is the CPU mirror with the sun as baked. `sample_static_gi_relit` takes the frame's
`sun_relight(volume, settings, lights)`, which is what the renderer applies.

## Agent surface

`render.get_gi_mode` returns, under `baked`:

- `lookup: { deringing, leak_guard, sun_relight }`: the switches in use.
- `sun_relight`: the ground factor of the last frame. It is 1 when the sun stands where it was baked, when the
  relight is off, and before the first frame that used the volume. It is below 1 for a lower sun and above 1
  for a higher one.

`render.sample_baked_gi` looks the installed volume up on the CPU at given points: the shader's mirror,
with the renderer's settings, the last frame's light factors and its sun relight. Each of `deringing`,
`leak_guard` and `sun_relight` can be overridden for that call only, so one call with a switch on and one with
it off show what it changes at a point:

```json
{"method": "render.sample_baked_gi", "params": {
  "points": [{"p": [12.0, 0.05, -3.0], "n": [0, 1, 0]}, {"p": [12.4, 1.2, -3.0], "n": [-1, 0, 0]}],
  "leak_guard": false}}
```

Parameters:

- `points`: 1 to 1024 receivers `{ p, n, v }`. `n` defaults to up and `v` (toward the viewer) to `n`; both are
  normalized.
- `deringing`, `leak_guard`, `sun_relight`: optional booleans. They default to the renderer's settings. The sun
  relight comes from the last frame, so `sun_relight: true` has no effect while the renderer has it off or before a
  frame used the volume.
- `visibility_filter` (`"per_tap"` or `"moments"`) and `leak_reduction` (`0..=0.95`): optional overrides of
  `BakedGiSettings::visibility_filter` and `::leak_reduction` for this call (ADR-1105,
  [Baked GI visibility](book/agents/baked-gi-visibility.md)).
- `zh3`: optional boolean override of `BakedGiSettings::zh3`: the ZH3 (`true`) or L1 (`false`) evaluation of the
  SH (ADR-1377, [GI sampling](book/agents/gi-sampling.md)).

The result is `{ samples, lookup, scales, sun_relight, from_frame }`:

- `samples`: one per point, `{ irradiance_over_pi, components: { sun_bounce, sky, fill, emissive }, coverage,
  visibility }`.
- `lookup`: the switches this call used.
- `scales` and `sun_relight`: the light factors and the ground factor applied.
- `from_frame`: whether those came from the last frame. When it is `false`, no frame has used the volume yet,
  so the baked light levels (every factor 1) and the baked sun are used.

Errors:

- `F0003` (not found): no runtime renderer, or no volume installed.
- `F0002` (invalid params): bad points, a non-boolean switch, an unknown `visibility_filter` or a
  `leak_reduction` outside `0..=0.95`.

`regia bake-gi --sample` prints the same lookup with the default switches and the baked sun.

To see the effect on a whole frame instead, use the GI validation route ([GI validation](book/agents/gi-validation.md)):

1. Capture `seeing.compare` against `seeing.reference_trace` with `aov: "indirect_diffuse"`.
2. Have the host call `FrameRenderer::set_baked_gi_settings` with the switch off.
3. Capture again and compare the two results.

The switches themselves are host settings, like the biases: no agent method sets them for the renderer.

## The analytic check

`crates/regia_pt/tests/baked_gi_quality.rs` runs on the CPU only: the CPU probe tracer bakes and the CPU mirror
looks up, so no GPU is needed. It bakes three scenes with exact answers and looks each one up twice, with the
switches off (baseline) and on (quality):

| Scene | Exact answer | Targets |
|---|---|---|
| `open_ground` | An infinite Lambertian ground (ρ = 0.5) under a uniform sky and a sun. A receiver facing `n` (`c = n·up`) reads `L(1+c)/2 + ρL(1−c)/2` of sky and `ρ E sin h/π · (1−c)/2` of sun bounce. Baked at 60°, looked up at 60°, 25° and 80°. | `sun_relight` |
| `emissive_panel` | A 2 × 2 m one-sided emitter over a black floor. Lambert's polygon formula on the panel, clipped to the receiver's hemisphere. | `deringing` |
| `sealed_room` | A closed room with 10 cm walls on the open ground, with probes 0.78 m apart, some under the floor. The inside is black. | `leak_guard` |

Two more rows are measured but not targeted: the sealed room with an INTERIOR brick over its inside, with the
brick's faces on the inner walls or inset 0.12 m from them (see "INTERIOR bricks on the walls" below). They only have
to be no worse with the switches on.

The test prints the table, and writes it to `$REGIA_GI_TABLE/baked_gi_quality.md` when that variable is set. It
fails when any metric of any scene gets worse. The one exception is the panel's energy ratio; the test file explains
why. It also fails when the moved-sun ground error does not drop by at least half (and below 5 %), when the panel's
error does not drop, or when the sealed room leaks more than 5 % of the outdoor light.

```text
cargo test -p regia_pt --test baked_gi_quality -- --nocapture
REGIA_GI_TABLE=/tmp/gi-table cargo test -p regia_pt --test baked_gi_quality -- --nocapture
```

The metrics, per scene:

- **rel RMSE**: RMSE over the mean exact value. For the sealed room it is over the open ground's value.
- **energy**: mean estimate over mean exact value.
- **max error**: the largest error, on the same scale as rel RMSE.
- **light in the dark**: the mean estimate where the exact value is black: behind the panel, or inside the room.

### The prototype measurement

Before the Rust code was written, every change was measured in a numerical prototype of the bake and the lookup.
The prototype is outside the repository: it is single-channel, with its own one-bounce tracer.

| Scene | Metric | Baseline | Quality |
|---|---|---|---|
| open ground, sun 60° → 25° | rel RMSE | 0.295 | 0.006 |
| open ground, sun 60° → 80° | rel RMSE | 0.066 | 0.004 |
| open ground, sun 60° → 25° | energy | 1.189 | 1.004 |
| room with a door, sun moved (8 cases) | rel RMSE | 0.07–0.43 | 0.06–0.22 (better in all 8) |
| emissive panel | rel RMSE | 0.523 | 0.450 |
| emissive panel | light behind the source | 0.030 | 0.024 |
| emissive panel | max error | 4.37 | 3.90 |
| emissive panel | energy | 1.013 | 0.981 (see below) |
| sealed room, 10 cm walls, 0.78 m probes | mean leak | 0.104 | 0.000 |
| sealed room, 10 cm walls, 0.78 m probes | max leak | 1.25 | 0.000 |

Five other room layouts (wall thickness 0.1–0.4 m, probe spacing 0.8–2 m) did not leak at baseline, and they
still do not. The room's outdoor receivers did not
change. The first run of the Rust test replaces this table with the engine's own numbers.

The panel's energy moved from 1.3 % over to 1.9 % under, for this reason:

- De-ringing gives every probe its exact mean over the sphere. The unit test
  `deringing_keeps_the_mean_and_first_moment_and_never_goes_negative` shows this.
- The clamped linear form adds about 9 % at |r1| = 1.8·r0.
- Near a small source the interpolation between probes falls short by about 2 %, and that surplus more than
  made up for it.

## What was measured and not changed

- **Windowing** (scaling the L1 band down, fixed or just enough to keep the linear form non-negative) was worse on
  every panel metric. Example: rel RMSE 0.523 → 0.64–0.81, light behind the source 0.030 → 0.12–0.30. A narrower
  lobe is the fix; a flatter one is not. The non-linear L1 reconstruction from the Frostbite talk (Hazel's) lowered
  the error but doubled the light behind the source, because its constant term never reaches 0.
- **Normal and view bias**: a sweep of (0.1–0.4, 0.3–0.6) on the open ground changed nothing measurable. The
  defaults stay.
- **Interior/exterior blending**: a band over the last cell inside an INTERIOR brick, gated by how much of the
  terrain layer's cell sees the receiver, did not lower the error or the seam at a doorway. The doorway's error comes
  from the coarse outdoor layer, not from the switch. The ADR-281 rule stays: no blend.
- **INTERIOR bricks on the walls**: an INTERIOR brick whose faces lie on the room's inner wall faces puts probes on
  the wall surfaces. In the prototype, the floor next to the walls of the sealed room then read 40 % of the outdoor
  light. With the brick inset by 0.12 m (a sixth of its 0.69 m cell), it read none. This is a placement concern for
  `auto_bricks` (an ADR-861 follow-up), not a lookup one.

## Limits

- The sun relight models ground bounce only. A sunlit wall's bounce keeps the baked factor when the sun's azimuth
  moves. A bake with several sun positions would cover that, and it would change the format.
- De-ringing works per channel on the summed SH, after the corners are blended. A cell whose corners point their
  light in different directions gets a smaller summed L1 and stays linear.

<!-- source: book/agents/baked-gi-light-inputs.md -->
# Bake light inputs: HDRI skies and area emitters

A GI bake (`regia bake-gi map.bake.ron`, [Baking GI from meshes](book/agents/baked-gi-bake.md)) is lit by the sun, the
sky, sky bodies and emissive surfaces. `.bake.ron` v2 (ADR-1095) adds two inputs:

- **`sky_hdri`**: an equirect HDRI map as the sky, with an optional **sun extraction** that lifts the sun out
  of the map into the bake's sun.
- **`sky_atmosphere`**: the runtime's physical sky (`planet: Earth`, `Mars` or `Airless`) for the description's
  sun direction, the same sky-view table the raster frame draws and lights with.
