- `brick_visibility` and `terrain_visibility` (0..1) say how much of each layer's cell sees the
  point. Each layer's light is weighted by its share times its visibility (plus a small floor), so a
  layer whose probes are hidden from the point gives way to the other.
- `brick_corners` and `terrain_corners` list the corner probes each layer visited. Each has `index`,
  `position`, `valid`, `walled`, `trilinear` (position weight), `visibility` (how well the probe
  sees the point, from its distance moments), `weight` (after the facing and visibility terms) and
  `share` (its part of the layer's light, summing to 1). A rejected corner has `valid: false` and no
  weight. A `walled` corner is valid, but a baked wall between probes (or the leak guard) puts it on
  the other side from the point, so it adds no weight either.
- `findings` holds short codes: `outside_volume` (no layer reaches the point), `all_corners_rejected`,
  `rejected_corners` (some corner was rejected, so the light leans on its neighbors),
  `walled_corners` (some corner sits behind a baked wall), `interior_brick`, `partial_coverage`
  (at the volume's edge).

## `render.set_gi_debug_overlay`

Draws a view as a gizmo in the world. A later call replaces the drawing and `"mode": "off"` removes
it. A bad call leaves the previous drawing alone.

| Mode | Draws |
|---|---|
| `validity` | A sphere per probe: green kept, yellow relocated by the bake, red inside geometry, magenta under the terrain, orange rejected for another reason. |
| `irradiance` | A sphere per probe in the light it holds, divided by the peak channel of the drawn set (`peak` in the reply). `exposure` scales the result. Rejected probes are dark grey. |
| `weights` | For the point `p` (with `n`, `v`): a white sphere at `p` and a line to each corner probe. Lines are blue to white by the corner's share; rejected corners are red, corners behind a baked wall orange. |

`validity` and `irradiance` take the same `center`, `radius`, `max` (default 400, at most 5000) and
`filter` as `render.get_gi_probes`. `size` sets the sphere radius (default 0.15 m). The reply has
`mode`, `drawn`, `matched`, `peak` and a `note`. Nothing is drawn when nothing matches.

## Finding out why a spot is dark

1. `render.get_gi_probes {"max": 0}`: are many probes `invalid`? `under_terrain` rejects are normal
   near steep ground; `inside_geometry` rejects mean the bake placed probes in meshes.
2. `render.set_gi_debug_overlay {"mode": "validity", "center": [..], "radius": 20}` and a
   `seeing.screenshot`: a ring of red or magenta spheres around the spot shows rejected probes.
3. `render.explain_gi {"p": [..], "n": [..]}` at the dark pixel's world point (`world.pick`): look
   for `rejected_corners`, a corner with most of the `share` and a low `luminance`, or `outside_volume`.
4. `render.set_gi_debug_overlay {"mode": "weights", "p": [..]}` draws the same corners.
5. `"mode": "irradiance"` shows whether the light varies smoothly. A probe far darker than its
   neighbors usually saw a wall up close (`mean_distance` small).

## Limits

- The views are the CPU mirror, not a capture of the GPU pass. The mirror is checked against the GPU
  lookup by `crates/regia_pt/tests/baked_gi_runtime.rs`.
- Capsule occluders (`render.set_gi_occluders`) are applied in the screen pass and are not part of
  `render.explain_gi`.
- The editor viewport installs no volume, so the methods apply to runtime apps and play-in-editor
  hosts that install one.
- `render.get_gi_probes` walks every probe of the volume per call, which costs a few milliseconds on
  a large bake. It is not a per-frame call.

<!-- source: book/agents/baked-gi-ao.md -->
# Baked GI and screen-space AO

A baked GI volume ([Baked GI volumes](book/agents/baked-gi.md)) already holds the occlusion of the geometry it
was baked with. A probe beside a wall sees the wall, so the probe light at the wall's foot is
already darker. The screen-space AO (SSAO, GTAO rows) then darkens the same light again for the
same wall. Without a correction, the foot of a baked wall or the inside of a bay lost its sky light
twice. The capsule occluders of dynamic units have the same problem: the capsule darkens the baked
light next to a unit, and the SSAO sees the unit too.

Since v0.1.28 the renderer splits the work by scale (ADR-1104). This is on by default.

## What the split does

- Where the volume's light covers a pixel, each SSAO sample counts for the probe light only if its
  point is low over the surface: below about half the probe cell (`PROBE_AO_RESOLVE` = 0.5 × the
  cell edge, ramped from a quarter to three quarters of the cell). Higher points are above the
  probes, so the probe light already holds them.
- A detail brick resolves at its largest cell edge. With 1 m bricks, the SSAO keeps contact
  shade up to about 0.25 m and drops it by 0.75 m.
- The terrain layer resolves at its column spacing. 8 m columns resolve nothing the 1.2 m kernel
  sees, so terrain-lit pixels keep the whole SSAO, as before.
- The sky light outside the volume's coverage keeps the whole kernel.
- Each capsule occluder leaves to the SSAO the share of its occlusion the kernel counts. That is the
  kernel's falloff at the capsule's distance, times the same height weight. Beyond the kernel's
  1.2 m reach, the capsule keeps all of its occlusion. With SSAO off, capsules keep all of theirs.

The split never darkens a pixel compared with the old product, and the probe share is never lighter
than the probe light alone.

## What it costs

The baked screen pass now runs before the SSAO. It writes three extra words per lookup texel (the
two shares, the brick's and the terrain layer's resolve distances; about 0.7 MB more at 1440p).
Where several baked volumes blend (tiles, a streamed level's bake, a nested set piece), the shares
and resolve distances blend with their light, so each texel carries its own. The SSAO kernel reads
them once per AO texel and does two extra multiply-adds per sample. Frames without a baked volume
run the kernel exactly as before.

## Host API

- `BakedGiSettings::probe_relative_ao` (default `true`). Set it with
  `FrameRenderer::set_baked_gi_settings`. `false` multiplies the whole SSAO and the whole capsule
  occlusion into the baked light (the old look).
- `BakedGiStatus::probe_relative_ao` reports whether the last main-view frame ran the split: the
  setting is on, a volume lit the frame and the SSAO ran.
- `StaticGiSample` (from `sample_static_gi` and `sample_static_gi_blend`) carries `brick_share`,
  `terrain_share`, `brick_cell` and `terrain_cell`. Each share is the layer's part of the coverage
  as the lookup blends it (weighted by how much of its cell sees the point).
- `regia_render::baked_gi::ProbeAoSplit` is the split on the CPU. `ProbeAoSplit::of(&sample)`
  builds it, and `ssao_visibility` and `capsule_ssao_share` mirror the kernel and the
  screen pass. `capsule_visibility_split` is `capsule_visibility` with the SSAO's share taken out.

## Agent methods

- `render.get_gi_mode` returns `baked.probe_relative_ao` (the status above).
- `render.set_baked_gi_ao {"probe_relative": false}` switches the split off, and `true` switches
  it back on. It returns `{ before, probe_relative, ran_last_frame, volume_installed, note }`. It
  applies from the next frame.
- Errors: `F0002` (invalid params) when `probe_relative` is missing or not a boolean. `F0003` (not
  found) when the app has no runtime renderer.

## Checking it

1. On a baked map, `render.get_gi_mode`. `baked.active` and `baked.probe_relative_ao` are both
   `true`. If `probe_relative_ao` is `false`, check that the preset runs SSAO (`render.get_profile`).
2. Frame a set piece's wall foot, a doorway or a vehicle bay under a detail brick. `play.pause`, then
   `seeing.screenshot`.
3. `render.set_baked_gi_ao {"probe_relative": false}`, `play.step 1`, and screenshot again. The old
   look is darker in a band along the wall foot and inside the bay. Contact lines right at the
   corner stay dark in both.
4. With a unit and its capsules (`render.set_gi_occluders`), compare the ground beside the unit.
   The old look has a darker, wider halo.
5. Switch back with `{"probe_relative": true}`.

## Evidence in the repo

`crates/regia_render/src/baked_gi/ao_split.rs` tests the split on model scenes. A floor receiver
sits beside static geometry lit through a 1 m brick, or beside a dynamic sphere with a capsule. The
exact cosine-weighted visibility is ray cast. The probe field and an idealised kernel are modelled,
and the mean error is compared over receivers 0.05 to 1.2 m from the occluder:

| Scene | Old product | Split |
|---|---|---|
| 3 m wall | 0.089 | 0.072 |
| Overhang 0.6 m up | 0.110 | 0.087 |
| 1 m block | 0.025 | 0.017 |
| 0.3 m curb (under the probes) | 0.018 | 0.019 |
| 1 m sphere, capsule, terrain-lit | 0.056 | 0.011 |
| 1 m sphere, capsule, brick-lit | 0.056 | 0.013 |

The split leaves a residual. The probe field's visibility is a smoothed field, not a ray cast from
each receiver, so part of a tall wall's double count remains at its foot. Geometry that is neither
baked nor a capsule (a dynamic prop without capsules) keeps only its low SSAO under a brick.

`crates/regia_render/src/baked_gi.rs` checks that the lookup reports its brick and terrain shares,
and that the shared WGSL ramp is the same text in `ssao.wgsl` and `baked_gi_screen.wgsl`.

<!-- source: book/agents/baked-gi-visibility.md -->
# Baked GI leak control in the lookup

A baked GI volume (`.fgiv`, see [Baked GI volumes](book/agents/baked-gi.md)) lights a point from the eight
probes at the corners of its cell. Each probe also stores how far it sees in every direction (its
distance moments). The lookup uses them to drop a corner probe the point is hidden from: a probe
on the far side of a wall should not light the point.

The moments are coarse (4 × 4 or 8 × 8 directions per probe). Next to a thin wall, the two moment
taps around the direction to the point can disagree: one sees the wall in front of the point, the
other sees past it. Filtering the moments first (DDGI as published) averages them into one mean
far beyond the point with a large spread, so the point reads as visible and the far room's light
leaks onto the floor at the foot of the wall.

Since ADR-1105 the lookup does two things by default:

- **Per-tap visibility** (`per_tap`). It takes the visibility bound (Chebyshev, on the moments) at
  each of the four taps and then filters the four results, like percentage-closer filtering of a
  shadow map. A tap that sees the wall keeps its share of the probe hidden.
- **Light-bleeding reduction** (`leak_reduction`, default 0.25). The bound's tail from 0 to the
  amount maps to 0, and the rest is stretched back to 0..1. A probe that the moments find only
  partly visible counts for less. A point that every probe sees fully is not affected.

On open ground the new lookup only re-weights corners the moments already find partly hidden. The
repro test (`crates/regia_render/tests/baked_gi_thin_wall.rs`) holds the average change on open
ground under a light gradient below 2 %. A uniform light reads exactly as before, because the
corner weights are normalized.

What it does not fix: an enclosure smaller than one probe cell, which the moments cannot resolve
at all. Give such a room an interior brick ([Baked GI volumes](book/agents/baked-gi.md), *Interiors*).

## Agent methods

- `render.get_baked_gi_visibility` returns `{ visibility_filter, leak_reduction,
  effective_leak_reduction, default, max_leak_reduction, filters, volume_installed }`.
  `visibility_filter` is `"per_tap"` or `"moments"`.
- `render.set_baked_gi_visibility` changes the settings on the renderer from the next frame.
  `preset: "legacy"` gives the lookup before ADR-1105 (`moments`, reduction 0), for a comparison.
  `preset: "default"` restores the defaults. `visibility_filter` and `leak_reduction` (0 to 0.95)
  set one field on top. It returns `{ before, after, note }`. A host's own
  `FrameRenderer::set_baked_gi_settings` call replaces it.
- `render.sample_baked_gi {points: [{p, n, v}], visibility_filter?, leak_reduction?}` (see
  [Baked GI quality](book/agents/baked-gi-quality.md)) reads the installed volume's light at points through the
  CPU mirror of the shader's lookup. `visibility_filter` and `leak_reduction` override the
  renderer's settings for that call only, and `lookup` in the reply says which were used: call it
  once as is and once with `{visibility_filter: "moments", leak_reduction: 0}` to compare a point
  with the legacy lookup. Capsule occluders are not applied.

Errors: `invalid_params` (`F0002`) for a bad `preset` or `visibility_filter`, or an out-of-range
`leak_reduction`; `not_found` (`F0003`) when the app has no runtime renderer, or
`render.sample_baked_gi` finds no installed volume.

## Checking a leak

1. Find a bright patch on a dark floor beside a wall (`seeing.screenshot`).
2. Pick its world point with `world.pick` or `camera.raycast`, then call
   `render.sample_baked_gi {points: [{p, n: [0, 1, 0], v}]}` there, then again with
   `visibility_filter: "moments", leak_reduction: 0`, and compare `irradiance_over_pi`.
3. `render.set_baked_gi_visibility {preset: "legacy"}`, take the same screenshot, then
   `{preset: "default"}` and take it again.

## Host API

- `BakedGiSettings::visibility_filter` (`regia_render::baked_gi::GiVisibilityFilter`:
  `PerTap`, the default, or `Moments`) and `BakedGiSettings::leak_reduction` (default
  `DEFAULT_LEAK_REDUCTION`, 0.25; clamped to `MAX_LEAK_REDUCTION`, 0.95; a non-finite value turns it
  off).
- `BakedGiSettings::legacy_visibility()` is the default settings with the lookup before ADR-1105.
- `regia_render::sample_static_gi` follows the same settings, so a gameplay query sees what the
  frame shows.

The GPU cost is three more bound evaluations per corner (the four moment taps were already read).
The `.fgiv` file and the bake are unchanged.

<!-- source: book/agents/probe-bake-performance.md -->
# Probe bake performance

How `regia bake-gi` keeps a probe-volume bake fast, what its summary reports about it, and how to
measure a change. Design: ADR-862. Baking itself: [Baking GI from meshes](book/agents/baked-gi-bake.md).

## What the bake does to save time

None of these change a valid probe's result except where noted. The tests in
`crates/regia_pt/tests/probe_bake_perf.rs` check each claim on the real kernels.

| Speed-up | What it does | Effect on the result | Switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coherent ray order | Each probe's rays run in Morton order over the octahedral map, so the rays a GPU wave traces together point the same way. | The same rays and paths. Only the order of the sums changes, so the last bits change. | `ProbeTraceSettings::coherent_rays` (on) |
| Path compaction | After the first bounce, only the paths still going are dispatched, from a queue, through an indirect dispatch. | None: the same paths, bit for bit. | `ProbeTraceSettings::compact_paths` (on) |
| Geometry-only relocation | Relocation rounds record only each ray's first hit (distance, face). They do no shading and send no shadow rays. | Relocation reads only those values, so it decides exactly as before. | `GiBakeSettings::geometry_only_relocation` (on) |
| Retrace only moved probes | A relocation round traces again only the probes the previous round moved. Every probe keeps its own random stream, so the others would trace the same and decide the same. | None. | Always on |
| Skip probes inside geometry | A probe whose last relocation trace, at its final position, saw back faces on at least half of 64 or more rays is marked inside geometry without the main trace. A probe the last round moved first gets one geometry-only classification trace at its final position (progress stage `classify`). | Its flags are the same (`INSIDE_GEOMETRY`, not `VALID`). Its stored SH are 0 instead of traced values that nothing reads. | `GiBakeSettings::skip_inside_fraction` (0.5; above 1 is off) |
| One GPU wait per batch | The batch's sample submissions run back to back. The readback waits once. | None. | Always on |
| Multithreaded BVH | Large meshes build their BVH on every core. Meshes build in parallel with each other. | None: the tree does not depend on the thread count. | Always on |

`GiBakeSettings::without_shortcuts()` turns off every switch in the table. Use it as the reference
when you check a result or time a change.

## The summary

The `report` object of the `regia bake-gi` summary (`GiBakeReport`) has these fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `relocation_traces` | Probe traces the relocation rounds ran, plus the classification traces. With N live probes and R rounds this is at most N·(R + 1), and usually close to N. |
| `inside_skipped` | Probes marked inside geometry from their relocation trace, without the main trace. These probes are also counted in `inside_geometry`. |
| `relocation_seconds`, `trace_seconds`, `encode_seconds` | Wall time of the relocation rounds, of the main trace, and of the filter plus encoding. Their sum is a little less than `seconds`, which also covers setup. |
| `rays_traced` | Rays of the main trace. A skipped probe adds none. |

The fields are additive: older readers ignore them.

## Measuring

```text
cargo run --release -p regia_pt --example probe_bake_bench -- [--scene scattered-hills] [--runs 3] \
    [--rays 256] [--samples 16] [--cpu-only] [--bvh-tris 1000000]
```

The bench prints one JSON object per line:

- `"bench": "bvh"`: one large mesh's BVH, built on one thread and on every core. It reports the time of
  each, the speed-up, the SAH cost and `same_tree`, which must be `true`. This part needs no GPU.
- `"bench": "bake"`: each built-in scene, plus `scattered-hills`, baked in five modes, best of `--runs`.
  `scattered-hills` is `rolling-hills` with 300 boulders and four closed houses, each house inside a 1 m detail
  brick. It has buried probes and deep bounces, which the built-ins mostly lack. The modes:
  - `reference` is `without_shortcuts()`.
  - `coherent` adds only the ray order.
  - `compact` adds only path compaction.
  - `relocation` adds only geometry-only relocation and the inside skip.
  - `fast` is the default settings.
- `"bench": "speedup"`: the reference time divided by each mode's time.

The `reference` mode still uses the speed-ups that are always on. To time the bake before ADR-862, run
`regia bake-gi <scene>` from a build of the commit before it and from a build of this one.

## Errors

`PathTracer::trace_probe_streams` (and `ProbeTracer::trace_streams`, which the bake calls on the GPU and
the CPU tracer alike) takes one stream per probe. It returns an error (`PtError::Scene`) in two cases: the
stream count differs from the probe count, or a stream is 2^24 or more. The bake never passes either.

# UI text fields (agents)

Guide topic: `agent.guide {"topic": "ui_text_input"}`. ADR-273 gap W01 parts 1 and 2, ADR-336, ADR-7208, ADR-9340.

A runtime-UI `TextInput` edits like a desktop text field. This page lists what it does, how an agent drives and
reads it, and what is not done yet.

## What the field does

Keys go to the focused, enabled field. Ctrl also works as Cmd (Meta); word moves also take Alt (Option).

| Keys | Effect |
|---|---|
| Left / Right | One caret stop left / right on screen (a grapheme cluster: a letter with its accents, an emoji sequence). In right-to-left text Right moves toward the start of the text; across a left-to-right / right-to-left boundary the logical caret jumps to the stop that is next on screen. At a line's edge the move goes on to the neighboring line. Without a layout (no fonts) the move is logical. With a selection and no Shift, the selection collapses to its left / right end on screen. |
| Ctrl+Left / Ctrl+Right | The next word edge on screen to the left / right (Unicode word boundaries): in left-to-right text the start of the previous word / the end of the next word; in right-to-left text the end of the next word / the start of the previous word; in mixed text the edges come in screen order. At the line's edge the move goes on to the neighboring line. A `secret` field, a field with an IME composition and a field without a layout move logically (start of the previous / end of the next word). |
| Up / Down | Multi-line: the previous / next visual line at the same x. Single-line: left to focus navigation. |
| Home / End | Start / end of the visual line in a multi-line field, of the text in a single-line field, with the caret drawn at the line's visual start / end edge: left / right in a left-to-right paragraph, right / left in a right-to-left one, even where a run of the other direction touches the edge. Ctrl+Home / Ctrl+End: the whole text. |
| Shift + a move | Extends the selection from its anchor. |
| Backspace / Delete | Deletes the selection, else one grapheme cluster. With Ctrl: to the word boundary. |
| Ctrl+A, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+V | Select all, copy, cut, paste through the UI clipboard. A `secret` field is never copied or cut. |
| Ctrl+Z; Ctrl+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y | Undo; redo. Typing joins one undo step until a new word starts, the caret moves or another kind of edit happens; consecutive single Backspace or Delete presses join one step. 100 steps are kept. |
| Enter | Single-line: sends `Submitted(text)`. Multi-line: inserts a line break; Ctrl+Enter submits. |
| Tab, Escape | Focus navigation, as for every widget. |

Ctrl+Alt is AltGr on many layouts, so Ctrl+Alt+key types the character instead of running a shortcut.

Pointer: a press focuses the field and places the caret at the nearest caret boundary of the shaped glyphs (Shift
extends the selection), dragging selects, a double click selects the word (or the run of spaces, or the punctuation
mark) and a triple click the line (the whole text in a single-line field). Carets come from the glyph clusters
`cosmic-text` shaped, so Arabic and other right-to-left text hit-tests by its visual position, and a ligature is split
evenly between the characters it covers.

Each edit sends `ValueChanged(Text)` once per frame with the new text. `read_only` fields select and copy but do not
change. `filter` takes `Integer`, `Numeric` (both accept a partly typed number such as `-` or `3.`) or `Custom(fn)`,
a rule over the whole text after the edit; an edit the filter refuses is dropped whole, a paste is never half applied.
`max_chars` keeps whole grapheme clusters. Line breaks pasted into a single-line field become spaces.

A field with a definite width and height scrolls: single-line fields scroll sideways and multi-line fields wrap and
scroll down, so the caret stays visible. A field sized by its content keeps its old layout and does not scroll.

### IME composition

While an input method composes (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese telex and other input methods), the
composition (`preedit`) is drawn inline at the caret, underlined, in the label's style; the caret is drawn inside it at
the input method's cursor (`preedit_cursor`, else the composition's end) and the selection highlight is hidden. The
composition is not part of `text` and sends no `ValueChanged`; the commit replaces the selection like typing.

The focused field reports a rect in window physical pixels (`ime_rect`): the caret, or the whole composition while
composing. It follows typing, the field's own scroll and the field's layout, and goes to the platform layer through the
`regia_platform::ImeCursorArea` resource, which hands it to the OS window (`set_ime_cursor_area`), so the candidate
window opens next to the text. Android input methods show candidates on the soft keyboard, so the rect is not passed on
there.

The caret, the selection rectangles and the label are child nodes marked `TextInputPart::{Caret, Selection, Label}`;
`ui.query` lists them as plain nodes.

Moving focus away (click, Tab, agent) abandons an in-progress composition: the `preedit` is dropped, the label loses
the underlined ghost immediately, and no `ValueChanged` fires for it. Only a commit (`ImeEvent::Commit`) inserts text.

In a multi-line field a long composition wraps like typed text; the reported `ime_rect` then covers the caret's (last)
line only, not the whole wrapped composition.

### Clipboard

Copy, cut and paste go through the `UiClipboard` resource, which holds one `ClipboardProvider`. The default uses the
system clipboard on Linux, Windows and macOS and keeps an app-local copy, so copy and paste still work inside the app
where the platform has no clipboard (Android today, or a desktop without a display). Tests insert
`UiClipboard::new(MemoryClipboard::default())`.

## Methods

Positions are character indices (Unicode scalar values), not bytes.

- `ui.key { keys, node?, name? }`: presses each chord in order on the next update. A chord is modifiers (`Ctrl`,
  `Shift`, `Alt`, `Meta`) joined with `+` to a key: `Left`, `Right`, `Up`, `Down`, `Home`, `End`, `Enter`, `Backspace`,
  `Delete`, `Tab`, `Escape`, `Space`, a character such as `a` or `é`, and `Ctrl++` for the plus key. Each chord sends
  its modifier keys down, the key down and up, then the modifiers up, through the same keyboard messages a window
  sends, so focus navigation and the field see real keys. Up to 64 chords per call. Keys go to the focused node; `node`
  or `name` names a TextInput to focus first. Returns `{ node, sent, applies: "next update" }`. Mutating; permission
  `edit_scene`.
- `ui.text_state { node?, name? }`: the focused field, or the one named. Returns `{ node, focused, text, length,
  caret, anchor, selection: [start, end], selected_text, line, column, multiline, read_only, secret, filter,
  max_chars, placeholder, scroll, preedit, preedit_cursor, ime_rect, visual_caret, can_undo, can_redo }`.
  `preedit_cursor` is `[start, end]` in characters of `preedit` (null: at its end). `ime_rect` is `[x, y, w, h]` in
  window physical px, the rect handed to the OS for the IME candidate window; `visual_caret` is `{ x, y, height }`, the
  drawn caret (in mixed-direction text a boundary offset has two screen positions, and this is the one shown). Both are
  null while the field is not focused or before its first layout. A `secret` field returns its masked text and a null
  `selected_text`. Read-only.
- `ui.text_select { caret, anchor?, node?, name? }`: sets the caret and selection at once (clamped, moved back to a
  grapheme boundary) and returns the `ui.text_state` answer. `anchor` defaults to `caret`. Mutating; permission
  `edit_scene`.

`ui.type { text }` (page [Runtime UI](book/agents/ui.md)) still commits text as IME input; use `ui.key` for shortcuts.

```json
{"method": "ui.focus", "params": {"name": "email"}}
{"method": "ui.type", "params": {"text": "ada@example.com"}}
{"method": "ui.key", "params": {"keys": ["Ctrl+Shift+Left", "Ctrl+C", "End", "Ctrl+V"]}}
{"method": "play.step", "params": {"frames": 1}}
{"method": "ui.text_state", "params": {"name": "email"}}
{"method": "ui.text_select", "params": {"name": "email", "anchor": 0, "caret": 3}}
```

## Right-to-left and mixed text (ADR-9340)

A paragraph's direction is its base level by UAX #9 rules P2 and P3: the first strong character decides, so
`123 مرحبا` is a right-to-left paragraph even though it opens with a number (digits are weak). Every visual line of a
wrapped paragraph has the paragraph's direction (`CaretLine::rtl`, `CaretMap::line_rtl`).

The line's two edges belong to its logical ends: the visual start (the right edge in a right-to-left paragraph) is the
line's first byte and the visual end its last. Home in `123 مرحبا` puts the caret at offset 0 drawn at the right edge,
right of the number; End puts it at the end of the text drawn at the left edge. `ui.text_state`'s `visual_caret`
reports the drawn position, `caret` the logical one.

Ctrl+Right walks the word edges on screen (`CaretMap::visual_word_step`): from the left end of `كلمة اخرى ثالثة` it
lands on the start of `ثالثة`, then `اخرى`, then `كلمة`; in `ab كتب قلم cd` it lands after `ab`, then on the start of
`قلم` (the right edge of the leftmost Arabic word on screen), then after `كتب`, then after `cd`.

## Errors

Errors carry `data.reason`:

| Reason | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ui_no_focus` | No node named and nothing has focus. |
| `ui_not_text_input` | The node is not a `TextInput`. |
| `ui_node_not_found` | No node has that id or name. |
| `ui_node_ambiguous` | More than one node has that name; pass `node`. |
| `ui_bad_key` | A chord has an unknown modifier or names no key. |
| `ui_key_empty` | `keys` is missing or empty. |
| `ui_bad_param` | A parameter has the wrong type (for example a negative index). |

## Not done yet

- Delete and Backspace (with or without Ctrl) stay logical in right-to-left text.
- A label with an ellipsis (`TextOverflow::Ellipsis`) drops a number that opens a right-to-left paragraph
  (cosmic-text 0.19; fields and plain labels lay it out since ADR-9340).
- At a left-to-right / right-to-left run boundary the caret stops keep one stop per screen position: the run that does
  not have the paragraph direction gets no stop of its own, so a caret exactly on that boundary byte can jump two stops
  on a Left / Right. Stops of zero-width clusters (combining marks) collapse to one, and the same-position dedup
  (0.5 px) uses a different tolerance than the visual-caret hint match (0.75 px). Movement edge cases in complex
  scripts, not corrupting.
- On Android the system clipboard is not connected; copy and paste stay inside the app.

<!-- source: book/agents/ui-menus.md -->
# UI popups and menus (agents)

Guide topic: `agent.guide {"topic": "ui_menus"}`. ADR-273 lane 5, ADR-332.

## The popup layer

Dropdown lists, tooltips and menus open on the popup layer (`regia_ui::popup`). Each open popup is its own UI root
with `sort_order` 10 000 (plus its nesting depth for submenus), so no owner clip or later root covers it: a dropdown
inside a clipped scroll view opens fully visible.

Placement is a pure function of rectangles (`place_popup`). The panel goes below, above, left or right of its anchor,
flips to the other side when its side lacks room and the other side has more, then shifts on both axes to stay inside
the safe area (the window minus `SafeArea` and the device policy's title-safe margin, `popup_bounds`). Below and above
align left edges; left and right align top edges; a context menu anchors at the pointer. A popup is laid out hidden on
its first frame to measure it, then placed and shown on the next, so it never flashes in the wrong place. A popup
root copies the nearest `ThemeScope` above its anchor.

Interactive popups (menus, dropdown lists) are input layers (`ui_only`): only the top popup gets pointer and
navigation input, and its first item (the selected option of a dropdown, the search field of a long menu) takes focus.
They close on a press outside every open popup panel (a press inside a parent menu closes only the submenus above it),
on `Escape` or gamepad B, when their anchor despawns, and when their parent closes. Closing gives focus back to the
node that opened the popup. Tooltips are passive: no input, no focus, no outside-press closing.

## Widgets

| Widget | Opens | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Dropdown` | click, Enter or A | List below the dropdown (above near the bottom edge), at least as wide. Type-ahead: letters typed while the dropdown or its list has focus pick the option starting with them; one repeated letter cycles; a pause of 1 s starts over. |
| `Tooltip` | hover for `delay` s, or focus in navigation mode for `focus_delay` s (0.8) | Hidden while the host is pressed. |
| `PopupMenu` | click, Enter or A on the host | `placement` picks the side. |
| `ContextMenu` | secondary click or long press (at the pointer); `ContextMenu` key, Shift+F10 or gamepad Y on a focused node inside the host (below it) | |
| `MenuBar` | click on a title | Hovering another title while a menu is open switches menus; Left/Right in a top-level menu move to the neighbouring menu. |

Menu entries are `MenuEntry::Item(MenuItem)` or `MenuEntry::Separator`. An item has `id` (the path segment; empty uses
the label), `label`, `enabled`, `checkable`, `checked`, `shortcut` (display text; when empty, the row shows the chord
[`ui.shortcuts`](book/agents/ui-shortcuts.md) binds to the item's id, or its label without one; ADR-5665) and `submenu`. Keyboard and gamepad: Up/Down move, Enter or A activates, Right or A on an item with a submenu opens it,
Left or B closes the submenu. Hovering an item with a submenu opens it. A menu with more than 12 entries (or
`MenuSearch::Always`) starts with a search field that hides items whose label does not contain the text; Enter in the
field activates the first item left.

Activating an item flips a checkable item, sends `ValueChanged(Text(path))` on the host (item ids joined with `/`),
records a `MenuActivation { host, path, checked }` in the `MenuActivations` resource (dropped at the start of the
second `ui_widgets` run after it, so every system sees it for at least one frame) and closes the menu. Looks come from the theme types `Menu`, `MenuBar`, `MenuItem`,
`MenuItem.checked`, `MenuItem.shortcut`, `Separator` and `Tooltip`.

`.ui.ron`: `widget: popup_menu([...])`, `widget: context_menu([...])` and `widget: menu_bar([...])` take entries
`(id: "save", label: "Save", shortcut: "Ctrl+S", checkable: false, checked: false, enabled: true, submenu: [...])` or
`(separator: true)`. A menu bar's entries are its menus (their `submenu` is the menu). The menu widgets are `.ui.ron`
version 2 (ADR-1381); v1 files load unchanged and `regia upgrade-project --write` renumbers them.

## Methods

- `ui.open_popup { anchor, popup?, placement? }`: opens what the anchor hosts. `anchor` is a node id or a filter object
  (`{"name": "file_menu"}`). `popup` picks `dropdown`, `tooltip`, `menu`, `context`, or a menu bar title (label, id or
  index). An agent-opened tooltip stays until `ui.close_popup`. Returns the popup (`popup`, `panel`, `kind`, `anchor`,
  `opener`, `parent`, `interactive`, `placement`, `placed` with `rect`, `flipped`, `shifted` once placed, and `host`
  and `menu_path` for menus), `already_open` and the open `stack`. Opens at once; `placed` is `null` until the next
  frame. Mutating; permission `edit_scene`.
- `ui.close_popup { popup? }`: closes the newest popup, or the one whose popup or panel id is given, and its
  submenus. Returns `{ closed, focus, stack }`. Mutating; permission `edit_scene`.
- `ui.menu { node, menu? }` (or `name`, `text` or `class` in place of `node`, as for the other `ui.*` node
  methods): lists the entries of a `MenuBar`, `PopupMenu`, `ContextMenu` or `Dropdown` node (or of
  an open menu's popup, panel or row). Each item: `index`, `separator`, `id`, `label`, `path` (ids from the top),
  `enabled`, `checkable`, `checked`, `shortcut` (the text the row shows, registry chord included), `submenu`. A menu bar lists its menus as items; a dropdown lists its
  options with the selected one checked. Also `kind` (`menu_bar`, `popup_menu`, `context_menu`, `dropdown`), `open`,
  `popup` and the `stack`. `menu` picks `popup` or `context` when a node hosts both. Read only.
- `ui.menu_activate { node, path, menu? }`: activates an item as a click does. `path` is a list of ids, labels
  (case-insensitive) or indices, or one string joined with `/`; a menu bar path starts with the menu. On a dropdown the
  path is one option and selects it. Returns `{ node, path, id, checked, closed }`. Works whether the menu is open or
  not; the host's open menus close. Mutating; permission `edit_scene`.

```json
{"method": "ui.menu", "params": {"name": "main_menu"}}
{"method": "ui.menu_activate", "params": {"name": "main_menu", "path": ["view", "grid"]}}
{"method": "ui.open_popup", "params": {"anchor": {"name": "main_menu"}, "popup": "File"}}
{"method": "ui.close_popup", "params": {}}
```

## Errors

Errors carry `data.reason`; the node filter errors of `book/agents/ui.md` (`ui_node_required`, `ui_node_not_found`,
`ui_node_ambiguous`) apply too.

| Reason | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ui_popup_unavailable` | The anchor hosts no popup of the asked kind. |
| `ui_popup_not_found` | `popup` is not an open popup or panel id. |
| `ui_no_popup_open` | `ui.close_popup` with nothing open. |
| `ui_menu_not_found` | The node hosts no menu, or the menu bar has no menu by that name. |
| `ui_menu_path_not_found` | A path segment names no item. |
| `ui_menu_item_disabled` | The item is disabled. |
| `ui_menu_item_has_submenu` | The item opens a submenu; add one of its items to the path. |
| `ui_bad_param` | A parameter has the wrong type or value (`path`, `popup`, `placement`). |

<!-- source: book/agents/ui-screens.md -->
# UI screens and page history (agents)

Guide topic: `agent.guide {"topic": "ui-screens"}`. Gap W18, ADR-273; integrated by ADR-1563.

A screen is any node with `UiScreen { id, mode, transition }`, usually a full-window
child of one `UiRoot`. `ScreenStack` is the history, bottom first. Only the top screen
is shown (`Display::None` hides the rest) and only the top receives input: it holds an
`InputLayer` with the screen's `mode`, so push/pop restores the previous visibility
and input mode through the layer stack. The control that had focus when that screen
was covered is focused again if it is still focusable and not disabled; otherwise the
layer's default focus stands.

<!-- ignore-reason: `ScreenError` does not implement `std::error::Error`, so the examples' `?` has no harness to run in -->
```rust,ignore
push_screen(world, title)?;
push_screen(world, options)?;
pop_screen(world, None)?; // back to title, focus and UiOnly restored
show_screen(world, title)?; // pops everything above title, or pushes it
```

`show_screen` returns whether the visible screen changed. Despawning a stacked screen
(or removing its `UiScreen`) prunes it on the next frame and focus recovers instead of
locking. `ScreenChanged { pushed, popped, top }` tells transition drivers what happened;
`screen_list(world)` is the read side (id plus `visible`, bottom first).

## Transitions

The switch itself is instant so layout is untouched. `ScreenTransition` (`instant`,
`fade`, `slide`) is metadata: read it on `ScreenChanged` and drive the animation with
`ui.tween` (for example a fade on `Opacity`). Reduced motion jumps to the end value.
Error codes are `unknown_entity`, `not_a_screen`, `already_on_stack`, `empty_stack`
and `not_on_top` (use `show_screen` to jump back).

## `ui.screens`

`ui.screens { action?, entity? }` (`play` permission) reads and drives the stack. The answer is
always the stack after the call: `screens` (bottom first, `entity`, `id`, `visible`), `depth`,
`top`, `top_id` and the `focused` node.

```json
{ "method": "ui.screens" }
→ { "screens": [ { "entity": 4294967310, "id": "title", "visible": false },
                 { "entity": 4294967312, "id": "options", "visible": true } ],
    "depth": 2, "top": 4294967312, "top_id": "options", "focused": 4294967313, "applied": false }
{ "method": "ui.screens", "params": { "action": "pop" } }
→ { "screens": [ { "entity": 4294967310, "id": "title", "visible": true } ], "depth": 1,
    "top": 4294967310, "top_id": "title", "focused": 4294967311, "popped": 4294967312 }
```

- `list` (the default) changes nothing and answers `applied: false`.
- `push` needs `entity` (a node with `UiScreen`); the previous top is hidden.
- `pop` removes the top screen (or `entity`, which must be the top) and answers `popped`.
- `show` needs `entity`: it pops back to a stacked screen or pushes a new one, and answers
  `changed` (false when it was already on top).

Errors (lowercase codes in `error.data.code`): `unknown_entity` (no such entity), `not_a_screen`
(no `UiScreen` on it), `already_on_stack` (push of a stacked screen: use `show`), `empty_stack`
(pop with nothing stacked) and `not_on_top` (pop of a buried screen: pop the top or `show` it).

## Recipes

- *Does Back return to the title with focus on Play?* `ui.screens { action: "push", entity:
  options }`, then `ui.screens { action: "pop" }`: `top_id` is `title` and `focused` is the Play
  button.
- *Wait for a menu to open*: `play.wait_until` cannot read the stack (it is a resource without
  reflection); poll `ui.screens` until `top_id` names the screen.


## Opt-in back handling

`ScreenStack::set_back_pop(true)` opts the stack into Escape/gamepad B popping. The default is
false. A `ScreenBack::Pop` or `ScreenBack::Ignore` component overrides the default for one screen.
Only the top screen owning the active input layer can pop; an overlaid modal, game-only input
mode, disabled screen or input-rebinding capture keeps the back press from popping it.
The existing pop path restores focus on the previous screen, skipping disabled descendants.
No `.ui.ron` field is introduced here; screen definition authoring belongs to the format lane.

`ui.screens` adds `action:"set_back"` with `back:"pop"|"ignore"`. With `entity`, this sets a
per-screen override; without it, it sets the stack default. `action:"back"` exercises the
active layer's policy and returns `changed` and `applied` (false when nothing popped).
The stack result now includes `back`; every screen row includes its override `back`, null when
it inherits the stack default. Existing entity errors still apply. Invalid `action` or `back`
uses the shared invalid-parameter error `F0002`.

```json
{"method":"ui.screens","params":{"action":"set_back","back":"pop"}}
{"method":"ui.screens","params":{"action":"set_back","entity":4294967312,"back":"ignore"}}
{"method":"ui.screens","params":{"action":"back"}}
```

<!-- source: book/agents/ui-focus-ring.md -->
# UI focus ring

The focus ring shows a keyboard or gamepad user which `regia_ui` widget has focus. It follows
`docs/specs/ui-default-design.md` §§ 2.2, 3 and 5 (lane D9, ADR-372; gap I05).

## When it shows

Focus and the ring are separate:

- **Focus** moves with navigation (arrows, Tab, the D-pad, the left stick), with `ui.focus`, and in code
  (`FocusState`, the `Focused` marker). A pointer move, click or touch never moves or drops focus.
- **The ring** draws on the focused node only while `FocusRingPolicy` says so. The policy is a resource:

| Policy | Agent name | Ring shows |
|---|---|---|
| `NavigationOnly` (default) | `navigation_only` | in `UiInputMode::Navigation` only |
| `Always` | `always` | whenever a node is focused (an accessibility setting) |
| `Never` | `never` | never (the game draws its own focus visuals) |

The last device used sets the input mode. Any keyboard navigation key or gamepad input switches to
`navigation`. A cursor move, a mouse button or a touch switches to `pointer`. So with the default policy a
click hides the ring, focus stays where it was, and the next arrow press shows the ring again on the same
node.

The theme's `focused` state layer applies whenever the node has focus, ring or not. A widget that wants a
focus look after a click (a text field's accent border) puts it there. The `focus_visible` layer (ADR-7827) applies
over `focused` only while the ring shows (keyboard or gamepad focus under the default policy), so a clicked control can
keep a quieter look than one reached by navigation: `StyleClass::focus_visible` in code-built classes and
`ThemeOverride`; `StyleState::focus_visible` says whether it applies, and `ui.inspect`'s style replay names the winning
layer `focus_visible`. A `.theme.ron` file cannot set it yet (that needs a theme format step).

## How it looks

| Token | Default (dark / light) | High contrast | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `color.focus-ring` | `#9cd3ff` / `#0b4f9e` | `#ffd400` / `#002a6e` | ring colour |
| `border.width.focus` | 2 | 3 | band width (UI px) |
| `border.width.focus-offset` | 2 | 2 | gap between the widget's border box and the ring |
| `border.width.focus-inset` | -2 | -3 / -2 | the offset list rows use: minus the width, so the band lies just inside the row |

The ring is concentric with the widget: its inner edge has the widget's corner radius plus the offset,
and its outer radius is clamped to half the ring's short side (a pill keeps a pill ring). A widget type
overrides the ring with the `focus_ring` property (`[colour, width, offset]` in any order of colour and
numbers, width first) or with `focus_ring_width` / `focus_ring_offset`. `List.row` (and every variation
that extends it, such as `Panel.list-item`) sets `focus_ring_offset: "@border.width.focus-inset"`, so a
scroll clip cannot cut the ring of a row.

Slider, toggle and progress fills use the theme's `color.accent` (`Themed::accent`), not the ring colour.

## Agent surface

- `ui.state` has `focus_ring`:
  `{ visible, policy, node, rect, width, color }`. `visible` is true when the focused node draws its ring.
  `rect` is the ring's outer edge `[x, y, width, height]` in physical pixels, `width` is the band width in
  physical pixels and `color` is sRGB hex. They are null when no ring shows.
- `ui.query` nodes have `focus_visible`.
- `ui.focus` switches the input mode to `navigation`, like a Tab press, so the ring shows on the next frame.
  `ui.type` with a target focuses it the same way. `ui.click` switches to `pointer` and hides the ring.

Check that a click hides the ring and keeps focus:

```json
{"method": "play.pause", "params": {}}
{"method": "ui.focus", "params": {"name": "settings"}}
{"method": "play.step", "params": {"frames": 2}}
{"method": "ui.state", "params": {}}
{"method": "ui.click", "params": {"name": "play"}}
{"method": "play.step", "params": {"frames": 3}}
{"method": "ui.state", "params": {}}
```

The first `ui.state` has `input_mode: "navigation"` and `focus_ring.visible: true`. The second has
`input_mode: "pointer"`, the same `focus` and `focus_ring.visible: false`.

There is no method that sets the policy. A game sets it in code:
`world.insert_resource(FocusRingPolicy::Always)`.

## Notes

- A mode flip re-resolves only the focused node, from the style cache: no other node does any work.
- Geometry is `regia_ui::focus_ring_geometry`, used by both the extract pass and `ui.state`.
- Ring goldens per widget are not blessed yet; the headless checks in `crates/regia_ui/tests/focus_ring.rs`
  read the ring quads from the draw list.

# UI focus graph and gamepad navigation (agents)

Guide topic: `agent.guide {"topic": "ui_navigation"}`. UI lane 9, ADR-516. Code: `regia_ui::focus_graph`.

Keyboard arrows, Tab, the D-pad, the left stick and the shoulder buttons all move focus through one focus graph. The
graph holds the navigable nodes of the active scope (the top input layer, else the open focus scope): `Focusable`
nodes that are not `Disabled` and have a laid-out rect with area. Nodes are kept in reading order (top to bottom,
then left to right, then entity id), so every tie breaks the same way on every run.

## How a move is decided

For up, down, left and right, from the focused node:

1. **Explicit link.** A `NavLinks` target wins when it is navigable now. A link to a disabled, hidden or
   out-of-scope node falls through to geometry. A link to the node itself blocks that direction (the calibration
   screen uses this for sliders that step their own value).
2. **Innermost group.** If the node sits inside one or more `FocusGroup` containers, the innermost group is searched
   first with the geometric score (nearest in the direction, aligned nodes preferred; `focus::nav_score`).
3. **Edge rule.** When the group has no candidate in that direction, its edge rule decides:

| Rule | Effect |
|---|---|
| `escape` | Search the enclosing group, or the whole scope after the outermost group (the default). |
| `stop` | No move. |
| `wrap` | Jump to the node on the far side of the group, in the same row or column. |

4. **Remembered child.** A move that enters a group created with `remember` lands on the child that had focus last,
   not on the nearest one.

Without any group the result is the same as before ADR-516: geometry over the whole scope, no wrap at the edges.

Next and prev (Tab, Shift-Tab, the right and left shoulder) walk the Tab order: nodes with a positive `TabIndex` first,
ascending, then the rest in reading order. A negative `TabIndex` takes the node out of Tab order; arrows still reach
it. The order wraps at its ends. Inside a group with `tab: cycle`, Tab cycles through that group's members only.

| Preset | Edges | Tab |
|---|---|---|
| `FocusGroup::new()` | all `escape` | `pass` |
| `FocusGroup::trap()` | all `stop` | `cycle` |
| `FocusGroup::wrap()` | all `wrap` | `cycle` |
| `FocusGroup::wrap_horizontal()` | left/right `wrap`, up/down `escape` | `pass` |
| `FocusGroup::wrap_vertical()` | up/down `wrap`, left/right `escape` | `pass` |

`.remembering()` adds the memory to any preset; `.with_edge(direction, rule)` changes one edge.

## Focus that goes stale

- With nothing focused, the first press reveals focus on the default node (`DefaultFocus` inside the scope, else the
  first node in Tab order) without moving.
- If the focused node is despawned, or hidden after it had been visible, while the input mode is `navigation`, focus
  moves at once to the nearest navigable node (else the default). The focus ring never sits on nothing. A node that is
  focused in code before its first layout is left alone.
- In `pointer` mode a despawned focus is cleared; a hidden one is kept (the ring does not show in pointer mode) and
  recovers on the next press.
- A press while focus is outside the active scope (a dialog opened over it) goes to the scope's default node. Before
  ADR-516 such a press did nothing.
- A disabled focused node keeps focus; moves start from its rect.

## Methods

- `ui.nav_graph {}`. Returns `{ scope, focused, input_mode, nodes, groups, count, truncated }`. Each node:
  `{ entity, rect: {x, y, w, h}, tab_index, groups, links: {up, down, left, right}, moves, name, declared }`;
  `name` is the node's name (or `null`); `declared` is `{ up, down, left, right, resolved }` with the neighbor names
  its `.ui.ron` `nav` field declared (ADR-7827; `resolved: false` while a name matches no node of its document), or
  `null`. The resolved targets are in `links`, so a declared name that matched shows there as an entity; `moves` holds
  `up`, `down`, `left`, `right`, `next` and `prev`, each `{ target, reason }`, computed exactly as a press would go now
  (remembered children included). Each group: `{ entity, edges: {up, down, left, right}, tab, remember, remembered,
  members }`. At most 512 nodes; `truncated` says when there are more. Read-only.
- `ui.nav_move { direction }`. `direction` is `up`, `down`, `left`, `right`, `next` or `prev`. Applies one press at
  once through the same graph and switches the input mode to `navigation`, so the focus ring shows. Returns
  `{ direction, from, to, moved, reason, focused, input_mode }`. Mutating; permission `edit_scene`.
- `ui.nav_lint { start? }`. Checks the graph's structure (remembered children are ignored). Returns
  `{ start, nodes, clean, issues: [{ code, node, other, direction }] }`. Reachability starts at `start` (entity bits),
  else the focused node, else the default node. Read-only.

```json
{"method": "ui.nav_graph", "params": {}}
{"method": "ui.nav_move", "params": {"direction": "right"}}
{"method": "ui.nav_lint", "params": {}}
```

A typical check: drive a menu with `ui.nav_move`, confirm the focus with
`play.wait_until {"condition": {"predicate": "ui.node_state", "name": "settings", "state": "focused"}}` (see
[UI](book/agents/ui.md)), then run `ui.nav_lint` to confirm every button is reachable by controller.

### Reasons

| Reason | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `initial` | Nothing was focused: the press revealed the default node. |
| `recovered` | Focus was gone, hidden or outside the scope and moved to the nearest or default node. |
| `explicit` | A `NavLinks` target. |
| `geometry` | The best geometric candidate. |
| `wrap` | A `wrap` edge jumped to the far side of a group. |
| `remembered` | Entering a remembering group restored its last focused child. |
| `tab` | The next or previous node in Tab order. |
| `stop` | A `stop` edge, or a link to the node itself: no move. |
| `edge` | No candidate and nothing to wrap to: no move. |

### Lint codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `unreachable` | No sequence of moves from the start node reaches this node. |
| `dead_end` | No move leaves this node in any direction, and the graph has other nodes. |
| `dead_link` | An explicit link points to a node that is not navigable now (`other` names it). |
| `one_way_link` | The link target's opposite move does not come back to this node. |
| `duplicate_rect` | Two nodes share one rect, so geometry cannot tell them apart. |

## Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `unknown_direction` | `ui.nav_move` got a direction other than the six names. |
| `no_focusables` | The active scope has no navigable node. |
| `not_navigable` | `ui.nav_lint` `start` is not in the graph. |
| `ui_not_installed` | The app has no runtime UI (`UiPlugin`). |

Not covered yet: `.ui.ron` has no `FocusGroup` or `TabIndex` field (add them in code). The focus ring's look and
when it shows (pointer or navigation mode) belong to the focus ring work (ADR-372), not to this page.

# Tooltips and hints (agents)

Tooltips and the controller hint bar are part of the runtime UI (`regia_ui`). An agent reads them through
`ui.state` and drives them with the same input a player uses: move focus with `ui.focus`, press a button with
`ui.click`, wait with `play.wait_until`. Guide topic: `agent.guide {"topic": "ui"}`. See [Runtime UI](book/agents/ui.md) for the
rest of the `ui.*` methods.

## What `ui.state` reports

- `tooltip` is `null` when no tooltip is open. Otherwise `{ node, text, trigger }`: the node that owns it, the text
  on screen (hint placeholders already expanded for the last device) and `trigger`, `hover` or `focus`.
- `hints` is `{ device, bar }`. `device` is `keyboard_mouse`, `xbox`, `playstation` or `steam_deck`. `bar` is the
  hint-bar lines for that device, such as `"A Select"` and `"B Back"`; it is empty when the screen sets none.
  A hint bar belongs on screen only while `input_mode` is `navigation`.

There are no tooltip-only methods or error codes. `ui.open_popup` with `popup: "tooltip"` keeps a node's tooltip open
until `ui.close_popup` ([popups and menus](book/agents/ui-menus.md)).

## Agent request details

`ui.state {}` takes no parameters. For the focus workflow, registered `ui.focus` accepts one selector: `node` (the
id from `ui.query`), `name`, `text`, `text_contains`, `class`, `type` or `state`. `ui.click` accepts the same
selectors plus `button` (`left`, `right`, `middle`) and `count` (1 to 8).

`ui.focus` reports `ui_node_required`, `ui_node_not_found`, `ui_node_ambiguous`, `ui_node_disabled`,
`ui_node_blocked_by_layer` or `ui_node_not_focusable`; `ui.click` can also report `ui_node_not_visible`. These use
`F0002` for invalid/ambiguous/refused nodes and `F0003` for `ui_node_not_found`. Both methods return `F0013`
(`ui_not_installed`) when the app has no runtime UI hook. The stable reason is in `error.data.reason`.

## The rules

| Rule | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Candidate | In `pointer` mode the hovered node; in `navigation` mode the focused node. Only one tooltip is open at a time. |
| Delay | The node's `delay` (default 0.5 s) of hover. Focus waits the node's `focus_delay` (0.8 s by default). |
| Warm-up | While a tooltip is open, and for 0.4 s after one closed, the next tooltip opens without waiting. |
| Leave | Moving off the node (or moving focus away) closes it and resets the wait. |
| Dismiss | A press on the node, Enter or A (submit), Escape or B (cancel) and a scroll close it. It stays closed until the pointer or focus leaves the node. |
| Auto hide | Off by default; `TooltipPolicy::auto_hide` closes it after a number of seconds. |

These delays step on `RealTime`. `play.step` still moves them, because a manual step advances `RealTime`
by the step before `Time` is scaled. Pause and `time_scale` do not freeze or stretch a tooltip. A live
run uses the frame's real delta, not a separate wall-clock wait outside the frame.

## Gamepad text and glyphs

A node can carry `TooltipNavText`, which replaces the tooltip text while the UI is in `navigation` mode. Both
texts accept placeholders that expand to the glyph of the last device: `{activate}`, `{back}`, `{secondary}`,
`{menu}`, `{prev_tab}`, `{next_tab}`, `{page_up}` and `{page_down}`. Unknown names stay as written.

| Action | Keyboard | Xbox | PlayStation | Steam Deck |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| activate | Enter | A | Cross | A |
| back | Esc | B | Circle | B |
| secondary | Shift+Enter | Y | Triangle | Y |
| menu | F10 | Menu | Options | Menu |
| prev_tab | Ctrl+PgUp | LB | L1 | L1 |
| next_tab | Ctrl+PgDn | RB | R1 | R1 |
| page_up | PgUp | LT | L2 | L2 |
| page_down | PgDn | RT | R2 | R2 |

The host sets the `HintDevice` resource from the last device used; it defaults to `keyboard_mouse`. A screen sets
the `HintBar` resource (`bar.set([(HintAction::Activate, "Select"), (HintAction::Back, "Back")])`).

## Checking a tooltip

```text
ui.focus { "name": "buy_button" }
play.step { "frames": 60 }          # about one second at 60 fps, past the 0.8 s focus delay
ui.state  ->  { "tooltip": { "node": 4294967301, "text": "Press A to buy", "trigger": "focus" }, ... }
```

Captured failure on lavapipe:

Request:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ui.focus","params":{"text":"__capture_missing_tooltip_target__"}}
```

Response:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"error":{"code":-32001,"message":"no UI node matches","data":{"code":"F0003","hint":"call ui.query with fewer filters to see what exists","reason":"ui_node_not_found"}}}
```

<!-- source: book/agents/ui-scroll.md -->
# UI scroll containers (agents)

Guide topic: `agent.guide {"topic": "ui_scroll"}`. ADR-520 (UI design series d-12). Lists and the interactive
scrollbars themselves are on the [UI lists and scrollbars](book/agents/ui-list.md) page.

## Scroll containers

A `ScrollView` scrolls its children; `ScrollOffset` holds the offset (physical px, positive moves toward the end of
the content). Adding a `ScrollView` also adds `ScrollOffset`, `ScrollVelocity` and `ScrollMotion` (gesture state).
`regia_ui::scroll_container(style, view)` spawns a clipping container in one bundle: the node, its style,
`ClipChildren` and an `Interactable` so drags and the wheel over its empty space reach it. Clips nest: a child
container's clip rect is the intersection of every clipping ancestor, and hit testing uses the same rects, so a row
scrolled out of view cannot be clicked.

Settings on `ScrollView` (all have defaults that keep the earlier behavior):

| Field | Values | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `axes` | `Both` (default), `Vertical`, `Horizontal` | The axes the view scrolls. A delta on the other axis passes to the enclosing view (a carousel inside a page). `ScrollView::vertical()` and `ScrollView::horizontal()` build these. |
| `overscroll` | `Clamp` (default), `Bounce` | `Bounce`: a drag pulls the content past its edge through a rubber band and a fling runs past it; a critically damped spring brings it back without overshooting into the content. |
| `chaining` | `Chain` (default), `Contain` | `Contain` keeps every delta inside the view: scrolling it never moves the views around it. |
| `inertia` | seconds (default 0.18) | Fling time constant. A fling at `v` px/s coasts `v * inertia` px if it runs until the velocity is zero and nothing blocks it. Motion also stops under 4 px/s, about `4 * inertia` px sooner, and a view stops at an edge. 0 turns flings off. |
| `wheel_smoothing` | seconds (default 0) | The wheel eases toward its target instead of jumping. Notches during the easing add up. |

## Input

- **Wheel.** It goes to the innermost scroll view under the pointer (a hovered scrollbar counts as its view). That
  view takes what fits on its axes and the rest passes outward. With no pointer (an agent or a test) it goes to the
  views around the focused node, and with no focus either, to every view as before ADR-520. A wheel notch never
  flings and never pulls past an edge.
- **Drag.** A drag on any node inside a scroll view moves the innermost view around it, and chains the same way.
  The content follows the pointer. A drag that starts on a scrollbar part is the scrollbar's.
- **Fling.** At release, the fling velocity is the mean drag velocity over the last 100 ms of the gesture. A finger
  that rests before lifting does not fling. Inertia is integrated exactly, so the distance does not depend on the
  frame rate.
- **Press.** Pressing inside a moving view stops its fling or spring. Releasing without a drag does not restart it.
- **Focus.** Focus moving to a node inside a view scrolls it into view on both axes, once per focus move.

## Scrollbar styles

`Scrollbars::styled(ScrollbarStyle::…)` (or `Scrollbars::overlay()` / `Scrollbars::classic()`) builds a named look.
Every preset covers both axes; a bar shows only when its axis overflows.

| Style | Look |
|---|---|
| `overlay` | The default design's bar: 10 px, 14 px under the pointer, pill-shaped, no track. The thumb is the text color at 25 % (40 % hovered, 55 % pressed). It hides after one idle second. |
| `compact` | The overlay bar at compact density: 8 px, 10 px under the pointer. |
| `classic` | Always visible, 12 px, square, with a track. |
| `hidden` | No bars. The view still scrolls by wheel, drag, keys and focus. |

The new `Scrollbars` fields are `hover_thickness`, `rounded`, `thumb_hover_color` and `thumb_active_color`.
`Scrollbars::default()` is unchanged.

## Performance

A frame where only scroll offsets moved does not run the flexbox pass. Layout walks the cached result again, at
the new offsets: positions and clip rects follow, and nothing is reconciled, measured or computed. Rows outside the
clip produce no draw quads. `UiLayoutStats` counts the runs (`full_runs`, `incremental_runs`, `scroll_runs`) and
the nodes the last run walked and changed. The 10,000-row test scrolls a plain container with no full or
incremental layout. For 10,000 items with only the visible rows alive, use a virtualised `ListView`.

## Method

`ui.scroll { entity, action?, ... }` where `entity` is the node id from `ui.query` (`node` works as an alias). It is
mutating (permission `edit_scene`).

- `action: "state"` (default) returns `{ entity, offset, max, viewport, content, velocity, overscrolled, axes,
  overscroll, chaining, inertia, wheel_smoothing, dragging, held, flings, settled, scrollbars, chain }`.
  `overscrolled` is how far each axis sits past its edge. `scrollbars` is the preset name, `custom` or null. `chain`
  lists the scroll views around the entity, innermost first. `settled` is true when no fling, drag, wheel easing or
  overscroll is left.
- `action: "wheel"` with `delta: [x, y]` scrolls like a wheel over the view: it fills first, then chains outward. It
  stops any motion on the chain. The answer adds `moved: [{ entity, offset }]` for each view of the chain.
- `action: "fling"` with `velocity: [x, y]` (px/s) starts a fling. The velocity is limited to the view's axes and
  to 12,000 px/s. The answer adds `distance: [x, y]`, `velocity * inertia` on each axis: the coast if
  the view ran until the velocity was zero and nothing blocked it. The view may stop sooner at an edge,
  or once speed falls under 4 px/s (about `4 * inertia` px short of `distance`). Poll `state` until
  `settled` is true.
- `action: "stop"` ends the motion and moves an overscrolled view back onto its edge.
- `action: "style"` with `style`: `overlay`, `compact`, `classic`, `hidden`, or `none` to remove the bars. The view
  needs a parent node, because the bars are its siblings.
- `action: "config"` with any of `axes`, `overscroll`, `chaining`, `inertia`, `wheel_smoothing` edits the view.

Error codes:

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `unknown_entity` | The entity does not exist. |
| `not_scrollable` | The entity is not a `ScrollView`. |
| `unknown_scroll_style` | `style` names no preset. |
| `no_bar_parent` | `style` on a view without a parent node. |

Bad or missing parameters return `F0002`.

<!-- source: book/agents/ui-layout.md -->
# UI layout edge cases (agents)

ADR-518. How `regia_ui` lays out the cases that are easy to get wrong: right-to-left mirroring, wrapping, grid
tracks, min/max sizes, aspect ratios, safe areas, and style values that make no sense. Layout is taffy (CSS
flexbox and grid); the rules below are where Regia Engine's style differs from plain CSS or picks one reading of it.

## Checking layout from an agent

`ui.query` returns each node's `rect` (`[x, y, width, height]` in physical pixels) and its `layout_dir` (`ltr` or
`rtl`, the direction it lays out its children in). To check a layout, query the nodes and compare rects; to check
mirroring, switch the locale and query again.

```json
{"method": "ui.query", "params": {"name": "inventory_row"}}
```

The reply has `"layout_dir": "rtl"` for a node under an Arabic or Hebrew locale (or under an explicit `rtl`), and
the rects of its children run from the right edge.

## Right to left

- A node's `text_dir` is `auto`, `ltr` or `rtl`. `auto` inherits the parent's direction; a root with `auto` takes
  the active locale's direction (ar, he, fa, ur, ps, sd, yi, dv, ug, ckb are right to left). So an `ltr` panel
  inside a right-to-left screen keeps left-to-right children, and everything under it that says `auto` does too.
- In a right-to-left node, `row` runs from the right edge, `rowreverse` runs from the left, `justify_content:
  start` packs to the right, grid columns are placed right to left, and in a `column` the cross-axis `start` is the
  right edge.
- The left and right values of `margin`, `padding`, `border` and `inset` are start and end: in a right-to-left
  node they swap sides. `padding: (16, 0, 0, 0)` pads the right edge under an RTL locale.
- Safe-area insets do not swap: a notch on the left stays on the left.
- Changing a node's `text_dir` re-lays out every `auto` node below it on the next frame.

## Alignment

`justify_content: start` and `end` are flex-relative: they pack toward where the first item goes. A `rowreverse`
row with `start` hugs the right edge (left in RTL), like `flex-start` in CSS.

## Wrapping

With `flex_wrap: true`, items fill a line until the next one (plus the gap) would cross the content edge, then
start a new line. Items never shrink by default (`flex_shrink` is 0 unless set), so an item wider than the
container sits alone on its line and overflows it. `gap` is `[horizontal, vertical]`.

## Grid tracks

- `Px(n)` and `Percent(p)` tracks are fixed: content wider than the track overflows it instead of widening it
  (CSS `100px` / `50%`).
- `Fr(n)` shares the free space, but never shrinks below its content (CSS `minmax(auto, 1fr)`).
- Items are placed in reading order, filling each row of columns before the next row.
- A grid whose height is fixed stretches its auto rows to fill it; give the grid an `auto` height to keep rows at
  their content height.

## Min, max and aspect ratio

- `min_size` beats `max_size` when they conflict, on both axes.
- With `aspect_ratio` (`width / height`) and one axis given, the other axis is derived from it.

## Safe areas

A root with `SafeAreaPadding` adds the platform's safe-area insets to its own padding. Percentage padding on such
a root still counts (it resolves against the window width first). Insets that add up to more than the window
(a bogus platform report) are scaled down to fit it, so the root never grows past the window.

## Values layout refuses

Layout must not produce NaN or infinite rects from user content. Before taffy sees a style:

| Value | Becomes |
|---|---|
| a non-finite length, or a negative `size`, `min_size`, `max_size`, `padding`, `border`, `gap` or `flex_basis` | `Auto` (the property's initial value: no padding, no gap, no limit) |
| a negative margin or inset | kept (they are legal) |
| a length beyond ±1,000,000 physical px, a percentage beyond ±10,000 % | clamped |
| a non-finite or negative `flex_grow` / `flex_shrink` | 0 |
| an `aspect_ratio` that is not finite and positive | none |
| a grid track that is non-finite or negative | an `Auto` track |
| a non-finite or negative window size or safe-area inset | 0 |

These rules are checked by seeded property tests over random style trees (`crates/regia_ui/tests/layout_edge_cases.rs`):
random hostile trees always produce finite rects with non-negative sizes, and every random flex or grid tree laid
out under an RTL locale is the mirror image of its LTR layout.

## Not covered yet

- Scrolling: a right-to-left scroll view still measures its overflow toward the right, and the scroll offset
  still moves content to the left.
- Text inside a node shapes by its own bidi rules; `text_dir` changes box layout, not glyph order.

# UI motion presets (agents)

Guide topic: `agent.guide {"topic": "ui_motion"}`. UI default design D14, ADR-522. Built on
[UI tweens and the visual transform](book/agents/ui-animation.md).

## What a preset is

A node with `regia_ui::UiMotion` animates four events without game code:

| Trigger | Preset | What moves | Timing (spec § 2.6) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enter | a reveal: `fade`, `slide` (offset in UI px), `zoom` (scale at the hidden end) | opacity 0 → 1, plus the offset → 0 or the scale → 1 | the node's speed token (`motion.slow` by default) with `ease.enter` |
| Exit | a reveal | opacity → 0, plus → the offset or the scale; then `hide` (`Display::None`) or `despawn` | 0.75 × the speed token with `ease.exit` |
| Hover | a pose: `lift`, `grow`, `sink`, `shrink`, `rest` or `{translate, scale}` | the node's `UiTransform` | `motion.fast` with `ease.standard` |
| Press | a pose | the node's `UiTransform` | `motion.fast` with `ease.standard` |

Durations and curves come from the active theme's tokens (`motion.fast`, `motion.base`, `motion.slow`, `motion.page`,
`ease.standard`, `ease.enter`, `ease.exit`), so a child theme retimes every preset. A token the theme lacks keeps the
spec value. Poses change only the visual transform: layout, siblings and the layout rect stay put.

Named sets:

| Set | Enter / exit | Hover | Press | Speed | Exit action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `button` | - | - | `sink` (1 px down) | - | - |
| `card` | - | `lift` (2 px up) | `sink` | - | - |
| `popup` | zoom 0.96 | - | - | `slow` | hide |
| `dialog` | slide 12 px | - | - | `slow` | hide |
| `toast` | slide 24 px | - | - | `slow` | despawn |
| `page` | fade | - | - | `page` | hide |

Rules the driver (`run_ui_motion`, `Update`) follows:

- The enter plays when the presets are added (`enter_on_add`, on by default in code, off by default through the agent)
  and on request. An exit plays on request. A node in the middle of an enter or exit turns round from where it is.
- Hover follows the pointer (`Hovered`), or focus in gamepad / keyboard navigation (`Focused` while the input mode is
  navigation). Hover is off in touch mode. Press follows `Pressed`; without a press pose the hover pose stays. A
  disabled node rests.
- A tween the game or `ui.tween` started is not replaced by a pose: the pose follows when it ends. Enter and exit
  replace any running tween.
- An exit with no exit preset hides or despawns at once; an enter with no enter preset shows at once.

## Reduced motion

Reduced motion is on when either source is: `ActiveTheme::reduced_motion` (the host's theme selection) or the player's
setting `GameSettings.accessibility.reduced_motion` (`ui.accessibility {"reduced_motion": true}`, see
[UI accessibility](book/agents/ui-accessibility.md)). Then:

- Presets follow the spec: transforms (slide, zoom, poses) jump, opacity fades are capped at `motion.fast`.
- Plain tweens (`ui.tween`, game code) jump to their end value.
- A theme swap applies at once instead of cross-fading.

`ui.motion` with no parameters reports both sources and the effective value.

## Method

`ui.motion { action?, entity?, ... }`

| Action | Parameters | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `query` (default) | `entity?` | Without `entity`: `{ reduced_motion: { effective, theme, accessibility }, tokens: { fast, base, slow, page, ease_standard, ease_enter, ease_exit }, presets, poses, count, truncated, nodes }` (at most 64 nodes). With `entity`: the node (below). |
| `set` | `entity`, `preset?`, `enter?`, `exit?`, `hover?`, `press?`, `speed?`, `exit_action?`, `enter_on_add?` | Adds or edits the node's presets. Starts from the named `preset` set, else the node's current presets. A field set to `null` removes that preset. |
| `play` | `entity`, `trigger` (`enter` or `exit`) | Queues the enter or exit; it starts on the next update. |
| `clear` | `entity` | Removes the presets. Answers `{ entity, cleared }`. |

Value shapes: a reveal is `"fade"`, `"slide"` (24 px down), `"zoom"` (0.96), `{"slide": [x, y]}` or `{"zoom": s}`. A pose is
a name or `{"translate": [x, y], "scale": s}` (each optional). Ease values in answers are a curve name or
`[x1, y1, x2, y2]`.

A node answer is `{ entity, motion, state: { phase, pose, pending, running }, tweening, plans, reduced_motion }`.
`phase` is `shown`, `entering`, `exiting` or `hidden`; `pose` is `rest`, `hover` or `press`. `plans` lists the tween each
preset would start now (`{ duration, parts: [{ property, from, to, duration, ease }] }`), with reduced motion applied, so
an agent can check timing without running frames.

```json
{"method": "ui.motion", "params": {"action": "set", "entity": 4294967321, "preset": "dialog"}}
{"method": "ui.motion", "params": {"action": "play", "entity": 4294967321, "trigger": "enter"}}
{"method": "play.wait_until", "params": {"condition": {"predicate": "ui.tweening", "entity": 4294967321, "is": false}}}
{"method": "ui.motion", "params": {"entity": 4294967321}}
```

A `despawn` exit removes the node, so wait for it with the `ui.tweening` atom without `entity`, or with `ui.query`.

## Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `missing_entity` | `entity` is required for this action |
| `bad_entity` | `entity` is not entity bits |
| `unknown_entity` | the entity does not exist |
| `bad_action` | `action` is not `query`, `set`, `play` or `clear` |
| `bad_preset` | `preset` names no preset set |
| `bad_reveal` | `enter` or `exit` has the wrong shape |
| `bad_pose` | `hover` or `press` has the wrong shape |
| `bad_speed` | `speed` is not `fast`, `base`, `slow` or `page` |
| `bad_exit_action` | `exit_action` is not `hide` or `despawn` |
| `bad_value` | `enter_on_add` is not a boolean |
| `bad_trigger` | `trigger` is not `enter` or `exit` |
| `no_motion` | `play` on a node without presets |

## In code

```rust,ignore
use regia_ui::{MotionPose, RevealPreset, UiMotion, UiMotionState};

// A popup that zooms in when spawned and out when closed.
commands.spawn((popup_node, UiMotion::preset("popup").unwrap_or_default()));
// Later: close it.
state.request_exit(); // state: Mut<UiMotionState> of the popup
// A custom tile.
let tile = UiMotion::new()
    .with_reveal(RevealPreset::Slide([0.0, 16.0]))
    .with_hover(MotionPose::GROW)
    .with_press(MotionPose::SHRINK);
```

## Limits

- Poses and reveals share the node's `UiTransform`; a game transform on the same node is overwritten while a preset runs.
- Timing follows the active theme, not a `ThemeScope` subtree theme.
- Scale does not scale border width, corner radius, shadow blur or glyph size (see [UI tweens](book/agents/ui-animation.md)).
