# UI accessibility tree and screen readers (agents)

UI series L14, ADR-865 (roadmap L03). `regia_ui::a11y` builds a platform-neutral accessibility tree from the
runtime UI and hands its changes to a screen-reader backend. Accessibility settings (text scale, reduced motion,
right-to-left layout) are a separate page: [UI accessibility](book/agents/ui-accessibility.md).

## The tree

`build_a11y_tree(world)` walks every `UiRoot` (by `sort_order`) depth first. For each node:

- **Role** from the widget: `UiRoot` → `window`, `Button` → `button`, `Toggle` → `check_box`, `Slider` → `slider`,
  `ProgressBar` → `progress_bar`, `TextInput` → `text_input`, `Dropdown` → `combo_box`, `TabBar` → `tab_list`,
  `Modal` → `dialog`, `RadialMenu` → `menu`, `ListView` → `list`, `ScrollView` → `scroll_view`, `Text` → `label`,
  `UiImage` → `image`, anything else → `group`. `heading`, `region`, `status` and `alert` come only from
  `Accessible`.
- **Name**: `Accessible::label_key` (a localization key, used when the table defines it) or `Accessible::label`,
  else the node's own text, else the text of its label children (childless `Text`
  children, which then do not appear on their own), else a text field's placeholder.
- **Description and hint**: `Accessible::description` and `Accessible::hint`, each with a `_key` form that resolves
  through `Localization` (the literal is the fallback when the key is undefined; an undefined key with no literal
  shows the table's missing-key text). The tree is rebuilt every frame while a reader is live, so a locale change
  re-resolves them, and the diff reports a `name_changed`. The hint is a short usage line ("Double tap to open") read
  last in the spoken summary.
- **Value**: a slider's number, a progress bar's percentage, a text field's text (masked when it is secret), the
  selected option of a dropdown or the active tab.
- **States**: `focused`, `focusable`, `disabled`, `selected`, `invalid`, `checked` (check boxes), `expanded`
  (dropdowns, dialogs), `inert` (outside the top input layer, such as a menu under an open dialog) and
  `read_only` (a text field that takes no edits).
- **Bounds** from the layout, in physical px.

An unnamed container with no role, no `Accessible` and no focus is flattened: its children move up to its parent.
`Display::None` subtrees and nodes with `Accessible { hidden: true }` (`Accessible::decorative()`) are left out.

`spoken_summary()` is what a reader says on focus, for example "Volume, slider, 50" or "Subtitles, check box,
checked".

## The custom-widget hook

Add `Accessible` to a node to set what inference cannot know:

```rust,wrap
# use regia::prelude::*;
# use regia_core::math::{Vec3, Quat};
# use regia_scene::Transform;
# let mut commands: Commands = todo!();
# let world: &mut World = todo!();
# let app: &mut App = todo!();
# use regia_ui::a11y::*;
commands.spawn((UiNode, Text::new("Ready"), Accessible::default()
    .with_role(A11yRole::Status)
    .with_live(Politeness::Polite)));
```

A live region (`live` polite or assertive) announces its new name or value whenever it changes.

## Backends

`ScreenReaderBackend` is the platform seam: `name`, `is_active`, `tree_updated(tree, events)` and, for recorders,
`recent_events`. The `ScreenReader` resource owns the backend. Each frame (after text shaping) `sync_screen_reader`
rebuilds the tree only while the backend is active or exporting was turned on (`ScreenReader::set_exporting`), so a
game with no screen reader pays nothing. It diffs the tree against the last one and sends `added`, `removed`,
`name_changed`, `value_changed`, `states_changed`, `screen_changed`, `focus_changed` and `announcement` events.
`screen_changed` fires when the top input layer changes (a dialog opened or closed, `from` and `to` are the layer
roots), so a bridge knows when to move the reader's cursor. The first sync after
activation reports every node as added. `ScreenReader::announce(text, politeness)` queues speech.

- **Linux**: `atspi::AtSpiStub` maps roles onto AT-SPI 2 role names ("push button", "check box", "entry", ...) and
  events onto the signals an AT-SPI bridge emits (`object:children-changed:add`, `object:state-changed:focused`,
  `object:property-change:accessible-name`, `object:announcement`, ...), with object paths
  `/org/a11y/atspi/accessible/<id>`. It records them and does not connect to D-Bus yet. It is active when
  `REGIA_SCREEN_READER=1`.
- **Windows, macOS, Android**: no backend yet (`none`). UI Automation, NSAccessibility and Android
  `AccessibilityNodeInfo` bridges plug into the same trait.

## Requests: what a reader can do

Reading is half of it. A reader also presses, steps, types, focuses, dismisses and scrolls. An `A11yRequest` is a
node id plus an `A11yAction`; a backend queues them (`ScreenReaderBackend::drain_requests`, empty by default) and
`route_a11y_requests` (`PreUpdate`, only while the reader is live) runs each through `apply_request`, which checks it
against a fresh tree and sends it down the path a key press, click or wheel takes. Then it tells the backend how it
ended (`request_result`).

| Action | Does | Refused when |
|---|---|---|
| `press` | clicks a button, flips a check box, opens a combo box, focuses a text field | slider, or a node that is not a control |
| `raise`, `lower` | steps a slider by its own `step` (a tenth of its range when it has none), clamped | not a slider |
| `set_text` | replaces a text field's text the way typing it would: control characters are stripped, `max_chars` cuts whole grapheme clusters | not a text field, it is read-only, the field's filter refuses the text, or the text is longer than 4096 characters |
| `focus` | moves keyboard focus (the focus ring shows, as after a Tab) | node is not focusable |
| `close` | dismisses the dialog the node is, or is inside, the way Cancel does | no dialog, or `close_on_cancel` is off |
| `scroll_into_view` | scrolls the enclosing scroll view until the node shows | no enclosing scroll view |
| `page_up`, `page_down`, `page_left`, `page_right` | scrolls the node's scroll view (or the enclosing one) by 90% of its size | no scroll view |

Every request is refused, with no effect, when the node is unknown or not in the tree (`unknown_node`), `Disabled`
(`node_disabled`, as a click on a disabled control is) or outside the top input layer (`node_inert`, a menu under
an open dialog). Widgets react in the same update, so the result shows after the next frame.

`RecordingReader` is the headless backend for tests: always active, records events and request results, and takes
requests through its `RecordingHandle`. The OS bridge is the `accesskit` feature (ADR-1998): see
[Screen-reader OS bridge](book/agents/ui-a11y-platform.md) for the platform tree and simulated platform actions. Without it,
`atspi::request_from_call(path, action, text)` maps AT-SPI calls to requests and `AtSpiStub::request_queue()` takes
them.

## Methods

- `ui.a11y_tree { node? }` (read-only, permission `read`). Builds the tree now, whatever the backend. `node`
  (alias `entity`) limits it to one node and its descendants. Returns `{ backend, live, builds, focus, count,
  top_layer, nodes: [{ id, parent, children, role, name, description, hint, value, states, bounds, live,
  summary }], announcements, backend_events, requests: [{ node, action, accepted, reason }], sync_cost }`. `backend_events` are the backend's last 64 signals (the AT-SPI stub's on
  Linux). `sync_cost` (ADR-5379) is `{ samples, total, mean_ms, p99_ms, max_ms, stages_mean_ms, ui_entities }`: what the per-frame screen-reader
  sync (`regia_ui::a11y::sync_screen_reader`) cost on its last 512 live frames (a reader connected, or exporting
  on). `stages_mean_ms` splits the mean into `build`, `diff` and `backend`; `ui_entities` is the UI node count. Frames with no reader cost one resource lookup and are not counted. `null` without a `ScreenReader`.
- `ui.a11y_announce { text, priority? }` (permission `play`). Queues `text` for the next frame. `priority` is
  `polite` (default) or `assertive`. Returns `{ queued, backend, live, priority }`.
- `ui.a11y_act { node, action, value? }` (permission `play`). Does what a reader's request would (table above).
  `node` (alias `entity`) is a tree node id; `action` is one of `press`, `raise`, `lower`, `set_text`, `focus`,
  `close`, `scroll_into_view`, `page_up`, `page_down`, `page_left`, `page_right`; `value` is the text for `set_text`.
  Returns `{ node, action, accepted, summary, note }` where `summary` is the node's spoken summary as of the call;
  the widgets react in the next frame, so wait a frame (`wait_until`) and read `ui.a11y_tree` for the result.
  `ui.a11y_tree` lists the last 32 requests with `accepted` and the refusal `reason`.

```json
{"method": "ui.a11y_tree", "params": {}}
{"method": "ui.a11y_announce", "params": {"text": "Checkpoint reached", "priority": "assertive"}}
{"method": "ui.a11y_act", "params": {"node": 4294967300, "action": "raise"}}
{"method": "ui.a11y_act", "params": {"node": 4294967310, "action": "set_text", "value": "Ada"}}
```

Checks worth automating: every focusable node has a non-empty `name`; nothing outside an open dialog is focusable
without `inert`; a status text is a live region.

## Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `bad_entity` | `node` is not a node id |
| `unknown_entity` | the entity does not exist |
| `not_in_tree` | the node is hidden, decorative or a flattened container |
| `a11y_text_missing` | `text` is missing |
| `bad_text` | `text` is not a non-empty string |
| `text_too_long` | `text` has more than 1024 characters, or `set_text`'s `value` more than 4096 |
| `bad_priority` | `priority` is not `polite` or `assertive` |
| `a11y_node_missing` | `ui.a11y_act` without `node` |
| `a11y_action_missing` | `ui.a11y_act` without `action` |
| `a11y_value_missing` | `set_text` without `value` |
| `bad_action` | `action` is not a string, or not one of the eleven names |
| `bad_value` | `value` is not a string |
| `unknown_node` | the node is gone, hidden, decorative or a flattened container |
| `node_disabled` | the node is `Disabled` |
| `node_inert` | the node is outside the top input layer |
| `unsupported_action` | the node cannot do that action (see the table) |
| `not_dismissable` | the dialog has `close_on_cancel` off |
| `no_scroll_view` | the node is in no scroll view |
| `ui_not_installed` | the app has no `ScreenReader` (no `UiPlugin`) |

## Known limits

- Without the `accesskit` feature no backend talks to a real screen reader: the AT-SPI stub records signals only.
  With it, [the OS bridge](book/agents/ui-a11y-platform.md) does (ADR-1998; TalkBack on Android is ADR-3454). Steam Deck
  game mode has no screen-reader path; desktop mode on the Deck is AT-SPI.
- Hints and labels take a key without arguments; a label that needs arguments is a `Text` child with a
  `TextContent::Loc`.
- Text inside a text field is reported as one value; caret and selection are not exported.
- List rows are exported as they exist: a virtualised list exposes only its live rows.
- The tree walk is bounded: at most 512 hierarchy levels (`MAX_A11Y_DEPTH`) and 65,536 nodes (`MAX_A11Y_NODES`),
  depth first, so the first nodes in reading order are kept; past either limit the rest is left out and a warning
  is logged.

<!-- source: book/agents/ui-theme-switch.md -->
# UI runtime theme switch (agents)

UI series D15, ADR-865 and ADR-1309. Builds on the theme resolver (D6, ADR-289): writing `ActiveTheme` swaps the
theme on the next frame and cross-fades every themed node's colors over the theme's `motion.base` (160 ms in the
built-in themes), along its `ease.standard` curve, blended in OKLab. This page covers what makes the swap complete
on screen, how to shape the fade, the change messages and the `ui.theme_mode` method.

## What follows the theme

- **Background, border and text colors** of every themed node (a node with `Classes` or a `ThemeOverride`)
  cross-fade together. A second switch during a fade starts from the colors on screen, so nothing jumps.
- **Label text.** The themed node's own `Text` and its label children (childless `Text` children without a look of
  their own) take the theme's text color every frame of the fade. Glyphs are recolored without a reshape.
  Only theme-owned spans change: spans at the default color (`TextStyle::default().color`) or at the color the theme
  wrote last. Authored colors (a red warning) stay. Add `KeepTextColor` to a `Text` to opt it out.
- **High contrast and reduced motion.** The player's `UiAccessibility::high_contrast` selects
  `<theme>-high-contrast` when loaded, else `regia-high-contrast`. The built-ins ship both `regia-high-contrast`
  (dark) and `regia-light-high-contrast`, so a light-scheme player stays light. `reduced_motion` makes the swap
  instant. They are copied into `ActiveTheme` when the setting changes. On the first frame only settings that are on
  are copied, so a host that preset `ActiveTheme::high_contrast` keeps it.
- **Scheme preference.** `ThemeMode { follow, dark, light, system_scheme }` selects `dark` or `light` (default
  `regia-dark` / `regia-light`) for a `dark`, `light` or `system` preference. With `follow: None` (the default)
  the host selects themes directly.
- **OS appearance.** The platform writes `SystemThemeChanged { window, dark }` and `system_scheme` follows it: on
  Windows and macOS when the window opens and whenever the OS appearance changes (winit); on Android from the
  activity's night mode when the window opens, on every resume and on every configuration change. Linux reports none
  yet: there the host writes `system_scheme` itself, or an agent passes `system_scheme`.
- **Settings menu.** A game stores the player's choice in `GameSettings` `accessibility.color_scheme` (`Dark`,
  `Light`, `System`, or `None` to leave it to the game); the settings plugin copies it into `ThemeMode::follow` and
  persists it with the other settings.

Idle frames never bump the theme generation; a change costs one generation.

## Shaping the swap fade

The `ThemeTransition` resource shapes the next swap (a running fade keeps the settings it started with):

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `duration` | `None`: the new theme's `motion.base` | Fade length in seconds, clamped to 0..10; `Some(0.0)` swaps at once |
| `ease` | `None`: the new theme's `ease.standard` (linear if missing) | `Easing::Linear` or `Easing::CubicBezier([x1, y1, x2, y2])` |
| `space` | `BlendSpace::Oklab` | `Oklab` moves lightness evenly; `Linear` is the plain linear-light blend |

Why OKLab: a linear-light blend from a dark surface to a white one is already at half the light's luminance a
quarter of the way in, which reads as most of the way to light: the screen seems to flash. OKLab interpolates
perceptual lightness, so the fade brightens evenly. A fill fading from or to transparent keeps its color and changes
only its alpha. State transitions (hover, pressed, selected) keep their own `transition` timing; a node whose state
changes mid-swap leaves the swap fade and animates to its new look.

Reduced motion (`ActiveTheme::reduced_motion` or the player's setting) still makes every swap instant.

## Change messages

- `ThemeChanged { from, to, generation, fade_secs }`: written in the frame a new theme generation applies (any
  `ActiveTheme` change, a density change or a theme set change). `from` is `None` for the first generation.
- `ThemeFadeFinished { theme, generation }`: written in the frame the cross-fade ends. An instant swap writes it in
  the same frame as its `ThemeChanged`; a swap replaced mid-fade by another writes it only for the last one.

A game switches its own non-UI colors (clear color, post-process tint) on these, in step with the UI.

## Method

`ui.theme_mode { theme?, follow?, system_scheme?, dark?, light?, high_contrast?, reduced_motion?, transition? }`
(permission `edit_scene`). With no parameters it only reports.

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `theme` | Select a loaded theme; following a scheme stops. |
| `follow` | `dark`, `light`, `system` or `off`. |
| `system_scheme` | `dark`, `light` or `unknown` (reads as dark): stands in for the OS setting. |
| `dark`, `light` | The themes the two schemes select. |
| `high_contrast`, `reduced_motion` | The live theme flags (`ui.accessibility` changes the player's settings instead). |
| `transition` | `{ duration_ms?, ease?, space? }` for the next swap. `duration_ms`: 0 to 10000, or `null` for the theme's `motion.base`. `ease`: `"theme"` (the theme's `ease.standard`), `"linear"`, `"cubic-bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2)"` or `[x1, y1, x2, y2]` (x values in 0..1). `space`: `"oklab"` or `"linear"`. Fields left out are kept. |

Result: `{ active, requested, previous, generation, applies_at_generation, animating, fade_seconds, transition,
fade, follow, system_scheme, dark, light, high_contrast, reduced_motion, themes }`.

- `active` is the theme nodes resolve against (after the high-contrast and fallback rules); `previous` the one
  before the last generation.
- `animating` counts nodes with any color animation running (swap or state transition).
- `fade_seconds` is the length the next swap would run.
- `transition` echoes the settings: `{ duration_ms (null = theme), ease ("theme", "linear" or [x1, y1, x2, y2]),
  space }`.
- `fade` describes the last swap: `{ fading, nodes, seconds, remaining_seconds, ease, space }`.

Wait for a swap to settle before a screenshot with the `ui.theme_fading` atom:

```json
{"method": "play.wait_until", "params": {"condition": {"predicate": "ui.theme_fading", "is": false}}}
```

The atom `{ predicate: "ui.theme_fading", is? }` holds when whether a swap fade runs equals `is` (default `true`).
It is broken (`bad_flag`) when `is` is not a boolean and (`ui_not_installed`) without the UI plugin.

```json
{"method": "ui.theme_mode", "params": {"theme": "regia-light"}}
{"method": "ui.theme_mode", "params": {"follow": "system", "system_scheme": "light"}}
{"method": "ui.theme_mode", "params": {"high_contrast": true}}
{"method": "ui.theme_mode", "params": {"transition": {"duration_ms": 400, "ease": "linear", "space": "oklab"}, "theme": "regia-light"}}
```

## Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `unknown_theme` | no loaded theme has that name (`themes` lists them) |
| `bad_theme` | a theme parameter is not a non-empty string |
| `bad_follow` | `follow` is not `dark`, `light`, `system` or `off` |
| `bad_scheme` | `system_scheme` is not `dark`, `light` or `unknown` |
| `bad_flag` | `high_contrast` or `reduced_motion` is not a boolean |
| `theme_and_follow` | both `theme` and a `follow` preference were given |
| `bad_transition` | `transition` is not an object, or has a field other than `duration_ms`, `ease`, `space` |
| `bad_duration` | `transition.duration_ms` is not a number from 0 to 10000 (or `null`) |
| `bad_ease` | `transition.ease` is not `"theme"`, `"linear"`, a `cubic-bezier(...)` string or four numbers with x in 0..1 |
| `bad_space` | `transition.space` is not `"oklab"` or `"linear"` |
| `ui_not_installed` | the app has no runtime UI themes |

## Known limits

- The OS light/dark setting reaches the engine on Windows, macOS and Android; on Linux the host feeds
  `ThemeMode::system_scheme`.
- Geometry (radius, border width, and a theme's `height`, `padding_x` and `gap`, which reach layout since ADR-9340)
  changes at the first frame of a swap; only colors fade.
- Images, icons with baked colors, and explicit `Background` components do not cross-fade.
- A text color tween (`ui.tween`) and a theme fade on the same text at the same time: the theme wins for that frame.

<!-- source: book/agents/ui-icons.md -->
# UI icons (agents)

UI series D16, ADR-865; spec `docs/specs/ui-default-design.md` § 2.7. `regia_ui::icons` is the icon mechanism:
atlases of named drawings at several sizes, the scaling rules, and tinting from the theme. The engine ships no icon
artwork: the default set is an owner choice (spec § 9 Q3, UI D4).

## Loading icons

An `IconSheet` is RGBA8 pages plus named rectangles (`IconSprite { name, page, rect }`).

- `IconSheet::from_grid(page, [w, h], names)` cuts one page into cells, row by row (an empty name skips a cell).
- A cooked `.atlas.ron` sprite atlas (`regia_2d::SpriteAtlas`) maps onto it one to one: each page becomes an
  `IconPage`, each sprite an `IconSprite` with its packed `rect`. `regia_ui` does not depend on `regia_2d`, so the
  host does this conversion; no new content format is involved.

Name a drawing `name@size` (`gear@16`, `gear@24`) to give one icon several drawings; a name with no `@size` is
drawn at its source height. `IconAtlas::add_sheet(sheet)` validates the sheet (`icon_bad_page`, `icon_bad_rect`,
`icon_bad_name`, `icon_duplicate`, `icon_bad_grid`), gives its pages renderer image ids from `ICON_IMAGE_BASE` up,
and adds the drawings. A later sheet's drawing replaces an earlier one at the same size. Pages reach the renderer in
`PostUpdate`.

Draw icons white on transparent: the tint multiplies them.

## Drawing an icon

```rust,wrap
# use regia::prelude::*;
# use regia_core::math::{Vec3, Quat};
# use regia_scene::Transform;
# let mut commands: Commands = todo!();
# let world: &mut World = todo!();
# let app: &mut App = todo!();
# use regia_ui::icons::*;
commands.spawn((UiNode, Icon::new("gear").with_size(IconSize::Small)));
```

- **Size** (`IconSize`): `Small`, `Medium` (default) and `Large` are the theme's `size.icon.sm/md/lg` (16 / 24 / 32
  comfortable, 12 / 16 / 20 compact); `Px(n)` is `n` UI px. The node is laid out at that size unless the author set its
  size (a node whose size is `Auto`, or still the size the icon wrote, follows the icon).
- **Scaling rules**, for the size in physical px (UI size times the UI scale):
  1. a drawing within 1 px of it draws at its own size, texel for texel;
  2. otherwise the smallest larger drawing, scaled down to whole pixels;
  3. otherwise the largest drawing, scaled up, flagged `upscaled` (softer).
- **Tint** (`IconTint`): `Theme` (default) takes the nearest themed ancestor's `icon_color`, else its text color, else
  the theme's `color.text`, so icons follow a theme switch and its cross-fade. `Color(c)` is fixed. `Original` keeps
  full-color artwork.

`IconState` records the outcome on the node: `missing`, `variant_px`, `draw_px`, `upscaled`, `tint`, `ui_px`. A
missing icon draws nothing.

## Method

`ui.icons { entity? }` (read-only, permission `read`).

- Without `entity`: `{ sheets, generation, pending_pages, icons: [{ name, sizes }], nodes: [...], missing,
  upscaled }`. `missing` lists the names of icon nodes whose icon is not loaded; `upscaled` counts soft icons.
- With `entity` (alias `node`): that node's `{ entity, name, missing, ui_px, variant_px, draw_px, upscaled, tint,
  resolved }`.

```json
{"method": "ui.icons", "params": {}}
{"method": "ui.icons", "params": {"entity": 4294967330}}
```

Checks worth automating: `missing` is empty; `upscaled` is 0 at the sizes the game uses.

The handler's lower-case reasons appear in `error.data.code`; malformed ids use JSON-RPC `-32602`, while absent
entities, non-icon nodes and an unavailable atlas use `-32001`, `-32001` and `-32004`, respectively.

## Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `bad_entity` | `entity` is not a node id |
| `unknown_entity` | the entity does not exist |
| `not_an_icon` | the entity has no `Icon` |
| `ui_not_installed` | the app has no `IconAtlas` (no `UiPlugin`) |

## Workflow

Call `ui.icons {}` to find missing or upscaled names, then use `ui.query` to find an icon node and call `ui.icons` with
its id to inspect the selected drawing and tint.

## Known limits

- `<icon=name>` in rich text still makes a span with the family `icon-name`, not an inline icon: inline icons need
  the text shaper to reserve space for an image (follow-up with D4).
- No signed-distance-field icons: very large icons scale up a bitmap. Ship a large drawing (`@64`) for them.

Captured failure on lavapipe:

Request:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":6,"method":"ui.icons","params":{"entity":0}}
```

Response:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":6,"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"`entity` must be a node id from ui.query","data":{"code":"bad_entity","hint":"omit it to list every icon"}}}
```

<!-- source: book/agents/ui-glyph-atlas.md -->
# UI glyph atlas (agents)

ADR-8832; spec `docs/specs/18-runtime-ui.md` § 2. The runtime UI rasterizes glyphs on demand into atlas pages:
`max_pages` square pages of `page_size` pixels for monochrome glyphs (R8) and as many for color glyphs (RGBA8),
shelf-packed. A glyph is keyed by face, size, weight and sub-pixel position, so the same letter at two sizes or two
sub-pixel offsets takes two slots.

## Read the atlas

`ui.glyph_atlas` (read-only, no parameters):

```json
{ "method": "ui.glyph_atlas" }
→ { "page_size": 512, "max_pages": 8, "mono_pages": 3, "color_pages": 1, "glyphs": 412,
    "wipes": 0, "thrash": 0, "thrash_frames": 0 }
```

- `mono_pages`, `color_pages`: pages in use per kind (at most `max_pages` each).
- `glyphs`: glyphs cached across both kinds.
- `wipes`: pages recycled so far. When every page of a kind is full, the least recently used page is cleared and
  its glyphs re-rasterize when next drawn. A few wipes after a screen change are normal.
- `thrash`: glyphs that were not drawn because every page of their kind held glyphs the same frame had already
  drawn. The UI extract pins each page it draws from until the frame ends, so a page is never recycled under quads
  that still point into it (the glyph would otherwise show another glyph's bitmap for a frame). A glyph that cannot
  fit is refused instead: it is missing from that frame. `thrash_frames` counts the frames that refused at least one
  glyph; the engine logs a `regia_ui` warning on the first such frame and then at every power of two.

`thrash` above 0 means one screen needs more distinct glyphs than the pages hold: many sizes, a dense CJK screen at
several sizes, or many sub-pixel positions. Fewer sizes, or `SdfText` for large text, bring it back to 0.

Errors: `ui_not_installed` (`F0013`): the app has no UI renderer (`regia_ui::UiPlugin`).

## Check it

```bash
cargo test -p regia_ui --lib atlas
cargo test -p regia_agent --lib ui_glyph_atlas
```

<!-- source: book/agents/ui-backdrop-blur.md -->
# UI backdrop blur (agents)

UI parity T11 / master-plan F7, ADR-1836. A node with `BackdropBlur { radius }` shows frosted glass: the frame
already drawn under its rect (the 3D scene and any earlier UI) is blurred with a Gaussian, through the node's
rounded rect, before the node's own background paints on top. Give the node a translucent `Background` for the
glass tint.

## In code

```rust,ignore
commands.spawn((
    UiNode,
    BackdropBlur { radius: 10.0 },          // Gaussian sigma in UI px
    Background { kind: BackgroundKind::Color(UiColor([0.05, 0.07, 0.1, 0.45])) },
    Border { radius: [12.0; 4], ..default() },
));
```

- `radius` is the Gaussian sigma in UI px (scaled by the UI scale), clamped to 0..=64 physical px; 0 or less draws
  nothing.
- The blur follows the node's corner radius (the `Border` radius or the theme radius) and the node's `Opacity`.
- Below the node in paint order is what gets blurred: earlier siblings, the parent's background and the scene.
  Children and later siblings draw sharp over it.
- Lower-level: a `UiQuad` with `texture: TextureRef::Backdrop` and `blur` = sigma does the same; follow it with a
  tint quad.

In a `.ui.ron` file (format v5) the same flag is the node field `backdrop_blur: 12.0`; absent means off.

## In the editor

The viewport's overlay chips (the stats block and the view label) can sit on frosted glass too:
`editor.set_viewport { overlay_blur: 8 }` (Gaussian sigma in points, 0 to 64; 0 is off, the default). The pane's finished
picture is blurred under each chip before egui samples it, on the GPU path with these same quads and on the software
path with `regia_ui::cpu_backdrop_blur`. `editor.viewport_stats` reports `overlay_blur: { chips, shaded_pixels }`. A tool
overlay with its own chip calls `regia_editor::viewport_blur::blur_behind_chips`.

## How it draws

The overlay pass splits at each backdrop quad: the frame region under it (plus the blur reach) is copied into a
scratch texture, blurred by a horizontal pass that also downsamples (factor 1, 2 or 4 for sigma up to 4, 16, 64)
and a vertical pass, and the result is composited through the quad's rounded rect in the next overlay pass. Factor 4
has a box prefilter pass first, so a thin line behind the panel does not flicker as it moves (at factor 2 the bilinear
taps already cover the block under them). All passes are scissored to the quad, so cost follows the panel size, not the
screen. Work is in the target's own space (linear for sRGB targets), so a black and white edge blurs to the linear mid
value. `regia_ui::cpu_backdrop_blur` is the ideal result on the CPU; `tests/backdrop_oracle.rs` compares the GPU passes
with it.

Limits: the target must allow `COPY_SRC` (every window surface the engine configures, offscreen targets and
screenshots do; a surface that cannot be read back skips the blur). At most 192 blur passes per frame (two per quad,
three at factor 4); later quads draw their tint only, and `ui.backdrop_stats` counts them as `skipped`. HDR and display-calibrated frames that go through the intermediate target blur in that
target's space.

## Cost

Measured with `cargo bench -p regia_ui --bench backdrop_blur` (one tinted panel on a 1920x1080 target, the same
draw with and without the blur, median of 12 frames, each frame waited for). `cost_ms` is the blurred draw minus the
plain one. The run below is on the software adapter (llvmpipe, 2026-11-02, the build server), so the milliseconds are CPU
rasterization and only show how cost scales; `shaded_px` and `samples` (also in `ui.backdrop_stats`) do not depend on
the adapter and are the numbers to budget with.

| panel | sigma | factor | passes | shaded_px | samples | cost_ms (llvmpipe) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 320x180 | 4 | 1 | 2 | 124,936 | 3,123,400 | 5.0 |
| 320x180 | 16 | 2 | 2 | 37,584 | 1,841,616 | 8.3 |
| 640x360 | 8 | 2 | 2 | 124,936 | 3,123,400 | 5.2 |
| 640x360 | 32 | 4 | 3 | 66,984 | 1,959,216 | 7.1 |
| 1280x720 | 4 | 1 | 2 | 1,881,976 | 47,049,400 | 28.0 |
| 1280x720 | 16 | 2 | 2 | 495,624 | 24,285,576 | 19.1 |
| 1280x720 | 64 | 4 | 3 | 258,404 | 14,569,208 | 18.7 |
| 1920x1080 | 4 | 1 | 2 | 4,147,200 | 103,680,000 | 54.1 |
| 1920x1080 | 16 | 2 | 2 | 1,036,800 | 50,803,200 | 30.4 |
| 1920x1080 | 32 | 4 | 3 | 388,800 | 13,219,200 | 13.6 |

What it shows: cost follows the panel's area and the sigma inside one downsample factor, and drops at each step up in
factor (a full-screen sigma 32 panel costs a quarter of a full-screen sigma 4 panel). Keep blurred panels small, or use
a sigma of 8 or more so the work runs at half or quarter resolution. Numbers on a real card come from the same bench
with `REGIA_GPU_UUID=<uuid> REGIA_GPU_STRICT=1`; they are not in this page yet.

## Agent surface

- `ui.set_backdrop_blur { node | name | text | ..., radius }` (permission `edit_scene`) sets or, with `radius: 0`,
  removes the effect on the one node the filters name. Reply: `{ node, radius, previous, changed }`.

| Error `reason` | Code | When |
|---|---|---|
| `ui_radius_required` | `F0002` | `radius` is missing or not a finite number |
| `ui_radius_out_of_range` | `F0002` | `radius` is outside 0..=64 |
| `ui_node_required` | `F0002` | no node filter was given |
| `ui_node_not_found` | `F0003` | no node matches |
| `ui_node_ambiguous` | `F0002` | more than one node matches |

- `ui.backdrop_stats {}` (read) reports what the last window draw did: `{ nodes, quads, blurred, skipped, passes,
  shaded_pixels, samples, copied_pixels, live_targets, live_target_bytes, targets_created, targets_freed }`. The
  per-draw fields are zeros after a draw with no backdrop quads, including a draw where the UI is empty.
  `skipped` above zero means a tint-only panel: no readable target, or the pass limit. The last four are the blur's
  render-target pool right now (ADR-5420), not the last draw: see below.

## Render targets

The blur keeps its scratch textures between frames: one full-size copy of the frame, plus a pair at reduced size for
each downsample factor (1, 2 or 4) a draw has used at the current target size and format. `live_targets` counts them
(at most 7), `live_target_bytes` is their memory, and `targets_created` and `targets_freed` count since the renderer
was made (`live_targets` is always `targets_created - targets_freed`). Closing a frosted panel keeps the pool
for 120 consecutive window draws without a successful backdrop blur (ADR-7869), so a quick reopen creates
nothing. At the 120th idle draw the pool releases all targets and their bind groups. Empty UI lists and
skipped blurs count as idle; a successful blur resets the count. A resize or a format change drops every
texture of the old size on the next blur, including pairs of
factors the new frame does not use. In Rust the same fields are on `UiRenderer::backdrop_stats()`
(`regia_ui::BackdropStats`).

For memory pressure, call `UiRenderer::trim_backdrop()` to release the targets immediately, even
when drawing is paused. Calling it again is harmless. It preserves the warmed pipelines and
uniform storage. `UiRenderer::BACKDROP_IDLE_FRAMES` documents the 120-draw idle limit. The next
blur allocates its frame copy and required downsample pair once, then returns to the warm path.
These counters measure references held by the pool; GPU work already submitted can retain its
resources until the device finishes it. There is no new agent method or error code.

After closing a panel, advance 120 window draws and call `ui.backdrop_stats {}`: expect
`live_targets: 0`, `live_target_bytes: 0`, and `targets_created == targets_freed`. Reopen once and
expect three live targets for one downsample factor; a second draw must not increase
`targets_created`. `tests/backdrop_targets.rs` checks this through the UI extraction/draw and
agent readout paths, as well as empty/skipped draws and restarting the idle count.

The baseline is the count after the first open and close: frame copy plus one pair per factor in use, so 3 for one
panel. If the live count rises after later short opens and closes at a fixed size, that is a leak. `tests/backdrop_targets.rs`
opens and closes a panel 50 times, at UI scale 1.0 and 2.25. After every close the count is back at the baseline,
and after the warm cycle the draws create no texture, pipeline or bind group.

To check a running game (the same 50 cycles on a device), toggle the blur on a panel that is on screen and read the
pool after each clear:

```text
ui.set_backdrop_blur { name: "controls.panel", radius: 12 }   # then let two frames draw
ui.backdrop_stats {}                                           # blurred: 1
ui.set_backdrop_blur { name: "controls.panel", radius: 0 }    # then let two frames draw
ui.backdrop_stats {}                                           # live_targets and targets_created as after cycle 1
```

Verify with `screenshot` before and after, or `ui.query` plus a screenshot crop.

<!-- source: book/agents/undo-redo.md -->
# Undo and redo in the editor

Every edit the editor makes, from a panel or an agent, is one entry on one shared undo stack. These
calls let an agent make the structural edits the outliner and inspector make, read the stack, and
step it. Each call below is one undo entry: an agent edit never merges into the edit before or
after it, unless it is inside an explicit transaction. See [shared history and recovery](book/agents/undo.md)
for the history panel, touched details, jump-to navigation and transaction methods.

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `editor.history {}` | `{ undo, redo, undo_depth, redo_depth, dirty, cap, remapped }`: `undo` and `redo` list what each step would do, next first ("Transform gizmo", "Set PointLight.intensity", "Delete 2 entities"); `dirty` is whether the level differs from its last save; `cap` is the history limit (500); `remapped` counts entity ids that an undo or redo changed. Read only. |
| `editor.spawn { name?, translation?, rotation?, scale?, parent? }` | Creates an entity in the open level (default name "New entity", at the origin, a root). With `parent`, the create and the parenting are one entry. Returns `{ entity, guid, name, parent, undoable }`. |
| `editor.delete { entities? }` | Deletes entities with their subtrees as one entry (`entities` absent = the selection). Undo brings them back with the same guids, components, level, parent and place among their siblings. Deleted entities leave the selection. An empty list is `F0002` with `data.hierarchy_error` `hierarchy_no_entities`. |
| `editor.reparent { entity, parent? }` | Moves an entity under `parent`, or to the root when `parent` is absent or `null`, as one entry. It is the outliner's move ([hierarchy drag and drop](book/agents/editor-hierarchy.md)): `entities` moves several at once and the world pose is kept unless `keep_world: false`. A cycle or the current parent is an `invalid_params` error (`data.reparent_error`), with no entry. |
| `editor.duplicate { entity }` | Copies the subtree with fresh guids, 1 m along +x, under the same parent. Returns the copy's root as `entity`. `entities` (or the selection) and `offset` duplicate several at once ([Outliner hierarchy edits](book/agents/hierarchy.md)); the copies become the selection. |
| `editor.add_component { entity, component, value? }` | Adds a reflected component: its default, or `value` in the JSON form `scene.get_entity` returns, with every field. If the entity already has it, the call is an error: use `editor.set_property`. |
| `editor.remove_component { entity, component }` | Removes a component; undo restores its value. |
| `editor.undo {}` / `editor.redo {}` | Step the stack: `{ undone \| redone, remaining, description, dirty }`. `description` is what was undone or redone. |

`editor.set_transform` and `editor.set_property` (on the [editor surface](book/agents/editor.md) page) are
one entry per call too.

## Ids across undo

Undoing a delete, or redoing a create, spawns the entities again: same guids, new entity ids.
The editor maps the old ids to the new ones, so the ids an agent already holds keep working in
every `editor.*` call that takes an entity, and the undo entries recorded before the delete keep
reaching the entity. Results always report the current id. Hosted scene-edit calls also follow
this map in the edit world. Scene read calls and runtime/play worlds use current ids: after an
undo, look the entity up again with `scene.query_entities` before making those calls.

## Dirty and saved

`dirty` compares the current state with the saved one, not the number of entries. Undoing back
to the last save makes the level clean again. Redoing past it, or editing after undoing below it,
makes it dirty. A level restored from an autosave stays dirty until it is saved.

## Errors

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `F0002` (`invalid_params`) | A missing or malformed parameter; an empty `entities`; a reparent cycle; `editor.add_component` on an entity that already has the component, or a `value` missing a field. A `dry_run` or `keep_world` on `editor.reparent` that is not a JSON boolean is not this error: `dry_run` counts as false and `keep_world` counts as true. |
| `F0003` (`not_found`) | The entity does not exist (an undo may have removed it), the component type is not registered, or the entity lacks the component to remove. |
| `F0001` (`internal`) | The spawn or insert did not take effect (see `logs.read`). |

## Example: build, check, undo everything

```console
$ BASE=$(regia agent call editor.spawn '{"name":"Base"}' | jq .entity)
$ ROCK=$(regia agent call editor.spawn "{\"name\":\"Rock\",\"parent\":$BASE,\"translation\":[1,0,0]}" | jq .entity)
$ regia agent call editor.add_component "{\"entity\":$ROCK,\"component\":\"PointLight\"}"
$ regia agent call editor.delete "{\"entities\":[$BASE]}"
$ regia agent call editor.history
$ regia agent call editor.undo        # Base and Rock are back, under the same ids
$ regia agent call editor.set_transform "{\"entity\":$ROCK,\"translation\":[2,0,0]}"
```

## In the editor

Ctrl+Z undoes, and Ctrl+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y redoes (Cmd on macOS). These shortcuts do nothing while
a text field has focus, since the field has its own undo, or while the game is playing. The Edit
menu shows the next step's description. A gizmo drag, a slider scrub or a node drag is one entry.
The entry ends when the mouse button is released, so two drags are two entries.

## Asset panels on the shared stack

The asset panels' edits are entries on the same stack (P-322, ADR-8365): curve, chooser and data
tables, the car, trailer and aircraft in Vehicle Tuning, the Theme panel's draft, the UI Animation
editor's library and the UI designer's documents. `editor.undo` and Ctrl+Z step them like scene
edits. Each panel's own Undo button or method steps the same stack, but only when the next step is
an edit of the document that panel has open (otherwise it answers its nothing-to-undo error, as
before; the editor's Undo steps everything):
`editor.theme_panel_set { history: "undo" }`, `editor.ui_anim_edit { op: "undo" }`,
`editor.ui_designer_edit { op: "undo" }` and `editor.vehicle_tuning_undo { asset: "trailer" }`
(or `"aircraft"`); each answers with the state after the step, and while a transaction is open
they are refused with `transaction_active`, like `editor.undo`. The car's
`editor.vehicle_tuning_undo` and `editor.tables_panel_undo` step the shared stack whatever its next
step is. A discrete edit is one entry;
a drag is one entry however many frames it runs (the UI designer's drag of a field on several
selected nodes included). The panels' `undo` / `undo_depth` counts are the shared stack's.

A panel edit joins the stack at the next request boundary (before the next agent request, and at
the start of every frame), so the next `editor.history` lists it. An entry for a theme draft, UI
animation library or UI document that is no longer open changes nothing when stepped (the entry
stays); a table, car, trailer or aircraft entry opens its file again as it was left.

<!-- source: book/agents/editor-bake.md -->
# Bake runner panel (`editor.bake_gi`, `editor.bake_status`, `editor.bake_gi_cancel`)

The editor's **Bake runner** tab runs `regia bake-gi` ([Baking GI from meshes](book/agents/baked-gi-bake.md)) on a
built-in scene or one of the project's `.bake.ron` descriptions, shows its progress, can cancel it,
and shows the summary or the error. The bake runs in a child process: the path tracer gets its own
GPU device, the editor keeps drawing, and a crash in the bake leaves the editor running. The panel
and these methods share one state, so an agent sees a bake a user started and the other way round.
One bake runs at a time. To set a probe volume in the viewport and bake it, use the **Bake** tab
instead ([Baking from the editor](book/agents/baked-gi-editor.md)); its cancel method is `editor.bake_cancel`.

The editor runs the CLI named by `REGIA_CLI`, else `regia` next to the editor executable, else
`regia` on `PATH`. Build it with `cargo build -p regia_cli`.

## `editor.bake_gi`

Mutating, permission `assets`. Starts a bake and returns the status (the `editor.bake_status`
shape below).

| Param | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `scene` | string, required | `cornell`, `furnace`, `rolling-hills`, or a `.bake.ron` path (absolute, or relative to the open project). |
| `out` | string | The `.fgiv` to write. Default: beside the description (`maps/bore.bake.ron` → `maps/bore.fgiv`), or `.regia/bake/<name>.fgiv` in the project for a built-in. The folder is created. |
| `dry_run` | bool | Validate the description and lay out the probes without tracing (no GPU, nothing written). |
| `wait` | bool | Block until the bake finishes. Allowed only with `dry_run` (a full bake would freeze the editor). |
| `rays`, `samples`, `bounces`, `seed`, `probes_per_batch` | number | Override the description's trace settings (`--rays` and so on). |
| `no_filter` | bool | Skip the visibility-weighted filter. |

```json
{ "method": "editor.bake_gi", "params": { "scene": "maps/bore.bake.ron", "dry_run": true, "wait": true } }
```

## `editor.bake_status`

Read-only. Param `list` (bool, default false) adds `builtins` (the built-in scene names) and
`descriptions` (the project's `.bake.ron` files, project-relative, sorted; hidden folders and
`target` are skipped). The current or last bake:

- `job`: bakes started this session (the current one's number); `state`: `idle`, `running`,
  `succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled`; `running`.
- `scene`, `dry_run`, `out`, `args` (the exact `regia` arguments).
- `progress`: `{ stage, done, total, fraction, remaining, eta_seconds }` from the CLI's progress lines, or null
  (`eta_seconds` only from a checkpointed bake, ADR-3095; `checkpoint` reports the job output's checkpoint). It keeps
  the last value after the bake ends.
- `summary` on success: `dry_run`, `out`, `bytes`, `probes`, `valid`, `invalid` (null for a dry
  run), `bricks`, `seconds`, `device`, and the CLI's whole JSON summary under `cli`.
- `error` on failure: `{ code, path, message }`.
- `log`: the last 40 lines of the bake's stderr.

Poll it until `running` is false to follow a bake: the call is cheap, drains the bake's output
and never blocks.

## `editor.bake_gi_cancel`

Mutating, permission `assets`. Kills the running bake; nothing is written. Returns the status
with `cancelled: true`, or `cancelled: false` when no bake was running.

## Error codes

A bake that starts and then fails is **not** an RPC error: the call succeeds and the status has
`state: "failed"` with `error.code`:

- the CLI's description codes, passed through: `bake_scene_unknown`, `bake_source_missing`,
  `bake_desc_invalid` (with `error.path`, the key path at fault) and the other codes on
  [Baking GI from meshes](book/agents/baked-gi-bake.md);
- `bake_no_summary`: the CLI exited without a summary (no GPU adapter, a panic); `message`
  quotes its last stderr line and the exit status;
- `bake_failed`: the CLI printed `ok: false` without a code.

A bake that cannot start is an RPC error whose `data.bake_error` is:

- `bake_busy`: another bake is running (poll or cancel it first);
- `bake_spawn_failed`: the CLI could not be run (build it, or set `REGIA_CLI`);
- `bake_out_dir`: the output folder could not be created;
- `bake_wait_needs_dry_run`: `wait` was asked for a full bake.

## How to check a result

A dry run of a new description is the cheap check: `state: "succeeded"`, `summary.probes` and
`summary.bricks` match the layout you expect. After a full bake, `summary.invalid` counts the
probes the bake gave up on (inside geometry, under the terrain); open the volume in the level with
[Baked GI from the level](book/agents/baked-gi-maps.md) and look at it in the viewport.

<!-- source: book/agents/editor-budget.md -->
# Budget meters (`editor.budget`)

The Kit panel and the prefab-mode banner show **budget meters**: what a model, or every mesh of
the prefab being edited, measures against a model class's limits. They are the same limits as
`editor.model_report` (prop, character, vehicle, building; ADR-234 defaults) and the same limit
names for overrides. Measuring reads the glTF's JSON and the image headers only: no buffer is read
and no texture is decoded, so it is cheap enough to run on every kit open.

In the **Kit panel** the line `Budget <class> · <tris>/<limit> tris · <materials>/<limit>
materials · <MiB>/<limit> MiB` is colored by the worst meter, with a class picker beside it and
the meters under **Budget meters (n over)** (open by default when something is over). The class
defaults from `kit.json`: a kit whose skeleton root has the `{"tincal_kit": 1}` tag or whose kind
is `pilot` is a character, `hull` a vehicle, `structure` a building, anything else a prop.

In **prefab mode** the same line sits in the banner; hover it for the meters. It is measured again
when the prefab, the class, the entity count or the undo history changes, and on the ↻ button.

## `editor.budget`

Read-only. Params:

| Param | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | `scene` (default): every `MeshSource` of the edit world, which is the open prefab in prefab mode. `kit`: the Kit panel's model. |
| `class` | string | `prop`, `character`, `vehicle`, `building` or `hero`. Default: from `kit.json` for a kit; the banner's class (prop until changed) for a scene. |
| `limits` | object | Overrides over the class limits: `max_triangles`, `max_node_triangles`, `max_nodes`, `max_materials`, `max_materials_per_node`, `max_joints_per_skin`, `max_texture_dimension`, `max_texture_bytes`. 0 turns a check off. |

```json
{ "method": "editor.budget", "params": { "source": "kit", "class": "vehicle", "limits": { "max_triangles": 80000 } } }
```

Returns `{ source, prefab, budget, reports_read }` (`prefab` and `reports_read` for a scene only;
`reports_read` counts the model files read since the editor started, a cache hit reads none):

- `budget.class`, `budget.limits`, `budget.status` (the worst: `ok`, `near`, `over`), `budget.over`
  (rows over plus LOD levels that do not reduce).
- `budget.rows[]`, always in this order: `triangles`, `node_triangles`, `nodes`, `materials`,
  `materials_per_node`, `joints_per_skin`, `texture_side`, `texture_bytes`. Each is
  `{ key, label, subject, value, limit, fraction, status }`. `subject` names the peak: the node,
  skin or `material/slot` (a scene prefixes the model path, `assets/tree.glb: trunk`). `status` is
  `off` (limit 0), `ok`, `near` (at least 80 % of the limit) or `over`.
- `budget.lods[]` (kits): `{ level, authored, triangles, ratio, reduces }`. `ratio` is the share of
  LOD0's triangles; `reduces` is false when a level has no fewer triangles than the level above.
- `budget.models`, `budget.instances`, `budget.errors[]` (model files that could not be measured;
  any error makes the status `over`).

`editor.open_kit` returns the same `budget` object (the kit's class, default limits) beside its
other fields.

What counts:

- A kit counts LOD0: triangles of `_LOD<n>` nodes with n > 0 are left out of `triangles` (they are
  in `lods[]`). The cockpit model is not part of the hull's budget.
- A scene counts each `MeshSource` instance: triangles and nodes once per instance, texture memory
  once per model file, materials once per distinct material. A material override (`MeshSource.material`)
  replaces the model's own materials. Built-in primitives are left out.
- Texture memory is the report's estimate (width × height × 4 bytes × 4/3 for mips, once per
  distinct image). An image the header pass cannot size (a data URI, a path leaving the model's
  folder) counts as 0 × 0.

## Error codes (`data.budget_error`)

- `budget_bad_source`: `source` is not `scene` or `kit`.
- `budget_bad_class`: `class` is not one of the five.
- `budget_bad_limits`: an unknown limit name or a value of the wrong type.
- `budget_no_kit`: `source: "kit"` with no kit open.
- `budget_not_measured`: the kit's model could not be measured (the kit's warnings say why).

## How to check a result

Open the kit or the prefab, then read `budget.status` and the `over` rows. A failing LOD chain
shows as a `lods[]` entry with `reduces: false`. The panel and the banner draw exactly these
rows, so the JSON is what a user sees.

<!-- source: book/agents/editor-content-index.md -->
# Content Browser index (`editor.content_index`)

The Content Browser lists the project's `assets/` folder from a cached index (ADR-866):

- The tree is walked once, not twice per frame as before. The folder list and the asset list come
  from that one walk, with the same rules as `editor.list_assets`: hidden (`.`) entries and `.meta`
  sidecars are skipped, and files under a `*.meta` folder are not assets.
- The view for the current folder and search is built once and reused until the folder, the search
  or the index changes.
- Only the rows in view are laid out, so a folder of thousands of assets scrolls as cheaply as a
  short one.
- Outside changes (a file copied in, a folder deleted) are found by comparing every walked folder's
  modification time, at most once a second. That costs one `stat` per folder; only the folders that
  changed are listed again (ADR-1329; before, the whole tree was walked again). The live asset
  watcher re-lists the folders of the files it reports. The browser's own Import, New, Delete and
  Reimport rescan at once, and the ↻ button beside the toolbar forces a rescan.

## `editor.content_index`

Read-only. Params: `folder` (a folder from the folder list such as `assets/props`; default
`assets/`), `search` (a query in the [asset browser](book/agents/editor-asset-browser.md) syntax, any case; when
set it matches everywhere, best matches first), `limit` (paths returned, default 200, at most 5000),
`refresh` (check the folder times first and re-list the folders that changed; default false).

```json
{ "method": "editor.content_index", "params": { "search": "rock", "refresh": true } }
```

Returns:

- `root`, `assets` (how many assets are indexed), `folders` (how many folders are indexed);
- `visible` (the view's size) and `paths[]` (its first `limit` entries: `{ path, kind }`, kind as in
  `editor.list_assets`);
- `stale` (the refresh found a change);
- the counters `scans` (full walks), `stamp_checks` (folder-time checks), `views_built` (filtered
  views built) and `generation` (bumped by each walk or refresh);
- `dirs_read` (folders listed by walks and refreshes), `refreshes` (partial re-lists),
  `search_tested` (assets tested against a query) and `searches_narrowed` (searches that filtered the
  previous hits); see the [asset browser](book/agents/editor-asset-browser.md) page.

The counters are how an agent checks the browser's cost without a clock. With an unchanged tree,
repeated calls and redraws leave `scans` and `views_built` alone; a new search adds one view and
no walk.

Errors: no project open is a `not_found` error with `data.index_error = "index_no_project"`. A search
that is not a valid query fails with `data.index_error` set to `search_bad_type` or
`search_empty_filter` ([asset browser](book/agents/editor-asset-browser.md)).

`editor.list_assets` still walks the tree on every call, so it always answers from the disk. Its
`search` takes the same query syntax.

## Token completion

`editor.content_index { complete: "type:te" }` returns
`{ completion: "type:texture", candidates: ["type:texture"] }` without running a search or
requiring an open project. `completion` is null when no token can grow; `candidates` is a sorted,
deduplicated array of full queries. A non-string `complete` returns `bad_query` (JSON-RPC invalid parameters).

The Content Browser search box uses the same vocabulary and token parser. Tab completes the
last token and displays its candidates; further Tab presses cycle the retained candidates.
Editing the query starts a new completion sequence. Shift+Tab leaves the search field.

<!-- source: book/agents/editor-hierarchy.md -->
# Hierarchy drag and drop (`editor.reparent`)

In the Outliner, drag a row onto another row to parent it there, or onto the empty space under
the tree (it reads **Move to root** during a drag) to unparent it. The rest of the panel (search,
range select, hotkeys, group/duplicate/delete) is in [Outliner hierarchy edits](book/agents/hierarchy.md).

- **What moves.** Drag a selected row and the whole selection moves with it. Drag an unselected
  row and only that entity moves. A selected entity whose parent is also selected stays under
  its parent: the parent moves and the child rides along.
- **Where it ends up.** By default each entity keeps its place in the world: it gets the local
  transform that puts it where it was under the new parent. Hold **Alt** while dropping to keep
  the local transform instead, so the entity moves with its new parent. A parent that combines
  non-uniform scale with a rotation can shear its children; that shear cannot be stored in a
  translation-rotation-scale transform, so it is dropped.
- **Refused drops.** A row inside the dragged subtree (the drop would put an entity under itself)
  is outlined in the error color and the drop does nothing. A drop onto the current parent
  changes nothing and pushes nothing.
- **Undo.** The whole drop is one undo entry: one Ctrl+Z (or `editor.undo`) restores every parent
  and every local transform.

## `editor.reparent`

Mutating, permission `edit_scene`. The same move as a drop. This is the only `editor.reparent`:
the undo surface (`undo-redo.md`) and the Outliner surface (`hierarchy.md`) both describe this
method (ADR-1354).

| Param | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `entities` | array | Entity ids (from `editor.hierarchy` or `scene.query_entities`). |
| `entity` | number | One entity id (the same as `entities: [id]`). |
| `parent` | number or null | The new parent; null or absent moves to the root. |
| `keep_world` | bool | Keep each entity's world pose (default true); false keeps the local transforms. A value that is not a JSON boolean counts as true. |
| `dry_run` | bool | Validate and report without applying (default false). A value that is not a JSON boolean counts as false, so the move is applied, and is not `F0002`. |

With neither `entities` nor `entity`, the editor selection moves. `entities: []` (or an empty
selection) is refused. Ids from before an undo follow the re-spawned entity.

```json
{ "method": "editor.reparent", "params": { "entities": [4294967301], "parent": 4294967298 } }
```

Returns `{ moved, unchanged, carried, pose_not_kept, parent, applied, keep_world, entities,
undoable }`:

- `moved` lists the ids of the top-most entities that change parent (ADR-1354 made it a list; it
  was a count).
- `unchanged`: given, but already under `parent`. `carried`: given, but an ancestor of theirs is
  also given, so they ride along. `pose_not_kept`: moved under a parent whose world matrix is
  singular (a zero scale), so they keep their local transform.
- `applied` is false for a `dry_run`.
- `entities[]` has one entry per id passed in: `{ entity, parent, translation, rotation, scale,
  world_translation }`. `translation`, `rotation` and `scale` are the local transform after the
  move; `world_translation` is composed from the parent chain.
- `undoable` is the undo depth after the call.

`scene.reparent` stays the runtime's plain reparent: it is not undoable, and it keeps the local
transform.

## Error codes (`data.reparent_error`, `data.hierarchy_error`)

`data.code` is the catalog code: `F0002` for a refused move, `F0003` for a missing entity.

- `reparent_cycle` / `hierarchy_cycle`: the parent is one of the moved entities or inside one of
  their subtrees.
- `reparent_nothing_to_move`: every entity is already under that parent (no `hierarchy_error`).
- `reparent_target_gone` / `hierarchy_parent_missing`: the parent does not exist.
- `reparent_entity_gone` / `hierarchy_entity_missing`: one of the entities does not exist.
- `hierarchy_no_entities` (no `reparent_error`): `entities` is empty, or absent with an empty
  selection.

A refused call changes nothing and pushes nothing on the undo stack.

## How to check a result

`world_translation` should be unchanged when `keep_world` is true. `editor.undo` should then return
`undone: true`, and `scene.get_entity` should show the old parent again.

<!-- source: book/agents/hierarchy.md -->
# Outliner hierarchy edits

The editor's Outliner shows the level as a tree. A human drags rows to reparent them and uses the context menu
or hotkeys to group, duplicate and delete; an agent makes the same edits with the methods below. Both paths call
the same code (`regia_editor::hierarchy_ops`), so each edit is **one entry** on the editor's shared undo stack,
whether it moves one entity or fifty. `editor.undo` / `editor.redo` step it.

`editor.reparent`, `editor.duplicate`, `editor.delete` and `editor.group` fall back to the editor selection
when `entities` is absent (`[]` is an error, not the selection). `editor.select_hierarchy` falls back the same
way when `entities` is absent, but an empty array is not an error: `mode` `"set"` clears the selection and
`"add"` leaves it. `editor.reparent`, `editor.duplicate` and `editor.delete` are one method each,
shared with the undo surface ([Undo and redo](book/agents/undo-redo.md)) and the drag-and-drop page
([Hierarchy drag and drop](book/agents/editor-hierarchy.md)); they also take `entity` (one id) and accept ids from before
an undo (ADR-1354). Ids come from `editor.hierarchy` or `scene.query_entities`. Editor-internal entities
(window markers, bookkeeping) are never listed and cannot be edited.

## `editor.hierarchy`

The tree as the Outliner draws it: roots and children sorted by name.

Params: `root` (only this entity's subtree), `max_depth` (levels below the roots; `0` = roots only), `filter`
(keep entities whose name contains this text, case-insensitive, and the ancestors that lead to them, like the
panel's search box).

Returns `roots[]` of `{ entity, name, guid, parent, selected, child_count, children[] }` and `count`.
`count` is the number of nodes in the filtered tree, including descendants that `max_depth` leaves out of
`children`. `max_depth: 0` returns the roots with `children: []` and a `count` that still includes every
descendant. `child_count` is the full number of children even when `max_depth` cuts `children` off. Each node also
carries the row's `kind` (or null), derived `role`, `unclassified` flag and grouping `category`
([Entity kinds](book/agents/entity-kinds.md), ADR-2488).

```json
{ "method": "editor.hierarchy", "params": { "max_depth": 1 } }
```

## `editor.reparent`

The Outliner's drag and drop. Moves `entities` under `parent` (`null` or absent = the root).

Params: `entities` (or `entity`), `parent`, `keep_world` (default `true`: each entity gets the local transform
that keeps its world pose, so nothing moves on screen; `false` keeps the local transforms, so entities move with
their new parent), `dry_run` (a JSON boolean: validate and report, change nothing). A `dry_run` or `keep_world`
that is present but not a JSON boolean is not `F0002`. `dry_run` then counts as false, so the move is applied,
and `keep_world` counts as true.

Returns `moved` (ids that change parent), `unchanged` (already under `parent`), `carried` (given, but an ancestor
of theirs is also given: they travel inside it and keep their place in its subtree), `pose_not_kept` (the parent's
world matrix is singular, for example a zero scale: those keep their local transform), `parent`, `applied`,
`undoable` (undo depth after the call), and `keep_world` and `entities[]` (each given entity's parent and local
and world translation after the call; see [Hierarchy drag and drop](book/agents/editor-hierarchy.md)).

The call is all or nothing: if any entity would land in its own subtree, nothing moves. A call where every entity
is already under `parent` is refused with `data.reparent_error` `reparent_nothing_to_move` and pushes nothing.

```json
{ "method": "editor.reparent", "params": { "entities": [4294967301, 4294967302], "parent": 4294967300 } }
```

Check it worked: `editor.hierarchy { "root": <parent> }` lists the entities as children, and a capture or
`scene.get_entity` shows the same world positions as before.

## `editor.group`

Creates an empty entity named `name` (default `"Group"`) at the centroid of the entities' world positions,
under their common parent (the root when their parents differ), and moves them under it keeping their world
poses. One undo entry; the group becomes the selection.

Returns `{ group, members, parent, undoable }`. `members` are the top-level entities given (descendants of other
members stay where they are inside them).

## `editor.duplicate`

Duplicates the entities with their subtrees: fresh guids, each copy under the same parent as its original,
its local translation moved by `offset` (default `[1, 0, 0]`). One undo entry; the copies become the selection.

Params: `entities` or `entity` (one id), `offset`. Returns `{ entities, entity, source, parent, undoable }`:
`entities` are the copies' roots in the order given; `entity`, `source` and `parent` describe the first copy. Only scene entities (with an
`EntityGuid`) can be duplicated; `scene.duplicate` copies the components of any entity without undo.

## `editor.delete`

Deletes the entities with their subtrees. One undo entry; undo brings them back under their old parents (with
their guids, so earlier undo entries still find them) and redo deletes them again. Entities without an
`EntityGuid` are deleted but cannot come back.

Returns `{ deleted, undoable }`.

## `editor.select_hierarchy`

Selects relatives: `scope` `"subtree"` (each entity and all descendants), `"children"` (direct children) or
`"parent"`. `mode` `"set"` (default) replaces the selection, `"add"` extends it. Returns the selection like
`editor.get_selection`. `entities: []` with `mode` `"set"` succeeds and leaves the selection empty. `entities: []`
with `mode` `"add"` succeeds and does not change the selection. Neither call is `hierarchy_no_entities`.

## Error codes

Refusals carry the catalog code in `error.data.code` (`F0002` bad parameters, `F0003` not found, `F0001`
internal; see [protocol](book/agents/protocol.md)) and one of these in `error.data.hierarchy_error`:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `hierarchy_no_entities` | `entities` is empty, or absent with an empty selection, on `editor.reparent`, `editor.duplicate`, `editor.delete` or `editor.group`. Not on `editor.select_hierarchy` |
| `hierarchy_entity_missing` | an entity (or `root`) does not exist |
| `hierarchy_entity_internal` | an entity is editor-internal |
| `hierarchy_parent_missing` | `parent` does not exist |
| `hierarchy_parent_internal` | `parent` is editor-internal |
| `hierarchy_cycle` | `parent` is one of the entities or inside one of their subtrees; for delete, duplicate and group, an entity sits on a `ChildOf` cycle (malformed data: reparent one of them to the root first) |
| `hierarchy_no_guid` | duplicate of an entity without an `EntityGuid` |
| `hierarchy_scene` | the scene snapshot or spawn behind a duplicate or group failed (see `logs.read`) |
| `hierarchy_feed_owned` | the entity is owned by a content feed (`FeedOwned`); bake it with `dcc_feed.bake`, or edit it in the content tool |

## The panel

- The search box keeps rows whose name contains the text (case-insensitive) and their ancestors, drawn open; the
  collapse state comes back when the search is cleared. Drag and drop works on the filtered rows.
- Click selects; Ctrl-click toggles; Shift-click selects the drawn rows from the primary selection to the clicked
  row; Ctrl+Shift-click adds that range.
- Dragging a selected row drags the whole selection; dragging an unselected row drags that row alone. Dropping on
  a row reparents under it (the row outlines in the error color when the drop would create a cycle and is
  refused); dropping on the empty space under the tree moves to the root. A drop keeps world poses; hold Alt
  while dropping to keep the local transforms instead.
- The context menu acts on the selection when the clicked row is part of it: Duplicate, Group, Unparent, Select
  subtree, Select children, Delete (Rename and Create empty child for one row).
- With the pointer over the panel: Delete, Ctrl+D (duplicate), Ctrl+G (group), Ctrl+Z (undo), Ctrl+Shift+Z or
  Ctrl+Y (redo).

`regia_editor::outliner::OutlinerRows` (a world resource) records where the rows, their toggles, the search box
and the root drop zone were drawn, and the search text, for tools and tests
that drive the panel with synthetic pointer input. `seeing.screenshot` shows the panel itself.

During a multi-client play-in-editor session, `editor.hierarchy { client }` answers for that client's world
(`client` is the 0-based index of `editor.pie_net_clients`).

<!-- source: book/agents/mobile-lifecycle.md -->
# Mobile lifecycle, thermal and touch controls

Android takes the window away on every home press or screen-off. The renderer must drop every
surface before the callback returns and create one per window on resume, keeping the GPU device.
The OS also throttles a hot phone, and touch screens have no keys. These methods let an agent test
all three on a desktop, without a phone (ADR-527).

| Method | Permission | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `lifecycle.get` | read | Lifecycle state, the drill queue and the surface audit. |
| `lifecycle.drill` | play | Queue synthetic suspend → resume cycles. |
| `thermal.get` | read | The thermal reading in effect, the override and the quality governor. |
| `thermal.set_override` | play | Force a thermal reading, or clear the override. |
| `input.touch_controls` | read | Touch zones, gesture bindings, which finger holds which zone. |

## Suspend/resume drills

`lifecycle.drill { "cycles": N }` (1..=1000) queues N cycles. The windowed runner runs one cycle
per frame. Each cycle sends `Suspended` then `Resumed` through the runner's own lifecycle tracker,
the same path a Steam Deck wake takes. On a desktop the real surfaces are dropped and recreated,
audio output stops and starts again, and gameplay time does not advance. `{ "cancel": true }`
drops the queue.

```json
{ "cycles": 20 }
→ { "queued": 20, "pending": 20, "completed": 0 }
```

When the app is not running (before the first resume, suspended by the OS, or exiting), nothing
is queued:

```json
{ "cycles": 20 }
→ { "queued": 0, "refused": "lifecycle_not_running", "state": "suspended" }
```

| `refused` code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `lifecycle_not_running` | The app is not in the `running` state; wait until `lifecycle.get` reports it. |

Bad parameters (`cycles` missing, 0, or over 1000) are `INVALID_PARAMS` (`F0002`).

## The surface audit

The renderer reports to the surface audit after every lifecycle transition. The audit checks three
rules:

| Violation `code` | Rule broken |
|---|---|
| `surface_kept_while_suspended` | A surface was still alive after `Suspended` or `WillTerminate`. |
| `surface_missing_after_resume` | After `Resumed`, fewer surfaces were alive than windows exist. |
| `surface_count_mismatch` | Surfaces created − dropped ≠ surfaces alive (a leak or a double drop). |

`lifecycle.get`:

```json
{}
→ { "state": "running", "resume_count": 21,
    "drill": { "pending": 0, "completed": 20 },
    "audit": { "clean": true, "suspends": 20, "resumes": 21, "live": 1, "windows": 1,
               "created_total": 21, "dropped_total": 20, "violation_count": 0, "violations": [] },
    "surfaces": { "live": 1, "created_total": 21, "dropped_total": 20, "lost_streak": 0 } }
```

`surfaces` is `null` without the renderer. The audit keeps the first 32 violations; each has
`code`, `event`, `resumes` (resumes seen before it) and the counts it saw. `violation_count` keeps
counting after 32.

A full check: `lifecycle.drill { "cycles": 50 }`, then `play.wait_until` on `lifecycle.get`'s
`drill.pending == 0`. Then expect `audit.clean` to be true and `audit.resumes` to have grown by 50.
Take a `seeing.screenshot` to confirm the frame came back.

On a phone, the platform layer logs one `regia surface audit: suspends=… resumes=… created=…
dropped=… live=… windows=… violations=…` line per resume. `cargo xtask android-lifecycle` (and
`android-pass`) reads the last one and fails the run when `violations` is above 0.

## Thermal override

`thermal.get` returns `reading` (the `ThermalState` in effect: Android's `PowerManager` status and
10-second headroom, idle on desktop) and `override` (the forced reading, or `null`). It also
returns `governor`: `enabled`, `level` 0..=3, `factors`, `min_scale`, `relax_seconds`, `max_fps`
(the frame cap per level), `base_render_scale`, `holding_max_fps` and `base_max_fps`.

`thermal.set_override { "status": "severe", "headroom": 0.95 }` forces a reading from the next
frame. Statuses are `none`, `light`, `moderate`, `severe`, `critical`, `emergency` and
`shutdown`. Headroom is optional, `>= 0` (1.0 = the severe threshold). `{ "clear": true }`
removes the override, and the OS reading returns. The answer is `{ before, after }`.

The governor then steps the render scale down at once, and back up one level per `relax_seconds`
of cooler readings. When the host set `ThermalGovernor::max_fps` for that level, it also caps the
frame rate. Each level change writes a `ThermalLevelChanged { from, to, reading }` message. Games
read it to shed their own load: simulation detail, particle budgets, AI tick rate.

A check: `thermal.set_override { "status": "critical" }`, step a frame, then expect
`render.get_profile`'s `thermal.governor_level` to be 3 and the render scale to have dropped. Then
`thermal.set_override { "clear": true }`. The scale returns only after the relax time, so turn the
governor off from game code when a test needs the scale back at once.

## Touch controls

A host maps touches to actions with the `regia_input::TouchControls` resource (code, not a RON
file):

- **Zones**: rectangles in normalized window coordinates (0..1, top-left origin, y down). The
  first finger that lands in a zone claims it until the finger lifts. A `Button` zone holds its
  action at 1.0. A `Stick` zone is a floating stick: the finger's offset from where it landed, y
  up, divided by `radius_px`, clamped to unit length, with a `dead_zone`.
- **Gesture bindings**: `tap`, `double_tap`, `long_press`, `swipe` (any direction; the value is
  the direction; the recogniser emits it only for a drag of at least 48 px that lifts within
  1 second), `swipe_up` / `swipe_down` / `swipe_left` / `swipe_right`, `pinch` (x = scale − 1)
  and `two_finger_pan` (movement in screen heights, y up). Each pulses its action for `frames`
  frames, optionally only inside a rectangle. A zone claims the finger that starts inside it.
  Gesture suppression uses the gesture's point: a tap, double tap or long press uses its position
  (the lift or the hold), a swipe uses its start, and a pinch or two-finger pan uses its center.
  A tap that lifts outside a zone still pulses when the finger went down inside one.

The values go through `InputInjection`, like the UI's virtual sticks, so triggers and phases work
as they do for a key.

`input.touch_controls`:

```json
{}
→ { "installed": true,
    "zones": [{ "name": "move", "action": "move", "rect": { "min": [0, 0], "max": [0.5, 1] },
                "kind": { "type": "stick", "radius_px": 120, "dead_zone": 0.1 } }],
    "gestures": [{ "gesture": "swipe_up", "action": "jump", "rect": null, "frames": 2 }],
    "claims": [{ "finger": 1, "zone": "move" }], "held_actions": ["move"],
    "fingers": [{ "id": 1, "phase": "Moved", "start": [200, 600], "current": [260, 540] }] }
```

Without the resource the answer is `{ "installed": false, "fingers": [...] }`. Drive the zones
with `play.inject_input` touch events (`{ "type": "touch", "id", "phase", "x", "y" }`, see
[testing](book/agents/testing.md)), then read the action with the input methods.

## Not covered

- The drill runs on a desktop. It does not reproduce Android's own teardown order (the activity's
  `onPause` before the window goes) or a native window that comes back at a new size. The device
  pass still covers those.
- The thermal override does not change what the OS throttles, only what the engine sees.
