| `resolution` | 8 to 256 | 64 | Cells along the longest axis. Higher finds smaller notches; memory and time grow with the cube. |
| `max_concavity` | 0 to 1 | 0.01 | Concavity a part may keep (and a merge may add), as a fraction of the mesh volume. Lower gives more, tighter hulls. |
| `max_depth` | 0 to 16 | 10 | Most cuts to any one part. 0 means no cuts: one hull. |
| `max_hull_vertices` | 0, or 4 to 4096 | 64 | Most vertices per hull; 0 for no cap. |

## Method

`physics.convex_decompose { entity, max_hulls?, resolution?, max_concavity?, max_depth?, max_hull_vertices?,
points? }` reads the entity's `Collider`, whose shape must be `ColliderShape::TriMesh`, and returns:

- `hull_count`, `total_volume` (the hulls' summed volume; compare it with the mesh's volume to see how
  tightly the hulls fit),
- `hulls`: per hull `vertices` and `triangles` (counts), `volume`, `centroid` `[x, y, z]`, and with
  `points: true` the vertex positions `points`, largest hull first, in the collider's local space,
- `params`: the values used, defaults filled in.

The call is read-only: it does not change the collider. It is a heavy call (rate class `heavy`).

```json
{ "method": "physics.convex_decompose", "params": { "entity": 4294967296, "max_hulls": 8 } }
{ "result": { "entity": 4294967296, "hull_count": 2, "total_volume": 3.01,
  "hulls": [ { "vertices": 8, "triangles": 12, "volume": 2.0, "centroid": [0.5, 1.0, 0.5] },
             { "vertices": 8, "triangles": 12, "volume": 1.01, "centroid": [1.5, 0.5, 0.5] } ],
  "params": { "max_hulls": 8, "resolution": 64, "max_concavity": 0.01, "max_depth": 10, "max_hull_vertices": 64 } } }
```

## Errors

A missing entity, or an entity without a `Collider`, answers `F0003`. Everything else answers `F0002` with a
lowercase code in the message, in brackets:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `not_trimesh` | The collider's shape is not a `TriMesh`. |
| `bad_mesh` | The trimesh names a vertex it does not have, or has a non-finite position. |
| `empty_mesh` | The trimesh has no triangles. |
| `zero_area` | Every triangle has zero area. |
| `flat_mesh` | The vertices are coplanar: the mesh encloses no volume. |
| `bad_max_hulls` | `max_hulls` is not an integer from 1 to 64. |
| `bad_resolution` | `resolution` is not an integer from 8 to 256. |
| `bad_max_concavity` | `max_concavity` is not a number from 0 to 1. |
| `bad_max_depth` | `max_depth` is not an integer from 0 to 16. |
| `bad_max_hull_vertices` | `max_hull_vertices` is not 0 or an integer from 4 to 4096. |
| `bad_points` | `points` is not a boolean. |

The same codes come from `DecompositionError::code()` in Rust (`empty_mesh`, `zero_area`, `flat_mesh` and the
`bad_*` parameter codes).

## Checking a decomposition

- `total_volume` close to the mesh's volume means the hulls fit; much larger means a notch was bridged.
  Lower `max_concavity` or raise `max_hulls`.
- A notch narrower than two cells cannot be found: raise `resolution`.
- After building the compound collider, drop the body and look at it with `physics.raycast` or a screenshot.

## At import

The glTF importer cooks the hulls for you. Set, in the asset's `.meta` importer settings:

```ron
(collision: ConvexDecomposition, collision_hulls: (max_hulls: 8, resolution: 64))
```

Each mesh primitive then gets a sibling sub-asset `collision/<node>/primitive_<i>` (type
`regia_physics::HullSet`, format in `docs/formats/hull-set.md`) holding its convex hulls, built with the
same algorithm and parameters as `physics.convex_decompose` (`collision_hulls` takes the same fields and
defaults). `regia_physics::hull_set::HullSet::to_collider_shape` turns one into a collider shape. The cook
is cached per mesh bytes and settings; a primitive with no volume logs a warning and gets no hull set; a bad
setting fails the import naming the field. `collision: None` (the default) cooks nothing.

<!-- source: book/agents/vehicles.md -->
# Vehicles: wheel state, driver input, reset

Read, drive and reset the ray-cast vehicles in a running app (`regia_physics::vehicle`). Each
vehicle is an entity with a `VehicleController` (the chassis body and its wheels) and a
`VehicleInput`. These calls need `regia_physics::PhysicsPlugin` and
`regia_physics::vehicle::VehiclePlugin`. Without a physics world, or for an entity that is not a
vehicle, they return `NOT_FOUND` (`F0003`) with a hint.

Axes follow the engine: the chassis' forward is its local −Z, right is +X, up is +Y. Distances are
meters, angles radians, speeds m/s.

## Which vehicle?

These vehicles are physical: rapier chassis with tires, a drivetrain and suspension (and the hover craft
below). They give the same bits on the same build and CPU architecture, which suits servers, replays and
single-player, but not a lockstep simulation, which must use the kinematic models of
`regia_detsim::ground_vehicle` (tracked and wheeled, the same bits on every architecture;
[Ground vehicles (lockstep)](book/agents/det-ground-vehicles.md), `detsim.ground_vehicle_simulate`) or the lockstep hover
([Hover step (lockstep)](book/agents/det-hover.md)). A lockstep simulation never reads a rapier pose (ADR-8841). The table
per genre is in [Movement models](book/user-guide/movement-models.md).

## Read every vehicle

`physics.vehicles` lists the vehicles in entity order. `entity` limits it to one.

```json
{}
→ { "count": 1, "vehicles": [ {
      "entity": 4294967310, "position": [0, 0.823, -14.72], "rotation": [0, 0, 0, 1],
      "forward": [0, 0, -1], "forward_speed": 9.7, "speed": 9.7, "rpm": 0.0, "gear": 0,
      "linear_velocity": [0, -0.06, -9.7],
      "angular_velocity": [0, 0, 0], "grounded_wheels": 4, "wheel_count": 4,
      "input":   { "throttle": 1.0, "brake": 0.0, "steer": 0.0 },
      "applied": { "throttle": 1.0, "brake": 0.0, "steer": 0.0 },
      "steps": 420, "last_error": null, "error": null,
      "wheels": [ { "index": 0, "grounded": true, "compression": 0.077, "suspension_length": 0.273,
                    "steer_angle": 0.0, "spin_angle": 41.2, "center": [-0.8, 0.35, -16.0],
                    "contact_point": [-0.8, 0.0, -16.0], "contact_normal": [0, 1, 0],
                    "ground_entity": 4294967296, "suspension_force": 2943.0,
                    "slip_ratio": 0.0, "slip_angle": 0.0 }, ... ] } ] }
```

- `forward_speed` is the chassis velocity along `forward`, negative when reversing. `speed` is the
  chassis speed in its own plane, never negative.
- `rpm` and `gear` are the geared drivetrain's (below); a `Simple` car reads `0` for both.
- `slip_ratio` is `(ω·r − v) / max(|v|, 1 m/s)`: positive driving, negative braking, `0` for a `Simple`
  car and in the air. `slip_angle` is `atan(v_side / |v_along|)` of the contact against the ground in
  radians, positive when it moves toward the wheel's right, `0` in the air or below 0.1 m/s.
- `input` is the entity's `VehicleInput` now; `applied` is what the last fixed step drove with
  (after clamping). They differ until the next fixed step runs.
- `compression` is `rest length − suspension_length`: positive when compressed, `0` in the air. A
  car with `n` equal wheels resting on flat ground compresses each by about `g / (n · stiffness)`.
- `grounded: false` means the wheel's ray found nothing within `rest length + radius`. Its
  contact fields are `null` and it pushes with no force.
- `steer_angle` is the wheel's rotation about the chassis' +Y: a right turn reads negative.
  `spin_angle` grows while the wheel rolls forward.
- `center` is the wheel center in world space, posed against the current chassis pose.
- `ground_entity` is `null` when the ground collider belongs to no entity.
- `linear_velocity` is rapier's end-of-step velocity. A car resting on its springs reads about
  −0.06 m/s vertically while its position holds still: the suspension impulse lands once per step
  and gravity acts across the solver's substeps. Check rest with positions over a few steps.

`config_digest` is `VehicleConfig::digest` of the configuration the vehicle runs (FNV-1a of its compact
RON, 16 hex digits) and `config_revision` counts `Vehicle::set_config` calls since spawn: a retune from the
Vehicle Tuning panel (below) shows up as a new digest and a revision one higher.

`steps` counts fixed-step updates since spawn or the last reset. `last_error` is the code from the
last fixed-step update; `error` is the code from reading the vehicle for this report. Both are
`null` when all is well.

### Error codes in the report

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `vehicle_chassis_missing` | The chassis body is gone from the physics world (despawned or removed). |
| `vehicle_chassis_not_dynamic` | The chassis body was switched to fixed or kinematic; wheels cannot move it. |
| `vehicle_chassis_massless` | The chassis body has no mass (no collider with mass). |
| `vehicle_invalid_time_step` | The fixed step was zero, negative or not finite. |
| `vehicle_invalid_pose` | A reset pose was not finite, or its rotation was degenerate. |
| `vehicle_no_wheels` | The vehicle's configuration has no wheels. |
| `vehicle_too_many_wheels` | The configuration has more than 32 wheels. |
| `vehicle_invalid_wheel` | A wheel field is out of range or not finite (every wheel setting is at most `1e9`, `MAX_VEHICLE_SETTING`, ADR-7431). |
| `vehicle_invalid_config` | A vehicle-wide field is out of range or not finite (drivetrain, anti-roll and aero settings at most `1e9`). |
| `vehicle_no_physics_world` | The app has no `PhysicsWorld` resource. |
| `vehicle_no_gearbox` | `physics.vehicle_shift` on a car with the `Simple` drivetrain. |
| `vehicle_invalid_gear` | `physics.vehicle_shift` named a gear the gearbox does not have. |
| `vehicle_tire_damper` | `physics.vehicle_tire_curve` on a wheel with the `Damper` tire, which has no slip curve. |
| `vehicle_tire_no_wheel` | `physics.vehicle_tire_curve` named a wheel the vehicle does not have. |
| `vehicle_state_not_finite` | The car's own state (chassis velocity, wheel or drivetrain state) is not finite, so a client prediction world could not carry it into a rebuilt world; it keeps the old world until the next authoritative state (logged as `net.vehicle_statics_sync_failed`). |

The configuration codes come from creating a vehicle in code (`spawn_vehicle`). Over the wire you
see the chassis and time-step codes in `last_error` and `error`. A refused `physics.vehicle_reset`
names its code in brackets at the start of the message, for example
`[vehicle_chassis_missing] the vehicle's chassis body is not in the physics world` (`F0003`).

## Drive

`physics.vehicle_input` sets the driver input. Fields you leave out keep their value. The next
fixed steps drive with it until you change it.

```json
{ "entity": 4294967310, "throttle": 1.0, "steer": -0.5 }
→ { "entity": 4294967310,
    "before": { "throttle": 0.0, "brake": 0.0, "steer": 0.0 },
    "after":  { "throttle": 1.0, "brake": 0.0, "steer": -0.5 } }
```

- `throttle`: +1 full forward, −1 full reverse, 0 off.
- `brake`: 0 off to 1 full. On a wheel that can brake, braking cancels its engine force, so
  throttle and brake together hold the car.
- `steer`: +1 full right, −1 full left.

A value outside its range is refused with `F0002` before the call runs. This call needs the `play`
permission.

Drive, then check:

```json
{ "method": "physics.vehicle_input", "params": { "entity": 4294967310, "throttle": 1.0 } }
{ "method": "play.step", "params": { "frames": 120 } }
{ "method": "physics.vehicles", "params": { "entity": 4294967310 } }
```

## Reset

`physics.vehicle_reset` puts the vehicle back at rest: zero velocity, no accumulated forces, the
wheels cleared (spin, steering, suspension record) and the input released. With no pose it returns
to its spawn pose. `position` sets the chassis center; `yaw` sets the heading in radians about +Y.
`position` without `yaw` resets to no rotation.

```json
{ "entity": 4294967310 }
→ { "entity": 4294967310, "position": [0, 0.9, 0], "rotation": [0, 0, 0, 1] }

{ "entity": 4294967310, "position": [5, 1, 0], "yaw": 1.5708 }
→ { "entity": 4294967310, "position": [5, 1, 0], "rotation": [0, 0.7071, 0, 0.7071] }
```

After a reset no wheel is grounded until the next fixed step casts the wheel rays. This call needs
the `play` permission.

## Working with the results

- Entity ids work everywhere: `scene.get_entity` for the chassis `Transform`, `play.expect`
  conditions, `physics.raycast` from a wheel `center`.
- The chassis `Transform` is the stepped pose; the wheel poses are posed against it, so a host can
  parent wheel meshes under the chassis with each wheel's chassis-space pose (see
  `book/user-guide/vehicles.md`).
- Same build, same inputs, same fixed step: same result. `physics.stats` `digest` compares runs.

## Drivetrain telemetry and gears

A car with `drivetrain: Geared(..)` in its `.vehicle.ron` (`docs/formats/vehicle.md`) has an engine, a slip
clutch, a gearbox, differentials and a spin per wheel. `physics.vehicle_telemetry` reads them; `entity` limits it to
one vehicle.

```json
{ "entity": 4294967310 }
→ { "count": 1, "vehicles": [ {
      "entity": 4294967310, "steps": 420, "digest": "6f1c0b9d2a33e710", "drivetrain": "geared",
      "speed": 21.4, "forward_speed": 21.4, "rpm": 4310.0, "gear": 2, "target_gear": 2,
      "shifting": false, "automatic": true, "upshifts": 1, "downshifts": 0, "last_shift_rpm": 6204.0,
      "clutch_torque": 287.1, "clutch_slipping": false, "engine_torque": 287.1,
      "applied_throttle": 1.0, "traction_factor": 1.0, "error": null,
      "wheels": [ { "index": 2, "grounded": true, "slip_ratio": 0.031, "slip_angle": 0.0,
                    "angular_speed": 63.0, "tire_force": 2710.0, "load": 3120.0,
                    "drive_torque": 985.0, "abs_factor": 1.0 }, ... ] } ] }
```

- `gear`: −1 reverse, 0 neutral, 1 and up forward. A shift keeps the old gear for `shift_time` with the clutch open and
  the throttle shut; `target_gear` names the new one and `shifting` is `true` until it engages.
- `rpm` follows the driven wheels through the ratios while `clutch_slipping` is `false`. At a launch it runs ahead.
- `traction_factor` is traction control's cut on the throttle, `abs_factor` is ABS's on that wheel's brake: `1` is no
  cut. Both stay `1` with the aid off.
- `digest` covers the drivetrain's state and the step count. With `physics.stats` `digest`, which covers the chassis, it
  compares runs: same build, same inputs and fixed step, same digests.
- A `Simple` car reads `"drivetrain": "simple"`, `rpm` and `gear` `0`, `null` per-wheel spin and force, and has none
  of the gearbox fields.

`physics.vehicle_shift` changes gear. It takes the gears from the automatic until you hand them back. It needs the `play`
permission.

```json
{ "entity": 4294967310, "gear": 3 }       // -1 reverse, 0 neutral, 1 and up forward
{ "entity": 4294967310, "shift": "up" }   // or "down"
{ "entity": 4294967310, "automatic": true }
→ { "entity": 4294967310, "gear": 2, "target_gear": 3, "shifting": true, "automatic": false }
```

`gear` and `shift` together are refused, and so is a call with none of the three (`F0002`). A gear the gearbox does not
have is `F0002` with `[vehicle_invalid_gear]`, and a `Simple` car is `F0002` with `[vehicle_no_gearbox]`.

With a geared car, `throttle` follows the gear. A throttle against the direction of travel brakes; near a stop (under
1 m/s) the automatic takes reverse or first and drives. A manual gearbox keeps its gear and keeps braking.

Launch, then watch the shifts:

```json
{ "method": "physics.vehicle_input", "params": { "entity": 4294967310, "throttle": 1.0 } }
{ "method": "play.step", "params": { "frames": 600 } }
{ "method": "physics.vehicle_telemetry", "params": { "entity": 4294967310 } }
```

`samples/vehicle_lab` is a rear-wheel drive car and a hover craft on a flat track with a ramp, for this kind of run. Start it with
`--no-script`, which leaves them parked for you: without the flag a looping script writes their input every frame.

## Hover craft

`regia_physics::hover` adds a second kind of vehicle: a chassis held above the ground by ray-cast
thrusters (spring and damper along the ground normal), with drive, brake, yaw and lateral-grip impulses
that act only while a thruster has ground. It reads the same `VehicleInput` as a car, so
`physics.vehicle_input` drives it (`F0003` only when the entity is neither a car nor a hover craft). The
rest of the axes match the car: forward is local −Z, steer +1 turns right.

`physics.hovercraft` lists them in entity order; `entity` limits it to one.

```json
{}
→ { "count": 1, "hovercraft": [ {
      "entity": 4294967311, "position": [0, 0.94, -8.1], "forward": [0, 0, -1],
      "forward_speed": 6.2, "lateral_speed": 0.01, "linear_velocity": [0, 0, -6.2],
      "grounded_thrusters": 4, "thruster_count": 4, "hover_height": 1.0,
      "input": { "throttle": 1.0, "brake": 0.0, "steer": 0.0 },
      "steps": 420, "last_error": null, "error": null,
      "thrusters": [ { "index": 0, "grounded": true, "distance": 0.94, "compression": 0.06,
                       "force": 1470.0, "contact_point": [-0.9, 0.0, -9.4] }, ... ] } ] }
```

- `distance` is the mount point's distance to the ground along its ray (the ray reaches twice
  `hover_height`); a craft with no ground in reach has `grounded: false` and applies no force.
- `compression` is `hover_height − distance`, `0` when not compressed.
- A craft settles at `hover_height − g / stiffness` (its total spring force is `mass · stiffness · compression`, shared by the thrusters).
- Error codes in `last_error` / `error`: `hover_no_thrusters`, `hover_too_many_thrusters`,
  `hover_invalid_config`, `hover_invalid_pose`, `hover_invalid_time_step`, `hover_chassis_missing`,
  `hover_no_physics_world`.

## Ray layers

A car's wheel rays and a craft's thruster rays hit every collision layer by default. `ground_layers` (a
bitmask of layer indices) and `query_layer` (a row of the `PhysicsLayers` query matrix) restrict them: a
ray hits only colliders on layers in `ground_layers & query_row`. Without a `PhysicsLayers` resource the
`query_layer` has nothing to read and only `ground_layers` applies. A wheel whose ray misses by layer
reads `grounded: false`, like one over a hole.

## Check a `.vehicle.ron`

`physics.vehicle_config_check` parses and validates the text of a `.vehicle.ron`
(`docs/formats/vehicle.md`) without spawning anything.

```json
{ "ron": "(format_version: 3, name: \"car\", config: ())" }
→ { "ok": true, "name": "car", "format_version": 3, "wheel_count": 4, "chassis_mass": 1200.0,
    "steered_wheels": 2, "driven_wheels": 2, "braked_wheels": 4, "ground_layers": null,
    "query_layer": null, "drivetrain": "simple", "gears": null, "anti_roll_bars": 0, "aero": false,
    "abs": false, "traction_control": false, "slip_tires": 0, "warnings": [] }
```

A v1 or v2 file answers with `format_version` 3: it migrated on the way in, with every tire `Damper`.

`warnings` lists tuning hints about the tires: the file is valid, but probably not what you meant. Each is
`{ code, wheel, message }`:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `tire_mixed_axle` | Two wheels side by side have different tire models: the car pulls to one side in a turn. |
| `tire_roll_influence_low` | A slip tire's `roll_influence` is under 0.5: its side force acts near the center of mass's height, so load transfer is understated. |
| `tire_load_far_from_nominal` | The static load per wheel is under a third or over three times the tire's `nominal_load`: the load factor extrapolates. |
| `tire_slide_angle_large` | The curve peaks past about 20 degrees of slip at the static load: `cornering_stiffness` is low for `peak_friction`. |
| `tire_no_static_hold` | `stick_speed` is 0: a held brake creeps down a slope. |
| `tire_side_friction_ignored` | A slip tire has `side_friction_stiffness` other than 1, which only the damper tire reads. |

A bad file is an `F0002` error whose message starts with the stable code in brackets:
`vehicle_asset_parse`, `vehicle_asset_version`, `vehicle_asset_name`, or a `VehicleError` code such as
`vehicle_no_wheels` or `vehicle_invalid_config`.

## Slip tires

A wheel with `tire_model: Slip((..))` in a `.vehicle.ron` v3 (`docs/formats/vehicle.md`, ADR-2719) makes its side force
from the slip angle, on a brush or Magic Formula curve, instead of rapier's sideways velocity damper. Its grip falls
with load (`load_exponent`), the lengthwise force (the drivetrain's) takes its share first on a friction ellipse, the
side force acts at the contact's height (`roll_influence`), a held brake on a slope inside the grip does not creep, and
on a dynamic ground body the wheel pushes the ground back.

`physics.vehicle_tire_curve` reads a wheel's tire as force against slip angle without stepping anything. Give a spawned
vehicle (`entity`) or the text of a `.vehicle.ron` (`ron`), not both.

```json
{ "ron": "(format_version: 3, name: \"car\", config: (wheels: [(tire_model: Slip(()))]))", "wheel": 0, "points": 5,
  "max_slip_angle": 0.4 }
→ { "wheel": 0, "tire_model": "slip", "curve": { "kind": "brush" }, "load": 3000.0, "load_factor": 1.0,
    "friction": 1.0, "peak_force": 3000.0, "peak_slip_angle": 0.197, "cornering_stiffness": 45000.0,
    "roll_influence": 1.0, "stick_speed": 0.3,
    "points": [ { "slip_angle": 0.0, "lateral_force": 0.0 }, { "slip_angle": 0.1, "lateral_force": -2629.0 },
                { "slip_angle": 0.2, "lateral_force": -3000.0 }, ... ] }
```

- `load` (newtons) defaults to the tire's `nominal_load`; `max_slip_angle` (radians, up to π/2) to 0.5; `points` (2 to
  361) to 41, evenly from 0.
- `lateral_force` is along the wheel's right and opposes the slip: a positive slip angle gives a negative force.
- `friction` is `peak_friction · load_factor`, the grip per newton at that load; `peak_force` is `friction · load`.
- A wheel with the `Damper` tire is `F0002` with `[vehicle_tire_damper]`; a wheel the vehicle does not have is `F0002`
  with `[vehicle_tire_no_wheel]`; a bad file names its code as `physics.vehicle_config_check` does. An entity that is
  not a vehicle, or no physics world, is `F0003`.

`physics.vehicle_telemetry` reports every tire, slip or damper, in each wheel row:

- `tire_model`: `"slip"` or `"damper"`.
- `lateral_force`: the mean side force over the last step along the wheel's right, newtons (rapier's side impulse for a
  damper tire). Turning right, it is positive.
- `longitudinal_force`: the lengthwise force the tire used, newtons (the drivetrain's or rapier's, plus the hold).
- `tire_load`: the tire's load, newtons (suspension plus anti-roll; the suspension alone for a damper tire).
- `tire_slip_angle`: the slip angle the slip tire saw on that step (`0` for a damper tire).
- `stuck`: the slip tire held still this step (below `stick_speed`).

Check a corner, then the limit:

```json
{ "method": "physics.vehicle_input", "params": { "entity": 4294967310, "throttle": 0.4, "steer": 0.5 } }
{ "method": "play.step", "params": { "frames": 300 } }
{ "method": "physics.vehicle_telemetry", "params": { "entity": 4294967310 } }
{ "method": "physics.vehicle_tire_curve", "params": { "entity": 4294967310, "wheel": 0, "load": 3600 } }
```

A wheel whose `lateral_force` is near the curve's `peak_force` at its `tire_load` is at its limit.

For vehicles in multiplayer (replication, prediction, seats), see [net vehicles](book/agents/net-vehicles.md).

## Tire transients and feedback

A `.vehicle.ron` v4 slip tire (`docs/formats/vehicle.md`, ADR-3276) can add, each off by default:

- `relaxation_length` (m): the side force builds over that much rolling, time constant `relaxation_length / speed`;
  it holds while the car stands still and does not ring at walking speed.
- `pneumatic_trail` (m): the self-aligning torque. It turns the wheel back toward its path and fades to 0 at the
  curve's peak slip angle (slightly past 0 beyond it for the Magic Formula), so the steering goes light at the limit.
- `camber_stiffness` (N/rad) and `static_camber` (rad, negative = top toward the center line): camber thrust, toward
  the side the wheel leans, from the static camber plus body roll and slope.
- `combined_slip`: `Ellipse` (default) or `SlipWeighted(shape, stiffness)`, which takes side grip away as the wheel
  spins or locks (its slip ratio) and keeps the resultant within `µ · load`.

`physics.vehicle_telemetry` adds to each wheel row:

- `lagged_slip_angle`: the slip angle the side force used (the lagged one with a relaxation length, else
  `tire_slip_angle`).
- `aligning_torque`: newton-meters about the contact normal, positive turning the wheel left (the sign of
  `steer_angle`). Turning right it is positive: the tires push the wheels back toward straight. 0 for a damper tire,
  with no trail, or while the tire is stuck.
- `camber`: the camber the tire saw, radians, positive leaning its top toward its right (0 without a
  `camber_stiffness`).
- `camber_thrust`: the part of `lateral_force` that is camber thrust, newtons along the wheel's right.

and to each vehicle row:

- `steering_torque`: the sum of the steered wheels' `aligning_torque` (newton-meters). This is the raw torque for a
  force-feedback wheel (before any steering ratio); Regia drives no wheel device.
- `steering_axles`: `[{ position_z, wheels, torque }]`, the same split per steered axle.
- `feedback`: `{ low, high, strength, device, requests }` when the entity has a
  `regia_framework::vehicle_feedback::VehicleFeedback`, else `null`.

`physics.vehicle_tire_curve` adds `pneumatic_trail` and `aligning_torque` to every point, and the tire's
`relaxation_length`, `pneumatic_trail`, `camber_stiffness` (N/rad at the asked load), `static_camber` and
`combined_slip` (`{ "kind": "ellipse" }` or `{ "kind": "slip_weighted", "shape", "stiffness" }`):

```json
{ "ron": "(format_version: 4, name: \"car\", config: (wheels: [(tire_model: Slip((pneumatic_trail: 0.04)))]))",
  "points": 3, "max_slip_angle": 0.2 }
→ { ..., "pneumatic_trail": 0.04, "relaxation_length": 0.0, "combined_slip": { "kind": "ellipse" },
    "points": [ { "slip_angle": 0.0, "lateral_force": 0.0, "pneumatic_trail": 0.04, "aligning_torque": 0.0 },
                { "slip_angle": 0.1, "lateral_force": -2629.0, "pneumatic_trail": 0.0085, "aligning_torque": -22.3 },
                { "slip_angle": 0.2, "lateral_force": -3000.0, "pneumatic_trail": 0.0, "aligning_torque": 0.0 } ] }
```

The aligning torque peaks well before the side force: a steering wheel that goes light warns of the limit.

### Rumble from the tires

Add `VehicleFeedbackPlugin` (after `VehiclePlugin`) and put a `VehicleFeedback` on the vehicle entity, with the
gamepad's device id to rumble it (`None` computes the channels only). After every fixed step:

| Channel | From | Map (defaults) |
|---|---|---|
| `low` | the steering torque | 0 below 5 N·m, 1 at 150 N·m, linear between |
| `high` | the largest change of a wheel's load in one step, over its static share of the weight (curbs, landings, impacts) | 0 below 0.25, 1 at 1.5, then fading by `e` every 0.12 s |

Both are in [0, 1] and both are 0 driving straight on flat ground. A `RumbleRequest` carries one strength, so it gets
`max(low, high) · strength_scale` for `request_duration` (0.1 s), sent every step the strength is above 0. Change the
map through `VehicleFeedback::map` (`VehicleFeedbackMap`). No new error codes: a vehicle the feedback cannot read is
skipped.

Check the feel of a corner:

```json
{ "method": "physics.vehicle_input", "params": { "entity": 4294967310, "throttle": 0.4, "steer": 0.6 } }
{ "method": "play.step", "params": { "frames": 120 } }
{ "method": "physics.vehicle_telemetry", "params": { "entity": 4294967310 } }
```

`steering_torque` should be positive in a right turn and grow, then fall back as the front tires pass their peak;
`feedback.low` follows it.

## Vehicle Tuning panel (editor)

The editor's **Vehicle Tuning** panel (`Panel::VehicleTuning`, ADR-9760) edits a `.vehicle.ron` in typed
sections (chassis, wheels with their tire model, engine and its torque curve, gearbox, clutch, differentials,
anti-roll, aero, aids), plots it, sends it to a running car without a respawn, and records scripted runs side
by side. Every button has a method here, and the panel and the methods share one state.
Trailers (`.trailer.ron`), aircraft (`.aircraft.ron`), the proving-ground tracks and towing are on
[Vehicle tuning: trailers, aircraft and proving-ground tracks](book/agents/vehicle-tuning.md) (ADR-7745).

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `editor.vehicle_tuning_open { path, create? }` | Opens a `.vehicle.ron` under the project (the panel's **Open**); `create: true` starts the default car named after the file when it does not exist (**New**), written at the first save. `create: true` on a path whose file already exists refuses with `vehicle_tuning_exists` — it never opens or overwrites that file. Opening drops the state bound to the previous file: a queued Apply, the explicit Apply target, the recorded runs and the live telemetry entity. |
| `editor.vehicle_tuning_state { plots?, wheel? }` | The edited `config`, `config_digest`, `dirty`, `validation`, tire `warnings`, `undo_depth`/`redo_depth`, the last `error`, `last_apply`, the recorded `runs` and the play car's last `telemetry` frame. `plots: true` adds the plot samples (below); `wheel` picks the wheel the tire and suspension plots show. |
| `editor.vehicle_tuning_set { field, value }` | Sets one field (one undo step). |
| `editor.vehicle_tuning_undo`, `editor.vehicle_tuning_redo` | Steps back or forward one edit (**Undo**, **Redo**); `changed` says whether there was one. |
| `editor.vehicle_tuning_apply { entity? }` | **Apply**: at the next editor frame, sends the edited configuration to a play vehicle through `Vehicle::set_config`. Read the answer in `state.last_apply`. |
| `editor.vehicle_tuning_save { path? }` | **Save**: writes `.vehicle.ron` v4 atomically (default: the open file). |
| `editor.vehicle_tuning_run { script, seconds, label? }` | **Run accel** / **Run skidpad**: drives the edited car on the proving ground and records the run. |

### Fields

`field` is a dotted path into the configuration's JSON shape: `chassis_mass`, `center_of_mass`,
`wheels.0.radius`, `wheels.0.suspension_stiffness`, `drivetrain.gearbox.final_drive`,
`drivetrain.gearbox.forward_ratios`, `drivetrain.engine.torque_curve` (a list of `[rpm, N·m]`),
`drivetrain.engine.torque_curve.2.1` (one torque), `drivetrain.rear_differential.torque_bias`,
`wheels.1.tire_model.cornering_stiffness`, `aero.drag_coefficient`, `aids.abs`, or `name`. An enum's
variant is passed through (`drivetrain.gearbox` is inside `Geared`, a slip field inside `Slip`), and a whole
section can be replaced: `{ "field": "drivetrain", "value": "Simple" }`, `{ "value": { "Geared": {} } }`
(missing fields take their defaults), `{ "field": "aero", "value": null }`.

```json
{ "field": "drivetrain.gearbox.final_drive", "value": 4.44 }
→ { "dirty": true, "undo_depth": 1, "config_digest": "…", "config": { … }, … }
```

A value the configuration refuses changes nothing. The error is `INVALID_PARAMS` with `data.reason` set to the
code `physics.vehicle_config_check` gives for the same file, and `data.field` set to the path:

```json
{ "field": "drivetrain.gearbox.final_drive", "value": -1.0 }
→ error { "data": { "reason": "vehicle_invalid_config", "field": "drivetrain.gearbox.final_drive" } }
```

In the panel a drag of a number or of a torque-curve point is one undo step however many frames it lasts.

### Apply in play

Apply needs a play session whose world has `PhysicsPlugin` and `VehiclePlugin`. The target is `entity` when
given (bits from `physics.vehicles` in the play world), else the vehicle running the opened file's
configuration, else the only vehicle. `Vehicle::set_config` keeps the chassis pose and velocity, the step
count and the input; a geared drivetrain keeps its rpm and gear (clamped to the new range and top gear) and
the wheels their spin; a wheel-count or drivetrain-kind change starts those fresh. The rules are listed on
`Vehicle::set_config`.

```json
// state.last_apply after the next frame
{ "ok": true, "answer": { "entity": 4294967310, "config_digest": "…", "config_revision": 1,
  "change": { "chassis_updated": false, "wheels_kept": true, "drivetrain_kept": true,
              "gear_clamped": false, "rpm_clamped": false, "tires_kept": 0 } } }
```

`physics.vehicles` then reports the same `config_digest` and `config_revision: 1` for that car. While play
runs the panel reads the car every frame into its telemetry strip (speed, rpm, gear, and per wheel the slip
ratio, slip angle and load); `state.telemetry` is the last frame.

### Runs

A run drives the edited car alone on a flat 30 km plane at 60 Hz (`regia_physics::vehicle_proving`), after one
second settling, with the same `VehicleInput` `physics.vehicle_input` sets: `accel` is full throttle straight
ahead; `skidpad` steers half lock right while the throttle holds a target speed that rises 1 m/s per second.
The answer, and each row of `state.runs`:

```json
{ "script": "accel", "seconds": 20.0 }
→ { "label": "run 1", "script": "accel", "seconds": 20.0, "zero_to_100_s": 6.69, "top_speed_kmh": 189.9,
    "max_lateral_g": 0.0, "distance_m": …, "upshifts": …, "digest": "…", "config_digest": "…" }
```

The vehicle lab's car (`samples/vehicle_lab/assets/rwd_car.vehicle.ron`) runs 0 to 100 km/h in 6.69 s and tops
out at 189.9 km/h in 20 s; with its final drive 20 % higher, 6.67 s and 189.2 km/h.
Its skid pad holds 1.09 g.

`zero_to_100_s` is `null` when the car never reached 100 km/h; `max_lateral_g` is the highest yaw rate × speed
held over half a second. The run reads no clock, so the same configuration gives the same `digest`. The panel
keeps the last 8 runs and shows them side by side with their speed traces.

### Plots

`state { plots: true }` returns the samples the panel draws, computed from the runtime's own math:
`torque_power` (`[{ rpm, torque_nm, power_kw }]` from idle to redline, `EngineConfig::torque_at`),
`wheel_force` (per forward gear `{ gear, total_ratio, points: [[km/h, N]] }`: torque × efficiency ×
`total_ratio` / driven wheel radius), `tire_side_force` (the selected wheel's slip tire at its nominal load,
the same numbers as `physics.vehicle_tire_curve`) and `suspension` (`{ rest_length, travel,
static_compression, points: [[m, N]] }`).

### Save

Save merges the edit into the file's text, so comments and layout stay; an older file's `format_version`
becomes 4. When the merged text would not load as exactly the edited asset, the panel writes the canonical
`VehicleAsset::to_ron` text instead and says the comments were lost (`comments_kept: false`).

### Error codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `vehicle_tuning_nothing_open` | No `.vehicle.ron` is open. |
| `vehicle_tuning_no_project` | No project is open. |
| `vehicle_tuning_bad_path` | The path climbs out of the project or does not end in `.vehicle.ron`. |
| `vehicle_tuning_not_found` | The file does not exist (pass `create`). |
| `vehicle_tuning_exists` | `create` was passed for a path whose file already exists; it refuses so **New** cannot silently overwrite a tuned file. |
| `vehicle_tuning_io` | Reading or writing the file failed. |
| `vehicle_tuning_no_path` | Save has no path (a created asset with none given). |
| `vehicle_tuning_bad_field` | The configuration has no such field (or a slip field on a damper tire). |
| `vehicle_tuning_bad_value` | The value has the wrong shape for the field. |
| `vehicle_tuning_bad_script` | `script` is not `accel` or `skidpad`. |
| `vehicle_tuning_bad_seconds` | `seconds` is not above 0 and at most 120. |
| `vehicle_tuning_not_playing` | Apply without a play session. |
| `vehicle_tuning_no_target` | No play vehicle matches (several and none runs the file: pass `entity`). |
| `vehicle_tuning_no_physics` | The play world has no `PhysicsWorld`. |
| `vehicle_*` | A refused value or retune: the `VehicleError` / `VehicleAssetError` code above. |

# Physics: debug draw, materials, torque breaks and the physics lab

Four physics features an agent can check without a window. They need `regia_physics::PhysicsPlugin`; without it
the calls return `NOT_FOUND` with a hint. Decision: ADR-2424. Format page: `docs/formats/physmat.md`.

## Parented bodies (the spec 15 § 1 hierarchy warning)

`physics.parented_bodies` answers `{ count, bodies: [{ entity, parent }] }`: the play world's `Dynamic`
`RigidBody` entities parented under an entity with no `RigidBody`. Rapier simulates and writes a dynamic
body's world pose back, but the body's `Transform` is local to a parent the simulation knows nothing about —
the hierarchy and the simulation fight — so the spec recommends bodies as hierarchy roots. `Static` and
`Kinematic` bodies under a group node are the normal, supported case and are not listed. Each offending
entity is logged once (a `tracing::warn!`, visible in the editor's log during play) and counted here;
findings are pruned when the body despawns. The check runs wherever `PhysicsPlugin` runs (a play world — the
editor's edit world has no physics).

## Debug draw

`physics.debug_draw` turns the physics debug draw on or off and chooses what it shows. Call it with no
parameters to read the state.

```json
{ "on": true, "kinds": ["contacts", "joints", "com"] }
→ { "on": true, "kinds": ["contacts", "joints", "com"], "gizmo_group_enabled": true,
    "lines": 0, "collections": 0, "lines_emitted": 0, "dropped": 0 }
```

- `contacts`: each touching contact point with a short line along its normal. `joints`: the body-to-anchor arm
  of both bodies and the gap line between the two anchors (a long gap line is a stretched joint). `com`: a cross at
  the center of mass of every dynamic body. The default is all three.
- Turning it on also enables the `physics` gizmo group, so the lines are visible; that group draws collider
  outlines too. Turning it off leaves the group as it is (use `debug.set_gizmos` for that).
- It costs nothing while off: the collection system does not run, and `collections` stays where it was. After
  turning it on, `play.step` and read the state again: `collections` counts the frames drawn, `lines` is the last
  frame's line count, `dropped` counts lines past the 50,000 per frame cap.
- Errors (the stable code is in brackets at the start of the message): `physics_debug_flag` (`on` is not a
  boolean), `physics_debug_kinds` (`kinds` is not an array of strings), `physics_debug_kind_unknown`.

## Physics materials

A `.physmat.ron` names friction, restitution, density and the combine rules a collider takes
(`docs/formats/physmat.md`).

- `physics.material_check { ron }` validates the text of a `.physmat.ron` and returns a summary. A bad file is an
  `F0002` error whose message starts with the stable code: `physmat_parse`, `physmat_version`, `physmat_name`,
  `physmat_value`.
- `physics.material_register { ron }` validates and adds the material to the registry (the same name replaces).
  Colliders with a `PhysicsMaterialRef("<name>")` component take its values on the next frame. The result adds
  `registered`, the number of materials. Set the component with the usual entity editing methods.
- The default material equals the collider defaults, so a scene without references is bit-identical to before.
  A reference to an unregistered name leaves the collider alone and shows up in `PhysicsMaterials::unresolved`.

## Joint torque break

`JointBreakTorque(n)` next to a `Joint` breaks the joint when its torque, estimated in newton-metres, exceeds
`n` on a step, in addition to `Joint::break_force`. A `JointBroken` message is raised as for a force break, and the
joint stays broken until its `Joint` changes. The estimate adds the moment of the joint's linear reaction about the
joint point to its angular reaction, so a load hanging to the side of a joint counts. Check a break with
`play.step` and `physics.stats` (`joints` drops by one).

## The physics lab

`samples/physics_lab` is a headless, deterministic scene: a stack, a lever joint with a torque limit and one
without, a hanging chain, a default and an ice box on a 20 degree ramp, a ragdoll drop and the debug draw. Run it
with `cargo run -p physics_lab`; the report ends in a digest that two runs share. Its `tests/agent_dogfood.rs`
drives it over this protocol.

```json
{ "method": "play.pause", "params": {} }
{ "method": "physics.debug_draw", "params": { "on": true } }
{ "method": "play.step", "params": { "frames": 3 } }
{ "method": "physics.debug_draw", "params": {} }
```

<!-- source: book/agents/load-memory.md -->
# Load memory: the staging flush

A level's first frame uploads every new material texture and mesh. wgpu copies each
`write_texture` / `write_buffer` into a staging buffer of its own and keeps it until the next
submit, and the renderer submits once per frame. Before ADR-1346 the whole level's textures sat in
staging at once, on top of the CPU copies the materials hold: the DO27 map pak (4.9 GiB of
textures) peaked at about 9 GiB of RSS.

The staging flush bounds that. The renderer counts the bytes written on a thread since its last
submit; at the cap it submits the pending writes on their own, and the frame path waits for its
previous flush before it writes more. A load then holds about two caps of staging (one the GPU
copies while the CPU fills the next) instead of the level.

The frame draws the same pixels: wgpu applies every pending write before the next submit's
command buffers, so a write moved into an earlier submission changes what no pass reads
(`a_frame_flushed_at_every_write_draws_the_same_pixels`). A steady frame writes far less than the
cap and never flushes.

## Read

`seeing.memory_report` carries the flush and the process peak RSS next to the GPU categories:

```json
seeing.memory_report { "top": 3 }
→ { "available": true, "backend": "Vulkan", "rss_bytes": 2491..., "peak_rss_bytes": 5372...,
    "staging": { "cap_bytes": 134217728, "flushes": 38, "flushed_bytes": 5100273664,
                 "waits": 37, "peak_pending_bytes": 139460608 },
    "categories": { ... }, "labels": [ ... ] }
```

- `peak_rss_bytes`: the process's peak resident set. Linux and Android report `VmHWM`; Windows
  reports the peak working set, macOS `ru_maxrss` (ADR-5860). `null` on other targets and when the OS query fails.
  It never goes down, so compare two settings in two processes.
- `staging.cap_bytes`: the cap in force (`0` = the flush is off).
- `staging.flushes`, `staging.flushed_bytes`: flushes since start and the bytes they moved.
- `staging.waits`: flushes that waited for the flush before them. Set-up writes through handles
  that do not know their device flush without waiting, so `waits` can be lower than `flushes`.
- `staging.peak_pending_bytes`: the most bytes ever written on one thread between two submits:
  the largest staging wgpu held at once for one thread. With the flush on it stays at most the cap
  plus the largest single write; with it off it is about the largest first frame's upload.

## Set the cap

- Default 128 MiB.
- `REGIA_STAGING_FLUSH_MIB=<MiB>` sets it at start; `0` or `off` turns the flush off (the
  behavior before ADR-1346, for A/B runs).
- A host calls `regia_render::set_staging_flush_cap(Some(bytes))` before a level load (for
  example lower on a handheld or a phone), and `set_staging_flush_cap(None)` to go back to the
  environment or the default.

Each flush is one empty submit and, on the frame path, one wait for the previous flush, which is
normally already done. A smaller cap means more of them.

## Measure

- `pak_load_bench load --paks DIR --frame 1280x720` (a shipped map from paks) and
  `load_rss_bench [--materials 64] [--side 2048]` (a synthetic scene of distinct BC7/BC5 chains,
  no content needed) print the peak RSS before and after the first frame. Run each with
  `REGIA_STAGING_FLUSH_MIB=0` and without, in separate processes.
- `docs/evidence/perf/load-rss-20261021/ab.sh` runs both, alternating, under the GPU lock.

Related: `seeing.memory_report` on the [seeing](book/agents/seeing.md) page (GPU memory by category),
`render.memory_budget` (load sets against a tier budget), and
`docs/evidence/perf/memory-20261007.md` (the DO27 memory budgets).

## Host memory budget (ADR-7891)

The renderer draws an uploaded mesh from its GPU buffers; the CPU copy is only needed again by a
CPU reader, after device loss, or when the GPU copy is evicted. A host that keeps its meshes in a
`regia_render::host_memory::HostMeshStore` gets a cap on those copies:

- `insert_pak(reader, asset_id)` loads a cooked mesh and keeps the pak source; `insert_owned(..)`
  keeps a procedural mesh (never dropped, counted as `unsourced_bytes`).
- Each frame: `prepare(&renderer, &quality, draws)` re-reads the dropped copies the frame needs,
  `frame_mesh(..)` builds each `FrameMesh` (a dropped copy is a *resident draw*: empty slices, drawn
  from the GPU buffers), and `after_frame(&renderer)` drops copies least recently drawn first until
  `cpu_mesh_bytes` fits the budget.
- `pin(id)` / `unpin(id)` mark a CPU consumer (a collider build, picking, CPU skinning or morphs, a
  mask decal or scalar overlay); a pinned mesh is never dropped. `cpu_geometry(id)` serves a late
  reader (re-read from the pak when dropped).
- Only meshes the renderer can draw without bytes are dropped: none while the visibility buffer,
  DDGI probes, the traced sun, ReSTIR GI or lightmap receivers are on, and never one whose material
  is an emissive mesh light, a surface graph or transmissive. Those frames count over-budget ticks.
- Texture payloads are counted (`set_cpu_texture_bytes`) against `cpu_texture_bytes`, not dropped yet.

The budget is `RenderProfile::host_memory` (per preset: Mobile Low 128/64 MiB; Mobile High, Deck and
Desktop Low 512/256 MiB; Desktop High 1536/512 MiB; Desktop Ultra and Cinematic 3072/1024 MiB, mesh/texture),
unless the process-wide override is set.

| Method | Params | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| `render.set_host_budget` | `cpu_mesh_bytes` (integer, optional), `cpu_texture_bytes` (integer, optional), `clear` (boolean, optional) | the `host` block below; a side left out keeps its value, `clear: true` removes the override |
| `render.memory_budget` | as before | adds `host: { budget: { cpu_mesh_bytes, cpu_texture_bytes }, override, cpu_mesh_bytes, cpu_texture_bytes, dropped_bytes, drops, reread_bytes, rereads, over_budget_ticks, pinned_bytes, unsourced_bytes, mapped_touched_bytes }` (`null` budget side = unlimited) |

Errors: `host_budget_bad_params` (INVALID_PARAMS): no byte value and no `clear`, a byte value that is
not a whole number of 0 or more, a `clear` that is not a boolean, or `clear` with byte values.

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"method":"render.set_host_budget","params":{"cpu_mesh_bytes":67108864}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":8,"method":"render.memory_budget","params":{"tier":"deck"}}
```

`tier` is `minimum` (the default), `deck`, `desktop_high` or `integrated_low` (the integrated-GPU floor: 2.5 GiB RAM,
1.5 GiB GPU memory; the budget a host running Very Low admits against, ADR-8878).

`mapped_touched_bytes` is the size of the pak entries read through the pak's memory mapping: those
file pages count in the process RSS while the pak is mapped (clean, reclaimable), so compare RSS with
`cpu_mesh_bytes + mapped_touched_bytes`. The same counters are in `regia_render::memory_report`'s
`MemoryReport::host` and in the telemetry window record's `memory.host`.

Tests: `cargo test -p regia_render --test host_mesh_budget` (512 MiB drawn under 64 MiB, resident
draws pixel-equal, re-read after the GPU copies go, a pinned mesh kept) and `--test host_mesh_rss`
(process RSS growth within the derived bound, Linux).

<!-- source: book/agents/determinism-matrix.md -->
# Determinism matrix: thread counts, executors and builds

A Regia Engine simulation stepped on a fixed timestep with the same input should reach the same state on every run. The
[schedule shuffle](book/agents/schedule-shuffle.md) checks one way that breaks (system order). The determinism matrix checks the
others: the schedule executor, the size of the compute thread pool, and the build profile (debug against release). It
is a test harness, not a runtime feature, so there is no agent-protocol method: an agent runs the test and reads its
failure message (ADR-1347).

## Run it

```sh
cargo test -p regia_test_utils --test determinism_matrix
cargo test -p regia_test_utils --test determinism_matrix --release     # the release side of debug vs release
REGIA_DET_THREADS=1,3,16 cargo test -p regia_test_utils --test determinism_matrix
```

It needs no GPU. `REGIA_DET_FRAMES` (default 240) sets the run length; the pinned-trace check only runs at 240.

Each scene must give the same trace:

| Test | Compares |
|---|---|
| `a_scene_is_repeatable_in_one_process` | two runs in the same process |
| `the_executor_does_not_change_any_scene` | the single-threaded and the multi-threaded executor |
| `the_compute_pool_size_does_not_change_any_scene` | compute pools of 1, 2, 4 and 8 threads, one child process each |
| `every_scene_matches_its_pinned_trace_in_this_build` | the trace pinned for this target in `crates/regia_test_utils/tests/fixtures/determinism/` |

The pool is process-global and sized once, so the thread-count test re-runs its own test binary once per size with
`REGIA_DET_CHILD_THREADS=<n>` and reads the traces the child prints. The child checks that it really got `n`
threads. With `--nocapture` the test also prints, per thread count, on how many steps the `race` spawners ran out of
lane order (`det_matrix::race_out_of_order`; always 0 on the single-threaded executor). That number is evidence
that the race happened; it depends on timing and is never asserted.

## Reading a failure

A trace is the snapshot hash of the whole world every 20 frames, plus one hash per `<entity>/<Component>` at the last
frame. The snapshot is the one the schedule shuffle uses: reflected components keyed by entity `Name`, entity ids left
out. A failure reads:

```text
1 vs 4 threads: scene race: first differs at frame 60; at the last frame: race0-48/Transform, race1-48/Velocity, ...
```

- The **first differing frame** brackets when the drift started (between it and the checkpoint before it).
- The **keys** name the components that moved. The systems that write them, or that spawn those entities, are the
  suspects.
- `not comparable` means the two runs used different frame counts: check `REGIA_DET_FRAMES`.

A pinned trace that differs in one build only (say, release) points at code whose result depends on optimization:
an integer overflow that panics in debug and wraps in release, a float expression the optimizer evaluates at compile
time, or `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` code that writes state.

## Blessing the pinned traces

The pinned file is per target (`<scene>.<arch>-<os>.trace`): the platform math library and rapier's float reductions
differ between targets. Write it like a golden image, on the reference machine, and give the reason in the commit
message:

```sh
REGIA_BLESS=1 cargo test -p regia_test_utils --test determinism_matrix every_scene_matches_its_pinned_trace
```

A missing file fails on Linux x86_64 (the gate's target) and is only reported elsewhere. Like a golden image, the
check is skipped when `REGIA_SKIP_GOLDENS=1` (the real-GPU pass). glibc picks FMA variants of
`sin`, `cos` and `exp` at run time, so a new CPU or glibc can differ from the reference: compare the failing keys
before re-blessing.

## Debug against release directly

Without a pinned file, run the child test in both profiles and compare what they print (the trace lines start with
`regia-det-trace`, `cp`, `key`, `scene`, `frames`, `every` or `end`):

```sh
for p in dev release; do
  REGIA_DET_CHILD_THREADS=4 cargo test --profile "$p" -p regia_test_utils --test determinism_matrix \
    det_matrix_child -- --exact --nocapture | grep -E '^(regia-det|scene|frames|every|cp|key|end)' > "trace-$p.txt"
done
diff trace-dev.txt trace-release.txt && echo "debug and release agree"
```

The first differing `cp` line is the first checkpoint that drifted; differing `key` lines name the components.

## The scenes

- `smoke`: the schedule-shuffle scene (falling boxes, a walking character, spring bones, a clip and a socket).
- `race`: three spawner systems with no order between them drop colliding boxes into a walled bin on the same steps,
  and a reaper despawns boxes after 75 steps. On the multi-threaded executor the spawners run in parallel, so they get
  their entity ids, and reuse the reaped ones, in thread-timing order.
- `ragdoll`: three limp humanoid ragdolls (capsule bodies on limited joints) dropped on a floor and on each other.

`det_matrix::scenes()` lists them; add a scene there (a `fn() -> App` that steps one fixed step per update with a
manual clock) and bless its pinned trace.

## Rules that keep a simulation deterministic

- **Order by arrival, not by entity id.** `Commands::spawn` reserves an entity id when the command is *recorded*, so
  two systems that spawn in the same pass on different threads get their ids in timing order. The commands are
  applied in a fixed order. Code that must process new entities in a repeatable order sorts them with
  `regia_ecs::spawn_order` instead of by `Entity`:

  ```rust,wrap
  # use regia::prelude::*;
  # let app: &mut App = todo!();
  # #[derive(Component)] struct Projectile;
  use regia_ecs::spawn_order::{SpawnOrder, try_track_spawn_order};

  // In the plugin, before any entity has the component. Treat an error as fatal: the
  // fallback order is entity ids, which parallel spawns reserve in thread-timing order,
  // so a simulation that sorts by it diverges between replays.
  if let Err(error) = try_track_spawn_order::<Projectile>(app.world_mut()) {
      panic!("spawn-order tracking of Projectile failed: {error:?}");
  }

  // In the system:
  fn launch(order: Res<SpawnOrder<Projectile>>, new: Query<Entity, Added<Projectile>>) {
      let mut entities: Vec<Entity> = new.iter().collect();
      order.sort_by_spawn(&mut entities, |e| *e);
      // ...
  }
  ```

  Physics (bodies, colliders, joints; 2D bodies and colliders) and the aero feed already do
  this, and their plugins panic at build time when tracking cannot start
  (the component already in use, or its `on_add`/`on_remove` hooks taken by another owner) —
  add those plugins before anything inserts the tracked components. The script pass tracks
  `Scripts` with the soft `track_spawn_order`
  (`crates/regia_framework/src/script.rs`); it returns false, and the keys fall back to
  entity ids, when tracking cannot start, so it never panics. The soft call is meant for
  non-simulation uses; the script pass is the remaining simulation user (see the fixrev-07-k
  fragment's Known issues). Never insert a tracked simulation
  component through `ParallelCommands`: its per-thread queues apply in thread-arrival order,
  so cross-thread arrival order is thread-timing order again.
- **Order every spawning system against what reads its entities.** A sync point applies the commands of every system
  that has finished, ordered before it or not. A spawner with no order to the physics step lands its bodies before or
  after a step depending on timing: order it `.before(PhysicsStep)` (or `.after`).
- **Use the fixed step's time in `FixedUpdate`**: `FixedTime::step()`, not the frame delta.
- **Expect f32 math on constants to differ between builds by an ulp.** The compiler evaluates `sin`, `exp`, `powf`
  and `powi` with constant arguments while compiling, in f64, and rounds once; at run time the f32 functions (and
  repeated multiplication for `powi`) can land one ulp away. Release builds inline more, so they fold more. Keep
  values that seed a simulation (initial rotations, tables) in data, or compute them in f64, and write small integer
  powers as multiplications. `crates/regia_core/tests/float_folding.rs` checks that `sqrt`, `mul_add` and f64 calls
  fold to the run-time bits, and reports the f32 cases that do not.
- **Iterate maps in a fixed order.** `HashMap` iteration order changes per process. Sort, or use a `BTreeMap`, before
  anything that writes state or spawns.

## In your own tests

```rust,wrap
# fn build_my_app() -> regia::prelude::App { todo!() }
use regia_test_utils::det_matrix::{Executor, diff, record};

let single = record("mine", build_my_app, 240, 20, Executor::SingleThreaded);
let multi = record("mine", build_my_app, 240, 20, Executor::MultiThreaded);
assert_eq!(diff(&single, &multi, 12), None);
```

For thread counts, copy the `det_matrix_child` / `run_children` pair from
`crates/regia_test_utils/tests/determinism_matrix.rs` into your test file: the child test must have a unique name in
its binary.

<!-- source: book/agents/ui-a11y-platform.md -->
# Screen-reader OS bridge (AccessKit)

With the `accesskit` feature, the accessibility tree from [ui.a11y_tree](book/agents/ui-a11y.md) reaches the platform's
assistive technology through AccessKit: AT-SPI on Linux (Orca), UI Automation on Windows (Narrator, NVDA),
NSAccessibility on macOS (VoiceOver) and TalkBack on Android (ADR-3454). The bridge is off by default
(ADR-1998).

```toml
regia = { workspace = true, features = ["accesskit"] }
```

The three methods below exist on every build. Without the feature they answer `platform_bridge_off`.

## How the bridge works

- **Idle until a screen reader connects.** No tree is built or sent while no assistive technology is connected
  (and exporting is off). When one connects, the next frame sends the whole tree.
- **Incremental after that.** Each frame sends only the nodes that changed. Structural changes always go: new
  nodes, nodes whose children changed, the dialog that is modal, announcements, including when that count
  is past the budget. Property-only changes (a label, a value, a state, bounds) fill the slots left after
  those structural nodes: at most `256 - structural_count` that frame, and the rest go in later frames.
- **Stable ids.** A platform node's id is the id `ui.a11y_tree` reports (the entity bits). The window root is
  `0`. The two announcers (polite, assertive) are `4294967296` and `8589934592`. No entity can have these ids
  (an entity id's low 32 bits are never 0).
- **Requests come back through the UI's request path.** A screen reader's click, focus, increment, set value or
  close runs like `ui.a11y_act`: it is refused for disabled, inert and unknown nodes, and the outcome shows
  under `requests` in `ui.a11y_tree`.

| Engine | AccessKit |
|---|---|
| role `window` (a `UiRoot`) | `Pane` under the synthetic `Window` root |
| other roles | the same role (`progress_bar` is `ProgressIndicator`) |
| name | label |
| description, hint | description (`description. hint`) |
| value | value; sliders and progress bars also have `numeric_value`, `min`, `max`, `step` |
| bounds (x, y, width, height) | bounds (x0, y0, x1, y1), physical px in the window |
| `disabled`, `selected`, `invalid`, `checked`, `expanded`, `read_only` | the same states (`checked` is `toggled`) |
| the open dialog of the top input layer | `modal`, with custom action `1` "Close" |
| live region politeness | `live` |
| announcements | the label of the polite or assertive announcer |

| AccessKit action | Engine request | Offered by |
|---|---|---|
| `click` | `press` | buttons, check boxes, combo boxes, other focusable nodes |
| `focus` | `focus` | focusable nodes |
| `increment`, `decrement` | `raise`, `lower` | sliders |
| `set_value` (text), `replace_selected_text` | `set_text` | editable text fields. A numeric `set_value` is accepted and queued, then left unmapped (`maps_to` null); the text stays unchanged. Pass a string to set it. |
| `custom_action` 1 | `close` | dialogs |
| `scroll_into_view` | `scroll_into_view` | every node under the root |
| `scroll_up`, `scroll_down`, `scroll_left`, `scroll_right` | `page_up` ... `page_right` | scroll views, lists |

A disabled or inert node offers no actions. Other AccessKit actions (tooltips, text selection, ...) are counted
and dropped.

## Methods

- `ui.a11y_platform_tree {}` (permission `read`) returns the tree the OS adapter holds, depth first from the
  window root. Each node has `id`, `parent`, `children`, `role` (the AccessKit role name), `label`,
  `description`, `value`, `numeric_value`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `bounds`, `actions`, `custom_actions`,
  `toggled`, `expanded`, `selected`, `disabled`, `read_only`, `modal`, `invalid` and `live`. The result also has
  `adapter` (`atspi`, `uia`, `ns_accessibility`, `android`, or `null` with no window), `adapter_error`,
  `android` (`os`, `registered`, `attached`, `status`, `detail`), `active`,
  `needs_full_tree`, `root`, `focus`, `last_error` and `stats` (`updates`, `full_updates`, `nodes_sent`,
  `delivered`, `superseded`, `invalid_updates`, `resyncs`, `actions`, `actions_dropped`, `activations`,
  `deactivations`). `resyncs` counts the times a screen reader connected while a frame's updates were on their
  way to the adapter, so the whole tree went instead.
- `ui.a11y_platform_connect { connected }` (permission `play`) simulates a screen reader connecting (`true`: the
  next frame sends the whole tree) or leaving (`false`). Use it to check the bridge with no screen reader.
  The result includes the same `android` object as the tree.
- `ui.a11y_platform_action { node, action, value? }` (permission `play`) queues an AccessKit action request as the
  OS adapter would. The node must offer the action (its `actions`, or for `custom_action` its `custom_actions`).
  `value` is text or a number for `set_value`, text for `replace_selected_text`, and the action id for
  `custom_action`. Text `set_value` and `replace_selected_text` map to `set_text`. A number for `set_value`
  is queued and left unmapped (`maps_to` is null, and the field's text does not change); pass a string to
  set the text. The request runs in the next frame. The result is `{ queued, node, action, maps_to, note }`,
  where `maps_to` is the engine request (`press`, `raise`, ...) or `null`.

```json
{"method": "ui.a11y_platform_connect", "params": {"connected": true}}
{"method": "ui.a11y_platform_tree", "params": {}}
{"method": "ui.a11y_platform_action", "params": {"node": 4294967300, "action": "increment"}}
{"method": "ui.a11y_platform_action", "params": {"node": 4294967310, "action": "set_value", "value": "Ada"}}
{"method": "ui.a11y_platform_action", "params": {"node": 4294967320, "action": "custom_action", "value": 1}}
```

A typical check: connect, wait one frame, read the platform tree and check that every control has a `label`
and the actions you expect. Then act, wait one frame, and read `ui.a11y_tree` `requests` and the platform tree
again.

## Error codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `platform_bridge_off` | the build has no `accesskit` feature, or the app installed another screen-reader backend |
| `bad_connected` | `ui.a11y_platform_connect` without a boolean `connected` |
| `a11y_node_missing` | `ui.a11y_platform_action` without `node` |
| `a11y_action_missing` | `ui.a11y_platform_action` without `action` |
| `a11y_value_missing` | `set_value`, `replace_selected_text` or `custom_action` without a usable `value` |
| `bad_entity` | `node` is not a non-negative integer |
| `bad_action` | `action` is not a string, or not an AccessKit action name |
| `bad_value` | `value` is neither a string nor a finite number |
| `text_too_long` | a text `value` over 4096 characters |
| `unknown_node` | the node is not in the platform tree (the tree is empty until a screen reader connects) |
| `unsupported_action` | the node does not offer that action |

## Environment

- `REGIA_ACCESSKIT=0` keeps the OS adapter off. The bridge and its platform tree still work, and the agent
  reports `adapter_error`.
- `REGIA_SCREEN_READER=1` marks the bridge as connected at start-up (headless runs).

## Known limits

- Android (ADR-3454): TalkBack activates the bridge and the next update is a full tree. There is no
  callback when TalkBack turns off, so the bridge stays active until the process ends or
  `ui.a11y_platform_connect` is `false`. The adapter checks `AccessibilityManager.isEnabled()` before each
  update and holds updates while it is off, then sends the whole tree once it is back on (ADR-4932). The delegate class is loaded from the crate (`embedded-dex`);
  the activity shim is unchanged. `set_window_focused` does nothing on Android. One adapter per
  process, on the primary window's surface view. A JNI failure is logged and the bridge is disabled.
  A shipping build (`panic = "abort"`) still ends if AccessKit unwraps after that preflight.
- Steam Deck game mode has no assistive-technology path (no screen reader in game mode). Desktop mode
  on the Deck is Linux (AT-SPI).
- On X11 the window position is not sent to AT-SPI, so Orca's flat review may place nodes at the window origin.
- The Linux adapter's D-Bus thread panics if the accessibility bus fails in a way it does not expect. Shipping
  builds use `panic = "abort"`, so that panic ends the game. This is one reason the feature is off by default;
  `REGIA_ACCESSKIT=0` is the way out.
- With the feature on, the Windows and macOS window is created hidden and shown right after the adapter
  attaches (the Windows adapter must subclass the window before it is first shown).

(`cef03dc3e`) is integrated, but the UI accessibility fixes (`c114b1bc7`,

On the resumed candidate, record the exact commit, OS and named reader/version
for Orca/Linux and Narrator or NVDA/Windows, plus VoiceOver/macOS if available.
Record announcements, focus order, action results, and modal entry/exit. Keep
each unavailable session explicitly deferred. Exercise keyboard and physical

through restart. On TEST Pixel 9 Pro `54101FDAP0015H`, exercise actual touch,

packages. Check that the blurred modal preserves focus and that warm target

The lane handoff is
`<workspace>`.
It lists the exact checks still required. C10/C12 remain thin; this checkpoint
