## v0.5 C10/C12 acceptance checkpoint (2026-11-09, lane v05-a11y-runtime-b)

The prerequisites above are absorbed on `lane/sprint-v05-a11y-runtime-b`. The controls screen (a `RebindPanel` with
every option, inside a frosted panel) is covered through the AccessKit bridge by the `controls_screen` module of
`crates/regia_ui/tests/accesskit_bridge.rs` (`--features accesskit`). It checks names and descriptions, Tab, D-pad and touch reach,
a blur-neutral tree and Tab order, restart persistence of invert and dead zone, a rebind capture on a pause dialog,
and a phone flow: safe area, 200 % text, reduced motion, right-to-left, and the touch audit. These tests use a
recording adapter. They are not screen-reader results.

Still deferred, with the reason:

- Orca on Linux: no host with Orca and a desktop session is open to lanes. the workstation is the owner's desktop.
- Narrator or NVDA on Windows: on the N150 laptop, programs started over ssh cannot see the desktop. A GUI run
  needs an interactive scheduled task, and nothing remote can hear what Narrator says. A reader session needs
  someone at the machine.
- VoiceOver on macOS: ssh cannot capture the screen and gets no AppleEvents permission there. VoiceOver scripting
  needs a root-owned flag.
- TalkBack, touch and scale on the TEST Pixel 9 Pro `54101FDAP0015H`: the phone was not connected during the lane.

To run a reader session, open the First Person template's controls screen (F10) in a build with
`--features regia/accesskit`. Tab through one axis row and record what the reader says. Toggle invert, step the
dead zone, restart the game, and confirm the values come back. Then start a capture, press Escape, and confirm the
dialog stays open.

## Android device pass (2026-11-09, lane v05-a11y-android-talkback, ADR-4932)

Run on the TEST Pixel 9 Pro (`54101FDAP0015H`, Android 17, landscape 2142x960 px at OS scale 2.25). The build was
a debug APK of a project made from the First Person template, with `regia` `features = ["accesskit"]`.

- Turning TalkBack on (`settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services ...`) activated the bridge:
  `android.status` `attached`, `activations` 1, one full update of 82 nodes, no invalid updates. Later focus
  changes went out as small updates.
- `uiautomator dump` lists the screen's nodes as Android sees them. Buttons are `android.widget.Button`, toggles
  are `CheckBox` with `checkable` set, and the dead zone is a `SeekBar` with its value. Bounds are in physical px.
  Clicks are an `ACTION_CLICK` in the node's action list (`clickable` reads false; TalkBack uses the action).
- `accesskit_android` 0.7.5 gives TalkBack the label only. The Android adapter therefore folds each node's
  description into its label (`regia_platform::accessibility::fold_descriptions_into_labels`): `Invert Y` with
  `Move, gamepad` reaches TalkBack as `Invert Y, Move, gamepad`. `ui.a11y_platform_tree` still shows both fields,
  because it is the tree the UI sent, before the Android fold.
- An update sent after an accessibility client went away aborted the game: Android refused the event, and
  `accesskit_android` 0.7.5 unwraps that refusal on the UI thread. The adapter now holds updates while
  accessibility is off (`android_update_gate`) and resyncs with the whole tree after
  (`AccessKitBridge::request_resync`). On the fixed build, a drag right after `uiautomator` disconnected left
  the game running.
- Back is named `BrowserBack` (it had no winit key code), and leaves a rebind capture instead of being bound.
- TalkBack's own gestures cannot be driven from adb: events from `adb shell input` bypass TalkBack's touch
  explorer (a tap on a launcher icon opened the app instead of focusing it). Explore by touch, swipe navigation
  and the double tap therefore need a person with the phone. The report of the lane lists the steps.

## Android display size and reader cost (2026-11-10, lane v05-a11y-density, ADR-5379)

Run on the TEST Pixel 9 Pro (`54101FDAP0015H`). The build was a First Person template project with
`regia` `features = ["accesskit"]`. Its native code used the release profile's codegen in a debuggable APK, so
the agent could attach.

- **Display size.** The runner re-reads the density (`Configuration.densityDpi / 160`) after every resume,
  when the window gains focus, and on every configuration change. It writes `WindowScaleFactorChanged` when the
  density moved. With the controls screen open, `adb shell wm density 480` moved `ui.state` `scale.scale_factor`
  from 2.25 to 3.0 in the same process, and the Look button grew from 360x84 to 480x113 px.
  `ui.a11y_audit {"profile":"touch"}` reported 0 non-info findings at both densities. `wm density reset` went
  back to 2.25. Before the change, winit's scale stayed at the density the app started with.
- **Reader cost.** `ui.a11y_tree` `sync_cost` gives the cost of each live frame's sync over its last 512 frames,
  split into `build`, `diff` and `backend`. TalkBack was on before the game started, the game had focus, and the
  controls screen was open (81 nodes, 168 UI entities). Over four windows the mean was 0.27 to 0.58 ms and the
  p99 0.54 to 0.86 ms. The tree build was about 80 % of it. The HUD alone (7 nodes) had a mean of 0.12 ms and a
  p99 of 0.29 ms.
- **Measuring.** Turn TalkBack on before you start the game. When TalkBack is turned on, it first shows a
  permission prompt over the game. That pauses the game: it runs at the hidden rate (about 10 frames a second, no
  presents) and the numbers are higher (mean 1.38 ms, p99 2.32 ms). Keep the screen awake
  (`svc power stayon usb`, then restore it). Agent calls do not count as user activity, and the app stops
  answering once the screen times out and suspends it.

<!-- source: book/agents/ui-a11y-audit.md -->
# UI accessibility audit

`ui.a11y_audit` finds accessibility defects in the screen the UI shows now. It combines what the other checks
look at separately: `ui.theme_lint` checks a theme's token pairs, `ui.nav_lint` the focus graph and
`ui.a11y_tree` the names. A button with an empty name, white text on a light image panel, a 12 px close box or a
label cut off at 200 % text scale can pass all three. The audit looks at the computed layout, the accessibility
tree and each node's resolved theme look together (ADR-3025).

It reads. It adds no system to the frame, so a game that never calls it pays nothing, and the live UI is left as
it was. The 200 % check runs the real layout in a scratch world.

```json
{"method": "ui.a11y_audit", "params": {}}
{"method": "ui.a11y_audit", "params": {"profile": "touch", "rules": ["a11y_target_size"]}}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `root` | Only this node and its subtree (entity bits). Everything still paints, so backgrounds stay right. Omit it for every root. |
| `profile` | `desktop` (default) or `touch`. See `a11y_target_size`. |
| `rules` | The rule codes to run. Omit it for all of them. |
| `min_target` | Replaces the profile's minimum target, in UI px. |
| `text_scale` | The scale `a11y_text_clipped_at_scale` lays out at, 1 to 3. Default 2. |

## Reply

`{ clean, theme, profile, min_target_px, text_scale, reduced_motion, nodes, truncated, errors, warnings, infos,
findings_total, findings, exemptions, skipped }`

Each finding is `{ rule, severity, node, path, measured, required, criterion, hint, needs_eyes }`:

- **`severity`**: `error`, `warning` or `info`. `info` means the audit could not tell and a person has to look.
  It is never a pass, and `clean` is false while one is listed.
- **`node`**: the entity bits, for `ui.query` and `ui.click`. Valid in this run only.
- **`path`**: `NodeName`s, else `role[child index]` (`hud/panel[2]/button[0]`). It names no entity, so it stays
  the same between runs. Compare paths, not node ids.
- **`measured`** and **`required`**: what was found and what the rule needs (`2.10:1` and `4.50:1`).
- **`criterion`**: the WCAG 2.2 success criterion number, or `engine` for the engine's own contract.
- **`needs_eyes`**: true when a person has to check it.

Findings are sorted by rule, then severity, then path, so two runs over the same screen answer the same bytes.

`exemptions` lists `{ rule, path, exemption }` for each node a rule let pass because of a named exception, so a
reviewer can see what was excused. `skipped` lists `{ rule, reason }` for rules that could not run.

`truncated` is true when more than 32,768 nodes were visible. A reply lists at most 4,096 findings, and
`findings_total` counts them all.

## Rules

| Code | Criterion | What it reports |
|---|---|---|
| `a11y_unnamed_interactive` | 4.1.2 | A focusable or pressable node with no accessible name. |
| `a11y_text_contrast` | 1.4.3 | Text against its effective background: 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text. |
| `a11y_nontext_contrast` | 1.4.11 | The focus ring and a control's boundary against what is next to them: 3:1. |
| `a11y_target_size` | 2.5.8 | A target under the minimum, 24 UI px per side by default. |
| `a11y_focus_unreachable` | 2.4.3 | A node keyboard or gamepad navigation cannot reach. |
| `a11y_no_focus_indicator` | 2.4.7 | A focusable node that would draw no focus indicator. |
| `a11y_text_clipped_at_scale` | 1.4.4 | Text lost when the text scale goes to 200 %. |
| `a11y_motion_ignores_setting` | `engine` | An animation that keeps running with reduced motion on. |

### `a11y_unnamed_interactive`

A node with `Focusable` or `Interactable` whose name in `ui.a11y_tree` is empty, only spaces, or a missing
localization key. Severity is `error` for a focusable node or a node with a role. It is `warning` for a bare
pointer surface with no role, which may be a gesture catcher. Mark that with `Accessible::decorative()` if it
is one. Drag surfaces that hold other things (windows, scroll views, lists, dialogs) are not controls to name
unless they take focus.

Exemption: `decoration`.

### `a11y_text_contrast`

The background comes from walking down the paint order, the way the draw list paints: through solid and
translucent fills, including a panel that is a sibling behind the text and not an ancestor. A translucent layer
painted over the text (a dialog's scrim) tints glyphs and background alike. The ratio is the one `ui.theme_lint`
uses.

| Background | Result |
|---|---|
| Solid or translucent fills ending in an opaque one | `error` when under the ratio |
| A gradient | The worst stop counts. `error` when every stop fails, `warning` with `needs_eyes` when only some do |
| An image, a UI material, or a slider or progress fill | `info`, `needs_eyes` |
| Nothing opaque (the scene or the clear color shows) | `info`, `needs_eyes` |
| Partly over a fill | `info`, `needs_eyes`: the text spans two backgrounds |

An opaque fill over an image makes the background known again. Text under the ratio that has an outline in a
contrasting color is `info` with `needs_eyes`, because the outline gives the glyphs an edge of their own. Large
text is at least 24 UI px, or 18.66 UI px when bold. The live text scale counts.

Exemptions: `inactive_component` (disabled), `decoration` (`Accessible::decorative()`), `not_visible` (fully
transparent, or under an opaque cover).

### `a11y_nontext_contrast`

- **Focus ring:** the node's `focus_ring` color on what surrounds the node, or on its own fill for an inset ring.
  `measured` starts with `focus ring`.
- **Control boundary:** for sliders, toggles, radio buttons, spin boxes, text fields and combo boxes, and for
  focusable nodes with no text. The best of the border, the fill and a slider's or toggle's knob against what
  surrounds the control. `measured` starts with the kind (`text_input boundary`). The themes' `Panel.field` and
  `Button.field` classes have a 3:1 edge: use them for text fields and combo boxes.

An icon button is `info` with `needs_eyes`: its icon identifies it, and the audit does not read pixels. A surface
it cannot resolve is `info` with `needs_eyes` too.

Exemptions: `inactive_component`, `text_identifies_control` (a button with text needs no boundary).

### `a11y_target_size`

`desktop` measures each side of the node's rect in UI px and needs 24. `touch` needs the theme's `size.touch-min`,
or 44 without one, measured in device-independent px: physical px divided by the window's OS scale factor
(ADR-4932). A fingertip has a physical size, and a reference-resolution scale can shrink a UI well below the screen
density. On a 2142x960 phone at OS scale 2.25, the default 1920x1080 reference gives UI scale 1.0, so a 44 UI px
box is about 20 dp and fails. Without a known factor (no `UiScales`), `touch` measures UI px too. The `measured`
and `required` strings keep the `px` unit. `min_target` replaces either minimum, in the profile's unit. You can make a hit box larger than what
it draws: a `regia_ui::TouchTarget { min_px }` on the node grows its hit box to at least `min_px` per side around its
center (ADR-4903), and this rule measures that box. Hit testing uses the same box; layout and drawing do not change,
so space neighbors far enough apart that their boxes do not overlap.

The criterion's exceptions, each listed in `exemptions` when used:

| Exemption | How it applies |
|---|---|
| `spacing` | Measured, `desktop` only: a circle as wide as the minimum, centered on the target, touches no other target and no other small target's circle. A fingertip needs the size itself, so `touch` does not use it. |
| `equivalent` | Declared with the `TargetExemption` component: another control does the same thing and meets the size. |
| `inline` | Declared: the target sits in a sentence or a block of text. |
| `user_agent_control` | Declared: the platform decides the size. |
| `essential` | Declared: this size is essential to what the control conveys. |
| `inactive_component` | The engine's choice, not one of the criterion's five: a disabled control cannot be activated. |

### `a11y_focus_unreachable`

Reuses the lint behind `ui.nav_lint`, on the active scope's graph, from the focused node or the initial node.
`measured` is one of:

- `unreachable` (`error`): no sequence of moves gets there.
- `dead_end` (`warning`): no move leaves the node.
- `not_focusable` (`error`): a button, check box, slider, text field or combo box that takes clicks but has no
  `Focusable`. No keyboard or gamepad can reach it.

### `a11y_no_focus_indicator`

`measured` is one of:

- `no ring` (`error`): no `Themed` look, or a ring with no width or no color. A `Focusable` with no theme class
  has no ring at all.
- `the clip of an ancestor cuts the whole ring` (`error`): the band lies wholly outside the clip. Use an inset ring
  (`border.width.focus-inset`, as list rows do). A partly clipped ring still shows and passes.
- `FocusRingPolicy::Never: the game draws its own` (`info`, `needs_eyes`).
- `no ring; a motion preset moves on focus` (`info`, `needs_eyes`).

Exemption: `inactive_component`.

### `a11y_text_clipped_at_scale`

Lays each root out in a scratch world at `text_scale` and at 100 %, with the same layout code, window size and
fonts as the live UI, and reports text that:

| `measured` | Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `... cuts N px of the text` | `error` | A clipping ancestor cuts it |
| `text needs WxH px in a WxH px box that clips` | `error` | Its own box clips it |
| `cut short with an ellipsis` | `error` | It ends in an ellipsis |
| `text ends N px past the screen` | `error` | It leaves the window |
| `text spills N px out of its container` | `warning` | It leaves a filled or bordered parent but stays visible. Not reported when it does so at 100 % too |
| `fit-to-box holds the text at Nx` | `warning` | `ScaleToFit` loses nothing, but the text did not reach the size asked for |

A problem that shows at 100 % as well ends in `(at 100 % too)`. Text reported as lost gets no second line for
spilling. A scroll view or list above the text makes it reachable when its content overflows it and the view fits
the window. A view that grew with its content has nothing to scroll to, so it excuses nothing. A list below the fold
of a page that scrolls stays reachable through the page. Overlap between neighboring nodes is not checked.

Exemption: `captions` (they have their own size option, ADR-3025).

### `a11y_motion_ignores_setting`

A `UiTween` with `follows_reduced_motion` set says its plan already obeys reduced motion, so the tween system
plays it instead of jumping to the end. The rule reports a plan that would still animate anything but opacity, or
fade longer than `motion.fast`. The result does not depend on the setting being on now; `reduced_motion` in the
reply says whether it is. Plain tweens jump to their end value and are never reported.

## Error codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `bad_entity` | `root` is not an entity id. |
| `unknown_entity` | `root` names no entity. |
| `bad_profile` | `profile` is not `desktop` or `touch`. |
| `unknown_rule` | `rules` names a code that is not in the table above. |
| `ui_not_installed` | The app has no runtime UI. |

An unknown parameter or a wrong type answers `F0002`.

## Limits

- The audit does not read pixels: what an image shows always needs eyes.
- A focused state that differs only by its theme `focused` layer is not seen as an indicator. The audit looks for a
  ring.
- A pass is not a screen-reader test. Run the screen on real assistive technology too (see
  [the accessibility guide](book/user-guide/accessibility.md)).
- World-space and camera-target roots are audited at their target size, in their own paint stack.

# Render movie (editor)

**Sequence ▸ Render movie…** renders a saved `.seq.ron` of the project to frames or a movie file with the
editor's own renderer, as a cancellable editor job (ADR-7726). It runs the same job an agent runs with
[`render.out_job`](book/agents/render-jobs.md): the dialog builds a `.render_job.ron` and starts it in process, so the
frames, their hashes, the manifest and the file names are that job's ([render-out](book/agents/render-out.md)).

## The dialog

| Field | What it sets |
| --- | --- |
| Sequence | the project-relative `.seq.ron` (default: the file open in the [Sequence Curves panel](book/agents/seq-curve-panel.md)); the **saved** file is rendered, so save edits first |
| Output folder | a project-relative folder inside the project (default `renders/movie`); anything else is refused with `path_outside_project` |
| Format | `png` (default), `exr`, `raw`, `webm`, `ffv1`, `prores` or `dnxhr` (the movie formats need the render-out's encoder or `ffmpeg`; the job refuses a format it cannot write) |
| Frames | from a frame to a frame (the end not included), or **to the end** of the sequence |
| Size | width and height in pixels (1 to 16384) and frames per second |

**Render** starts the job. The dialog then shows the frame count and a progress bar with **Cancel**; the editor
keeps drawing between frames (one output frame per editor frame; the files are encoded and written by the
render-out's writer threads). The run is also the background task `render_movie` in the status bar. Starting a run turns off the Sequence Curves panel's
**Preview in level** (its values go back first), so the edit-world preview never fights the job's player.

The job has one take named `movie`, the game UI off, and a binding table so it plays the sequence itself: the
Sequence Curves panel's bindings for that file (each by its entity's scene guid, else its name), plus every other
track target an entity is named after. Frames go to `<out>/movie/movie_<frame>.<ext>` (the job's default path)
with the manifest beside them.

**Cancel** ends the job at the next frame. What stays are the whole frames delivered so far, from the first one
up: a frame file is written as `<name>.part` and renamed, so no partial frame is left and no later frame is
written.

## Agent methods

- `editor.render_movie { sequence, out?, format?, start?, end?, width?, height?, fps?, dry_run? }` (needs
  `edit_scene`) starts the run the dialog's **Render** starts and returns `{ task, job, job_text, frames, out,
  state }`: `job` is the render-out job id (`render.out_progress { job }` reads it too), `job_text` the
  `.render_job.ron` it runs, `frames` the frames it renders. `start` is the first timeline frame (default 0) and
  `end` the frame after the last (default: the end of the sequence). With `dry_run: true` it checks the settings
  and returns `{ dry_run, job_text }` without starting anything.
- `editor.render_movie_status` (read-only) returns `{ task, job, state, frame, frames, first_hash, manifest, error,
  sequence, out, format }`; `state` is `idle`, `running`, `done`, `cancelled` or `failed`, and `first_hash` the
  first delivered frame's hash (the render-out's, hex).
- Progress: each frame the job delivers and its end add a `render_movie` record to `events.read`, whose `data` is
  the status above.
- Cancel: `editor.cancel_task { id: "render_movie" }` (the dialog's Cancel).

Sending `job_text` to `render.out_job` renders the same frames with the same hashes.

```json
{"method": "editor.render_movie", "params": {"sequence": "assets/cine/intro.seq.ron", "out": "renders/intro", "width": 1280, "height": 720, "fps": 24}}
{"method": "events.read", "params": {"since": 0}}
{"method": "editor.render_movie_status", "params": {}}
{"method": "editor.cancel_task", "params": {"id": "render_movie"}}
```

## Errors

Refusals answer `F0002` (`F0003` without a project) with `data.reason`:

| Reason | When |
| --- | --- |
| `render_movie_no_project` | no project is open |
| `render_movie_bad_sequence` | `sequence` does not end in `.seq.ron`, leads out of the project, cannot be read or does not parse |
| `path_outside_project` | `out` is empty, absolute, climbs out with `..` or leads out through a symlink |
| `render_movie_bad_format` | `format` is not one of the formats above |
| `render_movie_bad_range` | `end` is not after `start` |
| `render_movie_bad_size` | a size of 0 or over 16384, or a frame rate outside 1..=1000 |
| `render_movie_busy` | a render-out is already running |

The job's own refusals pass through with their [`render.out_job` codes](book/agents/render-jobs.md) (`render_job_unbound`,
`render_job_no_source`, ...), and an editor started with `--no-gpu` answers `editor_headless`, as for
`render.out_job`. A run that fails ends `failed` with the render-out's error text in `error`.

## From Rust

`regia_editor::render_out_job::{job_for, start, tick, cancel, RenderMovieSettings, RenderMovieJob, MovieState}`;
`regia_agent::render_out_host::{out_job, progress, cancel, job_running}` call the render-out in process.

Not done: the dialog was driven by tests through its functions, not with egui input, and nobody has judged it on a
screen yet; it renders the saved file, not unsaved edits in the panel.

# Onboarding: setting Regia up (agents)

This page is for an AI assistant that installs Regia Engine on a user's machine. It holds the setup flow in detail,
the question script with its ids and defaults, the consent steps, and a fix for each common failure. The rules are
in `AGENTS.md` at the root of the engine folder (section "Rules"); this page does not repeat them and never
overrides them. The user's view of the same flow is [Set up with your AI assistant](book/start/assistant-setup.md),
and the hand install it automates is [Installing Regia Engine](book/start/install.md).

Regia is built from source on the user's machine: there is no installer and no prebuilt download. You run the steps
of the install page yourself, one at a time, asking the user as you go.

## The setup flow

1. **Read first, download later.** Read `AGENTS.md` (over the web when you were given the repository URL,
   https://github.com/Regia-Engine/Regia-Engine). Naming the repository is consent to read that file, not to
   download the engine.
2. **Introduce** Regia in at most five sentences, name the three working modes, and say you will ask about six
   questions.
3. **Questions 1 and 2** (below), from the OS facts; no `regia` exists yet.
4. **Bootstrap** as `AGENTS.md` step 2 gives it, per OS: the prerequisites (the user's administrator commands),
   `rustup-init` checked against its `.sha256` (never a piped installer script), the clone or the release archive,
   `rustup toolchain install` in the engine folder (it reads `rust-toolchain.toml`), then
   `cargo build --release -p regia_cli -p regia_editor`.
5. **Check the machine** with `<engine>/target/release/regia doctor --platform <this OS> --json` and fix each
   failed check with its `fix` ([Toolchain doctor (agents)](book/agents/doctor.md)); for a release archive, also
   `regia engine verify .`.
6. **Questions 3 to 6**, then create the project with `regia new`. Only `blank`, `first_person`, `third_person`
   and `top_down` have a desktop launcher crate (`<snake_case name>_launcher`): warm it with
   `cargo build -p <snake_case name>_launcher`, `regia run` once, then `regia editor`. `quick` has no launcher:
   warm it with plain `cargo build`, run it once with `cargo run`, and stop there. `net_game` has no launcher either: warm it with plain `cargo build` (its
   default members are the game and the client), start the server and a client as its `README.md` says, then
   `regia editor`.
7. **Modes 2 and 3:** for a non-`quick` template, write the project's MCP entry (below) and hand off to a new
   session in the project folder. For `quick`, explain that this path is cargo-only and recommend a full project
   template when the user wants an editor-connected session.
8. **The mode's opening**: mode 1, the editor tour ([Editor tour](book/start/editor-tour.md)); mode 2, a screenshot
   of the editor through MCP and "what would you like to change?"; mode 3, "what game should we make?" and a short
   decision list.

Until a new shell has Regia on its `PATH`, call `regia` by its absolute path, `<engine>/target/release/regia`
(`regia.exe` on Windows).

## The question script

Ask in this order, each at most once per setup; skip a question whose answer the user already gave. Label every
question exactly as in the first column, and every consent `(Consent · <step id>)`.

| Label | Ask | When | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| (Question 1 of 6 · machine) | "This looks like *Linux x86_64, 16 threads, 32 GB RAM, a discrete GPU with Vulkan, 400 GB free*. Set Regia up on this machine?" | always | yes |
| (Question 2 of 6 · install_from) | A git clone or the release archive (when the Releases page has one), and the engine folder | always | clone; Linux and macOS `~/Regia/regia-engine`, Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Regia\e` |
| (Question 3 of 6 · targets) | Platforms to build games for; this machine always; Android, Windows from Linux and Steam Deck add downloads | always | this machine only |
| (Question 4 of 6 · mode) | The three modes, one line each; the user can switch any time | always | 1, local-first |
| (Question 4b · client) | Which assistant app the editor connection is for | modes 2 and 3, when you cannot tell | the app you run in |
| (Question 5 of 6 · template) | The templates (`regia new --help`), one line each, with a recommendation | always | `first_person` |
| (Question 6 of 6 · project) | Project name and projects folder | always | `My Game`, `~/RegiaProjects` |

A git clone is its own engine folder. On Windows keep the engine folder's path short: build paths under `target/`
are deep.

## Consents

Ask one consent per step, with what it downloads or writes, from where, and how large. The user may say yes to
several at once after seeing them together; that never covers an administrator command, which the user always runs
themselves.

| Step | Does | Size to say |
|---|---|---|
| `rust_toolchain` | downloads `rustup-init` from `static.rust-lang.org`, checks it, installs rustup for the user | about 15 MB, then the toolchain |
| `engine_source` | clones the repository or downloads the release archive; `rustup toolchain install` in it | up to about 1 GB of source; about 300 MB of toolchain downloads (1.3 GB installed) |
| `build_tools` | `cargo build --release -p regia_cli -p regia_editor`: crates from crates.io, then compiling | about 150 MB of crates (1.5 GB unpacked); 6 to 10 GB under `target/`; 20 to 60 minutes |
| `shell_path` | adds `<engine>/target/release` to `PATH` in one shell profile file | one line; name the file |
| `android_tools` | the Rust Android targets, `cargo-ndk`, the Android SDK, an NDK, a JDK 17+ and Gradle | about 3 GB; the SDK's licenses are the user's to accept |
| `cross_tools` | Windows from Linux (`cargo-xwin`, the MSVC target) or Steam Deck (`cargo-zigbuild`, zig) | a few hundred MB each |
| `warm_build` | the new project's first build: `cargo build -p <snake_case name>_launcher` for `blank`, `first_person`, `third_person` and `top_down`; plain `cargo build` for `quick` and `net_game`, which have no launcher crate | a few more crates; minutes |
| `connect` | writes the `regia` MCP entry into the game project | one file in the project; name it |

The system packages of [Installing Regia Engine](book/start/install.md) § 2 (headers, the Vulkan driver), the
C/C++ compiler and GPU drivers are administrator commands: show the exact command and why; the user runs it.

## Connecting (modes 2 and 3)

The MCP server is `regia mcp --project DIR`: one MCP tool per agent-protocol method, attached to the project's
running editor or game ([Agent protocol](book/user-guide/agent-protocol.md)). With `--headless` it starts a
windowless editor when none answers and stops it when the server ends ([Headless editor](book/agents/headless-editor.md)); with
`--http` it serves Streamable HTTP on a loopback port with a bearer token ([MCP over HTTP](book/agents/mcp-http.md)).

For Claude Code, write `<project>/.mcp.json` in the shape of the template `dist/mcp/regia.mcp.json.example` (the
absolute path of `regia`, the absolute project path), keeping any other servers in that file. For any other client,
give the user the same command line for its MCP settings. Write nothing into the assistant's own user-wide settings.
A client reads the project's MCP file when a session starts in that folder: ask the user to start a new session
there and approve the `regia` server, then call `agent.hello` and take a screenshot. What the protocol may change is
set by the permission profiles in the project's `.regia/agent.toml`.

The `quick` template is outside this path: it is one Cargo crate with no editor project file, so do not tell the
user to run `regia editor` or write the MCP project entry for it. Keep the quick template in local-first mode, or
recommend a full project template when the user wants modes 2 or 3.

## Troubleshooting

Find the code in `regia doctor --json` (its `checks[].code` and `fix`) or the first error of the failed command,
then:

| Problem | What it means | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `rustc_missing`, `cargo_missing` | Rust did not run | Install rustup (`rust_toolchain`); open a new shell or use `~/.cargo/bin` |
| `rustup_missing` | A distribution `rustc` without rustup | Desktop builds work when its version matches `rust-toolchain.toml`; Android and Windows cross builds need rustup |
| `vulkan_missing`, `vulkan_no_device` | No Vulkan driver, or no device | The user installs the Vulkan driver (`book/start/install.md` § 2) |
| `vulkaninfo_missing` | A driver is installed, `vulkaninfo` is not | The user installs `vulkan-tools`; not needed to build |
| `windows_target_missing`, `cargo_xwin_missing` | Windows cross build tools missing | `cross_tools`: the doctor prints the commands |
| `cargo_zigbuild_missing`, `zig_missing` | Steam Deck build tools missing | `cross_tools`: the doctor prints the commands |
| A `pkg-config` or linker error while building | System headers missing | The user installs the distribution row of `book/start/install.md` § 2 |
| `error: toolchain ... is not installed` | The pinned compiler is missing | `rustup toolchain install` in the engine folder |
| `No space left on device` | The build did not fit | Free space or choose another engine folder; a build needs about 40 GB |
| The build is killed with no error | Out of memory | Build with fewer jobs: `cargo build --release -j 2 -p regia_cli -p regia_editor` |
| `regia engine verify` reports errors | The release copy is damaged or changed | Download the archive again |
| `agent.hello` cannot connect | No editor or game runs in that project | Start `regia editor` or `regia run` there, or use `regia mcp --headless` |
| The `regia` server is not listed | The session started elsewhere, or the server was not approved | Start a new session in the project folder and approve it |

Every other doctor code is on [Toolchain doctor (agents)](book/agents/doctor.md).

## Checks of these files

Two repository commands keep the onboarding files honest; both run in `cargo xtask preflight`.

`cargo xtask llms-txt [--check] [--out DIR]` writes `llms.txt` (the manual's index, in the layout of the public
llms.txt proposal) and `llms-full.txt` (the Start here, User guide, Systems and Agent guide pages in one file, each
after a `<!-- source: book/... -->` line, links rewritten to repository-root paths) into `dist/public-root/`.
`--check` writes nothing and fails when either file is stale, a linked page is missing, or a page has no `# ` title
or no first sentence.

`cargo xtask onboarding-lint` checks the user `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, the skills
(`dist/public-skills/`, published as `.claude/skills/`), the MCP template and this page against the onboarding
contract `xtask/onboarding/contract.md` (the question ids, consent steps, skills, prerequisites and the
`AGENTS.md` sections) and the `regia` command line. Its codes:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `onboarding_file_missing` | A file the lint reads is missing |
| `question_id_mismatch` | A `Question N` label names the wrong id for N |
| `question_total_mismatch` | A label's `of N` is not the number of questions |
| `question_missing` | A file that must carry the whole script lacks a question |
| `question_order` | Questions first appear out of script order |
| `label_template_missing` | `AGENTS.md` does not state both label templates |
| `consent_step_unknown` | A `Consent · <step>` label names no step |
| `command_unknown` | A `regia` command in code is neither a command nor listed as pending |
| `pending_command_exists` | A command listed as pending exists now: remove it from the list |
| `agents_md_marker_missing` | The user `AGENTS.md` does not start with its marker line |
| `agents_md_too_long` | The user `AGENTS.md` has more than 200 lines |
| `agents_md_sections` | The user `AGENTS.md` sections differ from the contract's outline |
| `claude_md_differs` | `CLAUDE.md` is not the contract's text |
| `skill_missing`, `skill_unknown` | A contract skill is missing, or a skill folder is not in the contract |
| `skill_front_matter` | A skill's `name` differs from its folder, or its `description` is empty |
| `skill_too_long` | A skill body has more than 120 lines |
| `skill_no_agents_link` | A skill does not link the `AGENTS.md` section it runs |
| `skill_duplicates_rule` | A skill copies a rule of `AGENTS.md` instead of linking it |
| `mcp_template_invalid` | The MCP template is not the configuration shape |
| `prerequisites_differ` | The per-OS prerequisite table differs from the contract's |
| `install_row_missing` | A distribution the prerequisites name has no row in the install page |
| `link_missing` | A relative link of a user file resolves nowhere |
| `forbidden_term` | A user file contains a term from the private forbidden list |
